Verùm sit ita, hoc quidem respectu, Genus istud Communicatio Idiomatum dici nequeat: potest tamen dari alius etiam respectus, ratione cujus appellatio isthæc, Generi huic negari haud queat : eo nimirùm, quo unum cum altero talem communionem obtinet, ut neutrum Unitorum seorsim, sed semper cum communicatione alterius agit. Quod ipsum sanè in Genere etiam hoc secundo evenit, quod circa officium & operationes Messiæ potissimùm occupatur. In his enim quæcunque fiunt aut aguntur, ea non Una natura, sive divina, sive humana, egisse dicitur : sed tota persona, ex vi utriusque naturæ : agente quidem & præstante unaquaque naturâ, quod est sibi proprium : Sed id tamen cum Communicatione alterius naturæ. Undè Græcis etiam Genus hoc κοινοποία sive κοινοποίησις dictum est, quia videlicet in eo, naturæ utriusque vis communiter concurrit, ad opus quodlibet officii, meriti, aut beneficii Christi Servatoris.

Quibus ita præmissis, de Definitione Generis istius, faciliùs erit statuere : quòd nimirùm sit vera ac realis naturalium & propriarum utriusque Naturæ in Christo operationum Communicatio, ad unum producendum Redemtionis effectum : Ubi persona non agit aut operatur, in, sive cum una, aut per unam Naturam tantùm : Sed in, cum, per & secundum utramque Naturam : Vel ut Concilium Chalcedonense loquitur : Ubi una natura operatur, cum communicatione alterius, quod cujusque proprium est. Hinc Christus noster est Mediator, Redemtor, Rex, summus Pontifex, caput, Doctor, Pastor &c. non secundum unam naturam tantùm, sive divinam, sive humanam : sed secundum utramque. Hinc est, quòd Scriptura agens de opere Mediationis, interdum ejusmodi phrasibus utitur, quæ ad divinam Naturam digitum intendunt : ut Jerem. 23, 6. Jehovah justitia nostra :

Actor. 20, 28. Deus suo sanguine acquisivit Ecclesiam: Rom. 5, 10. Reconciliati sumus Deo per mortem Filii ejus. Gal. 4, 4. Filius Dei liberavit nos à maledictione legis. 1. Joh. 3, 8. Filius DEI dissolvit opera Diaboli. 2. Interim verò Humanam Christi Naturam notat : ut Gen. 3, 15. Semen mulieris conteret caput Serpentis. Luc. 9, 56. Filius Hominis venit salvare animas. 1. Tim. 2, 5. Unus est Mediator DEI & hominum, Homo Jesus Christus. 3. Interdum denique toti personæ ἀποτελέσματα isthæc adsignat, ut, Gal. 3, 13. Christus factus pro nobis maledictum, redemit nos à maledictione legis. Eph. 2, 5. Christus dedit seipsum pro nobis hostiam & oblationem DEO, in odorem Svavitatis. Quæ sanè dicta, vera non essent, si vel prioris illius Generis propositiones, secundum Osiandrum de sola divinitate: vel posterioris generis enunciationes secundum Stancarum, de sola humanitate essent accipiendæ: Quin utrasque, quantumvis ad alterutram naturam digitum intendant, de tota tamen persona Christi, respectu utriusque Naturæ intelligendas esse, Tertii hujus generis propositiones liquidò demonstrant.

Ex qua observatione natæ sunt Regulæ Theologicæ, notatu dignissimæ.

I. Actiones & passiones non sunt Naturarum, sed personæ: salvis tamen naturarum proprietatibus.

II. Ad divisionem operationum, sequitur divisio etiam personæ: Siquidem non natura agit aut patitur: sed persona. Nisi enim totius personæ operatio requireretur: Unione duarum naturarum in unam personam, minimè fuisset opus.

III. Ad unum producendum effectum sive ἀποτέλεσμα, semper alterutra natura agit cum communicatione alterius, agente quidem una quàque quòd sibi est proprium: Concurrente tamen vi & facultate alterius naturæ. Exempli gratia: Divina natura agit ea, quæ divinitatis sunt propria: sed ut ἀποτέλεσμα Redemtionis perficiat, operationibus utitur humanitatis propriis: Sic Humana agit itidem, quæ sibi sunt propria: sed non hæc solum: verum etiam ea quæ humanitatis vires & facultates superant, vi communicatæ sapientiæ & potentiæ divinæ: uti mox in tertio Genere demonstrabitur.

Tumultuatur hoc loco Spiritus Calvinianus, nobisq; objicit Confusionem Secundi & subsequentis tertii Generis, eò, quòd statuamus, Humanam naturam concurrere ad perficienda Mediationis ἀποτελέσματα, non modò secundum vires & proprietates naturales, sed & secundum ea, quæ ex Communicatione Majestatis divinæ accepit. Sed rectè negatur Consequentia: Neque enim statim duo isthæc Genera confunduntur, quando asseritur, Secundum hoc genus præsupponere Humanæ Christi Naturæ ὑπερύψωσιν, tertio genere comprehensam: sed ostenditur tantùm, Undenam Natura humana habeat, ut præter & ultra vires suas naturales, divina etiam operari possit. Quæ verò & qualis illa sit ὑπερύψωσις: non in hoc secundo, sed subsequente tertio Genere explicatur.

Deindè objiciunt Regulam illam Concilii Chalcedonensis: Unaquæque natura agit, cum communicatione alterius, id quod cujusque est proprium, Quam sic intelligunt, quòd in perficiendis istiusmodi ἀποτελέσμασι, divina Natura agat divina: Humana verò tantùm etiam agat, quæ ex suis naturalibus proprietatibus operari potest, nempè Humana.

Respondeo: Fallit argumentum manifesto ψεύδει sive Crimine falsi: idque dupliciter:

1. Quod falsum omninò ac peregrinum Regulæ huic sensum assuunt: qui manifestè mutilant, ac si non certæ alicujus emphaseos illa essent verba, quæ in Regula exprimūtur: Naturam quidem unamquamque agere id, quod cujusque est proprium: Sed cum Communicatione alterius. 2. Quod hæc ipsa verba, tantum intelligunt de nuda παραστάσει sive assistentia, qua duæ naturæ in perficiendis illis ἀποτελέσμασι sibi tantùm mutuò adsint sine ulla reali operationum κοινωνίᾳ. A quo utroq́; commento, Regula Chalcedonensis modis omnibus abhorret: statuens ita unamquamque naturam agere id, quod cujusque proprium est, ut tamen illis intercedat invicem verissima communio: ut divina quidem natura operationibus humanis suo modo participet: Humana verò ita divinis operationibus communicet, ut præter naturalia, etiam divina operetur: idqueex gratia Unionis. Unde Patres Divinam Christi Actionem Humanatam: Humanam verò Deificatam: ἀποτέλεσμα denique sive Effectum ipsum, θεανδρικὸν, hoc est, Dei virile, appellare consveverunt.

Et profectò cum in hac ipsa Objectione impietatem Dogmatis sui manifestè prodant Adversarii, nos firmis & immotis rationibus demonstrabimus, Humanam naturam in perficiendis operationibus istis Mediationis, præter & ultra vires naturales, divina etiam operari & perficere.

I. Extra controversiam est positum, Divinas actiones officii Christi esse, Conterere caput Serpentis, redimere genus humanum, expiare peccata totius mundi, satisfacere infinitæ justitiæ divinæ, vivificare, regere & conservare universam Ecclesiam, pascere & salvare illam &c.

Atqui Scriptura Sacra actiones istas disertè Christo etiam adsignat, secundum assumtam humanitatem, quando in abstracto affirmat: Semen mulieris conteret Caput Serpentis. Gen. 3, 15. In semine Abrahæ benedicentur omnes gentes: Gen. 12 3. 18, 18. 22, 18. Filius Hominis venit salvare quod perierat. Luc. 9, 56. Germen Davidis est Jehovah, justitia nostra. Jerem. 23, 5. 33. 15. Caro Christi est vivifica Joh. 6, 51. & 53. Corpus Carnis Christi reconciliat nos DEO Patri, Coloss. 1, 22. Sangvis Christi emundat nos ab omni peccato 1. Joh. 1, 7. Heb. 9. 14. &c.

Quin ergò Humana Christi natura, in perficiendis istis ἀποτελέσμασι, præter & ultra naturales facultates edat & operetur etiam actiones divinas ex Communicata sapientia & potentia τοῦ λόγου: nemo certè pius unquam dubitaverit.

II. Opus Mediationis ut sit integrum & perfectum, non tantùm Merito sive acquisitione salutis, sed & ejusdem efficacia & applicatione constat.

Jam si Meritum tantùm, non item efficacia & applicatio salutis Christo secundum Humana etiam natura esset assignanda: consequens foret, Executionem officii, quæ in applicatione meriti acquisiti consistit, ad Christum secundum Humanam naturam nihil pertinere: & per consequens ipsum juxta eandem in conferendâ vitâ planè ociosum esse.

Quod cùm manifestè sit absurdum & scripturis contrarium, quippè quæ ipsam carnem Christi vivificam esse asserit: falsum utique fuerit, in hoc opere Mediationis perficiendo & consummando, Humanam naturam tantùm naturalem præstare actionem.

III. Miracula, in statu etiam Exinanitionis à Christo edita, quin divinam majestatem ac potentiam arguant, nemini potest esse dubium.

Atqui hæc ipsa Miracula, Christo etiam secundum humanam naturam sunt adscribenda. Ergò.

Minorem dupliciter probo: 1. Dilucidâ assertione ipsarum Scripturarum, quæ affirmant Christum in nuptiis Canæ Galileæ feciffe initium Signorum, & manifestasse suam gloriam, Joh. 2, 11. Moses sanè, Prophetæ & Apostoli edentes miracula nuspiam leguntur SUAM manifestasse gloriam, sed alienam. Hinc Petrus sanaturus claudum, non dicit: Ego tibi dico, Surge & ambula: Sed sic informat Sermonem : In nomine Jesu Christi Nazareni surge & ambula: Actor. 3, 6. Et cum Apostoli rogarentur à Scribis & Pharisæis: In qua virtute, aut in quo nomine fecerint hoc? Disertè respondent: In nomine Jesu Christi Nazareni astat iste coram vobis sanus. Actor. 4, 7. & 10. Cæterùm miraculum hoc in nuptiis factum, non à solo λόγῳ, sive à divina Christi naturâ, sed à Christo, quatenus Christus, hoc est, unctus est, perpetratum fuisse narrat Johannes, & quidem ut manifestaret SUAM Gloriam, eam nimirùm, quàm per Unionem quidem acceperat, sed sub servi formâ tectam occultabat. 2. Exemplo valdè illustri mulieris hæmorrhoüsæ, in cujus sanatione Christus virtutem EX SE egressam esse asserit: Luc. 8, 46. Jam verò iuxta Deitatem Christus hoc sentire non potuit: ut quæ ejusmodi sensionis, qualis hic exprimitur, prorsus expers est. Ergò in sancta sua Humanitate hoc sensit, ex se scilicet virtutem talem egressam: quatenus virtus Deitatis propria existens, in carne autem personaliter omni sua plenitudine habitans, per eandem carnem in sanatione mulieris se exercuit. Qua de re præclarè admodum Cyrillus: Quia intellexit mulier, quæ esset caro Sancta Sanctorum, iccircò accessit & ipsa. Ipsa quidem Carnem suam attingere non audet: nondum enim mundata erat: neque quæ perfecta sunt, apprehenderat: sed fimbriam tetigit vestimenti, quo sancta Caro tegebatur, & Fideli tactu VIRTUTEM elicuit EX CARNE, quâ se ab immundiciâ sanctificaret. Cyrill. lib. 4. in Levic.

IV. Act. 10, 34. inquit Petrus: Jesum Nazarenum unxit DEUS Spiritu Sancto & Virtute, qui pertransiit benefaciendo & sanãdo omnes oppressos à Diabolo: Quoniam DEUS erat cum illo.

secundum humanam naturam, Unctio haec ipsi obtigerit, necessarium & infallibile est consequens.

Ubi observationem etiam meretur, quòd Petrus inquit: Quoniam DEUS erat cum illo, sic manifestè innuens, DEUM λόγον personaliter unitum humanitati, edidisse prodigia non solùm, essentiali suâ divinâ Omnipotentiâ, sed per assumtam humanitatem, illam ipsam omnipotentiam suam exeruisse: non eâ ratione, quâ per Apostolos: sed longè sublimiore, quatenus nimirùm eam, infinitâ Spiritus sui plenitudine inunxit, hoc est, admisit eam in realem κοινωνίαν omnipotentis virtutis, quâ ea ederet miracula, quæ ex naturali virtute edere nunquam potuisset, ita ut Humana hæc natura in perficiendis hisce miraculis, non ὄργανον mortuum, exanime aut ἄπρακτον: sed maximè σύνεργον & efficax: & λόγος hanc ipsam carnem suam ad efficacem operationem miraculorum adhiberet: unâ utrinque virtute divinâ operante: sed diverso respectu: Quoad λόγον, originaliter & essentialiter: Quoad assumtam carnem, personaliter & ἑπομένως, hoc est, ex Unione hypostatica, & hanc consequente reali Idiomatum κοινωνίᾳ.

V. Et postremum argumentum monstrat Orthodoxa Antiquitas, cui testimonia in Appendice Libri Concordiæ legere licet. Sufficiat hoc loco unus Cyrillus, qui lib. de Incarnatione Unigeniti sic habet: Communes facit Unigenitus cum carne sua, divina suæ Majestatis operationes, ut possit etiam vivificare mortuos, sanare infirmos.

Et in cap. 6. Esaiæ: Quemadmodum pruna lignum quidem est naturâ: verum tota omni ex parte igni plena est, ejusque vim & efficacitatem habet: ad eundem modum, & ipse Dominus noster Jesus Christus, meritò potest intelligi: λόγος enim caro factus est, & commoratus inter nos. Verùm quamvis esset Homo visus nobis similis ratione dispensationis: omnis tamen plenitudo Divinitatis in eo habitavit, modo inquam adunationis. Hinc & in CARNE SUA DIVINISSIMAM OPERANDI VIRTUTEM habere cernitur. Tacto siquidem loculo mortuum Viduæ filium resuscitavit, & cum inspuisset, ludo inunctis oculis, cæcis visum restituit.

Quibus ita constitutis execranda est blasphemia Lamberti Danæi, quin in epistola ad fratres Tubingenses p. 19. & 20. Item in Examine libelli Chemnitii de duabus naturis in Christo, pag. 118. & 156. scribere non exhorruit, Naturam Christi humanam in patrandis miraculis plus non fecisse, quàm fecerit Virga Mosis, in miraculis coram Pharaone editis, Item, Vocem illam Christi excitantis Lazarum & dicentis, Lazare veni foràs: fuisse duntaxat nudum sonitum, qui ad vitam Lazari nihil contulerit. Undè manifestum est, ipsum & Socios, Humanitati assumtæ in miraculis nihil quicquam aliud præter externum illud Ministerium & Vocem tribuere (id quod Apostoli etiam præstare poterant) & ad hoc solum externum Ministerium, quo vocem vel tactum accommodabat Christi caro, restringere Patrum Testimonia, contra ipsorum etiam Patrum mentem & sententiam.

Etsi enim Athanasius dicit, Miracula facta esse MINISTERIO CORPORIS: tamen non tale ministerium intelligit, quale describunt Calviniani: Sed Ministerium etiam ad ipsam divinam operationem efficacissimè concurrens. Nominare autem voluit Ministerium, ut ostenderet, virtutem edendi miracula originaliter τῶ λόγῳ esse propriam: atque sic principatum miraculorum Christi residere penes Deitatem: minus principaliter autem, & vi unionis, competere eam Christo, quâ Homo est. Quo sensu idem Athanasius rectissimè etiam scripsit, Resuscitationē Lazari, non humanitàs, sed DIVINITUS esse designatam: nempè ratione Originis sive principatus Miraculorum. Interim verò minimè negasse ipsum, Humanam Naturam Christi potentiâ edendorum miraculorum, ex Unione, instructam & donatam esse, vel ex eo constat, quod in Evangelium de Sanctissima Deipara scribit: Hunc Hominem, quem dicimus, à λόγῳ gestatum, hunc ipsum DEUS Pater cooperatione Spiritus Sancti, unà simul collaborante Filio, inunxit Spiritu Sancto, tribuens ei omnem efficaciam, eundemque virtute Altissimi circumcinxit, ut posset sustinere omnem adversariae potestatis impetum, & operari deindè curationem in populo.

Et Dialogo quinto contra Apollinaristas: Sicut anima in corpore: Sic DEUS λόγ unitus homini edidit prodigia, non separatus à natura assumta: sed placuit ei, IN EA, CUM EA & per EAM, potentiam suam divinam exerere.

Et stolidum planè est, quòd Calvinianorum nonnulli hoc loco audent distinguere inter ἐνεργείας omnipotentes; & inter apotelesmata (leaνεργημα: quasi ad haec quidem, non verò ad illas perficiendas, efficaciter concurrat caro Christi. Quis enim ita bardus sit, ut negare ausit, Miracula esse omnipotentes ἐνεργείας? Siccinè ergò Caecis visui, surdos auditui, mutos vocis usuirestituere, leprosos sanare, imò vel absentes etiam verbulo dundaxat curare: quin jam verò mortuos in vitam revocare, & quae hujus generis stupenda opera sunt alia: humana, non verò divina erunt ἐνέργειαι? Sed nimirùm hoc sibi volunt Sophistae hac distinctione: Ex divina quidem virtute oriri isthæc miracula: sed in eorum executione, nullam prorsus inter Christum, quoad Humanitatem & inter Apostolos, esse differentiam: itaut quemadmodum his, ita illi externum tantùm Ministerium relinquatur. Quo nùm quicquam magis impium, & auditu intolerabilius in Ecclesia DEI unquam vel dictum, vel scriptum sit, meritò dubitatur. Et quô tandem evasura sit isthæc impietas, satis testatur Neuseri, aliorumque Calvinianorum, ad castra Mahometistarum transitus: qui apertè cum Turcis docuerunt: Christum hominem non aliter ac caeteros Prophetas & Apostolos, sua signa & miracula operatum esse.


### Chapter III. on the Effect of the Hypostatic Union of the two Natures in Christ: The Third Genus of the Communication of Idioms

This third kind of Communication of Idioms, which considers those ἀξιώματα that were communicated to the human Nature of Christ from the Union with the λόγῳ, and those not finite or created, but altogether infinite and divine: the Calvinist and Jesuit faction is accustomed to hate worse than a dog and a snake. For it is certain that both expressly derogate from the communication of divine Majesty to the humanity assumed by the λόγῳ, writing explicitly that the Idioms of Deity can in no way be really communicated to any created nature, and therefore not to the humanity of Christ, even with respect to the Union: And as we learned above in chapter 2 regarding the Calvinist heresy from Theodore Beza: If at any time the properties of the Natures seem to be interchanged, then that is done through ἀλλοίωσιν, or a verbal Communication of Idioms. This heresy is too foul to be sufficiently explained in words: for it undermines and overturns, as if with a single blow, the whole mystery of the union of the two natures in Christ. Lest we appear to assert this out of passion, it pleases us to argue from their own opinion.

To whatever nature the divine idioms of the nature of the Logos are not communicated,

And yet, according to the Calvinist opinion, the divine attributes of the Logos cannot in any way, not even with respect to the Union, be truly and really communicated to the assumed humanity.

Therefore, neither could the very ὑπόsασις of the Logos be communicated to the same: and consequently, it could not even be united in any way.

The connection of the major premise is clearly evident even from this: since the ὑπόsασις of the Logos and its divine ἰδιώματα are so much an indivisible and identical thing, that in reality there is absolutely no distinction between them: but necessarily, if one is denied, the other is also denied; if one is communicated, the other is also communicated.

This will appear more clearly from the arguments which we shall bring forward a little later for the confirmation of our doctrine.

ORTHODOX THESIS.

Our doctrine holds thus regarding this third Genus, that we believe and confess that the Logos or Son of God, by assuming human nature into the unity of his ὑπόsασις, communicated himself entirely, and thus all the attributes of his Divinity, really, so that whatever the Logos is and has by Essence, that the assumed humanity has by the grace of the Union. Whence in the Scriptures this Genus is called ὑπερύψωσις, Phil. 2:9, and by the Fathers it has been distinguished by the terms μεταποιΐα, βελτίωσις, θέωσις, ἀποθέωσις, and other words of that kind expressing the Majesty of the assumed humanity. Today in the Schools it has deservedly come to be called the Communication of Majesty.

With this θέσει (thesis) standing, a clear distinction soon emerges between the first and the Third Kind of Communication of Idioms: and it is threefold: First, in the first kind, because the divine Nature is subject to no changes or passions: therefore only concrete expressions have a place in it: In this Third kind, however, because human nature admits of change and its own perfection, and could be exalted without its own destruction: therefore abstract expressions also have a place, so that it may be said of the Flesh of Christ in the abstract, but not outside the Union, that it is Omnipotent, Omniscient, etc.

Then in the first kind the Communication is reciprocal, in the way that was shown above: In this third kind, however, Reciprocation has no place, but such a Communication is established which occurs from one side only, namely from the divine Nature into the human.

Finally, in the first Kind, distinctive particles show of which nature that which is enunciated in the concrete about the other nature, of which it is not proper, is the property. In the third Kind, however, the use of distinctive particles is to demonstrate according to which Nature the Communication of Majesty, or Exaltation, happened to Christ.

Moreover, two things especially must be demonstrated concerning this Third Kind: 1. That this Communication of Majesty is to be understood not of finite or created gifts, however excellent, but of infinite and uncreated gifts: indeed, of the divine Majesty itself. 2. That this very thing, of the infinite divine Majesty, truly and really happened to Christ according to the assumed humanity.

It is my pleasure to assert and confirm both members against the Sophistries of the Calvinists and Jesuits with the following arguments.

Latin:

TErtium hoc genus Communicationis Idiomatum, quod considerat ea ἀξιώματα, quæ humanæ Naturæ Christi, ex Unione cum λόγῳ, communicata sunt: eaque non finita aut creata: sed infinita planè & divina: Gens Calviniana & Jesuitica, cane & angve pejus odisse solet. Certum enim est, utrosque Communicationem divinæ Majestatis λόγꙋ assumtæ humanitati ex professo derogare: disertè scriptitantes, Idiomata Deitatis nulla planè ratione, ulli naturæ creatæ, ac proindè neque humanitati Christi, etiam respectu Unionis realiter communicari posse: Et ut supra cap. 2. in hæresi Calvinistica ex Theodoro Beza cognovimus: Si quando proprietates Naturaru videantur permutari, tùm illud fieri per ἀλλοίωσιν, sive verbalem Communicationem Idiomatum. Fœdior est hæc hæresis, quàm ut verbis satis explicari queat: Siquidem uno quasi ictu, totum mysterium Unionis duarum naturarum in Christo subruit & evertit. Quod ne ex affectu asseverare videamur, sic placet ex ipsorum sententia argumentari.

Cuicunque Naturæ non Communicantur Idiomata divina naturæ τꙋ λόγꙋ: eidem nec ipsa ὑπόsασις λόγꙋ communicari, ac nedum uniri potest.

Atqui ex sententia Calviniana, divina idiomata τꙋ λόγꙋ, assumtæ humanitati, nulla ratione, ne quidem respectu Unionis, verè ac realiter Communicari possunt.

Ergò neque ipsa ὑπόsασις τꙋ λόγꙋ eidem communicari: & per consequens, ne quidem ulla ratione uniri potuit.

Majoris connexum vel indè liquidò patet: Siquidem ὑπόsασις λόγꙋ ejusdemque ἰδιώματα divina, sic sunt Unum quid ἀδιαιρέτως, & ταυτὸ, ut revera nullum prorsus inter ea sit discrimen: sed necessariò negato uno, negetur etiam alterum: Communicato uno, communicetur etiam alterum.

Patebit hoc dilucidiùs ex iis, quæ pro Confirmatione nostræ doctrinæ, paulò pòst, proferemus argumenta.

THESIS ORTHODOXA.

SIc verò habet Doctrina nostra, quoad tertium hoc Genus, quòd credimus ac confitemur λόγον sive Filium DEI, assumendo naturam humanam in suæ ὑποsάσεως unitatem, seipsum totum, & sic omnia Divinitatis suæ Idiomata, realiter communicasse, ita ut quodcunque λόγꙋ est & habet per Essentiam, illud assumta Humanitas habeat per gratiam Unionis. Undè in Scripturis dictum est hoc Genus ὑπερύψωσις, Phil. 1, 9. à Patribus verò μεταποιΐα, βελτίωσις, θέωσις, ἀποθέωσις, & id genus aliis vocabulis, Majestatem assumtæ Humanitatis exprimentibus, insignitum est. Hodiè in Scholis usitatè Communicatio Majestatatis dici meruit.

Stante hac θέσει luculentum mox emergit discrimen inter primum, & Tertium Genus Communicationis Idiomatum: idque triplex: Primùm enim in primo genere, quia Natura divina, mutationibus sive passionibus nullis est obnoxia: ideò concretivæ tantùm locutiones in eo locum habent: In hoc autem Tertio genere, quia natura humana mutationem, suíq; perfectionem admittit, citraquè sui destructionem exaltari potuit: ideò abstractivæ etiam locutiones locum habent, ut de Carne Christi in abstracto, sed non extra Unionem, dici queat, quòd sit Omnipotens, Omniscia, &c.

Deindè in primo genere reciproca est Communicatio, eo modo, quo suprà ostensum: In hoc verò tertio genere, Reciprocatio locum non habet, sed talis Communicatio statuitur, quæ ex una tantùm parte fiat, nempè ex Natura divina in humanam.

Tandem in primo Genere particulæ distinctivæ ostendunt, cujus naturæ proprium sit id, quod de altera natura, cujus non est proprium, in concreto enunciatur. In tertio autem Genere distinctivarum particularum usus est, ut demonstrent, secundum quam Naturam Christo Communicatio Majestatis, sive Exaltatio obtigerit.

Cæterùm duo potissimùm circa Tertium hoc Genus, demonstranda veniunt: 1. Quòd Communicatio hæc Majestatis, non de finitis aut creatis, quantumvis excellentibus, sed de infinitis & increatis donis: imò de ipsa divina Majestate sit intelligenda. 2. Quòd hæc ipsa infinitæ Majestatis divinæ, Christo secundum assumtam humanitatem verè ac realiter obtigerit.

Utrumque membrum adversus Calvinianorum & Jesuvvitarum Sophisticationes, sequentibus argumentis asserere & confirmare libet.


### Chapter III. on the Effect of the Hypostatic Union of the two Natures in Christ: I. Argument from Communicated Omnipotence

I. ARGUMENT from Communicated Omnipotence.

1. It is placed beyond Controversy that OMNIPOTENCE or all power in heaven and on earth is clearly infinite and divine power.

But this very all power in Heaven and on earth has been Communicated to the assumed humanity of Christ.

Therefore it is necessary that infinite and divine power has been communicated to him.

The major premise is most certain in itself: nor can it be dragged into Controversy, even in appearance, at least plausibly. And even if it were dragged in as much as possible, yet that single description of this power which exists in Daniel would shake off all that attack. For thus those [verses] say, ch. 7, 13 & 14: He gave him power, and honor, and a kingdom: that all peoples, tribes, and Languages should serve him: his power is an eternal power, which shall not be taken away, and his kingdom, which shall not be corrupted.

The clear testimonies of the Scriptures demonstrate the minor premise most evidently: Psalm 8, 5 & seqq.: What is the SON OF MAN, that you visit him? You have made him a little lower than the Angels: but you have crowned him with glory and honor, and have set him over the works of your hands: You have subjected ALL THINGS under his feet. Daniel 7, 14: I was watching in the vision of the night, and behold with the clouds of heaven, as it were the SON OF MAN was coming, and he reached even to the ancient of days: And power and honor were given to Him, etc. Matthew 28, 18: All power in Heaven and on earth has been given TO ME. Matthew 11, 27: ALL THINGS have been delivered to me by my Father. 1 Cor. 15, 26 & 27: He subjected ALL THINGS under his FEET: except him who subjected all things to him: Which the Epistle to the Hebrews explaining, says: He subjected all things under his feet: In that therefore that he subjected all things to him, he omitted nothing that is not subjected to him. Ephesians 1, 20. GOD raised Christ from the dead and set him (by reason of that nature according to which he could be raised from the dead) at his right hand in the heavenly places above every principality, power, virtue, dominion, and above every name that is named not only in this age: but also in the future. Apocal. 5, 12: Worthy is the LAMB, who was slain, TO RECEIVE virtue, riches, wisdom, fortitude, honor, glory, etc. The Consensus of Orthodox antiquity is added: from which let it be permitted to hear one Athanasius, who, discoursing about the saving advent of Christ, says thus among other things: But if you hear Peter speaking, he made this very Jesus, whom you crucified, Christ and LORD: of whom do you understand this word HE MADE? If of the Divinity of the Word, why then do you rebuke the Arians? Since you think the same as they do. But if of the Form of a Servant, which was in the Word, why do you contend to fight with us? These things being thus established, our Conclusion remains invincible, namely that the Divine Omnipotence was truly and really communicated to the assumed Humanity of Christ. The Adversaries object two things especially in this place: 1. That these testimonies, both individual and universal, are to be understood not of the human Nature, but of the whole Person. 2. Although the Divinity of the λόγος, in itself and with respect to itself, can neither be exalted nor receive anything in time: yet it can in some way be said to be exalted, and indeed with respect to us: namely, in three ways: 1. Insofar as through the passion and death of Christ, a kind of darkness was as it were cast over his Divinity, so that afterwards, when it was removed by the Resurrection, it can be said to be in some way exalted: but with respect to us. 2. Insofar as through the preaching of the Gospel, the λόγος was more and more recognized among all nations: and thus exalted with respect to Men. 3. Insofar as GOD is said everywhere in the Psalms to be exalted, extolled, and glorified by men. I answer: That both Objections wander outside the olive groves, and therefore are truly devoid of proof. For as regards the former, we ourselves have also never denied that those testimonies of Scripture, already produced, are to be understood of the person: but not of the Human Nature considered separately. But the hinge of the Controversy does not turn on that: But this is asked: Whether those things which were given to the person of Christ in time, were given in respect of the divine, or in respect of the human, or in respect of both? Here is Rhodes, here is the leap. It must therefore be demonstrated to the Adversaries that divine Omnipotence was so communicated to the person of Christ in time: that in the meantime the assumed Humanity never arrived at a real κοινωνίαν or participation of it. Which they can never demonstrate: unless they wish either to divide the person of Christ into two persons: or to subscribe to the Arian impiety. That is for this reason, Because if this Majesty was communicated to the person: and indeed, according to the Calvinian hypothesis, the assumed flesh was not made a real participant of this Majesty: then that person would exist outside of this assumed flesh: as Nestorius blasphemed. But this is for this reason: Because if the communicated divine Majesty happened to the person of Christ in time: and that not in respect of the assumed humanity: then it must be that it happened to the person according to the divinity. Which being granted, it follows immediately that the Divine nature could be exalted in time, and endowed with divine Majesty. But Arius drags anyone who thinks such things into his company, as Leo rightly pronounced. It remains therefore, that that divine Omnipotence was indeed given or communicated to the Person: but in respect of the assumed human Nature.

The latter objection likewise maliciously perverts the state of the controversy. For it is not asked in this place about such an exaltation as might be defined in some way in respect of Men: But about such a one, by which Christ in himself in respect of himself was made better, crowned, exalted, and raised to the right hand of the Majesty, virtue, and power of GOD the Father, in respect of himself (even if no mortal were to acknowledge or believe it) truly and in reality, from a more ignoble condition was transferred and raised to the fellowship of the divine Majesty. Since such an Exaltation can be ascribed to the Divine nature of the λόγος in no species and by no probable reason: the Adversaries are found to be laboring entirely in vain, and fighting with the hood of their own brain. And if they were curable, we would correct their fictitious hypothesis in this manner: Whatever from eternity, on account of the most simple perfection and most absolute immutability of Nature, is entirely devoid of every mutation, as much regarding a better state as a worse: to it nothing of emptying or exaltation, nothing of glory or infamy, in respect of itself, can in any way happen in time. But that former point, concerning the divine nature of Christ, is self-evident among all Orthodox believers. Therefore this latter point also concerning the same Divinity of Christ ought to be placed beyond all risk of doubt. The very ἀντίθεσις and the proper affection of the contention most clearly demonstrate the infallible and irrefragable connection of the major premise. For whatever by any reason IN RESPECT OF ITSELF receives any mutation, either for the better or for the worse:

that cannot be or be called most simply perfect and most absolutely immutable. But it pleases me to press the Adversaries more strongly. Therefore let this be the second argument:

Latin:

I. ARGUMENTUM à Communicatâ Omnipotentiâ.

1. Extra Controversiam est positum, OMNIPOTENTIAM sive omnem potestatem in cælo & in terra esse infinitam & divinam planè potentiam.

Atqui hæc ipsa omnis potestas in Cælo & in terra Communicata est assumtæ humanitati Christi.

Ergò infinita planè & divina potentia ipsi communicata sit, necesse est.

Major per se est certissima: neque vel in speciem saltem probabiliter, in Controversiam rapi potest. Et si vel maximè raperetur, tamen vel unica illa potestatis hujus descriptio, quæ apud Danielem extat, omnem istum impetum concuteret. Sic enim illæ cap. 7. 13. & 14. Dedit ei potestatem, & honorem & regnum: ut omnes populi, tribus & Lingvæ serviant ei: potestas ejus potestas æterna, quæ non auferetur, & regnum ejus, quod non corrumpetur.

Minorem evidentissimè demonstrant perspicua Scripturarum testimonia: Psalm. 8, 5. & seqq. Quid est FILIVS HOMINIS, quòd visitas eum? Minuisti eum paulò ab Angelis: sed gloria & honore coronasti eum, & constituisti eum super opera manuum tuarum: OMNIA subjecisti sub pedibus ejus. Daniel. 7, & 14. Adspiciebam in visione noctis, & ecce cum nubibus cæli, quasi FILIVS HOMINIS veniebat, & usque ad antiquum dierum pervenit: Et pervenit Ei potestas em & honorem, &c. Matth. 28, 18. Data est MIHI omnis potestas in Cælo & in terra. Matth. 11, 27. OMNIA tradita mihi sunt à Patre meo. 1. Cor. 15, 26. & 27. OMNIA subjecit sub PEDIBUS ejus: excepto eo, qui ei subjecit omnia: Id quod explicans Epistola ad Hebræos: Omnia, inquit, subjecisti sub pedibus ejus: In eo ergò quòd omnia ei subjecit, nihil omisit, quod non sit subjectum ei. Ephes. 1, 20. DEUS resuscitavit Christum à mortuis & constituit ipsum (ratione illius naturæ, secundum quam ex mortuis excitari potuit) ad dexteram suam in cælestibus super omnem principatum, potestatem, virtutem, dominationem, & super omne nomen, quod nominatur non solùm in hoc seculo: sed & in futuro. Apocal. 5, 12. Dignus est AGNUS, qui occisus est, ACCIPERE virtutem, divitias, sapientiam, fortitudinem, honorem, gloriam, &c. Accedit Consensus Orthodoxæ antiquitatis: ex qua unum liceat audire Athanasium, qui de salutari adventu Christi differens, sic inter reliqua: Quòd si audieritis, Petrum loquentem, Christum & DOMINUM fecit hunc ipsum Jesum, quem vos crucifixistis: de quo hoc vocabulum FECIT intelligitis? Si de verbi Divinitate, cur Arianos igitur reprehenditis? Cùm idem cum illis sentiatis. Sin de Forma Servi, quæ fuit in Verbo, cur nobiscum pugnare contenditis? Quibus ita constitutis invicta manet Conclusio nostra, nempè Divinam Omnipotentiam verè ac realiter assumtæ Humanitati Christi communicatam esse. Duo potissimum hoc loco objiciunt Adversarii: 1. Quidem Testimonia isthæc singula atque universa, non de Natura humana; sed de Tota Persona intelligenda esse. 2. Etsi Divinitas λόγη, in se & respectu sui exaltari, vel in tempore aliquid accipere haud queat: aliquo tamen modo dici posse eam exaltatam, & quidem respectu nostri: idœ, tripliciter: 1. quatenus per passionem & mortem Christi, Caligo quasi quædam ejusdem Divinitati fuit offusa, ut postmodum eâ per Resurrectionem sublatâ, aliquo modo exaltata dici queat: sed respectu nostri. 2. Quatenus per prædicationem Evangelii, λόγος magis magisœ inter omnes gentes fuit agnitus: & sic exaltatus respectu Hominum. 3. Quatenus DEUS passim in Psalmis exaltari, extolli & glorificari dicitur ab hominibus. Respondeo: Utramque Objectionem extra oleas vagari, ac proindè verò ἐλέγχω destitui. Quoad priorem enim, Nos ipsi quoque nunquam negavimus, Testimonia illa Scripturarum, jam producta, de persona accipienda esse: non verò de Humanâ Naturâ seorsim considerata. Verùm in eo cardo Controversiæ non vertitur: Sed hoc quæritur: An ea, quæ persona Christi in tempore data sunt, respectu divinæ, vel respectu humanæ, vel respectu utriusq́, data sint? Hic Rhodus, hic saltus est. Demonstrandum ergò Adversariis, sic personæ Christi communicatam esse in tempore divinam Omnipotentiam: ut interim assumta Humanitas, in realem ejə κοινωνίαν sive participationem nunquàm pervenerit. Id quod in æternum demonstrare non possunt: nisi vel personam Christi in duas personas dirimere: vel Arianæ impietati subscribere velint. Illud ideò, Quia si personæ communicata est hæc Majestas: & verò, secundum hypothesin Calvinianam, Assumta caro Majestatis hujus non est realiter facta particeps: utique persona illa jam extra hanc carnem assumtam exiftet: uti Nestorius blasphemavit. Hoc verò ideò: Quia si personæ Christi obtigit in tempore communicata Majestas divina: idque non respectu assumtæ humanitatis: utique secundum divinitatem ea personæ obtigerit, necesse est. Quo concesso, statim sequitur, Divinam naturam in tempore potuisse exaltari, & Majestate divina donari. Sed talia sentientem, in societatem suam rapit Arius, uti rectè pronunciavit Leo. Relinquitur ergò, Personæ quidem datam sive communicatam esse illam divinam Omnipotentiam: sed respectu assumtæ Naturæ humanæ.

Posterior objectio itidem statum controversiæ malitiosè pervertit. Neque enim de tali exaltatione hoc loco quæritur, quæ respectu Hominum quodammodo definiri queat: Sed de tali, quâ Christus in se respectu sui melior factus, coronatus, exaltatus, & ad dextram Majestatis, virtutis & potentiæ DEI Patris evectus, respectu sui (si vel maximæ nullus mortalium illud agnosceret aut crederet) verè & reipsa, ex ignobiliore conditione in divinæ Majestatis consortium translatus & evectus fuit. Qualis Exaltatio cùm Divinitati λόγʊ nullâ specie, nullaque ratione probabili adscribi queat: frustrà omninò laborare, & cum proprii cerebri liripipio pugnare, deprehenduntur Adversarii. Et si sanabiles essent, hunc in modum fictitiam ipsorum Hypothesin corrigeremus: Quicquid ab æterno propter Naturæ simplicissimam perfectionem, & absolutissimam in mutabilitatem, omnis prorsus mutationis, tàm quo ad statum meliorem, quàm deteriorem est expers: illi nihil vel exinanitionis vel exaltationis, nihil vel gloriæ, vel infamiæ, respectu sui, in tempore ullo modo obtingere potest. Sed prius illud, de divina natura Christi, apud omnes Orthodoxos, est αυτόπισον. Ergò posterius etiam hoc de eadem Divinitate Christi extra omnem Dubitationis aleam debet esse positum. Majoris infallibile & irrefragabile connexum ipsa ἀντίθεσις & contentionis propria affectio luculentissimè demonstrat. Quicquid enim ullâ ratione RESPECTU SUI aliquid mutationis, vel in melius vel in deterius recipit:

illud simplicissimè perfectum, & absolutissimè immutabile esse, aut dici non potest. Sed placet fortiùs premere Adversarios. Argumentum ergò secundum hoc esto:


### Chapter III. on the Effect of the Hypostatic Union of the two Natures in Christ: II. a constructive Argument from the Anointing of Christ

II. A constructive ARGUMENT from the Anointing of CHRIST.

According to which Nature the Person of Christ was anointed in time with the oil of gladness above his fellows, or with the Holy Spirit not by measure: then according to the same he was instructed and adorned in time not with finite or created, but with gifts that are clearly infinite and divine.

But according to the Human Nature the Person of Christ was anointed in time with the oil of gladness above his fellows or with the Holy Spirit not by measure.

Therefore according to the same Human Nature he was also instructed and adorned in time with gifts that are clearly infinite and divine.

The connection of the major premise is sufficiently evident by itself: For these two things exclude each other: To be anointed with finite and created gifts: and to be anointed with the Holy Spirit not by measure. For whatever is not measured, can neither be finite and consequently cannot be created. Now whatever is unmeasured, infinite, and uncreated: that certainly cannot but be proper to the Divine Majesty.

I confirm the minor premise thus: Either the person of Christ was thus anointed, either according to the divine alone, or according to the human alone: or according to both at once. But the person of Christ was not thus anointed according to the divine nature, either alone or with the Human. Therefore it falls that it was according to both: And it remains that he could be thus anointed only according to the human Nature.

The reasons for this connection are these: 1. If Christ was anointed according to the divine Nature with the infinite fullness of the Holy Spirit: then this was done either from eternity: or in time. Not from eternity: Because thus Christ would have been from eternity: which is false.

For such He began to be in time: According to that of Peter, Acts 2:36. Let all the house of Israel know most certainly, that GOD HATH MADE that same Jesus, whom ye have crucified, both Lord and Christ: and Acts 10:38. GOD anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Ghost and with power. Nor does it stand in the way that in Ps. 2:2 the Son of GOD is called CHRIST: for in the prophetic manner of speaking, on account of the FUTURE INCARNATION, that He was so called by David is too well known to require laborious proof. It is added that in the whole of Holy Scripture, the eternal Generation of the Son is nowhere called an Anointing. Nor is this phrase analogous to the faith: The Son of GOD was anointed with the Holy Spirit in the eternal Generation. For thus the Generative principle would have to be referred not to the Father alone, but also to the Holy Spirit: Or certainly two different acts would have to be conceded by reason of the production of the Son: One of Generation, with respect to the Father: The other of anointing, with respect to the Holy Spirit: Which Since they are prodigiously absurd, nay manifestly blasphemous, it follows ex ἀνάγκης that this anointing cannot be understood of the divine nature with respect to eternity. 2. But neither was the divine nature anointed in time: because the λόγος could not be so anointed either before, or in, or after the incarnation, for the reason that no oil can be given or conceived of, except that oil of gladness and of the Holy Spirit, by which David and John testify that Christ was anointed: Ps. 45:8, John 3:34 & 35. Now if the divinity of Christ was anointed in time with such oil, that is, with the infinite fullness of the Holy Spirit, it must necessarily have lacked it before: which is impious and blasphemous. Nor do the adversaries profit even in the slightest by understanding this anointing as an ordination to office. For although we do not deny that Christ, according to both natures, was ordained by the eternal Father to the office of Mediator, John 10:36. We most simply deny, however, that that ordination is anything other than this anointing of which Scripture speaks. For ordination was accomplished from all eternity: 1 Pet. 1:20. But this anointing was due not from eternity, but in time. Lest we seem to affirm this beyond Scripture, we produce the prophet Daniel, who expresses the certain and definite time of this anointing in explicit words: Seventy weeks, he says, are determined upon thy people, and upon thy holy city, to finish the transgression, and to seal up sin: and to ANOINT the Most Holy. Hence the Messiah himself, speaking of himself, Isa. ch. 61:1, says: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me: because he hath anointed me: he hath sent me to preach to the poor: which the evangelist Luke, ch. 4:21, says was fulfilled at that time when the Messiah, brought forth into this light, undertook the office of mediation. Which very thing the Epistle to the Hebrews also intimates, asserting that that prophecy of Psalm 45:8, concerning Christ being anointed beyond his fellows, is to be referred to Christ incarnate, and placed at the right hand of God the Father. Heb. 1:4, 9, 13.

Let the authority of Damascenus be added by way of a conclusion, who in book 4, Orth. fid. c. 16, discourses thus concerning this Anointing of Christ: Some say that the name (CHRIST) belongs solely and properly to the Word begotten of GOD, understood and existing in Himself, but we do not teach or think or say so. For WHEN THE WORD BECAME FLESH, THEN we also say that He Himself became CHRIST: Because He was indeed anointed with the oil of gladness, that is, with the Holy Spirit, by GOD the Father. And for this cause He is named Christ. But that the Anointing takes place with respect to the HUMANITY, no one of those who are accustomed to think rightly will ever doubt.

And Ambrose, book 1, *de Fide*: GOD, your GOD, has anointed you with the oil of gladness above your fellows: it is GOD who anointed, and it is GOD who is anointed ACCORDING TO THE FLESH.

Latin:

II. ARGUMENTUM κατασκευαστικὸν ab Unctione CHRISTI.

Secundum quam Naturam Persona Christi, inuncta est in tempore, oleo lætitiæ ultra consortes, sive Spiritu Sancto non ad mensuram: utique secundum eandem non finitis aut creatis: sed infinitis ac divinis planè donis instructa & exornata est in tempore.

Atqui secundum Humanam Naturam Persona Christi inuncta est in tempore, oleo lætitiæ ultra consortes sive Spiritu sancto non ad mensuram.

Ergò secundum eandem Humanam Naturam infinitis etiam ac divinis planè donis in tempore instructa & exornata est.

Majoris connexum satis evidenter per se patet: Excludunt enim se mutuò isthæc duo: Finitis & creatis donis inungi: & non ad mensuram inungi Spiritu Sancto. Quicquid enim mensuratum non est, neque finitum & per consequens nec creatum esse potest. Jam quicquid immensuratum, infinitum & increatum est: illud utique non potest non Divinæ Majestatis esse proprium.

Minorem sic confirmo: Aut persona Christi sic inuncta est, vel secundum solam divinam, vel secundum solam humanam: vel secundum utramque simul. Non autem secundum divinam naturam, vel solam, vel cum Humana persona Christi sic est inuncta. Ergò corruit, quòd secundum utramque: Et relinquitur, quòd secundum solam humanam Naturam sic inungi potuerit.

Rationes connexi hujus sunt hæ: 1. Si Christus secundum divinam Naturam inunctus est infinitâ plenitudine Spiritus Sancti: tùm factum hoc vel ab æterno: vel in tempore. Ab æterno non: Quia sic ab æterno fuisset Christus: id quod falsum.

Talis enim in tempore esse cœpit: Secundum illud Petri Actor. 2, 36. Certissimè sciat omnis domus Israel, quia hunc Jesum, quem vos crucifixistis, FECIT DEUS & Dominum & Christum: & Act. 10, 38. DEUS unxit Jesum à Nazareth, Spiritu Sancto & virtute. Neque obstat, quòd Ps. 2, 2. Filius DEI appellatur CHRISTUS: nam prophetico loquendi genere ob FUTURAM INCARNATIONEM, sic ipsum à Davide appellati, notiùs est, quàm ut operosâ probatione indigeat. Accedit, quòd in universa Scriptura sacra, æterna Generatio Filii nuspiam nominatur Unctio. Neq; etiam hæc phrasis analoga est fidei: Filius DEI inunctus est Spiritu Sancto, in æterna Generatione. Sic enim principium Generativum non ad solum Patrem: sed ad Spiritum Sanctum etiam referendum esset: Vel certè duo diversi actus, ratione productionis Filii concedendi essent: Unus Generationis, respectu Patris: Alter inunctionis, respectu Spiritus Sancti: Quæ cum prodigiosè sint absurda, imò manifestè blasphema: ex ἀνάγκης conficitur: Unctionem hanc de divina natura, respectu æternitatis accipi non posse. 2. Sed neque in tempore Divina natura inuncta est: Quia neque ante, neque in, neque post incarnationem λόγος sic inungi potuit: propterea quòd Oleum dari aut excogitari nullum potest, præter Oleum illud lætitiæ & Spiritus Sancti, quo David & Johannes Christum inunctum esse testantur: Psal. 45, 8. Johan. 3, 34 & 35. Jam si Divinatis Christi in tempore tali oleo, hoc est, infinitâ plenitudine Spiritus Sancti inuncta fuit: prius eâ caruerit necesse est: Id quod impium & blasphemum. Neque vel tantillum proficiunt Adversarii, quòd Unctionem hanc de Ordinatione ad Officium intelligunt. Etsi enim non negamus, quin Christus secundum utramque naturam ab æterno Patre ordinatus sit ad officium Mediatoris, Joh. 10, 36. Ordinationem tamen illam nihil esse aliud, quàm Unctionem hanc, de qua Scriptura agit, simplicißimè negamus. Ordinatio enim facta fuit ab omni æternitate: 1. Pet. 1, 20. Unctio verò hæc, non ab æterno, sed in tempore debuit. Quod ne præter Scripturam affirmare videamur, producumus Prophetam Danielem, qui certum ac definitum Unctionis hujus tempus, disertis verbis exprimit: Septuaginta, inquiens, hebdomades determinatæ sunt super populum tuum, & super urbem sanctã, ut consummetur prævaricatio, & obsignetur peccatum: & UNGATUR Sanctus Sanctorum. Hinc Messias ipse dese verba faciens, Jes. c. 61, 1. Spiritus, inquit, Dominus super me: propterea unxit me: ad prædicandum pauperibus, misit me: Id quod Evangelista Lucas cap. 4, 21. tunc impletum fuisse dicit, quãdo Messias hanc in lucem editus, Officium Mediationis aggreffus est. Quod ipsum innuit etiam Epistola ad Hebræos, asserens vaticinium illud Psalmi 45, 8. de Christo inungendo ultra consortes suos, referendum esse ad Christum incarnatum, & collocatum ad dextram DEI Patris. Hebr. 1, 4. 9, 13.

Accedat Coronidis vice autoritas Damasceni, qui lib. 4. Orth. fid. c. 16 de Unctione hac Christi sic disserit: Quidam dicunt, quod nomen (CHRISTUS) conveniat soli, & propriè secundum seipsum intellecto & existenti ex DEO genito verbo, At nos non sic docemus aut sapere aut dicere. Nam QUANDO VERBUM CARO factum est, TUNC & ipsum dicimus factum esse CHRISTUM: Quia profectò unctus est oleo lætitiæ, id est, Spiritu Sancto, à DEO Patre. Et hac quod, causa Christus nominatur. Quod autem Unctio circa HUMANITATEM fit, nequaquam dubitaverit quispiam eorum, qui rectè sapere sunt consveti.

Et Ambrosius lib. 1. de Fide: Unxit te DEUS, DEUS tuus oleo lætitiæ præ consortibus tuis: DEUS est, qui unxit: & DEUS est, qui SECUNDUM CARNEM ungitur.


### Chapter III. on the Effect of the Hypostatic Union of the two Natures in Christ: III. Constructive Argument derived from the indwelling of the whole fullness of the Godhead in Christ

III. Constructive ARGUMENT derived from the indwelling of the whole fullness of the Godhead in CHRIST.

According to which Nature, the entire fullness of the Divinity truly and really dwells in Christ: according to the same, it is also necessary that CHRIST has truly and really become a κοινωνὸς of the infinite divine Majesty. But in Christ, according to the assumed Human Nature, the entire fullness of the Deity dwells. Therefore, according to the same assumed Human Nature, it is necessary that Christ has truly and really become a κοινωνὸς of the infinite divine Majesty.

The connection of the Major premise is partly evident enough in itself: and it will be more fully evident from the Confirmation of the Minor, in which lies τὸ κενούμενον.

Moreover, that classic aphorism in Colossians 2:9 confirms the minor premise: In Christ dwells all the fullness of the Godhead σωματικῶς, corporally. This aphorism, indeed, the more illustrious it is, the more foul is the sophistication of certain people by which they strive to obscure its clarity. For there are those who contend that the Apostle merely intends to hint at this: that Christ is full and perfect GOD. But this is clearly a gross ignorance of the refutation; for although by consequence the divinity of Christ can not ineptly be gathered and confirmed from this aphorism, the Apostle did not look directly to that, but rather wished to note that this indwelling of the entire Godhead is to be understood with respect to the flesh of Christ, as is demonstrated presently by firm arguments.

There are then, among whom our Author also is, who render this sense of the Apostolic Aphorism: In Christ dwells all the fullness of the Godhead bodily: that is: In other Saints GOD dwells by His Spirit, kindling new light and new motions: But in Christ He dwells not only by His Spirit; but also, so that by personal Union the human nature is united to the Divine. For as Pezelius infers, σωματικῶς according to the usage of the Greek language, signifies the same as ὑποστατικῶς personally, because σῶμα to the Greeks also signifies a person: as when the writer of the Peloponnesian war says: The city of the Athenians grew σώμασι καὶ χρήμασι that is, by the persons of the citizens and by wealth: And when Tertullian asks, whether λόγος is σῶμα: that is, a Person? I answer: That Philip's opinion is indeed not erroneous in itself, and in its own place is very true: but that it does not at all suit the present Apostolic Aphorism, inasmuch as it describes the Effect of the personal Union, rather than the Union itself: which will be most evidently demonstrated a little later.

As for Pezelius, he trifles rather than disputes. For even if among profane writers, σῶμα sometimes signifies a person: yet no sane man would deny that this is done συνεκδοχικῶς, with respect, namely, to the body. Wherefore if this sense were even most of all accommodated to the Apostolic Aphorism: certainly it would be consistent that not the person of the λόγος considered in itself and by itself: but the assumed nature itself, namely the flesh of Christ, is constituted the subject of this Indwelling. For just as the Attic citizens were called σώματα, in no other respect than insofar as they consisted of bodies, by which they also grew: so also in this place σωματικῶς, in the Apostle, cannot have reference to the ὑπόστασις τοῦ λόγου, which has nothing corporeal in itself: but only to the assumed flesh, or body: in respect of which this adverb σωματικῶς can have a place. As for Tertullian's question, he himself explains it thus: so that it is sufficiently evident that he used the word σώματος improperly and ὁμωνύμως.

But setting aside those impieties, we proceed to a more accurate explanation of the Apostolic Aphorism. At the beginning, however, the word HABITANDI (dwelling) comes under consideration: which clearly distinguishes the indweller from the indwelt: so that it expressly ascribes the act of indwelling to the whole fullness of the Divinity. This being presupposed, it becomes most plain that the sense of the Apostle's words cannot be given as: As if the whole fullness of the Divinity dwelt either in the person of the λόγος considered in itself, or in Christ according to the Divine Nature. For the person of the λόγος and his Divinity do not differ in reality: thus Deity and the fullness of Deity are something most simple, ταυτὸ, and therefore one dwelling in the other can be said only through a prodigious absurdity. It remains, therefore, that another dwelling place of the whole fullness of the Deity must be established: namely, the assumed FLESH OF CHRIST, in which, as in its own Temple, the whole fullness of the Divinity of the λόγος dwells. Next, the adverb σωματικῶς (corporally) deserves notation, which has great emphasis. For because neither the Deity, nor the fullness of the Divinity, nor the Person of the λόγος, as he is simply λόγος, is something σωματικὸν: certainly that adverb also denotes or defines none of those things. Furthermore, because the mode of union, or of the indwelling of the λόγος in the assumed human Nature, is not σωματικὸς (corporal). For the Human Nature did not assume the λόγος: but the person of the λόγος assumed flesh. Wherefore the mode of this union also, both from the person assuming and from the Term within which the Humanity is assumed, is called PERSONAL. It remains, therefore, for the adverb σωματικῶς to denote the subject in which the whole fullness of the Divinity dwells: namely, the flesh or human Nature of Christ, which has and possesses the whole λόγος, without any contraction or loss of his Infinity. And as Irenaeus speaks in lib. 3. cap. 18, it takes and comprehends: not as if the Divinity were enclosed as in a vessel, but by περιχώρησις, and an indivisible and utterly inseparable immanence in the assumed nature.

The whole Orthodox Antiquity confirms this interpretation of ours: as Cyril in lib. 2. ad Reginas: In whom did the whole fullness of the Deity dwell corporally? To think that this was done properly and separately in the Nature of the word would be very foolish. For it would be the same as if you said that the Only-begotten himself dwelt in himself.

The same in lib. 12. Thesauri cap. 15. The body of Christ is truly a Temple: For in it he willed that the whole fullness of the Deity should dwell corporally.

Athanasius de suscepta Natura hum. contra Apollin. When the Apostle says: That in Christ dwells the whole fullness of the Deity corporally: it is to be understood that that fullness dwells IN THE FLESH.

These things being thus established, the consequence of this argument of ours irrefragably infers that the whole fullness of the Divinity of the λόγος has been most truly and most really communicated to the Human Nature of Christ: and therefore also Omnipotence itself: which was to be demonstrated.

But in this place the Calvinist and Jesuit race rises up with great effort: and strives to overwhelm and overturn this assertion of ours with many arguments and absurdities: but at the beginning with an utterly vain effort, as will be evident from the Refutation of their arguments, in which they are accustomed to place the citadel of their victory.

THE FIRST is such: The finite is not capable of the Infinite: so that Solomon even affirms in 2 Paral. 6, 18, that the heaven of heavens does not contain the Lord. Therefore, neither is the finite Human Nature capable of infinite omnipotence, or of the whole fullness of the Divinity of the λόγος: and that so much the less, as it is smaller and narrower than this universe of things.

I answer. 1. That there is committed both a μετάβασιν εἰς ἄλλο γένος (transition to another genus), and a gross ignorance of the Elenchus, regarding that physical principle: The finite is not capable of the Infinite: For this, first of all, is deficient and false in our Theology and in matters of faith. Mary, certainly the virgin Mother of the Lord, in her womb, which was certainly finite, carried the infinite Son of GOD himself: thus the λόγος, who is infinite, was made flesh, which is certainly finite: Thus the Human Nature of Christ, which is certainly finite and does not have its own personality, has subsistence in the infinite ὑπόστασις of the λόγος. Either, therefore, this physical axiom must be utterly banished from our Theology regarding this Article: Or it will follow that not only the real communication of Idioms, but also the very real union of the two Natures, of which one is finite and the other is infinite, must be simply denied. Furthermore, even if some place is granted to this physical axiom to the greatest extent, it nevertheless does not militate against our doctrine: since it is true according to one thing, but false according to another. It is true when the Finite is considered from the property of its own Nature, where certainly there is no proportion of the Finite to the Finite. And indeed in this respect both the Union of Natures and the κοινωνία of Idioms are most rightly denied. But this axiom is false with respect to the singular, nay, supernatural action of GOD, where every Logical and Physical Reason collapses and expires: as in this place, where beyond the series of things GOD was made man, and anointed the assumed flesh with the infinite fullness of His divinity.

Finally, this argument suffers from a faulty opposition, as it is not in an equal, but in a most diverse degree and respect. For Human Nature is called finite by reason of magnitude and bodily bulk: But the fullness of the Divinity is and is called infinite, not by reason of magnitude or corporeal quantity, which it has none of, but by reason of power and virtue. Wherefore from this faulty opposition arises a non-sequitur of four terms. If the adversaries should object that in both members of the opposition they understand divine power, but not corporeal mass, let them remember that the Apostles, however much they were capable of only finite power in themselves, were nevertheless endowed with divine virtue and power: so that even by this one objection given, this exception collapses.

As for the saying of Solomon, it is most true: but it does nothing to infringe upon the communication of the divine Majesty, which has been made to the Flesh of Christ. For the reason for the diversity is easily detected. For just as the heaven of heavens cannot contain or comprehend GOD, because they do not constitute one hypostasis with Him: So the Human nature of Christ does contain GOD the Logos, and his entire fullness: Because it constitutes one hypostasis with the Logos, and has been rendered a sharer of the divine Nature, and consequently of the fullness of the Divinity itself to the Logos.

Latin:

III. ARGUMENTUM Κατασκευασικὸν ab inhabitatione totius plenitudinis Divinitatis in CHRISTO, petitum.

SEcundum quam Naturam, universa plenitudo Divinitatis in Christo verè ac realiter inhabitat: Secundum eandem etiam, infinita Majestatis divinæ verè ac realiter CHRISTUS κοινωνὸς factus sit, necesse est. Atqui in Christo secundum assumtam Humanam Naturam, inhabitat omnis plenitudo Deitatis. Ergò secundum eandem assumtam Humanam Naturam Christus infinitæ Majestatis divinæ, verè ac realiter factus sit κοινωνὸς, necesse est.

Majoris connexum partim per se satis evidenter patet: partim ex Confirmatione Minoris, in qua latet τὸ κενολ́μενον, fusius patebit.

Minorem autem confirmat Classicus ille Aphorismus Coloss. 2, 9. In Christo inhabitat omnis plenitudo Deitatis σωματικῶς, corporaliter. Qui sanè Aphorismus, quò illustrior est, tantò fœdior est quorundam Sophisticatio, quâ ejus claritatem obfuscare student. Sunt enim qui contendunt, Apostolum hoc duntaxat innuere: Christum esse plenum & perfectum DEUM. Sed crassa planè hæc est Elenchi ignoratio: Etsi enim per consequentiam haud ineptè divinitatis Christi ex hoc Aphorismo colligi & confirmari potest: haud tamen eò directè respexit Apostolus, sed id potiùs notatum voluit, Inhabitationem hanc Divinitatis universæ, respectu carnis Christi intelligendam esse, ut mox firmis rationibus demonstratur.

Sunt deindè, inter quos etiam Author noster est, qui hunc reddunt sensum Aphorismti Apostolici: In Christo inhabitat omnis plenitudo Deitatis corporaliter: id est: In aliis Sanctis habitat DEUS Spiritu suo, novam lucem, & novos motus accendens: Sed inChristo habitat non solùm Spiritu; sed etiam, ut personali Unione humana natura Divinæ unita sit. Nam inferente Pezelio, σωματικῶς ex usu lingvæ Græcæ, idem sonat ac ὑποσατικῶς personaliter, quia σῶμα Græcis etiam personam significat: ut cùm belli Peloponesiaci scriptor, ait: Urbem Atheniensium creviffe σώμασι καὶ χρήμασι id est, personis civium & opibus: Et cùm Tertullianus quærit, an λόγος sit σῶμα: id est, Persona? Respondeo: Philippi quidem sententiam per se non esse erroneam, suoque loco longè verissimam: sed præsenti Aphorismo Apostolico minimè convenire, quippè qui Effectum magis Unionis personalis, quàm Unionem ipsam describit: id quòd paulò post evidentissimè demonstrabitur.

Quoad Pezelium, nugatur ille veriùs, quàm disputat. Esto enim apud Scriptores prophanos, interdum σῶμα significet personam: tamen συνεκδοχικῶς istud fieri, respectu nimirùm corporis, nemo sanus negaverit. Quare si vel maximè hic sensus ad Aphorismum Apostolicum accommodetur: certè non personam λόγου in se, & per se consideratam: sed ipsam naturã assumtam, nempè carnem Christi, Inhabitationis hujus subjectum, constitui, fuerit consequens. Quemadmodum enim Cives Attici dicebantur σώματα, non alio respectu, quàm quatenus constabant ex corporibus, quibus etiam crescebant: ita etiam hoc loco σωματικῶς, apud Apostolum non potest respectum habere ad ὑπόστασιν τοῦ λόγου, quæ nihil corporei in se habet: sed tantùm ad assumtam carnem, sive corpus: cujus respectu Adverbium hoc σωματικῶς locum habere potest. Quoad Tertulliani Quæstionem, ipsemet ita eam explicat: ut satis constet ipsum impropriè & ὁμωνύμως vocabulum σώματος usurpasse.

Sed missis impietatibus istis, ad accuratiorem Aphorismis Apostolici explicationem accessum facimus. Initiò autem sub considerationem venit vox HABITANDI: quæ inhabitantem ab inhabitato luculenter distingvit: Ita ut omni plenitudini Divinitatis, Inhabitationis actum disertè adscribat. Quo sic præsupposito, planissimum evadit, sensum verborum Apostoli non posse dari istum: Quasi omnis plenitudo Divinitatis, vel in persona λόγου in se consideratâ, vel in Christo secundum Divinam Naturam habitet. Nam persona λόγου, & ejusdem Divinitas reipsâ minimè differunt: Sic Deitas & plenitudo Deitatis, sunt quiddam simplicissimum ταυτὸ, ac proindè Unum in altero inhabitare, non nisi per prodigiosam absurditatem dici potest. Relinquitur Ergò, aliud Habitaculum omnis plenitudinis Deitatis constituendum esse: nempè CARNEM CHRISTI assumtam, in quâ tanquam in proprio suo Templo, omnis plenitudo Divinitatis τοῦ λόγου inhabitat. Deindè notationem meretur Adverbium σωματικῶς corporaliter, quod magnam emphasin habet. Quia enim neque Deitas, neque plenitudo Divinitatis, neque Persona τοῦ λόγου, quâ simpliciter λόγος est, est quiddam σωματικὸν: utique adverbium etiam istud nihil istorum omnium notat aut definit. Deindè, quia Modus Unionis, sive inhabitationis τοῦ λόγου in assumta Natura humana, non est σωματικὸς corporalis. Neque enim Natura Humana assumsit λόγον: sed persona λόγου assumsit carnem. Quare Unionis etiam hujus modus, tùm à persona assumente, tùm à Termino, intra Quem Humanitas est assumta, PERSONALIS dicitur. Relinquitur Ergò Adverbium σωματικῶς, notare subjectum, in quo inhabitet omnis plenitudo Divinitatis: nempè carnem sive Naturam humanam Christi, quæ λόγον Totum, citra ullam ipsius coarctationem aut amissionem Infinitatis, habet & possidet. Et ut Irenæus loquitur lib. 3. cap. 18. capit & comprehendit: non quasi Divinitas, tanquam in vase concludatur, sed per περιχώρησιν, & indivulsam prorsusque inseparabilem, in assumta natura immanentiam.

Confirmat hanc interpretationem nostram universa Antiquitas Orthodoxa: ut Cyrillus lib. 2. ad Reginas: In quo inhabitavit omnis plenitudo Deitatis corporaliter? propriè quidem & seorsim in Naturâ verbi putare hoc esse factum, valdè stultum foret. Nam perindè esset, ac si diceres, Quod ipse Unigenitus habitavit in seipso.

Idem lib. 12. Thefauri cap. 15. Corpus Christi Templum est verè: In ipso enim voluit habitare corporaliter tota plenitudo Deitatis.

Athanaf. de fuscepta Natura hum. contra Apollin. Cùm dicit Apostolus: Quòd in Christo habitet omnis plenitudo Deitatis corporaliter: plenitudinem illam IN CARNE habitare intelligendum est.

Quibus ita constitutis, Argumenti hujus nostri consecutio irrefragabiliter infert, Humana Naturæ Christi verissimè ac realissimè communicatam esse omnem plenitudinem Divinitatis λόγꙋ: ac proindè ipsam quoque Omnipotentiam: id quod erat demonstrandum.

Sed insurgit hoc loco magno conatu Gens Calviniana & Jesuitica: nostramque hanc assertionem multis tùm argumentis, tùm absurditatibus obruere & evertere studet: sed initiò prorsus conatu, uti ex eorum argumentorum Refutatione patebit, in quibus arcem victoriæ collocare solent.

PRIMUM tale est: Finitum non est capax Infiniti: adeò ut Salomon etiam affirmat 2 Paral. 6, 18. cælos cælorum non capere Dominum. Ergò neq; Finita Natura Humana, est capax infinitæ omnipotentiæ, sive omnis plenitudinis Divinitatis τꙋ λόγꙋ: idq́; tantò minus, quantò minor ea est, & angustior hac rerum universitate.

Respondeo. 1. Committi tùm μετάβασιν εἰς ἄλλο γένος, tùm crassam Ignorationem Elenchi, Quoad principium illud physicum: Finitum non est capax Infiniti: Hoc enim primùm in Theologia nostra & rebus fidei deficit & falsum est. Maria certè virgo Mater Domini, in utero suo certè Finito, gestavit ipsum infinitum Filium DEI: sic λόγος qui est infinitus, factus est caro, quæ certè finita est: Sic Humana Christi Natura, quæ certè finita est, & propriam personalitatem non habet: subsistentiam habet in infinita ὑποστάσει τꙋ λόγꙋ. Aut ergo axioma hoc physicum ex Theologia nostra, quoad Articulum istum penitùs erit religandum: Aut consequens fuerit, non realem tantùm communicationem Idiomatum: sed ipsam quoque realem duarum Naturarum, quarum una finita est, altera infinita est, unionem simpliciter negandam esse. Deindè si vel maximè locus aliquis axiomati isti physico concedatur: tamen adversus doctrinam nostram non militat: Siquidem secundum aliud verum quidem illud est: secundũ aliud verò falsum. Verum est tùm, quando Finitum consideratur ex Naturæ suæ proprietate: ubi certè Finiti ad Finitum nulla est proportio. Et sanè hoc respectu & Naturarum Unio & Idiomatum κοινωνία rectissimè negatur. Falsum verò est axioma hoc, respectu singularis imò supernaturalis actionis DEI: ubi Ratio omnis Logica & Physica concidit & expirat: ut hoc loco: ubi præter rerum seriem DEUS homo factus est, & assumtam carnem infinitâ divinitatis suæ plenitudine inunxit.

Tandem hoc argumentum vitiosâ laborat oppositione: ut quæ sit, non in pari: sed diversissimo gradu & respectu. Humana enim Natura finita dicitur ratione magnitudinis & molis corporeæ: Plenitudo verò Divinitatis est & dicitur Infinita, non ratione magnitudinis : sive quantitatis corporeæ, quam nullam habet : sed ratione potentiæ & virtutis. Quare ex hac vitiosa oppositione oritur ἀσυλλογισία quatuor terminorum. Sin exceperint Adversarii, se in utroque oppositionis membro intelligere divinam potentiam : non verò molem corpoream, meminerint Apostolos, quantumvis ex se finitæ tantùm potentiæ capaces, divina tamen virtute & potentiâ fuisse præditos: ut vel una hac data ἐνςάσει, exceptio isthæc corruat.

Quoad dictum Salomonis, verissimum illud est: sed nihil facit ad infringendam communicationem Majestatis divinę, quæ facta est Carni Christi. Ratio enim diversitatis facilè deprehenditur. Quemadmodum enim cœli cœlorum ideò DEUM capere aut comprehendere non possunt, quia cum eo non constituunt unum ὑφιςάμενον : Ita Humana Christi natura ideò DEUM λόγον, & universam plenitudinem ejus capit : Quia unam cum λόγῳ ὑπόςασιν constituit, & consors reddita est Naturæ divinæ, & consequenter ipsius etiam plenitudinis Divinitatis τῶ λόγῳ.


### Chapter III. on the Effect of the Hypostatic Union of the two Natures in Christ: III. Constructive Argument derived from the indwelling of the whole fullness of the Godhead in Christ (continued)

The other argument is such: If the Human nature of Christ truly and really possesses the whole fullness of the Deity; it is necessary that it be deified, and made equal to the divine Nature.

But the former of those is true according to the opinion of the Ubiquitarians.

Therefore it is necessary that they also concede this latter.

They prove the connection of the major premise thus: Essential properties are not separated in the most simple Essence of Jehovah: otherwise the Essence of Jehovah would be divided into many diverse parts. Therefore to be omnipotent, to be omniscient, or to have the whole fullness of the Divinity, is the same as to be GOD essentially.

I ANSWER. A sophism is committed by taking what is said in a certain respect as if it were said absolutely. For the major proposition proceeds from a hypothesis which is not true absolutely, but only in a certain respect. And it is such: Whatever has or possesses the whole fullness of the Deity; that is deified, or is God.

This hypothesis is true only of him who, by the property of his own Nature, so possesses the whole fullness of the Divinity that he is essentially omnipotent, omniscient, etc., or that he is naturally Omnipotence, Omniscience, etc., itself. But it is false of him who is not the very fullness of the Deity by Essence, nor is naturally Omnipotence, Omniscience, etc., itself. But only by virtue and Union with another Nature participates in Omnipotence. The reason for the affirmation is: Because to be GOD, and to have omnipotence not from oneself by Essence, but through another, by participation and thanks, exclude each other. Now therefore, because according to our doctrine, the Human Nature of Christ is not the fullness of the Deity from itself, nor by essence: but through another, in respect of the Union, and has been rendered a sharer or participant of this fullness of the Divinity by a certain participation in time: it is manifest that that fabrication of the equalization of Natures, or of Definition, cannot justly be imputed to us.

Nor does the confirmation of the major proposition in this place militate in any part. For the question is not whether Essential properties are separated in the most simple Essence of the Divinity? that is, whether they can be separated, and whether they differ essentially and by subjects: Which we ourselves also constantly deny: But this is the question, whether the properties of the divinity can be truly, yet in their own way, communicated to the Humanity, in the Person of the Son of GOD, without its abolition or the equalization of the natures? To which we answer affirmatively, relying on those foundations which we have taken from the scriptures above. But the adversaries answer negatively. Which negation of theirs, however, necessarily involves the denial of the very union of the two Natures. For how, I ask, could he believe in the true communion of the natures themselves, who denies that what is less than the natures themselves can be communicated. And that we may press the adversaries more strongly, let them explain to us, is it not of infinite and immense, nay truly divine virtue, to recall men from the dead to life, to cast out demons with authority, to banish any diseases whatsoever even by a word? They will undoubtedly answer affirmatively, and rightly so. Now indeed, the communication of those virtues could occur, and indeed did occur, without any separation or division of Essential properties in the most simple divine Essence, to the Patriarchs, Prophets, and Apostles: to whom, however, the Divinity was not united hypostatically, but was only present by a gracious presence. What a stupendous absurdity this would be, therefore, to exclude the humanity of Christ, to whom the Holy Spirit was not given by measure, and in whom all the fullness of the Divinity dwells bodily, from a true and real communion of divine virtue and omnipotence, which nevertheless constitutes one hypostasis with the Logos: that which never happened, nor will happen, to any of the Saints.

The adversaries object; and they bring forward that saying of Damascenus, τὰ παρὰ φύσιν sunt Φθαρτικὰ τῶν κατὰ φύσιν: that is, those things which are contrary to nature are destructive of those things which are according to nature.

Therefore, if those supernatural and divine things are really communicated to the humanity: they will certainly be destructive of the nature itself: and consequently, if the communication of divine Majesty and Omnipotence is granted, it is necessary that the abolition of human nature be likewise granted.

I answer. The argument fails by the fallacy of Ignoratio Elenchi. For it is not those things which are above human nature: but those which are contrary to nature, and which cannot exist together in the same natural subject without its corruption, that destroy human nature:

Such are the ἀντιφυσικὰ (anti-natural) and παρὰ φύσιν (contrary to nature) things in Damascene: such as disease and health: light and darkness: life and death. But the condition of those infinite gifts, proper to the divine Majesty, which accrued to the human nature of Christ by the grace of the Union, is far other and different. For these are not παρὰ φύσιν, as Damascene speaks, or ἀντιφυσικά: but ὑπὲρ φύσιν (above nature), not destroying nature, but perfecting it. Certainly in a hyperphysical and plainly miraculous way the sun stood still, iron floated, fire did not burn, the barren conceived, a virgin gave birth: yet no abolition of the subject followed. How then could the exaltation of the human nature abolish or destroy the same, even though it may seem to surpass the accustomed order of nature and the condition of the human lot. For as Augustine rightly says somewhere: When Christ gave glory to his flesh, he did not take away its nature: And as Gerson adds: Glory does not take away humanity, but extols it: it does not kill, but perfects.

Then this objection would have a place if we were to posit that the divine idioms, or the whole fullness of the Divinity, had been poured into the human nature in such a way that it now inheres in it subjectively. By which arrangement, indeed, the abolition of the human nature would necessarily follow. But since that former point does not follow from our doctrine, it is evident that the latter cannot be elicited from it.

THE THIRD argument, by which the adversaries attack the communication of the whole fullness of the Divinity to the humanity of Christ, is this:

If the entire fullness of the Divinity has been communicated to the humanity of Christ: and for that reason it can be called omnipotent, omniscient, adorable, etc.: then for the same reason it will also be able to be called eternal, uncreated, spiritual. But this latter is absurd. Therefore, so is the former.

They prove the connection of the major premise from this: Because the divine idioms are one thing most simply, and cannot be distracted in any way: so that with one idiom communicated, another is necessarily communicated as well.

I answer 1. Generally, that we hold as the firmest anchor of faith that not certain divine properties of the Word were communicated to the humanity of Christ, and certain others not: but the whole fullness of the Divinity: as the Apostle speaks. For since the human nature of Christ has arrived at the κοινωνίαν ὑποστάσεως (communion of the hypostasis) of the Word: why should it not also have arrived at the κοινωνίαν of the whole Divinity of the Word, and thus at a most real communion of each and all of its idioms? Indeed, the hypostasis and the Divinity of the Word do not really differ, nor do their idioms. Then, however, regarding the connection of the major premise, I answer that it fails by the fallacy of the consequent.

Then, however, specifically, regarding the argument itself. For the reasoning of the consequence does not hold: The idioms of the Divinity are a most simple thing, the same. Therefore, if because of their real communion it is right to say: Human nature is omnipotent: then it will also be permitted to say: Human nature is eternal, spiritual, uncreated, etc. For a very evident reason for the diversity can be given. For although the divine idioms within the most simple essence of the Deity are one thing most simply, without any distraction: yet when they are weighed in operation toward the outside, either by consideration of another nature in the Union, or in respect of other creatures outside the Union: then indeed those very divine idioms, however much they are essentially one thing, obtain a certain distinction: nor do they admit an equal mode or reason of predication or enunciation in all things. For example: The eternity and omnipotence of God within the divine essence are a most simple thing, the same: meanwhile, however, it is not permitted to say: God created the world by his eternity: but by his omnipotence. Thus the mercy and justice of God within the essence of the Divinity are a most simple thing, the same: but yet they obtain a disparate reason of predication toward the outside: so that it is said that not the justice, but the mercy of God saves us: and that not the mercy, but the justice of God damns the impious.
