For it is true only secundum quid that where there is satisfaction for a debt, there a gratuitous remission of the debt cannot have a place: if, indeed, you consider the person of the debtor himself, who certainly, if he pays and satisfies for the debt, cannot be said to have received a remission of the debt. But if you look at the person of the creditor, then both can stand together. For when a debtor is reduced to extreme poverty and cannot pay even a farthing, and indeed the debt is satisfied and paid to the creditor by a surety, then certainly both satisfaction and remission of the debt can stand together: satisfaction with respect to the surety who pays the debt for the poor man; remission, however, with respect to the poor man himself, insofar as he is now fully liberated from the obligation of providing satisfaction for the debt. The Apostle describes a similar process as having been observed regarding our reconciliation: These things, he says, are from God, who reconciled us to HIMSELF through JESUS CHRIST: namely, because God was in Christ, reconciling the world to HIMSELF, not imputing their sins to them: For he made him, who knew no sin, to be sin for us, that we might be made the righteousness of God in him. 2 Cor. 5:18, 19, 21. Thus, therefore, the remission of sins, which comes to us, is satisfactory and merely gratuitous, without any contradiction. Satisfactory, insofar as God reconciled the world to HIMSELF through the Son; but merely gratuitous, insofar as this very reconciliation, provided through the Son, comes to us freely without any merit of our own.

Latin:

Misericordiam Dei esse Causam προηγουμένην Antecedentem, imo impulsivam Justificationis nostræ: clarius est, quam ut ulla probatione indigeat. Confirmant enim hoc evidentissimè Scripturarum testimonia. Eph. 2, 8. Gratia salvati estis. 2. Timoth. 1, 9. Salvos nos fecit secundum propositum suum, & Gratiam, quæ data est nobis in CHRISTO JESU. Tit. 3, 7. Justificati gratia ipsius, hæredes vitæ æternæ efficimur. Statuit autem purior Dei Ecclesia, Misericordiam hanc Dei, non esse absolutam: sed in CHRISTO, ejusdemque merito & satis factione unicè fundatam. Cujus fidei nostræ præcipua fundamenta sunt hæc.

I. Deus non modò fummè est misericors: sed & fummè justus, id quod Valentinus Schmalzius, se & complices ultrò largiri fatetur: licet neutram Deo naturalem esse, postmodùm contendat: Atqui Justitia hæc Dei exigebat ab universo genere humano eas pœnas, quas Deus ipse in Paradiso, primis parentibus, si legem propositam transgrederentur, denunciaverat. Mortem nimirum sive condemnationem æternam: ut infra Controversia tertia ex professo, invictis argumentis adstruemus. Ergo Misericordiæ Dei locus haud esse potuit, priusquàm Justitiæ divinæ esset satisfactum: id quod, si per Christum Mediatorem ejusdemq; meritum, nondum sufficienter est expeditum: Ostendant vel tandem hæretici, ecquis illud vel expedierit, vel aliquando expediturus sit? id quod tamen in æternum ostendere non possunt. Manet proinde ratum, firmum & fixum, Misericordiam hanc Dei locum habere non potuisse, nisi respectu, sive intuitu satisfactionis Christi. Et profectò tanta est vis argumenti hujus, ut, cùm Photiniani non inveniant, quod ad illud infringendum solidè proferre possint, duo isthæc, ne fando quidem prius audita, imò ipso externo tantùm sono horrenda παραλογήματα excogitarint. 1. Deum nunquàm iratum fuisse peccato. 2. In Deo nullam esse justitiam vindicatricem, sive punientem peccata, de quibus altera Controversia ex professo disquisitionem instituet.

II. Fundamentum monstrat ipsa Scriptura, quæ Misericordiam Dei, in describendo actu Justificationis nostræ, fermè semper expressè conjungit cum Redemtione & Satisfactione Christi, & quidem tali Satisfactione, quæ non in monstrandâ viâ salutis tantùm, uti Photiniani grunniunt: Sed in effusione Sanguinis & acquisitione salutis consistat. Ubi primarium fermè locum obtinet illud, quod Apostolus affirmat Rom. 3, 24. & 25. Deum proposuisse Christum propitiatorium in SANGUINE suo; Verba ipsa Apostoli valdè emphatica, sic habent: Justificati gratis, gratiâ ipsius, per Redemptionem factam in JESU CHRISTO, quem proposuit Deus propitiatorium per fidem, in sanguine ipsius, ad demonstrandam IUSTITIAM suam, per Remissionem peccatorum. Qui certè unicus Aphorismus Apostolicus ceu fulmine quodam Hæreticorum istorum blasphemiam prosternit.

Nam 1. docet, nos justificari gratis Gratiâ Dei, ubi omne nostrum meritum, & sic pænitentia quoq́; ratione Contritionis & Novæ obedientiæ excluditur 2. Ostendit hanc ipsam Gratiam Dei, non esse absolutam: sed fundatam in Redemptione, quæ facta est in Christo. 3. demonstrat, Redemtionem hanc factam sive expeditam esse, per effusionem sanguinis Christi. 4. Finem explicat, propter quem hæc Redemtio per effusum sanguinem expedita sit, & finem quidem geminum: Unum respectu Dei, ut sic demonstraret suam misericordiam, & quidem Justitiæ temperamento constantem: dùm nimirùm Filio suo unigenito non pepercit: sed tradidit ipsum pro nobis: Alterum respectu nostri, ut nimirùm per hanc Redemtionem Christi nobis obtingeret Remissio peccatorum.

Puriori huic doctrinæ blasphemo planè ore & calamo se opponunt recentiores Photiniani, contendentes, Misericordiam Dei ratione Effectûs sive Iustificationis nostræ esse simpliciter absolutam: neq́; ullo pacto esse fundatam in merito, λύτρῳ sive Satisfactione Christi.

Verba Fausti Socini sic sonant part. 3. de Christo p. 230. cap. 1. Nihil ferè magis impium excogitari potest, quàm sentire, à Deo peccata non remitti, nisi pro ipsis illi planè satisfiat.

Et paulo post: Iustus in sacris literis is intelligitur, qui purè aut innocenter vixerit: non autem, qui pro suis peccatis Deo à Christo aut aliquando satisfactum iri, aut jam satisfactum fuisse crediderit.

Et pag. 235. Nisi velimus, Deum eo tempore, quod in divinis literis gratia & benignitatis appellatur, restrictiorem fuisse, quàm eo, quod præ illo severitatis atq́; iræ appellari potest: concludendum prorsus videtur, in salute nobis, divinâ providentiâ per ChriSTVM parta, nullam veram pro delictis nostris Satisfactionem a quoquam accipere Deum voluisse : sed liberalissime ea universa pœnitentibus nobis ac resipiscentibus condonasse.

I. Deus miseretur quorum vult. Rom. 9, 15. & 18. Exod. 33, 20. Ergo remittit peccata, mera voluntate sua misericordia, sine ullo intuitu alicujus Satisfactionis per Christum præstitæ.

Et pag. 236. Si modò pœnitentia adsit, Deum pro ingenti bonitate sua, nulla vera Satisfactione accepta, nobis peccata remittere voluisse, in novo fœdere, quod nobiscum per Christum percutere dignatus est, constanter affirmo, & nunc potissimum contendo. Quomodo enim propitius fuisset Deus iniquitatibus nostris, si cùm eas nobis, nulla Satisfactione interveniente, remittere posset, pro ipsis sibi plenissimè satisfieri curasset? aut quomodo peccatorum nostrorum non recordatus fuisset, si ab humana natura in Christo, ipsorum omnium tam rigidè & exactè pœnas repetijsset? Vel potiùs quid mirum est, eum iniquitates nostras nobis non imputare, & peccatorum nostrorum non ampliùs recordari, si jam ei uberrimè satisfactum pro sceleribus nostris fuit, & jam eorum ita recordatus est, ut ne minimum quidem impunitum reliquerit? Quænam hæc est ipsius, quam tantopere prædicat, munificentia ac liberalitas, si de jure suo ne tantillum quidem remittere voluit?

Respondeo committi Sophisticationem παρὰ τὴν ἄγνοιαν ἐλέγχꙋ. Opponuntur enim voluntas Dei misericors, & Satisfactio Christi, tanquàm Contradictoria, quæ tamen sunt Subordinata. Valeat proindè & hîc Logicorum regula: Subordinata non pugnant, neque se mutuò excludunt. Jam verò habere se hæc duo ut Subordinata, vel ea evincunt Scripturæ testimonia, quibus paulò ante evicimus, Gratiam Remissionis peccatorum, fundatam esse in sanguine, sive Satisfactione Christi. Deinde voluntas in Deo Præsupponit quidem libertatem : siquidem voluntas planè non est, quæ Libera non est: sed non excludit Determinatinem voluntatis. Est enim ea quoque voluntas, quæ secundum certum ordinem liberè agit: ut quando Deus vult omnium hominum salutem: sed secundum ordinem à se sancitum, ut nimirùm omnes etiam credant in Christum : sic vult ipso actu Remittere peccata omnibus, sed credentibus, hoc est, Satisfactionem Christi sibi firmâ fide applicantibus : ubi semper Deus liberè agit quidem, sed non absolutè. Sudat in refutatione hujus argumenti Paræus, & quia videt laqueos hîc occultari, quibus à Photinianis absolutum prædestinationis Decretum Calvinisticum, sub ejusdem impietatis reatum constringi possit, σοφὸν excogitavit φάρμακον, distinguens inter geminam Dei misericordiam circà Remissionem peccatorum & salutem nostram : Unam Antecedentem, quæ sit absoluta, & constituat Electionem : Alteram Consequentem, quæ habeat respectum ad meritum Christi, fidem & pœnitentiam. Cui perversitati opponimus cum Scriptura immotum hoc axioma : quod in Deo ab omni æternitate, nulla unquàm fuerit vel voluntas vel misericordia respectu hominum absoluta, quâ sine intuitu mediorum salutis, Electionis decretum fecerit ullum absolutum. Sed hac de re alibi.

Cæterùm priusquàm Rationes hæreticorum istorum examinemus, probè dispiciendum fuerit: Quidnam propriè in Quæstionem sive Controversiam veniat? Initiò igitur non hoc quæritur: An in Deo sit absoluta aliqua bonitas & Misericordia, quæ neg, in merito Christi, neq, in ulla satisfactione sit fundata? Nam nos ipsi quoq; Affirmativam tenemus. Absolutæ enim voluntatis, bonitatis & Misericordiæ divinæ est, quòd Mundum hunc visibilem, quòd animalia, quòd Hominem Rationalem creavit : quòd genus humanum hodiéque propagat & conservat : quodque id genus alia misericordiæ suæ opera exercet, quæ à Satisfactione Christi minimè dependent.

Deindè neque illud contròvertitur: An Misericordia Dei, quatenùs ea intelligitur, de divino illo amoris affectu, quo erga genus humanum paterne affectus est; ratione principij sui, sit absoluta, an verò in alio quopiam fundata? Nam & hîc respondemus, Misericordiam hoc modo, nempè respectu Essentialis principij sui haud minus esse absolutam, atque ipse Deus est Ens quoddam absolutissimum atque purissimum.

II. Jes. 43, 25. Ego, ego sum inquit Dominus, qui deleo iniquitates tuas propter me, & peccatorum tuorum non recordabor: Ergo absolutè propter seipsum, & non propter Christi Satisfactionem aliquam, Deus nobis remittit peccata.

Verùm hoc in Controversiam venit : Num Misericordia Dei, quatenùs illa non ampliùs intra absolutissimum Essentiæ divinæ complexum manet, sed actu quasi secundo foràs ad lapsum genus humanum progreditur, & pœnas peccatis nostris justo Dei judicio debitas, remittit sine ullo intuitu Justitiæ divinæ, & sic sine ulla Satisfactione, justitiæ divinæ præstitâ, miserationis hujus suæ actus & Effectus exserat? Circa quam Quæstionem nos Negativam tenemus, ijs moti rationibus, quæ paulò antè expedivimus. Photiniani verò Affirmativam propugnare student : his potissimùm freti argumentis.

Respondeo: rursus committi ἔλεγχον vitiosè oppositorum: Fingunt enim hæretici, Deum ipsum & Satisfactionem Christi se mutuò tollere: cùm tamen ratione Subordinationis rectissimè conveniant. Cum enim dicit Jehovah : Ego deleo iniquitates tuas propter meipsum, nihil aliud innuit, quàm se delere peccata, non propter nos, aut nostram pœnitentiam : sed propter se, hoc est, propter ipsissimam hanc Satisfactionem suam. Christus enim est ille ipse Jehovah, qui Sanguine suo delet chirographum, quod adversum nos erat, & emundat nos ab omni peccato Coloss. 2, 14. 1. Joh. 1, 7.

HI. Si Deus non remitteret peccata absolutè: sed propter præcedentem satis factionem Christi: tùm frustra planè Misericordia & bonitas Dei in Scripturis prædicaretur. Nam ubi Satisfactio pro debito,ibi non gratuita remissio: Atqui hoc posterius est absurdum: Ergo & prius illud.

Respondeo committi Sophisma vitiosi Consequentis. Nam non ideò frustra in Scripturis prædicatur Misericordiâ Dei, quia ea fundata est in satisfactione Christi: sed vel indè potiùs clariùs ea elucescat. Nam hæc ipsa Satisfactio Christi est Effectus misericordiæ divinæ verè gratuitus. Nam teste Apostolo Rom. 5, 8. & 10. in eo vel maximè Deus commendat charitatem suam, quòd cùm nos inimici essemus, & ex nostra parte omnis deficeret Satisfactio, ipse non modò nostri misertus est, & de recipiendis nobis in gratiam paternè cogitavit: sed & ut Justitiæ suæ, quæ ob peccatum æternas pœnas à nobis exigebat, satis fieret, ipse sibi ipsi satisfecit, tradito in mortem filio suo unigenito, qui loco ac vice nostri expiaret omnem offensionem. Quæ sanè stupenda miseratio Dei tanta est, ut in ea prædicandâ Spiritus Sanctus passim sit occupatissimus, præsertim Joh. 3, 16. Sic Deus dilexit mundum, ut Filium suum unigenitum daret, ut omnis, qui credit in ipsum, non pereat, sed habeat vitam æternam. Et Rom. 8, 32. Deus filio suo non pepercit, sed pro nobis tradidit eum.

Deindè probatio Majoris non simpliciter & absolutè vera est. Nam secundùm Quid tantùm verum est, quòd ubi est Satisfactio pro debito; ibi non gratuita Remissio debiti locum habere possit: si nimirùm personam consideres ipsius debitoris, qui certè, si exolvit & satisfecit pro debito, non dici potest accepisse remissionem debiti: Verùm si personam creditoris spectes, tùm utrumque simul stare potest: Quando enim debitor ad extremam paupertâtem redactus, ne teruntium quidem exolvere potest: & verò Creditori per fidejussorem satis fit & exolvitur debitum : tùm profectò & Satisfactio & Remissio debiti simul stare possunt: Satisfactio respectu fidejussoris qui exolvit debitum pro paupere: Remissio verò, respectu ipsius pauperis, quatenùs jam ipse à satisfactione pro debito præstandâ, plenè est liberatus. Parem processum describit Apostolus observatum fuisse circa nostri Reconciliationem: Hæc, inquiens, sunt ex Deo, qui reconciliavit nos SIBI, per JESUM CHRISTUM: nempè quia Deus erat in Christo, mundum reconcilians SIBI ipsi, non imputando eis peccata ipsorum: Fecit enim eum, qui non novit peccatum, pro nobis victimam pro peccato, ut nos efficeremur justitia Dei in eo 2. Cor. 5, 18. 19. 21. Sic ergò Remissio peccatorum, quæ nobis obtingit, est Satisfactoria & merè gratuita; sine ullâ Contradictione. Satisfactoria, quatenùs Deus sibi ipsi per Filium mundum reconciliavit: Merè verò gratuita, quatenùs hæc ipsa Reconciliatio per Filium præstita, nobis gratis sine ullo nostro merito obtingit.


### Subsequent Error of the more recent Photinians Concerning the Mercy of God in…: IV. If God were to remit sins on account of the satisfaction of Christ, it would follow that, in the salvation obtained for us through…

IV. If God were to remit sins on account of the satisfaction of Christ, it would follow that, in the salvation obtained for us through Christ, mercy and the justice opposed to it would have been joined together at the same time in the same subject. But this latter is absurd. Therefore, the former is as well. The assumption is proved: 1. because mercy and justice are opposites, which do not consist together in an excellent degree; 2. they require contrary subjects: mercy, a repenting man; justice, a non-repenting one; 3. they have contrary effects: mercy spares and saves; justice punishes and destroys. Therefore, they cannot be perfectly exercised at the same time in one and the same subject.

I answer that a fallacy is committed παρὰ τὸ πῆ καὶ ἁπλῶς. For the minor premise is true secundum quid, not ἁπλῶς. For then finally justice and mercy cannot consist in one and the same subject by reason of one and the same work: if, indeed, both are considered absolutely, and, as those heretics speak, in such an excellent degree that is plainly and simply absolute. In such a degree and absolute respect, God could not have had mercy on us; for his immutable justice stood in the way. Therefore, so that the mercy of God might rightly agree with his very justice, it was necessary that some temperament of divine justice and mercy should intervene, by reason of which the justice of God would urge its right, and at the same time mercy could also have a place. Such a temperament, and indeed a far more perfect one, can be seen in one and the same work of our salvation, by reason of one and the same subject, namely CHRIST the Savior. For he, being about to reconcile the world, and that not without a singular affection of mercy, saw that justice had first to be satisfied. Therefore, he derived the punishments due to our sins into himself; he was made sin for us; he truly bore our infirmities, and thus, having become obedient to God the Father even unto the death of the cross, he satisfied divine justice completely, and thus reconciled the world not only to God the Father, but also to HIMSELF (ἑαυτῷ). Insofar, therefore, as the mercy of God in the completion of the work of salvation is considered not absolutely, but determinately toward the λύτρον of CHRIST, to that extent, certainly, without any contradiction, justice and mercy can stand together. The matter can be illustrated by an example: Some Emperor, by a common decree of the Estates of the Empire, passes sentence on certain subjects for some crime of lese-majesty, committed both against himself and his Son, that they be confined in perpetual prison, and not be liberated from there until each of them pays the λύτρον of one hundred tons of gold. Here, certainly, the Emperor cannot set these captives free out of any absolute and simple mercy; for thus his justice would be violated. But if the Son of the Emperor intervenes, and, moved by mercy, pays that entire amount of gold for the captives, and thus satisfies for them to himself as well, then certainly both justice and mercy are perfectly exercised in one and the same subject: mercy, however, not absolute, but tempered by plenary satisfaction. V. GOD can have mercy and forgive sins, regarding Satisfaction, because He is a most free agent, and can remit as much of His own right as He wishes. Therefore.

I answer that a fallacy is committed παρὰ τὸ μὴ αἴτιον (ignoring the cause). For if according to the Scholastic rule: The consequence from possibility to actuality is not valid: then certainly no strength at all resides in the argument: GOD can do this or that. Therefore He does it. Furthermore, if we consult the scriptures, we more correctly and simply deny the Antecedent: For because GOD is not only a most free agent, but also a most just one: And indeed according to the rigor of His Justice, He adjudged the human race to eternal damnation, on account of sin: certainly, without prejudice to His justice, He could not forgive sins, unless the price of the penalties had first been sufficiently paid: as will be expressly shown in the second Controversy. Which impossibility, however, is not of any imperfection, but rather of the most absolute perfection, which consists in this, that in GOD there are no contrary wills. Now indeed, contrary wills would be granted in GOD entirely, if according to justice He simply willed sinners to be damned, and according to another will, He willed the same ones simply, and indeed without satisfaction of justice, to be exempt from that punishment. Therefore, they are peddling mere trifles, as often as these heretics blather about the absolute power of GOD.

VI. GOD wishes to forgive us our sins without any true Satisfaction being accepted for them: but only on account of repentance and innocence of life. The reason is: Because GOD, in those to whom He forgives sins, requires nothing more than Faith, which is contained in purity and innocence of life.

I answer that a fallacy is committed παρὰ τὴν ἄγνοιαν τοῦ ἐλέγχου (ignorance of the refutation). For the state of the Controversy is changed. For it is not being disputed in this place what GOD requires from those to whom He forgives sins, but what that thing is, on account of which GOD remits sins. Where a begging of the question is involved, when the heretics say: That which GOD requires from man, is that very thing on account of which GOD forgives sin. For New Obedience is required from the faithful, not as a cause of the remission of sins: but only as a Fruit and Effect of true faith. Furthermore, that justifying faith, by reason of its ὑπόστασις or substance, is to be defined by purity and innocence of life, is likewise manifestly false. For whether we consider the Apostolic definition of faith Heb. 11, 1. or other equivalent descriptions, by which Faith is said to be trust, ἔλεγχος, πληροφορία, πεποίθησις, etc.: it is manifest that Faith can no more be defined by innocence of life, than this very innocence of life enters into the act of Justification, as will be demonstrated against the Romanists. Finally, this argument overturns itself: For if sins are forgiven, ON ACCOUNT OF innocence of life. Therefore this will be a Cause either Satisfactory, or meriting the Remission of sins: and consequently, the mercy of GOD forgiving sins will not be absolute: but founded on some Satisfaction: which is what these heretics nevertheless deny.

VII. GOD forgave many people their sins not on account of faith in Christ, but on account of the faith by which they pleased GOD, believing namely, that GOD is and that He is a rewarder of those who do good, Hebr. 11, 6. Thus GOD everywhere in the Old and New Testament promises to men the forgiveness of sins, if indeed they repent. Therefore.

I answer: 1. by retorsion: If GOD forgives sins on account of any faith whatsoever, and on account of repentance: Therefore He does not forgive by His absolute mercy, as the heretics wish. For that which is determined or limited cannot be absolute. Furthermore, a gross ignorance of the refutation is committed: For faith is defined in the Scriptures in two ways: 1. By reason of the instrument, by which it is a firm trust believing that all sins are forgiven freely on account of the merit of Christ. 2. By reason of the various Objects, about which faith, as it were going forth internally, exercises itself. That various objects of this kind can be given here, none of us has ever denied: nor is this what is being asked: but that is being disputed: Whether Abel, Enoch and the remaining pious ones were justified by faith, insofar as it is considered in that former way ὀργανικῶς (organically) ever apprehending the merit of Christ: as we contend: Or whether insofar as it is viewed in the latter way: as the Photinians contend through a shameful begging of the question, which we simply deny. For the things they bring forward about Repentance are destitute of any true refutation: For this very thing is again in question: Whether the passages of Scripture, urging repentance as a condition of the remission of sins, are to be understood, I say, of such repentance as is outside of Christ, as the heretics again trifle through a begging of the question.

For although faith in Christ is not always explicitly and literally expressed: yet it is always implicitly understood. For just as the mercy of GOD is prepared for us in the blood of Christ: so Repentance without faith, applying to itself the merit of Christ, is mere hypocrisy in the sight of GOD: and so far from obtaining the Remission of sins: that it rather drives a man to desperation, as is evident from the example of Cain, Judas the traitor, and others.

VIII. He heaps together many little arguments, by which he attempts to show that the Satisfaction of Christ cannot stand with the mercy of GOD: but since we have hitherto abundantly demonstrated the contrary: and below the third Controversy is to treat this Question more fully, it does not pertain to deal with them more extensively in this place. It pleases, however, to include the whole matter in this place with certain observations.

I. The Satisfaction of Christ excludes the payment of debt with respect to us: for it is not required of us: But it does not exclude the compassion of GOD, which in this way satisfied itself. Therefore in one and the same work of the Remission of sins, the Mercy of GOD, and the Satisfaction of Christ can stand together. For it is of Mercy that He both satisfied for Himself, and on account of this Satisfaction freely remits sins to us, through faith in the Blood of Christ. Rom. 3, 24. & 25.

II. Satisfaction is contrary to Remission, if both are considered in one and the same Subject: It is not contrary, if in different ones: As in this place: Satisfaction is not required from those to whom sins are remitted: but the Satisfaction of another is given to them, and thus sins are pardoned: Which pardon is gratuitous with respect to us, insofar as we have not merited it: it is not gratuitous with respect to GOD, who views the Satisfaction of Christ in the place of merit.

III. The comparison which heretics frequently urge, concerning the remission of a debt or of money owed, does not apply. For one must distinguish between a pecuniary debt and natural law: The former can be remitted without Satisfaction. The latter cannot: because in that way the Justice of GOD would be endangered, indeed in that way GOD would not be or remain GOD.

IV. When in the Scriptures we are commanded to emulate the nature of GOD and to exercise mercy: the meaning is not that we ought to remit debts and every offense absolutely and simply without any Satisfaction: for thus all discipline among men would be abolished: but we are commanded only, partly to remit private injuries, and partly also not always to pursue the highest right ἀνεξικῶς: But this has nothing to do with the mercy and justice of GOD, which are occupied with neither private offenses nor ἀνεξοδικα,ον.

Latin:

IV. Si Deus remitteret peccata propter Satisfactionem Christi, sequeretur, in salute nobis per Christum parta, Misericordiam & huic oppositam Justitiam simul eodem tempore in eodem subjecto conjunctam fuisse. Atqui posterius hoc absurdum. E. & prius illud. Assumtio probatur. 1. quia Misericordia & Justitia sunt opposita, quæ simul non consistunt in gradu excellenti. 2. requirunt contraria subjecta: misericordia hominem resipiscentem: Justitia non resipiscentem. 3. habent contraria Effecta: misericordia parcit & servat: Justitia punit & perdit. Ergo non possunt simul in uno eodemque Subjecto, perfecte exerceri.

Respondeo, Sophisma committi παρὰ τὸ πῆ καὶ ἁπλῶς. Minor enim secundum Quid vera est, non ἁπλῶς. Tum demum enim Justitia & Misericordia uno eodemque Subjecto, ratione unius ejusdemque operis consistere non possunt: si nimirum utraque absolute consideretur, & ut hæretici isti loquuntur, in excellenti tali gradu, qui plane ac simpliciter sit absolutus. Tali profecto gradu atque respectu absoluto Deus nostri misereri non potuit: obstabat enim immutabilis ipsius justitia. Proinde ut misericordia Dei recte cum ipsa ejus justitia conveniret, necessum erat, ut interveniret temperamentum aliquod Justitiæ & misericordiæ divinæ: ratione cujus tum Justitia Dei suum jus urgeret, & simul misericordia etiam locum habere posset: Tale temperamentum & quidem longe perfectissimum cernere licet in uno eodemque salutis nostræ opere, ratione unius ejusdemque subjecti, nempe CHRISTI Servatoris. Hic enim mundum reconciliaturus, idque non sine singulari misericordiæ affectu, vidit Justitiæ prius satis faciendum esse: Ergo pœnas nostris peccatis debitas, ipse in se derivavit; ipse pro nobis factus peccatum; languores nostros vere tulit, & sic factus obediens Deo Patri ad mortem usque crucis, divinæ Justitiæ ex asse satis fecit, & sic non Deo Patri tantum, sed SIBIIPSI quoque ἑαυτῷ mundum reconciliavit. Quatenus ergo Misericordia Dei in opere salutis perficiendo non absolute, sed determinate ad λύτρον CHRISTI confideratur: eatenus certe sine ulla Contradictione, Justitia & misericordia simul stare possunt. Exemplo res illustrari potest: Imperator aliquis fert communi Ordinum Imperij decreto sententiam de subditis quibusdam ob aliquod crimen læsæ Majestatis, tum in se, tum in Filium admissum, perpetuo carcere concludendis, neque prius inde liberandis, quam quisque ipsorum λύτρον centum Tonnarum auri exolverit. Hic certe Imperator captivos istos non ex misericordia quapiam absoluta & simplici liberos præstare potest: sic enim violaretur Justitia ipsius. Sed si Filius Imperatoris interveniat, & misericordia motus, universam istam vim auri pro captivis exolvat, & sic sibi quoque pro istis satisfaciat: tum profecto & Justitia & Misericordia in uno eodemque Subjecto perfecte exercetur: Misericordia autem non absoluta, sed temperata satisfactione plenaria. V. DEUS potest misereri & condonare peccata, circa Satisfactionem, quia est agens liberrimum, & potest de suo jure remittere, quantum vult. E.

Respondeo committi Sophisma παρὰ τὸ μὴ αἴτιον. Nam si secundum regulam Scholasticam: A posse ad esse non valet Consequentia: utique nervus planè nullus militat in argumento: DEUS potest hoc vel illud facere. E. facit. Deindè si scripturas consulamus, rectiùs simpliciter negamus Antecedens: Quia enim DEUS non modò est agens liberrimum, sed & justissimum: Et verò secundùm rigorem Justitiæ suæ, æternæ maledictioni adjudicavit genus humanum, propter peccatum: utiq; salvâ justitiâ suâ, non potuit condonare peccata, nisi priùs pœnarum pretium sufficiens esset exolutum: uti Controversiâ secundâ ex professò ostendetur. Quæ tamen impossibilitas non est imperfectionis alicujus, sed potiùs absolutissimæ perfectionis, quæ in eo consistit, quòd in DEO non sunt contrariæ voluntates. Jam verò contrariæ voluntates in DEO omninò concederentur, si secundum justitiam vellet simpliciter peccatores damnatos, & secundum aliam voluntatem, vellet eosdem simpliciter, & quidem sine Satisfactione justitiæ à pœna illa exemptos. Proindè meras nugas venditant, quoties hæretici isti de absoluta DEI potentia blaterant.

VI. DEUS vult nobis peccata nostra condonare nullâ pro ipsis verâ Satisfactione acceptâ: sed tantùm propter resipiscentiam & innocentiam vitæ. Ratio est: Quia DEUS in ijs quibus condonat peccata, nihil ampliùs requirit, quàm Fidem, quæ puritate & innocentia vitæ continetur.

Respondeo committi Sophisma παρὰ τὴν ἄγνοιαν τὲ ἐλέγχο. Mutatur enim status Controversiæ. Neque enim quid DEUS requirat ab iis, quibus condonat peccata, sed quid sit illud, propter quod DEUS peccata remittit, hoc loco controvertitur. Ubi principii petitio involvitur, quando dicunt hæretici: Id, quod DEUS ab homine requirit, esse illud ipsum, propter quod Deus condonet peccatum. Requiritur enim Nova Obedientia à fidelibus, non ut causa remissionis peccatorum: sed tantùm ut Fructus & Effectus veræ fidei. Deindè Fidem justificantem ratione suæ ὑποσάσεως sive substantiæ definiendam esse puritate & innocentiæ vitæ, itidem manifestè falsum est. Nam sive definitionem fidei Apostolicam Heb. 11, 1. sive æquipollentes descriptiones alias consideremus, quibus Fides dicitur esse fiducia, ἔλεγχος, πληροφορία, πεποίθησις, &c: manifestum est, tàm non Fidem definiri posse per vitæ innocentiam, quàm non hæc ipsa vitæ innocentia, Justificationis actum ingreditur, uti contra Romanenses demostrabitur. Tandem semetipsum evertit hoc argumentum: Si enim condonantur peccata, PROPTER innocentiam vitæ. E. hæc erit Causa vel Satisfactoria, vel promerens Remissionem peccatorum: & per Consequens, misericordia DEI condonans peccata non erit absoluta: sed fundata in aliqua Satisfactione: id quod tamen negant hæretici isti.

VII. DEUS multis condonavit peccata non propter fidem in Christum, sed propter fidem quâ placuerunt DEO, credentes nimirùm, DEUM esse & efse remuneratorem bonorum, Hebr. 11, 6. Sic DEUS passim in Veteri & Novo Testamento promittit hominibus peccatorum veniam, si videlicet resipiscant. Ergò.

Respondeo: 1. per retorsionem: Si DEUS propter fidem quamcunque, & propter pœnitentiam condonat peccata: Ergo non absolutâ suâ misericordiâ condonat, uti volunt hæretici. Nam absolutum esse non potest, quòd est determinatum sive limitatum. Deindè committitur crassa ignoratio Elenchi: Fides enim duobus modis in Scripturis definitur: 1. Ratione instrumenti, quâ firma est fiducia credens propter meritum Christi condonari gratis omnia peccata. 2. Ratione variorum Objectorum, circa quæ fides interna forâs quasi egrediens, se exercet. Hic varia hujusmodi objecta dari posse, nemo nostrûm unquàm negavit: neque etiam hoc quæritur: sed illud controvertitur: An fide justificati sint Abel, Henoch & reliqui pij, quatenùs illa priore modo ὀργανικῶς unquàm medium apprehendens meritum Christi, consideratur: uti nos contendimus: An verò quatenùs posteriore modo illa spectatur: uti per turpem petitionem principii contendunt Photiniani, id quod nos simpliciter negamus. Nam quæ de Pœnitentia proferunt, omni vero elencho destituuntur: Hoc ipsum enim rursus in quæstione est: An loca Scripturæ, urgentia pœnitentiam, tanquàm conditionem remissionis peccatorum, An inquam de tali pœnitentia sint intelligenda, quæ sit extra Christum, uti rursum per petitionem principij nugantur hæretici.

Nam licèt non semper explicitè & secundum literam fides in Christum exprimatur: tamen implicitè semper subintelligitur. Quemadmodum enim miseratio DEI in Christi sanguine nobis est parata: ita Pœnitentia sine fide, Christi meritum sibi applicante, in conspectu DEI mera est hypocrisis: ac tantùm non Remissionem peccatorum consequitur: ut potiùs ad desperationem adigat hominem, sicut exemplo Caini, Judæ proditoris & aliorum patet.

VIII. Multas conglomerat ratiunculas, quibus monstrare conatur, Satisfactionem Christi non posse stare cum misericordia DEI: sed cùm diversum hactenus abundè demonstraverimus: & infra Controversia tertia Quæstionem hanc pleniùs sit pertractatura, fusiùs hoc loco de illis agere, haud attinet. Rem tamen universam certis quibusdam observationibus hoc loco includere placet.

I. Satisfactio Christi excludit solutionem debiti respectu nostri: à nobis enim ea non exigitur: Non verò excludit miserationem DEI, quæ hoc pacto sibiipsi satisfecit. Ergò in uno eodemque opere Remissionis peccatorum, Misericordia DEI & Satisfactio Christi simul stare possunt. Misericordiæ enim est, quod & sibiipsi satisfecit, & propter hanc Satisfactionem gratis nobis remittit peccata, per fidem in Sanguine Christi. Rom. 3, 24. & 25.

II. Satisfactio est contraria Remissioni, si utraqs in uno eodemq; Subjecto consideretur: Non est contraria, si in diversis: Ut hoc loco: Satisfactio non exigitur ab iis, quibus remittuntur peccata: sed donatur his aliena Satisfactio & sic condonantur peccata: Quæ condonatio est gratuita respectu nostri, quatenùs eam nos non sumus promeriti: non est gratuita respectu DEI, qui Satisfactionem Christi meriti loco intuetur.

III. Simile quod hæretici subindè urgent, de remissione debiti sive æris alieni, non militat. Distinguendum enim inter debitum pecuniarium & inter jus naturale: Illud remitti potest, sine Satisfactione. Hoc non item: quia sic periclitaretur Justitia DEI, imò sic DEUS non esset aut maneret DEUS.

IV. Quando in Scripturis jubemur DEI æmulari naturam & misericordiam exercere: non is sensus est, quòd debita & offensas quasqs absolutè & simpliciter sine ulla Satisfactione remittere debeamus: sic enim omnis disciplina inter homines tolleretur: sed jubemur tantùm, partim privatas remittere injurias, partim etiam non semper summum jus ἀνεξικῶς persequi: Sed nihil hoc ad misericordiam & justitiam DEI, quæ utraque neque circa privatas offensas, neque circa ἀνεξοδικα,ον occupatur.


### Special Controversy, with the More Recent Photinians, on the Vindicating Justice of God

That GOD was truly angry with the human race on account of sin committed, and according to the rigor of His Justice adjudged it to eternal punishments, the orthodox Church of GOD believes and confesses from the Holy Scriptures. The chief foundations of this our faith are these:

I. Genes. 2, 17. GOD brings forth this sentence: On whatever day you eat from this tree, you shall die the death. Isa. 59, 2. Your sins have divided between you and your GOD, and your sins have hidden his face from you, so that he would not hear. Isa. 63, 10. But they provoked him to ANGER, and afflicted his holy Spirit, and he fought against them. Isaiah 57, 15. & 16. Thus says the high one: I will not contend forever, nor will I be ANGRY unto the end. Isa. 64, 5. Behold we have sinned, and you are ANGRY.

Jerem. 3, 5. Will you be angry forever? And verse 12. I am holy, says the LORD, and I will not be ANGRY forever. John 3, 36. He who does not believe in the Son shall not see life, but the WRATH of GOD remains upon him. Rom. 1, 18. The WRATH of GOD is revealed from Heaven upon all impiety and injustice. And chapter 2, 2. We know the JUDGMENT of GOD is according to truth, against those who do such things. But what ought to be understood by this truth, the Apostle himself explains in the subsequent verse 5, through δικαιοκρισίαν τοῦ Θεοῦ, explaining it as the just judgment of God. But when the Apostle uses the demonstrative term, WE KNOW, he evidently argues that this is an indemonstrable Principle of faith, that God as a just judge is angry at every sin, and therefore in His justice will judge the world, Psalm 98, 9. For the word TO KNOW implies a full assurance resting on certain and immovable principles. And what need is there of many words, when the Apostle has set forth an almost complete Commentary on this Question, and indeed expressly, in Rom. 3, 9. & 19. First indeed arguing that the whole human race is corrupted by sin: then indeed asserting expressly that on account of this very thing it is subject to divine condemnation. The words of the Apostle are more emphatic, and cannot be eluded by any artifice: which are as follows: What then? Are we better than the Jews? In no way: for we have already charged: that Jews and Greeks are all under sin, as it is written: There is not a Just one, not even one, etc. But we know that whatever the Law has, it says to those who are in the Law: that every mouth may be stopped, and the WHOLE WORLD may become subject to the CONDEMNATION OF GOD. There is added the Universal assertion of the same Apostle. Eph. 2, 3. We were by Nature CHILDREN OF WRATH. The very analogy of Faith demands that this passage should be understood not actively, but passively concerning us. For let someone imagine, as Faustus Socinus imagines, that we are called children of wrath, not because GOD is angry with us, but because we are angry with GOD: then infinite absurdities will follow: besides the fact that the heretic has not yet proved his assertion from the Scriptures. For from the nature of opposites it will follow: that the faithful are called friends of GOD, not because GOD loves them, but because they love GOD: But Scripture affirms the opposite, therefore asserting that Lazarus was a friend of the Lord, because the Lord loved him. John 11, 3. & 11. Thus if the opinion of these heretics stands, we shall call him a Son of Death who adjudges another to death: not him who has been adjudged to death: which is prodigiously absurd, and fights against all reason.

Therefore, just as we call him a son of death who has been adjudged to death, even as the Prophet Nathan says to David: The Lord liveth, for the man who has done this is a son of death: And a little later, Thou art that man: So the Apostle names him a son of wrath, not one who is angry at GOD, but one with whom GOD is angry. What is more, according to the impiety of Socinus, GOD ought rather to be called a son of wrath than we: if indeed it be true, as he himself contends, that GOD never was moved against us by wrath: but rather that we conceived wrath against him: which is most blasphemous. Furthermore, let the heretics explain, if God was not made, nor could be made, our enemy on account of sin, but we only his, how it came to pass that Man was not reconciled to God: but rather that God had to be appeased and reconciled by Man? For he is appeased who is angry: he is reconciled who is an enemy. Besides, to what end was there need for Christ to restore and repair all things which are in the Heavens: Ephes. 1. v. 10. to what end also was there need for God the Father, through the blood of the cross of Christ, TO RECONCILE TO HIMSELF, all things which are in the Heavens: Coloss. 1, 20. if there was nothing in Heaven adverse and hostile to men.

Finally, this impiety utterly undermines and overturns many other articles of the Christian Faith: and especially Original Sin, and its most sad Effect, it completely enervates with respect to the Justice of God: and it grants to Man the powers of performing the Obedience due to the Law: not to mention now, that by this pact the providence of God will be greatly endangered: if indeed it is imagined that God, concerning punishing evil and sin according to his Justice, has thought nothing, let alone decreed anything: as will be more clearly evident from the following refutation.

The state of the Controversy, therefore, regarding the present Question will be true and legitimate: Whether God was ever so angry with the human race on account of sin, and decreed to punish them eternally according to his Justice, that his wrath could not be appeased, and his Justice satisfied, except by the intervention of the most perfect Satisfaction of Christ? Where we hold the Affirmative in all things, being thus taught by the oracles of the holy scriptures, which we have just now explained. The Photinians, however, embrace the Negative, positing that God has always loved us, and that he sought reconciliation from us rather than that he himself ever thought of being appeased by us. Their chief flowers are these:

1. The name of Justice, when it is referred to God, is never opposed to mercy in divine letters: but it signifies primarily and for the most part rectitude and equity: But that thing, which when referred to GOD, is opposed to mercy, is not called Justice by the Sacred writers: but is designated by either severity, or wrath, or indignation, or fury, or vengeance, or by some other similar name. Faust. Socinus part. 1. cap. 1. p. 7.

2. God does not therefore punish sinners who do not repent perpetually, because it is proper to him to punish those who sin (for this is that which is opposed to true mercy, which in itself is nothing other than to grant pardon to those who sin, without any regard for repentance or contumacy) but because not to grant pardon to those who do not repent, that finally is the divine nature, and

his decrees, and therefore is due and agreeable to rectitude and equity. ibid. p. 9.

3. I confess, not only the first parents, but the entire human race also, is subject to death and indeed eternal death on account of sin: but that did not flow necessarily from any justice of GOD, but from his free will. ibid. p. 10.

4. GOD could have, and indeed BY RIGHT, not consigned men, although sinning, to eternal death: but after he consigned them to death, he can, by his authority, exempt them, and indeed BY RIGHT, by his SOLE will. ibid. page 11.

5. There is no justice in GOD, which dictates that sin must absolutely be punished, and which he himself cannot renounce. part. 3. cap. 1. p. 224.

6. There is nothing for which GOD cannot freely, to whom he wishes, without any Satisfaction accepted, rightfully forgive sins. ibid.

7. It is false that it is necessary, if GOD is to be just, that he exactly punish the sins of delinquents: because, forsooth, Justice requires absolutely that his own be given to each, but that punishment is due to delinquents. ibid. page 227.

And what need is there of many words, when not only Socinus, but also Ostorodt, Schmalz, and the rest all confess with one voice: It is nowhere read in the Scriptures that GOD is angry at sin: but rather that He has always loved us, even then, when we were still His enemies, so that there was no need for any Satisfaction or Reconciliation on the part of GOD.

Latin:

DEUM generi humano ob peccatum admissum reverâ iratum fuisse, & secundùm rigorem Justitiæ suæ æternis pœnis illud adjudicasse, ex Scripturis Sacris orthodoxa DEI Ecclesia credit & confitetur. Cujus fidei nostræ fundamenta præcipua sunt hæc:

I. Genes. 2, 17. DEUS hanc fert sententiam: Quacunque die comederis de arbore hac, morte morieris. Jes. 59, 2. Peccata vestra diviserunt inter vos & DEUM vestrum, & peccata vestra absconderunt faciem ejus à vobis, ne exaudiret. Jes. 63, 10. Ipsi autem ad IRACUNDIAM provocaverunt, & afflixerunt Spiritum sanctum ejus, & ipse debellavit eos Jesaiæ 57, 15. & 16. Hæc dicit excelsus: non in sempiternum litigabo, neque usque ad finem IRASCAR. Jes. 64, 5. Ecce peccavimus, & tu IRATUS es.

Jerem. 3, 5. Nunquid irascêris in perpetuum: Et verf. 12. Sanctus ego sum dicit DOMINUS, & non IRASCAR in perpetuum. Joh. 3, 36. Qui non credit Filio, non videbit vitam, sed IRA DEI manet super eum. Rom. 1, 18. Revelatur IRA DEI de Cælo super omnem impietatem & injustitiam. Et cap. 2, 2. Scimus JUDICIUM DEI esse secundùm veritatem, adversus eos, qui talia faciunt. Quid autem per veritatem hanc intelligi debeat, ipse explicat Apostolus versu subseq. 5. per δικαιοκρισίαν τοῦ Θεοῦ, per justum judicium Dei illam exponens. Quâdo verò Apostolus utitur termino demonstrativo, SCIMUS, evidenter arguit, Principium fidei αναπόδεικτον hoc esse, quòd Deus ut justus judex, irascatur omni peccato, & propterea in justitia suâ judicaturus mundum, Psal. 98, 9. Nam verbum SCIRE innuit πληροφορίαν certis & immotis nitentem principijs. Et quid multis opus est, cum integrum quasi Commentarium de hac Quæstione, & quidem ex professo expediêrit Apostolus Rom 3, 9. & 19. Primùm quidem totum genus humanum peccato corruptum esse arguens: deindè verò ob hoc ipsum divinæ condemnationi obnoxim illud esse, expressè afferens. Verba Apostoli sunt ἐμφατικώτερα, neque ullo artificio eludi possunt: quæ sic habent: Quid igitur: Meliores ne sumus Judæis? Nullo modo: nam ante evicimus: Judæos & Græcos omnes esse sub peccato, sicut Scriptum est: Non est Justus ne unus quidem &c. Scimus autem, quæcunq, Lex habet, ijs qui in Lege sunt, dicit: ut omne os obturetur, & TOTUS MUNDUS obnoxius fiat CONDEMNATIONI DEI. Accedit ejusdem Apostoli assertio Universalis. Eph 2, 3. Eramus Naturâ FILII IRÆ. Quem locum non activè, sed passivè de nobis intelligi debere, ipsa analogia Fidei exigit. Fingat enim aliquis, uti Faustus Socinus fingit, nos perhiberi filios iræ, non quòd DEUS nobis iratus sit, sed quòd nos irascamur DEO: tùm sequentur infinita absurda: præterquàm, quod hæreticus assertionem suam ex Scripturis nondùm probavit. Nam ex oppositorum naturâ fequetur: Fideles dici amicos DEI, non quòd DEUS ipsos amet, sed quòd ipsi DEUM ament: Atqui diversum affirmat Scriptura, ideò afferens Lazarum fuisse amicum Domini, quia Dominus ipsum dilexerit. Joh. 11, 3. & 11. Sic si hæreticorum istorum stet sententia, Mortis Filium perhibebimus eum, qui alterum morti adjudicat: non qui morti adjudicatus est: id quod prodigiosè absurdum est, & cum omni ratione pugnat.

Proindè sicut Filium mortis dicimus eum, qui morti adjudicatus est, quemadmodum Nathan Propheta ad Davidem inquit: Vivit Dominus, quoniam Filius mortis est vir, qui fecit hoc: Et paulò pòst, Tu es ille vir: Sic Filium iræ nominat Apostolus, non qui irascitur DEO, sed cui DEUS est iratus. Quid quòd secundùm Socini impietatem, DEUS magis dici deberet Filius iræ, quàm nos: si modò verum, quod ipse contendit, DEUM nunquàm adversum nos irâ commotum fuisse: sed nos potiùs adversus ipsum iram concepisse: id quod summè blasphemum est. Porrò edisserant hæretici, si Deus propter peccatum non factus est, neque fieri potuit inimicus noster, sed nos ipsius tantum, quî factum sit, quòd non à Deo Homo: sed Deus potiùs ab Homine placari & conciliari debuerit? Nam ille placatur qui iratus est: ille reconciliatur qui inimicus est. Præterea quorsum opus erat, Christum restaurare & reparare omnia ea, quæ in Cœlis sunt: Ephes. 1. v. 10. quorsum etiam opus erat, Deum Patrem per sanguinem crucis Christi, RECONCILIARE SIBI, omnia quæ in Cœlis sunt: Coloss. 1, 20. si nihil in Cœlo hominibus erat adversum & inimicum.

Tandem impietas hæc plures alios Fidei Christianæ articulos funditùs subruit & evertit: & cumprimis Peccatum Originis, ejusdemque tristissimum Effectum, respectu Justitiæ Dei planè enervat: & Homini largitur vires præstandi Obedientiam Legi debitam: ut nihil jam dicamus, quòd hoc pacto Dei providentia plurimùm periclitabitur: si nimirùm de malo atque peccato puniendo Deus secundùm Justitiam suam, nihil cogitasse, nedùm decrevisse fingatur: quemadmodum ex refutatione subsequente dilucidiùs patebit.

Status proindè Controversiæ, quoàd præsentem Quæstionem verus ac legitimus erit ille: An Deus propter peccatum Generi humano unquàm ita iratus fuerit, & secundùm Justitiam suam æternùm punire decreverit, ut non nisi interventu perfectissimæ Satisfactionis Christi, ira ipsius placari, & Justitiæ ipsius satisfieri potuerit? Ubi nos Affirmativam per omnia tenemus, sic edocti sacrarum literarum oraculis, quæ jam modò expediyimus. Photiniani verò Negativam amplexantur, statuentes, Deum nos semper dilexisse, & à nobis potiùs petijsse reconciliationem quàm ut ipse de se nobis placando unquàm cogitaverit. Flosculi ipsorum præcipui sunt isti:

1. Justitiæ nomen, cùm ad Deum refertur, in divinis literis nunquàm opponitur misericordiæ: sed præcipuè & plerumq; rectitudinem & æquitatem significat: Ea verò res, quæ ad DEUM relata, misericordiæ opponitur, non Justitia appellatur à Sacris scriptoribus: sed vel severitas, vel ira, vel indignatio, vel furor, vel vindicta, vel alio quopiam simili nomine nuncupatur. Faust. Socinus part. 1. cap. 1. p. 7.

2. Non ideò punit Deus perpetuò peccatores non resipiscentes, quia proprium sit ejus, punire eos, qui peccant (hoc namq; illud est, quod veræ misericordiæ opponitur, quæ per se nihil aliud est, quam peccantibus veniam dare, nullâ pœnitentiæ vel contumaciæ ratione habitâ) sed quia non resipiscentibus veniam non concedere, id demùm natura divina, &

decretis ejus, & propterea rectitudini & æquitati debitum est ac consentaneum ibidem. p. 9.

3. Fateor, non primos parentes tantùm, sed universum etiam humanum genus, propter peccatum morti & quidem æternæ obnoxium esse: verùm id non ex aliquâ DEI justitiâ necessariò fluxit, sed ex libera ejus voluntate ibid. p. 10.

4. Potuisset DEUS & quidem JURE, homines, licet peccantes morti æternæ non mancipare: postquàm autem eos morti mancipavit, ex illius imperio eximere, & quidem JURE, suâ SOLA voluntate potest. ibid. pag. 11.

5. Nulla in DEO est justitia, quæ omninò peccatum puniri debere dictitet, & cui ipse renunciare non possit. part. 3. cap. 1. p. 224.

6. Nihil est, propter quod DEUS liberè, cui velit, nullâ Satisfactione acceptâ, peccata jurè condonare non possit. ibid.

7. Falsum est, necesse esse, si DEUS justus futurus sit, ut delinquentium peccata exactè puniat: quia scilicet Justitia omninò requirat, ut suum cuique tribuatur, delinquentibus autem punitio debeatur. ibid. pag. 227.

Et quid multis opus, cùm non modò Socinus, sed & Ostorrodius, Schmalzius, & reliqui uno ore fateantur omnes: Nuspiam in Scripturis legi, quod DEUS irascatur peccato: sed potiùs quòd semper nos dilexerit, etiam tùm, cùm adhuc inimici ipsius essemus, ita ut nulla vel Satisfactione, vel Reconciliatione ex parte DEI opus fuerit.


### Special Controversy, with the More Recent Photinians, on the Vindicating…: Moreover, the reasons with which they fight are chiefly these

Moreover, the reasons with which they fight are chiefly these:

I. The name of divine Justice, when it is referred to GOD, is never and nowhere in the Holy Scriptures opposed to mercy. Therefore, the Mercy of GOD forgiving sins does not look to any Justice in God by which He Himself is angry at sinners and decrees punishments, much less to any Satisfaction by which this justice must have been satisfied.

I answer, in the dissolution of this argument, two things must necessarily be premised, most worthy of explanation: First, in how many ways the term Justice is predicated of GOD in the Scriptures: Then, indeed, how Christ has declared this Justice of His through λύτρον, or the Satisfaction of Christ. With these two rightly explained, this whole dispute will be clearer, which otherwise does not lack obscurity and consequently some difficulty.

As to the first member, the Justice of GOD is not predicated of GOD univocally in the Scriptures: For first, it denotes that universal Justice or rectitude in GOD: and then it is opposed to injustice, iniquity, and malice: as when David pronounces of GOD that He is just, loves righteousness, and His countenance beholds the upright, Psalm 11:7. Then it denotes that legal justice, by which He does well to the good and ill to the evil: Which in

In the schools we call it distributive, διανεμητικὴν, and judicial, the effect of which is that to each his own is given, the wicked are punished, and the pious are rewarded. Photinians deny that this Justice of God is found expressed in the Holy Scriptures, and Andreas Osiander also denied it in previous years, contending that the legal justice of GOD is always defined in the Scriptures by the word of wrath or fury: But the contrary can easily be demonstrated, especially from Paul, who defines this vindicatory Justice of God specifically, Rom. 1:32, saying that the Gentiles know τὸ δικαίωμα θεᢁ, this Right of God, that those who do such things are worthy of death. Where surely no one, either sane or learned, will think that τὸ δικαίωμα should be translated as fury, wrath, severity, or any such similar word. Thus the same Apostle expressly assigns to God δικαιοκρισίαν, just judgment: and indeed, which deserves observation, he opposes this very δικαιοκρισίαν to the riches of the goodness, tolerance, gentleness, and kindness of God: so that he proclaims of this goodness of God that it entices men to repentance: but of the δικαιοκρισίαν, that it renders to each according to his works, verse 6. Therefore Socinus is caught as a liar twice. 1. Because he denies that that equity by which GOD punishes sins is ever called Justice in the Scriptures: but only wrath, fury, and severity: then because he denies that the vindicatory Justice of GOD is ever opposed to divine mercy in the Scriptures. Certainly where there is δικαιοκρισία opposed to Mercy: there it is necessary that the Justice of God itself also be opposed to the same, unless perhaps someone wishes to affirm that the just judgment of God is something remote and separated from the justice of God itself: which would be prodigiously absurd: since the Judgment of God does not derive this epithet from anywhere else than from his justice itself, and indeed from that distributive or Judicial Justice of God, which the Photinians stubbornly deny.

But there are also other testimonies of Scripture by which the impiety of those heretics can be refuted: such as Rom. 3:5. But if our injustice commends the justice of GOD, what shall we say? Is GOD unjust? where the Apostle in express words calls the punishments which are inflicted for our sins δικαιοσύνην θεᢁ, the Justice of God: bringing forward that the Justice of God shines forth even from the fact that he inflicts punishment on sinners: He who does not see that vindicatory Justice in God is established there, sees nothing. Of the same evidence is also that 2 Thess. 1:5 and 6, ἔνδειγμα τῆς δικαίας κρίσεως τῡ θεῡ: This is a demonstration of the just judgment of God: since it is just before GOD to repay affliction to those who afflict you, etc. In the Old Testament, and especially among the Prophets, almost nothing is read and heard more frequently than the frequent celebration of this judicial or vindicatory Justice: as when David exclaims: You are just, O Lord, and your judgment is just, Psalm 119:137, and all the saints pray that God may not deal with them according to this Justice of his, and at the same time they frequently oppose the Mercy of GOD to this Justice of GOD, not indeed as the Photinians wish, contradictorily: but privatively, as will be demonstrated more fully a little later in the dissolution of the objections.

Thirdly, the word Justice, when it is predicated of GOD, is sometimes equivalent to the truth of GOD, because GOD most constantly keeps those things which he promises: so that it deserves the encomium of Justice even from that, as Psalm 36:7, Your truth reaches to the clouds: And Psalm 117:2, The truth of the LORD remains forever.

Finally, the word Justice denotes the same as the goodness and mercy of GOD, forgiving sins, and exercising other effects of divine compassion among men: as when David prays, Psalm 31:2, in your Justice deliver me. And Psalm 35:24, Judge me according to your justice. And 1 Sam. 12:7, Samuel says to the whole multitude: Stand, that I may contend with you in judgment before the Lord, concerning all the mercies of the Lord: Where in the Hebrew it is concerning all the Justices אֶת כָּל־צִדְקוֹת of the Lord, which he did with you, and with your fathers. The Photinians urge only this fourth meaning, and from there they rise up against us. But anyone easily understands that their entire argument proceeds from a part, and therefore a shameful ἀδολεσχίαν (babbling) is committed. For it does not follow: in some places of Scripture, Justice of God signifies mercy: Therefore it signifies the same everywhere, and consequently there is no vindicatory justice in God.

Moreover, as for the other part of the Observation, the Justice of GOD in the work of our Redemption, accomplished through CHRIST, has declared itself quite evidently according to all four of those meanings. For first, nothing can be found alien to the rectitude and most absolute holiness of GOD, but rather a certain admirable harmony of all divine virtues shines forth from it. Thus, regarding the third and fourth meanings, GOD truly exercised his justice, that is, the truth of his promises, according to that of Zechariah: he redeemed his people and raised up a horn of salvation in the house of David, as he had spoken by the mouth of his holy Prophets, Luke 1:69 and 70, and according to that of Mary: Remembering his mercy, as he spoke to our fathers, Luke 1:54 and 55. Thus he truly exercised his Goodness and mercy in the same work of redemption: For in this God commends his charity, that while we were still enemies, Christ died for us, Rom. 5:8. Finally, regarding that second meaning, about which there is the most controversy, it cannot be denied by any reason that GOD also exercised that distributive and judicial Justice in the work of Redemption: since that most especially required that satisfaction be made to it, & indeed through the shedding of Blood: while it also demanded that the reward of eternal life should not fall to any but those who have applied this Satisfaction of Christ to themselves by true faith, and have endeavored to enter into eternal life through many tribulations. We seek the foundations of this assertion of ours from the Scriptures: The chastisement of our peace was upon him: Jehovah thus willed to crush him, Isa. 53, 5. Likewise, I will betroth thee unto me in righteousness and in judgment, and in mercy and in faithfulness, Hosea 2, 19. The Apostle confirms this more clearly in the New Testament, Rom. 3, 25 & 26. GOD set forth Christ as a propitiation through faith in his blood, πρὸς ἔνδειξιν τῆς δικαιοσύνης to demonstrate his righteousness, through the remission of sins: to demonstrate (I say) his righteousness in the present time, etc. To which also pertains that passage, 2 Thess. 1, 5. It is just with GOD to render retribution to those who suffer affliction.

These things having been thus premised, we finally respond to the first Argument of the Photinians by a simple denial of the Antecedent. For first, it is trivial that they contend that in the Scriptures the name of Justice, when it is predicated of GOD, is never opposed to his mercy. Then it is also trivial that they write that the thing which, when related to GOD, is opposed to mercy, is nowhere called Justice: but only severity, wrath, indignation, or vengeance. For the contrary has been evidently demonstrated thus far.

II. Argument: Justice, opposed to the mercy of GOD, is twofold: one, which GOD uses perpetually, punishing and exterminating all the wicked and contumacious: The other, by which he sometimes punishes sinners who are not even contumacious: nor impenitent. By this same reasoning the Mercy of GOD also behaves itself, so that it is indeed also twofold: One, by which he pardons all crimes to the penitent according to his promises, and bestows salvation and life; The other, by which he plainly anticipates men, and calls and entices to himself those still immersed in sins: and gratuitously, even to those not thinking of it, offers the forgiveness of offenses and salvation: He uses the former perpetually: but the latter only when it has pleased him: Now indeed neither of these mercies has any respect to any Satisfaction: but both are gratis gratuitous &: as Ostorodt writes: Out of pure grace and for nothing: Therefore neither does any Justice of God respect any Satisfaction: but whatever he does, he does out of mere and free will.

I respond that this whole argumentation consists of perpetual petitions of the Principle, or trifles, nay, of the grossest crimes of falsehood, or pseudographs in purer Theology. For first, the decision of the immediately preceding controversy has clearly demonstrated that it is vain and false that the heretics trifle about a twofold and indeed specifically different Mercy of GOD. For just as the essence of GOD is one in number: so is the mercy one in number, which admits of division into diverse species so little that, if it were to admit this, it would then utterly overturn the Essence of GOD. For whatever is divisible into diverse species: that must necessarily be not simple, let alone most simple: but composite. Now indeed all composition is only of a created Being: and that is either Physical, consisting of the concretion or concurrence of matter and generated form: or Metaphysical, consisting of act and potency: or Logical, in which genus and specific difference have the status of principles: But none of these can be piously predicated of GOD. Therefore. What? That from disparate species one Being cannot be made by itself, and indeed a most simple one. Then a base Sophistication of a vicious Consequent is committed. For no reason of Consequence militates: GOD promised out of his Mercy that he would gratuitously forgive the sins of the penitent. Therefore this Mercy of GOD is absolute, and does not respect the merit of Christ. The vice of this collection arises even from the fact that it falsely posits: Gratis gratuitous and Absolute, to be terms equivalent and simply convertible: which is detected to be most false even from this: that sins are said to be forgiven gratis gratuitously, not with respect to GOD, but only with respect to men: who do not merit this Remission in any way. Now indeed the question is not properly in this place, how this Remission of sins behaves itself on the part of men, and thus on the part of the patient: but how it behaves itself on the part of GOD the agent: where indeed, as this work is not merely gratuitous, but consists of the merit of CHRIST, and thus is truly compensatory: So it cannot be absolute either. These things having been thus discussed, the Minor proposition of the argument, which subsumes concerning the Justice of GOD, will now be easier to explain. For first, it is of the same vanity that the Photinians contend that there are two diverse species of Justice in GOD, etc. One perpetual: the other transient and mutable. For that he always punishes the impenitent and the wicked: but likewise sometimes afflicts the penitent with punishments: that does not constitute diverse species of Justice in God, but only distinct degrees of one and the same Justice in GOD.

Latin:

Cæterùm rationes, quibus pugnant, præcipuæ sunt hæ:

I. Justitiæ divinæ nomen, cum ad DEUM refertur, in Sacris literis nunquam & nuspiam opponitur misericordiæ. Ergò Misericordia DEI condonans peccata, nõ respicit Justitiam aliquam in Deo, quâ ipse peccatoribus irascatur & pœnas decernat, nedum Satisfactionem aliquam, quâ justitiæ huic satisfieri debuerit.

Respondeo, In dissolutione hujus argumenti, duo necessariò esse præmittenda, explicatu dignissima: Primùm quidem, quot modis Justitiæ vocabulum in Scripturis de DEO prædicetur: Deindè verò, quomodo Christus Justitiam hanc suam per λύτρον, sive Satisfactionem Christi declarârit. Quibus duobus ritè explicatis, tota disputatio hæc erit dilucidior, quæ aliâs obscuritate & consequenter difficultate aliquâ non caret.

Quoad prius membrum, Justitia DEI in Scripturis non univocè de DEO prædicatur: Primùm enim notat Universalem illam Justitiam sive rectitudinem in DEO: & tùm opponitur injustitiæ, iniquitati & malitiæ: ut quando David de DEO pronunciat, quòd sit justus, justitias diligat, & rectum videat facies ipsius Psal. 11, 7. Deindè notat legalem illam justitiam, quâ bonis benè & malis malè facit: Quam in

Scholis distributivam, διανεμητικὴν & judiciariam nominamus, cujus effectus est, ut suum cuique tribuatur, impii puniantur, pii præmiis afficiantur. Hanc Justitiam Dei Sacris in literis expressam reperiri, negant Photiniani, & negavit etiam superioribus annis Andreas Osiander, contendens, legalem justitiam DEI, semper in Scripturis definiri per vocem iræ aut furoris: Sed contrarium facilè demonstrari potest, cùmprimis ex Paulo, qui Justitiam hanc Dei vindicatricem in specie definit, Rom. 1, 32. Gentes inquiens cognoscunt τὸ δικαίωμα θεᢁ, Jus Dei hoc esse, quòd qui talia faciunt, digni sunt morte. Ubi sanè nemo vel sanus vel doctus τὸ δικαίωμα vertendum esse arbitrabitur per furorem, iram, severitatem, aut tale aliquod simile vocabulum. Sic idem Apostolus expressè Deo adsignat δικαιοκρισίαν justum judicium: & quidem, quod observationem meretur, hanc ipsam δικαιοκρισίαν opponit divitiis bonitatis, tolerantiæ, lenitatis ac benignitatis Dei: ita ut de bonitate hac Dei prædicet, quòd ad pœnitentiam homines alliciat: de δικαιοκρισίᾳ verò, quòd reddat unicuique secundùm opera ipsius, vers. 6. Bis ergò mendax deprehenditur Socinus. 1. Quòd negat æquitatem illam, quâ DEUS peccata punit, nuspiam in Scripturis nominari Justitiam: sed tantùm iram, furorem, ac severitatem: deindè quòd negat in Scripturis uspiam misericordiæ divinæ opponi Justitiam DEI vindicatricem. Certè ubi est δικαιοκρισία opposita Misericordiæ: ibi eidem ipsa quoque Justitia Dei opposita sit necesse est, nisi fortè quis affirmare velit, Justum judicium Dei esse aliquid remotum & separatum ab ipsa Dei justitia: id quod prodigiosè foret absurdum: siquidem Judicium Dei non aliundè hoc Epithethon fortitur, quàm ab ipsâ ejus justitiâ & quidem distributivâ illâ, sive Judiciariâ Justitiâ, Dei, quam præfractè negant Photiniani.

Sed sunt & alia Scripturæ testimonia, quibus impietas hæreticorum istorum retundi potest: ut Rom. 3, 5. Quòd si injustitia nostra, DEI justitiam commendat, quid dicemus? Nùm injustus est DEUS? ubi Apostolus disertis verbis pœnas, quæ nostris peccatis infligūtur nominat δικαιοσύνην θεᢁ Justitiam Dei: afferens vel indè Justitiam Dei elucescere, quòd pœnam infligit peccantibus: Ubi Justitiam in Deo vindicatricem stabiliri, qui non videt, nihil videt. Ejusdem evidentiæ est & illud 2. Thess. 1, 5. & 6. ἔνδειγμα τῆς δικαίας κρίσεως τῡ θεᢁ: Hæc est demonstratio justi judicij Dei: siquidem justum est apud DEUM ἀνταποδῦναι vicissim reddere ijs, qui vos affligunt, afflictionem &c. In Veteri Testamento & cumprimis apud Prophetas nihil frequentiùs fermè legitur & auditur, quàm crebra Justitiæ hujus judiciariæ, sive vindicatricis celebratio: ut cum David exclamat: Justus es Domine & justum judicium tuum, Psal. 119, 137. & sancti quique deprecantur, ne Deus cum ipsis agat secundum Justitiam hanc suam, & simul huic Justitiae DEI frequenter opponunt Misericordiam DEI, non quidem uti Photiniani volunt, contradictoriè: sed privativè, uti paulò post in dissolutione objectionum fusius demonstrabitur.

Tertiò, Justitiae vocabulum, quando de DEO praedicatur, interdum aequipollet veritati DEI, propterea quòd DEUS constantissimè servat ea, quae promittit: ita ut vel indè Justitiae encomium mereatur, ut Psal. 36, 7. Veritas tua usque ad nubes: Et Psal. 117, 2. Veritas DOMINI manet in aeternum.

Tandem Justitiae vox idem notat ac bonitas & misericordia DEI, condonans peccata, & alia divinae miserationis effecta, in hominibus exercens: ut quando David orat, Psalm. 31, 2. in Justitia tua libera me. Et Psalm: 35, 24. Judica me secundum justitiam tuam. Et 1. Sam. 12, 7. inquit Samuel ad universam multitudinem: State, ut judicio contendam adversum vos, coram Domino, de omnibus misericordijs Domini: Ubi in Hebraeo est de omnibus Justitijs אֶת כָּל־צִדְקוֹת Domini, quas fecit vobiscum, & cum patribus vestris. Hanc quartam significationem solùm urgent Photiniani, & indè adversum nos insurgunt. Sed quivis facilè intelligit, totam ipsorum disputationem ex parte procedere, ac proindè turpem committi ἀδολεσχίαν. Neque enim sequitur: in quibusdam Scripturae locis, Justitia Dei significat misericordiam: Ergo ubique idem significat, & per Consequens nulla est in Deo justitia vindicatrix.

Caeterùm quod alterum est Observationis membrum, Justitia DEI in opere Redemptionis nostrae, per CHRISTUM peracto, secundum omnes quatuor istas significationes, sese satis evidenter declaravit. Primùm enim nihil à rectitudine ac absolutissima sanctitate DEI alienum deprehendere licet, quin potiùs admiranda quaedam harmonia omnium virtutum divinarum indè elucescit. Sic quoad tertiam & quartam significationem verè exercuit DEUS justitiam suam hoc est, veritatem promissionum suarum, secundum illud Zachariae: redemit populum suum & erexit cornu salutis in domo David, prout locutus fuerat per os Sanctorum Prophetarum, Luc. 1, 69. & 70. & secundum illud Mariae: Recordatus misericordiae suae, sicut locutus est ad patres nostros, Luc. 1, 54. & 55. Sic verè exercuit in eodem redemptionis opere Bonitatem & misericordiam suam: Nam in eo commendat Deus charitatem suam, quòd cum adhuc inimici essemus, Christus pro nobis mortuus est, Rom. 5, 8. Tandem quoad secundam illam significationem, de quâ potissimùm controvertitur, negari nullâ ratione potest, quin DEUS in opere Redemptionis Justitiam quoque illam διανεμητικὴν distributivam & judiciariam exercuerit: dum illa vel maximè requirebat, ut sibi satisfieret, & quidem per effusionem Sanguinis: dùm item efflagitabat, ut præmium vitæ æternæ nón nisi iis obtingeret, qui Satisfactionem hanc Christi verâ fide sibi applicaverint, & per multas tribulationes in vitam æternam ingredi studuerint. Assertionis hujus nostræ fundamenta ex Scripturis petimus isthæc: Castigatio pacis nostræ super eum: Jehovah sic voluit eum conterere, Jes. 53, 5. Item desponsabo te mihi in justitia & judicio, in misericordia & fide, Hoseæ 2, 19. Clariùs in novo Testamento hoc confirmat Apostolus, Rom. 3, 25. & 26. DEUS proposuit Christum propitiatorium per fidem in sanguine ipsius, πρὸς ἔνδειξιν τῆς δικαιοσύνης ad demonstrandam justitiam suam, per remissionem peccatorum: ad demonstrandam (inquam) justitiam suam in præsenti tempore &c. Quò pertinet etiam locus ille, 2. Thess. 1, 5. Justum est apud DEUM retributionem præstare ijs, qui afflictionem patiuntur.

His ita præmissis respondemus tandem ad Argumentum primum Photinianorum, per simplicem inficiationem Antecedentis. Primùm enim nugatorium est, quòd contendunt, in Scripturis, Justitiæ nomen, quando de DEO prædicatur, misericordiæ ipsius nunquàm opponi. Deindè nugatorium etiam est, quòd scribunt, eam rem, quæ ad DEUM relata, misericordiæ opposita est, nusquam appellari Justitiam: sed tantùm severitatem, iram, indignationem aut vindictam. Contrarium enim hactenus evidenter demonstratum est.

II. Argumentum: Justitia, DEI misericordiæ opposita, est duplex: una, quâ DEUS perpetuò utitur, puniens & exterminans omnes scelestos & contumaces: Altera, quâ nonnunquàm peccatores etiam non contumaces: nec impœnitentes punit. Quâ ipsa ratione se etiam habet Misericordia DEI, ut nimirùm ea quoq; sit duplex: Una, quâ pœnitentibus, secundum promissiones suas omnia scelera condonat, & salutem vitamq́; largitur; Altera, quâ planè homines prævenit,& peccatis adhuc immersos ad se vocat & allicit: & gratuitò, necogitantibus quidem, delictorum veniam & salutem offert: Illa perpetuò utitur: hâc verò tùm demùm cum sibi libuerit: Jam verò neutra hæc misericordia ullum habet respectum ad Satisfactionem aliquam: sed utraq́; est gratis gratuita&: ut Ostorodi9 scribit: Aus lauter Gnaden vnd vmbsonst: Ergò neq; Justitia ulla Dei, Satisfactionem aliquam respicit: sed quicquid facit, ex merâ ac liberâ voluntate facit.

Respondeo, totam hanc argutationem perpetuis constare petitionibus Principii, sive ἀδολεσχίαις, imò crassissimis criminibus falsi, sive ψευδογραφήμασι in Theologiâ puriore. Primùm enim controversiæ proximè præcedentis decisio, luculenter demonstravit, vanum & falsum esse, quòd de duplici & specie quidem differente DEI Misericordia nugântur hæretici. Quemadmodum enim Una numero DEI est essentia: sic una numero misericordia, quæ usque adeò divisionem in species diversas non admittit, ut si hanc admitteret, tùm Essentiam DEI prorsus everteret. Quicquid enim in species diversas est dividuum: illud non simplex, nedùm simplicissimum: sed compositum sit necesse est. Jam verò omnis compositio est tantùm Entis creati: eaque vel Physica, constans concretione sive concursu materiæ & formæ genitæ: vel Metaphysica, constans actu & potentia: vel Logicâ, in quâ genus & differentia specifica rationem principiorum habent: Atqui horum nihil piè de DEO prædicari potest. E. Quid? quòd ex speciebus disparatis non potest fieri unum Ens per se, & quidem simplicissimum. Deindè turpis committitur Sophisticatio vitiosi Consequentis. Neque enim ulla militat Consequentiæ ratio: DEUS ex Misericordiâ suâ promisit, se gratis gratuitò remissurum peccata pœnitentibus. Ergò Misericordia hæc DEI est absoluta, neque Christi meritum respicit. Vitium collectionis hujus vel indè oritur, quòd falsò statuit: Gratis gratuitum & Absolutum, esse terminos æquipollentes ac simpliciter convertibiles: id quod falsissimum esse vel indè deprehenditur: quòd peccata dicuntur Gratis gratuitò remitti, non respectu DEI, sed tantùm respectu hominum: qui Remissionem hanc nullâ ratione promerentur. Jam verò quæstio non est propriè hoc loco, quomodo Remissio hæc peccatorum se habeat ex parte hominum, & sic ex parte patientis: sed quomodo se habeat ex parte DEI agentis: ubi profectò, uti opus hoc non est merè gratuitum, sed constat merito CHRISTI, & sic reverâ est compensatorium: Ita absolutum etiam esse nequit. Quibus ita discussis facilior jam explicatu erit Minor argumenti propositio, quæ subsurnit de Justitia DEI. Primùm enim ejusdem vanitatis est, quòd contendunt Photiniani, in DEO duas esse diversas species Justitiæ &c. Unam perpetuam: alteram transientem & mutabilem. Nam quòd impœnitentes & scelestos semper punit: pœnitentes verò itidem Interdum pœnis afficit: id non diversas species Justitiæ in Deo, sed unius ejusdemque Justitiæ in DEO, distinctos tantùm gradus constituit.


### Special Controversy, with the More Recent Photinians, on the Vindicating…: Moreover, the reasons with which they fight are chiefly these (continued)

Then the Adversaries basely confuse the first act of the Justice of GOD with the second act. For neither, because the second act is of the most free will in GOD; and can be either exercised or retracted, is there therefore to be established in GOD some peculiar species of Justice which is subject to mutability. For the Justice of GOD, insofar as it is an attribute of GOD, is always convertible with the Essence, and is no more divisible into species than the Essence of GOD. But the second act is of free will: yet not absolute, but determined, on this side indeed toward the penitent, on that side toward the impenitent. With respect to the latter, joined with wrath and fury: but with respect to the former, joined with mercy. For the divine mercy is indeed tempered with a certain Justice, if it sometimes corrects even the penitent, so that they may work out their salvation with fear and trembling with so much the more zeal, lest they be condemned with the world, 1 Cor. 11:32. Moreover, that GOD does not always afflict the penitent with punishments arises not from some singular species of divine Justice and mercy: by reason of which GOD does not exercise the rigor of His Justice toward the penitent: for the reason that CHRIST sustained those in their stead, as Isaiah ch. 53:5 attests: The discipline of peace was upon him, and by his stripes we are healed.

But Socinus objects, and brings forward two testimonies from the Holy Scriptures: One from Exodus ch. 34, v. 6 and 7. Jehovah, Jehovah, strong, merciful and compassionate, slow to anger, and abundant in mercy and truth: keeping mercy for thousands: taking away iniquity and transgression, and sin, and who by clearing will not clear. Here, says Socinus, after He professed that He is exceedingly merciful and forgives sins, He says: And who by clearing will not clear. Those words, however, seem to signify nothing else than that the Lord is indeed most inclined toward mercy and toward forgiving offenses for men: but yet that He does not absolve those who continue to be guilty and rebellious, because of that first and immutable Justice of His.

I answer: 1. The heretic has wandered off the path. For we move no dispute with anyone concerning this Justice of GOD immutably punishing headstrong and contumacious sinners. We ourselves urge and defend this very thing, but this is the Question: Whether, besides this perpetual and immutable Justice of GOD, another species of divine Justice can and ought to be established, which is not perpetual, but mutable? This is what we deny again and again against Socinus. Two things, however, come to be observed in this place. 1. The asystasia or inconsistency of Socinus, who shamefully contradicts himself. For in this place he argues that there is in GOD a perpetual and immutable Justice by which He punishes the guilty and rebellious: but in part 3, ch. 1, p. 224, he expressly writes: That there is no justice in GOD which dictates that sin must be punished at all. Indeed, on page 10 he writes: That the human race is subject to eternal death, not necessarily from any Justice of GOD: but from His free will. Then, however, a twofold depravation of the Mosaic saying which Socinus cites comes to be noted. For 1. he thinks that it deals only with the impenitent: which is diametrically opposed to the whole context, which is uniquely occupied in demonstrating the immense mercy of GOD, certainly not toward the impenitent: but the penitent: just as Moses himself explains himself in Deut. 5:9, asserting that GOD shows mercy to many thousands, but of those who love Him and keep His commandments. That this notation applies to none but the penitent is manifest in itself. The other depravation of the text by Socinus is that the Hebrew words, Exod. 34, verse 7, Venakkeh lo Jenakkeh, he renders as 'by clearing I will not clear,' that is, by remitting sin I will not remit: so that he may put a gloss on his own opinion, namely, that only the impenitent are the Object of that immutable divine Justice: when here the true and genuine sense of the words of Moses is rather: I will not acknowledge sin as not sin: or, by purifying, GOD will not purify sin: or as others have rendered it: by judging the innocent, He will not judge him innocent. All of which things ought indeed to be accommodated to the penitent as well.
