But lest that spiritual serpent, the Devil, should depart immune, therefore in the words that follow, concerning which there is controversy among us, with his speech turned to him, the Lord inflicts punishment upon him, and at the same time raises up men, most gravely disturbed by his fall, with the promise of the seed, that it would crush the Devil's head. Finally, it is placed beyond all shadow of doubt that that same seed of the woman, which is promised in this place, is also promised in Genesis 22:18: here indeed to the first parents: but there to Abraham, which is declared by the attributes of the same kind assigned equally in both places. For it is of the same [seed] both to crush the head of the serpent and to bring a blessing to all nations. Nay, one and the same divine work is indicated under merely different phrases. Whence it is most firmly gathered that, if, with the Apostle attesting in Galatians 3:16, the word of seed made in the promise to Abraham, Genesis 22, must be accepted concerning one Christ alone, that [word] in Genesis 3 must also be accepted concerning the same Christ alone, who was to crush the serpent's head, provided that the Remission of sins was to accrue to men: which was to be demonstrated against the Photinians. But let the Calvinists see how they wish to remove from themselves the suspicion of the Photinian heresy in this part, while they themselves also explain this passage of Genesis 3:15 concerning that natural enmity of men and serpents, as can be seen in Calvin in his Commentary on this very passage.

The THIRD foundation the Photinians do not indeed directly attack. For they themselves confess that in Genesis 22:18 is contained the promise given to Abraham concerning the Messiah: but yet, in order to show that this very promise has absolutely nothing in common with that which exists in Genesis 3:15 concerning the Seed of the woman: therefore they invent that the Messiah was first promised to Abraham; and that there was no people of GOD peculiar to Him before: but that the first Election was made in Abraham, as Sommer and Socinus write.

But from those things which we have just now said concerning the first promise, and its comparison with that which was given to Abraham, the vanity of this interpretation is spontaneously evident. For the heretics will never prove from the Scriptures that in those two promises of Gen. 3 and 22 one and the same Seed is not denoted: but that one Seed is that which crushes the head of the serpent, and another again that which brings a blessing to the nations. Furthermore, the heretics commit a manifest falsehood, asserting that the Messiah was first promised to Abraham. For the contrary is evident from chapter 3:15 of Genesis: as has already been demonstrated before: Furthermore, it would be false what the Holy Spirit affirms, that Jehovah spoke concerning the Messiah through the mouth of all the holy Prophets, who have been from the beginning, Luke 1:70, Acts 3:21. Thus it is a manifest lie that they affirm that no people, who were before Abraham, were peculiar to GOD. Was there then no Church of the pious or Elect on earth before Abraham, and indeed for more than two thousand years? For the promise made to Abraham falls in the year of the world 2023. This is impious and absurd. And what does Moses mean when he writes in Genesis 4:26 that in the time of Enos it began to be called upon the name of the Lord? The sense of which words is not that in the past two hundred years the name of the Lord was not preached: but this is the sense, that after the Church had previously been restricted to very narrow limits, so that the worship of GOD was performed within private walls. But now when Enos had been born, and he himself also had begotten sons and daughters, who themselves also, having contracted marriages, led out their own colonies: therefore it happened that when sacred worship was to be performed, they would now convene from those various colonies to a certain public place, and thus would celebrate not private, but public sacred assemblies. Shall we therefore think that this that the people thus gathered into one were not peculiar to GOD, in comparison with the rest of the peoples? Far be it that we should even think such a thing. Thus the third lie is also well and truly thick, that they invent that the First Election was made in Abraham? Will the heretics therefore affirm that in that whole multitude calling upon the name of the Lord, in the time of Enos, no one was elect? Of Enoch we certainly read in Genesis 5:24 that he walked with GOD, and therefore GOD took him away. Thus the Holy Spirit asserts that Noah was a just and perfect man: Genesis 6:9 and chapter 7:1. And Noah himself after the flood names GOD the GOD of Shem: thus implying that Shem was beloved by GOD, Genesis 9:26. Finally, it is also a gross lie that they trifle that Christ is nowhere named the seed or Son of Adam, but only of Abraham and of David. For the Genealogy of Christ is expressly traced back to Adam in Luke 3:38. But the fact that Christ is more frequently named in the Scriptures the Son of Abraham and David is because that promise issued to Adam was still more general, and indefinitely denoted some Seed of the woman. The subsequent promises, however, are more special, and expressly express a certain family in particular, from which Christ ought to be born: namely, the Family of Abraham and David.

Latin:

Cæterùm habent Photiniani rationes benè multas, quibus octo isthæc Fundamenta nostra evertere student. Primùm enim Comminationem illam Jehovæ Genes. 2. 17. eludere conantur, contendentes, de morte corporali eam accipi non posse, propterea quòd hæc Homini sit naturalis, neq́; Peccati Stipendium, sed Naturæ nostræ, quam ipsemet Adamus in Creatione accepit, propria sequela : ut scribit Socinus part. 3. c. 8. p. 294. Verùm nervum non tangit hæc cavillatio. Primùm enim non tam de morte Naturali, quàm Spirituali illa, hoc est, æternâ damnatione, quam Jehovah primis parentibus comminatus est, si comederint de arbore prohibita, proptiè hoc loco controvertitur: An nimirùm salvâ veritate ac Iustitia Dei, pœnam hanc sine ulla Satisfactione remittere illis, sive condonare Deus potuerit? Ubi affirmativam suam Photiniani nondùm probatam dederunt. Deindè, quoad Quæstionem de Morte corporis, quòd Homini etiam in Statu Integritatis, fuerit Naturalis, simpliciter negatè respondemus, si de actu ipso mortalitatis intelligatur Quæstio, uti Articulo de Creatione contra Bellarminum Negativam nostram evidenter demonstravimus. Tandem nugatorium planè est, quòd distinguunt inter Mortem ipsam & moriendi necessitatem, dicentes, Moriendi quidem necessitatem esse Effectum Comminationis illius: non verò Mortem ipsam, propterea quòd hæc Adamo fuerit Naturalis: Quid enim obsecro est Mors naturalis, quàm moriendi necessitas: ut quæ secundùm ipsorum hypothesin, dependet à Naturæ humanæ conditione post lapsum, ita ut Spiritus Sanctus etiam hanc moriendi necessitatem pijs cum impijs communem esse voluerit. Heb. 9, 27. Statutum est omnibus semel mori. Falsum proindè & absurdum, quod pij non necessariò, sed naturaliter tantùm moriantur : Impij verò & naturaliter & necessariò: Quasi verò non Universaliter & ex æquo se habeat ad pios & impios, quoad mortem Corporis & hujus necessitatem, Aphorismus ille Apostolicus Rom. 6, 23. Stipendium peccati est Mors: Ubi quicquid Mortis nomine venit, intelligendum esse statuimus, quanquàm ex Accidenti postmodùm sit, ut Mors hæc Corporalis impijs sit æternæ mortis sive damnationis initium: pijs verò transitus ex morte ad vitam, Joh. 5, 24.

Alterum fundamentum nostrum, petitum ex promissione illa prima Evangelica, de Semine mulieris, contrituro caput Serpentis, falsè rident, & stylo plusquàm hæretico contendunt, non esse promissionem, sed maledictionem & quidem temporalem, quæ inimicitias hominum & serpentũ significet, qua ante lapsum non fuerit. Iob. Sommerus Pirnensis l. 2. contrà Petrum Carolium cap. 3. pag. 73. Cæterùm blasphemam & contortam esse hanc interpretationem, constat. 1. vel indè, quòd tes, quæ verbis figuratis hoc loco de destructione regni Satanici est proposita, postmòdùm illustre suum complementum est sortita. Deinde nisi per contritionem capitis serpentis intelligatur excidium regni Satanici, consequens est, DEUM primis quidem parentibus dictasse pœnam: Serpenti autem sive Diabolo planè nullam dictasse: qui tamen lapsus illius tristissimi primaria fuit causa impellens: id quod cum Justitia DEI simpliciter pugnat. Tum hoc pacto DEUS illos reliquisset expertes ac inopes omnis solatii, ac in perpetuâ dubitatione fluctuantes. Atqui falsissimum hoc esse vel indè constat, quòd Heva per Semen illud mulieris intellexit virum illum Jehovah, qui à DEO promissus, redemtionem à peccato & æterna damnatione præstare deberet. Undè cap. 4, 1. Cainum enixa exclamat: Acquisivi virum Jehovah: existimans se jam edidisse promissum illud Semen mulieris, contriturum caput Serpentis 4. Præteera inepta planè, imò prorsus nulla esset verborum Dei cohærentia: si statuatur DEUS primùm comminatus esse naturalem illam inimicitiam serpentum & hominum: & mox post correctionem quasi quandam subjecisse, Hominem aliquo modo viribus ejusmodi esse instructum, ut interdum morsum Serpentum vel planè prohibere, vel certè mitigare aut sanare possit. Quid quæso hoc faceret ad lapsum jam commissum? quid ad Comminationem ipsam? quid ad Consolationem? imò quid ad Diabolum omnis mali Architectum? Nihil, nihil prorsus. 5. Insuper stante hac corruptelâ, sequeretur deteriorem fuisse conditionem Ecclesiæ illius Originalis sive primævæ: quàm fuit omnibus subsequentibus seculis ac temporibus: quibus semper jam indè à temporibus Abrahæ, solennes propositæ fuerunt promissiones Evangelicæ de liberatione à morte & æternâ damnatione, per Christum præstanda. Sola autem originalis Ecclesia tali promissione post lapsum caruisset, si præsens hæc promissio de Christo accipi non debeat: id quod prodigiosè absurdum. 6. Porrò manifestum est, Jehovam distinctè & separatìm naturali etiam serpenti suam dictare sententiam, in præcedentibus: Quia, inquiens, fecisti hoc, maledictus eris inter omnia animantia & bestias terræ: super pectus tuum gradieris, & terram comedes cunctis diebus vitæ tuæ. Ne autem spiritualis ille serpens Diabolus abiret immunis, ideò sequentibus deindè verbis, de quibus inter nos controvertitur, oratione ad ipsum conversâ, pœnam Dominus ei infligit, & simul homines suo lapsu gravissimè perturbatos, erigit promissione seminis, quòd Diaboli caput esset contriturum. Tandem extra omnem dubitationis aleam est positum, idem illud semen mulieris, quod hoc loco promittitur, promitti etiam Genes. 22, 18. hîc quidem protoparentibus: illîc autem Abrahamo, id quod declarant ejusdem generis attributa utrobique pariter assignata. Ejusdem enim est, & caput conterere serpenti, & benedictionem afferre cunctis gentibus. Imò, unum idemq; opus divinum sub diversis tantùm phrasibus indicatur. Undè e firmissime colligitur, si attestante Apostolo Galat 3, 16. vox seminis in promissione Abrahæ facta, Genes. 22. de uno solo Christo accipi debeat, esse etiam illud Genes. 3. de eodem solo Christo accipiendum, qui conterere debebat serpenti caput, dummodò Remissio peccatorum hominibus obtingere debuit: id quòd contra Photinianos erat demonstrandum. Viderint autem Calviniani, quo pacto Photinianæ hæreseos suspicionem, hâc in parte à se amoliri velint, dùm & ipsi locum hunc Genes. 3, 15. de naturali illa inimicitia hominum & serpentum exponunt, uti videre est apud Calvinum in Commentario ad hunc ipsum locum.

TERTIUM fundamentum non quidem directè impugnant Photiniani. Nam ipsimet fatentur Genes. 22, 18. contineri promissionem Abrahæ de Messia datam: sed tamen, ut ostendant, hanc ipsam promissionem cum ea, quæ extat Genes. 3, 15. de Semine mulieris, nihil prorsus habere commercii: ideò fingunt, Abrahamo primùm fuisse promissum Messiam; neque prius ullum aliquem populum DEI peculiarem: sed primam Electionem in Abrahamo factam fuisse, ut Sommerus & Socinus scriptitant.

Verùm ex iis, quæ jam modò de prima promissione, ejusdemque collatione cum ea, quæ Abrahamo data fuit, diximus, vanitas hujus interpretationis ultrò patet. Nam in æternum ex Scripturis non probabunt hæretici, in duabus istis promissionibus Gen. 3. & 22 nõ unum idemque notari Semen: sed aliud esse Semen, quod conterat caput serpentis, aliud rursum, quod benedictionem afferat gentibus. Deindè manifestum ψεῦδος committunt hæretici, asserentes Abrahamo primùm promissum fuisse Messiam. Diversum enim patet ex cap. 3, 15. Geneseως: uti jam antè demonstratum: Deindè falsum esset, quod Spiritus sanctus affirmat, Jehovam locutum esse de Messia per os omnium sanctorum Prophetarum, qui fuerunt à seculo Luc. 1, 70. Actor. 3, 21. Sic mendacium manifestum est, quòd affirmant, populum nullum, qui ante Abrahamum fuit, fuisse DEO peculiarem. Siccinè ergò nulla Ecclesia piorum sive Electorum ante Abrahamum in terris extitit, & quidem per annos bis mille ampliùs? Incidit enim promissio Abrahæ facta in A. M. 2023. Impium hoc & absurdum. Et quid sibi vult Moses, quando Genes. 4, 26. scribit, tempore Enos incœptum fuisse invocari nomen Domini? Quorum verborum non is sensus est, quòd præteritis annis ducentis, nomen Domini non sit prædicatum: sed hic sensus est, quòd postquàm priùs Ecclesia adhuc valdè angustis terminis esset coarctata, ita ut intra privatos parietes cultus DEI perageretur. Jam verò cum natus esset Enos, & ipse quoque filios ac filias procreasset, qui & ipsi contractis matrimoniis proprias colonias deducerent: ideò factum sit, ut quando cultus sacer efset peragendus, jam ex diversis illis coloniis, ad locum quendam publicum convenirent, atq; sic nõ privatos ampliùs, sed publicos conventus sacros celebrarent, Siccinè ergò putabimus, hunc populum sic in unum coactum, non fuisse peculiarem DEO, præ reliquis populis? Absit ut tale tale quid vel saltem cogitemus. Sic tertium etiam & benè spissum est mendacium, quòd fingunt, Primam Electionem in Abrahamo factam fuisse? Anne ergò in universa illa multitudine invocantium nomen Domini, tempore Enos, nullum electum fuisse, affirmabunt hæretici? De Henocho certè legimus Genes. 5, 24. quòd ambulaverit cum DEO, & ideò DEUS eum abstulerit. Sic Spiritus sanctus, asserit Noahum fuisse virum justum ac perfectum: Genes. 6, 9. & cap. 7, 1. Et Noahus ipse post diluvium DEUM nominat DEUM Sem: sic innuens, Semum esse dilectum DEO, Genes. 9, 26. Tandem crassum etiam mendacium est, quod nugantur, Christum nusquam nominari semen vel Filium Adami, sed tantùm Abrahæ & Davidis. Nam Genealogia Christi expressè usque ad Adamum deducitur Luc. 3, 38. Cæterùm quòd frequentiùs in Scripturis Christus nominatur Filius Abrahæ & Davidis, in causa est, quòd promissio illa Adamo edita, erat adhuc generalior, & indefinitè notabat Semen aliquod mulieris. Subsequentes autem promissiones sunt specialiores, & disertè certam quadam familjam in specie exprimunt, ex qua Christus nasci debuerit: nempè Familiam Abrahæ & Davidis.


### A Special Controversy Against the recent Photinians, On the Satisfaction for our Sins (continued)

The FOURTH Foundation, taken from the victims and Sacrifices of the Old Testament, they attempt to infringe with a few arguments.

For first they assert that the Ceremonies of the Levitical Sacrifices governed this end, that these being performed, GOD, because of His infinite mercy, wished to grant His people a plenary remission of sins, and thereby to render them entirely certain of those: but that the offering of these was not in itself so worthy and meritorious, much less did it have in itself the force of Satisfaction, inasmuch as in them neither could committed sins be punished, nor could any remuneration for benefits bestowed be rendered to GOD. Socin. part 2. cap. 11. p. 128.

But I reply that a fallacy of non-cause as cause is being committed: For it does not follow that: The Levitical Sacrifices contributed to the remission of sins in no respect at all, because they could not attain this end or Effect by themselves or of themselves. For another respect is given, which is and is called Typical, insofar as those Sacrifices, individually and collectively, pointed a finger at CHRIST, by whose faithful intuition the believers of the Old Testament truly obtained the Remission of sins: as has been demonstrated more fully above. The rest, which they attempt to deceive with regarding the infinite and absolute mercy of GOD, and regarding that subalternated end which consists in the certification of the Remission of sins, is partly a begging of the question, and partly τῷ ἄφ τό ἐλλιπὲς τῆς διαιρέσεως. And what, I ask, will these heretics answer to the Author of the Epistle to the Hebrews, who expressly asserts concerning the High Priest of the Old Testament that he offers gifts and victims for the sins of men, Heb. 5:1. If this is so, who, I pray, would have dared to deny that those were Satisfactory in their own respect?

Furthermore, Socinus makes a commotion that it is nowhere read in the Holy Scriptures that those sacrificing satisfied the Justice of GOD. But this too is a gross lie: for if victims were offered to God for the sins of men, even a blind man sees, and a dullard understands, that the respect was primarily instituted to nothing other than the immutable Justice of GOD, under the offering of sacrifices. What? That in 2 Sam. 24:21 and 25 it is expressly read that David built an altar to the LORD to strongly restrain the plague sent by the Lord. Is the Sacrifice of Christ therefore now of less efficacy? There is added the Hebrew word כפר Caphar, which not only, as Socinus grunts, signifies to cleanse, remove, cover, hide: but according to its native signification denotes the same as to appease, to reconcile: let anyone who has even a single ounce of sound mind left judge whether that can be done without Satisfaction of the Justice of GOD. Thus one may read this word in Genesis 32:20, I will appease his face with a gift. And Socinus himself admits on page 126 that the emphasis or proper signification of the word Caphar is shown by the word Chitte. Now indeed this word signifies to Recompense, to Satisfy, to render what is just or equitable: as in Genesis 31:39, I did not bring to you what was stolen, but I satisfied you for it, or I redeemed it with a certain price. We conclude therefore that the Sacrifices which are called in the Scriptures Cipurim truly signify not only a hiding, but also a Satisfaction for sins.

Thirdly, the heretic blathers that the Levitical Sacrifices were offered not for all sins, much less for great and grave ones: but only for light and small sins.

But even here he is found to be vain and a liar: For it is clearly evident from the Scriptures that Sacrifices were offered not only for ignorances or sins of Omission: but also for the most grave transgressions of all: such as for Ascham, an abomination, Levit. 4:3; for Maghal, that is, a sin committed against conscience: Levit. 6:2; for Gharonorh, that is, deliberate malice: Levit. 16:21; for Peschgaim, a defection from the Law of GOD, ibid.; for Thamorh, that is, impurities and contaminations: Levit. 16:19; indeed for manifest and publicly notorious crimes and outrages committed by a Magistrate, Levit. 4:22; indeed for all iniquities: Levit. 16:30; and indeed before the LORD, verse 34. Concerning which sacrifices, individually and collectively, Moses adds that they are an odor of sweetness to the LORD, not in the Photinian sense, as some kind of odor or sweetness: but a Satisfactory or Appeasing odor, so that whatever could be adverse and hostile to GOD from the sins of men, was now by the virtue of the Sacrifices, but in the Type of Christ, so expiated that men became acceptable and pleasing. Hence it is read that GOD, appeased by the sacrifices, remitted His wrath. 2 Samuel 21:14 and chapter 24:21 and 25. And it is to be noted that this eulogy of the sacrifices is in particular also accommodated to the sacrifices for sins, Levit. 4:31.

where Moses says: Taking away all the fat, as it is wont to be taken away from the victims of peace offerings, he shall burn it upon the Altar for a sweet-smelling savour to the LORD, and he shall pray for him, and it shall be forgiven him, &c. Finally, they bring forward this rancid quibble, that Christ did not complete his Sacrifice on the altar of the cross, but only now in the heavens: where, sitting at the right hand of the divine Majesty, he presents himself to his Father for us, preserves his ministry, defends, and protects the Church even to the last day, so that in this way the sins of men may be averted and taken away. Therefore, those things which are brought forward concerning the Satisfaction of Christ, performed on this earth, are false. He seeks proof of the antecedent from the Epistle to the Hebrews 8, 4. If he were on earth, he would not be a Priest.

I reply that this argument also is woven from mere vanities: For in the beginning, no reason supports the Consequent: Christ sitting at the right hand of the Father is our Pontiff and Priest. Therefore, he performed no Sacrifice on the altar of the cross. The vanity of the collection results from an Ignorance of the Refutation, and an insufficient enumeration of the parts of the Sacrifice of Christ: one of which was performed on this earth, meritorious or satisfactory, through the shedding of Blood on the altar of the cross by a transitory act, of which Peter speaks, chap. 1. 2, 24. Christ bore our sins in his body upon the tree: the other, however, is applicatory and eternal, and is performed in the Heavens, through incessant intercession for men, according to that passage in Rom. 8, 24. He sits at the right hand of the Father, that he may intercede for us.

Then, regarding the passage Heb. 8, 4, a gross Sophistry of the Figure of Diction is committed. For to be a Priest on earth already sounds to the Apostle as offering irrational victims after the manner of the rest of the earthly Priests. By this arrangement, Christ is certainly never or was never a Priest on earth: for thus he would have served only the Exemplar and the shadow. Therefore, the Apostle compares the Levitical Priests with Christ in that place, and shows that he is the supreme Pontiff for this reason, that is, the true one and the one prefigured by the Levitical ones, because he did not handle earthly victims: but offered himself; as is clearly evident from the text.

THE FIFTH Foundation, collected from the perpetual Testimonies of the Scriptures, which the Photinians oppose, they contend that, although it is read that Christ shed his blood for our sins, bore our sins, reconciled us to God, and performed other things of that kind for us, nevertheless these individual and universal things do not have the respect of merit, or of any Satisfaction, by which in our stead satisfaction was made to GOD. Hence Faustus Socinus has progressed to such impiety and blasphemy that he did not shudder to write that all those sayings, which assert that Christ was delivered up for our sins, are not to be understood as coming from the Decree of GOD, but only occasionally, because, forsooth, on the occasion of our sins he fell into death, not otherwise than when a merchant, running across the sea for the sake of riches, or because of riches, suffers shipwreck. Which execrable blasphemy we rightly leave to be avenged by the avenging flames of the underworld: convinced by the oracles of the Scriptures that Christ was delivered up not occasionally or fortuitously, but by the certain and definite counsel of God and the will of the Father: nay, that he himself also by his own will and power laid down his soul as a λύτρον καὶ ἀπολύτρωσιν for us. Acts 2, 23. and chap. 4, 27. and 28. John 10, 18. Hence in the Scriptures also, when Christ suffered for us, he is read to have done the will of the Father Heb. 10, 7. Which very will he also prays against quite anxiously on the mount of olives Matt. 26, 39. and 42. What? That the Adversaries bind and overturn themselves with the snare of impiety: For since Socinus writes explicitly that Christ, by falling into the curse occasionally, meanwhile freed us from the true curse of the law, it would certainly follow: that our liberation from the curse of the Law happened fortuitously and by accident? But since the heretic would hardly admit this very thing, it is also necessary that he concede that our redemption is not occasional, fortuitous, and accidental: especially since Scripture couples our redemption with the curse of Christ in an almost inseparable bond, as Effect and Cause per se. Furthermore, since Christ was ἀναμάρτητος, he certainly could not have become the curse of the law, or, as the heretics say, fallen into it, unless he had derived another's guilt, that is, our own, into himself. For where there is no sin, there is neither death, nor the curse of the law. It remains, therefore, that for us, that is, in our stead, Christ shed his blood &c.

But the Photinians also attack that which we drew from the Epistle to the Hebrews 9, 22: That the remission of sins cannot happen without the shedding of blood. For they say that mediation, expiation, and other effects of that kind are indeed assigned to the Blood of Christ in the Scriptures: but only insofar as it was a medium for confirming the covenant: but not that it was the medium through which that very covenant, which consists in the remission of sins, was acquired.

I reply: 1. That which the heretics assert, they do not prove, but rather they manifestly lie. For Scripture assigns both ἐξαρρησίαν to the Blood of Christ, namely that 1. it is the medium by which the New covenant was sanctioned and established, and therefore it can rightly be named the substance of the New covenant, Heb. 9, 14. and 15. Then, however, that this very blood is the medium through which that covenant, which consists in the remission of sins, was acquired: as manifest testimonies of the scriptures attest Heb. 9, 25 & 26. For Christ did not appear, that he might offer himself often, as the Pontiff enters into the Holy places, every year with the blood of others: but once AT THE DESTRUCTION OF SIN, he appeared through his own sacrifice. And the preceding verse 15. Therefore of the New Testament. CHRIST is the Mediator, that by his death intervening, for the redemption ἀπολύτρωσιν of those transgressions which were under the former covenant, they who were called might receive eternal life. And verse 12. Christ entered once into the Holy places through his own blood, having acquired eternal redemption. And chap. 10, 18. 19. 20. Where there is remission of sins, there is no longer need for a sacrifice for sin.

Latin:

QUARTUM Fundamentum à victimis & Sacrificiis Veteris Testamenti petitum, aliquot rationibus infringere conantur.

Primùm enim asserunt, Sacrificiorum Leviticorum Ceremonias hunc rexisse finem, ut ijs expeditis, propter infinitam misericordiam suam DEUS populo suo plenariam largiri voluerit peccatorum remissionem, deóque ea certos omninò illos reddere: non autem istorum oblationem per se usque adeò dignam ac meritoriam fuisse, nedum in se habuisse vim Satisfactionis, utpote in quibus nec peccata commissa puniri, nec DEO probeneficijs prestitis remuneratio aliqua præstari potuerint. Socin. part. 2. cap. 11. p. 128.

Sed respondeo committi Sophisma non Causæ ut Causæ: Neque enim ideò sequitur: Sacrificia Levitica nullo planè respectu contulisse remissionem peccatorum, quia non per se, sive ex se finem hunc sive Effectum assequi potuerunt. Datur enim alius respectus, qui est ac dicitur Typicus, quatenùs nimirùm Sacrificia illa fingula & universa digitum intenderunt ad CHRISTUM, cujus fideli intuitu Remissionem peccatorum reverâ consequebantur fideles Veteris Testamenti: uti supra fusiùs demonstratum. Reliqua, quæ de infinita & absoluta DEI misericordia, deque fine illo subalternato; qui consistit in certificatione Remissionis peccatorum, partim petitione Principii, partim τῷ ἄφ τό ἐλλιπὲς τῆς διαιρέσεως, fucum facere student. Et quid quæso respondebunt hæretici isti Autori Epistolæ ad Hebreos, qui de Pontifice Veteris Testamenti expressè asserit, quòd donatia & victimas pro hominum peccatis DEO offerat, Heb. 5, 1. Si hoc, quis obsecro Satisfactoria illa suo respectu fuisse, negare ausus fuerit?

Tumultuatur porrò Socinus, nullibi Sacris in literis legi, quòd Sacrificantes Justitia DEI satisfecerint. Sed crassum & hoc est mendacium: si enim Deo pro peccatis hominum oblatæ sunt victimæ, vel cæcus videt, & bardus intelligit, non nisi ad immutabilem D E I Justitiam, sub Sacrificiorum oblatione, respectum potissimùm fuisse institutum. Quid? quod 2. Sam. 24, 21. & 25. expressè legitur, quòd David ædificaverit altare DOMINO, ad fortiter cohibendam immissam plagam à Domino. Siccinè ergò minoris jam efficaciæ erit Sacrificium Christi? Accedit vox hebræa כפר Caphar, quæ non tantùm, uti Socinus grunnit, significat emundare, removere, inumbrare, occultare: sed secundum nativam suam significationem idem notat ac placare, reconciliare: quod, nùm sine Satisfectione Justitiæ D E I fieri possit, judicet, cui vel unica sanæ mentis superest uncia. Sic legere licet hoc verbum Genes. 32, 20. placabo faciem ejus munere. Et fatetur ipse Socinus pag. 126. emphasin sive propriam significationem verbi ….. Caphar, monstrari per verbum …. Chitte. Jam verò hoc verbum significat, Recompensare, Satisfacere, Jus sive æquum bræstare: ut Genes. 31. 39. Raptum non attuli tibi, sed satisfeci tibi pro eo, sive redemi illud certo pretio. Concludimus proindè Sacrificia, quæ dicuntur in Sacris Cipurim ---- non tantùm occultationem, sed & Satisfectionem pro peccatis reverà significare.

Tertiò blaterat hæreticus, Sacrificia Levitica fuisse oblata non pro omnibus peccatis, multò minus pro magnis & gravibus: sed tantùm pro leviculis & exiguis peccatis.

Sed & hîc vanus & mendax deprehenditur: Neque enim pro ignorantiis tantùm aut peccatis Omissionis: sed & pro gravissimis quibusque delictis Sacrificia oblata fuisse ex Scripturis luculenter patet: ut pro Ascham abominatione Levit. 4, 3. pro Maghal, id est, peccato contra conscientiam commisso: Levit. 6, 2. pro Gharonorh, id est, destinata malitia: Levit. 16, 21. pro Peschgaim, defectione à Lege D E I, ibid. pro Thamorh, id est, impuritatibus & contaminationibus: Levit 16, 19 imò pro manifestis & publicè notoris sceleribus atque flagitiis à Magistratu commissis, Levit. 4, 22. imò pro omnibus iniquitatibus: Levit. 16, 30. & quidem coram DoMINO vers. 34. De quibus Sacrificiis singulis & universis subjicit Moses, quòd sint odor suavitatis DOMINO, non sensu Photiniano, qualiscunque odor sive suavitas: sed odor Satisfactorius sive Placatorius, ut quicquid ex peccatis hominum DEO poterat esse adversum & inimicum, jam virtute Sacrificiorum, sed in Typo Christi, ita esset expiatum, ut grati acceptique evaderent homines. Hinc DEUS Sacrificiis placatus iram suam remisisse legitur. 2. Samuel. 21, 14. & cap. 24, 21. & 25. Et notandum quòd hoc Sacrificiorum elogium in specie etiam accommodatur ad Sacrificia pro peccatis, Levit. 4. vers. 31.

ubi Moses inquit: Omnem adipem auferens, sicut auferri solet de victimis pacificorum, adolebit super Altare in odorem suavitatis DOMINO, rogabitq; pro eo, & dimittetur ei, &c. Tandem proferunt rancidum hoc cavillum, Christus Sacrificium suum non peregit in ara crucis, sed nunc demùm in cœlis: ubi considens ad dextram Majestatis divina, Patri stio sese pro nobis præsentat, ministerium conservat, defendit, & Ecclesiam usque ad deum novissimum tuetur, ut ita avertantur & tollantur peccata hominum. Ergò falsa sunt, quæ de Satisfactione Christi, hisce in terris peractâ proferuntur. Antecedentis probationem petit ex Epistola ad Hebræos 8, 4. Si esset super terram, non esset Sacerdos.

Respondeo hanc quoque argutationem ex meris vanitatibus esse contextam: Nam initiò nulla militat ratio Consequentis: Christus sedens ad dextram Patris est noster Pontifex & Sacerdos. E. Sacrificium nullum peregit in ara crucis. Vanitas collectionis resultat ex Ignoratione Elenchi, & insufficienti enumeratione partium Sacrificii Christi: quarum una in his terris meritoria sive satisfactoria, per effusionem Sanguinis in ara crucis peragebatur actu transitorio, de quo Petrus, cap. 1. 2, 24. Christus portavit nostra peccata in corpore super ligno: altera verò est applicatoria & æterna, inque Cœlis peragitur, per intercessionem indefinentem pro hominibus, secundum illud Rom. 8, 24. Sedet ad dextram Patris, ut intercedat pro nobis.

Deindè quoad locum Heb. 8, 4. crassa committitur Sophisticatio Figuræ Dictionis. Nam in terra Sacerdotem esse, jam sonat Apostolo, ac in morem reliquorum Sacerdotum terrenorum, victimas irrationales offerre. Hoc sanè pacto Christus nunquàm est aut fuit Sacerdos in terra: sic enim inserviisset duntaxat Exemplari & umbræ. Confert proindè eo loci Apostolus Sacerdotes Leviticos cum Christo, & ostendit, ideò ipsum summum esse Pontificem, hoc est, verum illum & à Leviticis præfiguratum, quia non terrenas tractavit hostias: sed semetipsum obtulit; uti ex textu luculenter patet.

QVINTUM Fundamentum ex perpetuis Scripturarum Testimoniis collectum, ut oppugnent Photiniani, contendunt, licet Christus sanguinem suum pro peccatis nostris effudisse, peccata nostra tulisse, nos Deo reconciliasse, & id genus alia pro nobis peregisse legatur, tamen hæc singula atque universa, non habere respectum meriti, sive Satisfactionis alicujus, quâ vice nostri DEO sit satisfactum. Hinc Faustus Socinus eò impietatis & blasphemiæ progressus est, ut scribere non exhorresceret, omnia illa dicta, quæ asserunt, Christum traditum esse propter peccata nostra, non de Decreto DEI, sed tantùm occasionaliter esse intelligenda, quòd nimirùm occasione nostrorum peccatorum inciderit in mortem, haud secus, ac cùm mercator propter divitias, sive divitiarum causâ trans mare currens, naufragium patitur. Quam execrandam blasphemiam ultricibus inferorum flammis vindicandam meritò relinquimus: Scripturarum oraculis convicti, non occasionaliter, aut fortuitò, sed certò ac definito Dei consilio & voluntate Patris Christum traditum esse: imò ipsum quoque propriâ voluntate ac potestate animam suam posuisse λύτρον καὶ ἀπολύτρωσιν pro nobis. Actor. 2, 23. & cap. 4, 27. & 28. Joh. 10, 18. Hinc in Scripturis etiam Christus, quando pro nobis passus est, voluntatem Patris fecisse legitur Heb. 10, 7. Quam ipsam voluntatem satis anxiè etiam deprecatur in monte oliveti Matth. 26, 39. & 42. Quid? quòd seipsos impietatis laqueo constringunt & evertunt Adversarii: Cùm enim Socinus disertè scribat, Christum occasionaliter incidendo in execrationem, nos intereà à verâ legis execratione liberasse, certè cõsequens fuerit: Liberationem nostram, ab execratione Legis fortuitô & per accidens evenisse? Atqui hoc ipsum cùm vix admissurus sit hæreticus, cõcedat etiam necesse est, nostram redemtionem nõ esse occasionalem, fortuitam, & accidentalem: præsertim cùm Scriptura nostri redemptionem cum Christi execratione, individuo quasi nexu copulet, tanquàm Effectum & Causam per se. Præterea cùm Christus fuerit ἀναμάρτητος, certè execratio legis fieri, vel, uti hæretici loquuntur, in eam incidere non potuisset, nisi alienam culpam, hoc est, nostram in se derivasset. Ubi enim non est peccatum, ibi neq; mors, neq; execratio legis. Relinquitur proinde, pro nobis, hoc est, vice nostri Christum sanguinem suum effudisse &c.

Sed & illud impugnant Photiniani, quod nos ex Epistola ad Hebr. 9, 22. deprompsimus: Remissionem peccatorum sine sanguinis effusione nullam fieri posse. Dicunt enim, assignari quidem in Scripturis, Sanguini Christi mediationem, expiationem, & id genus alia effecta: sed tantùm quatenùs ille fuit medium confirmandi fœderis: non verò quòd ille fuerit medium, per quod acquisitum sit illud ipsum fœdus, quod consistit in remissione peccatorum.

Respondeo: 1. Quod asserunt hæretici, illud non probant, quin potiùs manifestè mentiuntur. Scriptura enim Sanguini Christi utramque ἐξαρρησίαν assignat, nempè quod 1. sit medium, quô sancitum & constitutum est Novum fœdus, ac proindè rectè nominari queat substantia Novi fœderis, Hebr. 9, 14. & 15. Deindè verò, quòd hic ipse sanguis sit medium, per quod acquisitum fœdus illud, quod consistit in remissione peccatorum: sic attestantibus manifestis scripturarum testimoniis Hebr. 9, 25 & 26. Neq; enim Christus, ut sæpè offerret semetipsum, quemadmodum Pontifex intrat in Sancta, per singulos annos in sanguine alieno: sed semel AD DESTRUCTIONEM PECCATI, per suam hostiam apparuit. Et vers. Præced. 15. Ideo Novi Testam. Mediator est CHRISTUS, ut morte interveniente, in redemtionem ἀπολύτρωσιν earum transgressionum, quæ erant sub priore fœdere, vitam æternam accipiant qui vocati erant. Et vers. 12. Christus semel introivit in Sancta per proprium sanguinem æternâ redemtione acquisitâ. Et cap. 10, 18. 19. 20. Ubi est peccatorum remissio, ibi non est ampliùs sacrificio opus pro peccato.


### A Special Controversy Against the recent Photinians, On the Satisfaction for our Sins (continued)

We have therefore the freedom to enter the Sanctuary BY THE BLOOD OF JESUS, which he dedicated for us as a new and living way, through the veil, that is, through his flesh.

Then this reasoning of the Photinians overturns itself: For if the Blood of Christ is the means of confirming the covenant, as they wish: it will certainly also be the means of acquiring the covenant. For the acquisition of the Covenant, that is, Reconciliation with God, was necessary before its confirmation. For that which has been acquired is finally confirmed. Now, however, if reconciliation with GOD cannot take place without the shedding of blood, or which is the same thing, the remission of sins: then the Blood of Christ will certainly be the means by which the Covenant, namely the Remission of sins, was acquired: But the former is true, as the Epistle to the Hebrews ch. 9, v. 22 teaches. Without the shedding of blood there is no remission. Therefore it is necessarily true also that the latter is the case, namely that the blood of Christ is that unique means by which the New Covenant, which consists in the Remission of sins, was not only confirmed, but also acquired.

The Photinians strive to impugn our sixth foundation with many arguments: The first and second can be formulated thus from their opinion: Just as we ought to lay down our lives for our brothers: so also Christ laid down his life for us: But we ought to lay down our lives for the sake of our brothers only, that we may benefit them: not in the place of our brothers, so that we might satisfy some divine Justice for them. Therefore Christ also died for us in this way. Socinus confirms the connection of the Major premise in part 2, ch. 8, p. 111, from that saying, 1 John 3:16. In this we have known love, that Christ laid down his life for us, and we ought to lay down our lives for our brothers.

I answer that the Major premise, as it is formulated by the Photinians, is simply false: For our Charity cannot or ought not to be that Archetype to which the Charity of Christ should be compared and considered: but vice versa, the Charity of Christ ought to be like an Archetype for us, which we should imitate and express in loving our brothers: which the Johannine passage indicates in express words. Then a Sophistry is committed ἀπὸ τῶν πρὸς ἄπλῶς: For the Apostle does not wish for an exact and absolute equality according to all degrees to exist between our love and the love of Christ: For such equality falls to no mortal: but the Apostle requires in us some degree of similarity, and that indeed opposed to hypocritical love, so that we may not love our brothers lightly, or superficially, or only in words: but so ardently that, in imitation of the Archetype, we do not hesitate even to lay down our lives for them (if indeed use and necessity so demand). With these things standing thus, the Minor premise is also found to be false, for we ought not only to lay down our lives for the sake of our brothers, that we may benefit them: but also in the place of our brothers, not indeed that we may satisfy divine Justice: for this is owed to the merit of Christ alone: but that we may promote their salvation even by this means.

The third argument is as follows: It is nowhere read in the Scriptures that Christ suffered in our place: or in our stead, but only that he died for us: that is, for the sake of our benefit, while indeed, about to free us from sin through his preaching, he fell into the greatest persecutions, indeed into death itself: not otherwise than as a good Shepherd sometimes lays down his life for the sheep in this way, yet without any satisfaction: or, as the Apostle is said in Colossians 1:24 to fill up the afflictions of CHRIST in his flesh for the Church, that is, for the edification of the Church, or for the sake of the Church's benefit.

I answer that these heretics basely beg the Question: for they do not prove what they say from the sacred writings. Furthermore, Scripture confirms that in those propositions which deal with the death and passion of Christ, these words or phrases, for us, in our place, or in our stead, are equivalent: although these latter are not found in the Scriptures. The truth of the statement is most clearly evident from 2 Cor. 5:14 and 15. The love of Christ urges us, that we should conclude this: If ONE died FOR ALL: THEREFORE ALL ARE DEAD, and Christ died for all: that those who live should no longer live for themselves etc. Let the heretics now explain, What is it for Christ to have died for us? Certainly, unless they wish to offer manifest violence to the words of the Apostle, they must confess: that it is the same thing as if we all had died. Now, however, we have not died, except in Christ. Therefore it follows infallibly that Christ died in our place, and in our stead, otherwise we would not have died in him. Moreover, that the price of Satisfaction might be exactly established for us, the Apostle adds in the following verse, 21: GOD made him, who knew no sin, to be sin for us, that is, a victim for sin, THAT WE might be made the Righteousness of GOD in him. Where the price of Satisfaction is expressly stated twice. 1. When it is asserted that Christ was made a victim for sin. For victims were offered not only for the sake of men, but also in the place and stead of men, under the type of the coming Messiah, as demonstrated above. 2. When the Effect of the death of Christ is defined as being our Righteousness in him, while indeed according to that of John, 1 ch. 1:7, The blood of Jesus Christ the Son of God cleanses US from all sin: Now, however, he could not cleanse us if it had not been shed in our place, if it were not also Satisfactory.

Regarding the Apostolic passage from ch. 1:24 to the Colossians, a manifest dissimilarity in the example is easily detected. For it is nowhere read that the Apostle suffered to redeem the Church of GOD, as that is asserted of the passions of Christ in almost infinite places. Therefore, just as in the Proposition concerning the passions of Paul, the particle FOR is rightly said to denote only the final cause, namely the benefit or edification of the Church: so in the propositions concerning Christ, the same particle signifies not only the final cause, but also the place.

For to suffer for another that which the other was to suffer, and by suffering it for him to free him, is truly to suffer not only for his sake, but also in his stead and place: But in this way Christ suffered for us. Therefore.

THE FOURTH argument of the heretics is as follows: The preposition 'propter' (for/on account of) nowhere has this meaning, that it signifies satisfaction for sins, but only denotes some cause: so that Christ is rightly said to have died on account of our sins, that is, by reason or occasion of our sins: but not that He made satisfaction for them. Thus we read in 1 Kings 14:16 that GOD delivered Israel on account of the sins of Jeroboam, who sinned and made Israel to sin, that is, by reason of the sins of Jeroboam.

I answer that a shameful 'adoleschia' (babbling) of a faulty consequence is committed, or rather more truly a childish 'adoleschia', while indeed from the negation of one part a collection is made to the whole negatively. For the logic of the consequence does not hold in this argument: The preposition 'propter' in certain places does not signify satisfaction: Therefore it signifies it nowhere. For the argument proceeds from a part. We therefore correct the argument by substituting this most true theological rule: Judgment must be passed concerning the force and proper meaning of words and phrases, not from the interpretation of one or another passage, but from a comparison of all the passages of Scripture dealing with the proposed subject: indeed, from the unanimous consent of the Evangelists and Apostles: Now, if such a comparison is instituted, it is manifest that the Scriptures, through the preposition 'propter' where it is predicated of the death of Christ, denote a 'lytron' (ransom), 'antilytron' (ransom-price), 'apolytrōsin' (redemption), 'prosphoran' (offering), 'thysian' (sacrifice), 'hilasmon' (propitiation) for our sins, as we have demonstrated above in our foundations. Away, therefore, with the empty sophistry of the heretics.

THE FIFTH argument sounds thus: It is indeed read expressly in the Scriptures that Christ reconciled us to GOD the Father (in the dative case), but it is nowhere read that Christ reconciled GOD the Father to us (in the accusative case): For if this were read, then it would follow that GOD had been angry with us, and could not be reconciled without satisfaction.

I answer: 1. The vanity of this argument can be evidently demonstrated from those things which we discussed above concerning the wrath of GOD upon the sins of men, and concerning the vindicatory justice of GOD: Where, by invincible oracles of the Scriptures, it was demonstrated that GOD was truly and seriously angry with us, and without the intervention of the satisfaction of Christ, He could not be reconciled to men. Furthermore, it is a manifest lie that it is nowhere read in the Scriptures in the accusative case that GOD is appeased toward us. Certainly, in Leviticus 1:3 we read thus: If his offering be a burnt sacrifice, he shall offer it at the door of the tabernacle, to appease the LORD for himself: Thus in Leviticus 14:29 we read: And the rest of the oil that is in the left hand, he shall put upon the head of him that is to be cleansed, to appease the LORD for him. Thus, as often as it is read in the Scriptures that Jehovah Himself was appeased through sacrifices, as

Exodus 32:14, 2 Samuel 24:25. Also in the vocative, 'appease, O LORD', Daniel 9:19, surely the sense emerges as nothing other than this, that sacrifices and prayers appeased the LORD? And what, I ask, will the heretics answer to that in Hosea 2:19, where Jehovah Himself speaks thus: I will betroth thee unto me in mercy, in justice, and in faith. Where the interpretation of the Photinians has no place, that men were angry with GOD: but not GOD with men: and therefore GOD only demanded this from men, that having laid aside their hatred they should allow themselves to be reconciled, or betrothed to GOD: but the sense here is: that GOD Himself wishes to betroth the human race to Himself in Christ: and indeed for this reason, because He had previously been angry with it: otherwise He could not have said, I will betroth thee unto me in MERCY: For mercy presupposes preceding wrath. Furthermore, this very betrothal was made IN JUSTICE: namely, by the intervention of another's satisfaction for our sins. Thus in 2 Corinthians 5:18 and 19 it is read that CHRIST reconciled the world 'heautō' TO HIMSELF, not only in the Photinian sense, through the ministry of reconciliation: but also by not imputing their sins to men, as verse 19 expressly states. Therefore, before this reconciliation was accomplished through Christ, the sins of men were imputed to them, which no one but a heretic would deny was a singular effect of divine wrath and justice.

Latin:

Habemus ergo libertatem ingrediendi Sacrarium PER SANGUINEM JESU, quam dedicavit nobis viam novam & vivam, per velum, hoc est, per carnem suam.

Deinde seipsam evertit hæc ratio Photinianorum: Si enim Sanguis Christi est medium confirmandi fœderis, uti volunt: certò erit etiam medium acquirendi fœderis. Prius enim necessaria erat acquisitio Fœderis, hoc est, Reconciliatio cum Deo, quàm ejusdem confirmatio. Confirmatur enim demùm id, quod acquisitum est. Jam verò si sine sanguinis effusione non potest fieri reconciliatio cum DEO, vel quòd idem est, remissio peccatorum: utique Sanguis Christi erit medium, per quod acquisitum Fœdus, nempè Remissio peccatorum: Atqui prius verum, sic docente Epistola ad Hebræos cap. 9. v. 22. Absque sanguinis effusione non fit remissio. Ergò necessario verum est & hoc posterius, nempè Christi sanguinem esse unicum illud medium, per quod non modò confirmatum, sed & acquisitum Novum Fœdus, quod consistit in Remissione peccatorum.

Sextum nostrum fundamentum multis rationibus impugnare student Photiniani: Prima & secunda sic informari possunt ex ipsorum sententia: Quemadmodum nos pro fratribus animas debemus ponere:ita & Christus posuit animam suam pro nobis: Atqui nos tantùm fratrum causâ animam debemus ponere, ut eis prosimus: non vice fratrum, ut pro illis alicui Justitiæ divinæ satisfaciamus. Ergò sic etiam Christus mortuus est pro nobis. Connexum Majoris confirmat Socinus part. 2. cap. 8. p. 111. ex illo dicto, 1. Johan. 3, 16. In hoc cognovimus charitatem, quòd Christus pro nobis animam suam posuit, & nos debemus pro fratribus animas ponere.

Respondeo, Majorem, prout ea à Photinianis informatur, simpliciter esse falsam: Neque enim nostra Charitas potest aut debet esse Archetypus ille, ad quem Charitas Christi exigi ac considerari debeat: sed vice versâ, Charitas Christi debet nobis esse instar Archetypi, quem in diligendis fratribus imitari & exprimere debeamus: id quod locus Johanniticus disertis verbis innuit. Deindè committitur Sophisticatio ἀπὸ τῶν πρὸς ἄπλῶς: Neq; enim exactam absolutamque æqualitatem secundum omnes gradus dilectioni nostræ cum dilectione Christi vult intercedere Apostolus: Talis enim æqualitas in neminem mortalium cadit: sed Gradum aliquem similitudinis, & eum quidem hypocriticæ dilectioni oppositum, in nobis requirit Apostolus, ut nimirum non leviter, aut obiter, vel verbis tantùm: sed càm ardenter fratres diligamus, ut ad Archetypi imitationem vel animas pro illis linquere, (si nimirùm usus & necessitas ita postulet) non dubitemus. Quibus ita stantibus Minor etiam falsa deprehenditur, Non enim tantùm fratrum causâ animam debemus ponere, ut ipsis prosimus: sed & vice fratrum, ut non quidem Justitiæ divinæ satisfaciamus: hoc enim soli merito Christi debetur: sed ut vel hac etiam ratione salutem ipsorum promoveamus.

Tertia ratio talis est: Nuspiam in Scripturis legitur, quòd Christus vice nostri: aut nostro loco passus sit, sed tantùm, quòd pro nobis mortuus sit: hoc est, nostræ utilitatis causâ, dùm nimirùm nos à peccato, per prædicationem suam liberaturus, in maximas persecutiones, immò in mortem ipsam incidit: haud secus, ac bonus Pastor hoc modo interdum ponit animam pro ovibus, sine omni tamen satisfaction ne: vel, quemadmodum Apostolus Coloss. 1, 24. dicitur explere afflictiones CHRISTI in carne sua pro Ecclesia, hoc est, pro Ecclesiæ ædificatione, seu causâ utilitatis Ecclesiæ.

Respondeo, Hæreticos istos turpiter petere Principium: neque enim ex sacris, quod dicunt, probant. Cæterùm confirmat Scriptura, quòd in propositionibus illis, quæ agunt, de morte & passione Christi, vocabula sive phrases hæ, pro nobis, vice nostri, aut loco nostro sint æquipollentes: licèt hæ posteriores in Scripturis non reperiantur. Dicti veritas luculentissimè patet ex 2. Cor. 5, 14. & 15. Charitas Christi urget nos, ut hoc statuamus: Si UNUS PRO OMNIBUS mortuus est: ERGO OMNES MORTUI sunt, & pro omnibus mortuus est Christus: ut & qui vivunt, jam non sibi vivant &c. Edisserant jam hæretici, Quid sit, Christum mortuum esse pro nobis? Certè nisi vim manifestam inferre velint verbis Apostoli, fateantur necesse est: idem illud esse, ac si nos omnes mortui essemus. Jam verò nos non mortui sumus, nisi in Christo. Ergò infallibiliter sequitur, Christum vice nostri, ac loco nostro esse mortuum, alioqui nos in ipso non essemus mortui. Insuper de Satisfactionis pretio exactè nobis constaret, mox versu subseq. 21. subjicit Apostolus: DEUS fecit eum, qui non novit peccatum, pro nobis peccatum, hoc est, victimam pro peccato, UT NOS efficeremur Justitia DEI in ipso. Ubi bis Satisfactionis pretium disertè exprimitur. 1. Cùm asseritur Christus factus esse victima pro peccato. Victimæ enim non modò hominum causâ, sed & hominum vice ac loco, sub typo venturi Messiæ offerebantur, uti suprà demõstratum. 2. Cùm Effectus mortis Christi definitur esse Justitia nostra in ipso, dùm nimirùm secundum illud Johannis, 1. cap. 1, 7. Sanguis Jesu Christi Filij Dei emundat NOS ab omni peccato: Jam verò emundare nos non posset, si non vice nostri esset effusus, si item non esset Satisfactorius.

Quoàd locum Apostolicum ex cap. 1, 24. ad Colossenses, manifesta dissimilitudo in exemplo facilè deprehenditur. Nuspiam enim legitur, Apostolus passus esse pro redimenda Ecclesia DEI, quemadmodum de Christi passionibus illud infinitis fermè locis asseritur. Proindè, uti in Propositione de passionibus Pauli, particula PRO rectè dicitur notare tantùm causam finalem, nempè utilitatem sive ædificationem Ecclesiæ: ita in propositionibus de Christo eadem particula non tantùm significat causam finalem, sed & vicem.

Nam pati pro alio id, quod alteri patiendum erat, & ab eo perpetiendo illum liberare, verè est, non tantùm Causâ, sed & vice ac loco illius pati: Atqui hoc modo Christus passus est pro nobis. Ergò.

QVARTA ratio hæreticorum talis est: Præpositio propter nusquàm habet hanc significationem, ut significet Satisfactionem pro peccatis, sed tantùm notat causam aliquam: ita ut Christus rectè dicatur mortuus esse propter peccata nostra, hoc est, causâ sive occasione peccatorum nostrorum: non verò, quòd pro ipsis satisfecerit. Sic legimus 1 Reg. 14, 16. Quòd DEUS tradiderit Israëlem propter peccata Jeroboam, qui peccavit & peccare fecit Israëlem, hoc est, causâ peccatorum Jeroboami.

Respondeo, turpem committi ἀδολεσχίαν vitiosi consequentis, imò veriùs puerilem ἀδολεσχίαν, dùm nimirùm ex negatione unius partis fit collectio ad totum negativè. Neque enim militat ratio Consequentiæ in hoc argumento: Præpositio propter in quibusdam locis non significat Satisfactionem: Ergò nusquàm eam significat. Nam ex parte procedit argumentum. Corrigimus proindè argumentum substituentes verissimam hanc regulam Theologicam: De vi ac significatione propria vocabulorum & phrasium, judicium est ferendum, non ex unius aut alterius loci interpretatione: sed ex collatione omnium Scripturæ locorum, de propositâ materiâ agentium: imò ex unanimi consensu Evangelistarum & Apostolorum: Jam verò si talis collatio instituatur, manifestum est, Scripturas per Præpositionem propter, ubi de morte Christi prædicatur, notare λύτρον, ἀντίλυτρον, ἀπολύτρωσιν, προσφορὰν, θυσίαν ἱλασμον pro peccatis nostris, uti in fundamentis nostris suprà demonstravimus. Facessas proindè hæreticorum inanis Sophisticatio.

QVINTA ratio sic sonat: Expressè quidem in Scripturis legitur, quòd Christus nos reconciliaverit DEO Patri (in casu Dativo) sed nuspiam legitur, quòd Christus nobis DEUM Patrem (in casu accusativo) reconciliaverit: Hoc enim si legeretur, tùm sequeretur, DEUM nobis iratum fuisse, & sine Satisfactione reconciliari non potuisse.

Respondeo: 1. Vanitatem hujus argumenti evidenter demonstrari posse ex iis, quæ suprà de Ira DEI super peccatis hominum, deq́ue Justitiâ DEI vindicatrice, disputavimus: Ubi invictis Scripturarum oraculis demonstratum, DEUM verè ac seriò iratum fuisse nobis, ac sine interventu Satisfactionis Christi, ipsum hominibus reconciliari non potuisse. Déindè manifestum est mendacium, in Scripturis nuspiam legi in accusativo casu, DEUM nobis placatum esse. Certè Levit. 1, 3. sic legimus: Si holocaustum fuerit ejus oblatio, offeret ad ostium tabernaculi, ad placandum sibi DOMINUM: Sic Levit. 14, 29. legimus: Reliquam autem partem olei, quæ est in sinistra manu, mittet super caput purificati, ut placet pro eo DOMINUM. Sic quoties in Scripturis legitur, quòd per Sacrificia placatus fuerit ipse Jehovah, ut

Exod. 32, 14. 2. Sam. 24, 25. Item in vocativo, placare DOMINE, Daniel. 9, 19. certè sensus non emergit alius, quàm isté, quòd Sacrificia & preces placaverint DOMINUM? Et quid quæso respondebunt hæretici ad illud Os. 2, 19. ubi Jehovah ipse sic loquitur: Ego desponsabo te mihi in misericordia, in justitia & in fide. Ubi interpretatio Photinianorum locum non habet, quòd Homines irati fuerint DEO: non verò DEUS hominibus: ac proindè DEUS illud tantùm ab hominibus flagitaverit, ut deposito odio patiantur se reconciliari, sive desponsari DEO: sed hic sensus est: quòd DEUS ipse velit sibi desponsare in Christo genus humanum: & ideò quidem, quia antea ei iratus fuerat: alioqui non dicere potuisset, Desponsabo te mihi in MISERICORDIA: Misericordia enim præsupponit antegressam iram. Porrò hæc ipsa Desponsatio facta est, IN JUSTITIA: nempè interventu Satisfactionis alienæ pro peccatis nostris. Sic 2. Cor. 5, 18. & 19. legitur, CHRISTUS mundum reconciliasse ἑαυτῷ SIBI IPSI, non duntaxat sensu Photiniano, per ministerium reconciliationis: sed & nó imputando hominibus peccata ipsorum, uti versu 19. disertè habet. Ergò priusquàm hæc reconciliatio per Christum esset peracta, imputabantur hominibus peccata ipsorum, id quod singularem Effectum fuisse Iræ ac Justitiæ divinæ, nemo nisi hæreticus negaverit.


### A Special Controversy Against the recent Photinians, On the Satisfaction for our Sins (continued)

THE SIXTH argument of the heretics is as follows: It was never accepted by any law or custom that one should die for another, as it were in the other's stead and place; nor can the death of one be made the death of another. Therefore, neither is CHRIST to be considered to have died in our stead, or in our place, in respect of any satisfaction.

But this argument also fails: 1. By begging the question. For if the entire syllogism is formed, the major premise will be found to be this: Nothing else is to be determined concerning the death of Christ than what is accepted and approved by common custom and human law. Which proposition is clearly false, and suffers moreover from 'tō exō tou elleipes' (a deficiency of what is outside): for it should have been added: Nothing is to be determined concerning the death of Christ except what is defined by the word of GOD. Furthermore, the minor proposition is not universally true. For the histories of the Romans clearly prove that many have met death for others, that is, in the stead and place of others, and that this was not disapproved by human laws. What is more, one may read a very illustrious example of this thing in the Sacred Scriptures, 2 Samuel 21:1 and following. For when a sufficiently harsh famine had most miserably afflicted the land for three whole years, on account of the cruelty and treachery of Saul against the Gibeonites, it is read that David, at the request of the Gibeonites, crucified seven men or youths from the posterity of Saul. Upon which being done, GOD is read to have been appeased toward the land, verse 14. Where it was surely most true that these seven men died in the stead and place of the rest of the Israelites, so that they would not perish by famine. But even if the minor premise were most true in human affairs, it would nevertheless turn out to be most false in the mystery of redemption. For we have just now demonstrated in the Refutation of the third argument from 2 Corinthians 5:14, that Christ died in our stead in such a way that we all died in him. Thus the same Apostle in Romans 5:6 & 7 testifies that the greatest dissimilarity intervenes between the death of Christ and those who seek death for the salvation of another. Christ, he says, died for the ungodly; scarcely for a righteous man will one die: for peradventure for a good man some would even dare to die: but GOD commends his love toward us, in that while we were yet sinners, or as he speaks in verse 10: while we were yet his enemies, Christ died for us.

while he had been. And the Prophetic oracle deals with this respect, which is so true that not even now, after the Satisfaction of Christ has been performed, is any one condemned for another, but every unfaithful soul dies for itself. But in the latter respect, and according to equity, which is defined by that admirable tempering of the Justice and mercy of GOD, the Soul of Christ, which did not sin, could die for men who have sinned: while, namely, the eternal Heavenly Father, seeing the law could not be fulfilled by men, and his Justice could not be satisfied, so tempered that strict Law of his, that he made the Son, who had not known sin, to be sin for us, that we might thus become the righteousness in him, 2 Cor. 5, last. It is therefore evident from this very solution that what the Photinians frequently have in their mouths is not simply true: namely, that one cannot die for another: For this is true according to strict justice, but not according to equity, the nature of which is such that the guilt of one or more can be transferred to one individual: just as in human affairs the Son of a Prince or of some King can transfer the guilt of many subjects onto himself, and expiate it before the Father, according to equity, but not according to strict Law. Finally, even if it were entirely without all these reasons: yet let human curiosity be silent, and lead reason captive under the obedience of faith, because all the works of GOD, however unsearchable to us, are Equity and Judgment. Psalm 66:3 and Psalm 111:7 & 8.

But the heretics press at this point and object that passage from Ezekiel 18:20: The soul that has sinned, it shall die: Which sentence is also contained in the law of GOD itself. Deut. 24:16. Therefore Socinus infers in part 3, chapter 3, p. 251 & 253: The Son, who is a person most closely joined to the Father, ought not, according to the judgment of GOD, to die for the sins of others, that is, in the stead or place of others.

Some respond to this argument that that Prophetic oracle is to be understood of the Law, but not of the Gospel: and therefore it is true according to the Law that Christ could not expiate the sins of others by his death: but that this is false according to the Gospel. Which response would indeed perhaps easily solve this knot, if only that which is presupposed could be admitted: namely, that GOD the Father laid the sins of us all upon the Son, and that the Son died for our sins according to the Gospel. Which assertion is indeed rather harsh, and fights diametrically against the nature and proper office of the Gospel specifically so called, and insofar as it is opposed to the Law as a contrary: since according to the voice and preaching of the Gospel, no one is adjudged to death, nor even sustains death, either on account of his own sins or those of others: but this happens simply according to the Law. For although the Death of Christ, by reason of its saving end, involves a respect to divine Mercy, and thus pertains to the Gospel: yet it is not directly or properly disputed in this place concerning this respect: But this is asked: Whether Christ sustained the punishments due to our sins according to the Law, or according to the Gospel? Where it is answered very ignorantly: That this was done according to the Gospel out of the mercy of GOD. For that our sins were laid upon Christ, that was of divine and indeed Legal Justice, which required that the human race, either by itself or through another, should satisfy the curse of the law and divine Justice. Hence Christ is said to have been made subject to the law, that he might redeem those who were under the curse of the law, Gal. 4:5. Therefore, dismissing this response, we think it is more correctly answered by a distinction between strict or supreme Law, and equity, which is subordinate to the Law. In the former respect certainly, if indeed GOD had wished to deal with the human race according to strict Law, then certainly no one else could have satisfied for it: but we ourselves would have had to fulfill the Law, or perish eternally. The seventh argument of the Photinians is thus formulated by Socinus in part 3, chapter 3, p. 251: It is unjust and monstrous, which not even men, however barbaric and cruel, do, to exact punishments from the innocent in the place of the guilty, with the guilty themselves being voluntarily released. But GOD is not unjust and monstrous. Therefore he did not exact punishments from the innocent Christ in our place: and therefore Christ did not die in our stead or place.

I respond: The major proposition is true in a certain respect, but not absolutely. For there can be certain conditions, in respect of which the punishment and guilt of the guilty can be transferred to the innocent: as when 1. the innocent one transfers some guilt onto himself not by compulsion, but voluntarily. 2. He is endowed with such powers that he can not only sustain the punishment, but also emerge from it by his own virtue. 3. When he seeks death not for private advantage, but for the salvation of those for whom he suffers. 4. When he can perform this work without injury to divine justice, which happens if he himself is clearly immune from all personal guilt. With these conditions joined together, that equity can have a place, so that the innocent can die for the guilty, without any loss to himself or injury to divine justice: so that it is not of monstrosity or cruelty, but of the immense wisdom and mercy of GOD, that one died for all, and in that one all died, 2 Cor. 5:14. But the adversaries reply: If God wished to testify to His immense mercy in this way, He testified to it much more clearly by deciding to remit the sins of men without any satisfaction.

I reply that the adversaries are talking nonsense: for it is not what seems so to us, but what Scripture affirms, that must be affirmed concerning the mercy of God. Furthermore, this objection would only hold if sins could have been remitted to us by the sole mercy of God, without regard for His justice; but the contrary has just been demonstrated to the eye above in the exposition of the first and second controversies. Whence we conclude that God could not have remitted sins to us without the intervention of a plenary satisfaction: not indeed because of any impotence, but because of the most absolute perfection of the divine nature, which, just as it could not lie, so it could not resign its justice without satisfaction. For this sentence of God stood unmoved: You shall die the death: To which the human race was simply subject, nor could it be freed from its rigor otherwise than by either its own or another's satisfaction.

The eighth argument of the Photinians attacks that point most especially, that we affirm that Christ rendered perfect obedience to the divine law. They deny this themselves, relying chiefly on three quibbles: First, they say that there is no word in the sacred writings about the law being fulfilled by Christ, or even that it was fulfilled; nay, rather the contrary, that men themselves can indeed love God with their whole heart, etc. Then, that Christ Himself was bound to fulfill the law for Himself: therefore not for others. Finally, that the curse of the law was eternal death: but now, since Christ did not undergo eternal death, they infer that He did not undergo or sustain the curse of the law for us.

I reply that these arguments also collapse through their own impiety and futility: For the first fails by a manifest crime of falsehood: for it is read many times in the Scriptures that Christ had to fulfill the law for us, nay, that He did fulfill it, as in Rom. 8:2, The law of the Spirit of life, which is in Christ Jesus, has freed me from the law of sin and death, verse 3, For what the law could not do, in that it was weak through the flesh, God sending His own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh, and for sin, condemned sin in the flesh, verse 4, That the righteousness of the law might be fulfilled in us. Gal. 3:13, Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us. Gal. 4:4 & 5, When the fullness of the time was come, God sent forth His Son, made of a woman, made under the law, to redeem them that were under the law. The second argument is manifestly impious and blasphemous. For that Christ was bound for Himself to fulfill the law, and like other men had to satisfy it for Himself, is prodigiously blasphemous. For although Scripture affirms that Christ was subject to the law, it always expressly adds that this was done not for His own sake, but for our sake, so that He might redeem not Himself, but us from the law. And where there is no transgression of the law, there is no need for any fulfillment of the law. But Christ was devoid of all sin. Therefore, the curse of the law had no claim upon Him. Thus, Scripture indeed asserts that Christ was bound to render obedience to the Father: but at the same time it explains that this very obedience was rendered to the divine law not for Himself, but in our place. Whence He Himself exclaims in Ps. 69:5: What I did not steal, I restored. And Isa. 43:24 & 25. You have made me serve in your sins, you have made me labor in your iniquities: I, even I, am He who blots out your transgressions for my own sake.

Latin:

SEXTA hæreticorum ratio talis est: Nullâ lege aut consuetudine unquam receptum fuit, ut unus pro altero, alterius quasi vice & loco moreretur neque etiam mors unius, alterius mors effici potest. Ergò neque CHRISTUS vice nostri, aut loco nostro respectu Satisfactionis alicujus mortuus esse, censendus est.

Sed fallit & hoc argumentum: 1. Petitione Principii. Quòd si enim integer formetur Syllogismus, major talis deprehendetur: Nihil aliud de morte Christi est statuendum, quàm quod consuetudine communi, & lege humanâ est receptum ac approbatum. Quæ sanè propositio manifestè falsa est, & laborat insuper τῷ ἔξω τοῦ ἐλλειπές: Addi enim debebat: Nihil est de morte Christi statuendum, nisi quod verbo DEI est definitum. Deindè Minor propositio non est Universaliter vera. Multos enim pro aliis, hoc est, vice ac loco aliorum mortem oppetiisse, neque legibus humanis id improbatum fuisse, historiæ Romanorum luculenter evincunt. Quid quòd in Sacris illustre admodùm hujus rei exemplum legere licet, 2. Sam. 21, 1. & seqq. Nam cùm fames satis dura integro triennio terram, ob crudelitatem ac perfidiam Saulis contra Gibeonitas, miserrimè afflixisset, legitur David, ad petitionem Gibeonitarum, septem viros sive adolescentes ex posteritate Saulis crucifixisse. Quo facto DEUS terræ placatus fuisse legitur, vers. 14. Ubi sanè verissimum erat, quòd septem isti viri, vice ac loco reliquorum Israëlitarnm ne fame perirent, mortui sint. Sed si vel maximè vera esset Minor in humanis, falsissima tamen evaderet in mysterio redemptionis, Nam jam modò in Refutatione Rationis tertiæ ex 2. Corinth. 5, 14. demonstravimus, Christum ita vice nostri mortuum esse, ut nos omnes in ipso mortui simus. Sic idem Apostolus Rom. 5, 6. & 7. maximam testatur dissimilitudinem intercedere morti Christi cum iis, qui pro alterius salute mortem oppetunt. Christus, inquiens, pro impijs mortuus est, vix pro justo aliquis moritur: nam pro bono forsitan aliquis mori sustineat : DEUS autem commendat charitatem suam erga nos, quòd cùm adhuc peccatores, vel ut versu 10. loquitur: cùm adhuc inimici ipsius essemus, Christus pro nobis mortuus est.

dum fuisset. Et de hoc respectu agit oraculum Propheticum, quod usque adeò verum est, ut ne quidem jam post præstitam Satisfactionem Christi, ullus pro altero damnetur, sed omnis anima infidelis per se moriatur. Cæterùm posteriore respectu, & secundum Ἐπιείκειαν, quod definitur admirando illo temperamento Justitiæ & misericordiæ DEI, potuit Anima Christi, quæ non peccavit, mori pro hominibus, qui peccarunt: dùm nimirùm æternus Pater Cœlestis videns legem ab hominibus impleri, suæq; Justitiæ satisfieri haud posse, sic strictum illud suum Jus temperavit, ut Filium, qui non noverat peccatum, pro nobis faceret peccatum, ut sic nos Justitia fieremus in ipso, 2. Cor. 5, ult. Patet proindè ex hac ipsa solutione, non simpliciter verum esse illud, quod Photiniani subindè in ore habent: nempè, unum pro altero non posse mori: Verum enim hoc est secundum ἀκριβοδίκαιον, non verò secundum ἐπιείκειαν, cujus ea est natura, ut culpa unius vel plurium derivari possit in unum aliquod individuum: quemadmodum in humanis Filius Principis vel Regis alicujus, multorum subditorum culpam in se derivare, & apud Patrem expiare potest, secundum Ἐπιείκειαν, non verò secundum Jus strictum. Tandem si vel maximè absq; rationibus istis omnibus esset: tamen conticescat curiositas humana, & Rationem sub obsequium fidei captivam ducat, propterea quòd universa opera DEI, quantumvis nobis impervestigabilia, sunt Æquitas & Judicium. Psal. 66, 3. & Psal. 111, 7. & 8.

Sed instant hoc loco hæretici & obvertunt illud Jezech. 18.20. Anima quæ peccaverit, ipsa morietur: Quæ sententia in ipsa quoq, lege DEI contineatur. Deut. 24, 16. Ergò infert Socinus part. 3. cap. 3. p. 251. & 253. Filius, qui est Patri conjunctissima persona non debuit ex sententia DEI pro aliorum peccatis, hoc est, vice sive loco aliorum mori.

Respondent ad hoc argumentum aliqui, intelligendum esse oraculum illud Propheticum de Lege, non verò de Evangelio: ac proindè secundum Legem verum esse, quòd Christus aliorum peccata, morte sua expiare non potuerit: falsum verò hoc esse secundum Evangelium. Quæ sanè responsio facilè fortassis nodum istum solveret, si modò illud, quod præsupponitur, admitti posset: nempè DEUM Patrem imposuisse Filio omnium nostrûm peccata, Filiumq; mortuum esse pro peccatis nostris secundum Evangelium. Quæ sanè assertio duriuscula est, & cum natura & proprio officio Evangelii specificè sic dicti, & quatenùs illud Legi ἀντιδιηρημένως opponitur, è diametro pugnat: siquidem secundum vocem atque concionem Evangelii, nemo quisquam vel propter sua, vel propter aliorum peccata morti adjudicatur, vel mortem etiam sustinet: sed hoc simpliciter fit secundum Legem. Etsi enim Mors Christi, ratione finis salutaris, involvit respectum Misericordiæ divinæ, & sic ad Evangelium pertinet: tamen de hoc respectu hoc loco non directè aut propriè controvertitur : Sed illud quæritur: An Christus pœnas peccatis nostris debitas sustinuerit, secundum Legem, an verò secundum Evangelium? ubi perquàm inscitè respondetur: Factum hoc esse secundum Evangelium de misericordia DEI. Nam quòd Christo imposita sunt peccata nostra, illud Justitiæ divinæ & quidem Legalis erat, quæ requirebat, ut Genus humanum vel per se, vel per alium legis maledictioni, & Justitiæ divinæ satisfaceret. Hinc Christus dicitur legi factus esse subditus, ut eos qui sub legis maledictione erant, redimeret Gal. 4, 5. Proindè missâ hac responsione, rectiùs responderi arbitramur per distinctionem inter Jus strictum sive summum, & inter Ἐπιείκες, quod Legi est subordinatum. Priore certè respectu, si nimirùm DEUS secundum Jus strictum cum genere humano agere voluisset, tùm certè nemo alius pro eo satisfacere potuisset: sed nobis ipsis vel Lex implenda, vel æternùm pereunSeptima ratio Photinianorum sic informatur à Socino part. 3. cap. 3. p. 251. Injustum & immane est, quod ne homines quidem, quantumvis barbari & truculenti faciunt, de innocentibus nocentium loco, ipsis nocentibus sponte dimissis, pœnas sumere. Atqui DEUS injustus & immanis non est. Ergò à Christo innocente nostro loco pœnas non sumpsit: ac proindè Christus nostrâ vice aut loco non est mortuus.

Respondeo: Majorem propositionem veram esse κατὰ τὶ, non verò ἁπλῶς. Dari enim possunt certę cõditiones, quarum respectu in innocentes pœna & culpa nocentium derivari potest: ut quando 1. innocens ille non coactè, sed sponte reatum aliquem in se derivat. 2. Ejusmodi viribus est præditus, ut non modò pœnam possit sustinere, sed & ex illa propria virtute emergere. 3. Quando non commodi privati, sed in salutem eorum, pro quibus patitur, mortem appetit. 4. Quando sine læsione justitiæ divinæ hoc opus peragere potest, id quod fit, si ipse planè ab omni culpâ propria sit immunis. Hisce conditionibus simul junctis Ἐπιείκεια illa locum obtinere potest, ut innocens pro nocentibus mori possit, sine ullo vel sui dispendio, vel divinæ justitiæ jactura: ita ut non immanitatis aut truculentiæ, sed immensæ DEI & sapientiæ & misericordiæ sit, quòd unus pro omnibus mortuus, & in illo uno omnes mortui, 2. Cor. 5, 14. Sed regerunt Adversarij: Si hoc pacto Deus immensam suam misericordiam testari voluit: multo clarius eam testatus est, quod sine ulla Satisfactione hominibus peccata remittere constituit.

Respondeo, Adversarios nugari: Non enim quod nobis videtur, sed quod Scriptura affirmat, de misericordia Dei affirmari debet. Deinde tum demum haec instantia subsisteret, si ex sola Dei misericordia, sine intuitu Justitiae ipsius, peccata nobis remitti potuissent: sed diversum jam modo supra in diexodo primae & secundae Controversiae ad oculum demonstratum est. Unde concludimus, Deum non potuisse sine interventu plenariae Satisfactionis nobis remittere peccata: non quidem ob impotentiam aliquam, sed ob absolutissimam Naturae divinae perfectionem, quae, uti non mentiri, sic neque Justitiae suae, sine Satisfactione resignare potuit: Stabat enim immota haec sententia Dei: Morte Morieris: Cui simpliciter Genus humanum subjacebat, neque ab ejus rigore aliter, quam vel propria, vel aliena Satisfactione liberari poterat.

Octava ratio Photinianorum illud potissimum impugnat, quod Christum legi divinae perfectam obedientiam praestitisse affirmamus. Hoc ipsi negant, tribus potissimum freti argutationibus: Primum enim dicunt, quod de Lege per Christum implenda, vel etiam impleta, nullum verbum extet in sacris: imo contrarium potius, quod nimirum ipsi homines possint Deum diligere ex toto corde &c. Deinde quod Christus ipse devinctus fuerit, Legem pro seipso adimplere: Ergo non pro alijs. Tandem quod Legis execratio fuerit mors aeterna: Jam vero, cum Christus mortem aeternam non subjerit: ideo neque execrationem legis pro nobis ipsum subijsse aut sustinuisse, inferunt.

Respondeo, has quoque rationes propria & impietate & futilitate concidere: Nam prima fallit manifesto crimine falsi: Christum enim Legem pro nobis implere debuisse, imo implevisse, multoties in Sacris legitur, ut Rom. 8, 2. Lex Spiritus vitae, qui est in Christo Jesu, liberavit me a Lege peccati & mortis, vers. 3 Nam quae Legis erat impotentia, cum per carnem infirmabatur, Deus Filium suum mittens in similitudine Carnis peccati, idq; pro peccato condemnavit peccatum in Carne, vers. 4. Ut Jus Legis impleretur in nobis. Gal. 3, 13. Christus nos redemit a maledictione Legis, factus pro nobis maledictum Gal. 4, 4. & 5. Ubi venit plenitudo temporis, misit Deus Filium suum, factum ex muliere, & legi subditum, ut eos, qui sub lege erant, redimeret. Altera ratio est manifeste impia & blasphema. Christum enim pro sese devinctum fuisse ad legem adimplendam, & aliorum hominum instar pro semetipso illi Satisfaciendum, prodigiose blasphemum est. Etsi enim Scriptura affirmat, Christum subjectum fuiffe Legi: tamen disertè semper adjicit, non propter se, sed nostri causa hoc factum fuisse, ut non se, sed nos à Lege redimeret.
