### Chapter II. Of the attributes: II. Controversy, on the Lutheran Church: Namely, what sort and where did it exist under the Papacy before the rise of Luther?

It is established from those things which we have already disputed concerning the first attribute of the Church, that the Church of Christ never perishes or fails entirely: and this is settled on both our part and that of the Pontiffs. and beyond doubt: It is agreed between us and them that that Church is αναμφισβητήτως (indisputably) the true Church which truly enjoys this praise of antiquity and duration; and conversely, that the false one is that which is new and bears no traces of antiquity. Hence, it is keenly disputed today between us and the Jesuits: Which of these two Churches, namely the Roman and the Lutheran, is the most ancient, and therefore undoubtedly the true one? The Romanists arrogate this title to themselves: but we contend that it is proper to our Church. Nor is this question entirely without difficulty; so that it may be explained more accurately, it must be well noted at the beginning what can, or rather what even ought to be called Old, and what New, in this dispute? We therefore define the Old to be, not that which has lasted for six or seven, or even more centuries, like the Papal Mass, the Invocation of the dead, the Poetic and Platonic Purgatory, Papal Traditions, and other dogmas of the Romanists of that kind. For concerning these there is deep silence in the Holy Scriptures, and not even a trace is found. How then can they be the property of the most ancient Religion? That can rather be affirmed of them which Paul has: Old things have passed away, and behold all things have become new. Following therefore the Holy Scriptures, we define the Old, nay the Most Ancient, and the first of all, and therefore the Truest doctrine and Religion, to be that which began immediately after the fall of our first parents in Paradise itself, concerning the Seed of the woman, who would crush the head of the serpent, Gen. 3:15, and was afterwards propagated in turn through the Patriarchs and Prophets; and was finally confirmed by Christ with clearly divine miracles, and was disseminated by the Apostles throughout the whole world. The sum and argument of this doctrine is this one thing: The blessed Seed, in whom all the nations of the earth are to be blessed, is the one and only Christ, Gal. 3:16, to whom all the Prophets bear witness, that all who believe in him receive remission of sins through his name, Acts 10:43. and indeed without the works of the law, as the Council of the Apostles at Jerusalem defined, with this golden Canon promulgated; opposed to the pseudo-apostles urging the righteousness of Works: Why do you tempt God, by putting a yoke upon the necks of the disciples, which neither we nor our fathers were able to bear? But we believe that we are saved in the name of Jesus Christ, just as they also are saved: Acts 15:10 and 11. This doctrine and faith was that of all the Patriarchs, all the Prophets, and finally all the Apostles: so that the Apostle does not hesitate to say Anathema even to an Angel from heaven, who should bring another Gospel, Gal. 1:8 and 9. This very doctrine and faith has been, ever since the times of the Apostles, the property of the Holy Fathers and of all pious men, that is, of the Elect, although Satan has endeavored to sprinkle some tares upon it at every time. This very doctrine and faith is the property of our, that is, Lutheran Church; and it is so much its property, that for this reason alone the Romanists hate our Church worse than a dog and a snake, because, having cast off the dross of our own works and merits, having rejected the trifles of worship devised by men, having repudiated our own satisfactions for sin whether for guilt or for punishment, we rest in the one and only seed of the woman, Christ the Savior, we have all our hope of salvation fixed and placed in his merit alone, freely imputed to us through faith, we adore, invoke, and glorify him alone with the Father and the Holy Spirit: from him alone we undoubtedly expect deliverance from all troubles and calamities, consolation, and finally eternal life. Let the whole Christian world now judge whether the doctrine and faith of our Church is new or rather old, nay most ancient: nay, let the Romanists themselves judge, and explain whether we hold another, new, and different foundation of faith from that which we have already demonstrated above that the Patriarchs, Prophets, and Apostles held. Now as for the other parts of divine worship which are observed in the Lutheran Churches, certainly nothing new occurs anywhere. For we do not have new Bibles: but those Old ones, which the universal Church of all times has acknowledged and venerated as Canonical: we do not have a new Baptism, or one different from that which was instituted by Christ: We do not have a new Supper of the Lord, we do not mutilate it, we do not celebrate it otherwise than as Christ himself administered it; We do not convert it to other Idolatrous or superstitious ends or uses, or ones that fight diametrically against Scripture: We do not have a new form of Absolution, or one different from that which we read that Christ himself and the Apostles used, the sum of which is: Take heart, son, all your sins are forgiven you: And that other: If you believe, and are baptized, you shall be saved: We do not invent new Symbols of the Church, but we firmly embrace those old ones, the Apostolic, the Nicene, the Athanasian, and we prefer them by far to any other confessions or Symbolic books. Finally, nothing new can be shown in our Churches concerning the worship of God. As for the rites and Ceremonies used in our Churches, we abhor all those to which an opinion of worship, or merit, or absolute necessity is attached: On the contrary, however, from the use of Christian liberty we freely observe those which make πρὸς τάξιν καὶ ἐυσχημοσύνην (for order and decency), as the Apostle commands in 1 Cor. 14, v. last, and which, according to the observations of Augustine, are easy, pleasant, pious, and useful.

And such indeed is our Church, commonly called Lutheran: more correctly Apostolic, Catholic. Now we must look in a few words at what kind of Church the Romanists have: but behold, Old things have passed away, and all things have become new 2 Cor. 5:17. It is new and simply unknown to true antiquity that a man is justified before God not in the name or merit of Christ alone, but also in our works, and indeed by merit. It is a novelty, and one plainly and contradictorily opposed to the Apostolic Canon promulgated in the Council of Jerusalem, that a man can by his own powers bear the yoke of the Law, nay, satisfy the Law of God: It is a novelty that the authority of the Church is greater than that of Holy Scripture: It is a novelty that the Holy Scriptures are adapted to the times, and variously understood, so that at one time they ought to be expounded according to the current rite of the Universal Church: that with the rite changed, the meaning of Scripture also changes: nay, that at one time in one way, at another time in another way, Scripture is explained:

as Nicolaus Cusanus did not shrink from writing in his 2nd and 7th Epistles to the Bohemians. It is a novelty that the Holy Scriptures should have no more validity than Aesop's Fables unless the authority of the Church were added to them: as Hosius attempts to defend against Dr. Brentius, book 3 on the authority of Scripture. It is a novelty that the Holy Spirit cannot refute any heresy through the Holy Scriptures: as Gretser blasphemed at Ratisbon. It is a novelty that the Roman Pontiff is the Head of the Universal Church as the vicar of Christ: that he holds all laws in the cabinet of his breast: that he has the same Consistory as God: that he has authority over the Angels themselves and over the four Gospels: that he cannot err in matters of faith when he speaks ex cathedra, etc. As the Canon law has produced almost countless new paradoxes of this kind, and ones that are plainly stupendous by the very birth of their words. It is a novelty that Baptism should be conferred even upon bells, so that they may obtain the power to drive away lightning and thunder and other storms. It is a novelty (as the Council of Constance itself admits) that the use of the Eucharistic Sacrament should be granted to the laity under one species only, but to the Mass-priests under both. It is a novelty that the Sacraments confer grace ex opere operato. It is a novelty that the Sacrament of the Supper is a propitiatory Sacrifice. It is a novelty that the body of Christ must be offered daily in an unbloody manner to God the Father for the sins, punishments, and faults of the dead and the living. It is a novelty that each and every sin committed in any way, whether by words, deeds, or thoughts, must be recounted in detail to the Priest; indeed, even the individual circumstances of the sins that could have changed the nature of the act. It is a novelty that the power of Absolution depends on the dignity and intention of the Priest. It is a novelty that a man can satisfy God for the punishments of sins, both eternal and temporal. It is a novelty that indulgences for sins can be sold and redeemed for a certain price. It is a novelty that perpetual celibacy must be observed by priests. It is a novelty that the Virgin Mary and the Saints must be invoked, and that their merits can benefit those who invoke them for eternal life. And what, I pray, can be given or shown that is truly proper to the Roman Church which is not new and unknown to the entire primitive and Apostolic Antiquity?

Let the whole Christian world now judge again and pass sentence: Does the title of primitive and Apostolic Antiquity belong by any right to the Roman Church, such as it has been for many centuries past and such as it still is today? There is certainly no doubt that this title can no more be attributed to it than the dignity and honor of an undefiled virgin can be bestowed upon a most impure prostitute.

Some of the Romanists object that the Antiquity of the Church should not be sought so precisely from conformity with the Apostolic Church, but that it is enough if conformity is sought from the state of other churches that immediately followed the Apostolic one.

But here lies the snake in the grass, which, in order to crush it thoroughly, we must proceed in an orderly and distinct manner. And first, I ask, what is the cause that the Romanists cannot bear the example of the Apostolic Church? Does this not most strongly argue their cauterized conscience, namely, that they are convinced within and in their hearts that if the judgment of the Antiquity and Truth of the Church is to be sought from conformity with the Apostolic Church, then the palm of Antiquity belongs entirely not to their church but to ours? Furthermore, what kind of monster is this, that they clamor that greater account should be taken of the daughter than of the mother, of the later church than of the primitive one and the very matrix, as it were, of all churches? This is, indeed, to pierce all the authority of the primitive Apostolic Church with a single obelisk. Every prudent person easily understands by what right, by what faith, or rather by what perfidy this is done.

Latin:

COnstat ex ijs quæ de primo Ecclesiæ attributo jam disputavimus, Ecclesiam Christi nunquàm intercidere aut penitùs deficere: estque hoc ex utraque tàm nostra, quàm Pontificiorum parte, ratum & indubium: Constat & illud inter nos & ipsos, illam Ecclesiam αναμφισβητήτως esse veram Ecclesiam, quæ vetustatis & durationis hujus laude, verè gaudet: falsam contra, quæ nova est, & nulla antiquitatis legit vestigia. Hinc acriter inter nos & Jesuvvitas hodiè controvertitur: Utra inter duas istas Ecclesias, Romanam videlicet & Lutheranam, sit antiquissima, ac proindè indubitatò vera? Romanenses hoc Elogium sibi arrogant: Nos verò nostræ Ecclesiæ proprium illud esse contendimus. Neque planè omni difficultate caret hæc quæstio; quæ ut accuratiùs explicetur, probè initiò, attendendum fuerit, quid hac in disputatione Vetus, & quid Novum dici possit, imò verò etiam debeat? Vetus igitur definimus esse, non quod sex vel septem, vel pluribus etiam seculis duravit, sicut Missa Pontificia, Invocatio defunctorum, Purgatorium Poeticum & Platonicum, Traditiones Pontificiæ, & id genus alia Romanensium dogmata. De his enim in Scripturis Sacris altum est silentium, & negry quidem reperitur. Quomodo ergò antiquissimæ Religionis possint esse propria? Id potiùs de illis affirmari potest, quod Paulus habet: Vetera transierunt, & ecce facta sunt omnia nova. Scripturas proindè sacras secuti, Veterem imò Vetustissimam, omniumqué primam, ac proindè Verissimam doctrinam & Religionem definimus eam, quæ mox post lapsum protoparentum in ipso Paradiso cœpit, de Semine mulieris, contrituro caput serpentis, Genes. 3, 15. postmodùm verò per Patriarchas, & Prophetas subindè propagata: ac tandem à Christo miraculis planè divinis confirmata, ab Apostolis verò in universum terrarum orbem disseminata fuit. Doctrinæ autem hujus summa & argumentum est unicum istud: Semen benedictum, in quo benedicendæ sunt omnes gentes terræ, est solus & Unus Christus, Galat. 3, 16. cui testimonium perhibent omnes Prophetæ, quòd Remissionem peccatorum accipiunt per nomen ejus, Omnes, qui credunt in eum, Actor. 10, 43. & quidem sine operibus legis, sic definiente Hierosolymis Concilio Apostolorú, aureò hôc pro mulgatô Canone; pseudoapostolis justitiam Operum urgentibus, opposito: Quid tentatis Deum, imponentes jugum Legis, super cervices discipulorum, quod nequè nos, neq; Patres nostri portare potuimus: Sed credimus in nomine Jesu Christi nos salvari quemadmodum & illi salvati sunt: Act. 15, 10. & 11. Hæc doctrina & fides fuit omnium Patriarcharum, omnium Prophetarum, omnium deniq; Apostolorum: ita ut Apostolus etiam Angelo de cœlo Anathema dicere haud dubitet, qui aliud Evangelium attulerit, Galat. 1, 8. & 9. Hæc ipsa doctrina & fides jam indè ab Apostolorum temporibus, Sanctorum Patrum & piorum quorumvis, h. e. Electorum fuit propria licet nullo non tempore Zizaniorum aliquid ei aspergere Sathanas studuerit. Hæc ipsa doctrina & fides nostræ, h. e. Lutheranæ Ecclesiæ propria; & usq; adeò est propria, ut ob id solùm Romanenses, nostram Ecclesiam cane & angue pejus oderint, quôd explosis propriorum operum ac meritorum scorijs, rejectis cultuú humanitûs excogitatorum quisquilijs, repudiatis proprijs nostris pro peccati sivè culpâ sivè pœnâ satisfactionibus, in uno & solo semine mulieris Christo Servatore acquiescimus, in solo ipsius merito, gratis nobis per fidem imputato, spem salutis omnem fixam locatamq́; habemus, ipsum solum cum Patre & Spiritu S. adoramus, invocamus, glorificamus : ab ipso solo liberationem ex omnibus ærumnis & calamitatibus, solatium, & tandem vitam æternam indubitatò exspectamus. Judicet jam universus orbis Christianus, nùm nova an verò antiqua imò antiquissima nostræ Ecclesiæ sit doctrina fidesque: imò judicent ipsi Romanenses, & edisserant, nùm aliud, novum ac diversum fidei fundamentum teneamus ab eo, quod Patriarchas, Prophetas, Apostolos tenuisse, jam supra demonstravimus. Jam quoad cætera cultus divini membra, quæ in Lutheranis Ecclesiis observantur, nihil certè novi uspiam occurrit. Non enim nova habemus Biblia: sed Vetera illa, quæ universalis omnium temporum Ecclesia pro Canonicis agnovit & venerata est : non novum habemus Baptismum, sive diversum ab eo, qui à Christo est institutus : Non novam habemus Cœnam Domini, non eam mutilamus, non alitèr celebramus, quàm prout Christus ipse eam administravit ; Non in fines sive usus alios Idolatricos, aut superstitiosos, aut cum Scriptura è diametro pugnantes, convertimus : Non novam habemus Absolutionis formam, aut diversam ab eâ, quâ Christum ipsum, & Apostolos usos fuisse legimus, cujus hæc est summa: Confide fili, remissa sunt tibi peccata, tua omnia : Et illa altera: Si credis, & baptizatus fueris, salvaberis: Non nova Ecclesiæ Symbola confingimus, sed vetera illa, Apostolicum, Nicenum, Athanasianum, firmiter amplectimur, & quibusvis alijs confessionibus, sive libris Symbolicis longè anteferimus. Non denique novi quicquam circa cultum Dei, nostris in Ecclesijs monstrari potest. Quoad ritus verò & Ceremonias nostris Ecclesijs usitatas, abhorremus ab omnibus illis, quibus vel cultus, vel meriti, vel absolutæ necessitatis opinio affingitur: Contrà verò, ex usu libertatis Christianæ liberè observamus eas, quæ faciunt πρὸς τάξιν καὶ ἐυσχημοσύνην, sic jubente Apostolo 1. Cor. 14. v. ult. quæq́; secundum Augustini observata sunt faciles, jucundæ, piæ, utiles.

Et talis quidem nostra est Ecclesia, Lutherana vulgò dicta: rectiùs Apostolica, Catholica. Nunc qualis Romanensium sit Ecclesia, paucis dispiciendum: sed ecce, Transierunt Vetera, & facta sunt omnia nova 2. Cor. 5, 17. Novum est & veræ antiquitati simpliciter incognitum non in solo nomine sivè merito Christi, sed & in nostris operibus, & quidem de condigno hominem justificari coram Deo. Novum est, & Canoni Apostolico in concilio Hierosolymitano promulgato planè contradictoriè oppositum, Hominem proprijs viribus posse portare Legis jugum, imò Legi Dei satisfacere: Novum est, majorem esse Ecclesiæ, quam Scripturæ S. autoritatē: Novum est Scripturas sacras esse ad tempus adaptatas, & variè intellectas, ita ut uno tempore, secundum currentem Universalis ritum Ecclesiæ exponi debeant: mutato ritu, sententia etiam Scripturæ mutetur: imò ut uno tempore, uno modo; alio tempore, alio modo Scriptura explicetur:

uti Nicolaus Cusanus, scribere non exhorruit, ad Bohemos Epist. 2. & 7. Novum est, Scripturas Sacras haud plus valituras, quàm Fabulæ valeant Æsopicæ, nisi Ecclesiæ accederet authoritas: uti Hosius contra D. Brentium defendere conatur, l. 3. de autor. script. Novum est, Spiritum Sanctum per Scripturas Sacras, non posse ullam refutare hæresin: uti Gretserus Ratisbonæ blasphemavit. Novum est, Pontificem Romanum esse Caput Vniversalis Ecclesiæ, tanquam Christi vicarium: habere omnia jura in scrinio pectoris: habere idem Consistorium cum Deo: habere imperium in ipsos Angelos, & in quatuor Evangelia: in rebus fidei simpliciter errare non posse, quando ex Cathedrâ pronunciat &c. Uti jus Canonicum innumera penè, & ipso saltem verborum fœto planè stupenda, hujus generis nova paradoxa prodidit. Novum est, Baptismum conferendum esse etiam Campanis, ut vim obtineant pellend fulgura ac tonitrua, aliasq́; tempestates. Novum est (fatente ipso Concilio Constantiensi) sub unâ tantum specie, Laicis concedendum usum Sacramenti Eucharistici: Sacrificulis verò Missaticis sub utraque: Novum est, Sacramenta conferre gratiam ex opere operato. Novum est, Sacramentum Cœnæ esse Sacrificium propitiatorium: Novum est, corpus Christi indies incruento modò debere offerri Deo patri, pro peccatis, pœnis & culpis, defunctorum ac viventium: Novum est, singula & universa peccata quocunq́; modo vel dictis, vel factis, vel cogitatis commissa, in specie enarranda esse Sacerdoti: imò singulas etiam peccatorum circumstantias, quæ speciem facti mutare potuerunt. Novum est, Absolutionis vim pendere à dignitate & intentione Sacerdotis. Novum est, Hominem posse Deo satisfacere, pro pœnis peccatorum tùm æternis tùm temporalibus. Novum est, indulgentias peccatorum certo pretio vendi & redimi posse. Novum est, Sacerdotibus perpetuum cœlibatum esse tenendum. Novum est, Mariam virginem & Sanctos esse invocandos: ipsorumq́; merita invocantibus posse prodesse ad vitam æternam. Et quid obsecrò dari aut monstrari possit, quod quidem Romanæ Ecclesiæ sit proprium, quod non novum sit, & toti primævæ ac Apostolicæ Antiquitati incognitum.

Judicet jam rursum totus orbis Christianus, & ferat sententiam, Num Ecclesiæ Romanæ, qualis quidem sub Pontificibus fuit pluribus retrò elapsis seculis, & qualis adhuc hodiè est, competat ullô jure Elogium Antiquitatis primævæ ac Apostolicæ? Nullum profectò dubium est, quin haud magis Elogium hoc illi tribui possit, atque scorto impurissimo, intemeratæ virginis decus ac honor impertiri potest.

Excipiunt Romanensium nonnulli, Antiquitatem Ecclesiæ non usq́; adeò precisè petendam esse, ex conformitate cum Ecclesiâ Apostolicâ: sed satis esse, si conformitas petatur, ex statu aliarum Ecclesiarum, quæ Apostolicam statim sunt infecutæ.

Verùm hîc latet anguis in herba, quem ut penitùs conteramus, ordine & distinctè progrediendum fuerit. Ac initiò quidem quæso causæ fuerit, quòd Romanenses Apostolicæ Ecclesiæ exemplum ferre nequeunt? Annon hoc cauteriatam ipsorum conscientiam fortissimè arguit, quòd nimirùm intùs & in corde sint convicti, si Antiquitatis & Veritatis Ecclesiæ judicium petendum sit, ex conformitate cum Ecclesiâ Apostolicâ; tùm non suæ sed nostræ Ecclesiæ, Antiquitatis palmam omninò deberi. Deindè quid hoc monstri est, quòd majorem Filiæ quàm matris, potiorem posterioris, quàm primævæ & ipsius quasi matricis Ecclesiarum omnium, rationem habendam esse clamitant? Hoc nimirùm est uno obelisco omnem Ecclesiæ primævæ Apostolicæ autoritatem configere. Quod quo jure, quave fide, imò potiùs quâ perfidiâ fiat, prudens quisque facilè intelligit.


### Chapter II. Of the attributes: II. Controversy, on the Lutheran Church: Namely, what sort and where did it exist under the Papacy before the rise of Luther? (continued)

Thirdly, let the Jesuits explain, I pray, could the exception of the Jews have had any place if, when Christ and the Apostles were disputing from Moses about the kingdom of the Messiah, about his office, about the abrogation of Circumcision and the entire Ceremonial law, about the Calling of the Gentiles, etc., they had objected that they were not precisely urging the authority of Moses, but that the Truth of the doctrine should be sought from the state of subsequent times, under the Israelite kings, when the Law had failed with the Priest and all the watchmen of the people were blind (2 Chron. 15:3)? I think they will answer in the negative. Let them remember, therefore, that the same must be established regarding their own exception. Finally, they strive to object to us such a mark of Antiquity from which nothing certain can be judged. For since, soon after the times of the Apostles, most grievous persecutions overtook the Church of God and harassed it in a horrible manner, it happened that heretics, and indeed even the Antichrist himself, gradually broke into the Church more and more, and with various mists of errors sought to obscure its illustrious face, and thus to lead it away from the genuine Apostolic purity and simplicity to the deviations of superstitions and human worships, and to cast the seeds of the Antichristian kingdom into the very bosom of the Church. Thus, therefore, they imagine that they can hide themselves more safely under the covering of this later church than under Apostolic conformity; a very cunning, but futile, plan.

Cast down from this first stronghold, the Romanists seek another and ask: Where in the Christian world was there a church after the times of the Apostles that taught the same thing that the Lutheran Church teaches today? Indeed, they are accustomed to rise against us thus: If Luther's doctrine and church are true, it follows that before his emergence there was no true Church of Christ on earth, because no such church existed then; and it would also follow that under the Papacy all were damned. But both of these are absurd, and indeed manifestly false, since the true Church never fails entirely. Now, in fact, the Lutheran Church did not exist then. Therefore, it is not the true Church.

But I reply that the connection of the major premise labors under a shameful ἀνακολουϑία: and this in many ways. 1. Because they suppose that in previous centuries no Church existed except the Roman: 2. Because they feign that the Lutheran Church began only then, when the blessed Luther began and perfected that blessed work of evangelical reformation not yet a hundred years ago. Where a sophistry of equivocation is also involved in the phrase, before the rise of the Lutheran doctrine: which phrase, if it be taken concerning the reformation and illustration of the Evangelical doctrine, previously obscured by the errors of the Romanists, nay, horribly corrupted: then we willingly admit it: and we readily concede that this Reformation does not yet exceed one hundred years. But if, in the Jesuitical sense, this phrase be understood concerning the first beginnings and as it were the first foundations of our doctrine, then we simply reject and deny it. The foundations of which negative of ours, that they may be able to stand against the insults of the Romanists, must be evidently demonstrated and confirmed by us in two points. FIRST: That at all times, even from the age of the Apostles, there have been those who held the same doctrine which the Churches of the Lutherans hold and defend today: and that the Papacy has never pervaded and infected the whole Christian world. Which being demonstrated, it will be a consequence, even if it were the case that no one had been saved under the universal Papacy: if also there had been no True Church in the Papacy: both of which, however, we deny: that the Church of Christ had not therefore utterly expired or failed in the world. LATTER: That under the Papacy itself, nay, in the midst of the Papacy, however much pressed and overwhelmed by the far densest darkness of errors, there was nevertheless a true Church, clearly of one mind with our Lutheran Church in the matter of salvation: although the Papacy itself was not that true Church: and consequently that very many were saved under the Papacy.

Concerning the First: After the times of the Apostles, for the first two hundred years, the Church of God publicly held and defended that kind of Christian doctrine which agrees entirely with the Lutheran dogma; as is evident from the writings of Ignatius, who admits no Transubstantiation at all, much less that sacrilegious mutilation of the Supper: he is also clearly ignorant of private Masses: but he defines public ones only through the legitimate dispensation of the Eucharistic Sacrament, as can be evidently demonstrated. Irenæus followed Ignatius in this first century: to whose writings we also fearlessly appeal. Thus, regarding the second century from the death of the Apostles, although we do not deny that in the books and writings of Clement of Alexandria, Tertullian, Cyprian, Origen, and Adamantius, many things are contained that conflict with the analogy of faith, which we cannot approve, nay, which are not even approved by the Romanists themselves in every respect: yet those errors were not then publicly received into the Church, nor did they establish the Primacy of the Roman Pontiff in any part: so much so that Cyprian, in Book 1, Epistle 3, quite gravely rebukes Cornelius, because, moved by the threats and terrors of heretics, he had received letters from them, and had not rather sent them back to their own Bishop in Africa: since it has been decreed by all Bishops that the case of each one should be heard there where the crime had been committed. He asserts likewise that the authority of the Bishops in Africa is no less than that of those who had heard their case at Rome. And such indeed was the face of the Church for the two first centuries after the death of the Apostles, in every way conformable to the Lutheran kind of public doctrine.

Although indeed in the subsequent centuries the Devil strove to work, propagate, and perfect more and more the mystery of iniquity, which he had begun to plot while the Apostles themselves were still living, with various abuses scattered here and there, which afterwards, collected as it were into one Body, completely perfected the Pontifical Idolomania: a thing which we know happened around the six hundredth year of Christ, by the miserable fate of the Church: so that if you look at the external form of the Church, the abominations of abuses and superstitions, the greatest conformity existed and exists today between those Churches and the Roman Pontifical one: yet there were not lacking in those times also Doctors of the Church who, even publicly, contradicted the then-rampant errors of the Pontifical Idolomania: as may be seen and known in the Catalogue of the witnesses of Truth.

Thirdly, from the six hundredth year of Christ, with the growing dominion of the Roman Pontiff, the purity of religion so decreased that if you had looked at the external form of the Church, at the abominations of the dogmas, at the abyss of abuses and superstitions, you would scarcely have detected any shadow of the purity and simplicity of the Apostolic and more ancient Church. Where, however, even then the Church of God did not fail, but lay hidden: with many thousands meanwhile surviving, who did not bow their knees before the Pontifical Roman Baal: as the exposition of the following second question will show more fully.

Fourthly, even if the Roman Papacy had so filled the whole West that under the Pontifical reign no one of the elect had remained, nor anyone had been saved under it: the Church of God would not therefore have failed entirely. For the Papacy did not occupy the whole world: but only the West: it never pervaded the East, not even in those times when the Eastern empire began to be wounded. The Church of the Greeks, therefore, although it was entangled in a grave error concerning the Procession of the Holy Spirit from the Father alone, nevertheless in the very foundation of faith and salvation, it remained intact and secure: as it also held in most other Articles of the Christian Religion the same orthodoxy which the Church of the Lutherans holds today: the same Baptism: the same Eucharistic Sacrament, whole and in no way mutilated. Nor do I think the Jesuits will deny that there was always a true Church among the Greeks, as long as it was devoted to Christianity and faithfully dispensed the administration of the Sacraments according to the form of Christ's institution. For wherever Baptism flourishes, sound and whole in respect of its substance, there is the true Church: and consequently true and living members of the Church also. The reason for the connection is: Because Baptism is from the Treasures of the true Church, Eph. 4, 5.

And through Baptism the entrance into the kingdom of Heaven is opened, John 3:5. And Baptism is the washing of regeneration, Tit. 3:5, and an effective instrument for the working of salvation, 1 Pet. 3:21. These things being thus presupposed, I infer against the Jesuits as follows:

If a true Church can be given, which has never approved the dominion of the Roman Papacy, nor ever acknowledged the Roman Pontiff as the head of the Church, nor ever held the Roman Church to be a true Church: It follows, 1. that outside the Roman Papacy in previous centuries, and indeed before the rise of the Blessed Luther, there was a true Church, in the foundation of faith, or at least in that most especially conformable to the Churches of the Lutherans, that it always held the Roman Pontiff and his Synagogue to be the Antichrist and the Church of the malignant: 2. that it is false, what the Jesuits grunt from time to time, that unless the Papacy itself is and was in previous centuries the true Church, then no one in the world could have been saved, and consequently the whole Church had defected.

But such a Church can be given, outside the Papacy: namely, the Oriental Church of the Greeks. Therefore. The assumption consists of two members: The former: that the Greek Church was a true Church: that which we will demonstrate a little later from the Sacrament of Baptism, from the foundation of faith and salvation asserted incorruptly, and from the remaining marks. The latter is: that the Greek, or Oriental Church, has always detested the Roman Papacy: that which can be proven by many evident documents. The Greek Church certainly, through the Patriarch of Constantinople, annually on Invocavit Sunday, publicly proclaimed the Roman Pontiff with his whole Church, by a solemn rite, as a heretic, and struck him with an Anathema. Furthermore, the Greek Church had it as a custom and habit that it would publicly excommunicate a Greek woman or virgin marrying an Italian or Spaniard: and that not, as the Jesuits dream, out of hatred for the Latin Nation, but rather for the Roman or Pontifical Religion. Hence it happened that the Greeks, when their legates whom they had sent to the Lateran Council returned home, cast them out not only from their Church but from all of Greece, because in that Council, being too eager for the society and concord to be established between the Roman and Greek, or Western and Oriental Church, they had consented to certain chapters of Pontifical Idolomania. Concerning which matter, as also other documents of that kind, the Catalog of the Witnesses of Truth can be read with profit. And it is very worthy of remembrance and not at all alien to our purpose, what John Mandeville reports concerning John XXII. the Roman Pontiff, that he wrote quite prolixly and in bombastic words to the Greeks, that there is only one Church, and one head of it, namely Himself, the vicar of Christ: and that all would perish if they did not adhere to so illustrious a head: Wherefore he warned them to repent as soon as possible, and to obey him. But that the Greeks replied briefly in this manner: We firmly believe your supreme power over your subjects: We cannot tolerate your supreme pride: We are unable to satisfy your insatiable avarice: The Devil be with you, because the Lord is with us. See the Catalog of the Witnesses of Truth, part 2, p. 683.

Latin:

Tertiò edisserant obsecrò Jesuitæ, Num locum aliquem habere potuisset exceptio Judæorum, si Christo & Apostolis de regno Messiæ, de ejusdem officio, de Circumcisionis, totiusq́; legis Ceremonialis abrogatione, de Vocatione gentium, &c. ex Mose disputantibus, objecissent: se non præcisè urgere autoritatem Mosis, sed doctrinæ Veritatem petendam esse, ex statu subsequentium temporum, sub regibus Jsraeliticis, ubi defecerat Lex cum Sacerdote, & speculatores populi omnes erant cæci. 2. Paral. 15, 2. Negatè opinor respondebunt. Idem ergò de sua exceptione etiam statuendum esse meminerint. Tandem talem nobis notam Antiquitatis obijcere student, ex qua nihil certi judicari possit. Cùm enim mox post Apostolorum tempora, persecutiones gravissimæ Ecclesiam Dei exceperint, & horrendum in modum exagitaverint, factum, ut Hæretici quoque, imò ipse etiam Antichristus paulatim magis magisque in Ecclesiam irrumperet, varijsque errorum nebulis, illustrem ejus faciem obscurare, & sic à genuinâ Apostolicâ puritate ac simplicitate, ad superstitionum, & cultuum humanorum deviâ abducere: regnique Antichristiani semina in ipso Ecclesiæ gremio proijcere studeret. Sic ergò tutiùs se sub posterioris hujus Ecclesiæ involucro, quàm sub Apostolicâ conformitate, latitare se posse, autumant: astuto perquàm, sed irrito consilio.

Ab hoc primo dejecti præsidio, aliud quærunt Romanenses, & rogitant: Vbinam post Apostolorum tempora fuerit in Orbe Christiano Ecclesia, quæ idem docuerit, quòd hodiè Lutherana doceat Ecclesia. Imò sic contra nos insurgere solent: Si vera est Lutheri doctrina & Ecclesia: sequitur antè ejus exortum, nullam Christi in terris veram fuisse Ecclesiam: quia nulla talis tùm extitit: quin & illud sequeretur, sub Papatu omnes damnatos fuisse. Atqui utrumq́; hoc absurdum, imò manifestè falsum: Siquidem nunquam Vera Ecclesia tota deficit. Iam verò Lutherana Ecclesia tùm non fuit. Ergò illa non est vera Ecclesia.

Sed respondeo Connexum Majoris, turpi ἀνακολουϑία laborare: idq́; multipliciter. 1. quòd autumant, Superioribus seculis, nullam Ecclesiam, præter Romanam extitisse: 2. quod fingunt, Ecclesiam Lutheranam cœpisse tum demum, quando B. Lutherus beatum illud reformationis Evangelicæ opus ante annos nondum centenos, cœpit & perfecit. Ubi æquivocationis etiam Sophisticatio involvitur in phrasi, ante exortum dostrina Lutherana: quæ phrasis si de reformatione & illustratione doctrinæ Evangelicæ, priùs Romanensium erroribus obscuratæ, imò horribiliter corruptæ, accipiatur: tùm libenter eam admittimus: & Reformationem hanc nondùm annos centum excedere, ultrò concedimus. Sin verò sensu Jesuvvitico phrasis hæc de primis initiijs & quasi fundamentis primis nostræ doctrinæ intelligatur, tùm simpliciter eam reijcimus & negamus. Cujus negativæ nostræ fundamenta, ut contra insultus Romanensium subsistere possint, duo nobis evidenter demonstranda & confirmanda sunt. PRIUS: Omnibus temporibus jam indè ab Apostolorum ætate, fuisse, qui eandem doctrinam tenuerint, quam hodiè tenent ac defendunt Lutheranorum Ecclesiæ: nequè Papatum unquàm totum Orbem Christianum pervasisse & infecisse. Quo demonstrato, Consequens erit, si vel maximè sub Papatu universo nemo salvatus fuisset: si etiam nulla in Papatu fuisset Ecclesia Vera: quod utrumque tamen negamus: non tamen propterea prorsus in mundo expirasse aut defecifse Ecclesiam Christi. POSTERIUS: Sub ipso, imò in medio Papatu, quantumvis errorum tenebris longè densissimis presso & obruto, veram tamen fuisse Ecclesiam, nostræ Lutheranæ in negocio salutis plane ὁμοψῆφον: licet Papatus ipse non fuerit illa vera Ecclesia: ac proindè plurimos sub Papatu salvatos fuisse.

De Primo: Post Apostolorum tempora ducentis primis annis Ecclesia Dei illud doctrinæ Christianæ genus publicè tenuit ac defendit, quod cum Lutherano dogmate ex asse concordat; uti patet ex Scriptis Ignatij, qui nullam prorsus Transsubstantiationem, nedùm Sacrilegam illam mutilationem cœnæ admittit: Missas etiam privatas planè ignorat: puplicas verò non nisi per legitimam dispensationem Sacramenti Eucharistici definit, evidenter demonstrari potest. Ignatium seculo hoc primo insecutus est Irenæus: ad cujus scripta nos quoque intrepidè provocamus. Sic quoad alterum seculum ab obitu Apostolorum, etsi non negamus, in libris ac scriptis Clementis Alexandrini, Tertulliani, Cypriani, Origenis, Adamantij, multa contineri cum analogia fidei pugnantia, quæ nos probare non possumus, imò quæ ab ipsis etiam Romanensibus per omnia minimè probantur: errores tamen illi, nondùm tùm publicè in Ecclesiam sunt recepti, neque Primatum Pontificis Romani, ulla ex parte stabiliverunt: adeò ut Cyprianus lib.1. Epist. 3. satis graviter Cornelium reprehendat, quòd minis & terroribus hæreticorum commotus, literas ab eis accepifset, & non potiùs eos remisisset ad suum Episcopum in Africam: cùm statutum sit ab omnibus Episcopis, ut unius cujusque causa illic audiatur, ubi crimen admissum esset. Asserit item, Episcoporum in Africâ non minorem esse autoritatem, quàm eorum, qui Romæ causam illorum cognovissent. Et talis quidem duorum primorum seculorum post Apostolorum obitum Ecclesiæ fuit facies, Lutheranæ quoad publicum doctrinæ genus per omnia conformis.

Quanquam verò subsequentibus seculis Diabolus mysterium iniquitatis, quod ipsis adhuc viventibus Apostolis moliri cœperat, paulatim magis magisque operari, propagare & perficere studuit, sparsis hinc indè varijs abusibꝙ, qui postmodum in unum quasi collecti Corpus, Idolomaniam Pontificiam penitùs absolverunt: id quod circa Annum Christi sexcentesimum, miserabili Ecclesiæ fato factum esse novimus: ita, ut si externam Ecclesiæ formam, abusuum ac superstitionum βδελύγματα spectes, summa conformitas illis Ecclesijs, cum Romana Pontificia intercesserit, hodieque intercedat: tamen non defuerunt illis quoque temporibus Doctores Ecclesiæ, qui grassantibus tùm Idolomania Pontificiæ erroribus, etiam publicè contradicerent: uti in Catalogo testium Veritatis videre & cognoscere licet.

Tertiò ab anno Christi sexcentesimo, crescente Pontificis Romani dominatu, puritas religionis ita decrevit, ut si externam Ecclesiæ formam, si dogmatum abominationes, si abusuum ac superstitionum voraginem spectasses, vix profectò umbram aliquam puritatis ac simplicitatis Apostolicæ & antiquioris Ecclesiæ deprehendisses. Ubi tamen ne sic quidem defecit Ecclesia Dei, sed latuit: multis interim millibus superstitibus, qui non curvârunt genua coram Baal Pontificio Romano: uti quæstionis subsequentis secundæ diexodus fusius ostendet.

Quartò, si vel maximè Romanus Papatus totum Occidentem ita implevisset, ut sub regno Pontificio Electorum nullus fuisset reliquus, neque quisquam sub eo salvatus fuisset: non tamen propterea Ecclesia Dei tota defecisset. Neque enim totum mundum occupavit Papatus: sed Occidentem duntaxat: in Orientem verò nunquam pervasit, ne quidem illis temporibus, quibus imperium Orientale saucisere cœpit. Græcorum ergo Ecclesia, licet gravi errore de Processione Spiritus Sancti a solo Patre, fuerit implicata, in ipso tamen fundamento fidei & salutis antiquissimo, sarto tecto asserendo: ut & in reliquis plerisque Articulis Religionis Christianæ eandem ὀρθοδοξίαν tenuit, quam hodiè Lutheranorum tenet Ecclesia : eundem Baptismum: idem Sacramentum Eucharisticum integrum, minimeque mutilatum. Neque opinor, negabunt Jesuitæ apud Græcos semper veram fuisse Ecclesiam, quamdiu quidem ea Christianismo addicta, Sacramentorum administrationem, secundum formam institutionis Christi fideliter dispensavit. Ubicunque enim viget Baptismus, ratione substantiæ salvus & integer, ibi est Ecclesia vera: & per consequens vera etiam ac viva Ecclesiæ membra. Ratio connexi est: Quia Baptismus est ex Thesauris veræ Ecclesiæ, Ephes. 4, 5.

& per Baptismum aperitur ingressus in regnum Cœlorum, Joh. 3, 5. Estque Baptismus lavacrum regenerationis, Tit. 3, 5. salutisque efficiendæ organum efficax 1. Petr. 3, 21. His ita præsuppositis, contrà Jesuitas sic infero:

Si dari potest Ecclesia vera, quæ neque Romani Papatus dominatum unquàm approbavit, neque Romanum Pontificem pro capite Ecclesiæ unquam agnovit: neque Romanam Ecclesiam pro vera Ecclesiâ unquàm habuit: Consequens est, 1. extra Papatum Romanum superioribus seculis & quidem ante exortum B. Lutheri, fuisse veram Ecclesiam, Lutheranorum Ecclesiæ in fundamento fidei, vel saltem in eo maximè conformem, quod Pontificem Romanum & Synagogam ejus, pro Antichristo & Ecclesia malignantium semper habuit: 2. falsum esse, quod Jesuitæ subinde grunniunt, nisi Papatus ipse vera sit & fuerit superioribus seculis, Ecclesia, tum neminem in mundo salvari potuisse, ac proindè Ecclesiam totam defecisse.

Atqui talis dari potest Ecclesia, extra Papatum: nempè Orientalis Græcorum. Ergò. Assumtum duobus constat membris: Prius: Græcorum Ecclesiam fuisse veram Ecclesiam: id quod ex Sacramento Baptismi, ex fundamento fidei & salutis incorruptè asserto, & ex reliquis notis paulò antè demonstrabimus. Posterius est: Græcam, sivè Orientalem Ecclesiam Papatum Romanum semper detestatam fuisse: id quod multis evidentibus documentis evinci potest. Græca certè Ecclesia per Patriarcham Constantinopolitanum quotannis Dominicâ Invocavit, Romanum Pontificem cum tota ipsius Ecclesia, solenni ritu tanquàm hæreticum publicè proclamavit, & Anathemate ferijt. Porrò Græca Ecclesia in more ac consuetudine habuit positum, ut fæminam vel virginem Græcam, nubentem Italo vel Hispano, publicè excommunicaret: idque non ut Jesuitæ somniant, Nationis Latinæ, sed potiùs Religionis Romanæ sive Pontificiæ odio. Hinc factum, ut Græci Legatos suos, quos ad Lateranense Concilium ablegaverant, domum reversos, non modò Ecclesiâ suâ, sed totâ Græcia ejecerint, eò quòd in illo Concilio nimiùm studentes societati & Concordiæ inter Romanam & Græcam, sive Occidentalem & Orientalem Ecclesiam sanciendæ, in quædam capita Pontificiæ Idolomaniæ consensissent. Quà de re, ut & id genus documentis alijs cum fructu legi potest Catalogus Testium Veritatis. Et memoratu perquàm dignum ac à nostro instituto minimè alienum est, quod Johannes Mandevilla de Johanne XXII. Pontifice Romano refert, scripsisse ipsum satis prolixè & ampullosis verbis ad Græcos, Vnicam tantum esse Ecclesiam, unicumquè ejus caput, nempè S E, Christi vicarium: periturosque omnes, si tam præclaro capiti non adhæserint: Quare monuisse, ut quam primùm resipiscant, & sibi obediant. Verùm Græcos breviter in hunc modum respondisse: Potentiam tuam summam circa tuos subditos firmiter credimus: Superbiam tuam summam tolerare non possumus: Avaritiam tuam inexplebilem satiare non valemus: Diabolus tecum, quia Dominus nobiscum. Vid. Catal. testium Verit. part. 2. p. 683.


### Chapter II. Of the attributes: II. Controversy, on the Lutheran Church: Namely, what sort and where did it exist under the Papacy before the rise of Luther? (continued)

The Romanists are in an uproar at this point, and there are not lacking among them those who think that judgment concerning the True Church must be made from the multitude of provinces and kingdoms, and indeed from the number of the men themselves, by which the West surpasses the East. But this is too gross and carnal a delirium. For Christ the Savior testifies that the truth of the Church is not to be measured by the multitude, but by the paucity of men: Luke 12:32, Matt. 7:13. What? That there are not lacking witnesses worthy of faith, and proven historians, who forbid that the Church of the West was surpassed by double, if not triple, by the Oriental assembly, even in those times in which the Pontifical kingdom was at its greatest amplitude.

Furthermore, the Pontificians object; that the Greek Church cannot be held as True, because it was not immune from errors. But I reply that no help accrues to the cause of the Romanists from that. For let it be that the Greek Church was not entirely immune from errors: especially in those times in which the inclination of the Oriental or Constantinopolitan Empire occurred: where also that trite impiety: νόσονς χώρης, κατ νοσες τῷ θεῷ, yet the Greek Church was never submerged into such a whirlpool of Idolomania or impiety, as we know the Roman Synagogue to have been absorbed. Then, the State of the Controversy is maliciously perverted by the Adversaries. For the example of the Greek Church is not urged by us at this point for that end, as if we wished to demonstrate that it was either entirely devoid of every error, or that some absolute conformity exists between our Lutheran Churches and the Greek: but only that we may show that the Roman Pontiff was never in previous centuries, even under those densest Pontifical shadows, acknowledged as the head of the Church and vicar of Christ throughout the whole Christian World. Finally, we have already shown above that the Greek Church cannot be despoiled of the praise of Truth: and the same is most clearly evident even from this, that that august Symbol of our Churches, namely the Augsburg Confession, translated into the Greek language by our people, and exhibited to the judgment of the principal Patriarchs throughout all of Greece, greatly praised it, and approved it as orthodox in many things, as can be seen from the Acts of the Würtemberg Theologians and the Patriarch of Constantinople, Jeremiah. Printed at Tübingen in the year 1584.

Thirdly, the Romanists object to that as well, that the Greek Church was not, or even now is, of the same mind (ὁμόψηφον) as the doctrine of the Lutheran Church, so that it is clearly absurd if the latter wishes to appeal to the conformity of the former. But I reply 1. that the state of the Controversy, which is proper to this question, is maliciously perverted, concerning which a little earlier. 2. The Adversaries assume what is false. For in the foundation of faith and salvation, concerning which it is chiefly controverted between us and the Romanists, that the greatest conformity exists between our Churches and the Greek Oriental, has been proven by us thus far and public monuments confirm this. For even if we were to pass over in silence the entire antiquity of the Greek Fathers, which is wholly ours, there exist moreover clear testimonies of that Church which today is found throughout the Greek East, by which they greatly approve and praise the Confession of our Churches: as is clearly evident from the recently cited Tübingen Acts.

Fourthly, there are those among the Romanists who invert our given response and clamor that it is manifest from this that the Lutheran Church is new, because it chose the Greeks as the final judges of its doctrine and sought to be received into the communion of the Church by the Patriarch of Constantinople, when it wished to submit the Augsburg Confession to his censure.

But I reply that a gross fallacy is committed, τῷ μὴ αἰτίῳ ὡς αἰτίῳ [treating the non-cause as the cause]. For the Augsburg Confession was not submitted to the censure of the Greeks by our people with the end or purpose that they should constitute the Patriarch of Constantinople as the judge of their doctrine, or that from his censure they should finally be rendered certain of the truth of their doctrine, or that they sought to be received by him into the communion of the Church. For none of these things could ever have entered the minds of our Churches, indeed it should not have; because, by the grace of God, our Churches are not so cut off, attenuated, or reduced to such straits, or even so lacking in counsel, that we have need of foreign aid for the certainty and defense of our doctrine, or (as that Pole writes) of foreign auxiliary soldiers, whom we might summon from distant places, by whom, once protected, we might think ourselves safe against the Romanists. But this was the true and principal cause of that action: that since the Greeks were seeking the friendship of our Churches both through envoys and through letters, and it was not yet entirely clear to our people whether the modern Greeks still kept that ancient purity of doctrine intact, it was therefore decided with prudent counsel that, by sending the symbol of the Augsburg Confession, it should be explored whether they were of one mind with us in the doctrine of faith or not. Since, therefore, it was clear from the rescript of the Greeks that they agreed with us on the foundation of the doctrine concerning the Person and Office of Christ and concerning justifying faith, it came about that our people gave many thanks to the Greeks for this consensus and labored vehemently to bring them fully to us: as the Tübingen Acts clearly testify.

Finally, there are not lacking those among the Papists who do not shrink from writing with an imprudent pen that the Eastern Churches agree in more articles with the Papists than with the Lutherans. But I reply that this is affirmed contrary to the truth. For the confessions of the Greeks clearly testify to the contrary. Furthermore, even if today there could be Eastern Churches that agree with the Roman Church in certain articles, such as concerning Auricular Confession and other abuses of that kind:

nevertheless, this cannot and ought not to prejudice those Eastern Churches which existed in previous centuries, nor indeed even those who in the most recent years have testified excellently to their consensus with our Churches. But this at last follows from it, that the Greek Church also has fallen away from the purity of doctrine and has been split into diverse opinions: for it was once clearly immune and free from such abuses; so much so that even the Canon Law, dist. 5, de Poenitentia, cap. 1, in the gloss admits: that confession is indeed necessary for mortal sins in the Roman Church, but not among the Greeks, because this tradition did not emanate to them. What? Even if the entire Greek Church were to pass over completely to the Roman, this would nevertheless not harm the purity and antiquity of our Church, since both depend not on the authority and consensus of this or that Church, whether Eastern, Western, or any other, but solely on the foundation of the Prophets and Apostles.

And thus far we have dispatched that first argument of our confirmation, showing that the Roman-Papal Church never invaded or occupied the whole Christian world, but that there have always existed those who manifestly contradicted the Papacy and openly retained and defended a kind of doctrine different from it.

The latter remains, by which it must be demonstrated that not even under the Papacy itself, however dense, did the Church of God fall away to such an extent that no true Church remained, much less that all were damned under it in general, although the Papacy itself was by no means a true Church.

And at the beginning, we affirm that the true Church then consisted of all those who in great number and spirit openly and sharply resisted the Roman Papacy and Dominion, and in public writings condemned it as the kingdom of the Antichrist, the series and doctrine of whom that golden book has woven together, whose title is Catalogus testium Veritatis [Catalog of Witnesses of the Truth], who before our age protested against the Roman Pontiff and his errors: first printed with a preface by Matthias Flacius Illyricus at Strasbourg in the year 1562; but later published twice as enlarged by the Sacramentarians at Lyon in the year 1597. Although therefore already from the year of our Lord six hundred, the kingdom of the Roman Pontiff grew in such a way that religion subsequently fell into a worse state, and day by day less and less of its pristine sincerity and integrity remained in it: yet GOD always, even under the very thickest Papacy, preserved not only seven, as in the times of Elijah, but many thousands of pious people, who resisted and contradicted those sprouting, growing, and rampant errors, not only with words and pen, but also with their very blood and martyrdom.

Bernard certainly, who lived five hundred years ago, namely around A.D. 1091, inveighs against the Roman Church thus: The very offices of ecclesiastical dignity have turned into shameful gain and the business of darkness: nor in these is the salvation of souls sought, but the luxury of riches: for this reason they are shorn, for this reason they frequent churches, celebrate masses, sing psalms: for bishoprics, archdeaconries, abbeys, and other dignities, they contend shamelessly today, so that the revenues of the churches may be dissipated in the use of superfluity and vanity. It remains that the man of sin be revealed, the son of perdition, a demon not only of the day, but also of the noon, who not only transforms himself into an angel of light, but is also exalted above everything that is called GOD, or that is worshipped.

To Bernard we add Anshelm, Bishop of Havelberg in the March, who more than 400 years ago raised such a complaint: Why are there so many novelties in the Church of GOD? Why do so many orders arise in it? Who could recount so many orders of clerics? Who would not marvel at so many kinds of monks? Who, finally, would not be scandalized? And among so many diverse forms of differing religions, who would not be affected by a tedious scandal? Indeed, who would not despise the Christian religion subjected to so many varieties? Diminished by so many inventions? Agitated by so many new laws and customs? Fluctuating almost annually by so many rules and manners of monks?

Latin:

Tumultuantur hoc loco Romanenses, & non desunt ex illis qui ex multitudine provinciarum & regnorum, quin ipsorum etiam hominum numero, quo Occidens Orientem superet, de Vera Ecclesia judicium faciendum esse autumant. Sed nimis crassum ac carnale hoc est delirium. Neque enim Ecclesiæ veritatem ex multitudine, sed ex paucitate hominum metiendam esse, Christus Servator testatur: Luc. 12, 32. Matth. 7, 13. Quid? quod non desunt testes fide digni, & probati historici, qui prohibent, duplo, si non triplo superatam fuisse ab Orientali cœtu, Ecclesiam Occidentis, ijs etiam temporibus, quibus Pontificij regni maxima fuit amplitudo.

Porrò excipiunt Pontificij; Græcam Ecclesiam pro Verâ haberi non posse, propterea quòd non fuerit immunis ab erroribus. Sed respondeo nihil indè præsidij, Romanensium causæ accedere. Esto enim ab erroribus non planè fuerit immunis Græca Ecclesia: illis præsertim temporibus, quibus Imperij Orientalis sive Constantinopolitani inclinatio facta est: ubi etiam impietum illud tritum: νόσονς χώρης, κατ νοσες τῷ θεῷ in tantam tamen vel Idololamaniæ vel impietatis voraginem nunquàm est demersa Ecclesia Græca, quâ Romanam Synagogam absorptam fuisse novimus. Deindè ab Adversarijs malitiosè pervertitur Status Controversiæ. Neque enim eo fine Græcæ Ecclesiæ exemplum hoc loco à nobis urgetur, quasi demonstrare velimus, vel omnis planè erroris illam fuisse expertem, vel nostris Ecclesiis Lutheranis cum Græcâ absolutam quandam intercedere conformitatem: sed tantùm ut ostendamus, Pontificem Romanum nunquàm fupcrioribus seculis, etiam sub densissimis illis tenebris Pontificijs, pro capite Ecclesiæ, & Christi vicario, per totum Orbem Christianum fuisse agnitum. Tandem Græcam Ecclesiam Veritatis laude non posse spoliari, jam supra ostendimus: & patet idem luculentissimè vel indè, quod augustum illud Ecclesiarum nostrarum Symbolum, confessionem nimirùm Augustanam, in linguam Græcam à nostratibus conversam, & censuræ Patriarcharum præcipuorum per universam Græciam exhibitam, magnoperè laudavit, & ut orthodoxam in multis approbavit, uti videre est ex Actis Theologorum Wvirtenbergiensium, & Patriarchæ Constantinopolitani Hieremiæ. Anno 1584. Tubingæ excusis.

Objiciunt tertiò Romanenses & illud, Græcam Ecclesiam in doctrinâ Lutheranæ Ecclesiæ non fuisse, aut etiamnum esse ὁμόψηφον, ut absonum planè sit, si hæc ad illius conformitatem provocare velit. Sed respondeo 1. malitiosè perverti statum Controversiæ, qui quæstionis hujus est proprius, de quo Paulò antè. 2. Falsum subsumunt Adversarij. Nam in fundamento fidei ac salutis, de quo potissimùm inter nos & Romanenses controvertitur, nostris Ecclesiis cum Græca Orientali maximam conformitatem intercedere, hactenùs à nobis probatum est; idque publica confirmant monumenta. Nam ut silentio jam involvamus totam Græcorum Patrum vetustatem, quæ tota nostra est: extant insuper luculenta illius etiam, quæ hodiè per Græciam Orientalem passim est, Ecclesiæ testimonia, quibus Ecclesiarum nostrarum Confessionem magnoperè approbant & collaudant: uti ex citatis modò actis Tubingensibus luculenter patet.

Quartò sunt ex Romanensibus, qui datam nostram responsionem invertunt, & vel indè manifestum esse clamitant, Lutheranam Ecclesiam esse novam, quia ea Græcos demùm doctrinæ suæ judices elegerit, & à Patriarcha Constantinopolitano in communionem Ecclesiæ recipi petierit, dùm ipsius censuræ Confessionem Augustanam subjicere voluit.

Sed respondeo crassum committi Sophisma τῷ μὴ αἰτίῳ ὡς αἰτίῳ. Neque enim confessio Augustana eo fine aut consilio, Græcorum censuræ à nostris submissa fuit, ut doctrinæ suæ judicem constituerent Patriarcham Constantinopolitanum, vel ut ex hujus censura, de doctrina suæ certitudine demùm redderentur indubii, vel ut in Ecclesiæ Communionem ab eo recipi peterent. Nihil enim horum nostris Ecclesiis unquàm in mentem venire potuit, imò nè debuit quidem, proptereà quòd per D E I gratiam, nostræ Ecclesiæ, non ita sunt accisæ, attenuatæ, aut in angustum adeò redactæ, vel etiam ita inopes consilii, ut nobis ad certitudinem & defensionem nostræ doctrinæ, alieno opus sit auxilio, aut (ut Polonus iste scribit) milite extraneo subsidiario, quem ex peregrinis advocemus locis, quo demùm muniti, adversus Romanenses tutos nos fore arbitremur. Sed hæc fuit vera ac principalis causa facti istius, quòd cùm Græci nostratum Ecclesiarum amicitiam tùm per legatos, tùm per literas ambirent, & verò nostris haudusque adeò liquidò constaret, nùm moderni Græci antiquam illam doctrinæ puritatem adhuc sartam tectam retinerent: ideò prudenti sanè consilio decretum fuit, ut transmisso Confessionis Augustanæ Symbolo exploraretur, nùm nobis essent in doctrina fidei ὁμόψηφοι nec nè. Cùm igitur ex rescripto Græcorum constaret, ipsos in fundamento doctrinæ de Christi Persona & Officio, deq́; fide justificante nobiscum consentire, factum, ut nostri Græcis de hoc consensu plurimùm gratularentur, ipsiśque plenè ad nos perducendis vehementer laborarent: uti Acta Tubingensia evidenter testantur.

Tandem non desunt ex Pontificiis, qui imprudenti calamo scribere non exhorrescunt: Orientales Ecclesias in pluribus articulis consentire cum Pontificijs, quàm cum Lutheranis. Sed respondeo præter fidem hoc affirmari. Diversum enim Græcorum confessiones luculenter testantur. Deindè si vel maximè hodiè dari possint Orientales Ecclesiæ, quæ in quibusdam Articulis, ut de Confessione Auriculari, deque aliis id genus abusibus, cum Romana Ecclesia consentiant:

nihil tamen hoc præjudicare vel potest vel debet, illis Ecclesiis Orientalibus, quæ superioribus fuerunt seculis, imò nec illis quoq;, qui annis superioribus proximis, de suo consensu cum nostris Ecclesiis egregiè testatæ sunt. Verùm illud tandem indè sequitur, Græcam quoque Ecclesiam à puritate doctrinæ defecisse, & in diversas opiniones scissam esse: quippè quæ olim ab ejusmodi abusibus planè fuit immunis & libera: adeò ut jus etiam Canonicum, dist. 5. de Pœnitentia, cap. 1. in glossa fateatur: Necessariam quidem esse confessionem in mortalibus in Romana Ecclesia: apud Græcos verò non, propterea quòd traditio hæc ad illos non emanaverit. Quid? si vel maximè Græca Ecclesia tota penitùs transiret ad Romanam; nihil tamen hoc nostræ Ecclesiæ & puritati & antiquitati incommodaret, quippè quæ utraque non ab hujus vel illius, sive Orientalis, sive Occidentalis, sive cujusquam alterius Ecclesiæ autoritate & consensu, sed unicè à fundamento Prophetarum & Apostolorum dependet.

Et hactenùs quidem priùs illud confirmationis nostræ argumentum expedivimus ostendentes Romano-Pontificiam Ecclesiam nunquàm totum orbem Christianum invasisse aut occupasse: sed semper extitisse, qui Papatui manifestè contradixerint, & diversum ab eo doctrinæ genus palàm retinuerint ac defenderint.

Superest Posterius, quo demonstrandum, ne quidem sub ipso Papatu licèt densissimo ita defecisse Ecclesiam DEI, ut nulla superfuerit Ecclesia vera, nedùm in universum omnes sub ipso damnati fuerint, licèt Papatus ipse, Ecclesia vera minimè fuerit.

Ac initiò quidem veram tùm Ecclesiam constituisse affirmamus omnes eos, qui magno numero ac spiritu Romano Papatui & Dominatui palàm acriter restiterunt, & publicis scriptis tanquàm Antichristi regnum improbarunt, quorum seriem & doctrinam pertexit aureus ille liber, cui titulus est Catalogus testium Veritatis, qui ante nostram ætatem Pontifici Romano ejusque erroribus reclamârunt: initiò cum præfatione Matthiæ Flacij Illyrici Argentinæ Anno 1562. excusus: postmodùm verò duplo auctior editus à Sacramentariis, Lugduni, Anno 1597. Etsi proindè jam indè ab anno Domini sexcentesimo, ita Pontificis Romani regnum crevit, ut subindè Religio in deterius rueret, ac indies minùs ac minùs pristinæ sinceritatis integritatisq; in ea remaneret: semper tamen DEUS sub ipso densissimo Papatu non septem tantùm, uti temporibus Heliæ, sed plura piorum millia servavit, qui illis pullulantibus, crescentibus & grassantibus erroribus restiterunt, ac contradixerunt, non tantùm verbis ac calamo: sed & sanguine ipso ac martyrio suo.

Bernhardus certè, qui ante annos quingentos, nimirùm circa A. D. 1091. vixit, in Ecclesiam Romanam sic invehitur: Ipsa Ecclesiasticæ dignitatis officia, in turpem quæstum, & tenebrarum negocium transivere: nec in his salus animarum, sed luxus quæritur divitiarum: propter hoc tondeatur, propter hoc frequentant Ecclesias, Missas celebrant, Psalmos decantant: pro Episcopatibus, archidiaconatibus, abbatijs, alijsq́; dignitatibus impudenter hodiè decertatur, ut Ecclesiarum reditus, in superfluitatis & Vanitatis usu dissipentur. Superest ut reveletur homo peccati, filius perditionis, dæmonium non modò diurnum, sed & meridianum, quòd non solùm transfiguretur in Angelum lucis, sed & extollitur supra omne, quod dicitur DEUS, aut quòd colitur.

Bernhardo adjungimus Anshelmum Episcopum Havelbergensem in Marchia, qui ante annos 400 amplius talem movet querelam: Quare tot Novitates in Ecclesia DEI sunt? Quare tot ordines in ea surgunt? Quis memorare queat tot Ordines Clericorum? Quis non miretur tot genera Monachorum? Quis denique non scandalizetur? Et inter tot diversas formas Religionum discrepantium, tadioso non afficiatur scandalo? Imò quis non contemnat Christianam Religionem tot varietatibus subjectam? tot adinventionibus minutatam? tot novis legibus & consuetudinibus agitatam? tot regulis ac moribus Monachorum fermè annuatim fluctuantem?


### Chapter II. Of the attributes: II. Controversy, on the Lutheran Church: Namely, what sort and where did it exist under the Papacy before the rise of Luther? (continued)

And after a few words: Behold, we see in the Church of GOD certain men who, according to their own whim, choose for themselves a new order of living, clothed in an unusual habit, and whether under the title of monastic profession or under the vow of canonical discipline, they assume for themselves whatever new mode of chanting they wish, and set for themselves limits of food: And they imitate neither the monks who fight under the rule of St. Benedict, nor the canons who lead their lives under the rule of Augustine: but doing everything new according to their own whim, they are a law unto themselves: they are an authority unto themselves: and those whom they can, they gather into their own society under the pretext of a new law.

That most useful treatise to read by Nicholas of Clemanges, a Parisian theologian, which he published two hundred years ago concerning the corrupt state of the Roman Church, and which we have caused to be reprinted here among us two years ago, pertains to this.

Moreover, it is easy to conjecture that where one such doctor, feeling more rightly and protesting against the Papacy, existed, there also many hearers, whose names and confessions were not committed to writing, existed, and that they embraced the same purity of doctrine against the Roman synagogue. It is also easy to conjecture that, besides these doctors or witnesses of the truth, there were many others who, either prohibited by fear from writing and daring not at all to include the heads of their doctrine in public monuments because of the greatest dangers, or even if they wrote anything, that it perished either by the injury of time or by the fraud and tyranny of their adversaries: just as it is read in many booklets still extant, that the adversaries strove with the greatest effort to ensure that all writings composed against their errors, tyranny, and impurity of life were utterly abolished. Thus there is no doubt that even today in the midst of Italy and Spain, and even in Rome, and here and there elsewhere, not a few lie hidden who detest the idolomania of the Papists from their heart: and thus even that of the prophet is fulfilled: As if a shepherd should rescue from the mouth of a lion two legs, or the tip of an ear: so shall the children of Israel be rescued, who dwell in Samaria? Amos 3:2. And these indeed constitute one group of the true Church, which existed even under the Papacy itself, although they are not recognized by all as the true Church.

The other group is constituted by that innumerable multitude of martyrs who, many centuries before Luther, openly called the Roman see the Kingdom of Antichrist, condemned it, groaned over so many and such great abominations of the Church, and shed their blood for the assertion of the truth. Their multitude was so great that if you wished to collect into one sum all the martyrs killed by the Roman Antichrist throughout Italy, Belgium, Spain, France, and other regions, hardly any calculation seems sufficient. Concerning this matter, the two volumes of the Martyrology of Doctor Ludwig Rabus, a most constant theologian, can be read with profit. And indeed GOD himself, as our blessed Luther notes, defined that group when he foretold through the prophet Daniel, chapter 11:41, that Edom, that is, that red or ruddy people, namely, stained by their own blood shed for the truth, was also to be saved from the hands of the Antichrist, among other nations: just as the unanimous consensus of all interpreters, even the most ancient, testifies that this prophecy is to be understood.

The third group of the true Church under the midst of the Papacy is constituted by the multitude of baptized infants, namely those who, sanctified by the washing of regeneration, ceased to be among the living before the Papist idolomania had perverted their understanding. Wis. 4:11. And GOD wished to note this group likewise through Daniel in the place already cited, when he foretold that the beginning of the children of Ammon was to be snatched from the kingdom of the Antichrist, where it is the constant opinion of all interpreters that infants are noted.

The fourth and last group of the true Church under the Papacy was constituted by those who are named Moab by Daniel, which sounds the same as 'from the Father.' By this term those faithful were noted who, from the chief chapters of the Catechism, from the history of the Lord's passion, from the summaries or pericopes of the Gospels and Sunday Epistles, knew CHRIST their Redeemer, and resting with simple faith in the mercy of GOD and the merit of Christ, breathed their last: repeatedly echoing that trite and ancient saying of Johannes Geiler von Kaysersberg: 'May the immense mercy of GOD the Father, the most precious merit of the most bitter Passion of Jesus Christ, appear to me in the final agony of death. The unfathomable mercy of GOD our Heavenly Father: The precious merit of the sorrowful suffering of our LORD JESUS Christ must appear to You and to Me, in our last needs: Whoever desires that from the heart, let him say Amen.' In a sermon on the first Sunday of Advent, held in Strasbourg more than a hundred years ago. I pass over now that it was repeatedly proclaimed to the dying, and to those already in their death throes, from the 'Little Garden of the Soul,' that they should place all hope and trust in no other thing than in the merit and death of Jesus Christ: that they should wrap themselves in this very death of his, and by it fortify and cover themselves against the fiery darts of the Devil.

Where there is no doubt that, with the remaining stubble of errors and Papist superstitions burned away by that fire of temptation, the very foundation of salvation was firmly retained, and thus very many died in faith in Christ and were saved.

Thus, therefore, the true Church consisted of four distinct groups under the midst of the Papacy, but miserably oppressed and all but completely suppressed: so that it could be said that the true Church did not indeed flourish, nor yet completely fail, but was hidden at that time. It is therefore an impudent calumny of the Jesuits to attribute to us the opinion that no one was saved under the Papacy, or that there was no true Church under it, or, what is greater, that we maintain that the Church of Christ has failed entirely.

But even in this place the Adversaries make a tumult, and with various arguments they have sought out, they rise up against those things which we have already said.

And at the beginning, indeed, they argue thus: If there was a true Church under the Papacy, as the Lutherans concede: but they defected from the Church under the Papacy: Therefore they defected from the true Church, and consequently, the Lutherans are not the true Church.

I answer 1. that a Sophism of Confusion of disparate questions is committed: For it is one thing to assert that there was a true Church under the Papacy: which we willingly concede: But it is another and different thing to affirm that the Papacy itself was that true Church: which we deny. Now, therefore, because the Papacy itself is not the true Church, we certainly did not make a secession from the true Church when we defected from the Papacy. For we remained with that group which, under the Papacy, contradicting the Papist idolomania, was of one mind with us in doctrine, and we did not defect from it by even a hair's breadth in the foundation of the faith. Just as, therefore, the title of true Church rightly belongs to those groups, so it also belongs to us.

2. A Sophism of a vicious Consequent is committed. For the crime of apostasy cannot be objected to us by any right: since we never defected from the true Church: indeed, properly speaking, we did not even defect from the Papacy; since we never agreed with it. But all apostasy, properly speaking, presupposes a preceding consent. We are therefore more correctly said to have exited from the Papacy, that is, to have publicly signified to the whole Christian world through the ministry of Blessed Luther that we do not agree with Papist doctrine in the least. Finally, regarding the example of Blessed Luther and others, who, initially immersed in Papist errors, later defected from them, it is to be well noted that not every defection is vicious and to be reprehended: but that there is an apostasy or defection that is good, and commanded by God Himself, as when He warns His people to turn themselves away from the very evil ways of their ancestors, from idols, from the pollutions, from the doctrine of false prophets, etc. when likewise the Apostle commands to beware of dogs and wolves: to go out from Babylon (which Jerome understands as Rome), indeed not even to say greeting to those who hold another and perverse doctrine of the Gospel. Thus most of the Apostles defected from the traditions of the Jewish Papists: Thus our ancestors also defected from the Roman Synagogue, which hardly anyone can doubt is a church of evildoers: and they passed openly to the true Church, or rather they did not so much pass as declare openly that they were in it. Meanwhile, we know there is another species of apostasy, vicious and damnable in all ways, when, namely, from the true knowledge of the true GOD, and thus from a purer Religion, a secession is made to a false church, either by hope of rewards or fear of dangers: In which manner it is too certain that Johannes Pistorius Nidanus defected from our true Church to the Papists, with the eternal loss of his salvation.

The other argument is such: Where the doctrine of Christ was entirely depraved, where the Holy Bible lay as if buried under a bench: where the clergy or ecclesiastical order was most deeply corrupted: there certainly the true Church cannot be. But the Lutherans clamor that the former happened to the Papacy in previous centuries. Therefore it will be false that they contend that nonetheless there was a true Church under the Papacy at that time.

I answer that the connection of the Major premise is simply false. There was certainly, in the times of the coming of Christ into the flesh, such a depravation of heavenly doctrine among the people of GOD that a greater one could hardly have been: Shall we therefore affirm that the true Church of GOD had then completely failed? The Arian heresy had once prevailed everywhere in the whole world, in such a manner that the true Church of GOD appeared nowhere, so much so that St. Jerome wrote, the whole world groaned and marveled that it was Arian. Shall we therefore think that the true Church of Christ had then completely failed? Not so: but rather we shall maintain with the same Jerome that the principal Orthodox Bishops and Prelates had indeed been exiled from their churches at that time: but that the Church of Christ had not been exiled from the whole world: that is, that the true Church had indeed been hidden under a most corrupt ministry, but had not completely failed. If, therefore, in those times in which a public depravation of doctrine, indeed an almost total loss and silence of the divine word prevailed, it was not right to assert that the Church of God had completely failed, as indeed the Romanists themselves would hardly concede this: much less, surely, will this have a place in the depraved Papist ministry; to which it cannot be denied by any reason that Baptism remained intact in its substance. For God saves and has always saved, even under the most corrupt ministry, His Elect, who did not allow themselves to be implicated in those Egyptian darknesses, or, as the Johannine Apocalypse speaks, to be made drunk with the wine of the fornication of the Babylonian harlot, that is, of the Antichrist or the Roman Pontiff.

Latin:

Et post pauca: Ecce videmus in Ecclesia DEI quosdam, qui pro libitu suo insolito habitu indutinovum vivendi ordinem sibi eligunt, & sive sub Monastica professionis titulo, sive sub Canonica disciplina voto, quodcunq; volunt, sibi assumunt novum psallendi modum, & cibariorum metas sibi statuunt: Et nec Monachos, qui sub regula S. Benedicti militant, nec canonicos, qui sub regula Augustini vitam gerunt, imitantur: sed omnia pro libitu suo Nova facientes, ipsi sibi sunt Lex: ipsi sibi sunt autoritas: & quos pos sunt, in suam societatem, sub prætextu novæ legis colligunt.

Pertinet huc Tractatus ille lectu utilissimus Nicolai de Clemangijs, Theologi Parisiensis, quem ante annos ducentos de corrupto Ecclesiæ Romanæ statu edidit: quemque ante biennium hîc apud nos recudi curavimus.

Cæterùm facilè est conjicere, ubi unus talis Doctor, rectiùs sentiens, & Papatui reclamans fuerit, ibi quoq; plurimos Auditorum, quorum nomina ac confessiones literis mandatæ non sunt, extitisse, eandemque doctrinæ puritatem, contra Romanam Synagogam amplexos fuisse. Facilè etiam est conjicere, præter hosce Doctores sive Testes Veritatis, alios quoque plurimos fuisse, qui vel metu prohibiti scribere, monumentisque publicis doctrinæ suæ capita comprehendere, ob maxima pericula minimè ausi sint: vel etiam, si quid scripserunt, id ipsum aut temporum injuriâ, aut Adversariorum fraude ac Tyrannide periisse: sicut in multis, adhuc extantibus libellis legitur, Adversarios summo studio id egisse, ut omnia scripta contra suos errores, tyrannidem & impuritatem vitæ conscripta, penitùs abolêrentur. Sic nullum est dubium, quin hodieque in media Italia & Hispania, quin etiam Romæ, & passim alibi lateant non pauci, qui Idolomaniam Pontificiani ex corde detestentur: & vel sic etiam impleatur illud Prophetæ: Quomodo si eruat pastor de ore leonis duo crura, aut extremum auricula: sic eruentur filij Israël, qui habitant in Samaria? Amos 3, 2. Et hi quidem unum constituunt coetum Ecclesiæ veræ, quæ sub ipso etiam Papatu fuit, licèt ab omnibus non sint pro vera Ecclesia agniti.

Alterum cœtum constituit innumera illa Martyrum multitudo, qui multis ante Lutherum seculis Romanam sedem apertè Regnum Antichristi nominarunt, damnarunt, ac super tot tantisque Ecclesiæ abominationibus ingemuerunt, ac pro asserenda Veritate sanguinem profuderunt. Quorum tanta fuit multitudo, ut si omnes per Italiam, Belgium, Hispaniam, Galliam & alias regiones, interfectos ab Antichristo Romano Martyres in unam summam colligere velis, vix ulla Calculi ratio sufficere videatur. Qua de re cum fructu legi possunt Tomi duo Martyrologi Doctoris Ludovici Rabus, Theologi costantissimi. Et profectò DEUS ipse, sic annotante B. Luthero nostro, cætum istum definivit, quando per Prophetam Danielem, cap. 11, 41 prædixit, de Anti-Christi manibus, inter alias gentes, salvandum etiam esse Edom, hoc est, populum illum rubeum sive rubrum, nempè proprio sanguine, pro Veritate profuso, tinctum: quemadmodum unanimis consensus omnium interpretum, etiam antiquissimorum, Vaticinium hoc intelligendum esse testatur.

Tertium cœtum veræ Ecclesiæ sub medio Papatu constituit multitudo Infantum baptizatorum, eorum videlicet, qui lavacro regenerationis sanctificati, prius in vivis esse desierunt, quàm Idolomania Pontificia intellectum ipsorum perverterat. Sap. 4, 11.
