Et hunc cœtum itidem per Danielem loco jam citato, notare voluit DEUS, quando ex Antichristi regno eripiendum esse prædixit, Principium filiorum Ammon, ubi infantes notari, constans omnium interpretum est sententia.

Quartum & postremum cœtum Ecclesiæ veræ sub Papatu constituerunt illi, qui à Daniele nominantur Moab, quod idem sonat, atque à Patre. Quo termino illi fideles notati sunt, qui ex præcipuis capitibus Catechismi, ex historia passionis Dominicæ, ex summatis sive pericopis Evangeliorum & Epistolarum Dominicalium, CHRISTUM Redemtorem suum cognoverunt, & simplici fide in DEI misericordia, Christique merito acquiescentes, animam exhalarunt: tritum & antiquum illud Johannis Keiserspergij subindè ingeminantes: immensa DEI Patris misericordia: pretiosissimum meritum acerbissimæ Passionis Jesu Christi, appareat mihi in ultimo mortis agone. Die vngründliche Barmherßigkeit GOTTES vnsers Himlischen Vaters: Der köstlich Verdienst des schmerßreichen Leidens vnsers HERRN JESU Christi muß Euch vnd Mir erscheinen / in vnsren leßten Nöthen: Wer das begehrt von Herßen der sprech Amen. Concione super Dominicam primam Adventus, ante annos centum ampliùs Argentina habita. Taceo jam, quod moribundis, & animam jam agentibus subindè ex hortulo animæ acclamabatur, ut omnem spem atq; fiduciam in nullam aliam rem collocent, quàm in meritû & mortem Jesu Christi: huic ipsius morti se involvant, eaq; cõtra ignita Diaboli tela se muniant & cõtegant.

Ubi nullum est dubium, quin reliquis errorum & superstitionum Pontificiarum stipulis, per ignem istum tentationis combustis, ipsum fundamentum salutis sit firmiter retentum, & sic plurimi in fide in Christum decesserint & salvati fuerint.

Sic ergò Ecclesia vera, quatuor distinctis constans cœtibus, sub medio Papatu fuit, sed miserè pressa, ac tantùm non penitùs oppressa: ut non quidem floruisse, neque etiam penitùs defecisse, sed latuisse tùm Ecclesia vera dici possit. Impudens proindè calumnia est Jesuitarum, eam nobis sententiam affingentium, quâ neminem sub Papatu salvatum, aut sub eodem Ecclesiam veram fuisse nullam, quodŕ, majus est, Ecclesiam Christi prorsus defecisse statuamus.

Verùm & hoc loco tumultuantur Adversarii, & variis conquįsitis argumentis, adversus ea, quæ jam diximus, insurgunt.

Ac initiò quidem sic arguunt: Si sub Papatu fuit Ecclesia vera, uti concedunt Lutherani: illi verò ab Ecclesia sub Papatu defecerunt: Ergò ab Ecclesia vera defecerunt, ac per Consequens, Lutherani non sunt vera Ecclesia.

Respondeo 1. committi Sophisma Confusionis disparatarum quæstionum.: Aliud enim est asserere sub Papatu veram fuisse Ecclesiam: id quod nos libenter concedimus: Aliud verò est & diversum, affirmare, ipsum Papatum fuisse illam Ecclesiam veram: id quod negamus. Jàm ergò, quia non Papatus ipse est vera Ecclesia, utique à vera etiam Ecclesia non secessiònem fecimus, quando à Papatu defecimus. Mansimus enim apud eum cœtum, qui sub Papatu Idolomania Pontificiæ contradicens, nobis in doctrina fuit ὁμόψηφος, & ab eo ne latum quidem unguem in fundamento fidei defecimus. Quemadmodum ergò cœtui isti, ita & nobis Ecclesiæ veræ Elogium jure competit.

2. Committitur Sophisma vitiosi Consequentis. Non enim Apostasiæ crimen ullo jure nobis objici potest: siquidem à vera Ecclesia nunquàm defecimus: imò propriè loquendo nequidem à Papatu defecimus; siquidem cum illo nunquàm consensimus. Omnis autem apostasia propriè loquendo, præsupponit antegressum consensum. Rectiùs proindè ex Papatu exiisse dicimur, hoc est, publicè per ministerium B. Lutheri toti orbi Christiano significasse, nos cum doctrinâ Pontificia minimè consentire. Tandem quoad exemplum B. Lutheri, & aliorum, qui erroribus Pontificiis initiò immersi postmodùm ab illis defecerunt, notandum probè est, non omnem defectionem esse vitiosam & reprehendendam: sed dari apostasiam sive defectionem bonam, & à Deo ipso præceptam, ut quando monet populum suum, ut avertat se à viis pessimis Majorum suorum, ab idolis, ab inquinamentis, à doctrina pseudoprophetarum &c. quando item Apostolus jubet cavere canes & lupos: exire à Babylone (quam Hieronymus Romam intelligit) imò ne ave quidem dicere illis, qui aliam & perversam doctrinam Evangelii tenuerint. Sic defecērunt Apostoli plerique à traditionibus Pontificiorum Judaicorum: Sic nostri etiam Majores defecērunt à Synagoga Romana, quam Ecclesiam malignantium esse, vix quisquam dubitare potest: & transierunt apertè ad veram Ecclesiam, vel non tam transierunt, quàm se in ea esse, apertè declararunt. Interim novimus aliam esse ἀποστασίας speciem, modis omnibus vitiosam & damnabilem, quando nimirùm à vera veri DEI agnitione, & sic puriore Religione, vel spe præmiorum, vel metu periculorum, fit secessio ad Ecclesiam falsam: Quo pacto Johannem Pistorium Nidanum à vera nostra Ecclesia ad Pontificios, cum æterno salutis dispendio, defecisse, nimis certum est.

Alterum argumentum tale est: Ubi doctrina Christi prorsus fuit depravata, ubi Biblia Sacra sub scamno quasi sepulta jacuerunt: ubi clerus vel ordo Ecclesiasticus penitissimè corruptus fuit: ibi certè vera Ecclesia esse nequit. Atqui prius illud Papatui superioribus seculis obvenisse, clamitant Lutherani. Ergò falsum erit, quòd contendunt, nihilominùs tum sub Papatu veram fuisse Ecclesiam.

Respondeo Connexum Majoris simpliciter falsum esse. Fuit certè temporibus adventantis in carnem Christi, tanta cœlestis doctrinæ in populo DEI depravatio, ut vix major esse potuerit: Ergoné veram DEI Ecclesiam penitùs tùm defecisse affirmabimus? Invaluerat quondam Ariana hæresis passim in toto terrarum orbe, eum in modum, ut nuspiam vera DEI Ecclesia appareret, adeò ut D. Hieronymus scripserit, ingemuit totus orbis, & Arianum se esse miratus est. Ergoné veram Christi Ecclesiam penitùs tum defecisse existimabimus? Haud ita: quin potiùs cum eodem Hieronymo statuemus, Exulasse quidem tum Ecclesiis suis præcipuos Episcopos & Antistites Orthodoxos: sed non exulasse toto orbe Ecclesiam Christi: hoc est, latuisse quidem sub corruptissimo ministerio, sed non penitùs defecisse veram Ecclesiam. Quod si ergò illis temporibus, quibus publica doctrinæ depravatio, imò omnimoda fermè verbi divini jactura & silentium obtinuit, fas non fuit asserere, Ecclesiam Dei penitùs defecisse, quemadmodum sanè ipsi quoque Romanenses hoc minimè concesserint: multò profectò minùs locum hoc habebit in depravato ministerio Pontificio; cui integrum per substantiam Baptisnum constitisse, negari nulla ratione potest. Servat enim & servavit semper DEus mirabiliter etiam sub corruptissimo ministerio suos Electos, qui non passi fuerunt, se quoque implicari tenebris illis Ægyptiacis, vel, ut Apocalypsis Johannitica loquitur, se inebriari vino scortationis meretricis Babylonicæ, hoc est, Antichristi sive Pontificis Romani.


### Chapter II. Of the attributes: II. Controversy, on the Lutheran Church: Namely, what sort and where did it exist under the Papacy before the rise of Luther? (continued)

Thirdly, the Papists urge that we point out with a finger, as it were, which individual church it was that is in all things of one mind with our Lutheran one.

I answer that there is no more need for us to prove this than there was need in the times of Ahab for someone to point out individually to the prophet Elijah the Church which, in the purity of its doctrine, was of one mind with him, especially when he complained that he alone of the Orthodox was still surviving. Just as, therefore, it was sufficient for the Prophet to have known from GOD that more than seven thousand of the Elect still survived, who had not bowed their knees before Baal, although they were not shown to him individually: So it is enough for us to have perceived and known that under the Papacy there was a True Church, and that it exists today, although we cannot point it out individually. And indeed, if the Romanists wish to urge us with this condition, they must necessarily stand by the same. Let them therefore show us which and where the true Church was individually under the Arian heresy, which spread through almost the whole world? While they cannot show this, they must necessarily confess one of two things: 1. Either that the true Church had then completely failed: which we simply deny: 2. Or that that true Church could not be pointed out: and consequently, that it is not of the property and Essence of the true Church that it can always be pointed out with the finger: which is what we affirm.

is he who is about to claim for himself the administration of the Church, who exalts himself above all that is called or is GOD: 2 Thess. 2. because also that famous Babylon (which John, Apocal. 17, declares to be the great city which has dominion over the kings of the earth, that is, Rome) is about to dement the kings of the earth, and the inhabitants in it, and the nations, and tribes, and languages, and peoples, with her spiritual fornication: Apocal. 17. How therefore, I ask, could the face of the Church of GOD have been illustrious then, and have had a pure and visible ministry, as the Adversaries dream? Certainly, as soon as any sincere confessor of the truth was seen at that time, the Antichrist immediately pursued him and dragged him to punishment, drunk with the blood of the saints and with the blood of the martyrs of Jesus: Where there was need of faith and patience. Apocal. 13. The Church therefore fled then from the eyes and sight of men, and withdrew into the desert, into hiding places, and caves, and remained there for a long time. Apoc. 12.

Sixthly, the Adversaries argue thus: If the true Church used a ministry under a corrupt Papacy: it will follow first that those Ministers served both GOD and the Devil at the same time: 2. That GOD, in preserving his Elect, also used a corrupt ministry. 3. That the true Church depended on the will of Satan and the Antichrist. 4. That the truth of the Gospel is preserved by false Doctors. That all these things are most absurd, there is hardly anyone who does not understand.

Fourthly, the Adversaries rise up thus: Christ, about to ascend into heaven, ordained a Ministry of the Gospel to be preached among all nations: Ephes. 4. And the Church is never destitute of pure Doctors.

I answer that a fallacy παρὰ τὸ μὴ ἑπόμενον [of the consequent] is committed. For it follows only from the Antecedent that Christ gave pure ministers who announced the Gospel. Meanwhile, however, it by no means follows that, if GOD, about to avenge the ingratitude and contempt of his Word, sends the efficacy of errors, 2 Thessal. 2, the public ministry cannot also be most corrupt. For the different state of the Church of both Testaments clearly proves this, as has been demonstrated hitherto by examples.

I answer that these absurdities are partly absurdities of our reason only, but not of faith; and partly that they do not follow at all from the antecedent. For as regards that first Absurdity, it is indeed true that no one can serve two masters at the same time, but only in a certain respect, namely, in the same thing and in the same respect. Thus, even those ministers under the Papacy could not serve GOD and the Antichrist at the same time in one and the same thing: Meanwhile, however, they could serve GOD in those things which are of GOD: but in those things which are of the Antichrist, they could serve the Antichrist. When, therefore, they conferred baptism upon infants, when they read the Gospels and Sunday Epistles, when they inculcated the merit of Christ and the mercy of GOD the Father to the dying: in this part, certainly, the Ministers were of GOD. But when they sowed pernicious errors, and changed silver into dross, then they were servants of the Antichrist.

Fifthly, the Adversaries object the clearest promises of GOD concerning the perpetuity of the Church, that not even the gates of hell shall prevail against it. Therefore, they say, it is not credible that GOD has so deserted his Church that the True Church has had to lie hidden so far under the shadows of errors.

I answer that the argument proceeds in part, and more is inferred in the consequent than the Antecedent permits. For no more can be inferred from it than that the true Church never fails entirely: which we also readily confess. But that the face of the Church of GOD must always be uniform, and equally conspicuous and illustrious: that, indeed, cannot be elicited from it. For here not only the promises, but also the threatenings of the Church must be noted, by which GOD predicted the most sad seduction under the reign of the Antichrist that would overflow into the Christian world: and indeed so great that, if it were possible, even the Elect would be led into error: nay, that such would be the affliction as has not been from the beginning of the world until this time, nor ever shall be, Matth. 24, because he is to sit in the temple of GOD, this

The other absurdity is clearly none at all: Since GOD himself predicted that it would come to pass, namely, that the Antichrist would sit in the very temple of GOD, and through his ministers would invade the government of the Church: 2 Thess. 2, 4. Thus, in the time of the birth of Christ, GOD used the corrupt ministry of the Pharisees. But that the Elect are preserved through such a ministry, that is of Accident: and is to be ascribed not to the corrupt ministry in itself, but to the singular operation of the Holy Spirit. Therefore, that practical rule is to be observed by the pious and faithful, that, indeed, as the case of necessity and tyranny thus bears it, they may not entirely neglect a corrupted ministry: in so far as it indeed sits upon the seat of Moses and the Prophets, Matt. 23, 2. But in so far as they foist corruptions upon the people, to that extent let them observe the precept of Christ, Matt. 16, 11. Beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees: And again Matt. 15, 14. Let them alone: for they are blind and leaders of the blind.

The third absurdity suffers from a faulty consequence. For we have just now shown that the pious and the Elect used the ministry under the corrupted Papacy, not in so far as it served the Antichrist, but in so far as it served GOD. Therefore, the true Church did not at that time depend simultaneously upon the will of Satan and the Antichrist. For it rather hated and opposed him.

Furthermore, this absurdity can easily be refuted by the example of the Church at the time of the birth of Christ, which indeed used the ministry of the Scribes and Pharisees, in so far as they sat upon the seat of Moses and the Prophets: yet it did not for that reason depend upon the will of Satan.

The fourth and last absurdity proceeds from a false hypothesis, which is that the Truth of the Gospel depends upon the quality of the Doctors of the Church: if this hypothesis were indeed true, then at the time of King Ahab, at the time of the birth of Christ, at the time of the rampant Arianism, there would have been no purity of doctrine in the whole Christian world, and consequently no true Church either. We therefore correct this hypothesis by showing that the purity of the doctrine, as well as that of the Church, is founded upon nothing but the foundation of the Prophets and Apostles: that is, upon the Word of GOD. This word, although those who are established in the ministry do not always keep it pure and uncorrupted: yet very many among the hearers keep it unblemished, who even then guard and preserve both the Truth of the Church and the purity of the Evangelical doctrine. For GOD always preserves for Himself some Holy seed, which with a simple heart assents to the Evangelical Truth, having bid farewell to the sophistries and corruptions of heretics. And in such a case every believer performs the office of a Minister, who detects and rebukes the errors of heretics.

Seventhly and lastly, the Adversaries object to us the authority of the Augsburg Confession, which among the marks of the True Church refers also to the pure preaching of the Word of GOD and the legitimate use of the Sacraments. Therefore, they say, it is of the Essence of the true Church that it should always have a ministry that is in every part uncorrupted.

I answer by distinguishing between the proper, or free, state of the true Church, and its accidental state, or one pressed by tyranny. The Augsburg Confession therefore considers the Church in so far as it subsists in its own proper, entire, and free state: where an uncorrupted ministry is required for the Essence of the True Church. But it must be determined otherwise concerning the state of the Church when it is pressed or enslaved, where heretics hold dominion. For here it suffices that the ministry be of whatever quality, even if it be corrupted: which can be clearly illustrated by the example of the Israelite Church under the Old Testament. For in so far as it enjoyed its own free and entire state, it sang with David from Psalm 147, v. 19 & 20: He declares His word to Jacob, His statutes and His judgments to Israel: He has not dealt so with any nation, and as for His judgments, He has not made them known to them. But in so far as it was pressed by the various corruptions of the priests, it groaned with the Prophet Isaiah that all its watchmen are blind. Isa. 56, 10.

Latin:

Tertiò urgent Pontificii, ut digito quasi indice monstremus, quenám in individuo fuerit Ecclesia illa, quæ Lutherana nostra per omnia sit ὁμόψηφος.

Respondeo, haud magis opus esse, ut hoc præstemus, quàm opus fuit, ut temporibus Achabi, aliquis Prophetæ Eliæ in individuo monstraret Ecclesiam, quæ ipsi in puritate doctrinæ sit ὁμόψηφος, præsertim cùm conquereretur, se solum ex Orthodoxis adhuc esse superstitem. Quemadmodum ergò Prophetæ sufficiebat, ex DEO cognovisse, plus quàm septem millia Electorum adhuc superesse, quæ non curvassent genua coram Baal, licèt in individuo ipsi illanon monstrarentur: Ita satis nobis est, perspectum cognitumq; habere, sub Papatu Veram fuiffe Ecclesiam, hodieq; esse, licèt in individuo eam monstrare non possimus. Et profectò, si hac nos conditione urgere velint Romanenses, eâdem stent necesse est. Monstrent ergò nobis, quænam & ubi in individuo fuerit Ecclesia vera, sub hæresi Ariana, quæ totum fermè orbem pervagata est? Quam dùm monstrare non possunt, alterutrum fateantur necesse est: 1. Vel Ecclesiam veram penitùs tùm defecisse: id quod simpliciter negamus: 2. Vel illam Ecclesiam veram, monstrari non potuisse:& per consequens, de proprietate & Essentia veræ Ecclesiæ non esse, ut semper digito monstrari possit:id quod nos affirmamus.

est Ecclesiæ administrationem sibi vendicaturus is, qui se extollat supra omne quod est aut dicitur DEUS: 2. Thess. 2. quòd etiam famosa illa Babylon (quam Johannes Apocal. 17. pronunciat esse civitatem magnam, quæ habeat Monarchiam super reges terræ, id est, Romam) spirituali sua fornicatione dementaturus sit reges terræ, & habitantes in ea gentes, & tribus, & linguas, & populos: Apocal. 17. Quomodo ergò quæso illustris tùm esse potuisset Ecclesiæ DEI facies, & purum ac visibile habere ministerium, uti somniant Adversarii? Certè quamprimùm illo tempore aliquis sincerus veritatis confessor conspiciebatur, statim Antichristus eum insecutus est, & ad supplicium rapuit, ebrius de sanguine sanctorum, & de sanguine Martyrum Jesu: Ubi fide & patientia opus fuit. Apocal. 13. Fugit ergò tùm Ecclesia ab oculis & conspectu hominum, & in desertum, in latebras, atq; cavernas concessit, ibiq; multo tempore commorata est. Apoc. 12.

Sextò, sic arguunt Adversarii: Si vera Ecclesia sub Papatu corrupto usa est ministerio: sequetur primùm Ministros illos simul inservisse & DEO, & Diabolo: 2. DEUM in conservandis suis Electis, corrupto etiam uti ministerio. 3. Ecclesiam veram pependisse ex arbitrio Satanæ & Antichristi. 4. Veritatem Evangelij conservari per falsos Doctores. Quæ omnia absurdissima esse, vix quisquam est, quin intelligat.

Quartò, sic insurgunt Adversarii: Christus in cælum ascensurus ordinavit Ministerium Evangelij inter omnes gentes prædicandi: Ephes. 4. E Ecclesia nunquàm destituitur puris Doctoribus.

Respondeo committi Sophisma παρὰ τὸ μὴ ἑπόμενον. Illud enim duntaxat ex Antecedente sequitur, quòd Christus dederit ministros puros, qui annunciarunt Evangelium. Interim autem minimè sequitur, quòd, si DEU singratitudinem & contemtum Verbi sui vindicaturus, errorum efficaciam immittat, 2. Thessal. 2. non etiam ministerium publicum possit esse corruptissimum. Diversum enim status Ecclesiæ Utriusque Testamenti luculenter comprobat, uti hactenùs exemplis demonstratum fuit.

Respondeo absurda hæc partim rationis tantùm nostræ, non autem fidei esse absurda; partim verò ex antecedente minimè consequi. Nam quoad primum illud Absurdum, verum quidem illud est, quòd nemo possit Dominis simul inservire duobus, sed secundum quid tantùm, nempè secundum idem & eodem respectu. Sic ministri etiam illi sub Papatu non potuerunt in una eademque re simul servire DEO & Antichristo: Interim autem potuerunt in iis, quæ DEI sunt, servire DEO: in iis autem quæ Antichristi sunt, servire Antichristo. Quando ergò Baptismum conferebant infantibus, quando prælegebant Evangelia & Epistolas Dominicales, quando moribundis inculcabant meritum Christi, & misericordiam DEI patris: hac certè parte Ministri fuerunt DEI. Quando verò errores affuebant perniciosos, & argentum in scorium commutabant, tùm servi erant Antichristi.

Quintò, obvertunt Adversarii clarissimas DEI promissiones, de perennitate Ecclesiæ, quòd ne quidem portæ inferorum adversus eam sint prævalituræ Ergò inquiunt credibile non est, DEUM Ecclesiam suam ita deseruisse, ut Vera Ecclesia usq; adeò sub errorum tenebris latere necessum habuerit.

Respondeo, ex parte procedere argumentum, & plus inferri in consequente, quàm permittat Antecedens. Plus enim ex eo inferri nequit, quàm Ecclesiam veram nunquàm totam deficere: id quod & nos ultrò fatemur. Cæterùm quòd semper uniformis, & pariter conspicua atque illustris debeat esse Ecclesiæ DEI facies: id profectò indè elici non potest. Nam hic non tantùm promissiones, sed & comminationes Ecclesiæ notandæ veniunt, quibus DEUS tristissimam prædixit sub Antichristi regno seductionem in orbem Christianum exundaturam: & tantam quidem, ut, si possibile foret, in errorem inducerentur etiam Electi: imò talem fore afflictionem, qualis non fuit ab initio mundi ad hoc usq; tempus, neq; futura unquàm Matth. 24. propterea quòd sessurus sit in templo DEI, hoc

Alterum absurdum planè nullum est: Siquidem illud ipsum prædixit DEUS, fore nimirùm, ut Antichristus sedeat in ipso templo DEI, & per suos ministros invadat regimen Ecclesiæ: 2. Thess. 2, 4. Sic DEUS tempore nati Christi usus est corrupto ministerio Pharisæorum. Quod verò per tale ministerium conservantur Electi, illud Accidentis est: neq; ministerio corrupto per se: sed singulari operationi Spiritus Sancti est adscribendum. Observanda proindè piis ac fidelibus illa est regula practica, ut nimirùm sic ferente casu necessitatis & Tyrannidis, Ministerium corruptum non planè negligant: quatenùs nimirùm illud sedet super cathedram Mosis & Prophetarum, Matth. 23, 2. Quatenùs verò corruptelas populo obtrudunt, eatenùs observent præceptum Christi, Matth. 16, 11. Cavete vobis à fermento Pharisæorum & Sadducæorum: Et rursum Matth. 15, 14. Omittite illos: Sunt enim cæci & cæcorum duces.

Tertium absurdum laborat vitioso consequente. Jam modò enim ostendimus, pios & Electos usos esse sub Papatu corrupto ministerio, non quatenus illud Antichristo, sed quatenùs DEO serviebat. Ergò vera etiam Ecclesia non pependit tum simul ex arbitrio Satanæ & Antichristi. Hunc enim ea potiùs oderat & impugnabat.

Deindè Absurdum hoc facilè elidi potest exemplo Ecclesiæ tempore nati Christi, quæ utebatur quidem ministerio Scribarum & Pharisæorum, quatenùs quidem illi sedebant super Cathedram Mosis, & Prophetarum: neque tamen propterea pendebat ab arbitrio Satanæ.

Quartum ac postremum Absurdum, ex falsa procedit hypothesi, quæ est quòd Veritas Evangelii dependeat à qualitate Doctorum Ecclesiæ: Hæc sanè hypothesis vera si esset, tùm tempore Regis Achab, tempore nati Christi, tempore grassantis Arianismi, nulla in toto orbe Christiano fuisset Doctrinæ puritas, ac proindè nulla etiam vera Ecclesia. Corrigimus proindè hypothesin hanc ostendentes, puritatem uti Doctrinæ, sic & Ecclesiæ fundatam esse, non nisi super fundamentum Prophetarum & Apostolorum: hoc est, super Verbum DEI. Hoc verbum, licèt non semper purum & incorruptum servent illi, qui in ministerio sunt constituti: servant tamen illud illibatum ex Auditoribus quam plurimi, qui etiam tum & Veritatem Ecclesiæ & puritatem doctrinæ Evangelicæ custodiunt ac conservant. Semper enim DEUS servat sibi semen aliquod Sanctum, quod simplici corde assentitur Veritati Evangelicæ, valere jussis hæreticorum strophis & corruptelis. Et tali casu Ministri officio fungitur quisq; fidelis, qui errores hæreticorum detegit & reprehendit.

Septimò & postremò objiciunt nobis Adversarii, autoritatem Confessionis Augustanæ, quæ inter notas Veræ Ecclesiæ referat etiam puram Verbi DEI prædicationem & legitimum Sacramentorum usum. Ergò inquiunt de Essentiâ veræ Ecclesiæ est, ut semper habeat Ministerium ex omni parte incorruptum.

Respondeo distinguendo inter Statum Ecclesiæ veræ proprium, sive liberum, & inter statum ejus accidentalem, sive Tyrannide pressum. Confessio ergò Augustana cõsiderat Ecclesiam, quatenùs ea in statu suo proprio & integro liberoq; subsistit: Ubi incorruptum ministerium ad Essentiam Ecclesiæ Veræ requiritur. Secus verò statuendum de statu Ecclesiae presso sive servo, ubi haeretici dominatum obtinent. Hic enim sufficit, ut quale, quale, etiam corruptum sit ministerium: id quod exemplo Ecclesiae Israeliticae sub Veteri Testamento evidenter illustrari potest. Quatenus enim statu suo libero atque integro fruebatur, canebat cum Davide ex Psal. 147. v. 19. & 20. Quia annunciat Verbum suum Jacob: justitias & judicia sua Israel: Non fecit taliter ulli nationi, & judicia sua non manifestavit eis. Quatenus verò pressa erat variis Sacerdotum corruptelis, ingemiscebat cum Propheta Jesaia, quòd omnes speculatores sui sint caeci. Jes. 56, 10.


### Chapter II. Of the attributes: Concerning the first attribute of the Church, which is: Of the Ordinary Succession of Bishops in a certain see

Among the remaining arguments by which the Jesuits today rise up against the Lutheran Churches as if they were new, is that primary one which they take from the ordinary succession of Bishops: arguing that since the Lutherans cannot provide an ordinary succession of Doctors who have followed one another in an uninterrupted series ever since the times of the Apostles, and have taught the same thing as Luther, therefore for this reason alone the Lutheran Church is to be held as false and new: whereas, on the contrary, their own Roman Church, which enjoys such an ordinary succession of Bishops, is to be held as true and most ancient. Hence, therefore, it has come about that a very sharp controversy has arisen between us and the Jesuits concerning this matter: which, in order that it may be defined more fully and more clearly, it must be well observed at the beginning, What properly comes into controversy, and what does not? But it is not being fought over whether there has always been and remained a true Church of GOD in the world. For on both sides this is confessed: as we have already demonstrated before. Nor is it disputed concerning this: Whether ever since the Ascension of Christ the Savior, the true Church has been propagated to us through some never-interrupted succession? For we also hold the affirmative here, although we define that ordinary succession differently than the Jesuits do: as will soon be evident. Thirdly, neither is it asked concerning this: Whether some certain order can or ought to be established among the ministers of the Church? For we do not deny this either, although we abhor the orders of the Romanists as partly superstitious and partly ridiculous.

Finally, neither does this come into Controversy: Whether obedience must be rendered to pastors legitimately called, and duly performing their office? For here too we concede to the affirmative: But this is what comes under contention: Namely, whether the truth of the Church depends infallibly upon an Ordinary, perpetual, and never-interrupted Succession of Bishops in a certain see? So that where such can be shown, there it must undoubtedly be pronounced the true Church: But otherwise, and the contrary must be determined, concerning that Church which is destitute of such a Succession? Concerning which State of the question, we simply hold the Negative, while the Jesuits fight for the Affirmative, strenuously indeed, but with vain success.

Moreover, that the foundations of our Negative may press more strongly upon our Adversaries, we divide this whole Controversy into three general Questions: of which the I. asks: Whether the Church of Christ, and consequently the Truth of the Gospel, be tied, either to any certain place, or to the Ordinary succession of Bishops...?

I I. In what does true Succession consist, from which a judgment can, or rather ought to be, made concerning the truth of the Church? And does it belong properly and truly to our Churches, or rather to those of the Papists?

I I I. Whether such an ordinary succession of place and bishops, as the Romanists imagine, is to be found in the Roman Pseudo-Catholic Church.

Latin:

INter reliqua argumenta, quibus Jesuitae hodiè adversus Lutheranas Ecclesias, tanquàm novas insurgunt, est primarium illud, quod ab ordinaria Episcoporum successione desumunt: arguentes, cum Lutherani non possint dare Ordinariam successionem Doctorum, qui jam indè ab Apostolorum temporibus serie nunquàm interrupta se invicem secuti sint, idemque quod Lutherus, docuerint, ideò vel hanc ob causam Lutheranam Ecclesiam pro falsâ & novâ: contra verò Romanam suam Ecclesiam, quae tali successione Episcoporum ordinaria gaudeat, pro verâ & antiquissimâ habendam esse. Hinc ergò factum, ut de hac materia acris omninò inter nos & Jesuitas oborta sit controversia: quae ut pleniùs ac planiùs definiatur, probè initiò observandum fuerit, Quid propriè in controversiam veniat, quid non? Non autem illud pugnatur, An semper in mundo vera DEI Ecclesia fuerit, & manserit? Utrinque enim hoc in confesso est: uti jam antè demonstravimus. Nequè de eo etiam controvertitur: An jam indè ab Ascensione Christi Servatoris, vera Ecclesia per nunquàm interruptam aliquam successionem, ad nos usque propagata sit? Affirmantem enim & hîc tenemus, licet ordinariam illam successionem aliter atque Jesuitae, definiamus: uti mox patebit. Tertiò neque de eo quaeritur, An certus aliquis ordo inter ministros Ecclesiae constitui possit aut debeat? Neque enim & hoc negamus, licèt ordines Romanensium partim superstitiosos, partim ridiculos aversemur.

Tandem, neque illud in Controversiam venit: An pastoribus legitimè vocatis, & munus suum ritè obeuntibus, sit obtemperandum? Nam & hic in affirmantem concedimus: Sed illud est, quod sub contentionem venit: An videlicet Ecclesiæ veritas infallibiliter pendeat ab Ordinaria, perpetuâ, & nunquàm interrupta Episcoporum, in certa quâdam sede, Successione? ita ut ubi talis monstrari possit, ibi indubitato pro vera Ecclesia pronunciari debeat: Secus verò ac contrarium statuendum sit, de ea Ecclesia, quæ tali Successione destituitur? Circa quem Statum, nos simpliciter Negativam tenemus, Jesuïtis contra pro Affirmativa strenuè quidem, sed irrito successu pugnantibus.

Cæterùm ut Negativæ nostræ fundamenta fortiùs premant Adversarios, dispescimus totam hanc Controversiam in tres Quæstiones generales: quarum I. quærit: An Ecclesia Christi, & consequenter Veritas Evangelij, alligata sit, vel ad certum aliquem locum, vel ad Ordinariam Episcoporum successionem...?

I I. Quâ in re consistat vera Successio, ex qua de Ecclesiæ veritate judicium fieri possit, imo debeat? Et nùm ea nostris, an verò Pontificiorum Ecclesiis propriè ac verè competat?

I I I. Utrum Ordinaria talis successio Loci & Episcoporum, qualem fingunt Romanenses, apud Romanam Pseudo-Catholicam Ecclesiam inveniatur.


### Chapter II. Of the attributes: Question I. Is the True Church of Christ bound to an Ordinary place and to the succession of Bishops?

WHETHER the true Church of Christ is bound to the Ordinary succession of place and Bishops?

Regarding this first Question, we distinguish at the outset between the Church of the Old and of the New Testament. For that ancient Church, which was confined within the narrow borders of Palestine and to the Israelite people alone, was by the command of GOD himself bound to a certain place; as may be seen in Exod. 25, 22: I will meet with you there, and I will speak with you from above the mercy seat, from between the two Cherubim which are upon the ark of the testimony. And Deut. 12, 5: To the place which Jehovah your GOD shall choose out of all your tribes, to put his name there, and to dwell there, you shall come. That this appointed place was in Jerusalem in the time of Solomon is evident from 1 Kings 9, 3, where GOD says to Solomon: I have sanctified this house which you have built, to put my name there. Whence the Lord says through the Prophet that he has his fire in Zion and his furnace in Jerusalem, Isa. 31, v. 9. And David, Psal. 132, 13. 14. Jehovah has chosen Zion, He has desired it for His habitation: This is My rest for ever and ever, here will I dwell, for I have chosen it.

Moreover, GOD himself has not so absolutely bound his worship to that place, that the duration of the true Church and the purity of doctrine should necessarily depend solely upon this succession of place: but with a limitation and with a condition, in so far, namely, as only that which he himself had commanded is taught in that place: Deut. 4, 6. et seqq. and chap. 6. 25. GOD will be merciful, if we shall have kept and done all his commandments before the LORD our GOD, as he has commanded us. Now, indeed, when the Jews, having corrupted the Word of GOD and neglected the commandments of the Lord, were contaminating and corrupting the worship of GOD with various ἐθελοθρησκείαις, certainly the truth of the doctrine did not then depend upon the ordinary place; so that the Prophet might answer the Jews who were boasting of the perpetual succession of the place: Trust ye not in lying words, saying, The temple of the Lord, The temple of the Lord, The temple of the Lord: For if ye thoroughly amend your ways, and walk not after other gods to your hurt, then will I cause you to dwell in this place: Behold, ye trust in lying words. Jerem. 7. 4. et seqq. What of the fact that GOD himself threatens the Jews that he will reject this place and choose another: as in the already cited chapter Jerem. 7. v. 12. Go I pray to my place, which was in Shiloh, where I made my name dwell at the beginning, and see what I have done to it for the wickedness of my people Israel: Now because you have done all these works, I will also do to this house, upon which my name is called, in which you trust, and I will cast you out of my sight. Nor did GOD merely threaten this: but as the wickedness of the people increased, he performed it in reality: so that the place, destined for divine worship, was many times changed, and indeed by GOD himself so disposing. Jacob the Patriarch certainly exercised divine worship in Bethel, a place solemnly consecrated. But GOD later rejected this, and chose Shiloh, where the ark of the mercy seat and the tabernacle of Moses was established. But GOD also rejected this place and chose Gibeah, which place GOD also repudiated, and chose the Jerusalem temple: Which itself however was also later rejected, when according to the prophetic threat, not only the city, but also the Temple was devastated, and burned with fire.

It is therefore most evidently clear, although in the Old Testament GOD destined a certain place for his worship, and indeed even made most ample promises to that place: yet the truth and perennial duration of the Church and doctrine did not even then depend absolutely upon the succession of a place: but only upon the observation of the commandments of the LORD. What therefore, I pray, would be the stupendous madness, under the kingdom of Christ in the New Testament, to urge such a perpetual succession of a Place, that is, of the City of Rome, upon which the Truth of the Church and Doctrine undoubtedly depends, and from thence must necessarily flow down into the remaining particular Churches, as from a head into the members?

It is added in the second place, that the very Nature of the Church of the New Testament by no means admits such an Ordinary succession of Place. For the preaching of the Gospel is no longer to a certain people, but to all nations which are under Heaven: and therefore it was not to a certain place, but to the whole world that it had to spread under the New Testament: according to the Ordinance of Christ, Mark 16, 15. Colossians 1, 6.

Thirdly, Christ himself removes this succession of place, nay, he utterly destroys and overturns it, John 4, 21. For when the Samaritan woman, having been taught thus by the Jews, urged the example of her ancestors and contended that one must worship only in a certain place, the Savior answers: Woman, believe me, the hour is coming, nay, it has already come, when you will worship the Father neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem: (and (verse 23) true worshipers will worship the Father in Spirit and Truth. Where by the word Worship, synecdochically, the entire divine cult is understood, which is not restricted to a certain place; but rather is spread to any corner of the earth where God is served in Spirit and Truth: according to the Prophecy of Malachi 1, 11. From the rising of the sun even to its setting, my name is great among the nations, and in EVERY PLACE incense (metaphorically, every true cult of God is denoted) shall be offered to my name, and a pure offering.

Fourthly, Christ himself confirms that it will be characteristic of false Doctors that they will, forsooth, restrict the Truth of doctrine and the Church to a certain place: to whom, however, one must by no means give credence: They will arise, he says, False Christs and False Prophets, who will say, Behold here is Christ: behold there: But do not believe them, Matthew 24, 23.

Finally, Orthodox Antiquity also opposes this ordinary Succession of Place: as when Jerome writes in Epistle 1 to Heliodorus: They are not the sons of the saints who hold the places of the saints: but those who exercise their works: nor does the chair make the Priest: But the Priest makes the Chair: nor does the place sanctify the man: But the man sanctifies the place: as Chrysostom infers somewhere.

Augustine: Whoever dissents from the Holy Scriptures concerning Christ, who is the head of the Church, in whatever place they are found, in which the Church is designated: they are not in the Church.

The 40th Distinction of the Canon Law Decree also pertains here, where Gregory XIII, Supreme Pontiff, refutes this vain boasting of the Romanists thus: We, who are in charge, ought to become known not by the dignity of Places or Lineage: but by the nobility of our morals: and not by the fame of cities, but by the purity of our faith.

The same Gregory, book 6, Epistle 5. Any hidden places whatsoever cannot save a soul without the grace of God: which is seen in the very errors of the elect. For Lot was righteous in the very perverse city: but he sinned on the mountain: But why do we say these things? when we know greater ones? For what is more pleasant than Paradise? What is more secure than heaven? and yet man fell from Paradise, and an Angel from heaven, by sinning.

Therefore, the figment which the Jesuits urge concerning the Ordinary Succession of Place expires and vanishes into smoke. Nor is that other thing, which they are accustomed to object to us concerning the ordinary succession of Bishops, of any greater strength.

Latin:

AN VERA CHRISTI ECclesia alligata sit ad Ordinariam loci & Episcoporum successionem?

CIrca primam hanc Quæstionem distinguimus initiò inter Ecclesiam Veteris & Novi Testamenti. Vetus enim illa Ecclesia, quæ angustis Palæstinæ finibus, & solo populo Israëlitico includebatur, ex ipsius DEI mandato, ad certum quendam locum erat alligata; ut videre est Exod. 25, 22. Conveniam tecum illuc, & loquar tecum è propitiatorio inter duos Cherubim, quod est supra arcam testimonij. Et Deut. 12, 5. Ad locum quem elegerit Jehova DEUS vester de cunctis tribubus vestris, ut ponat nomen suum ibi, ut habitet ibi, venietis. Hunc locum constitutum fuisse tempore Salomonis Hierosolymis, patet ex 1. Reg. 9, 3. Ubi DEUS ad Salomonem: Sanctificavi domum hanc quam ædificasti, ut ponerem nomen meum ibi. Undè apud Prophetam, ignem suum in Sion, & clibanum in Jerusalem se habere dicit Dominus, Jes. 31, v. 9. Et David Psal. 132, 13. 14. Elegit Jehova Sion, expetijt ut esset habitaculum sibi: Hæc requies mea usque in seculum seculi, hic habitabo, quoniam elegi eam.

Cæterùm non ita absolutè DEUS ipse cultum suum ad locum istum adstrinxit, ut veræ Ecclesiæ duratio, & doctrinæ puritas necessario à sola hac loci successione dependeret: sed limitate & cum conditione, quatenùs nimirùm illud tantùm doceatur in loco illo, quod ipse præceperat: Deut. 4, 6. & seqq. & cap. 6. 25. Erit DEUS misericors, si custodierimus & fecerimus omnia præcepta ejus coram Domino DEO nostro, sicut mandavit nobis. Jam verò cum Judæi corrupto DEI Verbo, & neglectis præceptis Domini, variis ἐθελοθρησκείαις DEI cultum contaminarent, & corrumperent: certè neque veritas doctrinæ tùm ab ordinario loco dependebat: ita ut Propheta Judæis de perpetua loci successione gloriantibus responderet: Nolite confidere in verbis mendacij, dicendo, Templum Domini, Templum Domini, Templum Domini: Quoniam si emendaveritis vias vestras, & post Deos alienos non ambulaveritis in malum vobis, tunc habitare faciam vos in loco isto: Ecce vos confiditis in verbis mendacij. Jerem. 7. 4. & seqq. Quid quòd DEUS ipse comminatur Judæis, se rejecturum locum istum & alium electurum: ut citato jam capite Jerem. 7. v. 12. Ite quæso ad locum meum, qui erat in Siloh, ubi habitare feci nomen meum in principio, & videte, quæ fecerim ei propter malitiam populi mei Israël: Nunc quia fecistis vos omnia Opera hæc, faciam & ego domui huic, super quam invocatum est nomen meum, in qua vos confiditis, & projiciam vos à facie mea. Neque comminatus saltem hoc est DEUS: sed & crescente populi malitiâ reipsa præstitit: ita ut Locus, cultui divino destinatus, multoties mutatus fuerit, & quidem DEO ipso sic disponente. Jacobus certè Patriarcha cultum divinum exercebat in Bethel, loco solenniter consecrato. Sed DEUS hunc postea rejecit, & elegit Siloh, ubi arca propitiatorii & tabernaculum Mosis erat constitutum. Sed & hunc locum repulit DEUS & elegit Gibea, quem ipsum quoque repudiavit DEUS, & elegit templum Hierosolymitanum: Quod ipsum tamen quoque postmodùm rejectum, cùm secundum comminationem propheticam, non urbs modò, sed & Templum devastatum, & igni exustum fuit.

Constat proindè evidentissimè, licèt in Vetere Testamento DEUS cultui suo certum quemdam locum destinaverit, quin etiam loco illi amplissimas promissiones fecerit: Ecclesiæ tamen & doctrinæ veritatem ac perennem durationem, ne tùm quidem pependisse absolutè à loci successione: sed tantùm ab observatione præceptorum DOMINI. Quæ ergò obsecrò stupenda fuerit vesania, sub regno Christi in Novo Testamento talem aliquam perpetuam Loci, hoc est, Urbis Romæ, urgere successionem, à qua Veritas Ecclesiæ & Doctrinæ indubitatò pendeat, & indè in reliquas particulares Ecclesias, tanquàm à capite in membra defluere necessum habeat?

Accedit secundo loco, quòd Natura ipsa Ecclesiæ Novi Testamenti talem Ordinariam Loci successionem minimè admittit. Prædicatio enim Evangelij non ampliùs ad certum quendam populum, sed ad omnes gentes, quæ sub Cælo sunt: ac proindè non ad certum quendam locum, sed ad universum terrarum orbem se debuit sub Novo Testamento diffundere : secundum Ordinationem Christi, Marci 16, 15. Coloss. 1, 6.

Tertiò Christus ipse hanc loci Successionem tollit, imò penitùs destruit & evertit Iob. 4, 21. Cum enim mulier Samaritana sic à Judæis edocta, exemplum majorum suorum urgeret, & non nisi certo loco adorandum esse contenderet, respondet Servator: Mulier crede mihi, veniet hora, imò jam venit, quando neque in monte hoc, neque Hierosolymis adorabitis Patrem: (ed (versu 23.) veri adoratores adorabunt Patrem in Spiritu & Veritate. Ubi Adorationis voce συνεκδοχικῶς universus cultus divinus intelligitur, qui non ad certum locum sit adstrictus; sed potiùs ad quemlibet terræ angolum, Ubi in Spiritu & Veritate servitur Deo, sit diffusus : secundum Vaticinium Malachiæ 1, 11. Ab ortu Solis usg, ad occasum ejus, magnum est nomen meum inter gentes, & in OMNI LOCO incensum (metaphoricè notatur omnis verus cultus Dei) offeretur nomini meo, & oblatio munda.

Quartò Christus ipse confirmat, hoc fore proprium falsorum Doctorum, ut nimirùm ad certum quendam locum, Veritatem doctrinæ & Ecclesiæ sint adstricturi : quibus tamen minimè sit credendum : Surgent, inquiens, Pseudo Christi & Pseudoprophetæ, dicturi, Ecce hic est Christus: ecce illic: Vos autem nolite credere, Matth. 24, 23.

Tandem repugnat ordinariæ etiam huic Loci Successioni Orthodoxa Antiquitas : ut quando Hieronymus scribit Epist. 1. ad Heliodorum : Non sanctorum sunt filij, qui loca tenent Sanctorum: sed qui exercent opera eorum: nec cathedra facit Sacerdotem: Sed Sacerdos Cathedram: nec locus sanctificat hominem: Sed homo sanctificat locum : uti alicubi infert Chrysostomus.

Augustinus: Quicunque de Christo capite Ecclesia, à Scripturis Sanctis dissentiunt, quocunq; loco inventantur, in quo Ecclesia designata est : illi non sunt in Ecclesia.

Pertinet huc etiam Distinctio 40. Decreti Juris Canonici, ubi Gregorius XIII P. M. vanam hanc Romanensium gloriationem sic retundit : Nos, qui præsumus non ex Locorum vel Generis dignitate: sed morum nobilitate innotescere debemus: nec urbium claritate, sed fidei puritate.

Idem Gregorius libro 6. Epist. 5. Quælibet occulta loca sine gratia Dei salvare animam non possunt: quod conspicitur in ipsis erratis electorum. Nã Loth in ipsa perversa civitate fuit justus : in monte autem peccavit: Sed cur ista dicimus? cùm majora noverimus? Quid enim Paradiso jucundius? Quid cælo securius? & tamen homo ex Paradiso, & Angelus de cælo, peccando cecidit.

Expirat proindè & in fumum evanescit figmentum, quod de Ordinaria Loci Successione urgent Jesuuvitæ. Neque majoris firmitudinis est illud alterum, quod de ordinariâ Episcoporum successione nobis obvertere solent.


### Chapter II. Of the attributes: On the Ordinary Succession of Bishops

ON THE ORDINARY SUCCESSION OF BISHOPS.

IN the Old Testament, God willed that there be a certain succession of High Priests or Pontiffs, and one indeed restricted to a certain tribe: But that for this reason the Truth of the Church and of doctrine was absolutely and simply restricted to this very succession of Bishops: that, certainly, God never said or willed. Nay, the contrary can rather be demonstrated from the Scriptures. For 1. those very High Priests or Pontiffs, notwithstanding the ordinary succession which they enjoyed, fell into horrendous errors, nay, into open Idolatry: as Aaron, the first Pontiff of the Jewish Church, who, while Moses was staying on the mountain for a long time, publicly instituted Idolatry and bound the whole people to a huge crime: Exodus 32, 2. Thus Aaron's two sons, Nadab and Abihu, offering strange fire against the commandment of the Lord, provoked the wrath of God in such a way that fire went out from him and devoured them: Leviticus 10, 1. and 2. Thus Uriah the Pontiff, established in the ordinary succession, built an Idolatrous altar in the temple of the Lord for the sake of the wicked king Ahaz: 2 Kings 16, 11. 15, 16. Thus the remaining priests, almost all of them, fell into similar Idolatry, so far were they from having preserved the Truth of the Church and of doctrine through the ordinary succession which they enjoyed. In the time of King Josiah, the priests and almost the entire people had so defected from God to Idols that the very volume of the Law itself had been lost, 2 Kings 22, 8. In the times of Isaiah, the Pontiffs or Priests did not know because of wine, and they erred because of drunkenness: so much so that the Prophet groaned: The watchmen of the people are all blind: they have all not known, Isaiah 28, 7. and chapter 56, 10. In the times of the Prophet Jeremiah, the Lord complains that the Shepherds do not feed, but scatter and destroy their sheep, Jeremiah 23, 2. that from the Prophet even to the Priest all deal falsely, Jeremiah 6, 13. that they have not known the Lord, that they neglect the law of the Lord, that they prophesy in Baal, Jeremiah 2, 8.

At the time of Christ being brought forth in the flesh, the high priests were Annas, Caiaphas, John, and Alexander: Acts 4:6, who had derived their pontificate from Aaron through an ordinary succession sanctioned by God himself. But meanwhile, they were the most sworn enemies of Christ and the Gospel: a fact which the history of the passion of Christ, as well as that of the Acts of the Apostles, clearly proves.

Hence, against the ordinary succession of bishops, which the Jesuits urge today, I infer as follows for the first argument of our confirmation:

If that ordinary succession, which had God himself as its author and institutor, and which was a type and figure of the eternal priesthood of Christ, could not preserve the purity of doctrine and the truth of the Church, then certainly that fictitious succession of bishops, which the Romanists require without a mandate from God as an infallible mark of the true Church, will be much less able to achieve this. But the former is true, as has already been shown. Therefore, this latter is also valid. And indeed, such is the force of this first argument that the apostate Pistorius could nowhere find what to answer, but replied quite childishly that he was less concerned about the Church of the Old Testament: In discept. de Ecclesia, p. 18. 256. 261. 262. By which single exception, he betrayed the vanity of his cause quite manifestly.

A second argument for our confirmation, flowing from the former, is as follows: If in the Old Testament the truth of the Church and the purity of doctrine did not depend upon the ordinary succession of priests, neither will it depend upon it in the New Testament. But the former is true, as has already been demonstrated. Therefore, the latter is true also.

The connection of the Major is evident from this, that the condition of both Churches is one and the same regarding the truth and purity of doctrine: the same foundation in both: the same mark in both. 2. In the New Testament, divine worship is not, as in the Old, bound either to a certain nation or to a certain tribe: But among every people, in every place, whoever shall worship God rightly, God now dwells, the partition of the middle wall having been broken down through Christ: Ephes. 2, 14.

The third argument of our confirmation is shown by those testimonies of Scripture which vehemently rebuke and disapprove of confidence in such an ordinary succession of Bishops as carnal and impious: as that the Savior in John 8:39 et seqq. sharply rebuked the Jews for the very reason that they measured the truth of their Church and Religion by a carnal succession from Abraham: which the Savior shows is not to be valued so highly, that the Jews are rather sons of their father the Devil, in that they do not imitate the faith and works of Abraham, but fashion for themselves a worship of their own from the instinct of the Devil.

To what purpose does that inference of the Apostle pertain, Rom. 9, 6. Not all who are of Israel are Israel; nor are they all children because they are the seed of Abraham: but in Isaac shall your seed be called: that is, as the Apostle interprets in Gal. 3, 7, & 9. They who are of faith, they are the children of Abraham, and shall be blessed with him.

The fourth argument may be drawn from the authority of the princes of the Apostles, Peter and Paul: the former of whom attests in express words that the Church is not bound to Bishops who succeed one another in place by ordinary succession, asserting that there shall be lying teachers in the Church who shall bring in pernicious sects, denying the Lord who bought them, and who shall bring the way of truth into disrepute, and through covetousness shall make merchandise of the elect with feigned words, 2 Pet. 2 & seqq.; the latter indeed (Paul) clearly foretold that the Antichrist or Roman Pontiff would sit in the very Temple of God, 2 Thess. 2, 4, nay, that from that very ordinary succession of Bishops, men would arise speaking perverse things, so as to draw away disciples after them, Acts 20, 30.

Fifth, if the Church of Christ consists in the ordinary succession of Bishops, and is bound to it, it will follow that it has also depended upon the most wicked men, nay, upon the very slaves of the Devil. The reason for this consequence is evident in two ways. For 1. Ecclesiastical history testifies that in those very Churches which had been planted by the Apostles, there succeeded, soon after the times of the Apostles, such men as asserted anything rather than the Truth of the Church. Peter had planted the Church of Antioch. But in the succession of that Church, Paul of Samosata immediately presents himself. Mark the Evangelist planted the Church of Alexandria: but from the succession of that Church came forth Arius.

The Romanists pretend that Peter himself planted the Roman Church: And yet he had successors among the other sons of perdition, including Marcellinus, who sacrificed to idols in the temple of Isis and Vesta; likewise, Liberius, infected with the Arian heresy; Anastasius II, likewise favoring the heretic Acacius, and for that reason excommunicated by the Roman clergy; Sylvester II, practicing magical arts, consulting devils, and delivering himself alive to them; Gregory VII and several of his predecessors, ascending to the pinnacle of the Roman See by magical arts and the work of Satan: whom Platina himself, a Papal writer, calls most hideous monsters. Furthermore, the logic of the consequence is evident even from the fact that those who, through manifest tyranny, strove to extirpate the true Church and its steadfast confessors rather than to cherish or preserve them, are included by the Romanists themselves in the catalog of this ordinary succession.

Sixth: Such ordinary succession is something external, carnal, and personal: but the Savior by no means willed that His Church be bound to conditions of this kind. Therefore. The minor premise is evident from these testimonies of Scripture.

Matth. 12, 46. Luc. 8, 20. when some said that his mother and brothers were outside, Christ, stretching out his hand, replied: Behold these are my brothers, who do the will of my heavenly Father.

John 1:13. The same Savior excludes every carnal privilege regarding the Truth of the Church: He says, He gave them power to become the sons of God, to them who were born, not of blood, nor of the will of man, nor of the will of the flesh: But of God.

Seventhly and lastly: Although the authority of Ordinary Succession was great in the primitive Church, especially when the dispute was about the authority of Ecclesiastical Writers, and likewise about the orthodoxy of certain particular Churches: where those were considered true Churches more quickly and easily which made use of the ministry of such Theologians as had descended from the very successors of the Apostles: yet in the progress of time, and through the various vicissitudes and siftings of Christian affairs and of the Church itself, it has utterly expired. And indeed what the Orthodox fathers determined concerning it is evident from their own reckoning.

Augustine against Petilian the Donatist, book 2, chapter 16: We do not say that we ought to be believed because Optatus of Milevis, or Ambrose of Milan, or countless other bishops have commended the very see which we hold. That which he says in his Commentary on Psalm 71 is the same as if someone were to say: I am of Paul, I of Apollos, I of Cephas; for which it should be said to all: I am of Christ: For this is justice, not to prefer servants to the Lord, nor to make them equal.

Hilary, in his work against Auxentius concerning the Church of his own times, testifies that it lies hidden in caverns rather than shining forth in primary seats and the eminence of bishops.

Jerome: Not all bishops are bishops: you attend to Peter, but consider also Judas: you look up to Stephen, but consider also Nicolaus, whom the Lord condemns in His Apocalypse.

Latin:

DE ORDINARIA EPIscoporum Successione.

IN Veteri Testamento, Deus certam summorum Sacerdotum sive Pontificum succesionem, & ad certam quidem tribum adstrictam esse voluit: Sed ut ideò Veritas Ecclesiæ & doctrinæ, ad hanc ipsam Episcoporum successionem esset absolutè & simpliciter adstricta: illud certè Deus nuspiam vel dixit vel voluit. Quin contrarium potiùs ex Scripturis demonstrari potest. Nam 1. illi ipsi Summi Sacerdotes sive Pontifices, non obstante ordinariâ Successione, quâ gaudebant, in horrendos errores, imò in apertam Idololatriam sunt prolapsi: ut Aaron primus Ecclesiæ Judaicæ Pontifex, qui Mose diutiùs in monte commorante Idololatriam publicè instituit, & totum populum ingenti scelere obstrinxit: Exod 32,2. Sic Aaronis duo filij, Nadab & Abihu, offerentes ignem alienum contra præceptum Domini, iram Dei ita provocarunt, ut ignis ab eo egressus devoraverit ipsos: Levit. 10,1. & 2. Sic Urias Pontifex in ordinaria successione constitutus, altare Idololatricum in gratiam impij regis Achabi extruxit in templo Domini: 2. Reg. 16, 11. 15, 16. Sic Sacerdotes reliqui fermè universi, in similem Idololatriam sunt prolapsi, tantùm abest, ut Veritatem Ecclesiæ & doctrinæ, per ordinariam, quâ gaudebant, successionem conservârint. Tempore Iosiæ Regis Sacerdotes & populus penè universus à Deo ad Idola ita defecerat, ut ipsum quoque volumen Legis fuerit amissum, 2. Reg. 22,8. Temporibus Jesaiæ, Pontifices sive Sacerdotes præ vino nesciverunt, & præ ebrietate erraverunt: adeò ut Propheta ingemisceret: Speculatores populi cæci omnes: nesciverunt universi, Ies. 28, 7. & cap. 56, 10. Temporibus Prophetæ Jeremiæ conqueritur Dominus, quòd Pastores non pascant, sed dispergant & profligent oves suas, Ierm 23, 2. quòd à Propheta usque ad Sacerdotem omnes faciant mendacium, Ierem. 6, 13. quòd non noverint Dominum, quòd legem Domini negligant, quòd prophetent in Baal, Ierem. 2, 8.

Tempore Christi in carnem editi Sacerdotes summi erant Hannas, Caiphas, Iohannes & Alexander: Actor. 4, 6. qui Pontificatum suum ab Aarone per ordinariam, & à Deo ipso sancitam successionem deduxerant. At interim juratissimi erant hostes Christi & Evangelij: id quod historia passionis Christi, ut & Actorum Apostolicorum luculenter comprobat.

Hinc contra ordinariam Episcoporum Successioné, quam hodiè urgét Jesuitæ, pro primo confirmationis nostræ argumento, sic infero:

Si ea ordinaria successio, quæ Deum ipsum autorem & institutorem habuit, quæq; typus & figura erat æterni Sacerdotij Christi, non potuit conservare puritatem doctrinæ, & Veritatem Ecclesiæ: multò certè minus hoc præstare poterit fictitia illa Episcoporum successio, quam sine mandato Dei, tanquàm infallibilem notam veræ Ecclesiæ requirunt Romanenses. Atqui prius est verum, uti jam ostensum. Ratum ergò & hoc posterius. Et profectò tanta vis est primi hujus argumenti, ut Apostata Pistorius quid responderet, nuspiam inveniret: sed satis pueriliter exciperet, se de Ecclesia Veteris Testamenti minùs esse sollicitum: In discept. de Ecclesia, p. 18.256.261.262. Quâ vel unâ exceptione, causæ suæ vanitate satis manifestè prodidit.

Alterum confirmationis nostræ argumentum ex priore profluens tale est: Si in Veteri Testamento Veritas Ecclesiæ, & Doctrinæ puritas non pependit, ab ordinaria Sacerdotum successione: neque in Novo Testamento ab ea pendebit. At prius Verum, uti jam demonstratum. Verum ergò & posterius.

Connexum Majoris indè patet, quòd una est eademque utriusque Ecclesiæ, quoad Veritatem & puritatem doctrinæ, conditio: idem utrobique fundamentum: eadem utrobique nota. 2. In Novo Testamento cultus divinus, non ut in Veteri, vel ad certam gentem, vel ad certam tribum est alligatus: Sed in omni populo, ubique locorum, qui Deum rectè coluerit, habitat nunc Deus, disrupto parietis intergerini septo per Christum: Ephes. 2, 14.

Tertium confirmationis nostræ argumentum ea monstrant Scripturæ testimonia, quæ fiduciam in talem ordinariam Episcoporum successionem tanquàm carnalem & impiam, vehementer redarguunt, & improbant: ut quòd Servator Johan. 8, 39. & seqq. Judæos vel idcò acriter objurgavit, quod Ecclesiæ & Religionis suæ veritatem metiantur ex carnali successione ab Abrahamo: Quam tanti non faciendam esse, ostendit Servator, ut potiùs Judæi sint filij patris Diaboli, eò quòd non Abrahæ fidem & opera imitentur, sed ex instinctu Diaboli proprium sibi cultum effingant.

Quò pertinet illa Apostoli illatio, Rom. 9, 6. Non omnes, qui sunt ex Israele, sunt Israel; neq; qui semen Abrahæ, illi etiam filij: sed in Isaac vocabitur tibi semen: hoc est, interprete Apostolo Gal. 3, 7, & 9. Qui ex fide sunt, illi sunt filij Abraham, & cum eo benedicentur.

Quartum argumentum peti potest ab autoritate principum Apostolorum, Petri & Pauli: quorum ille disertis verbis attestatur, Ecclesiam non esse alligatam ad Episcopos, qui sibi invicem in loco ordinariè succesdant: asserens, futuros in Ecclesia Magistros mendaces, qui introducturi sint sectas perniciosas, abnegantes Dominum, qui redemit eos, quique viam veritatis, maledictis sint incessuri: & per avaritiam factis sermonibus de Electis negotiaturi. 2. Petr. 2. & seqq. hic verò (Paulus) clarè prædixit Antichristum sive Pontificem Romanum sessurum in ipso Templo Dei, 2. Thess. 2, 4. imò ex illâ ipsâ ordinariâ successione Episcoporum, proventuros viros, loquentes perversa, ut abducant discipulos post se, Act. 20, 30.

Quintò, si Ecclesia Christi in ordinaria Episcoporum successione consistit, ad eamque est alligata, sequetur eam etiam à sceleratissimis hominibus, imò ab ipsis Diaboli mancipiis pependisse. Ratio consequentiæ patet dupliciter. Nam 1. testatur Ecclesiastica historia, quòd in illis ipsis Ecclesiis, quæ ab Apostolis erant plantatæ, mox post Apostolorum tempora successerint tales, qui nihil minùs quàm Veritatem Ecclesiæ asseruerunt. Antiochenam Ecclesiam Petrus plantaverat. At in successione illius Ecclesiæ statim se offert Paulus Samosatenus. Alexandrinam Ecclesiam Marcus Evangelista plantavit: at ex illius Ecclesiæ successione prodijt Arius.

Petrum fingunt Romanenses plantasse ipsam Romanam Ecclesiam: Atqui successores habuit inter reliquos perditionis filios, etiam Marcellinum, qui in templo Isidis & Vestæ Idolis sacrificavit: item, Liberium, hæresi Ariana infectum: Anastasium II. itidem hæretico Acatio faventem, ac à Clero Romano propterea excommunica tum: Sylvestrum II. artes Magicas exercentem, Diabolos consulentem eisq; se vivum tradentem: Gregorium IIX. & aliquot ipsius anteces sores, magicis artibus, operâque Satanæ Sedis Romanæ fastigium ascendentes: quos Platina ipse Scriptor Pontificius monstra teterrtma appellat. Deindè patet consequentiæ ratio vel indè, quòd ab ipsis Romanensibus in Catalogum Ordinariæ hujus Successionis referuntur illi, qui per manifestam Tyrannidem veram Ecclesiam, ejusque constantes confessores potius exscindere, quàm fovere aut conservare studuerunt.

Sextò: Successio talis ordinaria est externum quippiam, carnale, & personale: Atqui Servator Ecclesiam suam ad hajusmodi conditiones astringi nullo modo voluit. Ergò. Minor patet ex his Scripturæ testimonijs

Matth. 12, 46. Luc. 8, 20. cùm nonnulli matrem & fratres foris esse dicerent, Christus protensa manu respondet: Ecce hi sunt fratres mei, qui faciunt voluntatem Patris cælestis.

Johan. 1, 13. idem Servator omne carnale privilegium circa Veritatem Ecclesiæ excludit: Dedit inquit eis potestatem filios Dei fieri his, qui non ex sanguinibus, neque ex Voluntate viri, neque ex Voluntate carnis: Sed ex Deo nati sunt.

Septimò & postremò: Etsi Successionis Ordinariæ magna fuit autoritas in primitiva Ecclesia, præcipuè quando disputatio erat de autoritate Scriptorum Ecclesiasticorum, item de orthodoxia Ecclesiarum quarundam particularium: ubi pro veris Ecclesiis citiùs ac faciliùs habebantur, quæ uterentur ministerio ejusmodi Theologorum, qui ab ipsis Apostolorum successoribus descendissent: temporum tamen progressu, & varijs rerum Christianarum, ac ipsius Ecclesiæ vicissitudinibus ac cribrationibus, ea penitùs expiravit. Et sanè quid de ea statuerint Orthodoxi patres, ipsorummet calculo constat.

Augustinus contra Petil. Donat. l. 11. cap. 16. Nos non propterea dicimus nobis credi oportere, quia ipsam, quam tenemus sedem, commendavit Optatus Milevitanus, vel Mediolanensis Ambrosius, vel alij innumerabiles Episcopi. Id quod in Commentario ad Psalmum 71. dicit esse idem, ac si quis dicat: Ego sum Pauli, ego Apollo, ego Cephæ; pro quo dicendum sit omnibus: Ego sum Christi: Hæc enim est justicia, non anteponere servos Domino, nec æquare.

Hilarius adversus Auxentium de suorum temporum Ecclesiâ testatur, eam potiùs in cavernis delitescere, quàm in primarijs sedibus & Episcoporum eminentiâ elucere.

Hieron. Non omnes Episcopi sunt Episcopi: Attendis Petrum, sed & Judam: Stephanum suspiciis, sed & Nicolaum respice, quem Dominus in Apocalypsi sua damnat.


### Chapter II. Of the attributes: Question II. In what thing the True Church's succession consists: and whether the force of our (claim), or whether it belongs to the…

In what thing does the true succession of the Church consist: and whether it belongs to ours, or to the Papal Church?

The true succession of the Church is not founded in persons and places: but entirely in the doctrine of Christ: and as Tertullian speaks in his De Praescriptione, it depends entirely on the consanguinity of doctrine. Concerning this succession, which is of the essence of the true Church, and is most simply convertible with it, the prophet Isaiah treats in chapter 33, verses 20, 21, and 22. Look upon Zion, the city of our solemnities; thine eyes shall see Jerusalem a quiet habitation, a tabernacle that shall not be taken down; not one of the stakes thereof shall ever be removed, neither shall any of the cords thereof be broken. But there the glorious Lord will be unto us a place of broad rivers and streams; for the Lord is our judge, the Lord is our lawgiver, the Lord is our king; he will save us. Thus God himself willed that judgment concerning the truth and eminence of the Jewish Church be made only from the purity of the Word: Exod. 19, 5. If ye will obey my voice indeed, and keep my covenant, then ye shall be a peculiar treasure unto me above all people. Levit. 26, 3 and 11. If ye walk in my statutes, and keep my commandments, I will set my tabernacle among you, and my soul shall not abhor you. Isa. 8, 20. To the law and to the testimony: if they speak not according to this word, it is because there is no light in them. In the New Testament, Christ and the Apostles knew no other succession of the Church than that which consists in the purity of doctrine: as John 15, 7. If ye abide in me, and my words abide in you, ye shall be my true disciples, and ye shall know the truth. Ephes. 2, 20 and following. Built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ himself being the chief corner stone; in whom all the building fitly framed together groweth unto an holy temple in the Lord: in whom ye also are builded together for an habitation of God through the Spirit. According to this description of true succession, those are properly said to succeed into the place of the primitive Apostolic Church who profess the same doctrine and faith as it. Those who hold this are the true successors of the Apostles and of the faithful of all times, and in all places: nay, even the children of Abraham himself, the part of the believers, Rom. 9, 6 and following, Gal. 3, 7. To which sentiment Nazianzen also writes excellently in his Oration in praise of Athanasius: The succession of faith, διαδοχὴ πίστεως, is properly to be esteemed succession. For he who professes the same doctrine of faith is also a participant of the same throne: but he who embraces a contrary faith ought to be considered an adversary also on the throne: ὁ μὲν γὰρ ὁμόγνωμον καὶ ὁμόθρονον: τὸ δὲ ἀντίδοξον καὶ ἀντίθρονον: And this indeed has the name: but that has the thing itself and the truth of succession, ἀλήθειαν ἔχει διαδοχῆς: as the Greek words have it.

Furthermore, whether the eulogy of this true and Apostolic succession belongs to ours, that is, the genuine Lutheran, or rather to the Roman Church: let every pious person judge, namely, he who has learned to compare Apostolic doctrine with ours. But it can be an altogether infallible argument that not the Roman, but our Church is conformable to the Apostolic in doctrine, because we determine that our entire doctrine is to be examined and judged by no other standard and rule than that of the Apostolic writings: but the Romanists so greatly fear the Apostolic censure that they do not fear to write publicly that the judge of all dogmas is not the Holy Spirit speaking in the Prophetic and Apostolic Scriptures: but the Roman Pontiff, namely, a witness in his own cause.

These things being thus presupposed, it is clear what must be answered to that classic question which the Romanists frequently carry in their mouths: Namely, whether the blessed Luther had predecessors to whom he legitimately succeeded. For by a distinction the whole matter is most rightly resolved. For if the question is about true and legitimate succession, which consists in conformity of Apostolic doctrine, we answer affirmatively, that the blessed Luther had as predecessors the Apostles themselves, likewise the Doctors and Fathers of the purer antiquity: and finally all those who asserted the foundation of Apostolic doctrine whole and intact, who manfully contradicted the Papacy, and who finally bore witness to the Truth even by the shedding of blood. But if the question is about that spurious and illegitimate succession of bishops, such as the Jesuits urge, then we willingly concede that such a succession is clearly none in the Lutheran Church: nay, that it neither can nor ought to be for us. The reason is: Because if Luther had had orthodox predecessors in the ministry of the Church, if the Roman bishops and priests had not defected from the true Church: then there would never have been need for the Lutheran Reformation. Therefore, just as the Apostle Paul did not incur the mark of a false doctor because he was destitute of all ordinary succession, and was called neither by men nor through men, Gal. 1, 1. Just as the remaining Apostles also, lacking this ordinary succession, were nevertheless true Doctors of the Church: So the lack of this fictitious succession detracts nothing from our blessed Luther, so that he should not be named a true and orthodox Doctor of the Church.

Nor is there any reason for the Jesuit to object that the example of the Apostles was a thing clearly new and singular. For this brings no help to the Jesuit's cause: but rather confirms ours. For this is placed in the custom and habit of God, that when those who were in the ordinary succession defect from the true Church, God always raises up orthodox Doctors of the Church outside the order. Thus he raised up outside the order the prophets, Christ, the Apostles: and in the previous century the blessed Luther, and his faithful assistants or colleagues.

Latin:

Qua in re consistat Vera Ecclesiæ successio: & num nostra, an Pontificiæ Ecclesiæ ea competat?

VEra Ecclesiæ Successio non in personis locisq́; : sed tota in doctrina Christi fundatur: & ut Tertull. de præscript. loquitur, tota ex consanguinitate doctrinæ dependet. De hac Successione, quæ est de Essentia veræ Ecclesiæ, & cum ea simplicissimè convertitur, agit Propheta Iesaias cap 33. 20. 21. & 22. Respice Sion civitatem solennitatis nostræ, oculi tui videbunt Ierusalem habitationem quietam, tabernaculum quod non transferetur, nec emigrabunt clavi ejus in seculum, & cuncti funes ejus non rumpentur quia solummodo ibi magnificus est Dominus noster: Dominus enim judex noster: Dominus legifer noster, Dominus rex noster: ipse salvabit nos. Sic DEUS ipse de Ecclesiæ Judaicæ Veritate & eminentia tantùm ex Verbi puritate judicium fieri voluit: Exod. 19, 5. Si custodieritis pactum meum: si obedieritis voci meæ, eritis mihi thesaurus dilectus præ omnibus populis. Levit. 26, 3. & 11. Si in decretis meis ambulaveritis, & præcepta mea servaveritis, ponam tabernaculum meum in medio vestri, neque abominabitur vos anima mea. Jes 8, 20. Ad Legem & ad Testimonium: Nisi dixerint secundum hoc, non videbunt auroram matutinam. In Novo Testamento Christus & Apostoli non aliam noverunt Ecclesiæ successionem, quàm quæ in doctrinæ puritate consistat: ut Johan. 15, 7. Si manseritis in me, & verba mea manserint in vobis, veri discipuli mei eritis, & cognoscetis Veritatem. Ephes. 2, 20. & seqq. Ædificati super fundamentum Apostolorum & Prophetarum, ipso summo angulari lapide Christo Jesu, in quo omnis ædificatio constructa crescit in templum Sanctum Domino, in quo & vos coædificamini in tabernaculum Dei in Spiritu S. Secundum hanc descriptionem Veræ Successionis, dicuntur propriè in locum Ecclesiæ primitivæ Apostolicæ succedere, qui eandem cum ea profitentur doctrinam & fidem. Hanc quitent, sunt veri Successores Apostolorum & fidelium omnium temporum, & ubique locorum: quin ipsius etiam Abrahami Partis credentium filij, Rom. 9, 6. & seqq. Gal. 3, 7. Quam in sententiam præclarè etiam scribit Nazianzenus Orat. in laudem Athanasij: Successio fidei, διαδοχὴ πίστεως, propriè successio est æstimanda. Nam qui eandem fidei doctrinam profitetur, ejusdem quoq; throni particeps est: qui autem contrariam fidem amplectitur, adversarius quoq; in throno censeri debet: ὁ μὲν γὰρ ὁμόγνωμον καὶ ὁμόθρονον: τὸ δὲ ἀντίδοξον καὶ ἀντίθρονον: Atque hæc quidem nomen: illa verò rem ipsam & veritatem habet successionis, ἀλήθειαν ἔχει διαδοχῆς: ut Græca verba habent.

Cæterum, num veræ hujus & Apostolicæ Successionis elogium nostræ hoc est, γνησι Lutheranæ, an verò Romanæ Ecclesiæ competat: judicet pius quisque, ille videlicet, qui doctrinam Apostolicam cum nostra conferre didicit. Argumento autem prorsus infallibili esse potest, non Romanam, sed nostram Ecclesiam Apostolicæ in doctrina esse conformem, quòd nos universam doctrinam nostram non nisi secundum Canonem & amussim Scriptorum Apostolicorum examinandam dijudicandamque esse statuimus: Romanenses verò censuram Apostolicam usque adeò reformidant, ut pubolicè scribere non vereantur, Judicem omnium dogmatum non esse Spiritum sanctum in Scripturis Propheticis & Apostolicis loquentem: Sed Pontificem Romanum, nempè testem in causa propria.

His ita præsuppositis, patet quid respondendum sit ad Quæstionem illam classicam, quam subindè in ore ferunt Romanenses: An videlicet B. Lutherus antecessores habuerit, quibus ipse legitimè successerit. Nam per distinctionem res omnis rectissimè expeditur. Si enim de vera ac legitima Successione, quæ in doctrinæ Apostolicæ conformitate consistit, sit quæstio, respondemus affirmatè, B. Lutherum antecessores habuisse ipsos Apostolos, item Doctores & Patres purioris Antiquitatis: Omnes deniq; eos, qui doctrinæ Apostolicæ fundamentum sartum tectum asseruerunt, qui Papatui masculè contradixerunt, qui denique sanguinis etiam profusione Veritati testimonium perhibuerunt. Sin autem de spuria illa & illegitima successione Episcoporum, qualem urgent Jesuvvitæ, sit quæstio, tùm ultrò concedimus, talem Successionem in Ecclesia Lutherana planè nullam esse: quin imò nec esse nobis posse aut debere. Ratio est: Quia si Lutherus in Ecclesiæ ministerio antecessores habuisset Orthodoxos, si Episcopi & Sacrificuli Romani ab Ecclesia vera non defecissent: tùm nunquàm opus fuisset Reformatione Lutherana: Quemadmodum ergò Paulus Apostolus non ideò falsi Doctoris notam incurrebat, quod omni prorsus Ordinariâ Successione destitutus, neque ab hominibus, neque per homines vocatus esset Gal. 1, 1. Quemadmodum reliqui etiam Apostoli Successione hac ordinaria carentes, Veri tamen Doctores Ecclesiæ erant: Ita B. Luthero nostro nihil quicquam Successionis hujus fictitiæ carentia derogat, quò minùs verus & Orthodoxus Ecclesiæ Doctor nominari debeat.

Neque est, ut excipiat Jesuvvita, Apostolorum exemplum novum planè ac singulare quiddam fuisse. Nam nihil hoc causæ Jesuvvitæ affert præsidij: sed nostram potiùs confirmat. Hoc enim in more ac consuetudine Deo est positum, ut deficientibus à Vera Ecclesia ijs, qui in ordinariâ erant successione, Deus semper extra ordinem excitet Doctores Ecclesiæ Orthodoxos. Sic excitavit extra ordinem Prophetas, Christum, Apostolos: & superiore seculo B. Lutherum, & fideles ipsius parastatas sive collegas.


### Chapter II. Of the attributes: Question III. Whether the Roman Church truly glories in the ordinary and never-interrupted succession of Place and Bishops?

To this proposed question, we answer by simply denying it, on account of the following reasons, which are by far the most evident.

For 1. this fictitious succession of Roman bishops lacks its head, which they wish to be the Apostle Peter. For it is uncertain concerning him whether he ever reached Rome: more uncertain whether he remained there for 25 years: most uncertain that he acted as bishop there. Now, because it is established beyond all doubt from the Scriptures that Peter presided over the Church of Antioch for many years, it would follow that an ordinary succession of bishops, provided it depends upon Peter as its head, is restricted to the Church of Antioch, and not indeed to the Roman; and consequently, that not Rome, but Antioch, is the proper seat of apostolic succession. Or if the Jesuits are unwilling to grant this, they must necessarily admit that there are two different apostolic seats, and therefore also a double ordinary succession of bishops. This being granted, the whole structure of this figment immediately collapses, concerning one apostolic seat, and concerning one perpetual succession of bishops emanating from it.

Furthermore, this papal succession has been interrupted many times. Certainly in the year of our Lord 1045, there were three Popes, or rather Antipopes, at the same time, who all at one and the same time aspired to, or rather occupied, the papal chair, namely Benedict VI, Sylvester III, and Gregory VI, who each ordained several bishops, by whom others were in turn created.

Thirdly, these three Antipopes, after a foul schism had been stirred up, were all condemned by a Synod and cast down from the papal seat, with the Bishop of Bamberg, Clement II, being elected as Pope.

Fourthly, the papal chair was vacant several times for two years, as attested by Platina and Volaterranus.

Fifthly, an infamous harlot, a female pope, who had assumed the name of John VIII, held the papal seat. Thus, therefore, the succession of Roman bishops co-opts into its order female harlots, perhaps by the example of Christ, who in his kindness received the sinner Mary Magdalene, and the woman taken in adultery, John 8, 11.

Sixthly: The papal seat was moved from its place, and migrated from Italy into France, and remained there for over seventy years.
