Quicunq́; enim in substantialibus institutionem Servatoris, inviolatam retinent, deq́; Sacrosanctâ Trinitate, in cujus nomine Baptismus peragitur, rectè sentiunt: licèt in alijs doctrinæ Christianæ capitibus, errorem aliquem, & quidem in fundamentum fidei impingentem, foveant: illi verum & salutarem Baptismum administrant, Quâ de causâ à Pontificijs & Calvinianis baptizatos, verè ac ritè baptizatos esse statuimus. Neq́; obstat, quod Calvinianorum nonnulli ad castraArianorum haud obscurè declinant: id quod tùm multorum exemplis, tùm ipso doctrinæ genere, quod cumprimis de personâ CHRISTI fovent, satis evidenter constat, Cum enim Baptismus non sit privatum aliquod bonum, Ministrorum proprium: sed publicum, toti q́; Ecclesiæ concreditum: hinc adeò fit, ut quamdiu Ecclesia Calviniana publicè tenet sanam doctrinam de mysterio adorandæ Trinitatis: id quod de Ecclesijs Calvinianorum habemus persuasissimum: in quibus puriora sunt corda Auditorum, quàm ora Sacerdotum: quàmdiu etiam in substantialibus nihil mutat: tâm diu verum ac salutaremBaptismum ab eâ administrari statuamus. Neque etiam assertioni huic nostræ obstare potest error Calvinianorum, de Effectu Baptismi: quem præcedente capite notavimus: Siquidem effectus non à doctrinâ Ministri baptisantis: sed ab autoritate & voluntate instituentis DEI: ut à fide baptizati in solidum dependet.

Cæterùm quoad eos hæreticos, qui Trinitatis mysterium, vel ex toto, vel ex parte negant: vel ὁμοεσίαν personarum inficiantur: ac proindè Baptismum in nomine Sacrosanctæ & indivíduæ Trinitatis, vel planè non, vel sensu perverso, administrant: & tota quidem Ecclesia talem hæresin approbat: tùm tantùm abest, ut verum & salutarem Baptismum ab istis conferri statuamus, ut potiùs nullum prorsus ibi Baptismi Sacramentum esse judicemus. Si verò Ecclesia tùm de baptismi substantiâ tùm de Trinitatis mysterio rectè sentiat, tùm formam Baptismi à Servatore præscriptam servet inviolatam: Minister verò baptizans, sit vel Arianæ, vel Photinianæ, vel consimili alij clàm addictus: tùm nihil hoc baptizato officere potest. Ratio est: Quia Baptismus non unius aut alterius privati: sed totius Ecclesiæ bonum est, quæ baptizandum non Ministro, sed CHRISTO offert & commendat.

Tertius defectus Ministrorum baptizantium est vitæ, morumq́; consceleratio. Sæpè enim contingit, ut tales sint adulteri, usurarij, ebriosi, &c. De horum ergò ministerio si quæratur, sequimur decisionem articuli VIII. Confessionis Augustanæ, qui sic habet: Quanquam Ecclesia propriè sit congregatio Sanctorum, & verè credentiu: tamen cum in hac vitâ multi hypocritæ & mali admixti sint, licèt uti Sacramentis, quæ per malos administrantur, juxta vocem CHRISTI, sedent Scribæ & Pharisæi in Cathedrâ Moysis. Et Sacramenta & Verbum DEI, propter ordinationē & mãdatū Christi sunt efficacia, etiamsi per malos exhibeantur. Damnamus proindè Donatistas & similes, qui negabant licere populo uti ministerio malorum in Ecclesia, & sentiebant ministerium malorum inutile & inefficax esse. Suffragantur huic nostræ sententiæ ipsi quoq; Doctores Scholastici, inter quos Gabriel Biel rationes quinq; recenset. 1. Quia Sacramenta habent efficaciam suam à CHRISTO instituente, & assistente signo suo practico, ad causandum signatum ex determinatione voluntatis suæ. 2. Quia si ex bonitate ministri dependeret Baptismus, nunquàm posset aliquis certus esse, se recepisse verum Baptismum. Cùm enim nullus possit esse certus de bonitate propria, multò minus de bonitate alterius. 3. Quia omninò injustum esset, alterum pro alterius iniquitate puniri, Quod sanè fieret, si baptizandus propter malitiam ministri non acciperet Baptismi gratiam. 4. Quia Baptismus est Sacramentum maximæ necessitatis, præsertim quoad parvulos, qui non habent aliud salutis suæ remedium, quod illis omninò inefficax redderetur, si mali ministri non verè baptizarent. 5. Quia Patres quoq; hanc sententiam probant, præsertim Augustinus, qui Tractatu 5. super Johannem scribit: Aliud est baptizare per ministerium, aliud baptizare per potestatem. Baptisma enim tale est, qualis est ille, in cujus potestate datur: non qualis est ille, per cujus ministerium datur. Et circa finem: Quos baptizavit Judas, baptizavit Christus: Sic ergò quos baptizavit homicida, quos baptizavit adulter, si Baptisma Christi erat, Christus baptizavit. Non timeo adulterum, non ebriosum, non homicidam, quia Columbam attendo, per quam mihi dicitur, Hic est, qui baptizat. Vide plura testimonia apud Lombardum lib. 4. distinct. 5.

Ulterius quærit hoc loco Gabriel Biel: An ebrius ratione utens possit baptizare? Et respondet satis congruè, quod nec virtus Sacramentalis, nec ejus ministerium impediatur per culpam sive peccatum ministri. Sed quid? Si minister baptizans usq; adeò esset ebrius, ut circumstantes non possent percipere sensum verborum, & sic daret sine mente sonum? Respondet Gabriel, talem planè non baptizare: nec hanc ejus actionem pro baptismo esse habendam. Cui decisioni eactenùs subscribimus, si tanta sit ministri ebrietas, ut non modò ipse nesciat, quid agat: sed & verba: Ego baptizo te &c. quæ ipsam Baptismi Formam constituunt, pronunciare non possit, ut intelligi nequeant. Satius autem fuerit, infantem baptizandum, è templo domum reportare, si alterius alicujus ministri copia haberi nequeat, & usq; dùm ebrietas remittat, differre Baptismum, si modò infantes vires id permittant: quam tali ebrioso Sacramentum hoc conspurcandum prostituere.

II. Quæstio: An in casu necessitatis Laicus aliquis fidelis, vel mulier Baptismum veru & salutarem conferre possit? Sacramentarij in negantem concedunt, ita ut Calvinus scribat Epist. 326. Neminem privatum posse Baptismi legitimum esse ministrum. Et post pauca: Adulterum ergò baptismum censemus, qui administratus est à privato ho-

vire: ac in Ecclesia recte composita, tolerabilis non esset hæc temeritas. Et rursus post aliqua: Prodigiosa fuit audacia ut se præter naturæ legem, mulieres in hoc munus ingererent. Idem Epist. 51. Baptismum obstetricibus permittere, impia & sacrilega est Baptismi profanatio. Theodorus Beza Epist. 12. Petitur an Baptismum ab obstetricibus administatum probemus? Respondemus, non modò nobis improbari, sed etiam prorsus intolerabilem videri.

Nos verò hoc etiam loco à Calvinianis divortium facientes, Affirmantem omninò tenemus, sed eâ lege, & conditione, ut non nisi de extremo necessitatis casu, ubi nulla prorsus vel ministri, vel alius alicujus viri copia haberi potest, baptismum à mulieribus administratum à nobis approbari, intelligatur: Affirmativæ nostræ rationes præcipuæ sunt hæ:

1. Mulieres quoque ad imaginem DEI sunt conditæ: sunt sanguine Christi redemtæ: sunt in Baptismo per Spiritum Sanctum regeneratæ: sunt adoptatæ in filias DEI: sunt regale Sacerdotium: sunt cohæredes gratiæ: sunt pars Ecclesiæ, & per fidem CHRISTO unitæ: ita ut Apostolus affirmare non dubitet: In Christo Jesu neq; masculum esse, neq; fœminam: Gal. 3, 28.

2. Virtus & efficacia Sacramenti hujus non pendet â qualitate baptizantis, sive viri, sive fœminæ: sed ex virtute, potentiâ, & promissione instituentis DEI. Ergò Personæ etiam qualitas, Virtutem Sacramenti neq; perficit, neq; tollit.

3. Ex loco parium, argumentum minimè invalidum ducitur. Si Sacramentum Circumcisionis per fœminam administrari potuit: Quidni & Baptismus? At prius illud licuit: exemplo Ziporæ, Circumcisionis Sacramentum filio conferentis. Exod. 4, 25. exemplo etiam quarundam mulierum Macchabæarum, circumcidentium filios 1. Macchab. 1, 63. 2. Macchab. 6, 10.

4. Prædicatio verbi tùm laicis, tùm sexui muliebri in casu necessitatis permittitur: Quidni igitur hujus etiam Sacramenti administratio? Antecedens patet exemplo Deboræ Judic. 4, 4. Huldæ 2. Reg. 22, 14. Hannæ Luc. 2, 36. Priscillæ Actor. 18, 26. quam Apostolus suam in Domino coadjutricem nominat Rom. 16, 3. Neque obstat, quod idem Apostolus mulieribus silentium in Ecclesia præcipit 1. Cor. 14, 34. nam non simpliciter hoc præcipit: sed propter virorum præsentiam. Quo ipso innuere voluit Apostolus, diverso casu, & in defectu virorum, necessitatis præsertim casu, partibus docendi defungi, minimè mulieribus esse interdictum. Quo respexit sine dubio Licinius Imperator, lege prohibens, ne mulieres ac viri uno in loco Ecclesiæ congregarentur, sed viri seorsim ac separatim: mulieres itidem separatæ à viris, cultui divino vacarent: teste Eusebio lib. de vitâ Constantini c. 48.

5. Praxis Ecclesiæ, de quâ August. l. 2. contra epist. Parmeniani c. 13. Si laicus aliquâ pereuntis necessitate compulsus, dederit baptisma: nescio, an piè quisquam dixerit, esse repetendum. Nullâ enim cogente necessitate si fiat, alieni muneris usurpatio est:

‘Si autem necessitas urgeret, aut nullum, aut veniale ‘delictum est.

Objiciunt hoc loco Sacramentarij Decretum Concilij Carthaginensis IV. quo fœminæ sint prohibitæ ab officio baptizandi. Respondeo 1. ti tantùm, non verò simpliciter hoc mulieribus esse interdictum: si nimirùm adsint vel Clerici, vel Viri alij fideles. Hoc casu ‘mulieribus ta- ‘cendum esse prohibet Concilium illud, cui præsedit D. Augustinus. Sic enim habet Capitulum nonagesimum octavum illius Concilij: Laicus præsentibus Clericis, nisi ipsis jubentibus, docere non audeat. Et cap. 99. Mulier quamvis docta & sancta, viros in conventu docere, non præsumat. Et cap. 100. Mulier baptizare non præsumat.

Objiciunt alij autoritatem Tertulliani, qui γυναικοβαπτισμὸν improbârit. Verùm de publico & ordinario Ministerio Ecclesiastico, non verò de casu necessitatis ipsum loqui, satis manifestum est. Scribit quidem lib. de Bapt. Dandi Baptismum jus habere summum Sacerdotem, qui est Episcopus: dehinc presbyteros, & Diaconos, non tamen sine Episcopi autoritate: Veruntamen incumbente necessitate, idem jus etiam Laicis competere, idem Tertullianus eodem loco asserit.

III. Quæstio: An infans baptizatus vel à laico, vel à muliere, à ministro rebaptizari, & in templum deportari debeat: & quis processus ibi servandus? Respondetur ex praxi Ecclesiæ hactenùs usu recepta: Quòd nimirùm infan s sic baptizari, rebaptizari nullo modo debeant. Quemadmodum etiam Ceremoniæ & preces, quæ postmodùm super hujusmodi infantibus, ad templum deportatis, publicè adhiberi solent à ministro Ecclesiæ, non pro iteratione Baptismi sunt habendæ: sed sunt nihil aliud, quàm Baptismi antè accepti Confirmatio publica, facta quidem cum solennitate rituum: sed tamen sine Sacramentali essentiâ, quæ neque nova, neque altera per istam actionem instituitur.

Est verò hoc loco & illud observandum, ‘quod fortassis facilè evenire queat: Si nimirùm ‘mulieres postmodum à ministro Ecclesiæ interroga- ‘tæ, quid egerint nùm aquâ infantem, cum pronunci- ‘atione verborū, Ego te baptizo &c. asperserint, re- ‘spondeant, sibi non adeò exactè constare, quid in tali ‘perturbationis, & anxietatis statu egerint? Quid ‘tali casu sit faciendum? Hîc sanè consultissimum fuerit, sine morâ & hæsitatione ulteriore, puerum publicè & solenniter baptizare: propterea quòd mulieres nihil certi de infantis hujus baptismo potuerint testari.

IV. Quæstio: An infidelis aliquis non baptizatus, ut Judæus aut Turca aliquis baptismum conferre possit? Respondet Augustinus lib. 2. contra epist. Parmeniani, cap. 13. de hâc quæstione nihil temerè affirmandum esse sine autoritate tanti Concilij, quantum tantæ rei sufficit. In Tomo 3. Concil. tale extat rescriptum Nicolai Papæ: à quodam Judæo, nescitis utrum Christiano an pagano,


### Chapter Four: VII. Question: In what place ought Baptism to be administered?

you assert that many in your country have been baptized, and you have asked what should be done about it. If these people were indeed baptized in the name of the Trinity, or even only in the name of CHRIST (as is read in the Acts of the Apostles), it is one and the same thing, as Saint Ambrose explains, because it is not theirs, but His in part 3, q. 67, art. 5 & 6. He offers this reason for this affirmative: Because just as on the part of the matter, as far as the necessity of the Sacrament is concerned, any water suffices: so also it suffices on the part of the minister, any human being: And therefore even one not baptized can baptize in a case of necessity: but if this were done outside a case of necessity, it would be a sin. However, in the Canon Law, de Consecr. d. 4. c. quos à paganis, a limitation is added to this decision: Namely, if such an infidel who is baptizing observes the form and has the intention of the Church. But we concede the negative simply, for the reason that such an infidel neither believes rightly concerning the most holy mystery of the Trinity, nor acknowledges the merit of Christ; nor can he observe the form or the intention of the Church: For if he believed and held these things, then he would no longer be an infidel: and therefore we conclude that such a baptism is to be held as void, ineffective, and indeed as a mere mockery.

V. Question: Whether several can baptize one at the same time: or, Whether one can baptize several at the same time? I answer, regarding the latter, I affirm it without [doubt?], but with a limitation, namely that it be done in the due manner: that is, that one minister baptizing should not confer baptism upon several infants with one single act of sprinkling: but that he should sprinkle water on each one separately, with the pronunciation of the words directed to each one separately: I baptize thee, etc. Although on the day of Pentecost, when three thousand people were baptized, it is very likely that the opposite was clearly observed, and that baptism was conferred with one sprinkling and one recitation of the words: which, however, was a matter of the necessity of that time: and therefore a singular example not to be drawn into imitation, unless a case of similar necessity prevails.

There are some who think that nothing is lacking to the Sacramental form if one minister baptizes several at the same time with one act, and says while sprinkling water on all of them at once: I baptize you, etc. While I willingly allow these people to abound in their own sense, I approve more of that former manner of baptizing, both because the form of this Sacrament is observed more accurately, and because it renders the baptized more certain of their baptism.

Regarding the first part of the question, there are not wanting those who think that several can baptize one, in such a way that each one sprinkles water and says: I baptize thee, etc. But he who is thus baptized is to be judged not to have received as many baptisms as there were baptizers: but only he is to be thought to have baptized, as Bonaventure wishes, who speaks first and completes the whole. But if all were to say: We baptize thee, then it would have to be judged that no one is baptizing, because they would be changing the form, since the plural pronoun (we) doubles its singular. But a change of form takes away the baptism. Similarly, he would not baptize if one were to sprinkle or immerse the child in water, but another were to pronounce the words, because the one uttering the words, I baptize thee, etc., since he does not also sprinkle the water, is lying. But what need is there for these curious speculations: As if there were, or ever could be, any necessity that several ministers should baptize one. For here also that common saying prevails: What can be done by fewer should not be done by more. Furthermore, this rite of baptizing will cause confusion, and consequently will violate Order and Decorum: both of which the Apostle wishes to be observed in the Church. 1 Cor. 14, 40.

VI. Question: Whether in a case of necessity anyone (such as a captive) can or ought to administer baptism to himself? We answer in the negative. For just as no one can be the author of his own generation: so neither can anyone, whether free or captive, impart to himself the washing of regeneration. It is a Greek adage: I will wash myself, I will bathe myself: And one's own washing is the best washing. But in the Church that has no place.

Certainly if one's own dispensation could have had a place anywhere: it would have had it most of all in Christ. But baptism had to be conferred upon Him by another's ministry. Much more, therefore, is it necessary that this be done in the baptism of other men. 2. In the words of the institution, a double person is expressly noted, the one baptizing and the one to be baptized: I baptize thee: according to the tenor of Christ's words: Go baptize them in the name, etc. When, therefore, someone were to say: I baptize myself: certainly a change of form would emerge, which would take away the baptism. 3. No one can seize for himself the seal of divine grace: but it is necessary that he receive it from Christ, through someone who exhibits it in the place of Christ. It remains, therefore, firm and settled that one to be baptized can and ought to be baptized only by another.

VII. Question: In what place ought Baptism to be administered? Concerning which matter there exist decrees of Synods: For the Council of Meaux, held around the year of Christ 845, chapter 48, defines concerning the place thus: That no priest should presume to baptize, except in villages and baptismal churches, and at appointed times, unless for a cause of sickness, or indeed of necessity. And Canon 59 of the VI Constantinopolitan Synod: In an oratory which is inside a house, baptism should never be performed: But they should approach the Catholic Churches. The Synod of Cologne in the year 1549, canon 15, defined it thus: The pride of laymen is to be detested no less than the adulation of the pastors who comply with them, who, having despised the Church, wish their offspring to be baptized in their own homes, and for the baptismal water to be brought there: wishing to rescind this abuse entirely, we decree that no one, wherever they may have been born, ought to be baptized anywhere other than in the Church, etc.

Latin:

multos in patriâ vestrâ baptizatos esse, asseritis & quid indè sit agendum, consuluistis. Hi profectò si in nomine Trinitatis, vel tantum in nomine CHRISTI, (sicut in actis Apostolorum legitur) baptizati sunt, unum quippè idemque est, ut Sanctus Ambrosius exponit, quia non illorum, sed ejus est rebaptizari non debent. Citat hoc rescriptum Thomas part. 3. q. 67. art. 5. & 6. Affirmativæ hujus hanc profert rationem. Quia sicut ex parte materiæ, quantum ad necessitatem Sacramenti sufficit quæcunque aqua : ita etiam sufficit ex parte ministri, quicunque homo : Et ideò etiam non baptizatus, in articulo necessitatis potest baptizare: si verò extra articulū necessitatis hoc fieret, peccaretur. Additur autem in Jure Canonico, de Consecr. d. 4. c. quos à paganis, Decisioni huic limitatio : Si nimirùm talis infidelis baptizans, servet formam, habeatque intentionem Ecclesiæ. Verùm in negantem nos simpliciter concedimus, proptereà, quòd talis infidelis, neque de Sacrosancto Trinitatis mysterio rectè credit, neque Christi meritum agnoscit; neque formam, aut intentionem Ecclesiæ servare potest: Si enim hæc crederet, & teneret, tùm infidelis non ampliùs esset : ac proindè talem baptismum pro irrito, inefficaci, imò pro mero ludibrio habendum esse concludimus.

V. Quæstio : An plures simul possint unum baptizare : vel, An unus plures possit simul baptizare? Respondeo, quoad posterius hoc citra [?] affirma*, sed cum limitatione, ut nimirùm debito modo id fiat: hoc est, ut unus minister baptizans, pluribus infantibus, non simul uno aspersionis actu, baptismum conferat: sed ut singulis seorsim aquam aspergat, cum pronunciatione verborum, ad quemlibet seorsim directâ : Ego te baptizo &c. Quanquam in die Pentecostes, ubi tria millia hominum baptizata fuerunt, diversum planè observatum, & unâ aspersione, unaque recitatione verborum baptismum collatum fuisse, admodùm verisimile est : id quod tamen præsentis tùm erat necessitatis : ac proindè Exemplum singulare ad imitationem non trahendum, nisi similis necessitatis casus militet.

Sunt quidam, qui existimant, Formæ Sacramentali nihil decedere, si minister Unus plures simul baptizet uno actu, & dicat aspergens simul omnibus aquam: Ego vos baptizo &c. Quos uti ego suo sensu libenter abundare patior: ita priorem illam baptizandi rationem magis probo, tùm quòd forma Sacramenti hujus accuratiùs observatur, tùm quòd baptizatos de baptismo reddit confirmationes.

Quoad prius quæstionis membrum, non desunt, qui existimant, plures posse Unum baptizare, ita ut quilibet aspergat aquam, & dicat: Ego te baptizo &c. Qui verò sic baptizatus est, non recepisse statuendus est, tot baptismos, quot fuerunt baptizantes : sed is tantùm baptizasse putandus est, ut vult Bonaventura, qui prior loquitur, & totum perficit. Si verò omnes dicerent: Nos baptizamus te, tùm nullum baptizare, statuendum esset, propterea, quòd mutarent formam, quia pronomen plurale (nos) ingeminat singulare suum. Mutatio autem formæ aufert baptismum. Similiter non baptizaret, si unus puerum aquâ aspergeret vel immergeret: alter verò verba pronunciaret, quia proferens verba, Ego te baptizo &c. cùm non aspergat quoque aquam, mentitur. Verùm quid opus est curiosis istis speculationibus: Quasi verò ullius necessitatis vel sit, vel unquàm esse possit: ut plures ministri Unum baptizent. Nam & hîc militat illud vulgatum: Quod potest fieri per pauciora, nõ debet fieri per plura. Deindè Confusionem pariet, iste baptizandi ritus, & per consequens violabit Ordinem & Decorum: quod utrumque tamen in Ecclesia observari vult Apostolus. 1. Cor. 14, 40.

VI. Quæstio: An in casu necessitatis aliquis (ut captivus) sibi ipsi baptismum administrare possit, aut debeat? Respondemus negatè. Quemadmodum enim nemo sibi ipse generationis autor esse poteit: ita neque regenerationis lavacrum quisquam, sive liber, sive captivus, sibi ipse impertire potest aut debet. Græcorum adagium est: ἑμαυτὸν λύσω, ἑμαυτῶ βαλανεύσω: Et propria lotio, optima est lotio. Sed in Ecclesiâ illud locum non habet.

Certè si propria dispensatio locum uspiam habere potuisset: in Christo vel maximè habuisset. Atqui alieno ministerio baptismus ipsi conferendus fuit. Multò id magis ergò in aliorum hominum baptismo fieri necessum est. 2. In verbis institutionis duplex persona expressè notatur, baptizans & baptizanda: Ego baptizo te: secundum tenorem verborum Christi: Vos baptizate eos in nomine &c. Quando ergò aliquis diceret: Ego baptizo me: certè mutatio formæ emergeret, quæ baptismum tolleret. 3. Nemo potest sigillum gratiæ divinæ sibiipsi rapere: sed necesse est, à Christo accipiat, per aliquem, qui illud loco Christi exhibeat. Firmum ergò & ratum manet, baptizandum non nisi ab alio baptizari posse & debere.

VII. Quæstio: In quo loco Baptismus administrari debeat? Quâ de re extant Synodorum decreta: Nam Concilium Meldenfe, habitum circa A. C. 845. cap. 48. de loco sic definit: Ut nemo presbyterorum baptizare præsumat, nisi in vicis, & Ecclesiis baptismalibus, atque temporibus constitutis, nisi causa ægritudinis, vel certè necessitatis. Et Canon. 59. Synodi Constantinopolitanæ VI. In æde oratoriâ, quæ est intra domum, baptismus nunquàm peragatur: Sed ad Catholicas Ecclesias accedant. Synodus Coloniensis Anno superiore 49. supra sesquimillesimum, can. 15 sic definivit: Detestanda est non minus laicorum superbia, quàm pastorum eis obsequentium adulatio, qui contemptâ Ecclesiâ proles suas volunt in domibus suis baptizari, & eò baptismi aquam deferri: quem abusum prorsus rescindere volentes, statuimus, neminem alibi, quàm in Ecclesiâ, quocunque loco natus sit, debere baptizari &c:


### Chapter Four: IX. What about Godparents?

But what need is there of many words, when the very nature of the Sacrament, which is ordinarily bound to the public assembly of the Church, demands that any Sacrament whatsoever be administered in a public and sacred place, unless a case of necessity requires otherwise.

VIII. Question: At what time or day ought Baptism to be conferred? We answer: first, regarding the Sacrament itself considered in itself, it is bound to no certain time: so that it is not free from either rashness or superstition that it was anciently thought that baptism ought to be conferred only on the more solemn feast days. Then, however, regarding the Object of Baptism, which concerns either infants or adults, this Sacrament admits of a certain observation of time entirely. For regarding adults, since instruction in the articles of faith and also confession of the mouth ought to precede their baptism: baptism of these can certainly be deferred until they are able to perform both of these correctly. It is not, however, of necessity that this be done only twice a year, namely on the solemnity of Easter and Pentecost: as the Canon Law defined beyond all reason, part 3 of the Decree: dist. 4. de Consecr. c. 12. & seqq. Just as the Jesuits also stand on our side in this matter, having no regard for the authority of Siricius, Epist. 1. decretal, and cap. 2. and Leo, epist. 4., as can be seen in Gregory of Valencia: Tom. 4. of the Theological Commentaries, disp. 4. q. 3. point 3. Furthermore, regarding infants, their baptism ought by no means to be deferred: for the sooner they are regenerated through baptism, the more certainly can one judge of their salvation, whatever case may happen afterwards.

Cyprian is a witness that in his time a certain Bishop, by the name of Fidus, contended that infants ought not to be baptized before the eighth day. Which opinion, however, was condemned by a provincial Synod of sixty-six Bishops. Therefore the Anabaptists err, who put off Baptism until the years of discretion, which for them is generally the seventh. Princes, Nobles, and the more wealthy also sin, who defer the Baptism of their infants for several weeks, and often for several months: not without the greatest danger to the infants: of whose life, in such tenderness of age, they cannot be certain even for a moment of an hour, whatever and however great care may be applied. To Christ the Savior, indeed, the thirtieth year of age was pleasing for his own person: but it was fitting for him thus to fulfill all righteousness, Matt. 3:15, and it is not fitting for us to accommodate our actions to the form of Christ's deeds rather than his words.

Some object in this place to the custom of the Ancient Church, where Christian parents were not compelled to offer their infants to be baptized immediately, but it was free for them to defer it until they became Catechumens through age. Hence Augustine writes of himself in book 1 of his Confessions, chapter 11, that as a boy he was seized by illness and wished to be baptized, but when he felt himself recovering, he put off the baptism. Thus Eusebius reports of the Emperor Constantine that he deferred Baptism until his old age. But here too that saying holds: that one must judge not by examples, but by laws. What is more, that old custom never deserved the approval of the Church and the orthodox: as our Blessed Luther wrote not badly, in his book of Table Talk, chapter on Baptism, that this old error was indeed pious: but that it gave occasion for malice. For, says Luther, since Augustine and others were baptized late, they had learned to despise Baptism, so that afterwards they refused to be baptized. It is therefore safest that little ones, while still infants, be baptized. It is added that that old custom was not entirely without a case of necessity, on account of the atrocious persecutions of tyrants and heretics, as Ecclesiastical history testifies.

IX. The question is about Godparents who are present partly as witnesses to the baptismal action, and partly indeed promise as sureties for the infants: What is to be determined concerning this rite? It is certain, however, that this rite was very ancient, so that Dionysius the Areopagite mentions it, in his book on the Ecclesiastical Hierarchy, chapter 2, and Tertullian in his book on Baptism. Yet nothing certain can be defined from histories concerning its first origin. Furthermore, although it is ancient: it is nevertheless an adiaphoron, and in itself free to be observed: introduced by human choice: so that although it is not placed in the choice of any private individual to neglect it today: it can nevertheless be omitted without any danger in a case of necessity. But others define the cause for which this rite was first introduced in different ways.

The Jesuits [claim] this was done for this reason, that because infants are destitute of their own faith when they are baptized, they might be baptized into the alien faith of the godparents: and thus obtain the benefit of regeneration from an alien faith. The vanity of which error we have refuted above evidently. Therefore, another cause for the introduction of this custom, and this indeed the principal one, seems to have been that, because the primitive Church was interspersed everywhere with paganism, it could be established by their testimony who had been made a participant of Baptism. From which it is a consequence that this rite is not of the substance of this Sacrament. In later times, however, it was retained, and is still retained for grave and useful causes: one of which is this, that infants may be brought to Christ through them, and be commended to him by their prayers, by whom they may be adopted into the fellowship of his kingdom and his people. Another: That when parents are deceased, they may not lack those by whose exhortations they may be instructed in the pursuit of the Christian faith, piety of life, and honesty of morals. Concerning which duty sponsors are piously admonished by Augustine: Sermon 6, Paschal: and on the 10th Sunday after Trinity: Let them see to it that they strengthen their tongue, lest the infants, when they have grown older, utter shameful songs. Likewise: Brothers, always chastise and correct both those who are born of us, and those whom you receive from the font, so that they may live piously, justly, and soberly.

Indeed, those things which are usually moved concerning godparents otherwise can be included in these hypotheses.

1. A godparent, because for the instruction of the infant

Latin:

Sed quid multis opus est, cum ipsa Sacramenti ratio, quæ ad publicum Ecclesiæ cœtum, ordinariè est alligata, flagitet, ut in loco publico & sacro Sacramentum quodlibet administretur, nisi diversum casus necessitatis exigat.

VIII. Quæstio: Quo tempore sive die Baptismus conferri debeat? Respondemus: primò quoad Sacramentum ipsum in se consideratum, illud ad nullum certum tempus est alligatum: ita ut vel temeritate, vel superstitione non careat, quòd festis tantùm solennioribus, baptismum conferri debere, antiquitùs existimatum fuit. Deindè verò quoad Baptismi Objectum, quod vel infantes, vel adultos respicit, Sacramentum hoc certam temporis observationem omninò admittit. Nam quoad adultos, cum horum baptismum præcedere debeat Informatio in articulis fidei, & oris etiam Confessio: utique eo usque baptismus istorum differri potest, donec utrumque istud rectè præstare possint. Non tamen necessitatis est, ut hoc fiat bis tantùm quotannis, nempè in solennitate Paschatis & Pentecostes: uti præter omnem rationem definivit Jus Canonicu, part. 3. Decreti: dist. 4. de Consecr. c. 12. & seqq. Quemadmodum Jesuitæ quoque hac in parte à nostra stant parte, nihil morati autoritatem Syricij Epist. 1. decretali, & cap. 2. & Leonis epist. 4. uti videre est apud Gregorium de Valentia: Tom. 4. Commentariorum Theol. disp. 4. q. 3. puncto 3. Cæterùm quoad infantes, baptismus illorum nullatenùs differri debet: Quò citiùs enim per baptismum regenerantur, eò certiùs de ipsorum salute judicari potest, quicunque tandem casus postmodùm obveniat.

Testis est Cyprianus, suo tempore Episcopum quendam, cognomento Fidum, contendisse, ante diem octavum infantes non esse baptizandos. Quæ tamen sententia à Synodo provinciali sexaginta sex Episcoporum damnata fuerit. Errant proindè Anabaptistæ, qui ad annos usque discretionis, qui ipsis plerumque est septimus, Baptismum protrahunt. Peccant etiam Principes, Nobiles, & Opulentiores, qui infantum suorum Baptismum, in aliquot septimanas, sæpiùs in menses aliquot differunt: non sine summo infantum periculo: de quorum vitâ, in tantâ ætatis teneritudine, ne quidem ad momentum horæ certi esse possunt, quæcunque & quantacunque etiam adhibeatur cura. Christo Servatori sanè tricesimus ætatis annus, pro suâ personâ placuit: Verùm sic ipsum omnem justitiam adimplere decuit Matth. 3, 15. & non ad factorum magis quàm dictorum Christi formam, actiones nostras accommodare nobis convenit.

Objiciunt nonnulli hoc loco consuetudinem Veteris Ecclesiæ, ubi parentes Christiani non cogebantur statim infantes suos baptizandos offerre, sed liberum erat illis, differre id, donec per ætatem fierent Catechumeni. Hinc Augustinus de seipso scribit l. 1. Conf. cap. 11. quòd puer morbo correptus voluerit baptizari, sed cum se convalescere sensisset, baptismum distulisse. Sic de Constantino Imperatore refert Eusebius, quòd Baptismum in senectutem usq́; distulerit. Verùm & hîc valet illud: Non exemplis, sed legibus judicandum esse. Quid quòd vetus ista consvetudo Ecclesiæ atque orthodoxorum approbationem nunquàm meruit: ut haud malè scripsit B. Lutherus noster, in lib. Sermonum convivalium, cap. de Baptismo, pium quidem fuisse istum veterem errorem: sed occasionem malitiæ dedisse. Nam, inquit Lutherus, cum Augustinus & alij cùm serò baptizarentur, didicerant Baptismum contemnere, ita ut postea baptizari renuerent. Tutissimum igitur est, parvulos adhuc infantes baptizari Accedit, quòd vetus illa consuetudo, non planè omni necessitatis casu caruit, propter tyrannorum atque hæreticorum atroces persecutiones, uti historia Ecclesiastica testatur.

IX. Quæstio est de Patrinis qui partim actioni baptisticæ ut testes adsunt, partim verò pro infantibus, ut fidejussores spondent: Quid de isto ritu sit statuendum? Constat autem ritum hunc longè antiquissimum fuisse, ita ut ejus meminerit Dionysius Areopagita, lib. de Hierarchiâ Ecclesiasticâ cap. 2. & Tertullianus in libro de Baptismo. De primo tamen ejus ortu nihil certi ex historijs definiri potest. Cæterùm antiqua sit licèt: adiaphora tamen est, & in se observatu libera: humano arbitrio inducta: ita ut licèt in privati cujusvis arbitrio, eum negligere, hodiè non sit positum: sine periculo tamen ullo, in casu necessitatis omitti possit. Causam autem, ob quam ritus iste primùm fuit introductus, alij aliam definiunt.

Jesuvitæ ideò hoc factum fuisse, ut quia infantes baptizari propriâ fide destituuntur, in alienam nempè patrinorum fidem baptizati possint: & sic ex alienâ fide regenerationis beneficium consequantur. Cujus erroris vanitatem suprà evidenter refutavimus. Causa ergò introductæ hujus consuetudinis alia, & hæc quidem præcipua fuisse videtur, ut quia gentilitati passim interspersa fuit Ecclesia primitiva, horum testimonio constare posset, quisnám Baptismi compos esset factus. Ex quo illud est consequens, ritum istum non esse de substantiâ hujus Sacramenti. Posteris tamen temporibus, idem retentus fuit, retineturque adhuc propter causas graves atque utiles: quarum una hæc est, ut infantes Christo per hos adducantur, & precibus horum eidem commendentur, à quo in consortium regni & populi sui adoptentur. Altera: Ut defunctis parentibus non desint, quorum exhortationibus ad studium fidei Christianæ pietatem vitæ, morumque honestatem illi instruantur. De quo officio ab Augustino susceptores piè admonentur: Serm. 6. Paschali: & Dominica 10 post Trinitatis: Videant, ut eorum lingvam firment, ne turpia cantica majores facti infantes proferant. Item: Fratres, tam illos, qui de nobis nati sunt, quàm eos, quos de fonte suscipitis, semper castigate, & corripite, ut piè, justè & sobriè vivant.

Possunt verò ea, quæ de Patrinis aliàs moveri solent, hisce hypothesibus includi.

1. Patrinus, quia ad instructionem infantis


### Chapter Four: On the Ceremonies of Baptism

at least he is bound by promise in those places where there is danger regarding religion; such a one ought to be chosen who can instruct the one received piously and sincerely. Concerning which matter Dionysius the Areopagite warns in his book on the Ecclesiastical Hierarchy, part 2, last chapter, and Augustine in a certain Paschal Sermon, which is cited in De Consecratione, dist. 4, c. Vos ante omnia. From which it follows that, if there is no such danger, the unlearned and even the learned can be chosen.

2. He who is not himself baptized cannot perform the office of a sponsor: de Cons. dist. 4, cap. In baptismate.

3. No father, nor the mother herself, ought to perform the office of sponsorship.

4. That spiritual kinship is feigned to be contracted by this rite is a fabrication of the Papists, and devised solely for the sake of making money: so that if such persons wish to join themselves in marriage, it is not permitted to them, unless a certain sum of money intervenes, by which a dispensation for this matter is obtained from the Pope.

5. Regarding the number of godparents, it is to be noted what is said: in the mouth of two or three witnesses shall every truth consist, Deut. 17, 16, and c. 19, 15. Abundance and a multitude in the wealthier sort betrays partly luxury, partly folly: in the poorer sort, it betrays an end of begging. Both of which ought to have been most alien to this most sacred action.

6. Catechization, as they say, that is, that interrogation concerning the renunciation of Satan and concerning faith in Christ, to which godparents are accustomed to respond in place of the infant, is indeed adiaphorous and indifferent regarding infants: but regarding adults, it is necessary: and it was introduced for this reason, that there might be some conformity between the Baptism of infants and of adults: and as Bonaventure speaks, Where there is only one Sacrament, one rite also should be observed. Furthermore, regarding adults, catechization, or that instruction concerning the principal chapters of the Christian religion, is deservedly placed before their Baptism: as is the profession of faith: both because Christ commanded this, Mark 16, 16, and because Baptism is the Sacrament of faith. For by the same right and for the same reason that they are to be baptized, they are also to be catechized. The godfather, however, when he responds for the infant, I BELIEVE: does not predict that the boy will believe when he has grown up (for thus it would have to be said HE WILL BELIEVE), nor does he promise that he will only devote effort so that when he has reached the years of discretion he may be instructed in the faith: but he issues a profession of present faith, which is communicated to the infant, by means of this Sacrament and the prayers of the Church.

Latin:

saltem ex promisso obligatur in ijs locis, ubi de religione est periculum, talis debet eligi, qui susceptum piè & sincerè instruere possit. Quâ de re monet Dionys. Areop. lib. de hierarch. Eccl. part. 2. cap. ult. & Augustinus Sermone quodam Paschali, qui allegatur de Consecr. dist. 4. c. Vos ante omnia. Ex quo est illud consequens, si sit absq; isto periculo, idiotas & doctos etiam posse eligi.

2. Qui ipse non est baptizatus, munere susceptoris fungi non potest: de Cons. dist. 4. cap. In baptismate.

3. Pater nemo, neque mater ipsa susceptionis munere fungi debet.

4. Quod cognatio spiritualis contrahi hoc ritu fingitur, id Pontificiorum commentum est, & ad quæstum faciendum unicè comparatum: ut si tales personæ matrimonio se copulare velint, id illis non liceat, nisi interveniente certâ pecuniæ summâ, quâ rei hujus dispensatio à Pontifice impetretur.

5. De numero Patrinorum illud notandum, quod dicitur, in ore duorum vel trium testium consistit omne verum, Deut. 17, 16. & c. 19, 15. Copia & multitudo in ditioribus luxum partim, partim fatuitatem: in pauperioribus mendicandi finem prodit. Quod utrumque à Sacratissimâ hac actione debebat esse alienissimum.

6. Catechizatio, uti loquuntur, hoc est, interrogatio illa de abrenunciatione Satanæ, deqs fide in Christum, ad quam Patrini loco infantis respondere solent, est quidem quoad infantes adiaphora, & indifferens: quoad adultos verò necessaria: estque ea introducta ideò, ut conformitas aliqua esset inter Baptismum infantum & adultorum: & uti Bonaventura loquitur, Ubi unum tantum Sacramentum est, unus quoque ritus observetur. Cæterùm quoad adultos, meritò istorum Baptismo præmittitur Catechizatio, sive instructio illa de præcipuis religionis Christianæ capitibus: ut & professio fidei: tùm quia Christus hoc præcepit Marc. 16, 16. tùm quia Baptismus est Sacramentum fidei. Quo enim jure & quâ ratione sunt baptizandi, eadem sunt etiam cathechizandi. Patrinus autem, quando pro infante respondet, CREDO: non prædicit crediturum puerum, cum adoleverit, (sic enim dicendum foret CREDET) neque operam se tantum daturum promittit, ut cùm ad annos discretionis pervenerit, de fide instruatur: sed de præsente fide professionem edit, quæ infanti, mediante hoc Sacramento, & precibus Ecclesiæ communicatur.


### Chapter Four: X. Question. What rites or ceremonies can and ought to be observed concerning the action of Baptism?

X. Question. What rites or ceremonies can and ought to be observed concerning the action of Baptism?

Concerning the resolution of this Question, it is to be noted at the beginning that by rites and ceremonies are not understood those things which are substantial to this Sacrament; nor even prayers and thanksgivings; nor finally the catechizations of both infants and adults, of which mention was just made: But those accidental, adiaphorous traditions are understood, which contribute nothing at all to the substance of the Sacrament: such as are in our own Churches, the Sign of the cross: Exorcism: The imposition of a name: Gifts, which are accustomed to be given to infants by godparents as if in place of a pledge. Among the Romanists, however, there are: The blessing of the font, Salt, Spittle, Exsufflation, The sign of the cross, Exorcism, The laying on of hands, anointing, abstinence from wine, meats, and the marriage bed regarding adults, the time of Easter and Pentecost, the kiss of peace, the anointing of chrism, a lighted candle, a white garment: and if there are any others. Concerning each and all of which it is first to be observed generally, if either one, or many, or all of these are missing, the Sacrament is not for that reason any less true and holy, provided the Word and the Element are there. Therefore, these things contribute either nothing, or certainly very little, to the Baptismal action: indeed, if these things are applied to the file of a purer judgment, it will be evident that they are partly useless, partly foolish and troublesome, and partly merely superstitious. The blessing of the font, certainly, is partly superfluous, and partly an injury and blasphemy against that first consecration of all waters made by Christ in the Jordan.

Oil and Chrism are partly borrowed from the Levitical rites of the Old Testament, and partly entirely foreign to the example of Christ and all the Apostles. The use of salt in Baptism is most inept: serving more for academic hazing than for the Baptismal action.

By the exsufflation and spittle of the priest, the most holy Sacrament is foolishly and impiously spat upon and defiled out of a certain impious κακοζηλίᾳ (misguided zeal).

The use of the Sign of the Cross and Exorcism among the Romanists is clearly magical and superstitious. For although even the Reformed Churches in some places retain the use of those ceremonies, there is absent both the opinion of necessity and the assertion of an effective power which consists in the casting out of devils; but also those rites are used with the most free will, to be omitted if the contrary pleases our Churches and seems to be for the benefit and use of those present: and they are not employed except for the purpose of signification.

The imposition of a name seems to draw its origin from the Old Testament: so that just as names were then imposed upon sons in Circumcision, as is evident also from the history of the circumcision of Christ: so today under the Gospel the same is accustomed to be done, for this purpose especially, that as often as the baptized person hears his name, he may always be reminded of his baptism and the covenant initiated with GOD.

A gift is given by the sponsor to the infant, for this purpose, that it may serve him as a certain memorial, by which he may from time to time be reminded of the faith given in baptism to Christ the Savior.

XI. Question: Why are such rites and ceremonies, and especially the Sign of the Cross and Exorcism, retained in the Reformed Churches? But this most simple and true answer is given, that although rites of this kind are not of the essence of this Sacrament: because, however, they pertain partly to the solemnity of the Sacrament: and partly contain useful reminders and significations, they are certainly, out of Christian Liberty, without any superstition, rightly and conveniently employed, according to the Apostolic rule, which commands that all things be done in the Church decently, ευσχημόνως 1 Cor. 14. last. Moreover, these rites contribute 1. to exciting greater devotion and reverence in the faithful.

2. They are useful for the instruction of the common people, just as much as paintings and images. 3 They clearly admonish concerning the use and efficacy of this Sacrament, which they shadow forth by a manifest prefiguration. And indeed, specifically regarding the Sign of the cross, the Romanists do indeed pretend that it has some power to expel the Devil. But to us, it is clearly ἀδιάφορον, and significant, so that by this rite both the one to be baptized and those standing by are admonished that there is no other medium by which an infant can be snatched from the power of the Devil and transferred into the kingdom of Christ, except for the Cross or the merit of Christ the Savior.

But regarding Exorcism, it is retained in certain reformed Churches under the category of an adiaphorous, or indifferent, ceremony: with an end and use far different from the observation of the Papists.

1. For the Papists pretend that it relies on Apostolic authority: as can be seen in Bellarmine, book 1 on Baptism, chapter 25, page 390, letter D. Indeed, Gregory of Valencia writes that it was instituted by Christ himself, namely at the time when He gave the Apostles the power of casting out Demons, Vol. 4, Theological Commentaries, disp. 4, quest. 6, point 1. But to us, Exorcism is a Ceremony introduced only by human authority, ancient indeed, and received by use in the times of Tertullian, Cyprian, Gregory Nazianzen, Optatus of Milevis, Augustine, and the age of other fathers: but entirely free and indifferent.

2. The Papists attribute such power to Exorcism that it confers a Spiritual effect ex opere operato, and effectively drives away Devils by some inherent and occult power. Whence the Council of Trent defined that it cannot be omitted without sin. Sess. 7, Can. 13, March 3, Year 1547, under Pope Paul III. But to us, the Use of Exorcism is only σημαντικος ἡ τυπικός, so that it shadows forth as if from a distance in what miseries a newborn infant is situated outside of baptism, being by nature a child of wrath, and that he cannot be snatched from them except through the washing of regeneration.

With these marks of the differences well observed, it is easy to gather what Spirit drove the Calvinists twenty years ago to stir up such a disastrous war against Exorcism in this Electorate of ours. Certainly, the controversy was not about the Exorcism of the Papists, which we ourselves readily concede is defiled with various mud of superstitions and is in itself impious and blasphemous. Nor was the question about any bodily obsession of Devils, for the solving of which in infants there is need of Exorcism: such an obsession no Orthodox person has ever posited. But neither was it asked whether that rite, in those places where it has once been abolished, ought to be brought back and recalled into use after the fact. For we ourselves hold the negative again, to the extent that if it were to be abrogated even in those Churches in which it is still observed, for just causes, in a legitimate manner, and with the knowledge and consent of the Church, no orthodox person would easily protest. Fourthly, neither was this in controversy: Whether Exorcism ought to be held as either of absolute necessity or as a substantial part of Baptism? For we also embrace the negative. Finally, neither was it contended: Whether Exorcism can and ought to be abrogated on account of abuse. For we also concede to the affirmative. But the hinge of the controversy consisted in this alone: Whether this rite of Exorcism is to be held in the census of indifferent things which they call ἀδιαφορα: or whether it ought to be referred to things vicious, impious, and superstitious in their whole kind? The Sacramentarians affirming the latter: but we embracing the former. However, that group had nothing more plausible for their side by which to build up their sense than this one thing: That the rite is Papistical. Which itself, however, could not be demonstrated: since the contrary was shown by our side, that this rite was not first invented under the Papacy, but is far more ancient: and also that it is not observed by our side for the same end and use as by the Papists. Its antiquity, however, is shown from those writings of the Fathers who are far more ancient than the Papacy: namely, Cyprian, Epist. book 4, ep. 7; Gregory Nazianzen in his Oration on the washing of Holy Baptism; Ambrose on the Sacraments, book 1, chapter 5; Augustine on the merits and remission of sins, book 1, chapter 34; likewise on Marriage and Concupiscence, book 1, c. 20, and book 2, chapter 18.

The reasons, however, for which our Churches did not wish to abrogate Exorcism for the sake of the Calvinists, are mainly these.

1. Because they urged this abrogation not as brethren in religion: but as enemies of the Truth, affecting lordship over our faith and religion.

2. Because they urged it, not as a matter of something indifferent: but as something impious, superstitious, and detestable.

3. Because under this abrogation they were attempting to encrust that Calvinistic dogma of theirs concerning the holiness of infants from the maternal womb before the reception of Baptism.

4. Because through this abrogation the enemies of the truth would be confirmed in their errors; but the weak and our associates in religion would be greatly offended.

5. Because in a case of Confession, every appearance of denied Truth is to be avoided entirely: and especially when we notice that our purer Religion is being attacked, as it were, indirectly and obliquely.

6. Because they desired that the proper Effect of Baptism be weakened through this abrogation.

7. And lastly: Because by the example of the Apostle, in such cases, one must not yield to false brethren even for an hour; so that the Truth of the Gospel may remain safe and sound, Gal. 2, 4. & 5. But rather one must stand in the liberty, into which we have been asserted through Christ: Gal. 5, 1.

XII. And the final question is: Whether those who are addicted to the Papal doctrine; can with a good and uninjured Conscience be employed as witnesses at the Baptism of our infants: and whether Lutheran Ministers ought to admit such persons? Regarding the decision of this question, those who live in places where the Roman Papacy is clearly exiled easily lean toward the negative; just as those who weigh a little more accurately the primary end, for the sake of which this custom of adopting godparents or witnesses was introduced in ancient times: which was no other than that godparents should duly instruct in the Christian religion and faith the sons and daughters already orphaned of their parents. With this end certainly weighed, Lutheran parents would be altogether cruel who would commend their children to be educated by Papists through this public rite. For which reason it would be the duty of the ministers of the Church to admonish their auditors seriously and frequently about this end: for thus they themselves would spontaneously shrink from godparents addicted to a different religion. Moreover, since whether by the negligence of the ministers or the fault of the auditors, hardly anyone today thinks about that end, but another clearly different and merely political one prevails and is looked to: namely, that children may sometimes have witnesses that they were born of an honest and legitimate bed: that they may also more freely use the help and counsel of such godparents: hence it also happens that, with the primary end changed, another decision of this question must be given. There is added also this, that in those places where men of both religions live mixed and together, such is the state of the polity that, without huge confusion and more serious disturbances, Papists cannot be clearly excluded from this office of testifying. And indeed, that they should not be excluded even in such a case, sufficiently evident reasons seem to militate. For first, although the Romanists have added to the Sacrament of Baptism ceremonies that are inept and partly ridiculous and clearly unknown to the primitive Church: they themselves nevertheless confess that they were added merely for the sake of ornament, and therefore, as far as the substance of Baptism is concerned, they do not dissent from us at all. Next, we determine that as many as are to be baptized in Papist churches have received the true Sacrament, and that they are not to be rebaptized. How then and by what right could those be barred from public testimony whom we voluntarily acknowledge and confess ought to be rightly baptized? And from this the canon without doubt drew its origin, which exists in De Consecr. dist. 4. cap. In Baptismate: He who is not himself baptized cannot perform the duty of a sponsor. Thirdly, just as strangers were rightly removed from this office in ancient times, or those of whom the Apostle pronounces that they are outside and have nothing to do with us: so indeed the Romanists in this case can neither be nor ought to be considered as strangers: because they agree with us in all things concerning the most holy Trinity, which is religiously recited and adored in the administration of this Sacrament. Fourthly, if the observation of this ceremony, which is in itself indifferent, neither confers nor detracts anything from Baptism itself: if also the dignity or indignity of the minister himself neither benefits nor harms the Sacrament: certainly, and indeed much less, will the impiety of the godparents bring any detriment to Baptism. Fifthly, if for most serious causes [...]

the Church does not rebaptize those baptized by Papists: why would it not bear those who are merely employed as witnesses, even if something were greatly desired in them? For this whole ceremony could be omitted, with Baptism nonetheless remaining safe. For neither John nor the Apostles, baptizing so many men at once, are read to have employed godparents: nor when Philip baptized the Ethiopian on the journey from the flowing water was a witness present at his Baptism. Histories testify, however, that Hyginus, a Greek by nationality and Roman Bishop, in the year 141 after the birth of Christ, first employed godparents or sponsors for Baptism. Sixthly, this matter is devoid of all danger. For while the Evangelical minister uses our ceremonies used in the churches: but the Papist neglects them: certainly by this very fact he testifies that he is initiating this infant into the true reasons of piety: and that he is to be educated not in the Papist, but in the Evangelical religion. Seventhly, the godparents themselves, however much they are Papists, by the very fact that they are present at our Baptism, openly and publicly testify that they entirely approve of our churches and our sacraments. Finally, it cannot be denied that many addicted to the Papist religion, when godparents were employed in our churches, and they heard everything proposed religiously and indeed from the scriptures, and understood that the accusations of their doctors, which they vomit against us, are false: not only thought more equitably and honorably of our churches, but finally came over to us entirely and openly professed the truth. Led by these reasons, we determine that in those places especially where men of both religions live together and use the same magistrate and the same laws, Papists are not to be excluded from this kind of testimony: which, however, we do not understand of such Papists who are blasphemous against the Evangelical doctrine, and who despise, annihilate, and persecute our Church and sacraments: for we determine that such are to be simply excluded, and not to be admitted until they have made it publicly testified that they hold and acknowledge our sacraments as true.

Some object to this decision that Apostolic saying: Do not bear the yoke with the impious and unbelievers. But they commit a manifest sophistry ὠδὲ τὸ σχῆμα της λέξεως. For to bear the yoke with the impious and unbelievers is for the Apostle the same as to approve, whether seriously or feignedly, the impiety and unbelief of such: and to join oneself to the church and society of these: neither of which is done by us: rather, the Papists by this pact associate themselves more with us and our churches than that we should in any way pass over to them.

Which same thing ought to be answered to that other precept of the Apostle, by which he commands that we should not mix ourselves with fornicators, the impure, and idolaters. For the Apostle does not want this, that we should renounce all association with the impious (for thus we would have to go out of the world, as the Apostle himself speaks in the same place) but that we should flee that association and familiarity of life and idol-mania which is with some approval of that impiety joined: that which the word for mixing implies, which seems to signify a closer association and a certain fellowship of faith. It is manifest that nothing of the sort is happening in the present case, which is the subject of inquiry.

But others object, partly because of the danger to the infant, who could easily be seduced by such a Papist godfather; partly because of the scandal which is offered in this way to the weaker brethren. I answer that both of these points are relevant only when the question concerns the primary end of this ceremony, which was discussed above. But now, since that end has for the most part fallen away among our own people, who look more to a certain political or even economic advantage and profit, certainly neither danger nor any scandal arises any longer. What is more, in such a case the infant is not bound in Baptism to the Papist religion, but rather that Papist witness or godfather binds himself to the faith and confession of the Apostolic Creed. Now if he teaches the child he has sponsored those articles, there is no danger of seduction. But if he wishes to inculcate in the child a different doctrine that conflicts with these articles, he will no longer be judged a witness, but a traitor to the Truth. Nor is he who was sponsored at baptism bound to commit anything against the profession which he made through his godfather in Baptism. Thus, regarding scandal, it would indeed be desirable that all our hearers were so perfect that they understood the magnitude of the matter. However, since in such great human infirmity such a thing can hardly be hoped for, the lesser of two evils must certainly be chosen; and pains must be taken by the ministers, both that the weak who are offended by this act may be more rightly informed, and that in this practice such a method may be observed that we may not appear to indulge the Papists, nor yet by excessive rigor make them more hostile to our churches; but as far as can be done while preserving the truth of the Gospel, we should maintain external or political peace and concord between the people of both religions.

Latin:

X. Quæstio. Quinam ritus sive Ceremoniæ circa actionem Baptismi observari possint & debeant?

Circa hujus Quæstionis enodationem initiò notandum, per ritus atque Ceremonias non intelligi ea, quæ sunt Sacramenti hujus substantialia; neque etiam preces & gratiarum actiones; nec denique catechizationes tùm infantum, tùm adultorum, de quibus modò dictum: Sed intelligi traditiones illas accidentarias, adiaphoras, & ad substantiam Sacramenti nihil quicquam facientes: quales in nostris quidem Ecclesiis sunt, Signum crucis: Exorcismus: Impositio nominis: Donativa, quæ à Patrinis arrhæ quasi loco infantibus dari consueverunt. Apud Romanenses verò sunt, Benedictio fontis, Sal, Saliva, Exufflatio, Signaculum crucis, Exorcismus, Impositio manus, unctio, abstinentia vini, carnium, & rei uxoriæ quoad adultos, tempus Paschæ & Pentecostes, osculum pacis, Unctio chrismatis, cereus accensus, vestis candida: & si quæ sunt aliæ. De quibus singulis & universis illud primò genere est observandum, si vel unum, vel multa, vel omnia ex istis desint, non ideò minus esse verum Sacramentum, & sanctum, modò Verbum sit ibi & Elementum. Inserviunt proindè isthæc actioni Baptisticæ, vel nihil, vel certè perparum: quin si ad limam purioris judicij ista adhibeantur, partim inutilia, partim stolida & molesta, partim merè superstitiosa esse patebit. Benedictio certè fontis, supervacanea partim, partim in primam illam aquarum omnium consecrationem à Christo in Jordane factam, injuria & blasphema est.

Oleum & Chrisma partim mutuatitium est ex Veteris Testamenti ritibus Leviticis, partim à Christi & Apostolorum omnium exemplo prorsus alienum. Salis in Baptismo ineptissimus usus est: magis depositionibus Academicis, quàm actioni Baptisticæ subserviens.

Exufflatione & Sputo Sacerdotis sacratissimum Sacramentum ex impiâ quadam κακοζηλίᾳ stolidè & impiè conspuitur ac conspurcatur.

Signaculi Crucis & Exorcismi magicus planè & superstitiosus apud Romanenses usus est. Nam tametsi ceremoniarum istarum usum reformatæ etiam Ecclesiæ aliquibus in locis retinent: abest tamen tùm necessitatis opinio: tùm effectivæ virtutis, quæ in profligatione Diabolorum consistat, assertio: sed & liberrimâ cum voluntate ritus isti usurpantur, omittendi, si diversum nostris Ecclesijs placeat, atque ex re ac usu præsentium esse videatur: & non nisi in Significationis usu adhibentur.

Impositio nominis videtur jam indè ex Veteri Testamento suam trahere originem: ut quemadmodum tùm in Circumcisione filijs imponebantur nomina, uti ex historiâ etiam circumcisionis Christi patet: sic hodiè sub Evangelio idem fieri consuevit, eo potissimum fine, ut quoties baptizatus nomen suum audit, semper baptismi & fœderis cum DEO initi recordetur.

Donativum à susceptore datur infanti, eo fine, ut si ipsi, tanquàm memoriale quoddam, quo subindè admoneatur datæ fidei in baptismo Christo Servatori.

XI. Quæstio: Cur in Ecclesijs reformatis ejusmodi ritus ac Ceremoniæ, & cumprimis Signum Crucis & Exorcismus retineantur? Simplicissima autem & verissima isthæc datur responsio, quòd licèt ritus istiusmodi non sint de essentiâ hujus Sacramenti: quia tamen spectant partim ad solennitatem Sacramenti: partim verò utiles commonefactiones, & significationes continent, utiq; ex Libertate Christianâ, sine omni superstitione, rectè ac convenienter adhibeantur, secundum regulam Apostolicam, quæ jubet, ut in Ecclesiâ omnia fiant decenter, ευσχημόνως 1. Cor. 14. ult. Conferunt autem ritus isti 1. ad excitandam majorem devotione & reverentiam fideliu.

2. Utiles sunt ad instructionem vulgi, perindè atque picturæ & imagines. 3 De usu atque efficaciâ hujus Sacramenti, quam præfiguratione manifestâ adumbrant, luculenter admonent. Et quidem in specie quoad Signaculum crucis, fingunt quidem Romanenses, habere illud vim aliquam ad expellendum Dæmonem. Nobis verò illud est planè ἀδιάφορον, & significativum, ita ut hoc ritu admoneatur tum baptizandus, tum astantes, nullum aliud esse medium, quo infans ex potestate Diaboli eripi, inque regnum Christi transferri queat, præter Crucem sive meritum Christi Servatoris.

Sed quoad Exorcismum, sub adiaphori, sive indifferentis ceremoniæ ratione, in quibusdam reformatis Ecclesiis ille retinetur: fine ac usu à Pontificiorum observatione longè diversissimo.

1. Enim Pontificij autoritate Apostolicâ eum niti fingunt: uti videre licet apud Bellarminum lib. 1. de Bapt. cap. 25. pag. 390. lit. D. quin à Christo ipso institutum esse, scribit Gregorius de Valentiâ, tum nimirùm, quando dedit Apostolis potestatem ejiciendi Dæmonia Tom. 4. Commentar. Theol. disp. 4. quæst. 6. puncto 1. Nobis verò Exorcismus est Ceremonia, humanâ tantum autoritate introducta, antiqua quidem, & temporibus Tertulliani, Cypriani, Gregorij, Nazianzeni, Optati Milevitani, Augustini, & aliorum patrum ætate, modò usu recepta: sed libera prorsus & indifferens.

2. Pontificij eam vim tribuunt Exorcismo, ut ex opere operato conferat Spiritualem effectum, & Diabolos efficaciter insitâ & occultâ quadam vi propellat. Undè Concilium Tridentinum definivit, sine peccato eum omitti non posse. Sess. 7. Can. 13 d. 3. Martij. Anno 1547. Paulo III. Pontifice Romano. Nobis verò Usus Exorcismi tantùm est σημαντικος ἡ τυπικός, ut eminùs quasi adumbret, in quibus miserijs infans recens natus extra baptismum, quippè natura filius iræ, sit constitutus, & quod ex illis non nisi per instans lavacrum eripi possit.

Hisce differentiarum notis probè observatis, promptum est colligere, quis Spiritus ante annos viginti adegerit Calvinianos, quòd tàm funestum bellum adversus Exorcismum, in nostro hoc Electoratu moverunt. Certè non de Pontificiorum Exorcismo controvertebatur, quem vario superstitionum luto conspurcatum, & per se impium ac blasphemum esse, ipsi nos ultrò concedimus. Neque etiam de corporali aliquâ obsessone Diabolorum quæstio erat, ad quam in infantibus solvendam, Exorcismo opus sit: qualem profectò obsessionem nemo Orthodoxus unquam statuit. Sed nec de eo quærebatur, num ritus iste in locis, illis, in quibus semel est antiquatus; postliminio reduci, inquè usum revocari debeat. Negativam enim rursus nos ipsi tenemus, usque ideò, ut si in illis etiam Ecclesiis, in quibus adhuc ille observatur, justis de causis, modo legitimo, & consciâ ac consentiente Ecclesiâ abrogaretur, nemo orthodoxorum facilè reclamaturus effet. Quarto nec illud in controversia erat: An vel absolutæ necessitatis, vel pro parte substantiali in Baptismo Exorcismus haberi debeat? Negativam enim nos quoque amplectimur. Tandem neque illud contendebatur: An propter abufum Exorcismus abrogari possit & debeat. Nam nos quoque in Affirmantem concedimus. Verum in hoc solo cardo controversiæ consistebat: Num Exorcismus in censu rerum mediarum quas αδιαφορα vocant ritus iste sit habendus: an verò ad res toto genere vitiosas, impias & superstitiosas per se referri debeat? Sacramentarijs hoc posterius affirmantibus: Nobis verò prius illud amplectentibus. Nihil autem pro suâ parte plausibilius habuit gens ista, quo sensum suum astrueret, quam hoc unum: Ritum esse Pontificium. Quod ipsum tamen demonstrari non potuit: siquidem contrarium à nostris ostensum, neque sub Papatu ritum istum primò inventum, sed longè antiquiorum esse: neque etiam eodem fine ac usu à nostris, quo à Pontificijs observari. Antiquitas autem ejus monstrata ex illis Patrum scriptis, qui Papatu longè sunt antiquiores: Cypriani nimirùm Epist. lib. 4. ep. 7. Gregorij Nazianzeni in Oratione de S. Baptismi lavacro: Ambrosij de Sacramentis lib. 1. cap. 5. Augustini de peccator. meritis & remiss.lib. 1. cap. 34. item de Nuptijs & Concupisc. lib. 1. c. 20. & lib. 2. cap. 18.

Rationes autem, propter quas in gratiam Calvinianorum, Ecclesiæ nostræ Exorcismum abrogare noluerunt, præcipuæ sunt hæ.

1. Quia abrogationem hanc urserunt non in religione fratres: sed hostes Veritatis, domiminum in fidem & religionem nostram affectantes.

2. Quia eam urserunt, non ut rei alicujus adiaphoræ: sed ut impiæ, superstitiosæ, & detestandæ.

3. Quia sub hâc abrogatione conabantur incrustare dogma illud suum Calvinisticum de Sanctitate infantum ex utero materno ante perceptionem Baptismi.

4. Quia per hanc abrogationem hostes veritatis in erroribus suis confirmarentur; infirmi verò & in religione socij plurimùm offenderentur.

5. Quia in casu Confessionis, omnis prorsus species negatæ Veritatis est vitanda: & cumprimis quando per indirectum quasi & oblique puriorem nostram Religionem peti animadvertimus.

6. Quia Effectum Baptismi proprium, per abrogationem hanc; enervatum cupiebant.

7. Et postremò: Quia exemplo Apostoli, in ejusmodi casibus, ne quidem ad horam est cedendum falsis fratribus; ut Veritas Evangelij sarta tecta permaneat, Gal. 2, 4. & 5. Sed potiùs standum in libertate, in quam per Christum asserti sumus: Gal, 5, 1.

XII. Et postrema quæstio est: An qui Pontificiæ doctrinæ sunt addicti; possint bonâ & illatâ Conscientiâ adhiberi testes in Baptismo nostrorû infantum: & an Ministri Lutherani tales admittere debeunt? Circa quæstionis hujus decisionem facilè in negantem abeunt, quotquot ejusmodi in locis vivunt, in quibus Romanus Papatus planè exulat : quemadmodùm & illi, qui paulò accuratiùs expendunt finem primarium, cujus gratia consuetudo hæc adsciscendi patrinos sive testés, antiquitùs introducta fuit: qui fuit nullus alius, quàm ut patrini profilios, profiliasque parentibus jam orbatar, in Religione & fide Christianâ ritè edocerent. Hoc certè fine expenso, crudeles omninò forent parentes Lutherani, qui suos liberos Pontificijs erudiendos publico hoc ritu commendarent. Quam ob causam ministrorum Ecclesiæ officium esset, seriò & sæpiùs suos Auditores de hoc fine admonere: Sic enim ipsimet à Patrinis diversæ Religioni addictis suâ sponte abhorrerent. Cæterum cùm sive Ministrorum negligentiâ, sive Auditorum culpâ, de fine isto vix quisquam hodiè cogitet, sed alius planè diversus, & merè sermè politicus obtineat & spectetur: ut nimirùm liberi testes aliquando habere possint, se honesto & legitimo thoro esse progenitos: ut etiam ejusmodi patrinorum auxilio & consilio liberiùs uti possint: hinc etiam fit, ut mutato fine primario, alia quæstionis hujus decisio dari debeat. Accedit & illud, quòd in illis locis, ubi utriusque religionis homines mixtim & conjunctim vivūt, ea est politiæ ratio, ut sine ingenti confusione, & motibus gravioribus, Pontificij ab hoc testificandi officio non planè excludi possint. Et sanè quo minùs etiam tali casu excludantur, rationes videntur militare satis evidentes. Nam primò licet Romanenses Sacramento Baptismi ineptas & partim ridiculas, Ecclesiæq; primitivæ planè ignotas ceremonias addiderint: ipsimet tamen fatentur, eas ornamēti causa duntaxat esse additas, ac proinde, quantum ad substantiam Baptismi, nihil prorsus à nobis dissident. Deindè quotquot inEcclesijsPontificijs baptizandi sunt, verum Sacramentum percepisse, neque eos rebaptizandos esse statuimus. Quomodo ergò & quo jure à testimonio publico arceri possent illi, quos nos rectè baptizandos esse, ultrò agnoscimus & fatemur. Et hinc Canon ille sine dubio originem traxit, qui extat de Consecr. dist. 4. cap. In Baptismate : Qui ipse non est baptizatus, susceptoris munere fungi non potest. Tertiò, Quemadmodum rectè antiquitùs ab hoc officio remoti fuerunt extranei, sive illi, de quibus Apostolus pronunciat, quod foris sint, & nihil ad nos attineant: ita profectò Romanenses hoc casu pro extraneis haberi nec possunt nec debent: proptereà quòd de Sacrosanctâ Trinitate, quæ in Sacramenti hujus dispensatione religiosè & recitatur, & adoratur, nobiscum per omnia consentiunt. Quartò, si Ceremoniæ hujus per se adiaphoræ observatio, ipsi Baptismo nihil quicquam vel confert, vel derogat: si etiam ipsius Ministri dignitas aut indignitas, nihil Sacramento vel prodest, vel obest: utique, & quidem multò minus Patrinorum impietas aliquid detrimenti Baptismo allatura erit. Quintò, si gravissimas ob causas [...]

Ecclesia à Pontificijs baptizatos non retingit: cur non ferret eos, qui duntaxat testes adhibentur, si maximè in ipsis aliquid desideretur? Posset enim tota hæc ceremonia, salvo nihilo-minus Baptismo, prætermitti. Neque enim vel Johannes,vel Apostoli tot homines simul baptizantes, Patrinos adhibuisse leguntur: nec cum Philippus in itinere Æthiopem ex præterfluente baptizaret, testis ipsius Baptismo aderat. Testantur autem historiæ Hyginum natione Græcum, & Episcopum Romanum, anno demum post Christum natum 141. primùm Patrinos sive Compatres Baptismo adhibuisse. Sextò,res hæc caret omni periculo. Nam minister Evangelicus dùm ceremonijs nostris in Ecclesijs usitatis utitur: Pontificius autem negligit: certè hoc ipso facto testatur, se ad veras pietatis rationes initiare hunc infantem: eumque non in Pontificiâ, sed Evangelicâ Religione erudiendum esse. Septimò Patrini ipsi, quantumvis Pontificij, eo ipso, quod nostro Baptismo intersunt, palàm & publicè testantur, se nostras Ecclesias, nostraque Sacramenta, omninò approbare. Tandem negari non potest, multos Pontificiæ Religioni addictos, cum adhiberentur Patrini in nostris Ecclesijs, & audirent omnia religiosè, & quidem ex sacris proponi, ac intelligerent, criminationes suorum Doctorum, quas adversùm nos evomunt, falsas esse: non modò æquiùs & honorificentiùs de nostris Ecclesijs sensisse, sed tandem planè ad nos accessisse, & palàm veritatem professos. His rationibus adducti statuimus in illis potissimùm locis, ubi utriusque Religionis homines junctim vivunt, eodem Magistratu, ijsdemque legibus utuntur, Pontificios ab isto testimonij genere non esse excludendos: id quod tamen non intelligimus de ejusmodi Pontificijs, qui in doctrinam Evangelicam blasphemi sunt, Ecclesiam & Sacramenta nostra contemnunt, annihilant, & insectantur: Tales enim simpliciter excludendos, neque prius admittendos esse statuimus, quàm publicè testatum fecerint, se nostra Sacramēta pro veris habere & agnoscere.

Objiciunt nonnulli decisioni huic illud Apostolicum: Nolite ducere jugum cum impijs & infidelibus. Cæterùm manifestam committunt Sophisticationem ὠδὲ τὸ σχῆμα της λέξεως. Trahere enim jugū impijs & infidelibus idem est Apostolo, atque talium impietatem & infidelitatem, sive feriò, sive simulatè approbare: & sese horum Ecclesiæ, atque societati conjungere: Quorum neutrum fit à nobis:quin Pontificij hoc pacto se magis nobis,nostrisq; Ecclesijs associāt: quàm ut nos ad ipsos quoquo modo trāseamus.

Quod ipsum responderi debet ad illud alterum Apostoli præceptum, quo præcipit, ut ne cum scortatoribus, impuris, ac simulachrorum cultoribus nos commisceamus. Neq; enim hoc vult Apostolus, ut omni consuetudine impiorum nos abdicemus (sic enim è mundo nobis exeundum esset, uti ibidem ipse loquitur Apostolus) sed ut eam vitæ ac idolomaniæ consuetudinem & familiaritatem fugiamus, quæ cum aliquâ istius impietatis approbatione sit conjuncta: id quod Commiscendi verbum innuit, quod arctiorem consuetudinem, & quandam fidei societatem significare videtur. Quale nihil in præsenti casu, de quo quæritur, fieri manifestum est.

Sed objiciunt alij partim periculum quoad infantem, qui à tali Patrino Pontificio seduci facilè possit: partim scandalum, quod hoc pacto infirmiorribus præbeatur. Respondeo, utrumque istud militare tum, quando de primario fine hujus ceremoniæ, de quo suprà actum, est quæstio. Jam verò cum finis ille maximam partem apud nostros homines interciderit, qui politicum magis quoddam, vel etiam œconomicum commodum, atque emolumentum spectant: certè neque periculum, neque scandalum ullum ampliùs emergit. Quid? quod tali casu non ad Papisticam religionem infans in Baptismo adstringitur: sed multò magis testis, sive patrinus ille Pontificius, ad fidem & confessionem Symboli Apostolici semetipsum adstringit. Jam si puerum à se susceptum, articulos illos docuerit, nullum est seductionis periculum: Sin diversam, & cum his articulis pugnantem doctrinam puero inculcare velit, non jam ampliùs testis, sed proditor Veritatis judicabitur. Nec tenetur is, qui è baptismo susceptus est, aliquid committere contra professionem, quam per Patrinum in Baptismo fecit. Sic quoad scandalum optandum sanè foret, omnes nostros auditores ita esse perfectos, ut rei magnitudinem intelligerent: Cæterùm cum in tantâ hominum infirmitate tale quid sperari vix possit: utique inter duo mala quod minus, est eligengum: & operâ danda ministris, & ut infirmi, qui hoc facto offenduntur, rectiùs informentur: & hâc etiam in praxi talis servetur modus, ut ne nimirùm Pontificijs indulgere videamur: neque tamen eosdem nimio rigore magis nostris Ecclesijs infensos efficiamus: sed quantum salvâ veritate Evangelij fieri potest, pacem & concordiam externam sive Politicam, inter utriusque religionis homines conservemus.


## 21 On the Lord's Supper

The entire treatment of this Article, such as it appears in the book of Theological Commonplaces of Dr. Philipp Melanchthon, consists of two parts: the former of which contains certain prolegomena, the latter the exposition itself. The prolegomena are again tripartite. First, the author discourses partly on the divine manifestations, by which, as by illustrious testimonies, GOD has offered Himself to be known by the human race; and partly on the promises, by which He has revealed His will concerning the salvation of men; but in such a way that he has always added rites that strike the eyes, as certain and indubitable seals of the Evangelical promise. Then he recounts three causes of this fact: the first of which is that those using these signs might be reminded of the promise and the will of GOD toward us, and thus faith toward GOD might be excited and confirmed in us through them. Second, that the memory might be more publicly durable, and the promise might be more certainly propagated to all posterity; for things that are visible are more rightly conducive to refreshing and propagating memory than those which remain in the mind without these external aids. Third, that those rites might be the nerves of public assemblies, in which GOD wishes the voice of the Gospel to sound, and wishes to be celebrated and invoked, and a manifest separation of His people to be made from the congregations and sects of other religions. Finally, he speaks of the excellence of the Sacrament of the Eucharist, showing that among all other rites, not even excepting the sign which GOD established for our first parents in paradise in the tree of life, there is none more excellent in dignity, or more convenient in use, or more wholesome in efficacy than that which the Savior willed to be sanctioned for us before His death in this Sacrament, so that it might be a memorial of His death, and might not be abrogated by any other pledge of His grace, but remain until the very end of this world. And such are the Philippean prolegomena.

Regarding the exposition itself of this Article, Philipp himself willed it to be quadripartite. For first he shows how the Lord's Supper was instituted, not that it should be some empty spectacle, but such a sacrament in which CHRIST is truly present, giving through this ministry His body and blood to the one eating and drinking, to the end that both we may be in CHRIST, and CHRIST in us. Then he shows to whom this eating is profitable: not to those who abstain from its use, nor to the unworthy, but to those who bring faith and repentance to this Sacrament, to whom faith in the remission of sins is also confirmed through this medium. Where at the same time the author inveighs with just zeal against the dogma of the Scholastics and Papists concerning the work performed. Third, he admonishes who are to be admitted to the use of this Sacrament: not those who labor under manifest wickedness of life and morals, but the truly repentant, according to that: Do not give what is holy to the dogs!
