For GOD does not need a sacrifice: but the conscience of him who offers sanctifies the sacrifice, being pure, and causes GOD to accept it as from a friend. And Nazianzen in his oration on Julian: Announcing the death of the only-begotten Son of GOD JESUS CHRIST, and confessing His resurrection and likewise His ascension into heaven, we celebrate the bloodless worship of the sacrifice, and we approach the mystical blessings, and are sanctified, having been made partakers of the Holy Body and precious Blood of CHRIST.

The third difference is sought from the thing and matter of the sacrifice. For the primitive Church, as Irenaeus testifies in book 4, chapter 32, in its oblations offers to GOD from the first-fruits of its gifts, and from the creatures which are His. But the Romanists say that they offer to GOD the Father His very only-begotten Son: As will be demonstrated more fully in its proper place from the writings of the Pontificians themselves.

The fourth difference is taken from those things that conflict with the priesthood of CHRIST: For the Fathers determined that their sacrifice, or rather the sacrifice of the New Testament, was made and ratified in the priesthood of CHRIST Himself: But the Romanists think that the completion of the New Testament subsists not in the priesthood of CHRIST, but in the daily sacrifice of the Mass: as we shall hear in its proper place.

Whence it becomes manifest that there is as much difference between the sacrifices of the Holy Fathers and the opinion of the Romanists as there is between a shadow and a body, or rather as much as between the sun and darkness.

We do not, however, offer any violence to the writings of the Fathers: for we are certainly not ignorant that the Eucharist is called by the Fathers a holy, life-giving, bloodless sacrifice: but in the meantime we also know this, that the bloodless sacrifice is not defined by them in the Papistic sense: but in this Orthodox one, by which, indeed, the reason and definition of this bloodless sacrifice consists in memory, and in thanksgiving, and in the mystical exhibition of things through symbols.

Eusebius, Demonstratio Evangelica, book 1: CHRIST, he says, offered an admirable Sacrifice and an excellent victim for the salvation of us all, handing down also a memorial to us, which we shall always offer to GOD instead of a Sacrifice. We have learned to perform the memorial of this Sacrifice at the table through the Symbols of his Body and saving Blood, according to the laws of the New Testament. And a little later: We sacrifice the memorial of that great Sacrifice. Likewise again after a few words: We immolate to GOD θυσίαν ἀινέσεως, a Sacrifice of praise: We immolate the Sacrifice which the Prophet mentions, a contrite spirit and a humbled heart: we burn the prophetic incense, bringing to him in every place the sweet fruit of holy religion, offering it through our prayers to him.

Augustine agrees with these, book 20 against Faustus, chapter 23: The Flesh and Blood of this Sacrifice were promised through the victims of likenesses before the coming of CHRIST: they were rendered through the truth itself during the passion of CHRIST: they are celebrated through the Sacrament of memory after the ascension of CHRIST.

The remaining Fathers also hold this same opinion: Even if perhaps some present themselves who have spoken less appropriately: let the Romanists remember, however, that a dogma of faith is not

must be confirmed by the oracles of the Fathers, not of Councils, but of the Holy Spirit alone, revealed in the Word. Concerning which matter, more fully in its proper place.

Finally: to the error concerning the Mass-Sacrifice already refuted, there is added with good reason that superstition of the Romanists, by which, through a foolish κακοζηλίαν [bad zeal], in imitation of that Levitical water which they called the Water of Aspersion, and which was sprinkled with the ashes of a burnt red heifer, they have fabricated a certain Holy Water, and have ascribed to it some peculiar spiritual power of cleansing or expiating: but without any certain Word of GOD, without command, without promise. Therefore, having bidden farewell to those absurdities, we diligently observe that Apostolic command which bids us not to allow ourselves to be led away, as if by a return, to the weak and beggarly elements of this world, from which CHRIST has redeemed us and asserted us into a liberty empty of shadows and types.

To whom for this ineffable benefit also, be praise, honor, and glory, for infinite ages of ages, AMEN.

Latin:

Cæterum: fuerunt semper plurimi, hodieq; sunt, qui circa hanc doctrinã de Sacrificijs, varias & erroneas opiniones spargant. Ac initiò quidem occurrunt Gentiles sive Ethnici, qui de Judæorum Sacrificijs audientes, per impiam quandam κακοζηλίαν, varia excogitarunt Sacrificia, quæ tamen Suida admonente, in Sacrificia perfecta & imperfecta ab ipsis Gentilibus dividebantur.

Et Sacrificia quidem perfecta nominabant, in quibꝫ animalia, imò (proh scelus) ipsos etiã homines vivos & filios suos offerebant, uti videreest 2. Reg. 3, 27. de rege Moabitarum, qui in angustijs constitutus obtulit filium suum holocaustum super murum. Quæ impietas ad ipsos postmodum Judæos dimanavit. Deut. 12, 31. 2. Reg. 16, 3. cap. 21, 6. ubi Achas & Manasse leguntur filios suos igne cremasse.

Imperfecta Sacrificia nominabant, quæ ex quacunque materiâ vili & abjectâ: imò ex partibus etiam animantium offerebantur: Qualia Sacrificia erant Phaselitarum, qui Salsamenta Calabro immolârunt, teste Callimacho in Barbaricis institutis, ut est apud Suidam pag. 950. item sacra Nephalia θυσίας νηφάλιοι, in quibus vinum non bibebatur: sed aqua mulsa, uti rursus refert Suidas. p. 621.

Verùm habuerunt hæc gentilium Sacrificia suos irrisores, non modò impium illum Lucianum, in Dialogo Promethei & Jovis: ubi introducit Jovem expostulantem cum Prometheo, quòd inique partitus esset Sacrificium cum DEO suo Jove, unâ quidem ex parte positis ossibus, sed pelle victimæ tectis ex alterâ verò carnibus, quas solus ipse voraverat, relictis Jovi DEO suo duntaxat ossibus. Sed habuerunt etiam civiliter sapientes, qui Sacrificijs DEUM expiari negabant: ut Cato: Cùm sis ipse nocens, moritur cur victima pro te?

Et Ovid. Epist. 19. Heroid. Non bove mactato cælestia numina gaudent Sed quæ præstanda est, & sine teste, fide.

Verùm omissis Gentibus, quippè extra Ecclesiam constitutis, ea falsa dogmata accessum faciemus, quæ in ipso Ecclesiæ gremio fuerunt sparsa.

Et primam quidem errantium classem obtinent Pharisæi, qui quantumvis exhibito Messiâ nihilominus Sacrificiorum ritum adeò necessarium statuebant, ut ex opere operato illud prodesse statuerent, imò omnibus virtutibus & operibus charitatis, & sic consequenter ipsi Legi DEI morali, illa præferrent, dicentes, longè gratiorem esse cultum, si offert Sacrificia populus, quàm si sumtibus illis Sacrificiorum juvaret inopes parentes. Matth. 15, 5. & 6. Alteram classem occupant Judæi, qui hodieque Sacrificiorum Leviticorum ritum urgent: quorum tanta impietas jam modò est refutata.

Post Pharisæos nullos alios reperire licet hæreticos, qui item in Ecclesiâ publicè de Sacrificijs moverint, nisi eos fortassis huc vocandos esse statuas, qui Vetus Testamentum, & sic Sacrificiorum etiam universum cultum, prorsus repudiarunt: Quales Augustino, & Epiphanio testibus fuerunt, Simoniani, Cajani Archontici, Cerdoniani, Marcionitæ, Apellitæ, Severiani, Taciani, Manichæi &c.

Cæterùm posterioribus hisce seculis, Antichristus Filius ille perditionis, ex antro, & Infumibulo ipsius inferni novum produxit dogma, de Sacrificio quodam Propitiatorio, verè ac propriè sic dicto: Quod ipse, & ejus Sacrificuli, Missaticum nominare solent.

Quem Sacrificij terminum, si vel maximè sensu Sacrificij terminum generaliter, & ἐκπλᾶτη pro cultu quodam acciperent, ac Missam generaliter Sacrificium appellitari affirmarent: tamen ne sic quidem illud Idolum salvare possent: Manet enim firmum & immotum illud Servatoris, Matth. 15, 9. Frustrà colunt me, docentes mandata hominum. Totus siquidem cultus ille Missaticus, nullo verbo DEI, nullo mandato, nullâ promissione, nullo exemplo Ecclesiæ Orthodoxæ gaudet. Cæterùm, Quale Sacrificium Missaticum, nùm Methaphorico, an proprio sensu acceptum, intelligant, juvat ex ipsorum monumentis cognoscere. Sic ergò Concilium Tridentinum: Si quis dixerit, Missæ Sacrificium esse tantùm laudis & gratiarum actionis, aut nudam Commemorationem sacrificij in cruce peracti, non autem Propitiatorium: vel soli prodesse sumenti, nequè pro vivis & defunctis, pro peccatis, pœnis, satisfactionibus, & alijs necessitatibus offerri debere, anathema sit. Sess. 22. Can. 3. Quam impietatem novo quodam Paradoxo auget Bellarminus, l. 2. de Missâ: c. 2. afferens, Missam esse Sacrificium applicans promissiones Testamenti Novi, de Remissione peccatorum. Et cap. 4. affirmans, Sacrificium Missæ non habere vim solùm ex opere operantis, sed etiam ex opere operato.

Cæterùm, cùm ex professo adversus Missaticum hoc Idolum alibi nobis dicendum sit; nunc illud duntaxat expediemus, An S. Eucharistia Sacrificium propriè sic dictum appellari vel possit, vel debeat?

Cur sacram cœnam plerique Veterum nominarint Sacrificium, patebit ex evolutione illius ὁμωνυμίας sive æquivocationis, quæ in Patrum scriptis, circa usum vocabuli Sacrificij sese offert: Interdum enim per Sacrificium intelligunt oblationem munerum, sive ἀγαπῶν, inter quas panis & vinum, principem locum obtinebant, quæ nomine totius Ecclesiæ gratitudinis ergò offerebantur, uti videre est apud Irenæum l. 4. cap. 32. & 34. Interdum verò per Sacrificium nihil notant aliud, quàm memoriam Sacrificij veri illius & unici Sacrificij; quæ in usu Sacramenti Eucharistici à fidelibus institui debeat. Quâ de re sic Augustinus l. 10. contra Faustum cap. 18. Hebræi in victimis pecudum, quas offerebant DEO, prophetiam celebrabant futuræ victimæ, quam CHRISTUS obtulit: Christiani jam peracti Sacrificij memoriam celebrant, Sacrosanctâ oblatione & participatione corporis CHRISTI. Quod ipsum pluribus verbis explicat in libro de fide ad Petrum Diaconum (quanquam dubitatur, an hic liber sit Augustini) Idem l. 4 de Trin. c. 24.

Proindè nihil præsidij ex hisce Patrum locutionibus ad Romanensium fictitium Sacrificium stabiliendum redundare potest: Constat enim Sacrificiorum termino illos partim respexisse ad ἀγαπας, sive Eleemosynarum distributionem, quæ cum Sacræ Eucharistiæ celebratione antiquitùs conjungebatur: partim verò ad memoriam Sacrificij CHRISTI, quod in Symbolorum Sacramentalium distributione quodammodò adumbratur: eo fermè modo, quo Apostolus in oculis Galatarum CHRISTUM crucifixum fuisse affirmat, dùm illis prædicatio crucis fuerat proposita, & propè inculcata.

Interim verò minimè diffitemur, quòd progressu temporis Patrum nonnulli nimiùm deflexerunt ad Judaicum sacrificandi morem, & propius ad Legis umbram quasi inclinarunt, quàm vel CHRISTI Ordinatio, vel Evangelij ratio ferebat. Ubi tamen ne sic quidem Romanenses pro Sacrificio Missatico confirmando quicquam fundamenti invenient: Siquidem neque in istorum Patrum monumentis Eucharistia uspiam appellatur Sacrificium propriè sic dictum, nedùm Sacrificium propitiatorium pro peccatis, pœnis ac culpis, tâm defunctorum, quàm vivorum: Sed Sacrificium duntaxat Laudis, Gratiarum actionis, & memoriæ, ut videre est apud Eusebium lib. 1. de Demonstrat. & apud Augustinum lib. 20. contra Faustum, cap. 13.

Et sunt in promtu discrimina, quæ Ecclesiæ Patrum, & Synagogæ Pontificiæ circa usum vocabuli Sacrificij intercedunt: Etenim si rem accuratiùs expendamus, quatuor potissimùm modis Sacrificia illa Veteris Ecclesiæ, à Sacrificio Missatico differre videntur.

Prima differentiæ nota peti potest à Formâ & Modo utriusquè Sacrificij. In primitivâ enim Ecclesiâ Sacrificium dictum fuit, ipsa communis ac generalis κοινωνία sive dispensatio Cœnæ: Undè Eucharistia etiam Ambrosio, Chrysostomo, Augustino dicitur Exemplum, Figura, Signum, Imago unici illius veri Sacrificij CHRISTI. Et Cyrillus Epistola 11. Synodica: Si inquit, Christus non esset crucifixus, Sacrificium Corporis ipsius non ederemus.

Altera desumitur à Fine Sacrificij: Primitivæ enim illi Ecclesiæ Eucharistia non erat Sacrificium aliquod ἱλαστικὸν, sive propitiatorium, quod alijs esset ex ipsâ operis virtute applicandum. At Romanensibus Sacrificium Missaticum est ἱλαστικὸν pro peccato, pœnis ac culpis vivorum & mortuorum.

De quo discrimine præclarè Irenæus lib. 4. cap. 34. Non Sacrificia sanctificant hominem. Non enim indiget Sacrificio DEUS: sed conscientia ejus, qui offert, sanctificat Sacrificiũ, pura existens, & præstat, acceptare DEUM, quasi ab amico, Et Nazianzenus oratione in Julianum: Annunciantes mortem unigeniti Filij DEI JESU CHRISTI, & Resurrectionem ejus, atq; in Cælos ascensionem pariter confitentes, Incruentum celebram9 Sacrificij cultũ, & ad Mysticas benedictiones accedimg, & sanctificamur, Participes Sancti Corporis, & pretiosi Sangvinis CHRISTI effecti.

Tertia differentia à Re & Materiâ Sacrificij petitur. Primitiva enim Ecclesia, teste Irenæo l. 4, c. 32. in oblationibus suis offert DEO ex primitijs suorum munerum, & ex creaturis, quæ sunt ejus. Ac verò Romanenses offerre se dicunt DEO Patri ipsum Filium ejus unigenitum: Quemadmodum hoc suo loco fusiùs ex ipsis Pontificiorum scriptis demonstrabitur.

Quarta differentia à Pugnantibus cum Sacerdotio CHRISTI desumta est: Patres enim Sacrificium suum, vel Sacrificium potiùs Novi Testamenti, in ipsius CHRISTI Sacerdotio fieri, & ratum esse statuerunt: Ac verò Romanenses non in CHRISTI, sed in quotidiano Missæ Sacrificio, Novi Testamenti complementum subsistere autumant: uti suo loco audiemus.

Unde manifestum evadit, tantum discriminis S. Patrum Sacrificijs cum sententiâ Romanensium intercedere, quantum umbræ & corpori, imò quantum Soli & tenebris.

Nullam verò vim Patrum scriptis inferimus: nam certè non ignoramus, Eucharistiam Sacrificium sanctum, vivificum, incruentum à Patribus dici: sed interim novimus & illud, Incruentum Sacrificium non sensu Papistico ab illis definiri: sed hoc Orthodoxo, quo nimirùm Incruenti hujus Sacrificij ratio, ac definitio in memoriâ, & gratiarum actione, & in mystica rerum per Symbola exhibitione versatur.

Eusebius de Demonstrat. l. 1, CHRISTUS inquit, pro salute omnium nostrum admirabile Sacrificium, & victimam eximiam obtulit, memoriam etiam & nobis tradens, quam pro Sacrificio semper DEO offeremus. Hujus autem Sacrificij memoriam in mensâ perficere per Symbola Corporis, & salutaris Sangvinis ejus, juxta leges Novi Testamenti didicimus. Et paulo post: Sacrificamus memoriam magni illius Sacrificij. Item rursus post pauca: Immolamus, DEO θυσίαν ἀινέσεως, Sacrificium laudis: Immolamus Sacrificium, cujus Propheta meminit, Spiritum contritum, & Cor humiliatum: incendimus suffitum propheticum, in omni loco afferentes ei suavem fructum sanctæ religionis, per preces ad illum nostras offerentes.

Quibus adstipulatur Augustinus l. 20. contra Faustum cap. 23. Hujus Sacrificij Caro & Sangvis ante adventum CHRISTI per victimas similitudinum promittebatur: in passione CHRISTI per ipsam veritatem reddebatur: post ascensum CHRISTI per Sacramentum memoria celebratur.

Quam eandem sententiam reliqui etiam tenent Patres: Etsi fortassis sese offerunt nonnulli, qui minùs commodè locuti sunt: Meminerint tamen Romanenses, dogma fidei non

Patrum, non Conciliorum, sed solius Spiritus Sancti oraculis, in Verbo revelatis, esse confirmanda. Quâ de re suo loco copiosiùs.

Denique : errori de Sacrificio Missatico jam confutato, adjungitur suo merito illa quoque Romanensium superstitio, quâ per stultam κακοζηλίαν, ad imitationem Aquæ illius Leviticæ, quam Aspersionis vocabant, quæque cineribus vaccæ rufæ combustæ inspergebatur, confinxerunt Aquam aliquam Lustralem, eíque peculiarem aliquam purgandi, sive expiandi vim spiritualem adscripserunt : sed sine certo DEI Verbo, sine mandato, sine promissione. Proindè nos ineptijs istis valere jussis, illud Apostolicum sedulò observamus, quo jubet, ut ne postliminiò quasi abduci nos patiamur, ad infirma & egena mundi hujus Elementa, à quibus CHRISTUS nos redemit, inque libertatem, umbrarum & Typorum vacuam, asseruit.

Cui pro hoc etiam ineffabili beneficio, sit laus, honos, & gloria, in infinita seculorum secula, AMEN.


## 23 On Penance


### The Economy of the Future Treatment

The treatment of this Article is generally structured by all Methodical writers, as it is by our author Philip, in such a way that an inquiry into its integral parts is instituted at the beginning: then, indeed, these having been elicited and established, the definition of the thing itself is submitted, where, however, our author obtains that peculiar feature, that both at the front and at the back, that is, from the beginning and from the end of the treatment, he wished to set forth some things as a kind of garrison against various heresies. At the front, indeed, when he shows in place of a προβυλάξεως [precaution] that our Churches have nothing in common with the heresy of the Libertines, nor with that of the Novatians. At the back, however, when, like an ὑπερασπίσεως [defense], he touches upon and refutes the errors of the Papists, with the analogy of faith opposed in this Article as well. To which two members, if a third intermediate one is added, which explains the purer doctrine concerning the parts of penitence, namely contrition and Faith: the entire Philippean treatment emerges as tripartite.

they do not agree with the form of sound words, nor do they taste of ὀρθοδοξίαν [orthodoxy] in all things.

THE FIRST is that, in the refutation of the heresy of the Novatians, speaking of the irremissible sin or the sin against the Holy Spirit, following Augustine, he wrongly defines it by final impenitence and despair. For although these two are the παρεπόμενα [concomitants] or adjuncts of this sin: so that there is no sin against the Holy Spirit unless there is final impenitence: yet these are not ἀντιστρέφοντα [convertible] or reciprocal in both their parts: they are only ἀναστρέφοντα [consequent], indeed in such a way that every sin against the Holy Spirit always has final impenitence as an adjunct: but not vice versa, that every final impenitence is a sin against the Holy Spirit: as was expressly demonstrated in the digression of the Article concerning Sin.

The latter point is that the Author teaches that that former part of repentance, contrition, must be sought not from the Law alone, but from the Gospel, in these words: 'However, the voice of the moral law must be used for this part of the ministry: For that Law is the eternal and immutable sentence of GOD, declaring the wrath of GOD against sin: the voice of the Gospel must also be used, which accuses the world of contempt for wrath and mercy, which is seen in the Son being exhibited: therefore CHRIST says: The Holy Spirit will convict the world of sin, because they do not believe in me.' So far Philip, to whom we, having followed ὀρθοδοξίαν (orthodoxy) both founded in the Holy Scriptures and more deeply repeated and explained in the Symbolic book of our Churches, namely the Formula of Concord, can by no means subscribe. For this assertion, that not only the Law, but also the Gospel convicts of sins, removes the true and essential distinction between the Law and the Gospel, and indeed entirely. For the specific difference of the Law consists in this very thing, by which the Law is separated from the Gospel and distinguished ἀντιδιηρημένως (in opposition): namely, that it is the property of the Law, and entirely incommunicable to the doctrine of the Gospel properly so called, to convict of sins. Nor does the added proof taken from the words of CHRIST, John 16:9, sustain any strength of importance. For the Holy Spirit convicts the world of sin, not from the Gospel, but from the Law alone, which convicts, accuses, and condemns every doubt about GOD and unbelief: although the Gospel alone shows and proposes the object of this unbelief, namely CHRIST with his merit.

With those two errors excluded, the entire remaining Treatise of Philip easily deserves the praise of ὀρθοδοξίας (orthodoxy), although some harsher and less convenient phrases occur: such as especially this one: 'The Holy Spirit is given when we sustain ourselves by faith': Which assertion, if it is taken simply as it sounds, and indeed concerning that first bestowal of the gifts of the grace of the Holy Spirit, cannot be borne: since our Faith is not the meritorious cause of the gifts of the grace of the Holy Spirit, nor is it prior to that gracious

Latin:

Articuli hujus Tractatio, plerumque ab omnibus Scriptoribus Methodicis, ut ab Autore nostro Philippo, ita informatur, ut in partes ejus integrales initiò instituatur inquisitio: deindè verò his erutis & constitutis, ipsa rei definitio subjiciatur, ubi tamen Autor noster peculiare illud obtinet, quòd & à fronte & à tergo, hoc est, ab initio, & à fine tractationis, præsidij quasi loco adversus varias hæreses nonnulla expedire voluit. A fronte quidem, cùm προβυλάξεως loco ostendit, nostris Ecclesiis, neque cùm Libertinorum, neque cùm Novatianorum hæresi, quicquam commune esse. A tergo verò, cum instar ὑπερασπίσεως, errores Pontificiorum, analogiæ fidei hoc etiam in Articulo opposito, perstringit & refutat. Quibus duobus membris, si addatur intermedium tertium, quod puriorem doctrinam de partibus pœnitentiæ, contritione nimirùm & Fide explicat: universa Tractatio Philippea emergit tripartita.

formâ fanorum verborum non confentiunt, neque ὀρθοδοξίαν per omnia fapiunt.

PRIMUS est, quod in refutatione hæreseos Novatianorum, verba faciens de peccato irremissibili sive in Spiritum Sanctum, Augustinum secutus, perperàm illud definit per finalem impœnitentiam ac desperationem. Etsi enim duo isthæc Individua sunt peccati hujus παρεπόμενα sive adjuncta: ita ut peccatum in Spiritum Sanctum non sit, nisi ubi finalis est impœnitentia: sunt tamen hæc non ἀντιστρέφοντα sive utrâque sui parte reciproca: ἀναστρέφοντα tantùm, ita quidem, ut omne peccatum Spiritum Sanctum, habeat semper adjunctam finalem impœnitentiam: non verò vice versa, omnis finalis impœnitentia, sit peccatum in Spiritum Sanctum: uti in diexodo Articuli de Peccato ex professo demonstratum fuit.

POSTERIUS est, quod Autor, contritionem priorem illam pœnitentiæ partem non ex solâ lege, sed ex Evangelio, petendam esse docet, his verbis: Utendum est autem voce legis moralis, ad hanc ministerij partem: Est enim Lex illa, æterna & immutabilis sententia DEI, declarans iram DEI, adversus peccatum: utendum est & voce Evangelij, quæ accusat in mundo contemtum iræ & misericordiæ, quæ cernitur exhibito filio: ideò inquit CHRISTUS: Spiritus Sanctus arguet mundum de peccato, quod non credunt in me. Hactenus Philippus, cui nos secuti ὀρθοδοξίαν tùm in sacris literis fundatam, tùm in libro Ecclesiarum nostrarum Symbolico, Formulâ nimirùm Concordiæ altiùs repetitam & explicatam, subscribere nullâ ratione possumus. Hæc enim assertio, quod nimirùm non Lex tantùm, sed & Evangelium arguat peccata, verum ac essentiale discrimen Legis & Evangelij tollit, & quidem ex toto. Nam in hoc ipso specifica legis differentia consistit, quâ ab Evangelio Lex dirimitur, & ἀντιδιηρημένως distingvitur: nempè quòd Legis proprium sit, & doctrinæ Evangelij propriè sic dicti, prorsus incommunicabile, arguere peccata. Neque adjecta probatio petita ex verbis CHRISTI, Johan. 16, 9. quicquam roboris momenti sustinet. Nam Spiritus Sanctus arguit mundum de peccato, non ex Evangelio: sed ex solâ Lege, quæ omnem dubitationem de DEO, & incredulitatem, arguit, accusat, damnat: licet incredulitatis hujus objectum, CHRISTUM videlicet cum suo merito, solum Evangelium monstret & proponat.

Duobus istis erroribus exclusis, reliqua universa Tractatio Philippi ὀρθοδοξίας laudem facilè meretur, licèt occurrant phrases nonnullæ duriores, minusque commodæ: qualis cumprimis est hæc: Spiritus Sanctus datur, cùm fide nos sustentamus: Quæ sanè assertio si simpliciter, prout sonat, & quidem de primâ illâ collatione donorum gratiæ Spiritus Sancti accipiatur, ferri nequit: Siquidem Fides nostra non est causa promerens dona gratiæ Spiritus Sancti, neque etiam prior est illâ inhabitatio-


### The opinion of the ancient Novatians concerning penance

indwelling of the Holy Spirit: but faith in the order of nature is posterior, just as an effect is posterior to its cause. For faith is conferred upon man only by the Holy Spirit: and therefore in the believing man they are always present at the same time. But if it is understood regarding the increments of the gifts of the Holy Spirit, by reason of our renewal: we easily admit it. But we will not recall individual things to ἀκρίβειαν [precision]: rather, having followed the son of the Philippic treatment: in the beginning, in place of προλεγομένων [prolegomena], we will premise certain few things, concerning both that heresy of the Libertines and of the Novatians: of which our Author makes mention. To these, in the second place, we will subject the exposition of this Article itself, enclosed in three distinct chapters: of which the FIRST will explain τὸ τί ἐστὶ [what it is], What Penance is, and will show that it is most viciously defined by the Romanists as a Sacrament properly so called. THE SECOND will propose the purer doctrine of our Churches concerning the parts of penance, and will build upon immovable foundations. THE THIRD and last will cleanse that stable of Augeas, which the Romanists even today strive to establish and defend, filled with the foulest filth and dung of abominations concerning the three parts of penance.

PROLEGOMENA

Concerning the Heresy of the Novatians and Libertines, regarding this Article.

Enemies of true penance, and of our true conversion to GOD, can be called both those ancient Novatians and the more recent Libertines: although they have proceeded in different ways and studies to impugn the truth: the former indeed contending that penance is not useful to those who have fallen after Baptism: the latter indeed asserting that it is not necessary for them.

For as regards the Novatians, they denied, as Epiphanius testifies, that those who have fallen after Baptism can any longer obtain mercy: or as others report, that no hope of salvation remains for them, even if they knock at the doors of the Church with tears, groaning, and sorrow of heart, and perform all things pertaining to sincere conversion and pure conversion. Which heresy, although it was condemned in various Synods, gathered partly in Africa, partly in Italy, nevertheless always repullulated, so that it lasted until the times of Constantine the Great and the Nicene Council, that is, until the year of Christ 325: with Emperor Constantine indeed expending every effort so that it might at last be extirpated by the root: concerning which historians also report that in the Nicene Synod itself, he said to Acesius, a Bishop of this sect: Therefore, Acesius, set up a ladder to heaven, and ascend alone: thus implying that there is no one even from the assembly of the baptized who is ἀναμάρτητος [sinless], such as Acesius boasted himself and his accomplices to be; as Socrates testifies, book 1, hist. Eccl. ch. 7. And Sozomen, book 1, chapter 21.

Moreover, to this impious and sacrilegious heresy, examples of Scripture are to be opposed at the beginning, such as that of David, who through penance obtained pardon for adultery and homicide: indeed, having lost this again through the proud census of the people, yet having performed penance again, he returned into favor with GOD. Another example, and a very illustrious one, is also supplied by the history of Peter the Apostle: likewise that of the incestuous man, who, although delivered to Satan by the Apostle, 1 Cor. 5:5, nevertheless after penance obtained remission of the offense. 2 Cor. 2:8.

Then, the clear testimonies of sacred Scripture are to be opposed: such as that: Ezek. 18:23 and ch. 33:11. As I live, says the Lord, I do not desire the death of the sinner, but that the wicked man turn from his evil way, and live. Ps. 32:6. For the remission of sins every Saint will pray to you. Ezek. 33:12. Turn, turn from your worst ways, and why will you die, O house of Israel. Acts 17:30. Now GOD announces to all men everywhere that they should perform penance. 2 Pet. 3:9. GOD does not want any to perish, but all to return to penance.

Thirdly, these reasons argue the stupendous impiety of the Novatian dogma.

I. The scope of the Gospel consists solely in this, that not only once to those to be converted to the faith, but indefinitely to all who repent, grace and the remission of sins should be announced.

II. Unless the doors of grace were open to those repenting after a fall, the use of the keys in the Church would be entirely null; since the promise and certainty of Absolution was destined by CHRIST only for the fallen and for sinners, according to that passage in John 20:23: Whosesoever sins you remit on earth, they shall be remitted in heaven.

III. Thence it would follow that the sins of the fallen exceed the immensity of divine grace and the merit of Christ.

IV. The fifth petition of the Lord's Prayer would clearly become obsolete, and would be vain and void.

But the Novatians, to cloak that error of theirs, chiefly employed two testimonies of Scripture, taken from chapter 6, verses 4, 5, and 6, as also from chapter 10, 26, of the Epistle to the Hebrews. The former reads thus: It is impossible for those who were once enlightened, and have tasted of the heavenly gift, and were made partakers of the Holy Ghost, and have tasted the good word of God, and the powers of the world to come, and have fallen away, to be renewed again unto repentance, crucifying to themselves the Son of God, and putting him to an open shame. The latter, however, reads thus: For if we sin wilfully after that we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins.

But it is most rightly answered that a shameful sophistry of ignorance of the refutation and of the fallacy of the consequent is being committed. For neither passage treats of just any sins after

Latin:

ne gratiosâ Spiritus Sancti: sed fides ratione ordinis posterior est, uti effectus posterior est sua causa. Siquidem fides non nisi à Spiritu Sancto homini confertur: ac proindè in homine credente tempore semper simul sunt. Sin autem de incrementis donorum Spiritus Sancti, ratione renovationis nostræ intelligatur: facilè eam admittimus. Verùm ad ἀκρίβειαν singula non revocabimus: quin secuti potiùs filium tractationis Philippicæ: initiò προλεγομένων loco pauca quædam præmittemus, de utrâque illâ & Libertinorum & Novatianorum hæresi: quarum meminit Autor noster. His secundo loco subjiciemus ipsam Articuli hujus diexodon, tribus distinctis capitibus inclusam: quorum PRIMUM τὸ τί ἐστὶ, Quid sit Pœnitentia expediet, & quòd à Romanensibus vitiosissimè per Sacramentum propriè sic dictum definiatur, ostendet. ALTERUM puriorem Ecclesiarum nostrarum doctrinam de partibus pœnitentiæ proponet, & immotis fundamentis superstruet.. TERTIUM ac postremum expurgabit Augiæ illud stabulum, quod de tribus pœnitentiæ partibus, Romanenses hodieque fœdissimis abominationum fordibus ac stercoribus repletum stabilire & propugnare student.

ΠΡΟΛΕΓΟΜΕΝΑ

De Hæresi Novatianorum & Libertinorum, quoad hunc Articulum.

HOstes veræ pœnitentiæ, & nostræ ad DEUM conversionis veræ dici possunt tùm Veteres illi Novatiani, tùm recentiores Libertini: quanquàm diversis modis ac studijs ad impugnandam veritatem progressi sunt: illi quidem contendentes, lapsis post Baptismum pœnitentiam non esse utilem: hi verò asserentes, eam ijsdem non esse necessariam.

Nam quoad Novatianos, negabant isti, teste Epiphanio, eos qui post Baptismum lapsi sunt, posse ampliùs misericordiam consequi: vel ut alij referunt, nullam his salutis spem esse reliquam, licèt lachrymis, gemitu & dolore cordis Ecclesiæ fores pulsent, & cuncta, ad sinceram conversionem, & puram conversionem pertinentia, perficiant. Quæ hæresis licèt in diversis Synodis, partim in Africâ, partim in Italiâ congregatis, damnata fuerit, semper tamen repullulavit, ita ut ad tempora usq́; Constantini M. & Concilij Niceni, hoc est, ad Annum Christi 325. duraret: Constantino quidem Imp. omnem operam impendente, quô vel tandem radicitùs ea extirpari possit: de quo etiam referunt historici, quod in ipsâ Synodo Nicenâ, ad Acesium sectæ hujus Episcopum dixerit: Ergò tu Acesi scalas cœlo admove, & solus ascende: sic innuendo, neminem ex baptizatorum etiam cœtu dari posse, qui sit ἀναμάρτητος, qualem se, suosque complices mentiebatur Acesius; teste Socrate, lib. 1. hist. Eccl. c. 7. Et Sozom. lib. 1. cap. 21.

Sunt autem impiæ huic & Sacrilegæ hæresi opponēda initio Exempla Scripturæ, qualia sunt Davidis, qui per pœnitentiam, adulterij & homicidij veniam impetravit : imò hac rursus, per superbam populi recensionem amissa, tamen actâ iterum pœnitentiâ, in gratiam cum DEO redijt. Exemplum aliud, idque valdè illustre suppeditat etiam historia Petri Apostoli : item incestuosi illius, qui ab Apostolo Satanæ quidem traditus, 1. Cor. 5, 5. post pœnitentiam tamen remissionem delicti impetravit. 2. Cor. 2, 8.

Deindè opponenda sunt Scripturæ sacræ luculenta testimonia : quale est illud: Ezech. 18, 23. & cap. 33, 11. Vivo ego, dicit Dominus, Nolo mortem peccatoris, sed ut convertatur impius à viâ suâ mala, & vivat. Psal. 32, 6. pro peccatorum remissione orabit ad te omnis Sanctus. Ezech. 33, 12. Convertimini, Convertimini à vijs vestris pessimis, & quare moriemini domus Israel. Actor, 17, 30. Nunc annunciat DEUS omnibus ubiquè hominibus, ut pœnitentiam agant. 2. Petr. 3, 9. Non vult DEUS ullos perire, sed omnes ad pœnitentiam reverti.

Tertiò stupendam impietatem dogmatis Novatianorum arguunt hæ rationes.

I. Scopus Evangelij in eo unicè consistit, ut non semel tantùm ad fidem convertendis : sed indefinitè omnibus resipiscentibus, gratia & peccatorum remissio annuncietur.

II. Nisi pœnitentibus post lapsum fores gratiæ paterent, clavium usus in Ecclesiâ, prorsus esset nullus : siquidem non nisi lapsis & peccatoribus, destinata est à CHRISTO Absolutionis promissio & certitudo, secundum illud Johan, 20, 23. Quicunq́; remiseritis peccata in terris, remissa erunt in Cælis.

III. Indè sequeretur peccata lapsorum superare immensitatem gratiæ divinæ & meriti Christi.

IV. Quinta petitio Orationis Dominicæ planè exolesceret, & esset frustranea atquè irrita.

Cæterùm Novatiani errori isti suo palliando, duo potissimùm Scripturæ testimonia adhibebant : desumta ex cap. 6. versibus 4, 5. & 6. ut & ex cap. 10, 26. Epistolæ ad Hebræos. Illud sic habet : Impossibile est eos, qui semel sunt illuminati gustaveruntquè donum cæleste, & participes facti sunt Spiritus Sancti, gustaveruntquè nihilominùs bonum DEI verbum, virtutesque venturi seculi, & prolapsi sunt : rursum renovari ad pœnitentiam, crucifigentes sibimetipsis Filium DEI, & ostentui habentes. Hoc verò sic habet : Voluntariè peccantibus nobis post acceptam notitiam veritatis, jam non relinquitur pro peccatis hostia.

Sed rectissimè respondetur, turpem committi Sophisticationem ignorationis Elenchi & πλεονεξίας consequentis. Uterque enim locus non agit de peccatis quibusvis post ba-


### Opinion of the Libertines about Penance

baptism, but concerning a certain singular species of sin, which as it never falls under repentance, so it never obtains remission. Which sin is none other than that which the Savior names sin or κατ' ἐξοχὼ blasphemy against the Holy Spirit, which why it is and is called irremissible, and why it also never falls under repentance, we have shown in the Article concerning sin. Wrongly, therefore, is that which is most truly predicated of this singular species of sin: restricted to those sins which are committed by the baptized, either out of ignorance, or out of the infirmity of the flesh, or out of the dominion of concupiscence, against conscience.

2. Regarding the error of the Libertines, whom indeed our Author does not mention by name, it is certain that they, just as concerning sin, so also concerning repentance, have spread plainly horrendous errors. For just as they contended: That nothing is sin by its own nature, except only in the opinion of those who think they are sinning: and therefore that all things are lawful which one desires to perpetrate: so they also dreamed that the baptized or reborn cannot fall mortally: and although they fall against conscience, these nevertheless are, and will be saved, because the mercy of GOD is so great that salvation and eternal life are to come even to the devils themselves after the judgment.

To that fury there ought to be opposed in the beginning the examples of those who, once gifted with the Holy Spirit, pleased GOD: but afterwards fell into such atrocious crimes that some of them perished eternally: such as Saul, David, Judas Iscariot, Peter, and others.

Then indeed express testimonies evidently establish the same: such as, Ezek. 18:23 and ch. 33:11, where GOD twice testifies even under oath: that He does not desire the death of the sinner, but that he should turn and live.

Matt. 12:44 and 45. Luke 11:24 and 25. When the unclean spirit has gone out of a man, he walks through dry places, etc. Then he goes and takes seven other spirits, more wicked than himself, and entering they dwell there: and the last state of that man becomes worse than the first. 1 Cor. 10:12. Let him who stands take heed lest he fall. 2 Pet. 2:20, 21, 22. Rev. 2:5.

But very closely related to this fury is the error of the Sacramentarians asserting that the Elect and reborn cannot lose the Holy Spirit and faith, nor be damned, even if they perpetrate atrocious sins and crimes against conscience. Which indeed, that dogma standing, it follows of its own accord that there can be plainly no use for Repentance in the Church of the reborn and Elect.

And these two kinds of heretics our Author wished to touch upon: concerning whom let it suffice to have said these things: provided that this, as if ἐν παρόδῳ, be observed, that today those more recent Photinians throughout Transylvania and Poland are plainly recalling from the underworld the same error which was condemned several times in the Novatians by the Orthodox universal Church. They also contend that for sins committed voluntarily and by set purpose, no host or Sacrifice remains: and therefore that the merit of CHRIST, for expiating these sins, has no power or efficacy: but that only those sins are remitted to the penitent which were committed out of imprudence and the infirmity of the flesh: which are commonly accustomed to be named venial. Which doctrine indeed labors under the same impieties which we noted a little earlier in the heresy of the Novatians. Whence it can, and ought to be, refuted by the same arguments. To which, however, we add this one thing as if in the place of a conclusion, that the Photinians do not blush to lie boldly, that in the Old Testament no Sacrifice was ordained for voluntary sins. The contrary is indeed evident from even one sixth chapter of Leviticus, from verse 1 to the eighth: The soul that has sinned, and committed a transgression against the LORD, and has denied to his neighbor a deposit which had been entrusted to his faith: or has extorted something by force, or has defrauded his neighbor, or has found a lost thing, and denying it has sworn falsely, and has done any other of many things in which men are accustomed to sin, etc., he shall offer for his sin an unblemished ram from the flock, and shall give it to the Priest as a Sacrifice for his guilt: And the Priest shall reconcile him before the LORD, and it shall be forgiven him for each of the things which he did in sinning, etc. Whence I conclude thus irrefragably: If an expiatory sacrifice is given in the Old Testament for certain specific and expressly defined types of voluntary sin: then the opinion asserting the contrary is heretical.

But the former is true: For the text already cited defines hatred, avarice, evil deceit, perfidy, lying, perjury, etc., and for these it established an expiatory sacrifice. That all these sins are committed ἑκουσίως and voluntarily, hardly anyone will deny. Therefore.

And again: The judgment is the same concerning similar things. Therefore, if the primary types of voluntary sin easily had an expiatory sacrifice destined by GOD himself in the Old Testament: then the remaining lesser types of this sin must also be of the same condition, so that whoever is seriously sorry for having committed them may obtain forgiveness for them.

Now, that sacrifice of the Old Testament was a type of that one and most absolute sacrifice of CHRIST performed on the altar of the cross. Therefore, this will not be of narrower breadth or efficacy than that type was formerly: unless someone wishes to dream, through an unheard-of absurdity, that the shadow is more perfect than the body: which the Epistle to the Hebrews, chapter 10, 1, and elsewhere throughout, simply denies. But this question was discussed expressly in the Article on the justification of man before GOD.

ptismum commissis, sed de singulari quâdam peccati specie, quæ uti sub pœnitentiam nunquàm cadit, ita remissionem etiam nunquàm impetrat. Quod peccatum nullum est aliud præter id, quod Servator nominat peccatum sive κατ' ἐξοχὼ blasphemiam in Spiritum Sanctum, quæ cur sit & dicatur irremissibilis, quare etiam sub pœnitentiam nunquàm cadat, in Articulo de peccato ostendimus. Malè ergò id, quòd de singulari hac peccati specie verissimè prædicatur: ad ea adstringitur peccata, quæ vel ex ignorantiâ, vel ex carnis infirmitate, vel ex dominatu concupiscentiæ, contra conscientiam, à baptizatis designantur.

2. Quoad errorem Libertinorum, quos quidem Autor noster nominatim non exprimit, constat ipsos uti de peccato, sic etiam de pœnitentiâ, horrendos planè sparsisse errores. Quemadmodum enim contendebant: Nihil naturâ suâ peccatum esse, nisi tantùm eorum opinione, qui se peccare existiment: ac proindè omnia licere, quæ perpetrare libeat: ita somnia bant etiam, baptizatos sive renatos non posse labi mortaliter: & quamvis labantur contra conscientiam, istos tamen esse, & salvatum iri, proptereà quòd tanta sit DEI misericordia, ut Diabolis etiam ipsis salus & vita æterna post judicium sit obventura.

Furori isti opponi debent initiò exempla eorum, qui quõdam Spiritu Sancto donati, DEO placuerunt: postmodùm autem in atrociâ scelera ita sunt prolapsi, ut nonnulli ex illis æternùm perierint: ut Saul, David, Judas Ischariotes, Petrus & alij.

Deindè verò expressa testimonia idem evidenter astruunt: qualia sunt, Ezech. 18, 23. & cap. 33, 11. ubi bis DEUS etiam juratus testatur: se nolle mortem peccatoris, sed ut ille conversus vivat.

Matth. 12, 44. & 45. Luc. 11, 24. & 25. Cum immundus spiritus exierit ab homine, ambulat per loca arida &c. Tunc vadit, & assumit septem alios spiritus, nequiores se, & intrantes habitant ibi: & fiunt novissima hominis illius deteriora prioribus. 1. Cor. 10, 12. Qui stat videat ne cadat. 2. Petr. 2, 20. 21. 22. Apoc. 2, 5.

Perquàm autem cognatus furori isti est error Sacramentariorum asserẽtium, Electos & renatos non posse Spiritum Sanctum amittere & fidem, nec damnari, etiam si atrocia peccata & facinorâ contra conscientiam perpetrent. Quod sanè stante dogmate, ultrò consequitur, Pœnitentiæ in Ecclesiâ renatorum & Electorum, usum planè nullum esse posse.

Et duo quidem hæc hæreticorum genera noster Autor perstringere voluit: de quibus isthæc dixisse sufficiat: modò illud, quasi ἐν παρόδῳ observetur, hodiè recentiores illos per Transylvaniam & Poloniam Photinianos, eundem planè errorem ab inferis quasi revocare, qui in Novatianis ab Orthodoxâ universali Ecclesiâ aliquoties damnatus fuit. Contendunt a- & isti, pro peccatis sponte ac destinato consilio designatis, nullam superesse hostiam sive Sacrificium: ac proindè CHRISTI meritum, pro his expiandis peccatis, nullam habere vim aut efficaciam: sed ea tantùm peccata pœnitentibus remitti, quæ ex imprudentiâ & infirmitate carnis sunt commissa: quæ vulgò venialia nominari consueverunt. Quæ sanè doctrina ijsdem impietatibus laborat, quas in Novatianorum hæresi paulò antè notavimus. Undè ijsdem etiam argumentis refutari potest, & debet. Quibus unum tamen illud coronidis quasi loco addimus, quod Photiniani audacter mentiri non erubescunt, in Veteri Testamento nullum pro peccatis voluntarijs ordinatum fuisse Sacrificium. Contrarium profectò patet vel ex uno capite sexto Levitici, à versu 1. ad octavum usque: Anima quæ peccaverit, & transgressionem commiserit contra DOMINUM, & negaverit proximo, suo depositum, quod fidei ejus creditum fuerat: vel vi aliquid extorserit, aut defraudaverit proximum suum, sive rem perditam invenerit, & inficians insuper pejeraverit, & quidvis aliud ex pluribus fecerit, in quibus solent peccare homines &c pro peccato offeret arietem immaculatum de grege, & dabit eum Sacerdoti in Sacrificium pro delicto: Reconciliabitque eum Sacerdos Domino, & dimittetur illi pro singulis, quæ faciendo peccavit &c. Undè irrefragabiliter sic colligo: Si datur in Veteri Testamento Sacrificium expiatorium pro certis quibusdam, ac expressè definitis peccati voluntarij speciebus: utiquè hæretica est sententia diversum asserens.

Atqui prius illud verum: Nam textus jam citatus definit odium, avaritiam, dolum malum, perfidiam, mendacium, perjurium &c. & pro his Sacrificium expiatorium constituit. Quæ omnia peccata ἑκουσίως & voluntariè committi, vix quisquam inficiabitur. Ergò.

Et Rursus: De similibus idem est judicium. Ergò si species facilè primariæ peccati voluntarij, in Veteri Testamento, habuerunt Sacrificium expiatorium à DEO ipso destinatum: utique reliquæ etiam inferiores hujus peccati species, ejusdem conditionis sint oportet, ut qui de illis commissis seriò doleat, veniam eorum consequatur.

Jam verò Sacrificium illud Veteris Testamenti typus erat, ad unicum illud & absolutifsimum Sacrificium CHRISTI in arâ crucis peractum. Non igitur angustioris hoc erit, vel latitudinis vel efficaciæ, quàm fuit olim illud typum: nisi per inauditam absurditatem quis somniare velit, umbram perfectiorem esse corpore: id quod epistola ad Hebræos cap. 10, 1. & passim alibi, simpliciter negat. Verùm de hâc quæstione ex professo disputatum fuit, in Articulo de Justificatione hominis coram DEO.


### Opinion of the Libertines about Penance: On the Definition of Penitence

IF every true definition can then at last be rightly explained, when the ambiguity of the thing defined is first accurately unfolded: certainly the same method should be observed concerning the definition of repentance. For the word repentance, when it is predicated of men, contains a great breadth of meaning, as Scripture itself asserts.

For first, in a general and very broad sense, it denotes a change of counsel and purpose, even if only an apparent one, such as also falls to impious and unfaithful men.

Next, this word is sometimes taken for the sign of repentance, as when in the ancient Church, those who were undergoing the public censure of ecclesiastical discipline were said to do penance.

Thirdly: it is used for the effect and benefits following repentance: as when Esau, Heb. 12:17, is read not to have found a place for repentance, that is, to have felt no fruit of it, especially that which he sought, namely, the restoration of the birthright.

Fourthly: it more often signifies only the sorrow of mind conceived concerning sins, and is taken synecdochically for the other part of repentance, namely, contrition: as Mark 1:15, Repent, and believe the Gospel. Luke 24:47, It behooves that repentance and remission of sins be preached in his name. Acts 20:21, Paul testified to the Gentiles repentance and faith in Christ Jesus.

Finally, it is for the most part used in the sacred writings for the whole conversion to GOD: Matt. 3:2, Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has approached, and verse 8, Bring forth fruits worthy of repentance, Matt. 9:13, I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance, etc. In this article, our discourse is concerning the last or fifth species of meaning. For although the etymology and emphasis of this word is too narrow to express the entire nature and affection of true repentance: yet because it is received by the common usage of the Church: and the Latin Bibles use this term: we also shall use it in the present disputation, attributing more in this part to the necessity of the subject than to elegance or Latinity.

Moreover, Bellarmine clearly wastes his effort and oil, lib. 1 de Pœnit. cap. 7, arguing prolixly and anxiously that the word repentance draws its origin from punishment (pœna). For we ourselves readily grant this: but what the Esauite sophistically hides under this derivation, that we utterly deny. For it does not immediately follow that repentance is named from that species of punishments which it behooves a priest to impose upon penitents: since there are also other species of punishments which concur around the serious act of repentance, and yet are not meritorious. For first, generally in those things of which we are sorry and repent, there is a certain notion of punishment, so called in a broad sense: but then, the punishment is far more grievous which the conscience, terrified and prostrated by the thunderbolt of the law, and by the recognition of sin and the consideration of divine wrath, feels and suffers: so that there is no need for those punishments imposed by the priestling, nor for those assumed by us voluntarily. Nor does anything redound to the cause of the Esauite from the Hebrew word שׁוּבָה or תְּשׁוּבָה. For whether you look at its root שׁוּב, or the context of the sacred texts, it certainly never involves any respect to those canonical punishments about which the Esauite prattles: but it obtains the force and meaning of returning or reverting: and it corresponds most closely to the word conversion, which we are otherwise accustomed to use in this place. For just as by sinning a certain aversion from GOD occurs: so by repenting a return and conversion to the LORD occurs: just as Scripture itself speaks. Jer. 18:11, Ezek. 18:30, and a very elegant type of this matter is proposed in the return of the prodigal son to the affectionate father, Luke 15. Therefore it is a prodigious rashness that Bellarmine, in the place already cited, dares to write that the Hebrew שׁוּב by reason of its origin and derivation denotes external sorrow and punishment proceeding from internal conversion: and that therefore the Latin interpreter did better to use the word Penance than he would have done if he had wished to use the word Repentance.

A more accurate consideration of the Greek text ought deservedly to have restrained this petulance: which indeed expresses penance by three words, μετανοίας, μεταμελείας, ἐπιστρέψεως: but none of which points a finger to that penal satisfaction which the Esauite implies.

For μετάνοια, as to its etymology, is derived from subsequent thoughts, which by the Greek proverb are always wiser, and it denotes the same as to be wise only after the fact, to think otherwise, to correct an error, and to repent. Whence most interpreters render μετάνοιαν as Repentance.

Μεταμέλεια, from the verb μεταμέλεσθαι, denotes the same as any displeasure whatsoever that is conceived from the fact that something has been done: and it is attributed not only to those who truly repent, Matt. 21:29 and 32, but also to hypocrites and the impious: as to Judas the traitor, Matt. 27:3, and therefore it more often designates at least the beginning of repentance, or certainly an imperfect repentance.

Ἐπίστρεψις or Ἐπιστροφὴ signifies conversion or reversion, and corresponds most closely to the Hebrew word, denoting an aversion from evil and a conversion to good.

These things having been thus premised, it will have to be investigated how Holy Scripture defines Penance. For it is not true, as Bellarmine keeps writing, that the nature and essence of true penance is to be sought from the grammatical derivation and origin of the Latin word. For first, the Latin version is not authentic: and although the use of the word penance holds a place in the Church by right of prescription, it can in no way, nor ought it to, prejudice the truth of the thing itself which is being discussed. Then, Scripture does not restrict the nature and essence of true penance to those undue works

Latin:

SI omnis vera Definitio tùm demùm ritè expediri potest, cùm æquivocatio definiti priùs accuratè evolvitur: certè circa definitionem Pœnitentiæ eadem observanda fuerit methodus. Vocabulo enim Pœnitentiæ, ubi de hominibus prædicatur, magna inest significandi latitudo, sic ipsâ asserente Scripturâ.

Primùm enim in genere & latissimè quamvis consilij & propositi mutationem, etiam saltem apparentem notat, qualis quoque cadit in homines impios & infideles.

Deindè accipitur vox hæc interdum pro signo pœnitentiæ, ut quando in veteri Ecclesiâ, illi qui disciplinæ Ecclesiasticæ censuram publicam sustinebant, dicebantur agere pœnitentiam.

Tertiò: pro effectu & commodis pœnitentiam consequentibus usurpatur: ut cum Esavvus Hebr. 12, 17. legitur non invenisse locum pœnitentiæ, hoc est, fructum ejus nullum sensisse, eum præcipuè, quem expetebat, Primogenituræ scilicet restitutionem.

Quartò: Solum sæpiùs animi dolorem de peccatis conceptum significat, & pro alterâ pœnitentiæ parte, Contritione scilicet συνεκδοχικῶς accipitur: ut Marci 1, 15. Pœnitentiam agite, & credite Evangelio. Luc. 24, 47. Oportet in nomine ejus prædicari pœnitentiam & remissionem peccatorum. Actor. 20, 21. Paulus testificabatur gentilibus pœnitentiam & fidem in Christum Jesum.

Tandem, pro totâ ad DEUM conversione in sacris ut plurimùm ponitur: Matth. 3, 2. Pœnitentiam agite, appropinquavit enim regnum cælorum, & versu 8. Facite fructus dignos pœnitentiæ, Matth. 9, 13. Non veni vocare justos, sed peccatores ad pœnitentiam &c. Nobis hoc in Articulo sermo est de ultimâ sive quintæ significationis specie. Etsi enim etymon ac emphasis vocabuli hujus angustior est, quàm ut integram naturam & affectionem veræ pœnitentiæ exprimat: quia tamen usu Ecclesiæ vulgato est recepta: & Biblia Latina hoc termino utuntur: nos quoque in præsenti disputatione eo utemur, plus hac in parte rerum necessitati, quàm elegantiæ aut latinitati tribuentes.

Cæterùm Bellarminus operam planè atque oleum perdit, lib. 1. de Pœnit. cap. 7. prolixè & anxiè disputans, Pœnitentiæ vocabulum suam trahere originem à pœnâ. Nam nos ipsi ultrò hoc largimur: verùm quod sophisticè sub hâc derivatione occultat Esavvita, id verò pernegamus. Neque enim consequens statim est, Pœnitentiam dici ab eâ pœnarum specie, quas Sacerdos pœnitentibus imponere deceat: siquidem dantur etiam aliæ pœnarum species, quæ circa serium pœnitentiæ actum concurrunt, neque tamen sunt meritoriæ. Nam primùm generaliter in his, quorum nos piget ac pœnitet, inest quædam pœnæ ratio, ἐκ πλάτει sic dictæ: Deindè verò pœna longè gravissima est, quam conscientia legis fulmine territa & prostrata, & peccati agnitione & iræ divinæ consideratione, sentit & patitur: ita ut neque impositis illis à Sacrificulo, neque à nobis ultrò assumtis pœnis sit opus. Neque ad causam Esavvitæ præsidij aliquid redundat ex vocabulo Hebræo שׁוּבָה vel תְּשׁוּבָה. Nam sive radicem ejus שׁוּב, sive textuum sacrorum συνέπειαν spectes, certè nunquàm illud respectum aliquem involvit ad pœnas illas canonicas, de quibus garrit Esavvita: sed redeundi sive revertendi vim significationemque obtinet: ac conversionis vocabulo, quo aliàs hoc loco uti solemus, quàm proximè respondet. Nam quemadmodum peccando quædam fit à DEO aversio: ita resipiscendo reditus & conversio fit ad DOMINUM: sicut Scriptura ipsa loquitur. Jerem. 18, 11. Ezech. 18, 30. & hujus rei typus perelegans, in reversione filij acolasti ad partem Φιλόστοργον proponitur, Luc. 15. Ergò prodigiosa temeritas est, quod Bellarminus loco jam citato scribere audet, Hebræum שׁוּב ratione originis ac derivationis notare externum dolorem, ac pœnam ex internâ Conversione profectam: ac idcircò latinum Interpretem melius voce Pœnitentiæ usum esse, quam fecisset, si voce Resipiscentiæ uti voluisset.

Quam petulantiam coërcere meritò debuisset, textus Græci accuratior consideratio: qui tribus quidem Vocabulis μετανοίας, μεταμελείας, ἐπιστρέψεως, pœnitentiam exprimit: sed quorum nullum ad illam, quam Esavvita innuit, pœnalem satisfactionem digitum intendit.

Nam μετάνοια, quoad ἔτυμον, à posterioribus cogitationibus, quæ Græcorum adagio semper sunt σοφώτεραι, deducitur: & idem notat, ac post factum demum sapere, aliter cogitare, corrigere errorem, ac resipiscere. Undè plerique interpretes reddunt μετάνοιαν per Resipiscentiam.

Μεταμέλεια à verbo μεταμέλεσθαι, idem notat ac displicentiam quamcunque, quæ concipitur ex eo, quod factum est: ac tribuitur non modò ijs, qui verè pœnitent. Matth. 21, 29. & 32. sed etiam hypocritis ac impijs: ut Judæ proditori Matth. 27, 3. ac proindè sæpiùs initium saltem pœnitentiæ, vel certè imperfectam pœnitentiam designat.

Ἐπίστρεψις sive Ἐπιστροφὴ conversionem sive reversionem significat, & vocabulo Hebræo quàm proximè respondet, notans aversionem à malo, & conversionem ad bonum.

His ita præmissis, quomodo Scriptura Sacra Pœnitentiam definiat, investigandum fuerit. Neque enim verum est, quod Bellarminus scriptitat, veræ pœnitentiæ naturam atquè essentiam, ex vocabuli Latini Grammaticâ derivatione atq́; origine petendam esse. Nam primùm Latina versio non est authentica: & licet usus Vocabuli pœnitentiæ, Jure præscriptionis in Ecclesiâ locu obtineat: ipsius tamen rei, de quâ agitur veritati præjudicare nullo modo vel potest, vel debet. Deindè Scriptura, naturam & essentiam veræ pœnitentiæ, non restringit ad opera illa indebita


### Opinion of the Libertines about Penance: Causes & instrumentalities of penitence

& penal [things], which the Romanists invent: but by such phrases he circumlocutes Penance, so that if the question is about the nature of penance, one should not have recourse to the derivation of the Latin word: but rather this should be considered, how the Holy Spirit defines it. Now indeed for the Holy Spirit to do penance, in the Scriptures is the same as

1. To turn aside from evil, & to do good. Ps. 36. 27.

2. To turn oneself from one's impiety. Ezek. 18, 27.

3. To turn oneself from one's ways, & one's malice. Ezek. 18, 22. Acts 3, 26.

4. To return from one's evil & most wicked way: 1 Kings 13, 33. Jer. 18, 11. Hos. 3, 5.

5. To be converted to GOD, Ezek. 18, 31. Acts 14, 14. 2 Cor. 3, 16. 1 Pet. 2, 25.

6. To seek the LORD. Deut. 4, 28. Hos. 3, 5.

7. To be sorrowful according to GOD 2 Cor. 7, 9.

8. To do penance & to believe the Gospel: Mark 1, 15. Acts 20, 21.

With these sayings of Scripture well observed, it will be easy to judge the definition of Bellarmine, which is as follows: Penance is a penal action, by which someone with both mind and body turns away from past sins, and exacts vengeance for them from himself.

Which definition indeed agrees neither with the Holy Scriptures, nor sufficiently with itself. For it does not contain in itself those things which we have already shown are required of penitents in the Scriptures, and therefore, it expresses neither the essence of the matter about which the inquiry is made, nor the causes, nor the parts of either true or false repentance: nor does it express its own πάθη according to the scriptures: but it clings only to the external bark: that is, it shows how a penitent ought to take vengeance upon himself, so that his repentance may strike the eyes: which, however, constitutes neither the genus nor the specific difference of true and saving repentance: but is only a perpetual adjunct of hypocritical repentance, which is sorrow according to the world, and begets damnation.

We, therefore, following the footsteps of the Scriptures, define repentance as a movement of the heart, kindled by the Holy Spirit through the ministry of the Law and the Gospel, by which a man, seriously grieving over sins committed, embraces with true faith the promises concerning the free remission of sins on account of Christ, and applies them to himself, in order to please GOD more henceforth, through the pursuit of New Obedience, in his life and conduct.

This is a causal definition, sufficiently describing the causes, parts, and effects of true repentance.

For the efficient cause is established as GOD the Holy Spirit alone: Jerem. 31, 18. Turn me, O Lord, and I shall be turned. Lam. 5, 21. Turn us, O Lord, unto thee, and we shall be turned. Ezek. 36, 26. I, says GOD, will give you a new heart, and a new spirit will I put within you. Ps. 51, 12. Create in me a clean heart, O GOD: and renew a right spirit within me. 2 Tim. 2, 25. God gives repentance to the acknowledging of the truth.

The instrumental cause is expressed as the Law and the Gospel. For these two kinds of doctrine concur for saving repentance, according to the two diverse parts of repentance, Contrition and Faith: so that the former proceeds from the Law, the latter from the Gospel alone: as will be demonstrated in chapter 2.

The parts of repentance are established as those which we have already named, Contrition and Faith.

The principal effect, the Remission of Sins: The less principal, and as it were a consequence of the former effect, is New obedience, or the renewal and sanctification of life and conduct.

With this purer definition of Penance standing, the first principal state of the controversy emerges, which is today most especially disputable between us and the Esavvites: Namely, whether Penance ought to be defined by a Sacrament properly so called? Where we hold and defend the negative: but the Esavvites strive to maintain the affirmative. Furthermore, so that this state of the controversy, and the whole dispute depending therefrom, may be clearer, it will be necessary to inquire a little more accurately in this place into the Esavvitic doctrine.

Therefore, at the beginning they distinguish between two species of Penance: one of which they say is a virtue: the other, however, a Sacrament: the former they name internal, the latter, however, external penance.

Then they contend that only that penance is a Sacrament properly so called, which is in the New Testament, and is performed after Baptism has been received.

Finally, they add this limitation, that not even after Baptism is every penance a Sacrament: but only that which is manifested by external signs, with the word of Absolution added: that is, which consists of sacramental Matter and Form: where Bellarmine argues that the act of the one confessing is the matter: but the act of the one absolving, and saying, I absolve thee etc., is the Form of this Sacrament. Whence this state of the controversy, as it were limited, emerges: Whether Penance manifested by external signs, with the word of Absolution added to it, is a Sacrament of the New Testament properly so called? Which very state Bellarmine also posits, lib. 1. de Pœnit. cap. 8. And he fights strenuously for the Affirmative: but in such a way that he not only does not prove what is in controversy, and is denied by us: but rather proves a plainly absurd Theology, which is nothing else than an opinion, and as it were a certain sink of most absurd errors, impinging most shamefully not only upon the analogy of faith, but also upon sound reason.

THE FIRST, and that a most gross error, is that they define Penance, insofar as it consists of and is completed by the internal conversion of the mind and the detestation of sin, by a virtue. For 1. virtues are habits either acquired, such as those Ethical ones, of which the Philosophers speak: or 2. they are infused, such as those Theological ones: Hope, Faith, Charity. But indeed Penance or the conversion of a sinful man to GOD is not an acquired habit of the mind: for thus Penance could be obtained by use and long-standing custom: which is false: and fights diametrically against the Scriptures. For it is GOD alone who gives repentance, 2 Tim. 2:25, Acts 2:37, who takes away the stony heart

Latin:

& pœnalia, quæ fingunt Romanenses : sed ejusmodi phrasibus Pœnitentiam circumloquitur, ut si de naturâ pœnitentiæ sit quæstio, non ad derivationem vocis latinæ sit recurrendum: sed id potiùs pensi habendum, quomodo Spiritus Sanctus eam definiat. Jam verò Spiritui Sancto pœnitentiam agere, in Scripturis idem est, ac

1. Declinare à malo, & facere bonum. Psal. 36. 27.

2. Avertere se ab impietate suâ. Ezech. 18, 27.

3. Convertere se à viis suis, & malitiâ suâ. Ezech. 18, 22. Actor. 3, 26.

4. Reverti à viâ suâ malâ & pessimâ : 1. Reg. 13, 33. Jerem. 18, 11. Hos. 3, 5.

5. Converti ad DEUM, Ezech. 18, 31. Actor. 14. 14. 2. Cor. 3, 16. 1. Petr. 2, 25.

6. Quærere DOMINUM. Deut. 4, 28. Hos. 3, 5.

7. Contristari secundum DEUM 2. Cor. 7, 9.

8. Pœnitentiam agere & credere Evangelio : Marci 1, 15. Actor. 20, 21.

His Scripturæ dictis probè observatis, facilè erit judicium de definitione Bellarmini, quæ sic habet : Pœnitentia est actio pœnalis, quâ quis animo simul & corpore peccata præterita aversatur, & vindictam de illis à semetipso exigit.

Quæ sanè definitio neque cum Scripturis Sacris, neque secum ipsa satis congruit. Nam ea in se non continet, quæ à Pœnitentibus in Scripturis requiri, jam ostendimus, ac proindè, neque rei, de quâ quæritur, essentiam, neque causas neque partes vel veræ vel falsæ pœnitentiæ: neque propria ejusdem πάθη secundum scripturas exprimit : sed in cortice externo tantùm hæret : hoc est, ostendit, quomodo pœnitens vindictam de se sumere debeat, ut ipsius pœnitentia incurrat in oculos : id quod tamen neque genus, neque differentiam specificam veræ & salutaris pœnitentiæ constituit: sed perpetuum tantùm est adjunctum hypocriticæ pœnitentiæ, quæ est tristitia secundum mundum, & damnationem gignit.

Nos ergò secuti vestigia Scripturarum, definimus pœnitentiam, quod sit motus cordis, accensus à Spiritu Sancto per ministerium legis & Evangelij, quo homo seriò dolens de peccatis admissis, verâ fide promissiones de gratuitâ peccatorũ propter Christum remissione amplectitur, sibiquè applicat, ad probandum deinceps DEO magis, per Novæ Obedientiæ studium, vitam atquè mores suos.

Est Definitio hæc causalis veræ pœnitentiæ causas, partes, effecta, sufficienter describens.

Causa enim efficiens constituitur solus DEUS Spiritus Sanctus : Jerem. 31, 18. Converte me Domine, & convertar. Thren. 5, 21. Converte nos Domine ad te, & convertemur. Ezech. 36, 26. Ego, inquit DEUS, dabo vobis cor novum, & Spiritum novum ponam in medio vestri. Psal. 51, 12. Cor mundum crea in me DEUS: & Spiritum innova in visceribus meis. 2. Tim. 2, 25. Deus dat pœnitentiam in agnitionem veritatis.

Causa instrumentalis exprimitur Lex & Evangelium. Concurrunt enim duo hæc doctrinarum genera ad salutarem pœnitentiam, fecundum duas diversas pœnitentiæ partes, Contritionem & Fidem: ita ut illa ex Lege, hæc ex Evangelio tantùm proficiscatur: uti capite 2. demonstrabitur.

Partes pœnitentiæ constituuntur eæ, quas jam nominavimus, Contritio & Fides.

Effectus principalis, Remissio Peccatorum: Minus principalis, & ceu consequens prioris effectus est Nova obedientia, sive vitæ morúmque renovatio ac sanctificatio.

Stante puriore hac definitione Pœnitentiæ, emergit status controversiæ principalis primus, inter nos & Esavvitas hodiè vel maximè disputabilis: An nimirùm Pœnitentia definiri debeat per Sacramentum propriè sic dictum? Ubi nos negativam tenemus ac defendimus: Esavvitæ verò affirmativam tueri student. Cæterùm ut status iste controversiæ, totaque, indè dependens disputatio sit dilucidior, paulò accuratiùs hoc loco in doctrinam Esavviticam inquirendum fuerit.

Initiò igitur distinguunt inter duas Pœnitentiæ species: quarum unam dicunt esse virtutem: alteram verò Sacramentum: illam nominant internam, hanc verò externam pœnitentiam.

Deindè contendunt, Eam tantùm pœnitentiam esse Sacramentum propriè sic dictum, quæ est in Novo Testamento, & agitur post perceptum Baptismum.

Tandem limitationem hanc adjiciunt, ne quidem post Baptismum, omnem pœnitentiam esse Sacramentum: sed eam tantùm, quæ externis signis manifestetur, accedente verbo Absolutionis: hoc est, quæ constet Materiâ & Formâ Sacramentali: ubi Bellarminus disputat, actum Confitentis esse materiam: actum verò absolventis, & dicentis, Ego te absolvo &c. esse Formam hujus Sacramenti. Undè status controversiæ quasi limitatus emergit iste: An Pœnitentia signis externis manifestata, accedente ad eam verbo Absolutionis, sit Sacramentum Novi Testamenti propriè sic dictum? Quem ipsum statum ponit etiam Bellarminus, lib. 1. de Pœnit. cap. 8. Et pro Affirmatâ strenuè pugnat: sed ita ut non modò non probet, quod in controversiâ est, & à nobis negatur: verùm potiùs absurdam planè Theologiam probat, quæ nihil est aliud, quam sententia, & quasi colluvies quædam absurdissimorum errorum, non in fidei modò analogiam, sed & in sanam rationem turpissimè impingentium.

PRIMUS, isq; crassissimus error est, quòd Pœnitentiam quatenùs internâ mentis conversione, peccatiq; detestatione constat & absolvitur, definiunt per virtutem. Nam 1. virtutes sunt habitus vel acquisiti, quales sunt illæ Ethicæ, de quibus Philosophi: vel 2. sunt infusi, quales sunt illæ Theologicæ: Spes, Fides, Charitas. At verò Pœnitentia sive conversio hominis peccatoris ad DEUM, non est habitus animi acquisitus: sic enim usu & affuetudine diuturnâ Pœnitentia coparari posset: id quod falsum: & cum Scripturis è diametro pugnat. Solus n. DEUS est, qui dat pœnitentiã, 2. Tim. 2, 25. Act. 2, 37. qui aufert cor la-


### Opinion of the Libertines about Penance: Whether Penitence is a Sacrament

from our flesh, and gives a heart of flesh, Ezek. 36. 26. Thus it is not an infused habit of the mind. For although the Holy Spirit moves the heart of man to acknowledge sins: yet this very acknowledgment of sins does not proceed from inherent qualities of the will: but from the Law of GOD, Rom. 3, 20. Rom. 7, 7. Thus, and indeed much less with respect to Faith, as that which is a gift of GOD, Repentance is an infused habit of virtue: Since Faith, as in the Article of Justification, so in the present also, is not considered as a virtue or quality inherent subjectively: but only as a medium or organ apprehending the merit of CHRIST. What? That New obedience, or Sanctification or renewal of our mind, which we would perhaps not deny could be defined by some quality infused by GOD, is not a part constituting true repentance: but only its effect or consequent. The Scholastics themselves also noticed the vanity of this Papal assertion, and therefore, in order to weaken the force of our arguments in any way, they foolishly feigned that Repentance is a quiescent virtue, and one that only occasionally exerts itself. Which quiescence, indeed, although it is not denied regarding the secondary act of moral virtues: since that is very often interrupted, as the Philosopher truly wrote: At the time when we sleep, although we are happy, we do not differ from the miserable: yet by no means can or should this quiescence be applied to repentance. For those who have fallen and are to be converted to GOD are so far from being able to perform repentance from some habit of virtue, whether quiescent or energetic, whether they sleep or wake, that unless they are moved by the Spirit of GOD, such an act of repenting could never fall upon them: which cannot be affirmed of the habits of virtues, whose act, according to right reason, exerts itself freely, as much in the unregenerate as in the regenerate. What of the fact that even that perpetual repentance of the regenerate, or mortification of the flesh, proceeds from the singular grace of the Holy Spirit, according to that John 15, 5. Without me you can do nothing: And it does not admit such quiescence: since, as the Apostle testifies 2 Cor. 3, 18. The regenerate are transformed into the image of Christ, from glory to glory. And lest anyone think this happens from a habit of a quiescent Virtue, which only occasionally exerts itself, it is soon added: But by the Spirit of the LORD.

And indeed such is the force of truth, that both the Scholastics and more recent Papal writers do not even agree among themselves how the virtue of repentance ought to be defined. Thomas in 4. sent dist. 14. q. 1. reports that some establish that Repentance is not a Special Virtue, differing from other habits of Virtues: but is contained under all of them, insofar as indeed every virtue detests the vice opposed to it. But Thomas, dissenting from these, contends that Repentance is a Virtue in the will, as in a subject, part 3. q. 84. art. 4. and that it is divinely infused, art. 5. & 6. To whom, however, Scotus again contradicts, in 4. Sent. dist. 14. q. 3. & Durandus in the same dist. q. 2. who contends that Repentance is the very moral commutative justice itself. Cajetan art. 2. lib 4. sent. dist. 14. says that Repentance is Religion itself, finally Scotus in 4. Sent. dist. 14 q. 2. establishes four acts of this virtue: 1. to will to punish sin. 2. to be unwilling to have sinned. 3. to will to accept punishment for sin. 4. to bear the punishment received patiently. Which, indeed, the blindness of these blind gladiators clearly argues the futility of this dogma.

ANOTHER error of the Esauite race is clearly intolerable, that it invents one definition of repentance for the Old Testament, and another for the New; nay, and of the New Testament, one before Baptism is received: and another after Baptism. Which distinction, indeed, 1. cannot be demonstrated by even a single point from the Scriptures. 2. It is diametrically opposed to the Scriptures and the analogy of faith: for they expressly testify that the Repentance of both Testaments consists of the same matter, and the same form, namely Contrition and Faith: By the example of David, who, shuddering with his whole heart at the legal sermon of the Prophet Nathan because of the adultery and homicide committed, saying, I have sinned; he soon hears the joyful voice of absolution, The Lord has taken away your sin, you shall not die. 2. Sam. 12, 13. And the Esauite lies splendidly, asserting that in the Old Testament there was no power to remit sins with authority: nor that Nathan, or any other as a minister of GOD, absolved sinners, because that had not yet been heard: Whose sins you remit, they are remitted to them. lib. de Pœnit. cap. 11. For not even in the New Testament has any judicial power over the fallen or penitents been committed anywhere to the ministers of the Church, such as Bellarmine tacitly implies in this place, as if it were proper to the New Testament. But just as in the Old Testament the Priests were bound to the law and to the testimony, or the Gospel: to argue sins from the former: but from the latter they were commanded to heal the contrite: so today also in the New Testament no more power or authority regarding Absolution has been granted to ministers. Nor does it stand in the way that that had not yet been heard: Whose sins you remit, they are remitted to them. For no new method or form of Absolution was being promulgated by these words: But this was only a public and solemn commendation of the Ecclesiastical Ministry: and at the same time, according to the nature of the New Testament, a clearer explanation of the Evangelical doctrine, which in the Old Testament was wrapped in types and shadows: and its propagation to the whole world, which was previously enclosed within the narrow borders of the Jewish people. Nor is that other evasion of Bellarmine worth a single farthing, asserting that the example of the prophet Nathan has nothing to do with the matter, because Nathan did not say, I absolve you: or, I remit your sins to you: but only: The Lord has taken away your sin from you. Ibid. For where, I ask, did Christ the Savior prescribe this formula to the ministers of the New Testament? or where did he ever bind them to it? or where they attribute to this formula a certain fixed force or occult power, or even that judicial one, which he dreams of

The Esauvite has never anywhere ascribed this. These things are emptier than Sicilian trifles, and they argue too manifestly for the morbid theology of the Esauvites in this respect. There is one thing which we approve of most of all in this whole disputation, namely that the Esauvite expressly confesses in the same chapter: That the penance which Christ and John the Baptist preached was not a sacrament, and that an example of a sacramental penance is not found in the Scriptures before the resurrection of Christ. Let this assertion suffice for us as a foundation for the truth of our doctrine: indeed, let the penance shown by John the Baptist and Christ the Savior suffice for us; but let that which has not Christ, not the Apostles, but the son of perdition, the Roman Antichrist, as its author, be gone.

THE THIRD error is that the Esauvites contend that penance, which consists of external signs, that is, contrition of heart, confession of mouth, and satisfaction of work, and which has annexed to it the voice of absolution under this form: I absolve you, etc., is a sacrament of the New Testament properly so called. It is teeming with more falsities and absurdities than can all be enumerated. For 1. The definition of a sacrament does not fit penance. Therefore. The antecedent is clear: 1. because that rite which is required by the Romanists in penance was not instituted by Christ himself: a fact which Bellarmine himself confesses, book 2, on the Effect of the Sacrament, chapter 24. Now, however, true sacraments must have been instituted by Christ alone. 2. Because penance is a rite common to the Old Testament with the New. 3. Because it is destitute of an external element, or earthly thing. For Bellarmine is absurd, who dares to substitute the act of the one confessing for an external element: this is diametrically opposed to the nature and analogy of all the sacraments of both Testaments, none of which can exist where the action of a man constitutes an elementary part of the sacrament; but this must always be something subsisting outside the action of man. Thus Bellarmine is absurd, who writes: that the rite of the priest saying, I absolve you, concurs in the constitution of this sacrament: as if indeed the words of the minister constituted an essential part of the sacrament. If such a truly absurd theology were to stand, then the words of the minister saying, I baptize you, would have to be held as the external element: which is prodigiously absurd. II. Through the sacraments GOD deals with us; and He does this when a human action has an analogous likeness. But such an action is not penance; rather, it is a human action by which the main dealing is from man toward GOD: Therefore. III. All sacraments are so constituted that they can indeed be received whole without faith, but they are not salutary. But penance cannot stand without faith to such a degree that, in its absence, it is no longer penance, no more than a man can exist without a soul. Therefore. IV. Every sacrament properly so called consists of an earthly thing and a heavenly thing, sacramentally united. But penance does not consist of an earthly thing and a heavenly thing sacramentally united. Therefore. The assumption is clear: 1. even if the act of the one confessing is held to be the matter and earthly thing in the Esauvite sense (which is, however, false), yet no heavenly thing can be given which is sacramentally united with this earthly one.
