Eph. 2, 4. DEUS, qui dives est in misericordiâ, propter abundantem charitatem suam, quâ dilexit nos, & cùm essemus mortui peccatis, convivicavit nos in Christo. Coloss. 1, 19. & 20. Complacuit DEO Patri per Filium reconciliare omnia in ipsum, pacificans per sangvinem crucis ejus, & quæ in terris & quæ in cœlis sunt. 1. Tim. 2, 4. DEUS vult omnes homines salvos fieri, & ad agnitionem Veritatis pervenire. 2. Petr. 3, 9. DEUS non vult ullos perire, sed omnes ad pœnitentiam reverti.


### II. Member of the Antecedent Will in God. Redemption of the whole human race

We have just shown that the decree concerning sending the Son, and through him redeeming the human race, was of the immense mercy of GOD toward the fallen human race. Now, however, whatever the merciful GOD decreed from eternity in this part: that the Son in the fullness of time performed in effect, through his obedience and death, with the restoration or Redemption for the salvation of the whole world most fully accomplished. Where at the beginning shines forth that admirable temperament of divine justice and mercy. Justice, indeed, in that there was no place for the Redemption of the human race until CHRIST had sustained the punishments due to our sins: Mercy, however, in that through this very Satisfaction of the Son, GOD the Father reconciled the human race to himself, and received it into favor, 2 Cor. 9. Whence Augustine aptly says: God, he says, neither loses the severity of judgment in the goodness of mercy, nor in judging with severity does he lose the goodness of mercy: in Psalm 100. On this very stupendous tempering, the Apostle discourses expressly, Rom. 3, 24. & 25. Being justified freely by his grace, through the redemption that is in CHRIST JESUS, whom GOD hath proposed to be a propitiation, through faith in his blood, to the shewing of his justice, for the remission of former sins, through the forbearance of GOD, for the shewing of his justice in this time, that he himself may be just, and the justifier of him, who is of the faith of JESUS CHRIST.

Concerning this foundation of our salvation, the Oracles of the Scriptures testify: Isa. 53, 6. The Lord hath laid upon him (the Son) the iniquities of ALL of us: of all those who like sheep have gone astray: where it is clearer than to need proof that the inclusion of the whole human race is noted.

John 1, 29. Behold the Lamb of GOD, who takes away the sins of the world. John 3, 17. That the world may be saved by him. John 12, 47. I came that I might save the world.

John 6:51. I will give my flesh for the life of the world. Luke 2:10 & 11. I announce to you great joy, which will be for ALL people. Luke 19:10, Matt. 18:11. The Son of Man came to save that which was lost. 2 Cor. 5:14 & 15. One died for all. 2 Cor. 5:19. GOD was in Christ, reconciling the world to Himself. Col. 1:20. By the blood of Christ all things in Heaven and on earth have been restored or reconciled. 1 Tim. 2:6. Christ gave Himself a ransom for ALL. 1 Tim. 4:10. Christ is the Savior of all, especially of believers. Heb. 2:9. Christ tasted death for ALL. 1 John 2:2. Christ is the propitiation for our sins, and not for ours only, but for the sins of the whole world. And the Holy Spirit did not wish us to remain in suspense on this point to such an extent that He does not only make express mention of the whole world and all men in the cited testimonies: Whence the universal redemption of the whole human race is most evidently gathered and asserted: but He even explicitly explains the very nature of the redeemed, the impious, the reprobate, the perishing, and the damned. Certainly, in Rom. 14:15, the Apostle warns the Romans not to become a cause of perdition for him for whom Christ died. And in 1 Cor. 8:11, he exhorts the Corinthians not to deliver to perdition, through the abuse of Christian liberty, him for whom Christ died. And St. Peter, in chapter 2, verse 1, writes concerning false teachers and heresiarchs, that they deny the Lord who bought them, and thus involve themselves in sudden destruction. And the Epistle to the Hebrews, chapter 6:6 and chapter 10:30, affirms that he who has been sanctified by the blood of Christ, yet holds it in contempt and tramples it underfoot. By which oracles of the Scriptures, what could be said more plainly, what more forcefully, for our thesis, concerning asserting and demonstrating the universal redemption of the whole human race, we do not perceive.

But they err gravely who, in interpreting these oracles of the Scriptures, do not accept the word 'world,' with Beza and the remaining Sacramentarians, universally: but particularly for believers or the elect only. For 1. there exists no testimony in the entire Scripture by which the word 'world' is accommodated to the elect alone. 2. That Johannine Μερισμὸς does not admit this, unless we wish to give the sense of the words of the Holy Spirit, 1 John 2:2, which is far most inept: Christ is the propitiation not only for the elect: but also for the sins of the elect. 3. That world ought to be understood to whom the Gospel concerning Christ ought to have been announced, to whom also the Apostles were sent: Yet that consists in the breadth of the whole human race. Matt. 28:19, Mark 16:15, Acts 17:30, Rom. 10:18, Col. 1:6.

Finally, unless we understand by 'world' all men whatsoever, even the reprobate and the damned: truly no truth will stand in those assertions of the Scriptures which assert that very many are damned for this reason, because they spurn the merit of CHRIST offered in the Gospel: because they despise the counsel of God against themselves: because they do not leave a place for the congregation: because they repel the Word of God from themselves: because, invited to the wedding, they refuse to come: because they do not receive the beloved Truth: because they do not believe the Gospel and the Truth, Matt. 23:37, Matt. 22:5 & 6, Mark 16:16, Luke 7:30, John 3:18 & 36, Acts 7:51, Acts 13:46, 2 Thess. 1:8, 2 Thess. 2:10 & 12.

Then they err gravely who interpret the universality of redemption according to the universality of the Church, as Tossanus wished to sophistically argue, in this sense: that just as the Church is called Catholic, that is, universal by reason of the more excellent part, not because all and individual men are true members of the Church: so CHRIST is also called the universal Redeemer and Mediator of the whole world, not because the merit of CHRIST pertains to all men: but because with GOD there is no respect of persons, and the Gospel is the power unto salvation to every believer, whether he be Jew or Greek, or male or female: that is, that not individuals of kinds, but kinds of individuals, that is, from Jews and Gentiles, from all orders of men, the elect are redeemed by GOD.

Which interpretation indeed 1. ἄῤῥησίῳ fights with the testimonies of Scripture already cited, as those which extend the universality of redemption not to the elect alone, but to all men whatsoever, and explicitly to the reprobate also. 2. There is a huge dissimilarity in the example. For the definition of the Catholic Church looks to the faith of the members of the Church, and is therefore defined by the assembly of the faithful. But the universality of the merit of CHRIST looks to the merciful Will of God, which, with respect to the work of redemption, stands equally toward all men, as much the unbelieving as the believing. 3. The Apostolic διχοτομία of the whole world into Jews and Greeks does not hinder us at all. For just as by the term of Jews he understands the whole family and Jewish lineage: so also by the appellation of Greeks the Apostle understands all nations whatsoever. Whence again the universality of the world is most rightly gathered.

Nor does that passage from Romans 1:16 fit here: The Gospel is the power of GOD unto salvation to every believer: to the Jew and to the Greek. For in this place the Apostle does not distribute the whole world, but only believers into Jews and Gentiles: which distribution is distorted to the present business through gross ἄγνοιαν ἐλέγχε. Finally, that phrase is insidious, that the merit of CHRIST does not pertain to all, because of the ambiguous meaning it admits. For if it is taken concerning the saving effect, we ourselves assert that it is true:

Latin:

IMmensæ DEI misericordiæ erga lapsum genus humanum fuisse decretum illud de mittendo Filio, & per ipsum redimendo genere humano, modò ostendimus. Jam verò quicquid DEUS misericors hac in parte ab æterno decrevit: id Filius in plenitudine temporis effectum præstitit, per obedientiam & mortem suam, plenissimâ pro totius mundi salute restauratione sive Redemtione expedita. Ubi initiò elucescit admirandum illud temperamentum justitiæ & misericordiæ divinæ. Justitiæ quidem in eo, quòd Redemtioni generis humani non patuit locus, priusquàm pœnas peccatis nostris debitas, CHRISTUS sustinuisset: Misericordiæ verò, quòd per hanc ipsam Satisfactionem Filij DEUS Pater humanum genus sibi reconciliavit, & in gratiam recepit, 2. Cor. 9. Undè scitè Augustinus: Deus, inquit, nec in bonitate misericordiæ perdit judicij severitatem, nec in judicando cum severitate amittit misericordiæ bonitatem: in Psal. 100. De hoc ipso stupendo temperamento, ex professo differit Apostolus, Rom. 3, 24. & 25. Justificati gratis per gratiam ipsius, per redemtionē, quæ est in CHRISTO JESU, quem proposuit DEUS propitiationem per fidem in sangvine ipsius, ad ostensionem justitiæ suæ, propter remissionem præcedentium delictorum, in tolerantiâ DEI, ad ostensionem justitiæ ejus in hoc tempore, ut sit ipse justus, & justificans eum, qui est ex fide JESU CHRISTI.

De hoc salutis nostræ fundamento testantur Scripturarum Oracula: Esa. 53, 6. Dominus posuit super ipsum (Filium) iniquitates OMNIUM nostrûm: eorum omnium, qui tanquàm oves erraverunt: ubi totius generis humani complexum notari, clarius est, quàm ut probatione indigeat.

Joh. 1, 29. Hic est Agnus ille DEI, tollens peccata mundi. Johan. 3, 17. Ut mundus per eum servetur. Johan. 12, 47. Veni ut servem mundum.

Joh. 6, 51. Carnem meam dabo pro Mundi Vitâ. Luc. 2, 10. & 11. Annuncio vobis gaudium magnum, quod erit OMNI populo. Luc. 19, 10. Matt. 18, 11. Venit filius hominis salvare quod perierat. 2. Cor. 5, 14. & 15. Unus pro omnibus mortuus fuit. 2. Cor. 5, 19. DEUS erat in Christo, reconcilians sibi mundum. Coloss. 1, 20. Sangvine Christi restaurata sive reconciliata sunt omnia in Cælo, & in terrâ. 1. Tim. 2. 6. Christus dedit semetipsum precium pro OMNIBUS. 1. Timoth. 4, 10. Christus est Salvator omnium, maximè fidelium. Hebr. 2, 9. Christus pro OMNIBUS gustavit mortem. 1. Joh. 2, 2. Christus est propitiatio pro peccatis nostris, non pro nostris autem tantùm: sed pro totius mundi peccatis. Et usq; adeò Spiritus Sanctus nos in suspenso hærere hâc in parte noluit, ut non modò incitatis testimonijs, totius Mundi, & omnium hominum expressam faciat mentionem: Undè universalis Redemtio totius generis humani, evidentissimè colligitur, & asseritur: Verùm etiam ipsam speciem Redemtorum, impiorum, reproborum, pereuntium atq; damnatorum disertè explicet. Certè Rom. 14, 15. monet Apostolus Romanos, ne perditionis Causa fiant ei pro quo Christus est mortuus. Et in 1. Cor. 8, 11. hortatur Corinthios, ne per abusum libertatis Christianæ perditioni tradant eum, propter quem Christus sit mortuus. Et D. Petrus 2. Cap. 2. 1. de falsis Doctoribus & hæresiarchis scribit, Quod Dominum abnegent, qui ipsos mercatus sit, & sic seipsos subito exitio involvant. Et Epistola ad Hebræos cap. 6, 6. & cap. 10, 30. affirmat, eum quod, per Christi Sangvinem sanctificatum esse, qui eam tamen ostentui habeat, & pedibus conculcet. Quibus Scripturarum oraculis, quid planiùs, quid nervosiùs dici possit, pro thesi nostrâ, de Universali Redemtione totius generis humani asserenda demonstrandaque, non perspicuimus.

Graviter autem errant, qui in interpretandis istis Scripturarum oraculis Mundi Vocabulum, cum Beza & reliquis Sacramentarijs non universaliter: sed particulariter pro Solis Credentibus sive Electis accipiunt. Nam 1. nullum in universâ Scripturâ extat testimonium, quo Mundi Vocabulum solis electis accommodetur. 2. Μερισμὸς ille Johanniticus hoc non admittit, nisi Verborum Spiritus Sancti, 1. Joh. 2, 2. sensum longè ineptissimum dare velimus istum: Christus est propitiatio non tantùm pro electis: sed & pro electorum peccatis. 3. Ille mundus intelligi debet, cui annunciari debuit Evangelium de Christo, in quem etiam emissi sunt Apostoli: Atqui iste totius generis humani constat latitudine. Matth. 28, 19. Marci 16, 15. Actor. 17, 30. Rom. 10, 18. Coloss. 1, 6.

Tandem nisi per Mundum intelligamus omnes omninò homines, etiam reprobos & damnatos: nulla profectò Veritas constabit illis assertioribus Scripturarum, quæ asserunt ideò plurimos damnari, quia meritum CHRISTI in Evangelio oblatum asparnantur: quia Consilium Dei adversus seipsos spernunt: quia congregationi locum non relinquunt: quia Verbum Dei à se repellunt: quia ad nuptias invitati, venire recusant: quia dilectam Veritatem non recipiunt: quia Evangelio & Veritati non credunt, Matth. 23, 37. Matth. 22, 5. & 6. Marci 16, 16. Luc. 7, 30. Joh. 3, 18. & 36. Actor. 7, 51. Actor. 13, 46. 2. Thess. 1, 8. 2. Thess. 2, 10. & 12.

Deindè graviter errant, qui Universalitatem Redemtionis, secundum Universalitatem Ecclesiæ interpretantur, uti Tossanus sophisticari voluit, hoc sensu: ut quemadmodum Ecclesia dicitur Catholica, hoc est, universalis ratione partis præstantioris, non quòd universi & singuli homines sint vera membra Ecclesiæ: Sic CHRISTUS etiam dicatur Redemtor universalis & Mediator totius mundi, non quòd ad omnes homines pertineat meritum CHRISTI: sed quòd apud DEUM non est acceptio personarum, & Evangelium est potentia ad salutem omni Credenti, sive Judæus sit, sive Græcus sive mas, sive fœmina: hoc est, quòd non singuli generum, sed genera singulorum, hoc est, ex Judæis & Gentibus, ex omnibus ordinibus hominum, Electi sint à DEO redemti.

Quæ sanè interpretatio 1. ἄῤῥησίῳ pugnat cum Scripturæ testimoniis jam citatis, ut quæ Universalitatem Redemtionis non ad solos Electos, sed ad omnes omninò homines, & difertè ad Reprobos etiam extendit. 2. Ingens dissimilitudo in exemplo. Ecclesiæ enim Catholicæ definitio respicit membrorum Ecclesiæ fidem, ac proindè fidelium etiam Cætu definitur. Universitas autem meriti CHRISTI, respicit misericordem Voluntatem Dei, quæ respectu operis Redemtionis, ex æquo se habet erga omnes homines, tàm incredulos, quàm credentes. 3. διχοτομία Apostolica totius Mundi in Judæos & Græcos nobis nihil quicquam officit. Nam uti Judæorum termino universam familiam & propaginem Judaicam: Ita Græcorum etiam appellatione omnes omninò gentes intelligit Apostolus. Undè rursus Mundi Universitas rectissimè colligitur.

Neque huc quadrat illud Roman. 1, 16. Evangelium est potentia DEI ad Salutem omni Credenti: Judæo & Græco. Nam hoc loco Apostolus non totum mundum, sed tantùm Credentes distribuit in Judæos & gentes: quæ distributio ad præsens negotium per crassam ἄγνοιαν ἐλέγχε detorquetur. Tandem insidiosa est phrasis illa, Quòd meritum CHRISTI non ad omnes pertineat, propter ambiguam ejus significationem, quam admittit. Nam si de effectu salutari accipiatur, ipsi nos veram eam esse asserimus:


### Universal Calling

But if it is understood concerning the Intention & Will of GOD: we say that it is most false. Therefore, so that no ambiguity in this matter might produce either obscurity or error, we establish that the phrases which we use: such as: Christ died for all men: he bore the sins of the whole World: he redeemed the whole world: he is the propitiation for the sins of the whole world, and similar ones, are to be accurately distinguished from those which the Sacramentarians insidiously agitate as if they were equivalent: such as: The benefit of the Death of CHRIST pertains to all: all are indifferently cleansed from sins: All are sanctified into the temple of GOD. For the former denote the consummation of the work by which we have been redeemed: but the latter imply at the same time the application made by faith.

Finally, they err gravely who, to the sayings of the Scriptures proposed a little before, affix that sense which some of the Calvinists write of, that Christ satisfied for the sins of the whole world sufficiently indeed, but not efficiently. This distinction has indeed obtained use in the Church of God for a long time, but not in the Sacramentarian sense, as if the merit of CHRIST could be sufficient for the redemption of all men, if it had been destined for this by God the Father: which is blasphemous even to hear: But in the Orthodox sense, that the merit of Christ satisfied most sufficiently for the sins of the whole world: but that the salutary effect does not follow in the greatest part of the world, because the unbelieving do not apply this Merit to themselves through faith. In which sense and respect we indeed willingly accept this distinction: although the word Efficiently appears as a somewhat harsh catachresis: and the thing itself could be explained more clearly even without this distinction: but we devote to the curses that which is used in the Calvinistic sense. For what could be said or conceived that is more blasphemous, or even more insulting to the immense mercy of GOD, than to assert with the apostate Grynæus, that the Death of Christ was not destined by GOD to the end that it might have the value of expiating the sins of all men: And that this Counsel, this will of God concerning the death of Christ, never existed from eternity, nor did God ever bring this into his mind. Grynæus, disputation on true & Orthodox faith, Class 1, Theses 12 & 13. But Beza, in his 2nd Response to the acts of the Colloquy of Mömpelgard, page 217, rightly calls this distinction, used by his fellow-members, a mere evasion. And Piscator in his annotations on verse 6. of Chapter 2 of the first to Timothy, bears this judgment concerning it: This distinction has the appearance of erudition: but in reality it is inept: because it implies a Contradiction: For in the words of the Apostle (CHRIST gave himself a redemption for all:) That Preposition FOR, certainly denotes the end or scope of CHRIST offering himself, and consequently also the effect. For whatever CHRIST ever proposed to himself to effect, that he also actually effected. If therefore he proposed to himself to offer to the Father an expiatory sacrifice for the sins of individual men, certainly he actually effected that: and therefore it must be said that he is the propitiation for the sins of individuals, not only sufficiently, but also efficiently. But I say, CHRIST proposed to himself to offer himself for the elect alone, as was shown before from John 17: but not for the reprobate, and therefore not for individual men. Wherefore it is not to be said that CHRIST died for individual men indeed, but not efficiently: for this is just as if it were said, he died indeed for individuals, but yet he did not die for individuals. Which is a manifest Contradiction. Thus far Piscator, who indeed argues rightly for the elimination of this distinction, used in the Calvinistic sense: but in this he hallucinates gravely, that he contends that CHRIST died for the elect alone: which is clearly evident from what has already been said.

Latin:

Sin autem intelligatur de Intentione & Voluntate DEI: dicimus eam esse falsissimam. Proindè ut ne ambiguitas aliqua, hoc in negotio vel obscuritaté, vel errorem pariat, statuimus phrases quibus nos utimur:quales sunt: Christus pro omnibus hominibus mortuus: tulit peccata totius Mundi: redemit totum mundum:est propitiatio pro peccatis totius mundi, & consimiles, accuratè discernendas esse ab illis, quas ceu æquipollentes insidiosèexagitant Sacramentarij: quales sunt: Beneficium Mortis CHRISTI pertinet ad omnes: omnes indifferenter mundantur à peccatis: Omnes sanctificantur in DEI templum. Nam priores consummationem operis, quo redemti sumus, notant: Posteriores verò applicationem fide factam, simul implicant.

Tandem graviter errant, qui dictis Scripturarum paulò ante propositis, eum sensum affingunt, quo Calvinianorum nonnulli scriptitant, Christum satisfecisse pro peccatis totius mundi sufficienter quidem, sed non efficienter. Usum quidem in Ecclesiâ Dei jam olim hæc distinctio obtinuit, non verò sensu Sacramentario, ac si meritum CHRISTI sufficiens quidem esse posset, ad redemtionem omnium hominum, si ad hoc fuisset à Deo patre destinatum: id quod vel auditu blasphemum est:Verùm sensu Orthodoxo, quòd meritum Christi sufficientissimè satisfecerit pro peccatis totius mundi: sed effectum salutarem in maximâ mundi parte non subsequi, propterea quòd increduli, Meritum hoc per fidem sibi non applicant. Quo sanè sensu ac respectu nos distinctionem hanc libenter acceptamus: licèt in Verbo Efficienter κατάχρησις duriuscula appareat: & res ipsa etiam sine hac distinctione dilucidiùs explicari possit:sed sensu Calvinistico usurpatam diris devovemus. Quid enim blasphemum magis, quid etiam in immensam DEI misericordiam contumeliosiùs dici cogitarivè queat, quàm cum Grynæo apostata asserere, Mortẽ Christi à DEO non esse destinatã ad id, ut haberet valorẽ expiandi peccata omnium hominum: Et hoc Consiliũ, hanc voluntatem Deo de morte Christi ab æterno nunquàm constitiisse, neḡ hoc in animum suum Deum unquàm induxisse. Grynæus, disputat. de verâ & Orthod. fide Claß. 1. Thes. 12. & 13. Rectè autem Beza Resp. 2. ad acta Colloquij Möpelg. pag. 217. Distinctionem hanc à gregalibus suis usurpatam, meram tergiversationem nominat. Et Piscator in annotat. ad versum 6. Capitis 2. prioris ad Timotheum hanc de eâ fert ἐπίκρισιν: Hæc distinctio speciem habet eruditionis: sed reverà inepta est: quia implicat Contradictionem: Etenim in verbis Apostoli (CHRISTUS dedit semetipsum redemtionem pro omnibus:) Præpositio illa PRO, notat certè finem seu scopum CHRISTI sese offerentis, & ex consequenti etiam effectum. Quicquid enim CHRISTUS sibi unquàm efficere proposuit, id etiam reipsa effecit. Si ergò sibi proposuit, offerre patri sacrificium expiatorium, pro peccatis singulorum hominum, certè illud reipsa effecit: ac proinde dicendum erit, eum esse propitiationem pro peccatis singulorum, non solùm sufficienter, sed etiam efficienter. At inquam, CHRISTUS sibi proposuit sese offerre pro solis electis, ut antea ex Joh. 17. ostensum est: non autem pro reprobis, ac proindè non pro singulis hominibus. Quare nec est dicendum CHRISTUM pro singulis quidem hominibus mortuum esse, sed non efficienter: hoc enim perindè est: ac si diceretur, mortuus quidem pro singulis, sed tamen non est mortuus pro singulis. Quae manifesta Contradictio est. Hactenùs Piscator, qui rectè quidem disputat pro eliminandâ hac distinctione, sensu Calvinistico usurpatâ: in eo autem graviter hallucinatur, quòd CHRISTUM pro solis electis mortuum esse contendit: id quod ex jam dictis luculenter patet.


### Universal Calling: III. The Member of Antecedent Will in God. Universal Calling

III. The Member of Antecedent Will in God. UNIVERSAL CALLING.

Great indeed are the things that have been said concerning the immense mercy of GOD toward the salvation of all men, and concerning the most sufficient sacrifice of CHRIST for the sins of the whole world: but of no less evidence is that Third member of the Antecedent will in GOD, namely that GOD always willed and took care, and today still wills and takes care, that these very benefits be offered to the whole world through Evangelical preaching, and that all men be called to the enjoyment of these goods. This member consists of three distinct degrees. THE FIRST is: That GOD from eternity decreed and willed that the Word of Grace or the Gospel be preached and revealed to all men. THE SECOND: That all men hear the preached word and apprehend it by faith. THE THIRD: That all believers persevere in faith to the end, and thus be saved.

The whole Biblical history testifies concerning the first member. For to this end GOD himself undertook the parts of preaching, and announced that proto-Gospel concerning the Seed of the woman, who would crush the Head of the Serpent, to the first-formed, and willed that it be propagated in later times by the work of the Patriarchs and Prophets. Nor would anything have been more pleasing to him than that the Word of salvation be accepted by all, or at least by most, with an obedient mind. And although (which his own complaints in Genesis 6 and 8, and elsewhere throughout, clearly evince to have been most troublesome to GOD), the greater part of the world in all ages repudiated the word of Grace, and showed itself unworthy of eternal life, as the Apostle speaks in Acts 13:46, yet GOD did not leave himself without witness, Acts 14:17, but at least three times revealed his Word to the whole world. First after the creation of the world in the Adamic Church. Then after the flood in the house and family of Noah. Finally after the ascension of CHRIST into the Heavens, at the departure and dispersion of the Apostles into the whole world, as the command of CHRIST has it: Matt. 28:19, Mark 16:15, which the Apostle is a witness had already been fulfilled in his own time, Coloss. 1:23. Here indeed it would have been altogether just, that by posterity it should always be retained, and, which could likewise be done, be propagated equally to others. But the ingratitude of the greatest part in this matter was so foul, that by their own loss, and, what is more serious, by their own fault as well, they caused the loss of that treasure. But yet, under this very stupendous ingratitude of the world and contempt of the Word, God nevertheless willed that the rays of His mercy should shine forth in that also: because the Church of God, or the people who asserted the incomparable treasure of the divine Word to be safe and sound at any time, was always established in the world in such an illustrious place that it could easily be known to any peoples and nations, provided they were not extremely slothful, concerning the preaching of the divine Word. Just as indeed today it cannot but be sufficiently known to Jews and Turks concerning the Christian religion, as those who live everywhere in the midst of Christians, unless they themselves place an obstacle of extreme contumacy. And although that was the condition of the Israelite people in the Old Testament, which is also through the grace of God the condition of the Christian people in the New Testament, that God announced His Word to Jacob, His statutes and His judgments to Israel, and did not do so to every nation; Psalm 147:19; yet neither were the Gentiles thus excluded of old, nor are infidel peoples even today so cast away from the use of that Word, that God begrudges them this good, let alone salvation: rather, He has always had it in His wishes, and still has, that posterity should, as it were, recover the treasure of the Word, lost by the ingratitude of their ancestors: which the prophecies of the prophets concerning the calling of the Gentiles, and that command of Christ, Matthew 28:19, Mark 16:15, Go into the whole world, and preach the Gospel to every creature, etc., clearly show. To which also pertains that of Acts 17:26 and 27. Therefore He determined the appointed times, and the set boundaries of their habitation, that they should seek God, if perhaps they might grope for Him, and find Him, although He is not far from each one of us. And verse 30: The times of ignorance indeed God overlooked, but now He announces that all men everywhere should repent. And this is that very thing which God testified through the prophet, that He so ardently seeks the conversion of all men, that all day long He stretches out His hands to a people even incredulous. Isaiah 65:2. Yea, even to the refusers, and to those who despise all the counsel of God, and all His rebukes: Proverbs 1:24 and 25.

Human reason clamors at this point, and objects that of Ezekiel 18:20: The soul that has sinned, it shall die: the son shall not bear the iniquity of the father: and the father shall not bear the iniquity of the son. Now, however, many peoples are forced to pay for the fault of their parents and ancestors, while they cannot hear the preaching of the Gospel, lost not by themselves, but by their ancestors. I answer our thesis, by which we affirm that many peoples today lack the preaching or ministry

of the Word, which their ancestors indeed had, but lost through inexcusable contempt, is to be accepted in a qualified sense, and not simply, or too loosely. The sense therefore of our thesis is: That posterity pays for the fault of their parents and ancestors in that they are born outside the Church: but not that because of the ingratitude of the parents, every power of hearing the divine Word, or salvation itself, has been cut off and taken away from them. The former we assert: the latter we deny. The former is merely a temporal punishment, which, however much it may mean they are born outside the Church, does not exclude or bar them from access to the Church and the hearing of the Word: as was shown a little earlier.

For God invites even these today to the marriage of His Son, and cries out: All things are ready: Come to the marriage: Matthew 22:4. These peoples could therefore no less today aggregate themselves to the Church of God, just as of old many from heathendom associated themselves with the Jewish people: such as Jethro, Rahab the Gibeonites, Job, Ruth, Hiram King of Tyre, the Queen of the South, Naaman the Syrian, the Ninevites, Nebuchadnezzar, Darius, Cyrus, Ahasuerus, and the Persians converted by Mordecai the Jew. For God has placed the Church in an illustrious place today just as of old, so that the fame of God and the religion of the Christians may spread itself to all peoples and nations that are under heaven. Now, however, because these peoples partly cling contumaciously to the idolomania of their parents and ancestors, and partly laugh at and treat with contumely the true worship of God, or the God of the Christians: they are certainly not to be considered as bearing the sins of their parents now, but as perishing and being damned by the just judgment of God because of their own fault.

But furthermore, reason growls: Of a non-entity there are no qualities. But these infidel peoples have never actually had the Word of God and its preaching. Therefore it is wrongly asserted that they perish and are damned because of their own contempt of the divine Word.

I answer that the proposition is true concerning those things which exist in no pact or respect. Now as for the minor premise, which is true only in a qualified sense, although infidel peoples who are born outside the Church do not have the Word of God and its preaching in their midst in actual fact: and therefore they also lack that special act of contempt for the divine Word: since what one does not have in act, one cannot, speaking properly, be said to despise and reject: yet they do not for that reason lack every act of contempt for the divine Word simply. For insofar as they can seek and have the Word of God, in the sense and respect already explained: but they do not do so, but rather hate, nay, persecute the true God and the true religion worse than a dog and a snake: to that extent they certainly entangle themselves in the eternal guilt of contempt for the divine Word.

And this is the first degree of the Universal Vocation, which consists in this, that GOD wills that the Word of the Gospel be preached and revealed to all men.

THE SECOND Degree is that GOD wills that all men hear the preached Word, and through it believe in CHRIST. For the nature of this preached Word is not such that, although it is preached to many, GOD nevertheless wills it to be hidden, or useless, or even harmful to most: but He desires uniquely that it be heard by all, that once heard it be accepted, and indeed through the hearing of it He desires to work conversion and faith seriously in those who do not reject the Counsel of GOD against themselves, Luke 7:30. The Evangelical promises testify to this. Matt. 11:28. Come to me all you who labor and are burdened: I will refresh you. Matt. 28:19. Teach all nations: and Mark 16:15. Preach the Gospel to every Creature. Luke 24:47. It behooves repentance and remission of sins to be preached to all nations. John 1:7. He came to bear witness of the light, that all might believe through him. Acts 17:30. GOD now announces to men that all everywhere should repent. Eph. 3:9. To me this grace was given, to evangelize among the nations the unsearchable riches of CHRIST, and to enlighten all. Col. 1:28. We announce CHRIST, admonishing every man, and teaching every man, in all wisdom.

And in this will of His, GOD exhibits such constancy that He does not disdain to offer His Word even to the impious and obstinate. Isa. 65:2. All day long I have spread out my hands to an incredulous people. And Verse 12. I called and you did not answer, I extended my hand, and there was no one who looked. Prov. 1:24. I called and you refused, I extended my hand and there was no one who looked. Matt. 23:37. How often have I willed to gather you, as a hen gathers her chicks, and you would not.

But human reason objects here too, what is the profit of all being called, and indeed seriously called, when nevertheless not all can believe, because Faith is a gift of GOD, and is not given to all. But this is a fault of the accident. For GOD calls seriously, and omits nothing at all on His part that could profit and serve a man for the conceiving of faith. But that not all actually conceive faith, the fault lies with the Hearers of the Word themselves: Which the Savior in the parable of the fourfold field, through the way, the rock, and the thorns, wished to explain clearly enough. Matt. 13:3. Luke 8:5. et seqq. For some either do not hear at all, when they pretend to hear: Or certainly they hear with a prejudice which they do not think of laying aside. Others, lest they lose the grace of those whose favor they are courting, when they have begun well, proceed badly, and turn out to be πρόσκαιροι. Others finally, the Thorns of Pleasures, and a certain hardened habit of sinning suffocates, so that they cannot bear fruit.

Regarding the Apostolic passage: Faith is a gift of GOD, and is not of all, Col. 2:12, 2 Thess. 3:2, Phil. 1:29, again the same Fault of the Accident emerges. For GOD bestows and gives faith to men not immediately: but mediately, namely through the organ of the Word preached and heard. For Faith, as the Apostle testifies, is from hearing: and hearing through the Word of GOD, namely of the Gospel, which is the power of GOD unto salvation to every Believer. Rom. 1:16, Rom. 10:17. What wonder then, if those who either despise this Word, or hear it with prejudice, do not conceive Faith: but this Word becomes to them an odor of death unto death, 2 Cor. 2:16. Whence it is seen that the Sacramentarians are notably blasphemous, teaching that the Gospel is preached to the Reprobate for this sole end, and for this sole cause, not that they may be converted by it: but that they may be more grievously hardened and blinded. The same impiety plagues their twin figment concerning the twofold Vocation of GOD, one efficacious, the other inefficacious: and concerning the twofold drawing of GOD, serious and feigned. For although the works are diverse, to preach outwardly: to convert inwardly and make a believer: of which the former belongs to the minister, the latter primarily and properly to GOD: yet it is one action, one and the same Word, the same preaching, by which the conversion of man is effected: which being done, it is said that not a twofold drawing but one: not a twofold Vocation, but one has taken place. Now GOD commands that this Voice of the Gospel be announced to all: that they may hear this Voice of His Son, GOD commands all, and through the hearing of the same He promises that He will be efficacious for the faith and conversion of men. Although indeed a man can take nothing of spiritual things to himself, unless it has been given to him from above: much less either merit the grace of GOD, or prepare himself to grasp it, indeed he cannot even offer assent to the preached Word of himself: for such is the corruption of our nature that it does not perceive the things which are of the Spirit of GOD, indeed it cannot even do so: but it is foolishness to him, 1 Cor. 2:14, 2 Cor. 3:5. Nevertheless, a man can at least perform this, that he can offer external hearing to the Word, and apply carnal study in meditating upon it: as was demonstrated more fully in the Article on Free Will. That therefore the greatest part of the Hearers of the Word does not now conceive Faith: that certainly happens not by the fault or envy of GOD, but by their own vice.

For they could have performed that which is still placed in their own powers, namely to hear the Word, and to hear with a desire to learn. And if they had done this, undoubtedly GOD also, not indeed out of merit of congruity or condignity, but out of mere grace, by the power of His promises, would have been about to bestow Faith.

The third and final degree of the Universal Vocation is that GOD wills that all Believers persevere in faith to the end, and thus be saved. Scripture confirms this again most clearly.

Phil. 1, 6. He who began a good work in you will complete it even unto the day of JESUS CHRIST.

1. Cor. 1, 8. CHRIST will confirm you even unto the end, blameless, in the day of his coming.

1 Thess. 5:23 & 24. May the God of peace himself sanctify you through and through: that your whole spirit, and soul, and body may be preserved blameless at the coming of our Lord JESUS CHRIST: Faithful is he who called you: who also will do it. But we shall have to deal with this perseverance below in its own place at greater length.

And such indeed, with respect to its parts, is the Antecedent Will of GOD, and it is constant, eternal, and immutable, by which he pursues the salvation of the human race, most mercifully indeed, so that in it nothing at all can be desired for the sake of supreme love.

Latin:

III. Membrum Voluntatis Antecedentis in Deo. UNIVERSALIS VOCATIO.

MAgna quidem sunt & praeclara, quae de immensâ DEI misericordiâ erga omnium hominum salutem, & de sufficientissimo CHRISTI pro totius mundi peccatis sacrificio dicta sunt: sed haud minoris est evidentiae Tertium illud voluntatis in DEO Antecedentis membrum, quòd nimirùm haec ipsa beneficia per praedicationem Evangelicam toti mundo offerri DEUS, atq; ad perfruitionem bonorum istorum, homines universos vocari semper voluit & curavit, hodieq; vult & curat. Constat hoc membrum tribus distinctis gradibus. PRIMUS est: Quod DEUS ab aeterno decrevit & voluit, ut Verbum Gratiae sive Evangelium omnibus hominibus praedicetur & reveletur. ALTER: Ut omnes homines verbum praedicatum audiant & fide apprehendant. TERTIUS: Ut credentes omnes in fide ad finem perseverent, & sic salventur.

De primo membro universa testatur historia Biblica. Nam hoc fine ipse DEUS praedicationis partes suscepit, & prot-Evangelium illud de Semine mulieris, contrituro Caput Serpentis, protoplastis annunciavit, idq; posteris temporibus Patriarcharum & Prophetarum operâ propagatum voluit. Neq; gratius ipsi quicquam fuiffet, quàm ab omnibus, aut plurimis saltem, Verbum salutis obsequente animo acceptari. Et quanquàm (quod molestissimum DEO fuisse, querelae ipsius Genes. 6. & 8. passim alibi, luculenter evincunt), major pars mundi omnibus seculis verbum Gratiae repudiavit, seq; indignam vitâ aeternâ praestitit, ut loquitur Apostolus Actor. 13, 46. non tamen intestatum se reliquit DEUS Actor. 14, 17. sed tribus ut minimum vicibus, toti mundo Verbum suum revelavit. Primùm post creationem mundi in Ecclesiâ Adamicâ. Deindè post diluvium in domo & familiâ Noahi. Tandem post ascensum in CHRISTI ad Coelos, in exitu & dispersione Apostolorum in universum mundum, ut habet mandatum CHRISTI: Matth. 28, 19. Marci 16, 15. quod Apostolus, jam suo tempore impletum suisse, testis est, Coloss. 1, 23. Hîc sanè aequum omninò fuerat, à postetiæ semper retineri, &, quod fieri itidem poterat, ad alios pariter propagari. Sed maximæ partis hac in re tam fœda fuit ingratitudo, ut suopte tùm damno, tùm, quod gravius est, culpâ etiam propriâ, thesauri istius jacturam fecerit. Sed sub hâc ipsâ tamen stupendâ Mundi ingratitudine, & Verbi comtemtu, nihilo minus tamen DEUS misericordiæ suæ radios in eo quoque elucefcere voluit: quod Ecclesia DEI, sive populus, qui Verbi divini thesaurum incomparabilem sartum tectum, quovis tempore asserebat, ita semper in mundo in illustri loco constitutus fuit, ut quibusvis populis & nationibus, modò non extremè ignavis, de Verbi divini prædicatione facilè constare potuerit. Quemadmodum sanè hodieque Judæis & Turcis, de Religione Christianâ non potest non satis constare, ut qui in medio Christianorum ubique vivunt, nisi ipsi extremæ contumaciæ obicem ponant. Et quanquàm ea fuit populi Israëlitici conditio in Vetere Testamento, quæ est etiam per gratiam DEI populi Christiani in Novo Testamento, ut annunciârit DEUS Verbum suum Jacob, statuta & judicia sua Israëli, neque taliter fecerit omni nationi; Psalm. 147, 19. tamen neque olim sic exclusæ erant gentes, neque hodiè etiamnùm ita sunt projecti infideles populi, ab usu Verbi istius, ut illis bonum hoc, nedùm Salutem, invideat DEUS: quin hoc ipsum potiùs in votis semper habuit, & habet adhuc, ut thesaurum Verbi, majorum ingratitudine deperditum, posteri ad se postliminiò quasi repetant: id quod Vaticinia Prophetarum de Vocatione gentium, & mandatum illud CHRISTI, Matth. 28, 19. Marci 16, 15. Ite in mundum universum, & prædicate Evangelium OMNI Creaturæ &c. luculenter ostendunt. Quò pertinet etiam illud Actor. 17, 26. & 27. Ideò tempora præstituta definivit, & terminos statutos habitationis eorũ, ut quærerent DEUM, si fortè palpent eum, & inveniant, quamvis non longè absit ab unoquoq; nostrûm. Et Versu 30. Tempora quidem ignorantiæ dissimulavit DEUS, nunc autem annunciat, ut OMNES UBIQUE homines resipiscant. Et hoc est illud ipsum, quod testatus est DEUS per Prophetam, se usque adeò ardenter expetere omnium hominum Conversionem, ut totâ die expandat manus suas ad populum etiam incredulum. Jesai 65, 2. Imò ad renuentes etiam, & ad eos, qui despiciunt omne Consilium DEI, omnesque increpationes ejus: Proverb. 1, 24. & 25.

Obstrepit hoc loco humana ratio, & objicit illud Ezech. 18, 20. Anima, quæ peccaverit, ipsa morietur: Filius non portabit iniquitatem patris: & Pater non portabit iniquitatem Filij. Jam verò parentum & majorum suorum culpam præstare coguntur plurimi populi, dùm prædicationem Evangelij, non à se, sed à majoribus deperditam, audire non possunt. Respondeo thesin nostram, quâ affirmamus, Multos populos hodiè carere prædicatione sive Ministerio

Verbi, quod Majores ipsorum habuerunt quidem, sed per contemtum inexpugnabilem amiserunt, secundum quid, & non simpliciter, sive nimis laxè esse accipiendum. Sensus ergò thesews nostræ est: Quod posteri luant culpam parentum & majorum suorum in eo, quod extra Ecclesiam nascuntur: non verò quod propter ingratitudinem parentum omnis ipsis vel potestas audiendi Verbi divini, vel salus ipsa præcisa & ademta sit. Prius illud asserimus: Posterius hoc negamus. Prius illud temporalis duntaxat pœna est, quæ quantumvis extra Ecclesiam natos, non tamen excludit vel arcet ab aditu ad Ecclesiam & auditu Verbi: uti paulò antè ostensum.

Nam & hos DEUS hodieq́; invitat ad nuptias filij sui, & clamat: Omnia sunt parata: Venite ad nuptias: Matth. 22, 4. Possent ergò isti populi haud minus hodieq́; sese aggregare Ecclesiæ DEI, atq́; olim ex Gentilitate plurimi sese adsociârunt populo Judaico: ut Jethro, Rahab Gibeonitæ, Job, Ruth, Hiram Rex Tyri, Regina Austri, Naëman Syrus, Ninivitæ, Nebucadnezar, Darius, Cyrus, Ahasverus, Persæ à Mardocheo Judæo conversi. Nam æq́; hodiè atq́; olim DEUS Ecclesiam in illustri loco posuit, ut fama de DEO & Religione Christianorum ad omnes gentes & nationes quæ sub Cœlo sunt, se diffundat. Jam verò quòd populi isti, partim in parentum & majorum suorum Idolomania contumaciter hærent, partim verum DEI cultum, sive Christianorum DEUM rident & contumeliâ afficiunt: non certè jam parentum suorum peccata portare: sed propter propriam culpam Justo DEI judicio perire & damnari, statuendi sunt.

Sed porrò oggannit Ratio: Non entis nullæ sunt qualitates. Atqui populi isti infideles, Verbum DEI ejusq́; prædicationem actu nunquàm habuerunt. Ergò malè asseritur, quod propter proprium contemtum Verbi divini pereant & damnentur.

Respondeo, Propositionem veram esse de ijs, quæ nullo pacto aut respectu existunt. Jam quoad Minorem, quæ ϰατὰ tantùm vera est, licèt infideles populi, qui extra Ecclesiam nascuntur, non habent ipso actu Verbum DEI, ejusque prædicationem, in medio sui: ac proindè carent etiam actu isto speciali contemtus Verbi divini: siquidem quod quis actu non habet: illud propriè loquendo, non dici potest contemnere & rejicere: tamen non propterea omni simpliciter actu contemtus Verbi divini carent. Nam quatenùs verbum DEI inquirere & habere possunt, eo, quo jam explicatum est, sensu ac respectu: id verò non faciunt, sed verum potiùs Deum, veramque Religionem, cane & angve pejus oderunt, imò persequuntur: eatenùs certè æterno reatu contemtus Verbi divini seipsos implicant.

Et hic primus est Vocationis Universalis gradus, qui in eo consistit, quòd DEUS vult, ut Verbum Evangelij universis hominibus prædicetur & reveletur.

ALTER Gradus est, quod DEUS vult, ut omnes homines Verbum prædicatum audiant, & per illud in CHRISTUM credant. Neq; enim ea est Verbi istius prædicati ratio, quasi licèt multis prædicetur, id tamen plerisq; velit DEUS vel esse occultum, vel inutile, vel damnosum etjam: sed ab omnibus id audiri unicè cupit, auditum acceptari vult, imò per auditum ejus in his, qui non spernunt Consilium DEI adversus seipsos, Luc. 7, 30. Conversionem & Fidem ipse seriò operari desiderat. Testantur hoc promissiones Evangelicæ. Matth. 11, 28. Venite ad me omnes, qui laboratis & onerati estis: ego reficiam vos. Matth. 28, 19. Docete omnes gentes: & Marci 16, 15. Prædicate Evangelium omni Creaturæ. Luc. 24, 47. Oportet prædicari pœnitentiam & remissionem peccatorum in omnes gentes. Joh. 1, 7, Hic venit, ut testimonium perhiberet de lumine, ut omnes crederent per illum. Actor. 17, 30. DEUS nunc annunciat hominibus, ut omnes ubiq; respiscant. Ephes. 3, 9. Mihi data est gratia hæc, in gentibus Evangelizare investigabiles divitias CHRISTI, & illuminare omnes. Coloss. 1, 28. Annunciamus CHRISTUM, admonentes omnem hominem, & docentes omnem hominem, in omni sapientiâ.

Et in hâc voluntate suâ DEus tantam constantiam exhibet, ut ne quidem impijs & obstinatis Verbum suum offerre dedignetur. Esa. 65, 2. Totâ die expandi manus meas ad populum incredulum. Et Versu 12. Vocavi & non respondistis, extendi manum meam, & non fuit, qui aspiceret. Proverb. 1, 24. Vocavi & renuistis, extendi manum meam & non fuit, qui aspiceret. Matth. 23, 37. Quoties volui congregare te, sicut gallina pullos suos, & noluisti.

Sed obstrepit & hîc humana ratio, quid profit omnes vocari, & seriò quidem vocari, cum tamen non omnes credere possint, propterea quòd Fides sit donum DEI, & non detur omnibus. Verùm accidentis hoc est vitium. DEUS enim seriò vocat, & nihil quicquam intermittit ex suâ parte, quod ad fidem concipiendam homini prodesse & inservire queat. Quòd verò non omnes ipso actu fidem concipiunt, culpa est penes ipsos Auditores Verbi: Id quod Servator in parabolâ, de quadruplice agro, per viam, petram & spinas satis dilucidè explicare voluit. Matth. 13, 3. Luc. 8, 5. & seqq. Alij enim vel planè non audiunt, cùm se audire simulent: Vel certè cum præjudicio, quod non cogitant deponere, audiunt. Alij ne gratiâ eorum, quorum favorem aucupantur, excidant, cùm benè inceperint, malè progrediuntur, & evadunt πρόσκαιροι. Alios deniq; Spinæ Voluptatum, & obturatus quidam peccandi habitus suffocat, ut fructum ferre non possint.

Quoad locum Apostolicum: Fides est donum DEI, & non est omnium Coloss. 2, 12. 2. Thessal. 3, 2. Phil. 1, 29. rursum idem Accidentis Vitium emergit. Nam DEUS largitur & donat fidem hominibus non immediate: sed mediate, nempe per organum Verbi praedicati & auditi. Fides enim teste Apostolo, est ex auditu: auditus autem per Verbum DEI, nempe Evangelij, quod est potentia DEI ad salutem omni Credenti. Rom. 1, 16. Rom. 10, 17. Quid mirum ergo, si illi qui Verbum hoc vel contemnunt, vel cum praejudicio audiunt, Fidem non concipiant: sed Verbum hoc fiat ipsis odor mortis ad mortem 2. Cor. 2, 16. Unde conspicitur, insigniter blasphemos esse Sacramentarios docentes, Evangelium Reprobis hoc solo fine, & hanc solam ob causam praedicari, non ut eo convertantur: sed gravius indurentur atq; excaecantur. Qua eadem impietate laborat eorundem geminum figmentum de Vocatione DEI duplici, Efficace una, inefficace altera: deq; tractu DEI duplici, serio & simulato. Etsi enim opera diversa sunt, Foris praedicare: Intus convertere & Credentem facere: quorum illud ministro: hoc DEO primum ac proprie competit: una tamen actio est, unum atq; idem Verbum, praedicatio eadem, qua hominis Conversio efficitur: qua facta, non geminus tractus sed unus: non gemina Vocatio, sed una facta esse dicitur. Jam omnibus Vocem istam Evangelij annunciari jubet DEUS: ut Vocem istam Filij sui audiant, omnibus DEUS praecipit, & per auditum ejusdem sese ad fidem & conversionem hominum efficacem fore pollicetur. Quanquam vero homo nihil rerum Spiritualium sibi sumere potest, nisi datum ipsi fuerit desuper: nedum vel gratiam DEI promereri, vel ad eam capessendam sese praeparare, imo Verbo praedicato ex se ne quidem assensum praebere possit: tanta enim est naturae nostrae corruptio, ut non percipiat ea, quae sunt Spiritus DEI, imo ne possit quidem: sed stultitia ipsi sit 1. Cor. 2, 14. 2. Cor. 3, 5. Tamen id saltem praestare potest homo, ut externum auditum Verbo praebere, & carnale studium in eo meditando adhibere possit: uti in Articulo de Libero Arbitrio fusius demonstratum fuit. Quod ergo jam maxima pars Auditorum Verbi Fidem non concipit: id certe fit non culpa aut invidia DEI, sed ipsorummet vitio.

Poterant enim praestare id, quod in ipsorum viribus adhuc est positum, nempe audire Verbum, & cum discendi studio audire. Quod si fecissent, haud dubie DEUS quoq; non quidem ex merito vel congrui vel condigni, sed ex mera gratia, vi promissionum suarum, Fidem largiturus fuerat.

TERTIUS & postremus gradus Universalis Vocationis est, quod DEUS vult, ut Credentes omnes in fide ad finem perseverent, & sic salventur. Confirmat hoc rursum Scriptura dilucidissime.

Phil. 1, 6. Qui cepit in vobis opus bonum, perficiet usq; ad diem JESU CHRISTI.

1. Cor. 1, 8. CHRISTUS confirmabit vos usq; in finem irreprehensibiles, in diem adventus sui.

1. Thess. 5, 23. & 24. Ipse DEUS pacis sanctificet vos per omnia: ut integer sit Spiritus vester: & anima & Corpus irreprehensibiles, in adventu Domini nostri JESU CHRISTI servetur: Fidelis est, qui vocavit vos: qui etiam faciet. Sed de perseverantiâ hac infra suo loco pluribus agendum nobis erit.

Et talis quidem respectu suarum partium est Antecedens DEI Voluntas, eaq́; constans, æterna & immutabilis, quâ ille salutem generis humani prosequitur, misericordissima scilicet, ita ut in eâ ad summam dilectionem nihil quicquam desiderari possit.


### VI. Special Controversy, On the Quality, or Conditions and attributes of the Antecedent Will in God

Concerning the antecedent Will of GOD, it is also asked and debated today what kind it is, whether it is obscure and hidden: whether it is mutable: whether it is serious: whether it behaves equally toward the whole human race. And certainly, unless there is sufficient certainty about these conditions or attributes of the Antecedent Will of GOD, the whole dispute concerning Predestination becomes more obscure. Therefore, concerning each attribute separately.

And first indeed, the Scriptures themselves testify that this Will of GOD is not occult, not hidden, but revealed, open, clear, and manifest in the Scriptures. This assertion is opposed to the error of the Sacramentarians, by which they are accustomed to viciously name the Will of Good Pleasure instead of an occult and hidden Will, and with which they fight even today. And indeed, it does not escape us at all that in the Scriptures, according to the surface of the letter, some hidden Will of GOD is hinted at: as when the Apostle in Rom. 16:25, Eph. 1:9, Eph. 3:9 makes mention of a Mystery kept secret for eternal times: Likewise of the Mystery of the Will of GOD, and indeed of a mystery hidden by GOD from eternity. And hardly anyone would deny that it is a great mystery of godliness that God was manifest in the flesh, that is, that for his immense mercy God asserted the lost human race to salvation again: indeed, this mystery was and is such that, as the same Apostle testifies in Col. 1:26, it had been hidden from ages and generations, except that the Fathers of the Old Testament received a taste and a certain shadow of this light. But nothing at all is lost from our assertion thereby. For the same Apostle, in the places already cited, immediately adds in express words that the preaching of the Gospel is the revelation of that very mystery which had been kept secret from eternal times: Rom. 16:25. And that that Mystery of the divine Will concerning the salvation of men has been revealed to us, and is now manifest to the Saints, Eph. 1:9, Col. 1:26. And that the grace which was given to us in Christ before eternal times is now manifest through the appearing of our Savior JESUS CHRIST, 2 Tim. 1:9 & 10. Whence, for the confirmation of our thesis, we conclude invincibly: 1. That that arcane Will, once as it were hidden in GOD, has now been revealed to us through Christ in the Gospel, and so manifest to the whole world that it can no longer be called, nor ought to be called, arcane. 2. That no decree of the Will of GOD concerning our salvation is hidden at all: But whatever GOD from eternity willed, decreed, proposed, and defined concerning our salvation, which indeed concerns its Substance, Causes, parts, means, and other things of that kind, that rather every counsel of GOD is known to us. Known, however, not by nature or by the sharpness of our reason, which does not attain even the smallest part of this mystery hidden in GOD; for no one has ever seen GOD, John 1:18. But known by the benefit of evangelical revelation. For Christ, the son of GOD, who is in the bosom of the father, and who looks into the innermost recesses of the heart and of the councils in the same, he has declared it, John 1:18. The sum of which declaration is thus comprehended by the same: This is the Will of him who sent me, that everyone who sees the Son and believes in him may have eternal life, John 6:40. When the Apostle had preached this sum of the Gospel to his Ephesians, he does not hesitate to affirm that he had kept nothing in secret, but had announced to them the WHOLE counsel of GOD, Acts 20:27, and that he had spoken that wisdom of GOD which had lain hidden in a mystery, and which GOD had foreordained before the ages for our glory, 1 Cor. 2:7. Therefore, he must be impious who would want to invent another hidden and plainly contrary will concerning the same matter of salvation for this Will revealed in the Gospel concerning the salvation of men: indeed, it is also monstrously absurd and mendacious. For if there is some occult Will in GOD concerning our salvation, how, I ask, could it become known to the Sacramentarians? Or if it has become known, how can it still be called occult? Thus, this impiety labors under a double lie.

THE OTHER attribute of the Antecedent Will in GOD consists in this, that there is ONE Will in GOD for saving the human race: not double. For besides this revealed Will, there can be no other diverse and arcane Will in GOD for saving men: but just as there is not in GOD except in number One Mercy, by which alone GOD is understood to will the salvation of men: So there is only one Will by which he desires our Salvation to be promoted. And just as there is only one covenant which GOD has disposed among men, eternal: 2 Sam. 23:5, so also there is one and the same salvation which they can possess:

Thus the merciful and benign Will of saving is also nothing but one and the same. And although, as was shown a little before, the account of this Will is one thing, insofar as it was hidden in GOD for many ages from eternity: and another, insofar as it is now the same made manifest to us in the Gospel, yet in respect of substance it is one and the same everywhere, namely that very one which is revealed in the Word of the Gospel. Even if the respect of this very revealed Will is also one thing, if it is considered simply in itself: and another, if it is weighed relatively to an order: yet not even thus does a twofold Will arise in GOD: but it is and remains one in number: but ordered: Whence that twofold respect arises: as will be shown a little later. Therefore it would be both absurd and impious either to posit two contrary Wills in GOD: or to attribute to one and the same Will in number that it wills contrary things at the same time: Which both the Sacramentarians do, under that distinction between the Will of Sign and of Good Pleasure: just as was shown above.

The THIRD attribute of the antecedent Will in GOD consists in this, that just as the Will in GOD concerning the salvation of men is clear: so it is not feigned or simulated: but is most serious, and always constant to itself in all its parts. For seriously and ardently GOD sought from eternity the salvation of all men: seriously and more than seriously He provided for the same in the work of Redemption through the Son: finally, seriously, through the Word of the Gospel He willed the whole world to be converted and saved. The truth of this attribute is made manifest. 1. from the clear testimonies of Scripture, repeated several times hitherto: 1 Tim. 2, 4. 2 Pet. 3, 9. Matt. 23, 37. Ezek. 18, 32. Then the same is evident from the deposit of an Oath, a most religious attestation of the fact. Ezek. 33, 11. I live, says GOD, I do not desire the death of the wicked, but that he may be converted and live. Now if according to that of the Epistle to the Hebrews ch. 6, 16. Among men every controversy is terminated, if the confirmation of an Oath is added; surely we shall give faith to GOD without any doubt or hesitation, who, when He wished to show abundantly the immutable constancy of His Counsel concerning saving men, interposed an Oath: so that through two immutable things, by which it is impossible for GOD to lie, we might have firm consolation, as the author of the same Epistle speaks memorably in the same place. Finally, this becomes manifest by the Signs of wrath, indignation, sorrow, and tears, with which GOD pursued human hardness or stubbornness, as often as no place was left for His fatherly Will: as Jer. 8, 12. For the contrition of the daughter of my people I am contrite, and saddened, stupor has taken hold of me: And Luke 19, 41. with profuse tears He pursues the impenitence of the perishing Jerusalemites. To all of which things, both said and indicated, to affix simulation or deceit, and that a good and licit one (as the Calvinists blasphemously write), no one can do without extreme impiety.

Nor does that Oracle of GOD asserting, I will have mercy on whom I have mercy, and I will have compassion on whom I have compassion, imply anything different; Exod. 33, 19. Rom. 9, 15. For GOD did not distinguish between those to be pitied, as if He did not wish to deem all worthy of His mercy: and thus He Himself excludes some from His mercy. For this would simply fight against that Apostolic Aphorism, Rom. 11, 32. GOD concluded all under unbelief, that He might have mercy on ALL, but by this GOD wished to testify 1. that He truly and from the heart cares for the miserable, all of whom He may pity: 2. that He is moved not out of respect for human merits and axioms, but by His own mere and most free Will, so that He may pity mortals.

The FOURTH attribute of this Will is placed in this, that it is not either alternated, or distinguished by contrary decrees in respect of believers and non-believers: but is simple, indistinct, and therefore universal, nay most universally universal. For by that antecedent will of love and Mercy in GOD, not even one individual from the whole human race, not even that son of perdition excepted John 17, 12, was neglected or passed over. The effect of this attribute is that GOD sought the salvation of all mortals: that He destined His Son as Redeemer to the whole world equally: that He willed these benefits to be offered to all indiscriminately, even to those who in actual fact do not hear this Word, do not actually believe, are not actually saved: nay even to those whom GOD had known would not hear the Word, would never believe, would never even be saved. Therefore to feign or constitute particularity, or any decree of judgment or reprobation, in this antecedent Will of GOD, would be clearly wicked and impious.

The FIFTH and last attribute consists in this, that this antecedent Will of GOD is not absolute, or clearly indeterminate, or unlimited, or ἄτακτος: but ordered, that is, founded in CHRIST, and circumscribed by the order of means. For GOD never induced His mind to save any mortal without respect to CHRIST, and indeed CHRIST apprehended by faith: much less did He ever will indiscriminately and indifferently that all be saved whether they believe or not: Such an absolute respect Huberus feigns and dreams of: but just as we are held to be chosen in CHRIST before the foundation of the world: So this Will of saving in GOD is by no means to be separated from the respect of CHRIST and faith. For when we say CHRIST, we understand not only His merit, and the universal ransom for the sins of the world: but we include also the faith itself, by which the merit of CHRIST is apprehended, at the same time. For without faith CHRIST is clearly idle and useless to us. Just as therefore according to this antecedent Will GOD willed the whole human race to be saved: so also He willed that by the same whole human race faith should be placed in Christ, on account of whom, and in whom we have been chosen, and as the Apostle speaks, He willed that there be a coming to the acknowledgment of the truth. And just as it is false and erroneous if it be said that GOD wills all men to be saved, whether they arrive at the acknowledgment of the truth or not: so it is also impious and heretical to teach that GOD from eternity wills all men to be saved in Christ, whether they believe in Him or do not believe. From which it necessarily follows that Faith in Christ can in no way be eliminated or excluded from this antecedent Will of GOD, unless one wishes to completely overturn and weaken the τάξιν itself or the order of divine Election. But least of all does the evasion of Huber have a place here, who dreams that the respect of faith only then comes into consideration when at length in time it is believed, and the application of the merit of Christ and of divine grace is made. For the respect of faith pertains properly to the very integrity of the τάξεως or order, and thus to the consideration of the whole doctrine concerning the counsel of GOD and the good pleasure of saving men. For just as it pleased GOD that the human race be saved and redeemed through Christ: so He willed that the merit of Christ also be apprehended by faith. For GOD did not will the end only without the means: but He willed the end together with the means, or rather He willed the end through the means.

Nor indeed does anything depart from universality in this antecedent Will of GOD: but that very universality is accommodated only to the τάξιν of the means, by which it indeed pleased GOD to save the whole human race: but yet not ἀψύκτως to save them: but by a certain order and respect of means. Therefore the same GOD, who by this Antecedent will wills all to be saved: wills also that all hear the Word, conceive faith from it, and thus be saved through faith. But let this shine forth more clearly from the next subsequent controversy.

But it is to be observed in this place as if ἐν παρόδῳ: 1. That this Antecedent Will of GOD, such as we have defined it thus far by parts and attributes, is for the most part called in the Scriptures the Love of GOD. 2. That some otherwise Orthodox Theologians, before the Huber controversy was stirred up, attending to this universal Love of GOD, also established universal Election: taking the occasion from the Disputations of the Sacramentarians, who accepted both Election and Love in equal breadth and signification, and established both as absolutely particular. Thus, therefore, in the disputatious forum, where we are sometimes accustomed to use the Terms of the adversary party less properly, those Theologians deserved pardon. But if the more accurate account of the truth according to the Scriptures be attended to, it is clearly evident that they used the term Election improperly and καταχρηστικῶς: because there is a very great discrepancy between the Love and the Election of GOD, both as to the breadth of each, and as to the nature of the thing itself: as will be shown below expressly, where there will be a future disputation for us expressly concerning the particular decree of Election. Let it suffice at least to have noted and observed this in this place, that by this Antecedent Will Election is not so much completed, as it is not one part, but constitutes the whole itself. What? That this Love of GOD, or universal Antecedent Will, precedes Election: the contrary of which is accustomed to happen in human Election. The reason is: Because our love presupposes a thing to be good and lovable: but does not make it such: and therefore election must precede, so that love may come to be. But in GOD this Antecedent Love makes a thing lovable and acceptable, but does not presuppose it. Therefore there is no need for Election to precede. GOD therefore indeed willed, according to this antecedent will of mercy and Love, to save all men, and that they, having been brought to the acknowledgment and faith of Christ, should live eternally. But because the same GOD saw that not all would believe the Gospel: but that the greatest part would repudiate the offered benefits with foul ingratitude: it pleased Him by a Subsequent Will, that however much all the means of salvation were equally exposed, yet only those believing, and finally persevering in faith, should be elected, and eternally saved.

Latin:

DE Voluntate DEI antecedente quæritur etiam, & controvertitur hodiè, qualis ea sit, nùm ea sit obscura & abscondita: an mutabilis: an seria: an ex æquo erga totum genus humanum se habeat. Et sanè de his sive conditionibus, sive attributis Voluntatis DEI Antecedentis nisi satis constet, tota Prædestinationis disputatio evadit obscurior. Ergò de singulis attributis seorsim.

Ac primùm quidem Voluntatem hanc DEI, non occultam, non absconditam, sed in Scripturis revelatam, apertam, perspicuam ac manifestam esse, Scripturæ ipsæ testantur. Opposita est hæc assertio Sacramentariorum errori, quo pro occultâ & absconditâ Voluntate, quam Voluntatem Beneplaciti vitiosè nominare solent, hodieque pugnant. Et sanè nos minimè latet, in Scripturis secundum superficiem literæ, absconditam aliquam Voluntatem DEI subinnui: ut quando Apostolus Rom. 16, 25. Ephes. 1, 9. Ephes. 3, 9. mentionem facit Mysterij temporibus æternis taciti: Item Mysterij Voluntatis DEI, & mysterij quidem à DEO ab æterno absconditi. Et vix quisquam inficias iverit, magnum esse pietatis mysterium, quòd Deus manifestatus est in carne, hoc est, pro immensâ suâ misericordiâ perditum genus humanum ad salutem rursus Deus asseruit: imò tale hoc fuit & est mysterium, ut eodem Apostolo teste, Coloss. 1, 26. à seculis & generationibus esset absconditum nisi quod gustum, & umbram quandam huj9 lucis acceperunt Patres Veteris Testamenti. Verùm nihil quicquam indè assertioni nostræ decedit. Nam idem Apostolus locis jam citatis disertis verbis statim subjicit, Prædicationem Evangelij esse revelationem illius ipsius mysterij, quod à temporibus æternis fuerit tacitum: Rom. 16, 25. Et Mysterium illud Voluntatis divinæ, de salute hominum nobis revelatum, & nunc manifestum esse Sanctis Ephes. 1, 9. Coloss. 1, 26. Et gratiam eam, quæ data nobis est in Christo ante tempora seculatia, jam per apparitionem Servatoris nostri JEsU CHRISTI manifestam esse 2. Tim. 1, 9. & 10. Undè pro confirmatione theseωs nostræ invictè colligimus: 1. Voluntatem illam arcanam, & in DEO quondam quasi absconditam, jàm per Christuin in Evangelio nobis revelatam esse, & toti mundo ita manifestatam, ut arcana illa ampliùs dici nec possit nec debeat. 2. Nullum prorsus decretum Voluntatis DEI de salute nostrâ esse absconditum: Sed quicquid DEUS ab æterno voluit, decrevit, proposuit, ac definivit de salute nostrâ, quod quidem ejus Substantiam, Causas, partes, media & id genus alia concernit, quin notum potiùs sit nobis omne consilium DEI. Notum autem non naturâ, aut rationis nostræ acumine, quod mysterij istius in DEO absconditi partem ne minimam quidem assequitur; DEUM enim nemo vidit unquàm Johann. 1, 18. Sed notum beneficio revelationis Evangelicæ. Christus enim DEI filius, qui est in sinu patris, & intimos cordis & conciliorum recessus in eodem introspicit, is enarravit Joh. 1, 18. Cujus enarrationis summa sic ab eodem comprehenditur: Hæc est Voluntas ejus, qui misit me, ut omnis qui videt Filium, & credit in eum, habeat Vitam æternam, Joh. 6, 40. Hanc summam Evangelij cùm suis Ephesijs prædicasfet Apostolus, non dubitat affirmare, se nihil in arcano retinuisse, quin ipsis OMNE consilium DEI annunciaverit. Actor. 20, 27. quin se locutum esse illam DEI sapientiam, quæ in mysterio latuerat, & quam præfinierat DEUS ante secula in gloriam nostram. 1. Corinth. 2, 7. Impium ergò eum esse oporteat, qui Voluntati huic in Evangelio revelatæ de salute hominum aliam absconditam, planeque contrariam de eodem salutis negotio comminisci velit: imò monstrosè etiam absurdum & mendacem. Si enim occulta est aliqua in DEO de salute nostrâ Voluntas, quomodo quæso ea Sacramentarijs innotescere potuit? Vel si innotuit, quomodo occulta ampliùs dici poterit: Sic gemino mendacio impietas isthæc laborat.

ALTERUM Voluntatis in DEO Antecedentis attributum in eo consistit, quod UNA est in DEO de salvando genere humano Voluntas: non gemina. Nam præter hanc revelatam, dari alia diversa atque arcana in DEO Voluntas de salvandis hominibus planè nulla potest: sed uti in DEO non est nisi numero Una Misericordia, quâ solâ hominum salutem DEUS velle intelligitur: Ita Voluntas non est nisi una, quâ nostram Salutem promotam cupit. Et ut unum duntaxat fœdus est, quod inter homines disposuit DEUS sempiternum: 2. Sam. 23, 5. Salus item una atque eadem, quâ illi potiri possunt:

Ita Voluntas etiam clemens & benigna falvandi non est nisi una atq; eadem. Et quanquam, uti paulò antè ostensum, alia est ratio Voluntatis hujus, quatenus ab æterno in DEO plurimis seculis fuit abscondita: alia, quatenùs nunc est eadem in Evangelio nobis patefacta, tamen substantiæ ratione una utrobiq; est atq; eadem, nimirum illa ipsa, quæ in Verbo Evangelij revelata est. Etsi quoq; hujus ipsius revelatæ Voluntatis respectus alius est, si in se simpliciter consideretur: alius, si ad ordinem relatè expendatur: tamen ne sic quidem gemina in DEO oritur Voluntas: sed una est & manet numero: sed ordinata: Undè geminus ille respect⁹ oritur: uti paulò post ostendetur. Utrumq; ergò absurdum & impium fuerit, vel duas in DEO contrarias Voluntates statuere: vel uni numero eidemq; Voluntati, quod contraria simul velit, tribuere: Quod utrumq; faciunt Sacramentarij, sub distinctione illâ inter Voluntatem Signi & Beneplaciti: quemadmodum suprà ostensum.

TERTIUM Voluntatis in DEO Antecedentis attributum in eo consistit, quòd uti perspicua est in DEO de Salute hominum Voluntas: ita non ficta aut simulata: sed maximè seria est, fibiq; semper in omnibus suis partibus constans. Seriò enim atq; ardenter hominum omnium Salutem DEUS ab æterno expetijt: seriò & plusquam seriò eandem in Redemtionis opere per Filium curavit: seriò deniq;, per Verbum Evangelij totum mundum converti & salvari voluit. Patescit attributi hujus Veritas. 1. ex perspicuis Scripturæ testimonijs, aliquoties hactenùs repetitis: 1. Tim. 2, 4. 2. Petr. 3, 9. Matt. 23, 37. Ezech. 18, 32. Deindè liquet idem ex Juramenti deposito, religiosissimâ attestatione facti. Ezech. 33, 11. Vivo ego DEUS, nolo mortem impij, sed ut convertatur & vivat. Jam si secundum illud Epistolæ ad Hebræos cap 6, 16. Inter Homines omnis Controversia terminatur, si accedat Juramenti confirmatio; utiq; DEO fidem sine dubitatione sive hæsitatione ullâ adhibebimus, qui, cum abundanter ostendere vellet immutabilem Consilij de salvandis hominibus constantiam, Juramentum interposuit: ut sic per duas res immutabiles, quibus impossibile est mentiri DEUM, firmam consolationem haberemus, ut ibidem memorabiliter ejusdem Epistolæ autor loquitur. Tandem manifestum hoc fit Signis iræ, indignationis, doloris, lachrymarum, quibus humanam duritiem sive pervicaciam prosecutus est DEUS, quoties Voluntati suæ paternæ locus non fuit relictus: ut Jerem. 8, 12. Super Contritione filiæ populi mei contritus sum, & contristatus, stupor obtinuit me: Et Luc. 19, 41. profusis lachrymis impœnitentiam Hierosolymitanorum pereuntium prosequitur. Quibus omnibus tùm dictis, tùm indicijs simulationem sive dolum, eumque bonum & licitum (uti Calviniani blasphemè scriptitant) affingere, sine extremâ impietate nemo quisquam potest.

Neq; diversum quid innuit Oraculum illud DEI asseverantis, Misereor, cujus misereor, & commiseror, quem commiseror; Exod 33, 19. Rom 9, 15. Neq; enim inter miserandos distinxit DEUS, quasi non omnes sua misericordia dignari velit: & sic ipsemet a sua misericordia quosdam excludat. Hoc enim simpliciter pugnaret cum Aphorismo illo Apostolico, Rom. 11, 32. Conclusit DEUS omnia sub incredulitate, ut OMNIUM misereretur, sed hoc testatu voluit DEUS 1. se vere atq; ex animo curare miseros, quorum misereatur omnium: 2. non pro humanorum meritorum atq; axiomatum respectu, sed mera, eaq; liberrima sua Voluntate se moveri, ut mortalium misereatur.

QUARTUM attributum Voluntatis hujus in eo positum est, quod ea non vel alternata, vel respectu credentium & non credentium, decretis contrarijs discreta: sed simplex est, indistincta, ac proinde universalis, imo universalissime universalis. Nam voluntate ista antecedente dilectionis & Misericordiae in DEO, ne unum quidem individuum ex toto genere humano, ne quidem filio illo perditionis excepto Johann. 17, 12. neglectus est aut praeteritus. Attributi hujus effectus est ille, quod DEUS omnium mortalium salutem expetijt: quod Filium suum universo mundo Redemtorem aequaliter destinavit: quod beneficia ista omnibus promiscue offerri voluit, etiam his, qui actu ipso Verbum hoc non audiunt, actu non credunt, actu non servantur: imo his etiam, quos sciverat DEUS Verbum non audituros, nunquam credituros, nunquam etiam salvandos esse. Particularitatem ergo, vel decretum ullum judicij aut reprobationis, in hac antecedenti DEI Voluntate fingere aut constituere, nefas plane atque impium fuerit.

QUINTUM & postremum attributum in eo consistit, quod Antecedens haec DEI Voluntas non est absoluta, aut plane indeterminata, sive illimitata, aut ἄτακτος: sed ordinata, hoc est, in CHRISTO fundata, & mediorum τάξει circumscripta. Nunquam enim DEUS sine respectu CHRISTI, & CHRISTI quidem fide apprehensi, quenquam mortalium salvare in animum induxit: nedum promiscue ac indifferenter voluit unquam omnes salvari sive credant, sive non: Qualem absolutum respectum fingit & somniat Huberus: sed quemadmodum in CHRISTO electi esse perhibemur ante constitutionem mundi: Ita Voluntas haec salvandi in DEO, a respectu CHRISTI & fidei minime sejungenda est. CHRISTUM enim cum dicimus, non meritum tantum ipsius, & λύτρον pro peccatis mundi universale intelligimus: sed fidem etiam ipsam, qua apprehenditur CHRISTI meritum, simul includimus. Sine fide enim CHRISTUS nobis plane otiosus est atque inutilis. Sicut ergo secundum hanc antecedentem Voluntatem salvari totum genus humanum DEUS voluit: ita quoque voluit ab eodem universo genere humano credi in Christum, propter quem, & in quo electi sumus, & ut Apostolus loquitur, ad agnitionem veritatis veniri voluit. Et sicut salsum atque erroneum est, si dicatur, quod DEUS velit omnes homines salvos, sive ad veritatis agnitionem perveniant, sive non: ita impium etiam & hæreticum est, docere, quòd DEUS ab æterno velit in Christo salvari omnes homines, sive credant in ipsum, sive non credant. Ex quo necessario consequitur, Fidem in Christum ex hâc antecedente DEI Voluntate, eliminari sive excludi nullo modo posse, nisi τάξιν ipsam sive ordinem Electionis divinæ prorsus convellere & labefactare libeat. Minimè omnium autem locum hîc habet Huberi effugium, qui somniat, respectum fidei tunc demùm in considerationem venire, cùm in tempore demùm creditur, & fit applicatio meriti Christi ac gratiæ divinæ. Nam respectus fidei ad ipsam integritatem τάξεως sive ordinis, & sic doctrinæ totius, de consilio DEI & beneplacito salvandi homines consideratio, propriè pertinet. Nam sicut salvari, & per Christum redimi genus humanumDEO placuit: ita fide etiam Christi meritum apprehendi voluit. Non enim finem duntaxat sine medijs voluit DEUS: sed finem voluit unà cum medijs, imò potiùs finem voluit per media.

Neque verò indè quicquam decedit universalitati in hâc antecedente DEI Voluntate: sed ad mediorum duntaxat τάξιν illa ipsa universalitas accommodatur, quâ DEO placuit quidem salvare totum genus humanum: sed non tamen ἀψύκτως salvare: verùm certo mediorum ordine ac respectu. Idem ergò DEUS, qui voluntate hac Antecedente vult omnés salvos: vult etiam, ut omnes audiant Verbum, ex eo fidem concipiant, & sic per fidem salventur. Sed clariùs hoc elucescat ex controversiâ subsequente proximâ.

Est verò hoc loco illud tanquàm ἐν παρόδῳ observandum: 1. Quòd Voluntas hæc DEI Antecedens, qualem quidem hactenus per partes & attributa definivimus, in Scripturis plerumque Dilectio DEI nuncupatur. 2. Quòd nonnulli alioquin Orthodoxi Theologi, ante motam controversiam Huberianam, Dilectionem hanc DEI universalem attendentes, Electionem quoque universalem statuerunt: occasione sumtâ ex Disputationibus Sacramentariorum, qui & Electionem & Dilectionem in pari latitudine & significatione accipiebant, ac utramque absolutè particularem statuebant. Sic ergò in foro disputatorio, ubi adversariæ partis Terminis interdum minùs propriè uti solemus, veniam merebantur isti Theologi. Verùm sic accuratior veritatis ratio secundumScripturas attendatur, impropriè & καταχρηστικῶς Electionis termino ipsos usos fuisse, liquidò constat: propterea quòd inter Dilectionem & Electionem DEI maxima est discrepantia, tùm quoad utriusque latitudinem, tùm quoad rei ipsius quoque naturam : uti infrà ex professo ostendetur, ubi de particulari Electionis decreto, nobis ex professo futura disputatio. Illud saltem hoc loco & annotasse, & observasse sufficiat, Voluntate hâc Antecedente tàm non absolvi Electionem, quàm non pars una, totum ipsum constituit. Quid? quòd Dilectio ha̎c DEI, sive Voluntas Antecedens universalis, præcedit Electionem : cujus contrarium fieri consuevit in Electione humanâ. Ratio est : Quia nostra dilectio præsupponit rem esse bonam & amabilem: non autem facit talem: ideoque præcedere debet electio, ut fiat dilectio.
