Atqui in DEO Dilectio hæc Antecedens facit rem amabilem & acceptam, non verò præsupponit. Ideò Electione præcedente non est opus. Voluit ergò quidem DEUS secundum hanc voluntatem antecedentem misericordiæ & Dilectionis propriam, salvare homines universos, atque ad agnitionem & fidem Christi adductos æternùm vivere, Quia verò vidit idem DEUS, non omnes Evangelio credituros: sed partem maximam fœdâ ingratitudine, beneficia oblata repudiaturum esse : placuit ipsi Voluntate Consequente, ut quantumvis media salutis omnia ex æquo essent exposita, credentes tamen tantùm, & in fide finaliter perseverantes, sint electi, & æternùm salventur.


### VII. Special Controversy, Concerning the Consequent Will of GOD: and the difference of this from the Antecedent

Concerning the Subsequent Will of GOD: and the difference of this from the Antecedent.

Although GOD by His Antecedent Will seriously wills that all should conceive faith through the hearing of the Gospel, by this faith apply to themselves the universal merit of Christ, and thus be saved: Because, however, He foresaw and foreknew that the greatest part of the world would leave no place for the means of salvation: and therefore would not believe in Christ: therefore GOD made a Decree concerning saving only those whom He foresaw would actually believe in Christ: and concerning the remaining unbelievers to be eternally damned, by a decree likewise eternally made, and promulgated in the Scriptures. Whence now arises that other respect of the divine Will, which the Orthodox Church names the SUBSEQUENT Will of GOD: so called for this reason: because although it is of the same eternity as the Antecedent Will: yet it does not revolve in the mind of GOD alone: but also has some respect to men: and by reason of order, it is posterior to the Antecedent. For this Subsequent Will considers, not what can and ought to be done by men: but what is actually done, that is, who by the act itself, and indeed perseveringly, are to believe in Christ, and who are not? Whereupon there immediately and spontaneously emerges a διαίρεσις of the decrees in this divine consequent Will, which stand in relation to each other clearly ἀντιδιῃρημένως: the one of Predestination or Election to life: the other of Judgment and Reprobation to condemnation: neither absolute: but both ordered: the former indeed determined to foreseen persevering faith: the latter truly on account of the contempt and rejection of offered divine grace.

Hence emerges such a definition of the consequent Will, that it is the eternal counsel and decree of GOD, concerning saving only those who believe: but condemning all those, universally, who do not believe. Now if one should ask separately about any decree of this will, what and of what kind that is in the very mind of GOD, we answer from the Scriptures that the decree of Election is such: As I live, says GOD, I will and decree that everyone who believes in Christ, and perseveres in this faith even to the end, shall not perish, but have eternal life.

This decree was set forth by the Savior himself, John 3:16. For GOD so loved the world, that he gave his only begotten Son, that everyone WHO BELIEVES in him, should not perish, but have eternal life.

And Matt. 10:22. He who SHALL HAVE PERSEVERED to the end, shall be saved.

John 6:40. This is the Will of the Father who sent me, that everyone WHO BELIEVES in him should not perish, but have eternal life.

And 1 Cor. 1:21. ἐυδόκησε ὁ θεὸς IT PLEASED GOD through the foolishness of preaching to save THOSE WHO BELIEVE.

Mark 16:16. He who SHALL HAVE BELIEVED, and shall have been baptized, shall be saved.

John 3:18. He who BELIEVES in the Son, is not judged.

The eternal decree of REPROBATION is such: As I live, says GOD, I will and decree that he who does not believe in Christ, but perseveres in infidelity even to the end, shall be condemned: nay, even now, that is, from eternity, he is addicted to damnation.

This decree was set forth by the Savior, John 3:18. He who does not believe, is ALREADY judged.

Mark 16:16. He who shall not have believed, shall be condemned.

Indeed, GOD himself promulgated this Decree, Deut. 18, 18 & 19. I will raise up a Prophet for them (namely CHRIST, as the Apostle interprets, Acts 3, 29) and I will put my Words in his mouth, and he shall speak to them all things that I shall command him: But whoever shall NOT HEAR his Words, which he shall speak in my name, I will be the AVENGER.

And as often as in the Scriptures the good are separated and distinguished from the bad, the faithful from the unfaithful, the elect from the reprobate, those to be saved from those to be damned, so often is the antecedent Will of GOD openly distinguished from this consequent one; nay, rather, the latter is subordinated to the former ἐπαλλήλως (successively): and this twofold decree is set before our eyes more clearly than the splendor of the sun. For example: According to the Antecedent Will it was said by the Apostle, GOD wills all men to be saved: 1 Tim. 2, 4. According to the Consequent it was written by the same: It pleased GOD to save those who believe: 1 Cor. 1, 21. According to the Antecedent, Christ said: Come to me all you who labor and are burdened; Matt. 11, 28. According to the Consequent, the same said that on the last day it would be pronounced, Come you blessed of my Father: and, Depart from me you cursed into eternal fire. Matt. 25, 34, & 41. According to the Antecedent, GOD confirms with an oath, As I live, I do not desire the death of the sinner: Ezek. 33, 11. According to the Consequent, Christ pronounces: This is the will of him who sent me, that everyone who sees the Son, and believes in him, may have eternal life. John 6, 39. According to the Antecedent Will, he calls all to the great Supper, Luke 14, 16. According to the Consequent, it is said that of those who had indeed been invited, but did not appear, none shall taste of the great Supper: but that few are chosen. Matt. 22, 14. chap. 20, 16.

Nor, however, is each said to be opposite or contradictory: but merely subordinate and subaltern, so that no destruction or overthrow of either is made by the other: which becomes plain from the mutual differences and respects of these two wills: what these are, we shall show in a few words.

The Consequent Will therefore differs first from the Antecedent in the Determination of the Object. For the Antecedent Will embraces the whole human race simply, by offering to it the means of salvation. The Consequent Will respects the condition and distinction of men, insofar as they, by conforming themselves to the universal counsel of GOD, either believe in Christ through obedience: or do not believe through contumacy.

Then by the relation of Opposition. For the Antecedent Will has no opposite decree of Reprobation: but the Consequent is indeed distinguished by two different, and ἀντιδιῃρημένως (distinctly) opposed, decrees of Salvation and Damnation.

Thirdly, by the species of the act. For the Antecedent Will, by regarding the misery of men, effectively disposes and ordains the means of salvation to bring about restoration: but the Consequent Will destines believers to salvation: it consigns those who do not believe to damnation.

Finally, by the consideration of faith. For in the προηγουμένῃ (antecedent) Will, Faith is attended to as a part of the order which GOD, as far as it lies in himself, desires to be observed. In the ἑπομένῃ (consequent) Will, the same is attended to, not only in this way, by which GOD desires his order to be observed by men: but insofar as that order is in the very act either observed by believing, or not observed by not believing: Which, although it happens in time by reason of men: yet to GOD, by reason of his foreknowledge, it was most present, since to him, by the nature of eternity, nothing is future, but in the most simple τῷ νῦν (now) all things are most present from eternity. In respect of this last difference, the Consequent Will always attains its end, either to salvation or to damnation: but the Antecedent Will does not.

Latin:

De Voluntate DEI consequente: & hujus ab Antecedente, differentiâ.

ETsi DEUS Antecedente Voluntate seriò vult, ut omnes per auditum Evangelij fidem concipiant, fide hâc universale Christi meritum sibi applicent, & sic salventur: Quia tamen prævidit ac præscivit maximam mundi partem, medijs salutis locum minimè relicturam: ac proindè in Christum non credituram : ideo DEUS de illis tantùm salvandis fecit Decretum, quos actu in Christum credituros prævidit: de reliquis verò incredulis æternùm damnandis itidem æterno facto, & in Scripturis promulgato Decreto. Undè jam oritur alter ille Voluntatis divinæ respectus, quem Ecclesia Orthodoxa nominat Voluntatem DEI CONSEQUENTEM: ideò sic dictam : quia etsi cum Voluntate Antecedente ejusdem est æternitatis: tamen non in solâ DEI mente vertitur: sed ad homines etiam aliquem respectum habet : & ratione ordinis, Antecedente est posterior. Considerat enim Consequens hæc Voluntas, non quid ab hominibus fieri & possit & debeat: sed quid actu ipso fiat, hoc est, quinám ipso actu, & quidem perseveranter in Christum sint credituri, qui non? Ubi mox ultrò emergit διαίρεσις decretorum in divinâ hac Voluntate consequente, quæ se habent planè ἀντιδιῃρημένως : Unum Prædestinationis sive Electionis ad vitam : alterum Judicij & Reprobationis ad condemnationem : neutrum absolutum : sed utrumque ordinatum : Illud quidem determinatum ad prævisam fidem perseverantem : Hoc verò propter contemtum & repudiationem oblatæ gratiæ divinæ.

Emergit hinc Voluntatis consequentis Definitio talis, Quòd sit consilium & decretum DEI æternum, de salvandis solis credentibus : damnandis autem, qui non credunt, in universum omnibus. Jam si seorsim de quolibet voluntatis hujus Decreto quæratur, Quodnám & Quale illud sit in ipsâ mente DEI, Respondemus ex Scripturis, Electionis Decretum esse tale : Vivo ego DEUS, volo & decerno, ut omnis, qui credit in Christum, inque fide hac ad finem usque perseverat, non pereat, sed habeat vitam æternam.

Proditum est hoc Decretum ab ipso Servatore, Johan. 3, 16. Sic DEUS dilexit mundum, ut Filium suum unigenitum daret, ut omnis QUI CREDIT in eum, non pereat, sed habeat vitam æternam.

Et Matth. 10, 22. Qui PERSEVERAVERIT ad finem usq́, salvabitur.

Johan. 6, 40. Hæc est Voluntas ejus, qui misit me Patris, ut omnis, QUI CREDIT in eum non pereat, sed habeat vitam æternam.

Et 1. Cor. 1, 21. ἐυδόκησε ὁ θεὸς BENEPLACUIT DEO per stultitiam prædicationis salvare CREDENTES.

Marci 16, 16. Qui CREDIDERIT, & baptizatus fuerit, salvabitur.

Johan. 3, 18. Qui CREDIT in Filium, non judicatur.

REPROBATIONIS æternum Decretum tale est : Vivo ego DEUS, volo & decerno, ut qui in Christum non credit, sed in infidelitate ad finem usque perseverat, condemnetur : imò jam modò, hoc est, ab æterno damnationi sit addictus.

Proditum est hoc decretum à Servatore, Johan. 3, 18. Qui non credit, JAM judicatus est.

Marci 16, 16. Qui non crediderit, condemnabitur.

Quin DEUS ipse Decretum hoc promulgavit Deut. 18, 18. & 19. Prophetam suscitabo eis (CHRISTUM nimirùm, sic interpretante Apostolo, Actor. 3, 29.) & ponam Verba mea in ore ejus, loqueturque ad eos omnia, quæ præcepero illi: Qui autem Verba ejus, quæ loquetur in nomine meo, NON AUDIERIT, EGO ULTOR existam.

Et quotiescunque in Scripturis boni à malis, fideles ab infidelibus, electi à reprobis, salvandi à damnandis separantur & distingvuntur, toties & antecedens DEI Voluntas ab hoc consequente palàm discernitur, imò potiùs hæc illi ἐπαλλήλως substernitur: & geminum hoc decretum Solari splendore clariùs ob oculos constituitur. Exempli gratia : Secundum Voluntatem Antecedentem dictum est ab Apostolo, DEUS vult omnes homines salvos fieri : 1. Tim. 2, 4. Secundum Consequentem scriptum est ab eodem : Placuit DEO salvos facere credentes : 1. Cor. 1, 21. Secundum Antecedentem Christus dixit : Venite ad me omnes, qui laboratis & onerati estis; Matth. 11, 28. SecundumConsequentem idem dixit, in die novissimo pronunciatum iri, Venite benedicti Patris mei : &, Discedite à me maledicti in ignem æternum. Matth. 25, 34, & 41. Secundum Antecedentem juramento confirmat DEUS, Vivo ego, nolo mortem peccatoris : Ezech 33, 11. Secundum Consequentem Christus pronunciat : Hæc est voluntas ejus, qui misit me, ut omnis qui videt Filium, & credit in eum, habeat vitam æternam. Joh. 6, 39. Secundum Voluntatem Antecedentem omnes vocat ad Cænam magnam Luc. 14, 16. Secundum Consequentem dicitur, quòd eorum, qui invitati quidem fuerant, sed non comparuerunt, nullus gustaturus sit Cænam magnam: sed quòdPauci sint electi. Matth. 22, 14. cap. 20, 16.

Neque tamen oppositè utrumque dicitur, aut contradictoriè : sed subordinatè duntaxat, & subalternè, ita ut neutrius per alterum ulla fiat destructio aut eversio: id quod ex mutuis duarum istarum voluntatum differentiis & respectibus, planum evadit : Qui quales sint, paucis ostendemus.

Differt ergò primùm Voluntas Consequens ab Antecedente, Determinatione Objecti. Antecedens enim Voluntas totum genus humanum simpliciter complectitur, offerendo illi salutis media. Consequens Voluntas conditionem & discrimen hominum respicit, quatenùs nimirùm illi sese consilio DEI universali attemperando, vel per obedientiam in Christum credunt: vel per contumaciam non credunt.

Deindè σχέσει Oppositionis. Nam antecedens Voluntas nullum habet oppositum decretum Reprobationis : Consequens verò duobus diversis, & ἀντιδιῃρημένως oppositis, Salvationis & Damnationis decretis, est distincta.

Tertiò, specie actus. Antecedens enim Voluntas miseriam hominum respiciendo, ad restaurationem faciendam, salutis media efficaciter disponit ac ordinat : Consequens autem Voluntas credentes saluti destinat : non credentes damnationi mancipat.

Tandem consideratione fidei. Nam in Voluntate προηγουμένῃ Fides attenditur, tanquam pars ordinis, quem DEUS, quantum quidem in se est, observatum cupit. In Voluntate ἑπομένῃ eadem attenditur, non hoc solùm modo, quo DEUS ordinem suum ab hominibus observatum cupit: sed quatenùs ordo iste actu ipso vel observatur credendo, vel non observatur, non credendo : Quod licèt ratione hominum in tempore demùm fiat : DEO tamen præscientiæ ratione fuit præsentissimum, quippè cui per naturam æternitatis, nihil est futurum, sed in simplicissimo τῷ νῦν omnia ab æterno sunt præsentissima. Ultimæ hujus differentiæ respectu, Voluntas consequens, finem suum semper assequitur, vel ad salutem, vel ad damnationem: Voluntas verò Antecedens non item.


### VII. Special Controversy, Concerning the Consequent Will of GOD: and the difference of this from the Antecedent: VIII. Special Controversy, Concerning the eternal decree of Election, its own proper nature and affection

VIII. Special Controversy, Concerning the eternal decree of Election, its own proper nature and affection.

Here at last we enter the very abyss of eternal Predestination, consisting of a very broad complexity of matters and most abstruse questions: in which, to be duly searched out according to the Canon of the Scriptures, we shall observe such a Method that we may descend from more general Questions to more special ones.

Question I. Whether the eternal Election of those to be saved is to be placed in the Antecedent Will, or the Consequent?

Concerning this question, a crossroads of opinions offers itself, some leaning too much to the right, others further to the left, both deviating from the path of truth: though in a different way, respect, and end. For those who follow the party of Calvin maintain that the decree of Election must be sought in the Antecedent Will of GOD alone, but in such a way that they elicit from thence both that absolute and particular Will, and indeed also the absolute Election of a few men. Huber, however, likewise establishes Election in the Antecedent Will alone, which will, although he rightly argues against the Calvinists that it is universal, he nevertheless wrongly and falsely builds from it against the Orthodox an election that is universal and entirely unlimited. Therefore, just as Calvin removes and eliminates every respect of faith, so Huber removes and eliminates the very act of faith from the eternal decree of Election. Both of these errors, discordant with the analogy of faith, fail in this, that they completely separate Election from every consideration of justice imputed through faith on account of Christ. By which pact, indeed, it would be lawful to conclude no election at all, rather than either an absolute election of a few or a universal election of all. For the name of the Elect is nowhere in the whole of Scripture attributed except to those who actually believe and who persevere finally in faith. Furthermore, even the very sound of the words Election and Elect, and their proper affection, implies and proves some distinction or discrepancy in respect of men. For the Elect are called from a distinction of those who are not Elect: but now, that some distinction between men is established in the Antecedent Will, piety itself and the Christian faith deny. Therefore, making a divorce from both of these errors, the Orthodox Church places Election not in the sole and merely naked Antecedent Will of GOD, but rather in the Consequent. The reason for the affirmation is this: Because the holy Scripture pronounces only those to be elected and predestined to eternal life who actually believe in the name of the only-begotten Son of GOD, or at least are about to believe: but not those whom GOD wills to be saved by an absolute will without respect to faith: nor even all those whom GOD indeed wills by an antecedent will to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth: who nevertheless do not by the act itself come to the knowledge of the truth, and therefore also are never saved. Furthermore, if that antecedent will were the same as Election, it would certainly be necessary that these things be convertible with one another. But they are not: For GOD indeed wills all those to be saved, as many as are in the number of the Elect: but not vice versa: Whosoever GOD wills to be saved, they are the elect. For many are called, whom indeed GOD wills to be saved: but few are chosen. Finally, the Antecedent Will of GOD looks at the salvation of men nakedly, without consideration of whether they actually believe or not: but Election or Predestination implies also the order of salvation, and that not in part, but in whole, and consequently, the very act of faith. Therefore, from the Consequent will, the Election of those to be saved ought to be sought and defined.

Latin:

IIX. Controversia Specialis, De æterno Electionis decreto, ejusΰ propriâ naturâ & affectione.

HIc demùm ipsam Prædestinationis æternæ abyssum ingredimur, rerum & quæstionum abstrusissimarum latissimo complexu constantem: in quâ secundum Scripturarum Canonem ritè perscrutanda, eam observabimus Methodum, ut à Quæstionibus generalioribus ad magis speciales descendamus.

Quæstio. I. An æterna salvandorum Electio ponenda sit in Voluntate Antecedente, an Consequente?

CIrca hanc quæstionem, bivium sententiarum se offert, nonnullis ad dextram nimis, alijs ad sinistram longiùs, utrisque à veritatis tramite deflectentibus: diverso licèt modo, respectu, ac fine. Calvini enim partes qui sequuntur, Electionis decretum in solâ antecedente DEI Voluntate quærendum esse autumant, sed ita, ut & Voluntatem illam absolutam ac particularem, & verò absolutam quoque paucorum hominum Electionem indè eliciant. Huberus autem in solâ itidem Antecedente Voluntate Electionem constituit, quam voluntatem licèt rectè contra Calvinianos universalem esse pugnet, malè tamen & falsò indè contra Orthodoxos, Electionem universalem & prorsus illimitatam extruit. Quemadmodum ergò Calvinus omnem fidei respectum: ita Huberus ipsum actum fidei ab æterno Electionis decreto removet & eliminat. Uterque iste error, ab analogiâ fidei absonus, in eo deficit, quòd Electionem ab omni consideratione justitiæ, per fidem propter Christum imputatæ, penitùs sejungit. Quod sanè pacto, nullam potiùs omninò, quàm vel absolutam paucorum, vel universalem omnium Electionem, fas esset colligere. Nomen enim Electorum in universâ Scripturâ nuspiam nisi solis actu credentibus, & in fide finaliter perseverantibus attribuitur. Deindè vel ipse vocabulorum Electionis & Electorum sonus, & propria affectio discrimen aliquod aut discrepantiam, ratione hominum innuit & evincit. Nam Electi vocantur ex discrimine non Electorum: Jam verò in Antecedente Voluntate discrimen aliquod inter homines ut constituatur, pietas ipsa fidesque Christiana perhibent. Ergò ab utroque isto errore divortium faciens Orthodoxa Ecclesia, Electionem non in solâ atquè nudâ duntaxat Antecedente DEI Voluntate: sed in consequente potiùs collocat. Ratio affirmati est hæc: Quia Scriptura sacra solos eos ad vitam æternam electos ac prædestinatos esse pronunciat, qui in nomen unigeniti Filij DEI, actu ipso credunt, aut credituri saltem sunt: non autem eos, quos absolutâ voluntate citra respectum fidei salvos velit DEUS: neque eos etiam omnes, quos velit quidem DEUS antecedente voluntate salvos fieri, & ad agnitionem veritatis pervenire: qui tamen ipso actu non perveniant ad agnitionem veritatis, ac proindè nec nunquàm etiam salventur. Deindè, si voluntas illa antecedens cum Electione idem esset, utique convertibilia ista inter sese esse, necessum foret. At non sunt: Vult enim quidem DEUS omnes eos salvatos, quotquot sunt in numero Electorum: sed non vice versâ: Quoscunque DEUS salvatos vult, illi sunt electi. Multi enim sunt vocati, quos utique DEUS salvos vult: sed pauci sunt electi. Tandem Voluntas DEI Antecedens salutem hominum nudè respicit, sine consideratione, nùm actu ipso credant nec ne: Electio verò sive Prædestinatio, ordinem etiam salutis, eumque non ex parte, sed ex toto, ac per consequens, ipsum actum fidei implicat. Ex voluntate ergò consequente Electio salvandorum peti ac definiri debet.


### VII. Special Controversy, Concerning the Consequent Will of GOD: and the difference of this from the Antecedent: Question II. Whether some decree of Reprobation is also to be placed in the Will of GOD?

Question II. Whether some decree of Reprobation is also to be placed in the Will of GOD?

We hold the affirmative against Huber and his accomplices, following the oracles of the Scriptures, intrepidly. For from what has already been said, it is clearly evident that GOD by His consequent will wills only those who believe to be finally saved; but those who do not believe to be eternally damned: and indeed according to the eternal decree of the divine will: John 3:18. He who does not believe is judged already. Whence the Book of Christian Concord infers quite forcefully thus: Just as GOD in His ETERNAL counsel ordained that the Holy Spirit should call, illuminate, and convert the Elect through the Word: and should justify all those who embrace Christ with true faith, and should bestow eternal salvation upon them: Thus in His SAME (ETERNAL) counsel He decreed that He wills to harden, reprobate, and devote to eternal damnation those who, having been called through the Word, reject it and resist the Holy Spirit (who willed to work effectively in them through the Word and to be effective), and who persist obstinately in that contumacy. And according to these reasons must be understood what Scripture says: Many are called, but few are chosen, Matt. 20, 16 and ch. 22, 14.

But there are also other things which evidently confirm our affirmative; namely, both the immutable justice of GOD and that other part of heavenly doctrine, so that if the doctrine concerning the Reprobation of the incredulous is removed from the Church, it is necessary that the other part of Christian doctrine should perish. For, just as it is of the Mercy in GOD to will that men be saved, but under the condition of faith, so it cannot but be of the eternal justice of GOD that it is proper to Reprobation that as many as contumaciously turn away from the prescribed order and do not believe in Christ are eternally damned. Thus, therefore, the Mercy of GOD concerning our salvation must be asserted in such a way that in the meantime His justice suffers no harm—not some absolute justice, but revealed justice, punishing the contempt of the order of our salvation, established by GOD from eternity.

Furthermore, the Law, that other part of Christian doctrine, is the constant and eternal wisdom in GOD and the rule of justice; teaching what we ought to be and what we ought to do and omit, and at the same time promising eternal life to those who perform obedience, but on the contrary denouncing the penalty of eternal damnation to those who do not obey. Now if it is denied in the Huberian sense that GOD from eternity made a decree of Reprobation concerning the incredulous who are to be damned, what else follows but that the doctrine of the Law is eliminated and proscribed from the Church of GOD with a new Antinomian fury?

Moreover, how this Reprobation stands and how it ought to be vindicated from that Rhadamanthine and absolute Calvinistic decree, that accurate antithesis shows, which in this place ought to be instituted between Election and Reprobation, and between the parts, nature, and proper affection of each. For here too that saying truly holds its place: By contraries placed next to each other, Truth shines forth more clearly.

In the beginning, therefore, regarding the parts of Reprobation, as many of them are most rightly constituted as there are of Election itself; namely, three. For just as in Election three terms or parts offer themselves, namely, first the merciful Will in GOD; then the act of faith and the grace of justification; and finally eternal life: so in Reprobation likewise three occur: 1. The will to punish contumacy, and thus to desert the man. 2. The effect of infidelity, which in some, on account of peculiar sins, is joined with blindness in the mind, with aggravation regarding the hearing, and with induration in the heart and will. 3. Damnation.

Furthermore, the question is asked concerning the nature and truth of Reprobation, what the reason for each may be. Most of the Fathers before Augustine taught: that GOD indeed provides sufficient aids and means for salvation to all men, and as far as it is in Him, does not will that anyone be reprobated; but nevertheless, that man is left in the hand of his own free will, so that if they willed, they could be saved; if they did not will, it was permitted that they should sin, and by the guilt of sin fall into damnation. From which opinion the Efavvitae do not seem to differ much, so that Gregory of Valencia defines Reprobation as an act of the divine intellect by which GOD firmly determines to permit the sins of the reprobate, and on account of them to exclude them from the heavenly kingdom, and to punish them eternally. Tom. 1. of Commentaries on Thomas: disp. 1. q. 23. title concerning Reprobation. point 1. page 579. D. Although these things are not entirely false, yet in this there is a grave error, that this Reprobation is defined not obscurely by the permission of GOD itself; when it should rather be established that this permission is neither Reprobation itself, nor a part of Reprobation, for the reason that permission to sin has a place even in the elect themselves. Those, therefore, whom GOD foresaw would accept the offered grace of faith and justification, and would at least persevere in it finally, these He elected; but those whom He foresaw would reject the same and would persevere in perversity to the end, those He finally reprobated.

Thirdly, the question is asked concerning the cause of Reprobation, about which there is not one opinion of all. This was the doctrine of Augustine: Before the fall, indeed, the Will of GOD concerning the salvation of men was universal, and therefore He instructed the first parents with sufficient grace of free will: But after the fall, from the whole human race, one mass of perdition was made: From which afterwards it pleased GOD to make some vessels for honor, others for dishonor. Regarding the condition of the former state, a cause cannot be given on the part of man: But regarding the latter, it can be assigned, because GOD left those vessels in that mass of theirs. These things being granted, he infers that GOD not only permits that the reprobate can fall into sins, but also denies them that grace without which they cannot be saved: as to infants prevented by death He denies baptism: to infidels He denies the Word and Faith: to Christians believing for a time He denies perseverance. Where, however, he adds a limitation, namely, that this denial is not absolute, but is founded in the cause of original sin, and therefore is most rightly joined with the justice of GOD. Concerning this opinion of Augustine, one may read many things, Epist. 15, 106, 157. And in Enchir. ch. 95, de nat. & grat. ch. 8 & 9, de corrept. & grat. ch. 10, 11, 12, de bono perseverantiæ ch. 8 & 14.

1. Augustine sought the foundations of this doctrine of his from the Scriptures, which according to the surface of the letter seem to assert that sufficient grace of salvation has not been given to all men.

The first passage is cited from chapter 11, 21 of Matthew, in the book On the Good of Perseverance, chapter 14, concerning the Tyrians and Sidonians, who are said to have been about to believe if they had seen those miracles of Christ which had been performed by him in Judea. But since it was not given to them to believe, Augustine infers that even the means by which they might believe was denied to them.

The second passage is sought from John 12, 39, where it is said of the Jews that they could not believe because they were blinded, that is, left in the mass of perdition.

The third is produced from Acts 14, 16, concerning the Gentiles, whom GOD allowed to walk in their own ways.

The fourth from Acts 16, 6 and 7, where Paul and Silas are read to have been forbidden by the Holy Spirit from speaking the Word of God in Asia and Bithynia.

The fifth is the one he urges most: If sufficient grace were given to all, and he who accepted it were saved, and the other not: then man would distinguish himself, contrary to that which is said in 1 Cor. 4, 7: Who distinguishes you?

But the same Augustine also fights with arguments: as when he writes in epistle 105 and On Nature and Grace, chapter 8. Many infants die without Baptism, who not only are not Christians, but cannot even be. Therefore, sufficient grace will be taken away from them. And ibid. chapter 19, concerning an adult who died in that region where the name of Christ could not be heard, he says: If he could have been saved, he would have been saved by the law of nature and free will: thus Christ would have died for him in vain. If he could not be saved without the grace of Christ: therefore he was such, because he could in no way be otherwise.

But Augustine erred gravely in this part, and the arguments produced by him are not of such weight or moment that they can deserve applause in the Church of the Orthodox. For that first passage cited from Matthew proves only that superabundant grace was denied to them, but not sufficient grace. But prodigies and miracles are not even performed today: and yet it is not denied that a sufficient aid for salvation is given in the meantime.

The other passage of John manifestly deals with the punishment of preceding sins, not Original, but Actual. Whence Augustine rightly infers elsewhere, tractate 53 on John: Why could they not believe: I answer quickly, Because they did not want to: for GOD foreknew their evil will. But you ask, the Prophet says another cause, Not of their will: What? Because He gave them a spirit of compunction? But I answer that their will deserved even this: For thus GOD blinds, thus He hardens, by deserting, not indeed by helping. And a little before: Some say, what did the Jews do? or what was their fault, if it was necessary that the word of the Prophet be fulfilled? To whom we answer, that GOD, foreknowing future things, predicted through the Prophet the infidelity of the Jews: but He predicted it, He did not cause it. For He does not therefore compel anyone to sin, because He already knows the future sins of men: For He foreknows their sins, not His own.

the words of John: Behold again, attend to this particle (Because he said) as being not a cause, but an event. For neither did they not believe because Isaiah said it, or because they were not about to believe, therefore he said it. But why did the Evangelist not say it so, but said that incredulity was from prophecy, not prophecy from incredulity? Hence Scripture wishes to demonstrate great certainty, and that it happened no otherwise than it was prophesied. And a little later: They could not believe, that is, they would not believe.

Latin:

Quæstio II. An in Voluntate DEI ponendum etiam sit aliquod Reprobationis decretum?

Affirmativam contra Huberum ejusque complices, secuti Scripturarum oracula, intrepidè tenemus. Nam ex jam dictis liquidò constat, DEUM voluntate consequenti velle tantùm credentes finaliter salvari; non credentes verò æternùm damnari: & quidem secundum æternum voluntatis divinæ decretum: Johan. 3, 18. Qui non credit, jam judicatus est. Undè Liber Christianæ Concordiæ nervosè satis sic infert: Quemadmodum DEUS in ÆTERNO suo consilio ordinavit, ut Spiritus Sanctus Electos per Verbum vocet, illuminet atq́; convertat: atq́; omnes illos, qui Christum verâ fide amplectuntur, justificet, atq́; in eos æternam salutem conferat: Ita in EODEM (ÆTERNO) suo consilio decrevit, quòd eos, qui per Verbum vocati, illud repudiant, & Spiritui Sancto (qui in ipsis per Verbum efficaciter operari, & efficax esse voluit) resistunt, & obstinati in eâ contumaciâ perseverant, indurare, reprobare, & æternæ damnationi devovere velit. Et secundum has rationes intelligendum est, quod Scriptura dicit: Multi sunt vocati, pauci verò electi, Matth. 20, 16. & cap. 22, 14.

Sed sunt & alia, quæ affirmativam nostram evidenter confirmant; nempè tùm immutabilis DEI justitia: tùm pars illa doctrinæ cœlestis altera, ut si ex Ecclesiâ tollatur doctrina de Reprobatione incredulorum, mox altera partem doctrinæ Christianæ perire necessum sit. Nam, quemadmodum Misericordiæ in DEO est, velle homines salvos, sed sub conditione fidei: ita non potest non ex justitiâ DEI æternâ, Reprobationis esse proprium, ut æternùm damnentur, quotquot ordinem præscriptum contumaciter aversantur, & in Christum non credunt. Sic ergò asserenda est Misericordia DEI de salute nostrâ, ut interim nihil damni patiatur ejusdem justitia non absoluta aliqua, sed revelata, puniens contemtum ordinis salvationis nostræ, à DEO ab æterno constituti.

Deindè verò Lex, altera illa doctrinæ Christianæ pars, est constans atquè æterna in DEO sapientia, & justitiæ regula; docens, quales nos esse, quæque facere atque omittere debeamus: simulque promittens vitam æternam præstantibꝙ obedientiam: contra verò non obedientibus æternæ damnationis pœnam denuncians. Jam si negetur sensu Huberiano, DEUM ab æterno fecisse decretum Reprobationis de damnandis incredulis, quid aliud sequitur, quàm quòd doctrina Legis novo furore Antinomico ex Ecclesiâ DEI eliminatur ac proscribitur?

Cæterùm quomodo hæc Reprobatio sese habeat, & à Rhadamantéo illo absolutoquè decreto Calvinistico vindicari debeat, ostendit accurata illa ἀντίθεσις, quæ hoc loco inter Electionē & Reprobationem, ac inter utriusque partes, naturam & propriam affectionem institui debet. Nam & hîc verè locum obtinet illud: Contrarijs juxta se positis, Veritas magis elucescat.

Initiò igitur quoad Reprobationis partes, tot ejus rectissimè constituuntur, quot sunt ipsius Electionis: nempè tres. Nam quemadmodum in Electione tres se offerunt termini sive partes, nempè primò Voluntas in DEO misericors: deindè actus fidei & gratia justificationis: & tandem salus æterna: Ita in Reprobatione itidem tria occurrunt: 1. Voluntas puniendi contumaciam, & sic deserendi hominem. 2. Effectus infidelitatis, qui in nonnullis propter peculiaria delicta, cum excœcatione in mente, cum aggravatione quoad auditum, cum induratione in corde & voluntate est conjunctus. 3. Damnatio.

Deindè verò quæritur de naturâ & veritate Reprobationis, Quænám utriusq́; sit ratio. Plerique Patres ante Augustinum docuerunt: DEUM omnibus quidem hominibus sufficientia ad salutem auxilia & media præstare, nec quantum in ipso est, reprobatum quemquam velle: sed tamen in manu arbitrij sui relictum esse hominem, ut si vellent, salvari possent: si nollent, permissum esse, ut peccarent, peccatique culpâ in damnationem ruerent. A quâ sententiâ non multùm abhorrere videntur Efavvitæ, ita ut Gregorius de Valentia Reprobationem definiat, quòd sit actus divini intellectus, quo DEUS firmiter statuit, reproborum peccata permittere, & propter illa eos à regno cælasti excludere, ac in æternùm punire. Tom. 1. Commentariorum in Thomam: disp. 1. q. 23. tit. de Reprobat. punct 1. pag. 579. D. Quanquàm verò non planè falsa hæc sunt: in eo tamen graviter erratur, Quod Reprobatio hæc definitur haud obscurè per ipsam DEI permissionem: cùm potiùs statuendum sit, quòd permissio hæc neque est Reprobatio ipsa, neque pars Reprobationis: propterea quòd Permissio ad peccandum, in electis etiam ipsis locum habet. Quos ergò prævidit DEUS gratiam oblatam fidei & justificationis accepturos, in eaque saltem finaliter perseveraturos esse, hos elegit: quos verò eandem repudiaturos, & in pervicaciâ ad finem perseveraturos esse, illos demùm reprobavit.

Tertiò quæritur de causâ Reprobationis, circa quam non una est omnium sententia, Augustini hæc fuit doctrina: Ante lapsum quidem, Voluntatem DEI de salute hominum fuisse universalem, ac propterea sufficiente gratiâ libertatis arbitrij Proto-parentes instruxisse: Post lapsum autem ex toto genere humano factam esse unam massam perditionis: Ex quâ postmodùm placuerit DEO facere quædam vasa in honorem; alia in contumeliam. Quoad prioris status conditionem; ex parte hominis causam dari non posse: Posterioris verò eam adsignari posse, quod in massâ illâ suâ DEUS vasa illa reliquerit. His permissis infert, DEUM non tantùm permittere, ut reprobi in peccata prolabi possint: sed etiam negare illis gratiam eam, sine quâ non possint salvari: ut Infantibus morte præventis negare baptismum: Infidelibus negare Verbum & Fidem: Christianis ad tempus credentibus negare perseverantiam. Ubi tamen dinitationem subjicit, nempè Negationem istam non esse absolutam: sed fundari in causâ peccati originalis: ac proindè cum justitiâ DEI rectissimè esse conjunctam. De hac Augustini sententiâ benè multa legere licet, Epist. 15. 106. 157. Et in Enchir. cap. 95. de nat. & grat. capp. 8. & 9. de corrept. & grat. cap. 10. 11. 12. de bono perseverantiæ capp. 8. & 14.

1. Fundamenta doctrinæ hujus suæ petijt Augustinus ex Scripturis, quæ secundum superficiem literæ videntur asserere, non omnibus hominibus sufficientem salutis gratiam datam esse.

Primus locus citatur ex cap. 11, 21. Matthæi, lib. de bono Perseverantiæ cap. 14. de Tyriis & Sidoniis, qui credituri fuisse dicantur, si miracula illa Christi vidissent, quæ ab ipso in Judæâ fuerant edita. Sed quoniam, ut crederent, non erat eis datum, etiam undè crederent, negatum ipsis fuisse, infert Augustinus.

Secundus locus petitur ex Johan. 12, 39. ubi de Judæis dicatur, non potuisse ipsos credere, quia erant excæcati, hoc est, in massâ perditionis relicti.

Tertius ex Actor. 14, 16. producitur de gentibus, quas dimiserit DEUS ambulare in vijs suis.

Quartus ex Actor. 16, 6. & 7. ubi Paulus & Silas legantur prohibiti à Spiritu Sancto, ne loquerentur Verbum Dei in Asiâ & Bithyniâ.

Quintus est, quem maximè urget: Si omnibus daretur sufficiens gratia, & ille salvaretur, qui eam acceptaret, & alter non: tunc homo seipsum discerneret, contra id, quod 1. Cor. 4, 7. dicitur: Quis te discernit?

Sed & rationibus pugnat idem Augustinus: ut quando scribit epist. 105. & de Nat. & Grat. c. 8. Multi parvuli moriantur sine Baptismo, qui non tantùm non sunt Christiani, sed ne quide possunt esse. Ergò auferetur eis sufficiens gratia. Et ibid. cap. 19. de adulto in eâ regione defuncto, ubi non potuit audiri nomen Christi, inquit: Is si salvaripotuit, lege naturæ & libero arbitrio salvatus fuisset: sic frustrâ illi mortuus fuisset Christus. Si sine gratiâ Christi salvari non potuit: idcircò talis fuit, quia aliter esse nullo modo potuit.

Verùm graviter hac in parte erravit Augustinus, neque argumenta ab ipso producta, ejus sunt ponderis aut momenti, ut in Ecclesiâ Orthodoxorum applausum mereri possint. Nam locus ille primus ex Matthæo citatus, illud tantùm probat, Superabundantem gratiam illis fuisse negatam, non autem sufficientem. At prodigia & miracula neque hodiè etiam fiunt: & tamen sufficiens salutis auxilium dari interim non negatur.

Locus alter Johannis, manifestè agit de pænâ præcedentium peccatorum, non Originalis, sed Actualium. Undè rectè alibi Augustinus infert, tractat. 53. in Johannem: Quare non potuerunt credere: citò respondeo, Quia nolebant: Malam quippè eorum voluntatem præscivit DEUS. Sed aliam causam, inquis, dicit Propheta, Non Voluntatis eorum: Quam? Quia dedit illis Spiritum compunctionis? Sed etiam hoc Voluntatem eorum meruisse respondeo: Sic enim excæcat, sic obdurat DEUS, deserendo, non verò adjuvando. Et paulò antè: Dicunt quidam, quid fecerunt Judæi? vel quæ culpa eorum fuit, si necesse fuit, ut Sermo Prophetæ impleretur? Quibus respondemus, DEUM præscium futurorum per Prophetam prædixisse infidelitatem Judæorum: prædixisse autem, non fecisse. Non enim proptereà quenquam ad peccandum cogit, quia futura hominum peccata jam novit: Ipsorum enim præscit peccata, non sua.

verba Johannis: Ecce iterum hanc particulam (Quia dixit) non causam, sed eventus esse attenden Nequè enim Quia dixit Esaias, non crediderunt, seu quia non erant credituri, ideò dixit. Sed quare non ita dixit Evangelista, sed incredulitatem à prophetiâ, non prophetiam ab incredulitate esse dixit? Hinc magnam vult Scriptura certitudinem demonstrare, & quòd non aliter, quàm prophetatum sit, evenit. Et paulo pôst: Non potuerunt credere, hoc est, noluerunt credere.


### VII. Special Controversy, Concerning the Consequent Will of GOD: and the difference of this from the Antecedent: Question II. Whether some decree of Reprobation is also to be placed in the Will of GOD? (continued)

And Cyril, book 8, chapter 20 and 21, on John: The name of Power (they could not), he says, is placed here for Will.

The third passage from chapter 14 of Acts does not show them left without sufficient grace. For it is immediately subjoined that GOD did not leave Himself without witness: But this is what it means, that He did not propose His Word to the Gentiles as He did to the Jews at close range: but that they had the necessity to aggregate themselves to the Jews. This permission therefore regards the offering of that special grace which consists in the preaching of the Word of GOD, which was taken away from the Gentiles by the just judgment of GOD, their own ingratitude so deserving.

The fourth passage from Acts 16. It only shows what was done for the time being. For Paul also preached in Asia afterwards, and with him at that time, John in Asia, Rev. 1 and 2. But while Peter was preaching in Bithynia, 1 Pet. 1, 1, the Apostle could certainly profit more by preaching in another place, namely in Macedonia. For which reason the text itself hints, in verse 9, where a certain Macedonian man appeared to Paul by night, crying, Cross over into Macedonia, and help us. Therefore, the passage does not militate for an absolute prohibition.

In the fifth place from 1 Cor. 4:7, a distinction must be made between discernment for good and for evil. The former is from the grace of God: the latter is from man not accepting the offered grace.

Regarding the arguments, and first indeed, various things can be answered concerning infants: 1. There is a great difference between infants born outside the Church and those born within it. 2. There is likewise a great discrepancy between infants and adults. 3. For the salvation of infants, not indeed as a cause, but nevertheless as a condition, there is the reception of Baptism: which if it is lacking, and then the infant is not saved, it happens not by the fault of God, but of man. 4. Sin is contracted by the fault of another's will: and many adults perish by the negligence of their pastors: and the soul of an uncircumcised child was cut off from his people, Genesis 17:14. What wonder, if on the part of infants the fault of parents and ancestors must also be atoned for: not indeed regarding absolute reprobation, but regarding the lack of the means of salvation: and that again not simple, but such as lacks the present ministry. 5. That the foreseen impiety of these infants in this place excuses God from all fault can be in doubt to no pious person. 6. If the consideration of original sin is added to all these things, nothing will be said irrelevantly. But enough concerning the opinion of Augustine.

Much worse was the opinion of Thomas Aquinas, Scotus, Durandus, and certain other Scholastics, who place in GOD a Will, preceding all causes, by which, having chosen the elect from eternity, He left and reprobated all others. They maintained that a cause for this reprobation in general could indeed be given on the part of GOD, namely the manifestation of divine justice: which, however, is not a meritorious or motivating cause, but merely a final one: but in particular, that no cause could be given, except the Will of GOD alone, and His mere good pleasure. Which impious theology the Sacramentarians have today made their own under the title of absolute Reprobation.

But neither can the doctrine of the Esavvites on this matter be tolerated in the Church of the faithful, which, according to Bellarmine, is as follows: lib. 2. de grat. & lib. arbitr. cap. 16. Reprobation comprises two acts: the one negative, for which there is no cause on the part of men: the other positive, the cause of which is the foreknowledge of original or actual sin.

And a little later: The reprobate are opposed to the elect contradictorily and contrarily. For first, GOD does not have the Will to save them: then, He has the Will to damn them: and indeed, as regards the former act, no cause for it is given on the part of men: but for the latter, the cause given is the foreknowledge of sin.

And towards the end of the same chapter: GOD reprobates some on account of original sin only; such as unbaptized infants: others on account of actual sin only, such as baptized adults: others on account of both, such as infidel adults.

The Orthodox Church, making a divorce from these and other errors of this kind, is accustomed to resolve the present question and its solid decision with the following hypotheses.

I. Original Sin alone is not the cause of Reprobation, such that on account of it the reprobate were left in the mass of perdition. The reason for this assertion is this, because this sin, even in many reprobate, was removed by Baptism in respect of guilt and damnation. How therefore could it, so solitarily and considered in itself, be the cause of Reprobation? 2. The grace of Christ merited more than the sin of Adam harmed. Now if, on account of that sin of Adam, GOD had left the greatest part of the human race in the mass of perdition, with very few saved: then sin would have abounded above grace: which the Apostle denies as false and blasphemous, Rom. 5, 20. 3. In the Scriptures where mention is made of reprobation, original sin alone is nowhere assigned as the cause: but actual sins are expressly named. Rom. 1, 21. to the end. 4. To all Christians, aids and sufficient means are conferred for perseverance in grace, John 1, 12. As many as received him, to them gave he power to become the sons of God, etc. 1 Cor. 10, 13. God is faithful, who will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able: but will with the temptation also make a way to escape, that ye may be able to bear it. Hebr. 12, 21

The GOD of peace will make you perfect in every good work to do his Will, working in you that which is well-pleasing in his sight. And memorable is the sentiment of Augustine: That GOD, before He is forsaken, forsakes no one: art. 7. to the articles falsely imposed upon him. Now if this grace is given to all, the cause why they do not persevere cannot be abandonment in the mass of perdition: but their own evil Will, by which, when they could, they were unwilling to persevere.

II. It is more impious than impiety itself if anyone says that GOD, without any regard for infidelity or any sin: but only in general for the declaration of His justice: and in particular, from the sole choice and good pleasure of His Will, from the furthest eternity, reprobated the greatest part of the human race and adjudged them to infernal fire. This blasphemy 1. makes GOD, who is Φιλάνθρωπος (a lover of mankind), clearly μισάνθρωπος (a hater of mankind). 2. It utterly removes in GOD that antecedent Will concerning the salvation of men. 3. It completely inverts and undermines the order and degrees of divine providence. For since He provides for all natural things, even inanimate ones, the means to strive for their own ends: certainly if GOD, by His sole Will and good pleasure, denied to the greatest part of men the means to arrive at salvation: it follows that GOD has much greater care for brute beasts and inanimate things than for men: which is manifestly impious: since GOD created man alone in His own image, and for his sake alone created all the rest of the things that are on earth. Nor is there any weight in what some say, to cast a veil over their impiety, that GOD meanwhile offers sufficient grace even to these reprobate. For those who by an absolute decree are already excluded from grace and life from the furthest eternity, to them the means of Salvation are offered in vain. Let those, therefore, who object these things, see how they can free GOD from the suspicion of injustice. For does it befit divine justice to condemn, on account of neglected means of salvation, those whom He Himself, by an absolute decree and His sole Will, destined from eternity to destruction? 4. In the punished Adamic fall, in the damnation of the fallen Angels, and finally in the death of His Son, GOD has declared His justice abundantly enough, so that there is no need for this figment about the absolute reprobation of those to be damned.

III. Sufficient grace is given to all men, to infidels, that they may believe: to the faithful, that they may persevere. Therefore, the cause of reprobation is by no means to be placed in GOD. The antecedent is proved from the Scriptures, first by those testimonies which generally confirm the universal mercy of GOD over all men.

Ps. 119:64. The earth, O LORD, is full of thy mercy.

Ps. 145:9. The Lord is sweet to all, and his tender mercies are over all his works.

Joel 2:13. Turn to the Lord your God, because he is kind and merciful, patient and of great mercy, and such a one who repents over evil. Jonah 4:2. I know that you are a GOD clement and merciful, patient and of great compassion, and forgiving sins. Wis. 11:24. You have mercy on all, because you can do all things, and you overlook the sins of men, in long-suffering.

Then the same is proved from those Scriptures which show the desire for the salvation of all men in GOD. Matt. 18:14. It is not the will of your heavenly Father that one of these little ones should perish. 1 Tim. 2:4. God wills all men to be saved, and to come to the knowledge of the truth. 2 Pet. 3:6. GOD does not will any to perish, but all to be converted to repentance.

Thirdly, the same is demonstrated by those testimonies which teach that GOD condemns men unwillingly and with expostulation. 2 Sam. 14:14. GOD does not will a soul to perish, but withdraws, thinking, lest he who is cast out should perish utterly. Ezek. 18:32. Why will you die, O house of Israel? Because I do not will the death of the one who dies, says the Lord GOD, return and live. Ezek. 33:10 & 11. Thus you have spoken: our iniquities and our sins are upon us, and we are wasting away in them: how then shall we be able to live? Say to them: As I live, says the LORD: I do not will the death of the wicked: but that the wicked should turn from his evil way, and live. Isa. 30:18. The LORD waits, that he may have mercy on you. Ecclesiasticus 18:21 & 22. He has commanded no one to act wickedly, and he has given no one license to sin: for he does not desire a multitude of unfaithful and useless children. Ps. 4:3. O sons of men, how long will you be of heavy heart? why do you love vanity, and seek after lying.

To which pertains almost the entire fifth chapter of Isaiah: and the eighteenth chapter of Jeremiah.

Fourthly, the same is proved from the work of Redemption accomplished through Christ, which we have already shown above professedly to pertain to all men whatsoever.

Finally, this very thing is proved from the work of universal Evangelical preaching, from the hearing of which GOD willed that no mortal be absolutely prohibited or excluded. Now since both the merit of Christ and the preaching of the Gospel are most efficacious instruments for procuring our salvation: and since they are common to all: surely from this it is irrefragably gathered that for no one, by any absolute decree of GOD, is there a lack of the means sufficient for salvation.

IV. Human reprobation is nothing but from the side of men: and that is unbelief and final impenitence foreseen by GOD: and either followed by the act itself, namely in the damned adults: or at least about to follow, in unbaptized infants, snatched away by premature death. Mark 16:16. John

3:18. He who does not believe is already judged, because he does not believe in the name of the only-begotten Son of GOD. John 3:36. He who does not believe in the Son shall not see life, but the wrath of GOD remains upon him. Jer. 32:33. John 6:53. John 16:9. For just as GOD chose those whom he saw would accept the offered grace, and would persevere in it: so he reprobated those whom he foresaw would finally reject it: or as the Book of Concord speaks: Just as GOD in his eternal counsel ordained that the Holy Spirit should call the elect through the Word: and justify all those who embrace Christ with true faith, and confer eternal salvation upon them: so in that same counsel he decreed that he wills to reprobate and devote to eternal damnation those who, having been called through the Word, reject it, etc. GOD testifies to this explicitly in Hosea 13:9. Your destruction is from yourself, O Israel.

And since GOD is prepared to give sufficient help for salvation to all, it is prior that he is deserted, with salvation foreseen in the act, namely in the infants just mentioned, than that he himself deserts. Some, however, are so reprobated by GOD in this world, on account of certain most grave sins, that they never again obtain the grace of salvation, not only superabundant, but even sufficient in fact. Testimonies of this matter are held expressed in the Scriptures:

Ps. 95:11. To whom I swore in my wrath, if they shall enter into my rest.

Ps. 81:13. I dismissed them according to the desires of their own hearts.

Rom. 1, 28. GOD delivered them up to a reprobate sense.

But GOD does this only in those whom He foresaw would contumaciously reject the grace offered. For it is a most just punishment for sin, that he who would not do what was right when he could, should afterwards lose the ability when he wishes, as Augustine speaks, de lib. arb. l. 3. cap. 18. & de Naturâ & Grat. cap. 67. Just as therefore, though in a different kind of cause, a general of an army, as the war intensifies, withdraws himself, betraying his soldiers to the enemy, not because he himself drives them to slaughter, but because he deserts them of his aid: Which simile Chrysostom uses, in his homily on Adam & Eve at the end of the first Volume: And on that Roman. 1. GOD delivered them up to a reprobate sense &c. Or as a physician leaves an intemperate patient as the disease worsens; Which example Theophylact uses, on the same place of the Apostle Rom. 1. or as a ship captain allows a skiff to be carried along without a helmsman: Which simile Theodoret used in his explanation of the same place of the Apostle: so those who deny GOD as Creator, deny His Providence entirely.

…These therefore are the Reprobate, because in fact they were never to be converted: it would also be in vain if the grace, which they were not going to accept, were offered to them. Indeed in this case, it is not only a work of most just vengeance: but in its own way rather a work of mercy in GOD, not to offer than to offer grace. For by stubbornly rejecting offered grace, one would sin more grievously. And this is that which is said in Isa. 26:10: Let us show mercy to the impious, and he will not learn to do justice; or, Grace shall be offered to the impious: yet he shall not learn justice. Which passage Bernard explains most excellently, Tom. 1, Sermon on the worst Vice of ingratitude: just as it is a greater mercy not to give a sword to a madman than to give one with which he might strike himself. Moreover, such a reason as this can also be assigned for this matter: Because to Christ alone according to his assumed humanity was grace given without measure: John 3:34. To all others it is given with a certain measure, and according to distinct degrees, Rom. 12:3, Eph. 4:7. Just as therefore a certain measure of goods has been given to the elect out of the liberality of GOD: so the measure of sins has been predetermined for the reprobate. Gen. 15:16. The iniquities of the Amorites are not yet complete. Matt. 23:32. Fill up the measure of your fathers. 1. Thess. 2:16, so that he may always fill up his sins. Hence it is also read everywhere in the Scriptures that a certain time of repentance is predetermined for the impious: Isa. 5:2, Job 24:23, Luke 13:7, Rev. 2:21.

Latin:

Et Cyrill. lib. 8. cap. 20. & 21. in Johannem: Nomen inquit Potestatis (non potuerunt) ponitur hic pro Voluntate.

Tertius locus ex cap. 14. Actorum, non ostendit relictas sine sufficiente gratiâ. Statim enim subjungitur, DEUM non reliquisse seipsum intestatum: Verùm hoc vult, quòd gentibus non ut Judæis cominùs Verbum suum proposuerit: sed illi necesse habuerint, se aggregare Judæis. Permissio ergò hæc respicit specialis illius gratiæ oblationem, quæ consistit in præconio Verbi DEI, quòd à gentibus, ipsorum sic promerente ingratitudine, justo DEI judicio fuit ablatum.

Quartus locus ex Actor. 16. Quid pro tempore factum sit, tantùm ostendit. Nam Paulus etiam posteà in Asiâ prædicavit, cumque illo tempore, Johannes in Asiâ, Apoc. 1, & 2. In Bithyniâ verò Petrus concionaretur, 1. Pet. 1, 1. utique plus Apostolus alio loco, nempè in Macedoniâ concionando proficere poterat. Quam ob causam innuit textus ipse, Versu 9. ubi Paulo per noctem visus fuit vir quidam Macedo, clamans, Trajice in Macedoniam, & succurre nobis. Pro absolutâ ergò prohibitione locus ille non militat.

In loco quinto ex 1. Cor. 4, 7. distinguenda est discretio ad bonum, & ad malum. Illa est à gratiâ DEI: Posterior est ab homine non acceptante oblatam gratiam.

Quoad rationes, & primùm quidem de Infantibus varia responderi possunt: 1. Infantium extra Ecclesiam, & intra eandem natorum magna est diversitas. 2. Infantium & adultorum itidem magna est discrepantia. 3. Salutis infantium, ex ipsorum parte, non causa quidem, sed tamen conditio est, susceptio scilicet Baptismi: Quæ si desit, & tùm non salvetur infans; non DEI, sed hominis culpâ id fit. 4. contrahitur peccatum alienæ voluntatis culpâ: & adulti multi pereunt pastorum suorum negligentiâ: & anima pueri non circumcisi delebatur de populo suo, Genes. 17, 14. Quid mirum, si ex parte infantibus sit etiam luenda parentum & majorum culpa: non quidem quoad absolutam reprobationem, sed quoad defectum mediorum salutis: & eum rursus non simplicem, sed talem, qui caret præsenti ministerio. 5. Quin hoc loco prævisa infantum istorum impietas DEUM ab omni culpâ excuset, nemini piò potest esse dubium. 6. His omnibus si originalis peccati respectus accedat, nihil abs re dicetur. Sed satis de Augustini sententiâ.

Deterior multò fuit Thomæ Aquinatis, Scoti, Durandi, atœ;ue aliorum quorundam Scholasticorum opinio, qui in DEO ponunt Voluntatem, causas omnes antegressam, quâ cum ab æterno elegisset electos, alios omnes reliquerit & reprobârit. Reprobationis hujus in communi quidem causam ex parte DEI dari posse statuebant, Manifestationem justitiæ divinæ : quæ tamen non sit causa meritoria aut motiva : sed finalis duntaxat : in particulari autem causam dari nullam posse, præter Voluntatem DEI solam; & merum ejus beneplacitum. Quam impiam Theologiam, sub absolutæ Reprobationis titulo hodiè suam fecerunt Sacramentarij.

Sed neque Esavvitarum hâc de materiâ dočtrina, in Ecclesiâ fidelium tolerari potest, quæ interprete Bellarmino talis est : lib. 2. de grat. & lib. arbitr. cap. 16. Reprobatio duos actus comprehendit : alterum negativum, cujus nulla est causa ex parte hominum : alterum positivum, cujus causa est peccati Originalis, actualisve prævisio.

Et paulò post : Reprobi opponuntur electis contradictoriè & contrariè. Primùm enim non habet DEUS Voluntatem illos salvandi : Deindè habet Voluntatem eos damnandi : & quidem quod attinet ad priorem actum, nulla datur ejus causa ex parte hominum : posterioris autem datur causa prævisio peccati.

Et circa finem ejusdem capitis : DEUS alios reprobat propter Originale peccatum tantùm ; ut parvulos non baptizatos : alios propter actuale tantùm, ut baptizatos adultos : alios propter utrumque, ut infideles adultos.

Ab his & id genus alijs errorum devijs Orthodoxa Ecclesia divortium faciens, sequentibus hypothesibus præsentem quæstionem, ejúsque solidam decisionem expedire solet.

I. Solum Peccatum Originale non est causa Reprobationis, ita ut propter illud reprobi sint relicti in massâ perditionis. Ratio assertionis est hæc, quia peccatum hoc etiam in multis reprobis, ratione reatus & damnationis fuit ablatum per Baptismum. Quomodo ergò illud ita solitariè, & in se consideratum, causa esse queat Reprobationis? 2. Plus meruit gratia Christi, quam nocuit peccatum Adami. Jam si propter peccatum illud Adami, maximam generis humani partem, in massâ perditionis reliquisset DEUS, salvatis paucissimis : utique peccatum supra gratiam abundasset : id quod ceu falsum & blasphemum negat Apostolus, Rom. 5, 20. 3. In Scripturis ubi fit mentio reprobationis, nuspiam pro causâ assignatur solum peccatum originale : sed actualia disertè nominantur. Rom. 1, 21. ad finem usque. 4. Omnibus Christianis ad perseverantiam in gratiâ conferuntur auxilia & media sufficientia, Joh. 1, 12. Quotquot receperunt eum, dedit eis potestatem filios Dei fieri &c. 1. Cor. 10, 13. Fidelis Deus, qui non sinit vos tentari, ultrà id quodferre potestis : sed unà cum tentatione prastabit etiã exitum, ut sufferre possitis. Hebr. 12, 21

DEUS pacis perficiet vos in omni opere bono, ad præstandam ipsius Voluntatem, efficiens in vobis, quod acceptum sit in conspectu suo. Et memorabilis est Augustini sententia: Quòd DEUS, priùsquàm deferatur, neminem deserat: artic. 7. ad articulos sibi falsò impositos. Jam si gratia hæc datur omnibus, causa cur non perseverent, non potest esse derelictio in massâ perditionis: sed mala Voluntas ipsorum, quâ cùm possent, perseverare nolebant.

II. Impietate ipsâ magis impium est, si quis dicat, DEUM nullo infidelitatis, aut peccati cujusquam respectu: sed in communi solùm propter declarationem suæ justiciæ: in singulari autem, ex solo Voluntatis suæ arbitrio & beneplacito, indè ab ultimâ æternitate, maximam generis humani partem reprobasse, & igni infernali adjudicasse. Blasphemia hæc 1. ex DEO Φιλανθρώπῳ facit DEUM planè μισάνθρωπον. 2. Tollit in DEO prorsus antecedentem illam de salute hominum Voluntatem. 3. Providentiæ divinæ ordinem & gradus prorsus invertit & labefactat. Nam cùm rebus naturalibus omnibus, etiam inanimatis sua ad fines proprios contendendi media procuret: certè si maximæ hominum parti media ad salutem perveniendi, solâ suâ Voluntate & beneplacito negavit DEUS: sequitur, DEUM multò majorem brutorum & rerum inanimatarum, quàm hominum curam habere: id quòd manifestè impium: siquidem solum hominem ad suam imaginem creavit DEUS, & propter hunc solum creavit reliqua universa, quæ in terris sunt. Neque momenti quicquam habet, quod aliqui fucum impietati facturi, dicunt, DEUM interim etiam reprobis istis sufficientem gratiam offerre. Nam qui absoluto decreto jam ab ultimâ æternitate à gratiâ & vitâ sunt exclusi, his frustrà porrò Salutis media offeruntur. Viderint ergò, qui hæc objiciunt, quomodo DEUM ab injustitiæ suspicione liberare possint. Justitiæ enim divinæ non competit, propter neglecta media salutis damnare eos, quos tamen ipsemet absoluto decreto, & solâ suâ Voluntate, ab æterno ad exitium destinavit? 4. In lapsu Adamico punito, in lapsorum Angelorum damnatione, & tandem Filij sui morte abundè satis justitiam suam declaravit DEUS, ut figmento isto, de absolutâ damnandorum reprobatione non sit opus.

III. Omnibus hominibus sufficiens gratia datur, Infidelibus, ut credant: Fidelibus ut perseverent. Ergò in DEO Reprobationis causa minimè est ponenda. Antecedens probatur ex Scripturis, primùm per illa testimonia, quæ generatim confirmant universalem DEI misericordiam super omnes homines.

Psal. 119, 64. Misericordiâ tuâ DOMINE plena est terra.

Psal. 145, 9. Svavis est Dominus universis, Misericordia ejus super omnia opera ejus.

Joel. 2, 13. Convertimini ad Dominum Deum vestrũ, quia benignus & misericors est, patiens & multæ misericordiæ, & talis quem pœnitet super malo. Jonæ 4, 2. Scio, quia tu DEUS clemens & misericors, patiens & multæ miserationis, & ignoscens peccata. Sap. 11, 24. Misereris omnium, quia omnia potes, & dissimulas peccata hominum, in longanimitate.

Deindè probatur idem ex Scripturis illis, quæ desiderium salutis omnium hominum in DEO ostendunt. Matth. 18, 14. Non est voluntas Patris vestri cælestis, ut pereat unus de pusillis istis. 1. Tim. 2, 4. Deus vult omnes homines salvos fieri, & ad agnitionem veritatis pervenire. 2. Petr. 3, 6. DEUS non vult ullos perire, sed omnes ad pœnitentiam converti.

Tertiò idem demonstratur illis testimonijs, quæ docent, DEUM invitum & expostulabundum damnare homines. 2. Sam. 14, 14. Non vult DEUS perire animam, sed retractat, cogitans, ne penitùs pereat qui abjectus est. Ezech. 18, 32. Quare moriemini domus Israël? Quia nolo mortem morientis, dicit Dominus DEUS, revertimini & vivite. Ezech. 33, 10. & 11. Sic locuti estis: iniquitates nostræ & peccata nostra super nos sunt, & in ipsis nos tabescimus: quomodo ergò vivere poterimus? Dic ad eos: Vivo ego, dicit DOMINUS: nolo mortem impij: sed ut convertatur impius à viâ suâ malâ, & vivat. Esa. 30, 18. Expectat DOMINUS, ut misereatur vestri. Ecclesiastici 18, 21. & 22. Nemini mandavit impiè agere, & nemini dedit licentiam peccandi: non enim concupiscit multitudinem filiorum infidelium & inutilium. Psal. 4, 3. Filij hominum usquequo gravi corde estis? ut quid diligitis vanitatem, & quæritis mendacium.

Quò pertinet totum fermè caput quintum Esaiæ: & caput decimum octavum Jeremiæ.

Quartò probatur idem ex opere Redemtionis per Christum factæ, quod ad omnes omninò homines pertinere, jam suprà ex professò ostendimus.

Tandem probatur hoc ipsum ex opere universalis prædicationis Evangelicæ, à cujus auscultatione neminem mortalium absolutè prohibitum aut exclusum voluit DEUS. Jam cùm & meritum Christi, & prædicatio Evangelij universalis sint salutis nostræ procurandæ organa efficacissima: ea verò omnibus sint communia: utique vel indè irrefragabiliter colligitur, nemini ex ullo absoluto DEI decreto, deesse sufficientiæ ad salutem media.

IV. Reprobationis humanæ non est, nisi ex parte hominum: eaque est incredulitas & finalis impœnitentia DEO prævisa: & vel actu ipso secuta, nempè in adultis damnatis: vel secutura saltem, in infantibus non baptizatis, morte præmatura abreptis. Marc. 16, 16. Johan.

3, 18. Qui non credit, jam judicatus est, quia non credit in nomen unigeniti Filij DEI. Johan. 3, 36. Qui non credit in Filium, non videbit vitam, sed ira DEI manet super eum. Jerem. 32, 33. Johan. 6, 53. Johan. 16, 9. Nam sicuti elegit DEUS eos, quos gratiam oblatam vidit accepturos esse, in eaque perseveraturos: ita a quibus eam finaliter repudiandam esse prævidit, illos reprobavit : aut ut liber Concordiæ loquitur : Quemadmodum DEUS in æterno suo consilio ordinavit, ut Spiritus Sanctus electos per Verbum vocet : atque omnes illos, qui Christum verâ fide amplectuntur, justificet, atque in eos æternam salutem conferat : ita in eodem suo consilio decrevit, quod eos, qui per Verbum vocati, illud repudiant &c. reprobare & æternæ damnationi devovere velit. Testatur hoc disertè DEUS Oseæ 13, 9. Perditio tua ex te Israël.

Et cùm DEUS paratus sit omnibus dare sufficiens auxilium ad salutem, prius est quòd deseratur, actu salutem præviso, in infantibus scilicet modò dictis, quàm quòd ipse deserat. Aliqui tamen ita reprobantur à DEO in hoc mundo, propter peccata quædam gravissima, ut gratiam salutis non superabundantem tantùm, sed sufficientem etiam de facto, nunquàm ampliùs consequantur. Testimonia hujus rei habentur expressa in Scripturis :

Psal. 95, 11. Quibus juravi in irâ meâ, si introibunt in requiem meam.

Psal. 81, 13. Dimisi eos secundum desideria cordis ipsorum.

Rom. 1, 28. Tradidit eos DEUS in sensum reprobum.

Verùm non nisi in ijs hoc facit DEUS, quos gratiam oblatam contumaciter repudiaturos esse prævidit. Est enim justissima pœna peccati, ut qui rectum facere cùm posset, noluit, amittat postmodùm posse, cùm velit, ut Augustinus loquitur, de lib. arb. l. 3. cap. 18. & de Naturâ & Grat. cap. 67. Sicut ergò, in diverso tamen causæ genere, Dux exercitus, bello ingravescente se subducit, milites hostibus prodendo, non quod ipse in stragem eos impellat, sed auxilio suo deserat: Quâ similitudine Chrysostomus utitur, in homiliâ de Adam & Eva in fine primi Tomi: Et in illud Roman. 1. Tradidit illos DEUS in sensum reprobum &c. Aut sicut ingravescente morbo ægrum intemperantem medicus relinquit; Quo exemplo utitur Theophylactus, in eundem locum Apostoli Rom. 1. aut sicut navarcha, cymbam ferri absque rectore sinit: Quo simili Theodoretus in ejusdem loci Apostoli explicatione usus fuit: ita qui DEUM negant Creatorem, Providentiam ejus omninò negant.

Hi ergò Reprobi, quia de facto nunquàm erant convertendi : frustra etiam futurum esset, si gratia, quam non erant acceptaturi, illis offerretur. Imò hoc casu, non ultionis tantùm justissimæ : sed suo modo misericordiæ potiùs in DEO opus est, non offerre, quam offerre gratiam. Nam oblatam gratiam contumaciter respuendo, graviùs peccaretur. Et hoc est illud, quod Esa. 26, 10. dicitur: Misereamur impio, & non discet justitiam facere; vel, Gratia offeretur impio: nec tamen discet justitiam. Quem locum optimè explicat Bernhardus, Tom. 1. Serm. de pessimo Vitio ingratitudinis: sicut est major misericordia, non dare gladium insano, quàm dare, quo feriat seipsum. Potest autem hujus rei assignari etiam talis ratio: Quia soli Christo secundum assumtam humanitatem data est gratia sine mensurâ: Johan. 3, 34. Cæteris omnib9 data est cum certâ mensurâ, & secundum distinctos gradus, Rom. 12, 3. Ephes. 4, 7. Sicut ergò electis certa mensura bonorum ex liberalitate DEI data est: ita modus peccatorum præfinitus est reprobis. Genes. 15, 16. Nondum sunt completæ iniquitates Amorrhæorum Matth, 23, 32. Implete mensuram patrum vestrorum. 1. Thess. 2, 16. ut impleat peccata sua semper. Hinc passim etiam in Scripturis legitur impijs certum pœnitentiæ tempus esse præfinitum: Esa. 5, 2. Job. 24, 23. Luc. 13, 7. Apoc. 2, 21.


### VII. Special Controversy, Concerning the Consequent Will of GOD: and the difference of this from the Antecedent: Question III. Whether Election is absolute, or indeed ordered?

Question III. Whether Election is absolute, or indeed ordered?

The handle and occasion for explaining this question more accurately is provided not only by the figment of the Calvinists concerning the decree of Reprobation, as well as Election, as being absolute: But also by the dream of Huber, by which he imagines a semi-absolute Election, which indeed includes the merit of Christ, but without respect to faith. We, therefore, having sent a message of dismissal to both these flocks of fanatics, and having followed the oracles of the Scriptures, maintain that neither the Election nor the Reprobation of any man is absolute: but that both are ordered. For just as GOD from eternity proposed to choose men for eternal life, and to save the same: so he also established the order and the means, and decreed in his eternal counsel, by which means the Salvation of the Elect would be constituted, and which would never be separated from the defining of the decree of Election. But what this order is, and of what kind, must be looked into a little more accurately from the Scriptures.

The first place, therefore, in this is held by Christ the Savior with his merit. Scripture affirms this when it testifies, 1. That we were chosen in Christ. Eph. 1:4. Hence one may argue thus: Whoever are chosen in some certain object, or through or on account of it, or even in respect to it, they are not chosen absolutely, but in an ordered manner. For that which is done with certain respect to another is not absolute. But all the elect are chosen in Christ. Therefore they are not chosen absolutely, but in an ordered manner.

Then the Scripture in the cited passage asserts that GOD has blessed us with spiritual blessings in Christ, in whom he also chose us before the foundation of the world. Eph. 1:3 and 4. Hence it is gathered thus: Of the same kind as the spiritual blessing, which happens in time, is also the eternal election. But that is not absolute, but ordered in Christ: Therefore neither will this be absolute.

Thirdly, Eph. 1:5 it is said, That GOD predestined us unto the adoption of sons through Jesus Christ unto himself, according to the good pleasure of his will: which the Apostle explains in 2 Tim. 1:9, asserting that grace was given to us in Christ Jesus before the secular times. Which two testimonies fight no less for an ordered Election than the first two. And above all, the express notation of eternity must be observed in each of these places, which in no way permits us to interpret the words of the Apostle concerning a temporal execution. And indeed, as regards Huber, the matter concerning this first part of the order is clearer than what requires laborious proof.

THE OTHER part of this order is FAITH, apprehending the merit of Christ: concerning which a sharper dispute is agitated today. But that this Faith enters into the τάξιν or order of the Decree of Election is most evidently demonstrated by these reasons from Scripture.

I. Christ with all his benefits and his most abundant merit profits no one without faith. Therefore it is necessary that Faith should approach the τάξιν of divine predestination: so that those in whom this order is completed, not only by reason of the merit of CHRIST, but also by reason of faith apprehending that merit, these may be in the number of the elect: but the rest may be excluded from it, not by any absolute good pleasure of the divine Will: but by the fault and vice of their own incredulity and final impenitence.

II. Scripture itself clearly proves that Faith enters into the decree of eternal Election.

Eph. 1:1 and 12. Election is said to be properly of the FAITHFUL or those believing in JESUS: who themselves a little later, by a phrase customary in the Scriptures, are named those HOPING in Christ.

2 Thess. 2:13. GOD chose us from the beginning for salvation, in the faith of the Truth.

Tit. 1:1. The faith of Jesus Christ is called the faith of the Elect.

James 2:5. He chose the poor of this world, rich in faith.

And to reduce the matter to a few words: if it is impossible to please GOD without faith, Heb. 11:6. If no one can have eternal life unless he believes, John 6:39. If no Election was made outside of Christ, Eph. 1:4, but those who do not believe in him are outside of Christ: certainly Faith can by no means, nor ought it to be, excluded from the decree of election.

III. In the same way that the Grace of GOD relates to the remission of sins, in that same way it also relates to our Election. But the Grace of GOD never remits sins except to Believers, therefore the Grace of Election will not be obtained by anyone without faith. The connection

It is evident from this, 1. because in both cases there is one and the same grace. Rom. 11, 5. & 6. & 22. Ephes. 1, 5. 6. & 7. 2. Tim. 1, 9. & 20. 2. because they are not elected, except those to whom sins have been forgiven.

IV. GOD, by electing us, adopted us as sons. Ephes. 1, 5. But υἱοθεσία or adoption as sons is only of Believers: Joh. 1, 12. Gal. 3, 26. Therefore Election is also only of Believers.

V. Election tends toward life and eternal salvation: so that whoever are predestined, they are also justified and glorified, Rom. 8, 30. But the just man lives only by Faith. Rom. 1, 17. Hebr. 2, 4. nor are any glorified except believers alone.

VI. In the same way that the execution of the eternal decree of Election, which takes place in time, behaves, so also does the election itself behave: But the execution of the eternal decree behaves in such a way that no one is saved unless he believes in Christ. Therefore it is necessary that the eternal decree of Election itself also includes none but believers.

VII. Finally, there is added the Consensus of Orthodox Antiquity, and the most clear decision of the Book of Christian Concord, which simply explodes Huber's delirium concerning predestination made from eternity without regard to faith.

Theophylact certainly comments thus upon chapter 1 of Ephesians: To be chosen in Christ is nothing else than to be chosen in the faith of Jesus Christ.

Theophylact, in the explanation of this very first chapter to the Ephesians, is supported by Jerome, Chrysostom, Ambrose, and others.

The Epitome of the Book of Concord, however, holds thus: The eternal Election of GOD the Father is to be sought in Christ: He in His eternal Counsel decreed that He wills to save no one except those who acknowledge His Son JESUS CHRIST and truly believe in Him.

And we have already reviewed above those eight requirements which the Book of Concord establishes must always be joined together in the doctrine of Predestination: Among which number FAITH is even the greatest, and it is inculcated and repeated as most important: Wherefore the same Symbolic book adds: All these things are comprehended in the article of Predestination: we must include all those things under this article, and none of these is to be excluded or omitted.

With these things concerning Faith, as the second part of the Decree of Election, thus established, there finally emerges this full complement of this order: namely, that Christ with His merit, apprehended only by faith, constitutes the order of Election: and thus this latter part of the order, added to the former part, binds the universality and efficacy of the merit of Christ, by reason of its saving fruit, to believers alone.

Huber is in an uproar at this point, and he anxiously disputes how, or by what title, Faith can enter into the eternal decree of Election, and whether Faith ought to be called the cause of Election.
