Neq; relevat Esavvitas id, quòd prævisione peccati non priorem: sed posteriorem hanc reprobationem suam statuunt. Nam temporis ratione prius aut posterius in æternitate nihil est. Ordinis autem prioritatem, & posteritatem ne ipsi quidem Sacramentarij negabunt.

Accedit expressus consensus Calvinianorum, præsertim recentiorum, qui absurditatem dogmatis sui quoquo modo palliaturi, fingunt Decretum istud Reprobationis, non simpliciter, & ex omni parte esse absolutum: sed tantùm ratione prioris actus. Quod quomodo intelligendum sit, non aliundè patet, quàm ex Esavvitarum doctrinâ, qui Reprobationis actum duplicem constituunt: Unum Affirmativum, sive Positivum: alterum Negativum: uti paulò ante ex Bellarmino cognovimus. Distinctioni huic suffragium, & calculum suum adjicit Perkinsius, qui lib. de Prædest. pag. 25. sic disserit: Reprobationis actus duplex est: Prior est, propositum deserendi quosdam homines justitiamq́; in eis declarandi. Hic oritur ex mero DEI beneplacito, nullo habito respectu vel boni, vel mali in creaturâ. Nam voluntas DEI est causa causarum. Et proindè DEUS pro summo jure suo vasa ad iram facit, non invenit. Secundus actus est ordinatio ad pœnam, sive justum exitium.

Quam in sententiam scribit etiam Keckermannus System. Theol. pag. 208. Prior actus est propositum DEI deserendi quosdam homines, & sibi relinquendi. Hic actus est absolutus, pendens à solo & absoluto DEI arbitrio. Alter actus est decretum damnandi propter peccata. Hic actus non est absolutus, sed continet respectum ad conditionem peccati.

Sunt autem duo isti diversi Reprobationis actus non à recentioribus demùm Calvinianis excogitati: sed ex doctrinâ Scholasticorum hausti, qui & ipsi geminum actũ præteritionis confinxerunt: Unum Passivum & Negativum, & eum quidem plane absolutum: alterum Affirmativum & Activum, qui sit præparatio pœnæ, sive prædamnatio ab æterno, & habeat respectum ad peccatum. Quæ doctrina Scholasticorum, licet postmodùm sub Papatu obeliscum passa sit: hodiè tamen ab Esavvitis & Calvinianis in proscenium Ecclesiæ apertè revocatur. Undè de ipsorum Syncretismo in hoc etiam articulo dubitare non ampliùs licet.


### Part II. Πολεμικη (Polemic): III. the Error of Francesco Pucci; and of Dr. Samuel Huber and his followers I. on Puccianism

III. THE ERROR OF FRANCESCO Pucci; and of Dr. Samuel Huber and his followers.

I. ON PUCCIANISM.

Around the year of Christ fifteen hundred and ninety-two, Francesco Pucci of Filidino, a Florentine by birth, published a certain booklet, printed at Gouda, with this title: Catholic Assertion concerning the efficacy of Christ the Savior, etc., certainly composed in such a way that it evidently appears that that man was addicted to no certain religion, but fostered such a kind of doctrine as would confirm Schwenckfeldianism, Anabaptism, Jesuitism, Calvinism, Judaism: nay, would fundamentally undermine and overturn the entire Christian religion, good morals, and all piety: which may be seen from the following little flowers of his doctrine:

1. That interpretation of Holy Scripture is most humane and most equitable which is consistent with itself on all sides, and is agreeable to common and natural reason, and to divine and human equity. pag. 1. & 7.

2. The faith by which the ancient fathers were justified was natural and most well-known. pag. 57.

3. We must beware lest we accept or suppose, in place of a general faith common to all, the hope or faith in the Messiah conceived from the promises of GOD: pag. 60. Rat. 88.

4. They err as much as heaven is from earth, whoever accept this obscure hope of the ancients, conceived from the promises, as justifying faith. ibid.

5. Simple ignorance (of the Word and Sacraments) can be a detriment to no one: but destruction threatens only those who protest against the true servants of GOD (such as he proclaims himself and his associates to be). Rat. 58.

6. We must beware lest we think that anyone loses the right of inheritance from a simple lack of preaching or Sacraments: For the benevolence of the Heavenly King, embracing the whole human race, extends much more widely than those external rites, Rat. 81. 109.

7. In individual men there is ὑπόστασις or the substance of saving faith, and therefore all are born fit for eternal life. Rat. 9.

8. Individual mortals are in a state of salvation before they degenerate. Rat. 10.

9. All and individual men are to be held as believers before they, by their own malice and distrust, derogate from the faith of GOD and his servants. Rat. 43.

10. Destruction threatens no one except those who stubbornly adhere to worldly and dark sects: Since all ignorance excuses those who sin. Rat. 54. & 55.

11. Individual humans who are beneficent toward other men are to be recognized as Christians virtually, and are to be saved: But the inhumane are to be lost: which is most agreeable to divine equity. For since there are very few mortals who have been able to acknowledge Christ by name and historically: therefore it is most equitable that each one be judged according to how he has behaved toward the brothers of Christ. Rat. 47.

12. There is no sin unless it is voluntary, and therefore the stain of Original sin is not a sin, but a fuel for sin. Rat. 13.

13. Our first parents were not, through the fall, despoiled of the gifts and benefits with which they had been adorned by the best Creator. Rat. 14.

14. Original vice does not provoke the wrath, but the mercy of GOD. Rom. 11, 25. 28. 29.

15. Christian heralds will rise again a thousand years before other mortals: And the time of the final judgment will not be the work of one day, but of several, and at the very least seven years.

16. All and every individual human being, by the benefit and universal grace of the supreme Father, are saved through Christ, nor will any perish eternally, not even he who has lacked special grace, that is, faith and baptism: but only he who, by his own perpetual ingratitude and malice in this life, has prepared eternal punishments for himself: that is, he who has not received and embraced this dogma of Puccius: just as he explains himself. Rat. 58.

17. With respect to the sin of our first parents, eternal destruction does not threaten anyone: but rather a blessed resurrection, and liberation from that mortality which then came upon the human race, is effectively destined for individual human beings. Rat. 5.

18. The name Eve imposed upon the first parent shows that all human beings are to be brought to life equally through her: and that distinction which excludes a good part of humanity is from the evil Spirit.

This is, to be sure, a bilge and a sink of the grossest errors and blasphemies, utterly overturning the base and foundation of the entire Christian Religion. For, to pass over in silence now those errors which strike gravely and heretically at other Articles of the purer Religion: certainly that error is intolerable which wickedly defiles and contaminates the doctrine concerning the eternal predestination, or election of the children of GOD to salvation. For it defends such an efficacy of the merit of Christ, that all become participants in it, even those who are ignorant of Christ, provided only that they do not resist Nature and reason, which persuades each individual to have faith in GOD. And that this is the saving faith, the substance of which is in individual human beings: because all naturally believe that GOD is a benefactor to those who are devoted to Him: and therefore no one is to be held as an infidel, unless he neglects the Object most worthy of faith, namely GOD, and neglects His servants and common reason.

The opinion of those who have determined that even the sounder Gentiles, outside of Christ and faith, will eventually be saved, has a great kinship with this impiety: because they lived justly and honestly: and from the visible things of this world, they recognized and proclaimed the power, and the wisdom, and the immense goodness of GOD. In which opinion were Theobaldus Thamerus: Bart. Latomus: Jacobus Andradius: Martinus Isengrinius: Huldricus Zwinglius in his Confession to the King of the Gauls, who also places Hercules, Theseus, Socrates, Aristides, Antigonus, Numa, Camillus, the Catos, and the Scipios into the number of the Elect. Whose opinion also, from the Calvinian race, was praised with a full hand by Bullinger, Pastor of the Church of Zurich; Lavater in Hist. Sacram. p. 26; Rodolphus Gwaltherus, having published an apology for Zwingli his father-in-law. Although Beza opposed himself most rightly to all these, and condemned this opinion as impious and heretical: in his book on punishing heretics with the sword.

The principal arguments by which Puccius wished to fight for the confirmation of his dogma are derived partly from the universal and immense mercy of GOD: partly from the integrity of the powers of free will: and partly, finally, from those places of Scripture which assert that GOD wills all men to be saved. But these betray a manifest heresy: and when compared to the analogy of faith, they are clearly of no strength or moment. For first, the mercy of GOD is indeed universal and immense: yet it is not absolute: but ordered, imparting eternal salvation actually only to those who perseveringly believe in the Son. The second argument is constructed from false presuppositions. For in a man not yet reborn, there is so little virtue of free will remaining in spiritual matters that he does not understand the things that are of the Spirit of GOD, indeed he cannot even understand them, but they are foolishness to him: 1 Cor. 2:14. The third and final defense again confuses the absolute and the ordered will of GOD. God indeed wills all men to be saved, but in an ordered way, and under the condition of faith in Christ: Which failing, it comes to pass that even the far greatest part of men perish eternally. Since it is no less the will of GOD that he who does not believe shall be condemned, Mark 16:16 and John 3:18. Let this stupendous impiety of Puccius therefore depart from our Churches and Schools: which we deem unworthy of even a more laborious refutation. Whoever nevertheless desires it, let him consult the most learned writing of that great Theologian Dr. Lucas Osiander, expressly opposed to the Puccian blasphemies in the year 1593. We make our approach to HUBERIANISM.

but he contends that it is common even to those adults who receive the Sacrament of Baptism without any faith and under mere hypocrisy, that is, that hypocrites as well as believers are regenerated. The LATTER was concerning the Universal Justification of all men. For at the time when Christ was made a victim on the altar of the cross for the sins of the whole human race, at that very moment he contends that a universal justification of all men was also made before GOD: so that truly and properly, by the very act and work, all men in the universe were then justified in the sight of GOD.

To palliate this error in any way, he sought support from the article of Predestination: so that, just as he asserted an indeterminate Universality of Regeneration and Justification, so too he asserted an indeterminate Universality of Predestination, by a new and hitherto unheard-of dogma in the Christian world. Although by the benefit of divine clemency it came to pass that, upon the accurate information of both his colleagues and other Theologians, Huber recognized both of the former errors—and indeed the one concerning Justification more easily and readily, but the one concerning Baptism more slowly and with difficulty—and both first privately, and afterwards publicly, retracted and rejected them; which can be attested by the autograph of the Author himself: yet in the last error of Universal Predestination he fixed his foot, indeed he hardened his heart as it were, so that by no labors of the colloquies held, by no censures of the Academies, by no judgments of the Churches, has he been able to be brought to a sounder mind thus far: but even today he strives to keep his own corrupt mind, 2 Tim. 3:8.

But first of all, the true and legitimate state of the Controversy must be well observed, which the followers of Huber (who, however, by the grace of GOD are very few, and most of them hide timidly behind the bushes) are accustomed to obscure and pervert in various ways, so that the question of what is properly being disputed between the parties cannot be sufficiently understood.

Latin:

III. ERROR FRANCISCI Puccij; & D. Samuelis Huberi & asseclarum.

I. DE PUCCIANISMO.

CIrca annum Christi nonagesimum secundum supra sesquimillesimum, Franciscus Puccius Filidinus; Patriâ Florentinus, libellum quendam typis evulgavit, Goudæ impressum, cum hoc titulo: Assertio Catholica de Christi Servatoris efficacitate &c. ita certè conscriptum, ut evidenter pateat, hominem istum nulli certæ Religioni fuisse addictum, sed tale doctrinæ genus fovisse, quod Schvvenckfeldianismum, Anabaptismum, Jesuvvitismum, Calvinismum, Judaismum confirmaret : imò religionem Christianam universam, bonos mores, & pietatem omnem funditùs subrueret & everteret : id quod ex sequentibus doctrinæ ipsius flosculis videre licet:

1. Scripturæ sacræ ea interpretatio est humanissima, & æquissima, quæ undiq; sibi cohæret, & communi ac naturali rationi, æquitati divinæ & humanæ est consentanea. pag. 1. & 7.

2. Fides, quâ prisci patres sunt justificati, naturalis & notissima fuit. pag. 57.

3. Cavendum, ne pro fide generali, omnibus communi, accipiamus, aut supponamus spem sive fidem Messiæ, conceptam ex DEI promissionibus : pag. 60. Rat. 88.

4. Toto cœlo errant, quicunq; hanc obscuram spem antiquorum, ex promissionibus conceptam, pro fide justificâ accipiunt. ibid.

5. Simplex ignoratio (verbi & Sacramentorum) nemini potest esse fraudi : sed exitium imminet ijs duntaxat, qui veris DEI servis (qualem se solum, & socios venditat) reclamant. Rat. 58.

6. Cavendum est, ne putemus quenquam amittere jus hæreditatis ex simplice defectu prædicationis aut Sacramentorum : Nam Cœlestis Regis benevolentia, totum genus humanum complectens, multò latiùs patet, quàm externi illi ritus, Rat. 81. 109.

7. In singulis hominibus est ὑπόστασις sive substantia salvificæ fidei, ac proindè omnes sunt apti nati ad vitam æternam. Rat. 9.

8. Singuli mortales sunt in statu salutis, antequàm degenerent. Rat. 10.

9. Omnes & singuli homines habendi sunt pro fidelibus, antequàm suâ malitiâ, & diffidentiâ, DEO & servis ejus fidem derogant. Rat. 43.

10. Nemini exitium imminet, nisi qui pervicaciter adhærent mundanis, & tenebricosis sectis: Siquidem omnis ignoratio excusat peccantes. Rat. 54. & 55.

11. Singuli humani & benefici erga alios homines sunt agnoscendi pro Christianis virtualiter, & salvandi : Inhumani verò sunt perdendi : id quod divinæ æquitati maximè congruit. Nam cùm perpauci sint mortales, qui Christum nominatim & historicè agnoscere potuerunt : ideò æquissimum est, ut quisq; judicetur, prout se gessit, cum Christi fratribus. Rat. 47.

12. Nullum est peccatum, nisi voluntarium, ac proinde labes Originalis non est peccatum, sed fomes. Rat. 13.

13. Primi parentes per lapsum non sunt spoliati donis & beneficijs, quibus ab optimo creatore ornati fuerunt. Rat. 14.

14. Originale vitium non iram, sed misericordiam DEI provocat. Rom. 11, 25. 28. 29.

15. Præcones Christiani mille annis ante cæteros mortales resurgent: Et extremi judicij tempus, non unius diei, sed plurium, & ad minimum septem annorum opus erit.

16. Omnes & singuli homines beneficio & gratiâ Universali summi Patris, sunt per Christum servati, neq; ullus in æternum peribit, nec ille, qui gratiâ speciali, hoc est, fide & baptismo caruerit: sed is tantùm, qui suâ perpetuâ ingratitudine ac malitiâ in hâc vitâ, æternas sibi pœnas parârit: hoc est, qui dogma hoc Puccij non receperit, & amplexus fuerit: quemadmodum semetipsum explicat. Rat. 58.

17. Respectu peccati primorum parentum, non imminet cuiquam æternum exitium: sed beata potiùs resurrectio, & liberatio ab illâ mortalitate, quæ tunc supervenit generi humano, destinata est singulis hominibus efficaciter. Rat. 5.

18. Nomen Hevæ impositum primæ parenti, ostendit omnes homines ex æquo per illam vivificandos: & ea distinctio, quæ excludit bonam hominum partem, est à malo Spiritu.

Sentina nimirùm hæc est, & colluvies crassissimorum errorum, & blasphemiarum, universæ Religionis Christianæ basin ac fundamentum penitùs evertens. Nam ut eos errores, qui in alios Religionis purioris Articulos graviter & hæreticè impingunt, silentio nunc involvamus: certè intolerabilis est error ille, qui doctrinam de æternâ prædestinatione, sive electione filiorum DEI ad salutem nefariè conspurcat, & contaminat. Talem enim meriti Christi efficacitatem propugnat, cujus participes fiant omnes, etiam qui ignorant Christum, si modò non repugnent Naturæ & rationi, quæ singulis suadeat, ut DEO fidem habeant. Et hanc esse salvificam fidem, cujus substantia sit in singulis hominibus: quia omnes naturaliter credant DEUM esse beneficium sui Studiosis: & proptereà neminem habendum esse pro infideli, nisi qui Objectum, fide dignissimum, DEUM scilicet, negligat, servos ejus, & communem rationem negligat.

Magnam cum hâc impietate cognationem habet eorum sententia, qui Gentiles etiam saniores, extra Christum & fidem, tandem salvatum iri statuerunt: eò quòd justè ac honestè vixerint: & ex mundi hujus visibilibus, DEI & potentiam, & sapientiam, & bonitatem immensam agnoverint, & prædicârint. Quâ in sententiâ fuerunt Theobaldus Thamerus: Bart. Latomus: Jacobus Andradius: Martinus Isengrinius: Huldricus Zvvinglius in Confessione ad Regem Galliarum, qui Herculem quoque, Theseum, Socratem, Aristidem, Antigonum, Numam, Camillum, Catones, Scipiones, in numerum Electorum collocat. Cujus etiam sententiam ex gente Calvinianâ plenâ manu collaudarunt, Bullingerus Pastor Ecclesiæ Tigurinæ: Lavaterus hist. Sacram. pag. 26. Rodolphus Gwaltherus editâ apologiâ pro Zvvinglio focero suo. Quanquàm his omnibus rectissimè Beza se opposuit, & opinionem hanc, ceu impiam & hæreticam damnavit: in lib. de hæreticis gladio puniendis.

Argumenta præcipua, quibus Puccius pro confirmando suo dogmate pugnare voluit, petita sunt partim ab universali & immensâ DEI misericordiâ: partim ab integritate virium liberi arbitrii: partim denique ex illis Scripturæ locis, quæ asserunt, DEUM velle omnes homines salvari. Verùm manifestam hæresin isthæc produnt: & ad analogiam fidei collota, nullius planè sunt roboris & momenti. Nam primùm misericordia DEI est quidem Universalis & immensa: non tamen est absoluta: sed ordinata, salutem æternam actu illis tantùm impertiens, qui in Filium perseveranter credunt. Alterum argumentum ex falsis extructum est præsuppositis. Nam homini nondùm renato, usque adeò nulla virtus liberi arbitrii in spiritualibus est reliqua, ut non intelligat, quæ sunt Spiritus DEI, imò ne possit quidem intelligere, sed stultitia sint ipsi: 1. Corinth. 2. v. 14. Tertium & postremum præsidium rursus confundit voluntatem DEI absolutam, & ordinatam. Deus quidem vult omnes homines salvos, sed ordinatè, & sub conditione fidei in Christum: Quâ deficiente sit, ut etiam multò maxima hominum pars æternùm pereat. Siquidem haud minus DEI est voluntas, ut qui non crediderit, condemnetur, Marc. 16. v. 6. & Joh. 3. v. 18. Facessat proindè stupenda hæc Puccii impietas ab Ecclesiis, & Scholis nostris: quâ etiam operosiore refutatione in indignam arbitramur. Qui tamen eam desiderat, consulat scriptum eruditissimum Magni illius Theologi D. Lucæ Osiandri, Anno 1593. blasphemiis Puccianis ex professo oppositum. Nos ad HUBERIANISMUM accessum facimus.

sed adultorum etiam eorum, qui sine omni fide, & sub merâ hypocrisi Sacramentum Baptismi percipiũt, communem esse, hoc est, tàm hypocritas, quàm fideles regenerari contendit. POSTERIOR fuit de Universali omnium hominum Iustificatione, Nam quo tempore Christus in arâ crucis factus est victima, pro totius generis humani peccatis, eo ipso universalem etiam contendit esse factam coram DEO justificationem omnium hominum: adeò, ut verè & propriè, facto ipso atque opere, tùm in conspectu DEI omnes in universum homines fuerint justificati.

Utrique huic errori quoquo modo palliando, ex Prædestinationis articulo subsidium quæsivit: ita, ut, quemadmodum Regenerationis, & Iustificationis; ita Prædestinationis quoque indeterminatam Universalitatem, novo & prius inaudito planè in orbe Christiano dogmate, assereret. Quanquàm verò divinæ clementiæ beneficio factum est, ut ad accuratam tùm Collegarum, tùm aliorum Theologorum informationem, H. berns utrumq; priorem errorem, & eum quidem, qui est de Iustificatione, faciliùs & expeditiùs: eum verò, qui est de Baptismo, tardiùs & difficiliùs agnosceret, & ambos privatim primùm, posteà publice etiam retractaret & abjiceret; id quod ipsius Autoris ἀυτογράφῳ testatum effici potest: tamen in postremo errore Universalis Prædestinationis obtinendo pedem fixit, imò ita callum quasi obduxit, ut nullis colloquiorum habitorum laboribus, nullis Academiarum censuris, nullis Ecclesiarum judiciis, ad saniorem mentem reduci hactenùs potuerit: quin hodieq́ve κατεφθαρμένος τὴν νῦν, 2. Tim. 3. v. 8. ἵδιον φυλάττειν studeat.

Est autem primùm omnium status Controversiæ verus ac legitimus probè observandus, quem asseclæ Huberi (quorum tamen DEI beneficio paucissimi sunt, & plærique post carecta timidiusculè latitant) variè obscurare, & pervertere solent, ut quà de re propriè inter partes disceptantes sit quæstio, non satis intelligi possit.


### Part II. Πολεμικη (Polemic): II. Concerning Huberianism

II. Concerning Huberianism.

Although we do not join Dr. Samuel Huber to Francesco Pucci to that end, as if we were to establish that the doctrine and opinion of both concerning Predestination is absolutely one and the same: For we ourselves recognize a clear diversity: yet in general, a great kinship and similarity, with respect to the universal Predestination of all men to salvation, can by no means be denied to exist between Huber's dogma and Puccianism. For he teaches and contends: That all men to a man, with none at all excepted, are chosen and Predestined by GOD to eternal life and salvation.

But in the beginning, it is not disputed whether God has embraced the whole human race with fatherly love and favor: and whether He seriously wills all men, with no one excepted or excluded, to be saved? For on our part also, we hold and defend the affirmative entirely: indeed, we have asserted it thus far invincibly against the Calvinists.

Furthermore, neither does the hinge of the controversy turn on this, whether Christ rendered to his eternal Father a most full satisfaction and propitiation for the sins of the whole human race, and thus also for the sins of the reprobate, by the λύτρον of his death and obedience: of an eternal and most sufficient redemption, acquired by the merit of his passion for all men, not only for the faithful, but also for the infidels? For also concerning this

Moreover, two other frenzies rather than errors, introduced into the Church by the same man, provided the occasion for defending this fanatical opinion: the PRIOR of which was concerning REGENERATION, which Huberus constituted as a substantial part of Baptism: and therefore not only of the faithful, who are baptized in infancy, We agree with Huber in every respect regarding the affirmative of the question, against the Calvinists.

Finally, neither does this come into question: Is it the good pleasure and command of the eternal Father that the benefits acquired by the death of Christ be preached equally to not just someone, or a few, but to the whole creation, that is, to all men, not even one excepted, and once preached, be heard by all in the voice of the Gospel, and be received by true faith? For regarding this question, a most firm consensus exists between us and Huber.

But the proper and legitimate state of the controversy consists solely in this: Does the eternal election of those to be saved extend itself as much to the evil and unbelieving as to the good and faithful; so that all men, with no one excepted, were elected by GOD from eternity to eternal life: or does it pertain only to the good and believing, or the beloved sons of GOD, who, persevering in the faith of Christ to the very end, finally obtain eternal salvation in fact? Regarding which κρινόμενον (point of judgment), all Orthodox embrace the latter part affirmatively according to the Scriptures, and have hitherto defended it invincibly: Huber, however, having denied the latter part, has hitherto endeavored to assert the affirmative of the former by a new example and by stirring up a new schism: but with every effort and labor in vain.

The arguments with which he has unhappily fought hitherto, he could produce absolutely none from the Holy Scriptures, so much so that in the colloquies instituted with him, both elsewhere and especially at Torgau, being asked and admonished more than a hundred times to produce at least one single dictum of Scripture, or testimony of an Orthodox Father, by which he could prove the approbation of his dogma, in those terms, as they say, that terminate it: Scarcely at last, after an entire three days had already passed, did he bring forth the first chapter of the Epistle to the Ephesians, in which alone he asserted that the whole foundation of his opinion consisted: with six arguments especially constructed from it, in this order:

1. Whomever God has rendered dear through the Son, or has loved in the beloved, these He has also predestined to eternal life: Eph. 1:5-6. But He has rendered the whole world, or all men, dear to Himself through the Son, or has loved them in the beloved. John 3:16. Therefore, He has also elected all men to eternal life.

are, all things have also been restored by Christ reconciling them, verse 10. Therefore, all things also in heaven and on earth, namely all men, are also predestined.

V. If predestination was made according to the revelation of the secret good pleasure, then certainly we are all predestined. But the former is true, according to the Apostle, verse 9. Therefore, the latter is also. The reason for the connection in the proposition is this: Because that revelation of the good pleasure of God was made through the Gospel, which pertains to all men.

VI. Where Paul says that WE were elected before the foundations of the world were laid in Christ, there he says that we are all elected. But he says the former, verse 4. Therefore, this latter is also true.

And with these arguments indeed, taken from Scripture, Huber fought; what strength and moment they have will easily appear once the responses of our theologians have been observed.

The FIRST argument, therefore, fails by the sophism of equivocation, whence a shameful πλατυσπεῖα (broad-speaking) of four terms emerges. For there is one GENERAL Love, with which the minor proposition deals, from John 3:16, with which GOD pursues the whole human race equally. There is another SPECIAL Love, with which the Apostle deals in Eph. 1:6, with which not all are loved in the beloved, who by reason of universal merit have been redeemed by the beloved: but those who are found in the beloved by the act itself. However, he who is not in the faith of Christ is not in the beloved. This special love of GOD is not of all men, but is proper to the elect and the children of GOD: namely of those who, according to the clear description of the Apostle, are holy, are faithful in Christ Jesus, are blessed with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places, are blameless, are adopted as sons, are HAVING redemption through the blood of Christ, and the remission of sins according to the riches of His grace v. 1, 3, 4, 5, & 7. Whoever, with Huber, extends this special love of GOD to all men in general, he manifestly contradicts 1. the most open context of Paul's words. 2. the article of Justification, which is nothing other than the remission of sins, Rom. 4. v. 6. & 7. likewise the article of Sanctification, which is not common to all men. 3. He contradicts the doctrine περὶ τῆς ὑιοθεσίας concerning the adoption of the children of GOD, which does not befall all, but only believers, John 1. v. 12. & 13. Gal. 3. v. 7. 4. To all ancient and recent interpreters alike. It is therefore absurd to twist this special love of GOD to all men, even those not holy, not faithful to Jesus Christ, not blessed, not adopted as children of GOD, not having the remission of sins. FURTHERMORE, the crime of forgery is also committed in the corrupted Apostolic text: For verse 6 of the first chapter of Ephesians does not simply contain the verb of

I I. As far as the good pleasure of the will of God extends, so that the glory of His grace may be praised: v. 5 & 6, so far also does Predestination extend. But that good pleasure extends to all men. Therefore, so does Predestination.

III. Whomever God wills to be holy and blameless, they are chosen by God from eternity v. 4. But God wills all men to be holy and blameless. Therefore, all men also are chosen by God from eternity.

IV. Whatever things are restored through Christ: they are also predestined. But all things which are in heaven and on earth loving, as in John 3:16, but the more emphatic term for accepting into favor (ἐχαρίτωσεν), with which acceptance the wrath of GOD cannot be joined, to which the greatest part of the world is subject, whom nevertheless GOD is rightly said to love, but not to accept into favor, speaking properly and specifically. But that special love, which is proper to the Elect, the Savior himself asserts to be so constituted that it is always led through to the end: a thing which certainly cannot be affirmed of the reprobate and the damned; for they are pressed by the wrath of GOD, John 3:36. To this pertains that of John 13:1: Christ, who loved his own who were in the world, loved them TO THE END.

The major proposition of the second argument labors under a manifest begging of the question. The minor is simply false: 1. Because it overturns the Apostolic distinction between vessels of grace and of wrath, to the former of which alone the Apostle attributes the riches of his glory, Rom. 9:23. But Huberus attributes this to all men without distinction. Therefore he manifestly contradicts the Apostle. 2. Because it removes the distinction between law and Gospel. 3. The distinction between those to be saved and those to be damned. 4. Because it confuses the Church of Christ with the synagogue of the wicked: that is, it mixes heaven with earth: and removes the names of both cities, namely of GOD and of the devils. 5. It contradicts manifest Scripture, which asserts that it is impossible to please GOD without faith, Heb. 11:6, and declares that in Christ alone, apprehended by faith, the εὐδοκίαν (good pleasure) of GOD the Father is to be sought, Matt. 3:17 and ch. 17:5.

Huberus objects, and for the confirmation of the major, brings forward those sayings of Scripture which prove that all men were created through the Son, and indeed to the likeness of GOD: nay, created in Christ Jesus unto good works, Eph. 2:10. But a gross ἄγνοια ἐλέγχη (ignorance of refutation) is committed. For the former sayings treat of creation, and are most absurdly transferred to Predestination: otherwise even the devils would be predestined, because even the devils were created through the Son, Col. 1:16. The passage from ch. 2 of Ephesians treats only of those who are saved through faith, as the συνέχεια (continuity) of the whole text most clearly demonstrates. And this is also one of the new phrases of Huberus, that All men were created in CHRIST JESUS unto good works.

Huberus framed the third argument in another form also, but of the same sense, in these words:

Whoever so establishes election, that we are chosen in him, that we should be holy and blameless, and sons of GOD: he establishes Universal Election. But Paul so establishes Election. Therefore.

It is answered, however, that the proposition is manifestly false; which shines forth more clearly if two things are considered in that argument. 1. The mind of the Apostle, or the genuine sense of the words, which is not to be taken of a bare intention merely in the divine mind and will, which is very often hindered by the malice of men: but of the actual, or effectual acquisition of holiness and innocence, of which the Apostle also treats, Rom. 11:7: What Israel was seeking, he has not obtained: but the Election has obtained it. For this holiness and innocence always follows election in an inseparable bond. 2. The other is the proof, which is required in the major of the argument. But that is sought from the will of GOD, by which He wills all men to be holy and blameless: where the end is noted, not as Election attains it: but as it turns within the sole will and the bare terms of the divine intention. It is evident, therefore, that Huberus plays with an αμφιβολία (ambiguity) or equivocation of phrase, while he holds and accepts as the same thing the Election by which we are holy, and the will of GOD that we should be such: that is, he shamefully confuses the end of a bare intention with the act or effect of the work itself. Nor is it worth a farthing that Huberus infers thus in confirming the major: We are all created for the glory of GOD: which glory we do not place in the punishments of men, as the Calvinists are wont to do: but in holiness and ὑιοθεσία (adoption): and we are created unto good works. Therefore we are all adopted as sons, and consequently elected. For that is a frivolous digression: since that end of Creation was interrupted by the fall of Adam, so that now we are no longer rendered holy, blameless, and Sons of GOD from Creation: but from another principle entirely, and in another way and order, namely from the fullness of the merit of Christ through faith. Furthermore, if this quibble of Huberus militates in the present article of Election, it will also militate in the article of justification: in which it will be likewise permissible to argue thus: We are all created for the glory of GOD, which glory is to be placed in holiness and ὑιοθεσία (adoption). Therefore we are all justified. Or in this manner: GOD justifies us for this reason, that we might be holy before him, and blameless. But GOD wills that all men be such. Therefore all are justified, or are being justified.

Latin:

II. De Huberianismo.

QUanqvàm verò Doft. Samuelem Huberum non eo fine Francisco Puccio adjungimus, quasi statuamus, unam prorsus, eandemq́; utriusque de Prædestinatione esse doctrinam ac sententiam: Nam luculentam diversitatem ipsimet agnoscimus: in genere tamen magnam cognationem ac similitudinem, respectu universalis Prædestinationis omnium hominum ad salutem, Huberi dogmati cum Puccianismo intercedere, negari nullâ ratione potest. Docet enim ille, & contendit. Omnes ad unum homines, nullo omnium excepto, esse à DEO ad vitam & salutem aternam electos & Prædestinatos.

Initio autem non de eo controvertitur: An Deus totum genus humanum paterno amore & favore complexus sit: & universos homines, nemine excepto, aut excluso, seriò salvari velit? Nam ex nostra etiam parte affirmativam omninò tenemus & defendimus:- imò hactenus contra Calviniānos invictè asseruimus.

Deindè neq; in eo vertitur Controversiæ cardo, An Christus pro totius generis humani, & sic pro reproborum etiã peccatis, æterno suo Patri plenissimam Satisfactiōnem & propitiationem, mortis & obedientiæ suæ λύτρον præstiterit: æternæ & sufficientißimæ Redemtionis, omnibus hominibus, non fidelibus tantùm: sed infidelibus etiam paßionis suæ merito acquisitæ ? Nam & circa hujus

Occasionem autem fanaticæ huic opinioni defendendæ duo alii furores potiùs, quàm errores in Ecclesiam ab eodem invecti, præbuerunt: quorum PRIOR de REGENERATIONE fuit, quam Huberus partem Baptismi substantialem constituit: ac proindè non fidelium tantùm, qui in infantia baptisantur: Quæstionis Affirmativam, contra Calvinianos, Hubero per omnia adstipulamur.

Tandem neq; illud in quæstionem venit: An beneplacitum & mandatum sit æterni Patris, ut beneficia, morte Christi acquisita, non aliquis duntaxat, aut paucis quibusdam; sed universæ creaturæ, hoc est, omnibus hominibus, ne uno quidem excepto, ex æquo prædicentur, prædicata in voce Evangelii ab omnibus audiantur, & verâ fide recipiantur? Nam & circa hanc quæstionem consensus nobis & Hubero intercedit firmissimus.

Verùm in eo status controversiæ proprius ac legitimus unicè consistit: An æterna Salvandorum Electio extendat se tàm ad malos, & incredulos, quàm ad bonos & fideles; ita ut universi homines, nemine excepto, sint à DEO ab æterno electi ad vitam æternam: an verò pertineat duntaxat ad bonos & credentes, sive dilectos DEI filios, qui in fide Christi ad finem usque perseverantes, salutem æternam tandem ipso facto consequuntur. Circa quod κρινόμενον Orthodoxi omnes posteriorem ejus partem affirmatè secundum Scripturas amplexantur, & invictè hactenus propugnarunt: Huberus autem negatâ posteriori parte, Prioris affirmativam novo exemplo, novoq; Schismate concitato, hactenus asserere studuit: sed irrito omni conatu, & labore.

Argumenta, quibus infeliciter hactenus pugnavit, ex Scripturis sacris planè nulla proferre potuit, adeò, ut in distinctis tùm alibi, tùm Torgæ cumprimis cum ipso institutis colloquiis, plus centies rogatus, & admonitus, u. nicum saltem proferret Scripturæ dictum, aut Patris Orthodoxi testimonium, quo dogmatis sui approbationem, iis terminis, uti loquuntur, terminantibus, evincere posset: Vix tandem post integrum jam elapsum triduum, primum Epistolæ ad Ephesios caput protulit, in quo uno sententiæ suæ firmamentum omne consistere afferuit: sex potissimum argumentis inde extructis, hoc ordine:

1. Quoscunq; Deus charos reddidit per Filium, sive dilexit in dilecto, hos etiam prædestinavit ad vitam æternam: Ephes. 1. v. 5 6. Atqui totum mundum, sive omnes homines charos sibi reddidit per Filium, sive dilexit in dilecto. Ioh. 3, 16. Ergo omnes etiam homines ad vitam æternam elegit.

sunt, restaurata etiam sunt per Christum omnia reconciliantem vers. 10. Ergo omnia etiam in cælo & in terra, omnes nimirum homines etiam sunt prædestinati.

V. Si secundum arcani beneplaciti revelationem facta est prædestinatio, utiq; omnes sumus prædestinati. At prius verum, teste Apostolo, vers. 9. Ergo & posterius. Ratio connexi in propositione est isthæc: Quia revelatio illa beneplaciti Dei facta est per Evangelium, quod pertinet ad omnes homines.

VI. Ubi Paulus dicit, NOS esse electos ante jacta fundamenta seculi in Christo, ibi dicit, quod omnes simus electi. At prius illud dicit, vers. 4. Ergo & hoc posterius.

Et his quidem argumentis ex Scripturâ petitis pugnavit Huberus, quæ cujus sint roboris ac momenti, observatis nostrorum Theologorum responsionibus, facilè patebit.

PRIMUM igitur argumentum fallit Sophismate æquivocationis, unde turpis πλατυσπεῖα quatuor terminorum emergit. Nam alia est Dilectio GENERALIS, de quâ agit minor propositio, ex cap. 3. v. 16. Johannis, quâ totum genus humanum DEUS ex æquo prosequitur. Alia est Dilectio SPECIALIS, de quâ Apostolus agit Ephes. 1. v. 6. quâ in dilecto diliguntur non omnes, qui ratione universalis meriti sunt redemti per dilectum: sed qui ipso actu in dilecto reperiuntur. Non est autem in dilecto, qui non est in fide Christi. Hæc dilectio DEI specialis, non omnium hominum, sed electorum, & filiorum DEI est propria: eorum nim: qui secundum luculentam descriptionem Apostoli, sunt sancti, sunt fideles in Christo Iesu, sunt benedicti omni benedictione spirituali in cœlestibus, sunt irreprehensibiles, sunt adoptati in filios, sunt HABENTES redemtionem per sanguinem Christi, & remissionem peccatorum secundum divitias gratiæ ipsius v. 1. 3. 4. 5. & 7. Hanc dilectionem DEI specialem quisquis cùm Hubero ad omnes in universum homines extendit, ille manifestè contradicit 1. apertissimo verborum Pauli contextui. 2. articulo Justificationis, quæ nihil aliud est, quàm remissio peccatorum, Rom. 4. v. 6. & 7. articulo item Sanctificationis, quæ non omnibus hominibus communis est 3. Contradicit doctrinæ περὶ τῆς ὑιοθεσίας de adoptione filiorum DEI, quæ non omnibus, sed solis credentibus obtingit, Joh. 1. v. 12. & 13. Gal. 3. v. 7. 4. Omnibus veteribus simul & recentioribus interpretibus, Absurdum ergò, dilectionem hanc DEI specialem detorquere ad Omnes homines, etiam non sanctos, non fideles Iesu Christi, non benedictos, non adoptatos in filios DEI, non habentes remissionem peccatorum. DEINDE committitur etiam crimen falsi in depravato textu Apostolico: Nam vers. 6. Ephesiorum capitis primi non simpliciter habetur verbum Di-

I I. Quousq; beneplacitum voluntatis Dei tenditur, ut laudetur gloria gratiæ suæ: vers. 5. & 6. eousq; etiam extenditur Prædestinatio. Atqui beneplacitum illud extenditur ad omnes homines. Ergo etiam Prædestinatio.

III. Quoscunq; Deus vult esse sanctos & irrepensibiles, illi sunt à Deo ab æterno electi vers. 4. Atqui Deus vult omnes homines sanctos & irreprehensibiles. Ergo omnes etiam homines à Deo ab æterno sunt electi.

IV. Quæcunq; sunt restaurata per Christum: ea etiam sunt prædestinata. Atqui omnia quæ in cælo & in terrâ ligendi, ficut Johan. 3. v. 16. sed terminus ἐμφατικώτερος acceptandi in gratiam (ἐχαρίτωσεν) cum quâ acceptatione ira DEI conjuncta esse non potest, cui subjacet maxima mundi pars, quem totum tamen DEUS diligere, non verò in gratiam acceptare, propriè & fpecificè loquendo, rectè dicitur. Specialem autem dilectionem illam, quæ Electorum est propria, Servator ipse ita comparatam esse asserit, ut semper ad finem usq; perducatur: id quod certè de reprobis & damnatis affirmari non potest; quippè quos premit ira DEI Johan. 3. v. 36. Pertinet huc illud Joh. 13. v. 1. Christus qui dilexit suos, qui erant in mundo, IN FINEM USQUE dilexit eos.

SECUNDI argumenti Major propositio laborat manifestâ petitione principii. Minor simpliciter falsa est: 1. Quia evertit discrimen Apostolicum inter vasa gratiæ & iræ, quorum illis tantùm tribuit Apostolus divitiâs gloriæ suæ. Rom. 9. v. 23. At Huberus sine discrimine hoc tribuit omnibus hominibus. Ergò manifestè contradicit Apostolo. 2. Quia tollit discrimen legis & Evangelii. 3. discrimen salvandorum & damnandorum. 4. Quia confundit Ecclesiam Christi cum Synagogâ improborum: hoc est, cœlum terræ miscet: & tollit nomina utriusque civitatis, nempè DEI, & Diabolorum. 5. Contradicit manifestæ Scripturæ, quæ asserit, Impossibile esse, sine fide placere DEO, Hebr. 11. v. 6. inqve solo Christo fide apprehenso, εὐδοκίαν beneplacitum DEI patris quærendum esse pronunciat, Matth. 3. v. 17. & cap. 17. v. 5.

Excipit Huberus, & pro confirmatione Majoris profert ea Scripturæ dicta, quæ probant, omnes homines per filium esse conditos, & quidem ad similitudinem DEI: imò conditos in Christo Jesu ad bona opera. Ephes. 2. v. 10. Verùm crassa ἄγνοια ἐλέγχη commititur. Nam priora dicta agunt de creatione, & absurdissimè transferuntur ad Prædestinationem: alio quin etiam Diaboli essent prædestinati, quia etiam Diaboli per Filium sunt conditi. Coloss. 1. v. 16. Locus ex cap. 2. Ephesiorum agit tantùm de his, qui per fidem servantur, ficut totiùs textų συνέχεια clarissimè demonstrat. Et est hæc etiam una ex novis phrasibus Huberi, quòd Omnes homines conditi sint in CHRISTO JESU ad bona opera.

TERTIUM argumentum Huberus aliâ etiam formâ, sed ejusdem sensus informavit, his verbis:

Quicunq; electionem ita statuit, quòd sumus in eô electi, ut Sancti, & irreprehensibiles essemus, & filii DEI: is facit Electionem Universalem. Sed Paulus Electionem ita statuit. Ergò.

Respondetur autem, Propositionem manifestè falsam esse; id quod dilucidiùs elucefcit, si duo in argumento isto considerentur. 1. Mens Apostoli, sive genuina verborum sententia, quæ non est accipienda de nudâ duntaxat intentione in mente & voluntate divina, quæ sæpissimè per hominum malitiam impeditur: sed de ipsâ actuali, sive effectuali Sanctitatis & innocentiæ acquisitione, de quâ etiam Apostolus agit, Roman. 11. vers. 7. Quod quærebat Israel, non est assecutus: Electio autem assecuta est. Electionem enim Sanctitas & innocentiæ hæc, inseparabili nexu semper sequitur. 2. Alterum est, Probatio, quæ in majore argumenti requirenda est. Ea verò à voluntate DEI petitur, quâ velit omnes homines esse sanctos & irreprehensibiles: Ubi notatur finis, non ut illum Electio assequitur: sed ut ille intrà solam voluntatem, & nudos intentionis divinæ terminos vertitur. Patet ergò αμφιβολία sive æquivocatione phrasews ludere Huberum, dùm Electionem, quâ sumus sancti, & voluntatem DEI, ut tales simus, pro iisdem habet & accipit: hoc est, finem nudæ intentionis, cum ipso actu, sive effectu operis turpiter confundit. Neq; ullius teruntii est, quòd confirmandâ Majore sic infert Huberus: Omnes sumus conditi ad gloriam DEI: quam gloriam non ponimus in suppliciis hominum: ut Calvinistæ solent: sed in sanctitate, & ὑιοθεσία: Et sumus conditi ad bona opera. Ergò omnes sumus adoptati in filios, & per consequens electi. Nam frivolum h. e. diverticulum: siquidé finis ille Creationis, per lapsum Adami interversus est, ut jam nō ampliùs ex Creatione: sed ex alio planè principio, alioq; modo & ordine, nimirum ex plenitudine meriti Christi per fidem, reddamur sancti, irreprehensibiles, & Filii DEI. Deindè si militat hæc argutia Huberi in præsenti Electionis articulo, militabit etiam in articulo justificationis: in quo sic itidem argumentari licebit: Omnes sumus conditi ad gloriam DEI, quæ gloria ponenda est in sanctitate, & ὑιοθεσία. Ergò omnes sumus justificati. Vel in hunc modum: Ideò nos DEUS justificat, ut fimus sancti coram illo, & irreprehensibiles. Atqui vult DEUS, ut omnes homines sint tales. Ergò omnes sunt justificati, vel justificantur.


### Part II. Πολεμικη (Polemic): II. Concerning Huberianism (continued)

He was accustomed to weave the fourth argument in another form likewise in this manner:

Where, on account of the restoration of all things which are in heaven and on earth, which was done through Christ reconciling all things, we are said to be predestined: there a Universal Election of all is established, Eph. 1:10. But on account of this restoration of all things, done through Christ reconciling all things which are in heaven and on earth, we are said to be predestined: Eph. 1 in the verse already cited 10, and Col. 1:19 and 20. Therefore a Universal predestination of all is established.

I answer that this argument is of the same futility. For it concludes just as if someone were to gather in this manner: Where we are said to be predestined on account of the merit of redemption done by Christ: there a Universal Election is established. But the former is asserted by the Apostle in the cited passage: Therefore this latter is also established. There is, of course, no connection in the major. For the Apostle speaks of that ἀνακεφαλαιώσει (recapitulation) or restoration, which is done by Christ through his death, among

GOD and man, by which indeed men are reconciled with GOD: nay, even the society which had existed between men and the Angels is restored again. Coloss. 1. v. 20. From which restoration follows the gathering and conjunction of the spiritual kingdom of Christ, which was begun by Him through His death and resurrection, and also through the preaching of the Gospel, in which all things are subject to Him as Lord and head. Psalm 8. so that he who does not have Christ, has no part in GOD. Furthermore, this restoration made through Christ is no less the foundation of our Justification than of our Election. For if it had been without this restoration of Christ, no one could be justified, just as no one could be predestined. Now, however, just as Universal Justification is not effected by this restoration of Christ, so neither is Universal Predestination. Then Huber does not notice that the universal particle ALL in the Apostolic text does not so much refer to men, as, besides men, to God and the Angels, who are reconciled to one another through Christ. Thirdly, Reconciliation is confused with Predestination; neither of which, in relation to us, excludes Faith. For although by His merit He reconciled the whole world to God the Father, yet the fruit of this Reconciliation does not redound except to believers: as the Apostle attests, Col. 1. 22. & 23. He reconciled you in the Body of His Flesh through death, to present you holy, and unblemished, and irreproachable before Him: IF ONLY YOU REMAIN FOUNDED AND STABLE IN THE FAITH, AND WILL NOT BE MOVED from the hope of the Gospel which you have heard, etc. Finally, Huber cannot show even one interpreter who has explained this passage concerning Universal Election.

Huber is also accustomed to frame the FIFTH argument in this fashion: Wherever we are predestined according to the revelation of the secret good pleasure of God: there we are all predestined: Therefore we are all predestined. He proved the connection of the major premise thus: Wherever Scripture shows the Son, who restored all things, and there fully manifested Himself toward us: there we are predestined according to the revelation of the secret good pleasure: and consequently: All are predestined. But the Apostle in this chapter 1. Eph. v. 10. shows the Son, who restored all things. Therefore.

I answer that this argument consists of disconnected scopes, so that no legitimate connection of terms appears in his entire System: which I am pleased to demonstrate analytically. The parts of the argument are these: In the Gospel God revealed the mystery concerning the good pleasure of His will. Therefore, nothing concerning the will of God will be hidden any longer, nothing will be contrary to the revealed Gospel; now God has declared His will in the Gospel in such a way that He wills all men to be saved. Therefore, Election also does not exist otherwise.

I answer 1. that an ellipsis of parts is committed in this argument. For the mystery of predestination is not completed by that antecedent and benevolent will of GOD: but that order of means is required, through which it pleased God to bring us to salvation. 2. The sayings of Scripture testifying to that benevolent will of GOD are clearly opposed to the Huberian scope, that God does not will the death of the sinner: that He wills that all be saved: that no one perish, etc. but with the mention of the Order added, they require conversion, the acknowledgment of the truth, and repentance: without which order no Election is read to have been made anywhere in the Gospel. Huber therefore displays a stupendous ignorance, who fanatically dreams that some absolute and simple will concerning the salvation of men has been revealed in the Gospel: otherwise than the Book of Concord, which teaches that eight distinct requirements must be considered in this Article: most of which Huber passes over with dry feet, and ignorantly adapts from the eternal decree of Election to the application which occurs in time. Whence in the deduction of this argument he absurdly asserts that all men are called to the lot of God: when yet the Apostle, Col. 1, 12, expressly defines that lot as THE LOT OF THE SAINTS IN LIGHT: and the whole context most manifestly proves that both passages, both to Eph. 1. and to Col. 1. can be understood only of the saints and truly faithful. For Scripture constitutes a twofold, not a threefold lot: ONE of the saints; Dan. 12, 13. You shall stand in your lot: The OTHER of hypocrites, Matth. 24. v. 51. & cap. 25, v. 46.

Huber's SIXTH argument fixes its foot on the pronoun US, which he dreamed denoted the whole complex of the human race. But against and beyond the suffrage of the Apostolic text. For who the men are to be understood by the term of the pronoun, is evident by the Apostle himself as interpreter; namely, 1. Saints, 2. Believers in Christ, 3. blessed with every Spiritual blessing in the heavens: 4. adopted as sons of God, 5. gifted with the remission of sins, sealed with the Spirit of promise, and other marks of the Elect similar to these. But these characteristics were not even proper to all the Ephesians: much less to the whole human race. The pseudograph is therefore evident.

Then a refutation of irrelevance is committed while that which was done by Christ is immediately referred to that which is said to have been done by Christ. Certainly, propitiation for the sins of the whole world proceeds from Christ, 1. John 2, 2. But from this it is by no means consequent that all men, whether they believe or do not believe in Christ, are elected to life in Christ. For they are not said to be elected in Christ, except those who are in Christ through faith. For they are in Christ who have put on Christ in baptism, Gal. 3, 27. who are truly incorporated into Christ, 1. Cor. 12, 27. who have been grafted into the heavenly vine as fruit-bearing branches and remain there, John 15, 5. Nor does it have any moment that God is said to look upon the wounds of Christ in Election, so that from this the Universality of Election might be proven, because, forsooth, the merit of the wounds of Christ pertains to the universality of the whole human race. For God does indeed look upon the wounds of Christ: He does not look upon them merely as the works of men in the election of men, so that by the consideration of these men might be chosen, without any distinction, for eternal life, whether they believe or do not believe in the Son of God, who suffered wounds and death for us: but He looks upon them in that eternal order of His, insofar as the merit of those wounds is applied, and as it were appropriated, by the pious and believers through a faith that is true and persevering to the very end. Otherwise, this very merit of the wounds of Christ would have no more validity in the present article of election than it would in the article of justification.

And Huber ought to have remembered that the Formula of Concord expressly argues that that corruption of the Apostolic passage is false in several places. Indeed, he ought to have remembered what Blessed Luther left written in his book against the heavenly Prophets, in this manner: Scripture uses synecdoche in a common way: that is, it names some whole, and understands only some part of it: just as it does when it calls the Israelite people the people, and the peculiar people of GOD, when nevertheless the greater part of it was always the Devil's, but the lesser part was GOD's. Just as Paul also calls the Galatians, Corinthians, and other cities, Churches of GOD, when nevertheless the smallest part consisted of TRUE CHILDREN OF GOD.

Besides these six arguments, Huber also fought with many others taken from Scripture: but they are unworthy of refutation: for their middle term, or the nerve of the proof, is clearly the same as those already refuted. But he also fought with Reasons, the chief of which we shall taste in a few words.

REASON I. Most all mysteries of the Christian Religion, and benefits of GOD are universal: such as are: The love of GOD: Providence: Redemption obtained through Christ: Vocation, which happens through the preaching of the Gospel, likewise the Evangelical promise. Therefore also Predestination.

I answer with those words by which this argument was excepted against and refuted by some other Orthodox Theologian: namely, that since that whole thing proceeds from a part, it should have been proposed for the games of boys, not for the serious assemblies of learned men. But if the Universality of Predestination is rightly established from this reason: nothing can stand in the way of the Remission of sins, Justification, Regeneration, Sanctification, and finally Glorification also, or Universal Salvation being established entirely: that is, the entire Christian doctrine being converted into the foolish Puccianism. Furthermore, it is clearly ἀθεόλογον, and fights with the entire Scripture, that Huber imagines in his brain the same breadth of Election as there is of the Love of GOD: Providence; Redemption etc. For Scripture places only the Saved and the Elect in the same degree of breadth. Whence it is that it is not simply called Election: but the Election of the Saved or of the Children of GOD, this mystery is commonly called. Finally, by most of these benefits of GOD, only acquired goods are noted, which without fruition are considered only in respect to themselves. But Election pertains to the use of all divine benefits, which without faith can be nothing, and can fall to no one. And this indeed is the general Response given to this first reason.

In particular, it is answered concerning the individual members of the Antecedent. 1. Not every love of GOD is universal: but only that by which the world is loved: John 3, v. 16. enemies are loved: Rom. 5, v. 10. But this is not that by which the Elect are loved. For the love of these, as Scripture defines, is such that it is to the end, John 13, 1.

that they may be loved in the beloved, Eph. 1, v. 4. To which love alone the Election of the saved is to be attributed. 2. From the Providence of GOD, something firm will be gathered in this article only then: if Huber proves that Election pertains even to sparrows, sheep, and oxen. 3. In the remaining members, regarding Redemption, Vocation, and the universal Promise, paralogisms of the fallacy of composition are perpetually committed. For neither the merit of Christ, either alone or simply: nor that universal Vocation or Promise of the Gospel: but only with the respect and addition of faith, is the cause of our Election. 4. In particular, it is also to be noted concerning Evangelical Promises, that they also are of two kinds. For some are simply Universal, such as those are chiefly which flow from the history of the fact, for example: That Christ died for all. That He commanded the Gospel to be preached to every creature. But others are determinately Universal, that is, they contain the promise of salvation, but always with the determination of faith in Christ.

REASON II. Of Huber: GOD has appointed no one to wrath. Therefore all are Elect.

I answer: 1. A notable Ψευδογράφημα (false writing) is committed. For the Antecedent is taken from 1 Thess. 5, v. 9, and is distorted by Huber with manifest force into a foreign meaning. For the Apostle's discourse there is only about believers alone, about the children of light and of the day, v. 5, who do not sleep, AS THE REST, but are vigilant and sober: v. 6, who are clothed with the breastplate of faith and love, and for a helmet, the hope of salvation. Therefore, concerning all these it is true that they are not placed to wrath: and that by no will of GOD, either antecedent or consequent. But concerning the remaining children of darkness and of the night, who sleep securely, and are destitute of faith and the hope of salvation, although it is true that by an antecedent will GOD has appointed no one to wrath: yet by a consequent will, because of unbelief, by a just judgment, as a punishment for impiety, GOD has appointed and destined all the impious to wrath and just damnation.

REASON III. Of Huber: GOD by an Antecedent Will passed over no one in Election. Therefore He elected all.

I answer: There is absolutely no reason for the consequence to hold; since the antecedent will, taken alone, does not constitute election, much less does it perfect or complete it. For this has already been ordained by GOD from eternity to its own end by its own certain means. Huberus therefore washes a brick, and weaves ropes from sand.

REASON IV. Of Huberus: GOD created all men in his own image. Therefore he also chose them for eternal life.

I answer, 1. If the discussion is about the fact itself, it is true only of one of the protoplasts that he was created in the image of GOD: concerning other men this is true only insofar as regards the intention of GOD, by which GOD indeed willed that all men be created in Adam in his own image. But even this intention was not simple and absolute: but determined to the perseverance of Adam in the state of integrity. Now, however, through the most sad fall, this intention also has been subverted: and the very work of divine creation itself, corrupted and lost in the first-formed. Hence, therefore, from those lost goods, to present riches, as if they were not lost, a bad collection is made. Then, the diverse states of man are confused, before and after the fall: One of Innocence, to which creation in the image of GOD pertains: Another of Corruption, to which the loss of the divine image pertains: which, just as before the fall it was determined to perseverance in innocence: So the restoration of the same after the fall, which occurs in the Elect, is likewise determined to the believers alone. Finally, a fallacy of opposites is committed. For the first creation of man in the image of GOD, and eternal Predestination, are not opposed to one another in the Scriptures: For that first Creation does nothing at all toward our Election: but a second, and indeed a NEW creation is required, which is proper only to the sons, or the Elect of GOD, of which the Apostle speaks in 2 Cor. 5, verse 17: If any one is in Christ Jesus, he is a new Creature. This second, however, or new Creation is not founded on that communication of concreated perfection, or Original righteousness: but on the passion and death of the Son of GOD, apprehended by true and persevering faith. Now, however, the passion and death of the Son of GOD, as also Faith, do not pertain to man in the state of innocence, considered with respect to the first creation in the image of GOD: but only to man already fallen, and lost in sins. Whence a most inept method of arguing emerges in Huber.

Latin:

QUARTUM argumentum aliâ itidem formâ in hunc modum contexere solebat:

Ubi propter instaurationem omnium, quæ in cœlo & in terrâ sunt, quæ facta est per Christum, omnia reconciliantem, dicimur nos prædestinati: ibi Universalis omnium statuitur Electio, Ephes. 1. v. 10. Atqui propter hanc instaurationē omnium, factam per Christum, omnia reconciliantem, quæ in cœlo, & in terrâ sunt, dicimur prædestinati: Ephes. 1. versu jam citato 10. & Coloss. 1. v. 19. & 20. Ergo Universalis omnium statuitur prædestinatio.

Respondeo ejusdem futilitatis esse & hoc argumentum. Perindè enim illud concludit, ac si quis hunc in modum colligat: Ubi propter meritum redemptionis à Christo factæ prædestinati esse dicimur: ibi Universalis statuitur Electio. At prius illud apud Apostolum loco citato asseritur: Ergo stabiliter & hoc posterius. Nullâ nimirùm est in Majori connexio. Loquitur enim Apostolus de câ ἀνακεφαλαιώσει sive instauratione, quę est à Christo per mortem ipsius facta, inter

DEUM atq; hominem quâ nimirùm homines cum DEO sunt reconciliati:imò etiam instaurata rursus est societas, quæ hominibus cum Angelis intercesserat. Coloss.1.v.20. Ex qua instauratione sequitur collectio & conjunctio regni Christi Spiritualis, quod est ab ipso per mortem & resurrectionem ipsius, nec non per prædicationem Evangelii inchoatum, in quo ipsi tanquàm Domino & capiti omnia sunt subjecta. Psal. 8. ita, ut qui Christum non habet, ei nulla pars sit in DEO. Insuper Instauratio ista per Christum facta, haud minus est fundamentum Justificationis, quàm Electionis nostræ. Nâ si absq; istâ instauratione Christi fuisset, tàm non posset justificari quisquam, quàm non prædestinari. Jam verò sicut ex hac instauratione Christi non efficitur Justificatio Universalis: ita neq; Prædestinatio Universalis. Deindè non attendit Huberus, particulam universalem OMNIA in textu Apostolico,non tàm respicere homines,quàm pręter homines Deum & Angelos,qui per Christum invicem sunt conciliati. Tertiò confunditur Reconciliatio cum Prædestinatione;quarum neutra ratione nostri excludit Fidem. Etsi enim Christo suo merito totum mundum recôciliavit Deo Patri: tamen Reconciliationis hujus fructus non redundat,nisi ad credentes: sic attestante Apostolo,Col.1.22.& 23.Reconciliavit vos inCorpore Carnis suæ per mortem,ut exhiberet vos sanctos, & immaculatos, & irreprehensibiles coram ipso : SI MODO PERMANSERITIS IN FIDE fundati & stabiles, NEC DIMOVEBIMINI à spe Evangelii quod audistis&c.Tandem monstrare non potest Huberus vel unum interpretem, qui hunc locum de Universali Electione explicârit.

QUINTUM etiam argumentum aliter informare consuevit Huberus in hanc faciem:Ubicunq; secundum arcani Dei beneplaciti revelationę sumus prædestinati: ibi omnes sumus prædestinati: Ergo Omnes sumus prædestinati. Connexum Majoris sic probavit: Ubicunq; Scriptura monstrat filium, qui restauravit omnia,ibidemq; se penitùs manifestavit erga nos: ibi secundum arcani beneplaciti revelationem sumus prædestinati:& perConsequens: Omnes prædestinati. At Apostolus cap. hoc.1. Eph. v. 10. monstrat Filium, qui restauravit omnia. Ergo.

Respondeo, argumentum hoc constare scopis dissolutis, ut nulla legitima terminorů connexio in toto ejus Systemate appareat: id quod ἀναλυτικῶς demonstrare placet. Partes argumenti hæ sunt: In Evangelio revelavit Deus mysterium de beneplacito suæ voluntatis. Ergo nihil de voluntate Dei ampliùs absconditum, nihil Evangelio revelato contrarium erit; jam Deus voluntatem suâ inEvangelio ita declaravit,quòd omnes homines velit salvari.Ergo non aliter etiam se habet Electio.

Respondeo 1. committi ἔλλιψις partium in hoc argumento. Nam voluntate illaDEI antecedente & benevolâ, mysterium prædestinationis non absolvitur: sed τάξις illa mediorů requiritur, per quæ placuit Deo ad salutem nos adducere. 2. Dicta Scripturæ de benevolâ illâ DEI voluntate testantia, scopo Huberiano planè adversantur, Deum nolle mortem peccatoris:velle ut omnes salventur: ut nemo pereat &c. sed Ordinis additâ mentione, Conversionem, agnitionem veritatis, pœnitentiâ requirunt: Sine quo ordine nulla uspiam in Evangelio Electio facta esse legitur. Prodit er­ gò stupendam inscitiam Huberus,qui absolu­ tam aliquam& simplicem in Evangelio de sa­ lute hominum voluntatem revelatam essè fa­ naticè somniat: secus ac Liber Cōcordię,qui octo distincta requisita hoc in Articulo consi­ deranda esse docet:quorum plæraq; Huberus sicco pede præterit, &ex æternoElectionis de­ creto,ad applicationę,quæ in tempore sit, in­ scitè accômodat. Undè in argumenti huj9 di­ ductione absurdè asserit, omnes homines esse a-sscitos ad sortem Dei: cùm tamen Apost. Col. 1,12. expressè sortem illam definiat, per SORTEM SANCTORUM IN LUMINE:& totus contextus manifestissimè evincat,utrumq; locum, & ad Eph. 1. & ad Col. 1. non nisi de sanctis, & verè fi­ delibus accipi posse.Scriptura n.duplicę,non triplicem sortem constituit: UNAM Sanctorum; Dan. 12,13 Stabis in sorte tua: Alteram hypocrita­ rum, Matth. 24. v.51. & cap. 25, v. 46.

SEXTUM Huberi argumentum figit pedem in pronomine NOS, quod totum generis hu­ mani complexum notare ille somniau Verùm contra & pręter textus Apostolici suffragiů. Nam qui homines intelligendi sint termino pronominis, ipso Apostolo interprete constat; nempè, 1. Sancti, 2. Credentes in Christum, 3. be­ nedicti omni benedictione Spirituali cœlestibus: 4. adoptati in filios Dei, 5. donati remissione peccatorů, obsignati Spiritu promissionu, &quæ sunt his simi­ les aliæ Electorum notæ. At verò hæc γνωρί­ σματα ne Ephesiorum quidem omnium: ne­ dùm totius generis humani erant propria. Patet ergo ψευδογράφημα.

Deindè cōmittitur έλεγχος ἑτεροζητήσεως dum id,quod à Christo factů est, statim refer­ tur ad id, quod à Christo factum esse dicitur. Certè à Christo proficiscitur propitiatio pro peccatis totius mundi, 1. Joh. 2, 2. Sed hinc mi­ nimè est consequens,omnes homines,sive credant sive non credant in Christum,in Christo ad vitam e-­ lectos esse.Nam in Christo non dicuntur electi, nisi qui per fidē sunt in Christo In Cristo a.sūt, qui Christů in baptismo induerunt, Gal. 3, 27. qui Christo verè incorporati sunt, 1. Cor.12, 27. qui cœlesti viti, tanquàm palmites fructiferi inserti sunt & manent, Joh. 15,5. Nec momenti quicquá habet, quòd in Electione Deus vul-­ nera Christi spectare dicitur, ut hinc Univer-­ salitas Electionis evinci possit, quia videlicet vulnerů Christi meritů, ad totius generis hu-­ mani universitatē spectet. Nam Deus spectat quidem vulnera Christi: non humanorum o-­ perů illa non nudè spectat in Electione homi-­ num,ut horů intuitu eligantur homines, absq; ullâ differentiâ, ad vitâ æternâ, sive credant,si-­ ve non credant in Filium Dei, vulnera& mor. tem pro nobis passum: sed intuetur illa in æ-­ ternâ illâ suâ τάξει, quatenùs nimirùm vulne.­ rum istorů meritů, per fidem verâ & ad finem usq; perseverantē, à piis & credentibus appli-­ catur,& quasi appropriatur. Alioquin hoc i-­ psum meritů vulnerů Christi, in præsenti Ele-­ čtionis articulo, haud magis valeret, quàm in Justificationis articulo.

Et meminisse debebat Huberus Formulam Concordiæ, istam loci Apostolici depravationem pluribus in locis expressè falsitatis arguere. Imò meminisse debebat, quod B. Lutherus in libro contra cœlestes Prophetas Scriptum reliquit, in hunc modum: Scriptura vulgato modo usurpat Syne dochen: hoc est, nominat aliquod totum, & intelligit ejus tantùm partem aliquam: quemadmodum facit, cùm populum Israëliticum vocat populum, & peculiarem populum DEI, cùm tamen major semper illius pars Diaboli, minor verò DEI fuerit. Quemadmodum & Paulus Galatas, Corinthios, aliasq; civitates, Ecclesias DEI nominat, cùm tamen minima pars constaret ex VERIS FILIIS DEI.

Præter sex isthæc argumenta, pluribus etiam ex Scriptura petitis pugnavit Huberus: sed refutatione indignis: quippè quorum medius terminus, sive probandi nervus planè idem est cùm jam refutatis. Sed pugnavit etiam Rationibus, quarum præcipuas paucis delibabim9.

RATIO I. Pleraq; omnia mysteria Religionis Christianæ, & beneficia DEI sunt universalia: qualia sunt: Dilectio DEI sunt: Providentia: Redemtio per Christum parta:Vocatio, quæ fit per prædicationem Evangelii, item promissio Evangelica. Ergò etiam Prædestinatio.

Respondeo illis verbis, quibus hoc argumentum ab alio quopiam Orthodoxo Theologo exceptum & refutatum fuit:nempè cùm totum illud ex parte procedat, puerorum lufui, non literatorum congressibus feriis illud proponendum fuisse. Quod si ex hac ratione Prædestinationis Universalitas rectè constituitur: nihil obstare potest, quin Remissio peccatorum, Justificatio, Regeneratio, Sanctificatio, & tandem Glorificatio etiam, sive Salvatio Universalis omninò constituatur: hoc est, universa doctrina Christiana in metum Puccianismum convertatur. Deindè ἀθεόλογον planè est, & cùm universa Scriptura pugnat, quòd Huberus eandem in cerebro suo fingit Electionis latitudinem, cujus est Dilectio DEI: Providentia; Redemtio &c. Nam Scriptura tantum Salvandos & Electos eodem latitudinis gradu collocat. Undè illud est, quòd non simpliciter Electio: sed Electio Salvandorum sive Filiorum DEI, vulgò hoc mysterium appellatur. Tandem plærisque istis beneficiis DEI notantur duntaxat bona acquisita, quæ absque fruitione tantùm respectu sui confiderantur. Electio autem ad usum beneficiorum divinorum omnium pertinet, qui sine fide nullus esse, neminiq; obtingere potest. Et hæc quidem generalis datur ad primam hanc rationem Responsio.

In specie de singulis Antecedentis membris respondetur. 1. Dilectio DEI non omnis universalis est: sed ea duntaxat, quâ mundus diligitur: Joh. 3. v. 16. inimici diliguntur: Rom. 5. v. 10. Atqui hæc non est, quâ Electi dilipuntur. Nam istorum dilectio definiente Scripturâ, talis est, ut ad finem usque, Johan. 13, 1.

ut in dilecto diligantur, Ephes. 1. v. 4. Cui dilectioni soli Electio salvandorum acceptum referenda est. 2. Ex Providentia DEI tùm demum aliquid firmi in hoc articulo colligetur: si Electionem ad passeres etiam, oves atque boves pertinere, Huberus probaverit. 3. In reliquis membris, quoad Redemtionem, Vocationem, Promissionem, Universalem, perpetuì committuntur paralogismi ἐπὶ τὸ συνθετὸν διαιρέσεως. Nam neq; meritum Christi, vel solum, vel simpliciter: vel Vocatio aut Promissio illa Evangelii universalis: sed cum respectu & accessione fidei demùm, Electionis nostræ caussa est. 4. In specie etiam de Promissionibus Evangelicis illud est notandum, duùm eas quoque esse generum. Nam aliæ simpliciter sunt Universales, quales illæ sunt præcipuè, quæ ex historia facti defluunt, Exempli gratiâ: Quod Christus mortem pro omnibus oppetiverit. Quod Evangelium universæ creaturæ prædicari jusserit. Aliæ verò sunt determinatè Universales, hoc est,promissionem salutis continent, sed semper cum determinatione fidei in Christum.

RATIO II. Huberi: DEUS neminem constituit ad iram. Ergò omnes sunt Electi.

Respondeo: 1. Insigne committitur Ψευδογράφημα. Antecedens enim ex 1. Thess. 5. v. 9. petitur, per manifestam vim, in alienam sententiam ab Hubero detorquetur. Nam sermo ibi est Apostolo duntaxat de solis credentibus, de filiis lucis & diei, v. 5. qui non dormiunt, UT RELIQUI, sed sunt vigilantes & sobrii: v. 6. qui sunt induti thorace fidei & charitatis, & pro galeâ, spe salutis. De his ergò omnibus verum est, quod non sint positi ad iram: idque nullâ DEI voluntate, vel antecedente, vel consequente. De reliquis autem filiis tenebrarum & noctis, qui dormiunt securi, & destituuntur fide, ac spe salutis, tametsi verum est, quòd voluntate antecedente neminem ad iram Deus constituerit: Consequente tamen voluntate,propter incredulitatem, justo judicio, in pœnam impietatis, ad iram & damnationem justam DEUS impios omnes constituit & destinavit.

RATIO III. Huberi: DEUS Voluntate Antecedente in Electione neminem præteriit. Ergò omnes elegit.

Respondeo: Nullam prorsus millitare Consequentiæ rationem: siquidem Voluntas Antecedens solitaria, Electionem non constituit, nedùm perficit aut absolvit. Hæc enim certis suis mediis jam indè ab æterno à DEO, ad finem suum est ordinata. Laterem ergo lavet Huberus, & ex arena funes nectit.

RATIO IV. Huberi: DEUS omnes homines ad imaginem suam condidit. Ergò etiam ad vitam æternam elegit.

Respondeo, 1. Si de facto ipso sermo sit, par unum duntaxat protoplastorum ad imaginem DEI fuisse conditum: De cæteris hominibus hoc duntaxat verum est, quoad intentionem DEI, quâ DEUS quidem in Adamo omnes homines ad suam imaginem voluit esse conditos. Atqui & hæc intentio non erat simplex & absoluta: sed determinata ad perseverantiam Adami in statu integritatis. Jam verò per lapsum tristissimum hæc etiam intentio est interversa: & Opus etiam ipsum creationis divinæ, in protoplastis corruptum, & deperditum. Hinc ergò ex amissis illis bonis, ad præsentes opes, quasi non amissæ sint, mala fit collectio. Deindè confunduntur diversi status hominis, ante & post lapsum: Unus Innocentiæ, ad quem creatio ad imaginem DEI pertinet: Alter Corruptionis, ad quem amissio imaginis divinæ pertinet: quæ uti ante lapsum determinata erat ad perseverantiam in innocentia: Ita ejusdem restitutio post lapsum, quæ fit in Electis, itidem est determinata ad solos fideles. Tandem committitur elenchus oppositorum. Nam creatio hominis prima ad imaginem DEI, & æterna Prædestinatio, in Scripturis sibi invicem non opponuntur: Nam prima illa Creatio nihil quicquam facit ad nostri Electionem: sed altera, & quidem NOVA requiritur creatio, quæ solorum filiorum, sive Electorum DEI est propria, de quâ Apostolus 2. Cor. 5. vers. 17. Si quis est in Christo Jesu, nova est Creatura. Hæc altera autem, sive nova Creatio non fundatur in communicatione illâ concreatæ perfectionis, sive justitiæ Originalis: sed in passione, & morte Filii DEI, verâ & perseverante fide apprehensâ. Jam verò passio & mors Filii DEI, ut & Fides, nihil attinent hominem in statu innocentiæ, respectu primæ creationis ad imaginem DEI consideratum: sed tantùm hominem jam lapsum, & in peccatis perditum. Undè ineptissima disputandi ratio apud Huberum emergit.


### Part II. Πολεμικη (Polemic): Reason V. of Huber: Unless election is established to be Universal: all matter of solid consolation is taken away

REASON V. of Huber: Unless election is established to be Universal: all matter of solid consolation is taken away.

I answer that Huber borrowed this argument from Puccius, who himself also tried to cloak his dogma with this deception: dreaming with Huber that the nerve of all true and solid consolation is placed in this, if without distinction salvation and eternal life, and so also Election to salvation, are equally common to all men: and indeed from the eternal ordination of GOD, which has chosen all men. But they deceive most basely, and are deceived, changing all solace into most bitter wormwood, and all unshaken assurance of hope and faith into the snares of desperation. For what kind of consolation would this be, if one tempted and afflicted were to think himself equally with some Jew or Turk to have been chosen from eternity: Where nothing but anguish and the torments of desperation must necessarily arise. Now, however, those who establish that one can never fall from the certainty of election, who rest solely in the merit of Christ; and persevere in this faith to the very end: for them the most ample matter of consolation is proposed in the doctrine concerning the Election of believers: as was shown at length above in the first part toward the end.

And these indeed are the principal reasons of Huber, with which he wished to be troublesome to our people, but with a vain attempt.

Moreover, besides Huber, there are and are found others, and indeed Orthodox Theologians, who, although they have nothing in common with the futile and fanatical dogma of Huber, much less do they undertake its patronage; nevertheless, they have been accustomed to use some forms of speaking or assertions in this article: concerning which it is not without reason doubted whether they are conformable to the analogy of faith and Holy Scripture: which, that we may examine in a few words, will not be inconvenient.

THE FIRST assertion is, That to those who are named by the Savior πρόσκαιροι, that is, believers for a time, but who afterward fall away, the Title of Election can be attributed in a broader and more general signification. They seek the proof of this matter from 1 Thess. 1:4. Where Paul, Silvanus, and Timothy write to the Church of the Thessalonians in this manner: Knowing, brethren beloved by GOD, your election. Now they could not know this, except from the confession of faith and obedience toward the Gospel, which the whole Church of the Thessalonians displayed, although many in it could be πρόσκαιροι, who are nevertheless adorned with the title of Election.

But I answer that this proof cannot be accommodated to the proposed question apodictically, but at least seemingly in a probable manner. For 1. we simply deny that the title of Election is attributed to the Thessalonians in this place in a broader and more general signification: For although this inscription is directed to the whole Church of the Thessalonians: nevertheless, by the interpretation of our blessed Doctor Luther, it is always to be understood synecdochically, so that the whole is indeed named; but only its nobler part, which is that of the Elect, is understood. For it is impossible that in an assembly of the called, where the pure doctrine of the Gospel and the legitimate administration of the Sacraments resound: there should not also be some who are truly pious and Elect. Therefore, with respect to these, the title of Elect is accommodated to the whole Church, but synecdochically, and by reason of the better part. Where it is not right to feign some general and looser signification for the word Election: but rather it is to be taken determinately and restrictively toward that better part of the Church. 2. The consequence of the adduced proof is very weak; and it begs the question. For it has not yet been proven that the title of Elect is attributed to the whole Church of the Thessalonians on account of that external confession of faith and obedience toward the Gospel alone.
