But what is added: That the defection may be restrained, and sins sealed up, and iniquity expiated, to bring in everlasting righteousness, and to seal up the vision and prophecy, and to anoint the Holy of Holies, etc., by that it is not denied that the seventy weeks will have an end in the destruction of the city: nor is it affirmed that they are to be finished in the year of the death and passion of Christ, as some contend greatly: for otherwise Christ would have been anointed only in the year of his passion, when nevertheless he was anointed immediately at the very first moment of his conception, in the very womb of his mother. Now if the seventy weeks were terminated in the Anointing, that is, in the very conception of Christ: Therefore not in his death. Again, If in his death: Therefore not in the Anointing or conception. By no means, therefore, do the words of the Angel mean this. But this indeed: that while those seventy weeks were still enduring, and therefore before they were finished, the defection would be restrained, sin would be sealed up, iniquity would be expiated, etc. And that all these things would be performed for the Church before the space of time, precisely defined by GOD for the final destruction of the people and the holy city, had reached its established limit: and therefore the Holy of Holies and the promised Messiah are no longer to be expected after the passage of that time.

Furthermore, the Angel adds that after the last week the Sanctuary and the city would be destroyed by the people of the Leader who is to come. For the words sound thus: After seven and sixty-two weeks: when Christ is cut off (or Christ having already been cut off) the people shall destroy the city and the Sanctuary: or as it is simply in the Hebrew: and Christ shall be cut off, and the people shall destroy the city, etc. But those who are not ignorant of the Hebrew language know that this way of speaking is customary in that language, that what is expressed in the Latin language by two ablatives of sequence is proposed by copulative conjunctions. Now if the destruction of the city and the Sanctuary happens after the last week: Therefore this destruction necessarily constitutes the end of those weeks.

Finally, Christ himself confirms the same thing most evidently, Matt. 24:15, Mark 13:14: When you see that abomination of desolation, which was spoken of by Daniel the Prophet, standing in the Holy place (let him who reads, take note), then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains. Which words the same Savior explains in this manner in Luke 21:20: When you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, then know that its desolation is approaching: Then let those who are in Judea flee to the mountains, and let those who are inside it depart: and let those who are in the fields not enter it: For these are the days of vengeance, THAT ALL THINGS WHICH ARE WRITTEN MAY BE FULFILLED. Now, in the Old Testament, nowhere else than in this ninth chapter of Daniel were those things predicted which the Savior discussed in this place concerning the Idol of abomination standing in the holy place, and concerning the final desolation of the city of Jerusalem. Therefore, the Savior himself wished it to be explicitly noted that the prophecy of Daniel concerning the seventy weeks ends in the destruction of Jerusalem. Thus, therefore, the end of those weeks is certain and undoubted.

Now, however, regarding their beginning, doctors and interpreters again depart into various and conflicting opinions, which it is not our purpose to recount in this place. The Angel himself established that the beginning of those seventy weeks should be made from the going forth of the Word, or the publication of the edict concerning the restoration of the people and the rebuilding of the city of Jerusalem. Now, Sacred histories record that edicts of this kind were published at four different times by different Kings. The first is that of Cyrus, 2 Chron. 36:22, Ezra ch. 1. Which, however, was not carried into effect, but was hindered in various ways, partly while Cyrus was still living, and partly under the kings of the Persians, Ahasuerus and Artaxerxes, Ezra ch. 4. The second is that solemn edict by which Darius, King of the Persians, not only renewed, confirmed, and promulgated the mandate of Cyrus concerning the restoration of the temple permitted to the Jews, which had been anxiously sought and found, but also established a capital and infamous punishment for those who might in any way attempt to hinder this restoration of the Jewish polity: Ezra ch. 6. At which very time the Prophets Haggai and Zechariah, by the instinct of God, exhorted the people to this very restoration of the temple, and incited them by various promises and threats proposed. The third edict is that of Artaxerxes, who in the seventh year of his reign granted to the Jews and the Priests who wished to accompany Ezra a return to Judea: and he repeated, renewed, and more diligently sanctioned the edict of Darius concerning the expenses to be supplied for procuring sacrifices and offering them in the temple of Jerusalem. The fourth edict is when the same Artaxerxes, in the twentieth year of his reign, sends Nehemiah to Jerusalem with the power of fortifying the city. Neh. ch. 2.

Now, from which edict the beginning of the seventy weeks should be taken must be examined a little more accurately. That first edict of Cyrus does not fit here, because it was not carried into effect, but was hindered in many ways.

The third edict of Artaxerxes, however, repeated only some part of the edict of Darius concerning the expenses for sacrifices to be supplied by the Kings of the Persians. Therefore, it seems it cannot be called a full edict concerning the restoration of the city and the Temple. The fourth edict of the same Artaxerxes, in particular, only gives the Jews the power of rebuilding the walls of Jerusalem. It remains, therefore, that the Angel established the beginning of the seventy weeks from the going forth of the word, or the second edict, which is that of Darius, King of the Persians. And indeed, more accurate chronologists today concede to this opinion, moved by these reasons: 1. Because this edict of Darius was solemnly promulgated to the people, as it were, by God himself, the author of this prophecy, through the Prophets Haggai and Zechariah, and was approved by divine authority. 2. Because it was never hindered afterwards. 3. Because the end of those seventy weeks corresponds exactly to this beginning. For the destruction of the city of Jerusalem fell in the year of Christ 68, which was the year of the world 4017, in which year Vespasian, sent by Nero into Judea, not only afflicted the Jews with a most atrocious war, but also two years later, having taken and leveled the city of Jerusalem to the ground, miserably slaughtered the Jews and sold them into the whole world. Now, if the seventy weeks of Daniel, i.e., 490 years, are subtracted, they show the remainder to be the year of the World 3527, which was the second year, not of that Darius Hystaspis, but of that Darius who is called by Gentile writers Darius Nothus, who had Artaxerxes Longimanus as his predecessor parent, and Artaxerxes Mnemon as his son and successor.

Latin:

Prima autem hujus rei fundamenta posuit Herodes ipse, qui penultimo regni sui anno, omnes seniores ex tribu David ortos interfecit, & in eorum locum substituit legisperitos.

Jam sub finem regni Herodis natus est Christus, & vaticinium Jacobi revera impletum esse, licet non uno statim momento, sed

ALTERUM Scripturæ testimonium, quod tempus Nativitati Messiæ in Scripturis destinatū, ante multa secula præteriisse evincit, petimus ex loco, sive vaticinio illo Angeli, quod confirmat, Messiam nasciturum fuisse, completis septuaginta hebdomadibus Danielis, & apud ipsum Danielem secundum Hebræam versionem sic habet: Hebdomades septuaginta decisæ (determinatæ) sunt super populum tuum, & super civitatem sanctitatis tuæ (sive sanctam tuam) ad consummandum prævaricationem: & ad sigillandum (finiendum) peccata, & ad expiandam iniquitatem, & ad adducendū justiciam seculorum, & ad sigillandum visionem, & Prophetiam, & ad ungendum sanctitatem sanctitatum. Et scies, & intelliges ab exitu sermonis ad reditum, & ad ædificandum Jerusalem, usque ad Messiam duce, hebdomades septem, & hebdomades sexaginta & duæ redibit: & ædificabitur platea & murus, & in angustia temporum. Et post hebdomadas sexaginta duas excindetur Messias, & non erit: Et civitatem & sanctuarium dissipabit populus ducis venturi, & finis ejus in inundatione, & usque ad finem belli, determinatæ sunt desolationes. Et roboravit pactum multis hebdomada una & dimidia hebdomadâ cessare faciet Sacrificium, & oblationem, & super extensionem abominationum admirari faciet, & usque ad consummationem & finem durabit desolatio. Daniel. 9. 24. & seqq.

Summa vaticinii hujus, (quantum quidem ab præsentem quæstionem attinet) in eo unicè consistit, quòd prædicit Angelus, ab exeunte mandato de reparatione Templi & urbis, usque ad Messiam Ducem, novique fœderis confirmationem, septuaginta fore hobdomadas. Quas cùm & Judæi & Christiani non dierum, sed annorum esse fateantur: quales etiam lex Mosaica, in supputatione annorum Jubilæi observabat. Num. 14. 34. Ezech. 4. 6. Eas verò ante quindecim secula, & quod excurrit, ipsorummet Judæorum propriâ confessione completas esse constet:irrefragabili necessitate consequitur, Messiam jam modò, & quidem ante totidem secula, in hunc mundum reverâ venisse, & quæ ab Angelo hoc loco definiuntur officia, ritè singula & universa expertivisse Nimis autem dilutum & frigidum est, quod Judæi quidam hoc in vaticinio per Messiam intelligunt vel Cyrum, vel Nehemiam, vel Jehosuam Sacerdotem magnum, cujus fit mentio Hag. 1. 1. vel Zorobabelem. Nam initium fortasse, non verò complementum 70. Septimanarum, in istorum tempora incidit. Deindè singulis istis non competunt prædicata Messiæ, hoc loco expressa: nempè consummare prævaricationes: expiare peccata: adducere sempiternam justitiam: implere omnem visionem & prophetiam: abrogare Sacrificia Levitica: esse Sanctum Sanctorum &c.

Fecit autem Chronologorum dissensio, ut de initio, & de fine septuaginta istarum hebdomadum, non una omnium interpretum, etiam Orthodoxorum, sit sententia. Quam sanè litem nos nostram hoc loco non facimus: interim cum recentiore quodam, &

reliquis omnibus aceuratiore Chronologo sic statuentes: Diversitatis harum sententiarum causam præcipuam esse hanc, quod non prius tempus ipsum per se numerarunt, & postea res gestas ei applicârunt, & quòd mentem Prophetæ Danielis non ex ipfis verbis vaticinij eruere conati sunt: sed ipsa verba ad opinionem suam præconceptam contorserunt: Cùm tamen verba, si simpliciter spectentur, sepositis paululùm historiîs, cuilibet videantur obvia & aperta. Quod enim ad finem eorundem attinet, is manifestè statim in propositione vaticinij ostenditur, quando Angelus inquit: Septuaginta hebdomades determinatæ sive decisæ sunt super populum, & urbem sanctam. Si septuaginta hebdomades sunt determinatæ, hoc est, si septuaginta hebdomades sunt mensura temporis ejus, quo duratura est urbs sancta sive politia Judaica, tùm finiuntur utique illæ septuaginta hebdomades, excidio populi Judaici, & urbis Hierosolymæ: Aliâs enim mensura temporis esse non possent. Quod verò subjicitur: Vt cohibeatur defectio, & obsignentur peccata, & expietur iniquitas, ad adducendum justitiam sempiternam, & obsignandum visionem ac prophetiam, & ad ungendum Sanctum Sanctorum &c. eo non negatur hebdomades septuaginta in excidio urbis finem habituras: neque etiâ affirmatur, eas in anno mortis & passionis Christi ut quidam magnoperè contendunt, finiendas: aliâs einim Christus demùm anno passionis suæ unctus fuisset, cùm tamen unctus sit in ipso statim primo conceptionis momêto, in ipso utero matris. Jam si hebdomades septuaginta terminarentur in Unctione, hoc est, in ipsa conceptione Christi: Ergò non in morte. Rursus, Si in morte: Ergò non in Unctione sive conceptione. Nequaquam igitur hoc volunt verba Angeli. Sed hoc nimirùm: durantibus adhuc septimanis illis septuaginta, & proindè antequàm finiantur, cohibitum iri defectionem, obsignatum iri peccatum, expiatum iri iniquitatem &c. Et hæc omnia præstitum iri Ecclesiæ, antequàm spatium temporis, ultimo excidio populi, & urbis sanctæ præcisè à DEO definitum, terminum constitutum esset consecutum: ac proindè Sanctum Sanctorum, & promissum Messiam post illius temporis decursum non ampliùs esse expectandum.

Præterea addit Angelus, post ultimam septimanam destructum iri Sanctuariũ, & urbem à populoDucis venturi. Sic enim sonant urba: Post septem & sexaginta duas hebdomades: quando Christus excisus est (sive exciso jam Christo) urbem & Sanctuarium destruet populus: vel ut in Hebræo simpliciter est: & excidetur Christus, & urbem destruet populus &c. Sed hunc modum loquendi in Hebræâ linguâ usitatum esse, ut per Conjunctiones copulativas proponatur id, quod in linguâ Latinâ per duos ablativos consequentiæ effertur, norunt ii, qui ejus linguæ non sunt rudes. Jam si excidium urbis & Sanctuarii accidet post ultimam hebdomadem: Ergo excidium hoc constituit necessariò finem istarum hebdomadum.

Tandem Christus ipse idem confirmat evidentissimè, Matth. 24, 15. Marc. 13, 14. Quùm devideritis abominationem illam vastatricem, quæ dicta est per Danielem Prophetam, in loco Sancto positam (qui legit, animadvertat) tunc qui in Judædad fuerint, fugiant ad montes. Quæ verba hunc in modum explicat idem Servator Luc. 21. v. 20. Cùm videritis Hierosolymam cingi ab exercitibus, tunc cognoscite appropinquare vastationem ejus: Tunc qui in Judæâ sunt, fugiant in montes, & qui intra eam sunt, excedant : & qui in agris, non ingrediantur in eam: Nam hi sunt dies ultionis, UT IMPLEANTUR OMNIA, QUÆ SCRIPTA SUNT. Jam verò in Veteri nuuspiam, quàm in capite hoc nono Danielis, prædicta fuerunt ea, quæ de Idolo abominationis, stante in loco sancto, deque ultimâ desolatione urbis Hierosolymorum, hoc loco Servator differuit. Ergo Servator ipse difertè notatum voluit, vaticinium Danielis, de Septuaginta hebdomadibus, terminari in excidio Hierosolymitano. Sic ergo finis hebdomadum istarum certus est ac indubitatus.

Jam verò quoad initium earum, Doctores ac interpretes rursum in varias ac discrepantes abeunt sententias, quas hoc loco percensere nostri non est instituti. Angelus ipse initium septuaginta istarum hebdomadum, faciendum esse statuit ab exitu Verbi, sive publicatione edicti, de reducendo populo, deq; reædificandâ urbe Hierosolymâ. Jam verò hujusmodi edicta quatuor diversis temporib. à diversis etiam Regibus publicata fuisse, Sacræ commemorant historiæ. Primum est Cyri, 2. Paral. 36. v. 22. Esr. 1. cap. Quod tamen in actum non fuit deductum, sed variis modis impedi tum, partim vivente adhuc Cyro, partim verò sub Ahasvero, & Artaxerxe regibus Persarum, Esræ. 4. cap. Alterum est solenne illud edictum, quo Darius rex Persarum, mandatum Cyri de instauratione templi Judæis permissâ, sollicitè quæsitum & inventum, non modò renovavit, confirmavit, promulgavit: sed & capitale & infame supplicium constituit in eos, qui quoquo modo instaurationem hanc politiæ Judaicæ impedire conentur: Esræ c. 6. Quo ipso tempore Haggæus & Zacharias Prophetæ, ex instinctu Dei, ad hanc ipsam instaurationem templi, populum hortati sunt, & variis propositis tùm promissionibus, tùm comminationibus incitarunt. Tertium edictum est Artaxerxis, qui anno Imperii sui septimô concessit Judæis & Sacerdotibus, Esram comitari volentibus, reditum in Judæam: & edictum Darii de sumtibus suppeditandis ad comparanda sacrificia, & in templo Hierosolymitano offerenda, repetiit, renovavit, & diligentiùs sancivit. Quartum edictum est, quando idem Artaxerxes anno vicesimo sui regni, Nehemiam mittit Hierosolymam, cum potestate urbis muniendæ. Nehem. c. 2.

Jam à quo edicto initium septuaginta septimanarum sumendum sit, dispiciendum paulò accuratiùs. Primum illud Cyriedictum huc non quadrat, quia in actum non est deductum: sed multis modis impeditum.

Tertium verò Artaxerxis edictum, partem tantùm aliquam edicti Darii de Sacrificiis, sumtibus Regum Persarum suppeditandis, repetiit. Ergò plenum edictum de restauratione urbis & Templi nominari haud posse videtur. Quartum ejusdem Artaxerxis edictum, in specie tantùm potestatem facit Judæis, reædificandi muros Hierosolymitanos. Relinquitur ergo Angelum constituisse initium septuaginta hebdomadum, ab exitu verbi, sive edicti secundi, quod est Darii Regis Persarum. Et sanè in hanc sententiam accuratiores hodiè Chronologi concedunt, his moti rationibus. 1. Quia edictum hoc Darii, ab ipso Deo autore hujus vaticinii, per Haggæum & Zachariam Prophetas, solenniter quasi promulgatum populo, & divinâ autoritate approbatum fuit. 2. Quia illud nunquàm postea impeditum fuit. 3. Quia finis septuaginta istarum hebdomadum initio huic exactè respondet. Nam excidium urbis Hierosolymæ incidit in Annum Christi 68. qui fuit annus mundi 4017. quo anno Vespasianus, à Nerone missus in Judæam, non modò Judæos atrocissimo bello afflixit: sed & biennio post, Judæos, expugnatâ, & solo æquata urbe Hierosolyma, miserabiliter trucidavit, & in universum orbem divendidit. Jam si subducantur septuaginta septimanæ Danielis, h. e. anni 490. residuum exhibent annum Mundi 3527. qui fuit secundus annus, non Darii illius Hystaspis, sed Darii illius, qui ab Ethnicis Scriptoribus Darius Nothus appellatur, qui parentem habuit Artaxerxem Longimanum antecessorem: & Artaxerxem Mnemon a filium, Successorem.


### On King Christ or Messiah: Just now in (continued)

And we frankly confess that this calculation seems to us most accurate, proper to the words of the Angel, and less forced, without dwelling on the contradictions of others, the weight and moment of which the chronologists themselves may see. We meanwhile gather from it that, although the variety of interpreters or chronologists might disturb someone in this part, yet in that manifold variety of interpretations and opinions, this can be firmly maintained against the Jews: Wherever the beginning of those weeks is finally established, they have long since been finished, and that most especially in the overthrow of the second temple: and therefore the time destined for the Messiah has flowed away some centuries ago, which not even the saner Jews themselves can deny. Whence we, for the confirming of our opinion, irrefutably prove these two things: One: That the Messiah has already come, since he ought to have come while those seventy weeks were still running. The other: that according to the prophecy of the Angel, the promised Messiah of the World had to be cut off, i.e., to suffer and die: which was to be shown around the conclusion of the first argument of our Demonstration against the Jews.

Although the Jews are indeed convicted by the testimony of their own heart and conscience that the time for the advent of the Messiah, appointed by the oracles of the Prophets, has elapsed more than fifteen hundred years ago: nay, even more, being led by the certainty of this matter, having sent legates to John the Baptist, they did not hesitate to attribute the honor of the Messiah to him: yet, in order to satisfy in some way their insatiable hatred toward Christ and the entire Christian name, they prefer to accuse God himself of inconstancy and falsehood rather than leave room for the truth. For they clamor that the time indeed destined by the Prophets for the advent of the Messiah has long since expired: but that God, because of the sins of the Jewish people, changed the time and delayed the advent of the Messiah, and delays it to this day. The stupendous impiety of which fiction is laid bare of its own accord if the following reasons are weighed a little more accurately.

For 1. The divine promises or predictions concerning sending the Messiah into the world, and indeed sending him after the scepter had been taken away from Judah, and while the Weeks of Daniel were still running, were nowhere and never proposed under any condition of either the dignity or the indignity of the Jews: but simply.

2. God himself swears that, even if the descendants of David should not keep the commandments of GOD, he will nevertheless firmly keep the promise made to David concerning sending the Messiah, Psalm 89:3 and following. I will keep my mercy for David forever, and my covenant shall be firm to him: And if his sons forsake my law, and do not walk in my judgments: if they profane my statutes, and do not keep my precepts: then I will visit their transgression with a rod, and their iniquity with stripes. But I will not take my mercy away from him, nor will I lie concerning my truth. I will not make my covenant void, and I WILL NOT CHANGE what has gone out of my lips. Once I have sworn by my Holiness to David: I will not lie to David, etc. We conclude therefore: Let God be true; every man a liar, Psalm 116:11, Romans 3:4. And our unbelief does not make void the promise of GOD. Romans 3:3.

3. The argument of the Jews is inverted. For it was for this very reason that that promised Messiah had to come into this world in the fullness of time, so that he might expiate the sins of all men, of whatever kind and of whatever magnitude, and, as the prophecy of Daniel holds, at the end of the seventy weeks, might take away sins by his death and bring in justice. So far, therefore, is it from being the case that the sins of either the Jews or the Gentiles could inhibit or impede the defined advent of the Messiah, that they rather promoted it: just as the LORD testifies in express words in Jeremiah, that for this reason he wishes to hasten that new covenant, so that, namely, the sins committed against the old covenant of the Law might be blotted out by eternal oblivion: Jeremiah 31:31 and following.

4. Not even the Jews themselves dare, or are even able, to define that sin committed by them or by their ancestors, the atrocity of which was so great that it would render void, or at least retract or impede, the promise of God, which was confirmed so many times even by an oath.

5. Even if this fiction of the Jews were to hold, the descendants would still not pay the penalty for that sin designated by their ancestors, according to the immutable rule of divine justice: Ezekiel 18:20, The son shall not bear the iniquity of the Father.

6. And finally, this exception of the Jews is notably blasphemous against the eternal and infinite Omniscience of GOD. For if the advent of the Messiah had to be delayed because of the sins of the Jews or the Gentiles: God would certainly have foreseen those very sins, and consequently would have pre-ordained a different time for the advent of the Messiah.

But that we may compress into a few words what can further be said concerning this first circumstance of Time, we infer thus against the Jews: If that second Temple, built after the Babylonian captivity, ought not to have been destroyed and overturned before the promised Messiah of the World had illuminated it with his presence, his sermons, and his miracles, and by this means had rendered its glory more august and more magnificent than the Temple of Solomon: If also the Levitical ceremonies ought not to have been abrogated until the Messiah was brought into the world: it follows necessarily and absolutely invincibly, since that second Temple was utterly razed and overturned by Titus, the son of Vespasian, more than fifteen hundred years ago: nay, he himself also The rite of sacrifices was likewise antiquated for as many years, because, with the temple destroyed, the sacrifices themselves also had to cease, according to the divine law, which bound the rite of sacrifices to the tabernacle of the covenant alone, or the Temple, Deut. 12:5. It follows, I say, that the Messiah was also brought into the World as many years ago.

The antecedent consists of a twin member, but both are most clearly evident from the Holy Scriptures. For 1. That the second Temple ought not to have been destroyed before the advent of the Messiah is confirmed by Haggai ch. 2:7 and 8. Yet a little while, and I will move the heaven and the earth, the sea and the dry land, and I will move all nations, and THE DESIRED ONE OF ALL NATIONS SHALL COME, and I will fill THIS HOUSE with glory: The glory of this latter house shall be greater than the glory of the former, says the Lord of hosts. Concerning which prophecy, Rabbi Akiba says thus, in the book Sanhedrin, ch. Helec. The Prophet treats of the days of the Messiah, and of the King Messiah, and of the time which was after the destruction of the first house. Nor is it worth a penny that the more recent Jews attempt to obscure this statement, contending that the glory of the second Temple was and is called greater, not in respect of the Messiah, but in respect of duration, because this second Temple stood longer than that former one. But be it so, that the first Temple of Solomon lasted only four hundred and ten years: and the second indeed four hundred and twenty: will this difference of only ten years be of such moment, that on that account the Prophet should have predicted that the glory of the second Temple would be so great? It is not at all likely, &c. Malachi chap. 1. simply denies that.

Furthermore, this longer duration of the second Temple is the more obscure, the more numerous and serious devastations it has experienced in succession: already from Antiochus, who even carried off the vessels of the temple and demolished it; nay, he even erected a statue to Jupiter Olympius in that same place: already from Pompey, who, while Hyrcanus and Aristobulus were contending for the empire, coming to Jerusalem, after the city was captured and the temple devastated, approached even to the Holy place: already from Cassius, who in the seventh year of Cleopatra, having captured Judea, despoiled the temple itself. Since that first Temple of Solomon did not experience so many disruptions and devastations, its glory would certainly be greater if judgment were to be made from the duration and condition of the time.

Of the same weakness and vanity is whatever some chatter about the external ornament surpassing the splendor of the former Temple. For 1. one may read the contrary in the book of 1 Esdras, ch. 3, v. 12, so that those who compared the form of the second Temple with the splendor of the former Temple would break out into most profuse tears. 2. Not only was that former temple almost entirely covered, and its vessels golden; but the vessels of the second were for the most part bronze, as the Talmudists themselves report. 3. In the former Temple, fire having fallen from heaven consumed the burnt offerings: that the same happened in the second will hardly be proven. 4. In the former, the Glory of GOD appeared in the Holy of Holies between the Cherubim: concerning the second, this is nowhere asserted in the sacred writings. See the Talmud itself, book Sanhedrin Hierosol., chapter Elluhen haggòlin, that is: These are the captives.

The same is confirmed by Malachi, ch. 3, verse 1. Behold I will send my Angel, and he shall prepare the way before my face. And immediately the LORD, WHOM YOU SEEK, AND THE ANGEL OF THE COVENANT, WHOM YOU DESIRE, shall come to his Temple; Behold he comes, says the Lord of hosts.

As for the latter part of the Antecedent, namely the abrogation of the Levitical ceremonies, Jeremiah discourses about it thus, ch. 3, 15. I will give you pastors according to my heart (understand the Apostles) and they shall feed you with doctrine and knowledge. And when you have been multiplied and have grown in the land, in those days, they shall no longer say of the ark of the covenant of the Lord, nor shall it ascend upon the heart, nor shall they remember it, nor shall they visit it, nor shall it be sacrificed there any more: but in that time Jerusalem shall be the throne of the Lord, and all nations shall be gathered to it.

Daniel agrees with Jeremiah, when in the last Week, in which Christ is to confirm his covenant with many, he writes that the Sacrifice and oblation are to be abolished: ch. 9, v. 27. Whence the Messiah is also called a Priest according to the order of Melchizedek, not according to the order of Aaron. Psalm 110, verse 4.

Although all these things are clearer than the midday Sun, and irrefragably convince the Jews themselves that the Messiah has long since come into the world: yet such is their blindness, or rather contumacy, that, so that they would not have to receive our Messiah, they fabricated other false Messiahs, but with their own most present destruction: Such as were, before Jerusalem was destroyed, Theudas and Judas the Galilean: Acts 5, v. 36. Josephus, book 20 of Antiquities, 3. Such also was Bar Kochba, who in the fifty-second year after the city was destroyed sold himself as the Messiah: To whom, when very many of the Jews adhered, intending to throw off the yoke of the Roman Empire, it happened that under the Emperor Hadrian more of the Jews, than in the very devastation of the city, were miserably slaughtered together with their fictitious Messiah. Concerning which matter, let the Talmud of the Jews itself be seen, book Sanhedrin, page 97.

Latin:

Et hanc quidem supputationem nobis accuratissimam, & Angeli verbis propriam, minusque contortam videri, ingenuè profitemur, con morati aliorum contradictiones, quæ cujus sint ponderis ac momenti, viderint ipsi Chronologi. Nos interim illud indè colligimus, licèt interpretum, sive Chronologorum varietas, hac in parte turbare quempiam possit: in multiplici tamen ista interpretationum ac sententiarum varietate, illud contra Judæos firmiter obtineri posse, Ubicunque tandem septimanarum istarum initium constituatur, jam pridem eas finitas esse, & quidd vel maximè in eversione templi secundi: ac proindè Tempus Mesiæ destinatum ante aliquot secula defluxisse, id quod nec ipsi saniores Judæi negare possunt. Undè nos pro nostrâ sententiâ confirmandâ duo hæc irrefragabiliter evincimus: Unum: Quod Mesfias jam modò venerit, quippè qui currentibus adhuc septuaginta illis hebdomadibus venire debuit. Alterum: quod secundum vaticinium Angeli, promissus Mundi Mesfias excindi, h. e. pati & mori debuerit: id quod circa diexodon primi argumenti Demonstrationis nostræ, contra Judæos erat ostendendum.

Quanquam verò Judæi proprio cordis ac Conscientiæ testimonio convicti sunt, Tempus adventui Messiæ, oraculis Prophetarum præstitum, ante annos mille quingentos amplius effluxisse: quin imò certitudine hujus rei adducti, ad Johannem Baptistam missis legatis, Messiæ honorem ei deferre non dubitarunt: tamen ut insatiabile suum erga Christum, & universum nomen Christianum odium aliquo modo expleant, malunt Deum ipsum inconstantiæ & falsitatis arguere, quàm veritati locum relinquere. Clamitant enim, Tempo quidem Messiæ adventui per Prophetas destinatum jampridem expletum esse: sed Deum propter peccata populi Judaici mutasse tempus, & adventum Messiæ distulisse, hodieque differre. Cujus figmenti stupenda impietas ultrò patescit, si sequentes rationes paulò accuratiùs expendantur.

Nam 1. Promissiones sive prædictiones divinæ de mittendo Messia in mundum, & eo quidem post ablatum sceptrum de Judâ, & currentibus adhuc Septimanis Danielis, mittendo, nuspiam ac nunquàm, sub ullâ conditione vel dignitatis, vel indignitatis Judæorum sunt propositæ: sed simpliciter.

2. Jurat Deus ipse, si vel maximè posteri Davidis non servent mandata DEI, se tamen promissionem, de Messiâ mittendo, Davidi factam, firmiter servaturum, Psal. 89, 3. & seqq. In æternum servabo Davidi misericordiam meam, & pactum meum firmũ erit ipsi: Et si dereliquerint filij ejus legem meam, & in judicijs meis non ambulaverint: si statuta mea prophanaverint, & præcepta mea non custodierint:tunc visitabo virgâ prævaricationem eorum, & plagis iniquitatem eorum. Misericordiam autem meam non auferam ab eo, neq; mentiar in veritatem meam. Non irritum faciam pactum meum, & quod egressum est de labijs meis NON MIITABO.Semel Davidi juravi per Sanctitatem meam: Non mentiar Davidi &c. Concludimus ergò:Sit Deus verax; omnis homo mendax, Psal. 116. v. 11. Rom. 3. v. 4. Et incredulitas nostra promissionem DEI non evacuat. Rom. 3. v. 3.

3. Invertitur Judæorum argumentum. Nam propter hanc ipsam causam, Messias ille promissus in plenitudine temporum, hunc in mundum venire debuit, ut peccata omnium omnium hominum, qualia qualia, quanta quanta expiaret, & ut vaticinium Danielis habet, sub finem septuaginta hebdomadum, morte suâ auferret peccata, & justitiam adduceret. Tantum ergo abest, ut peccata vel Judæorum, vel Gentilium, definitum Messiæ adventum inhibere, aut impedire potuerint, ut illum potiùs promoverint: quemadmodum apud Jeremiâ disertis verbis testatur DOMINUS, quòd hanc ob causam accelerare velit fœdus illud novum, ut nimirùm peccata, contra vetus Legis pactum commissa, æternâ oblivione deleantur: Jerem. 31. v. 31. & seqq.

4. Ne ipsi quidem Judæi definire audent, vel etiam possunt peccatum illud à se, vel à majoribus suis commissum, cujus atrocitas tanta fuerit, ut promissionem Dei toties etiam juramento confirmatam, irritam redderet, vel saltem retraheret aut impediret.

5. Si maximè hoc figmentum Judæorum subsisteret, tamen peccati illius à majoribus designati pœnam non luerent posteri, secundum immotam justitiæ divinæ regulam: Jezech. 18, 20. Filius non portabit iniquitatem Patris.

6. Et postremo exceptio hæc Judæorum insigniter blasphema est in æternam ac infinitam DEI Omniscientiam. Si enim propter peccata Judæorum vel gentilium adventus Messiæ differri debuisset: utique Deus illa ipsa peccata prævidisset, & proindè aliud etiam tempus adventui Messiæ præfinivisset.

Cæterùm ut quæ de primâ hac Temporis circumstantiâ porrò dici possunt, in pauca contrahamus, sic contra Judæos inferimus: Si Templum illud secundum post Babylonicam captivitatem extructum, haud priùs destrui, & everti debuit, quàm promissus Mundi Messias illud præsentiâ suâ, concionibus & miraculis suis illustrasset, & hoc pacto gloriâ ejus Templo Salomonis augustiorem, magnificentioremq; reddidisset: Si quoq; ceremoniæ Leviticæ, non nisi in mundum edito Messia, abrogari debuerunt: necessariò, & prorsus invictè sequitur, cùm ante annos mille quingentos ampliùs, Templum illud secundum à Tito Vespafiani filio funditus sit dirutum atq; eversum: quin ipse quoq; Sacrificiorum ritus totidem annis sic antiquatus proptereà, quòd destructo templo ipsa quoque Sacrificia cessare debuerunt, secundum legē divinam, quæ Sacrificiorum ritum ad solum tabernaculum fœderis, sive Templi adstringebant, Deut. 12. v. 5. Sequitur, inquam, Messiam quoq; ante annos totidem in Mundum esse editum.

Antecedens gemino constat membro, sed utroq; ex Scripturis Sacris perspectissimo. Nam 1. Templum illud secundum ante adventum Messiæ destrui non debuisse, confirmat Haggæus cap. 2, 7. & 8. Adhuc modicum est, & ego commovebo cœlum & terram, mare & aridum, & commovebo omnes gentes, & VENIET DESIDERATUS omnibus gentibus, & replebo DOMUM ISTAM Gloriâ: Major erit gloria domus hujus posterioris gloriâ prioris, dicit Dominus exercituum. De quo vaticinio sic Rabbi Akiba, in lib. Sanhedrin, cap. Helec. De diebus Messiæ, & de Rege Messiah, & de tempore, quod fuit post destructionem primæ domus, agit Propheta. Neque ullius est teruntii, quòd recentiores Judæi dictum hoc obscurare conantur, contendentes, Gloriam secundi Templi fuisse & dici maiorem, non respectu Messiæ, sed durationis respectu, quia secundum hoc Templum priore illo diutius steterit. Sed esto, primum Templum Salomonis duraverit tantùm annis quadringentis & decem: secundum verò annis quadringentis viginti: annè differentia hæc decem tantùm annorum, tanti erit momenti, ut propterea tantam Templi secundi gloriam futuram Propheta prædixerit? Haud verò simile, &c. Malachias cap. 1. illud simpliciter negat.

Deindè diuturnior hæc duratio Templi secundi tantò est obscurior, quantò plures & graviores subindè devastationes experta est, jam ab Antiochio, qui etiam vasa templi abstulit, & demolitus est: imò Jovi Olympio ibidem simulachrum extruxit: jam à Pompejo, qui Hircano & Aristobulo de imperio dimicantibus, Jerosolymam veniens, captâ urbe, & templo devastato, usque ad Sanctum accessit: jam à Cassio, qui anno septimo Cleopatræ, Judæâ captâ templum ipsum spoliavit. Tot diruptiones, & devastationes, cûm primum illud Templum Salomonis non expertum sit, major utique ejus esset gloria, si ex duratione & conditione temporis faciendum esset judicium.

Ejusdem infirmitatis & vanitatis est, quicquid de externo ornatu, prioris Templi splendorem superante, nonnulli garriunt. Nam 1. contrarium legere licet lib. 1. Esdræ, c. 3. v. 12. ita, ut qui secundi Templi formam cum splendore prioris Templi conferebant, in lachrimas effusissimas prorumperent. 2. Non tantùm prius illud templum totum fermè erat obductum, & vasa ejus aurea; secundi verò vasa erant maximam partem ænea, ipsis Thalmudistis referentibus. 3. In priore Templo ignis cœlitus delapsus, holocausta comburebat: in secundo idem factum esse, vix probabitur. 4. In priore Gloria DEI in Sancto Sanctorum inter Cherubin apparebat: de secundo hoc nuspiam in sacris afferitur. Vide ipsum Thalmud lib. Sanhedrin Hierosol. cap. Elluhen haggòlin, hoc est: Isti sunt captivi.

Confirmat idem Malach. cap. 3. vers. 1. Ecce ego mittam Angelum meum, & parabit viam ante faciem meam. Et statim veniet ad Templum suum DOMINATOR, QVEM VOS QVÆRITIS, ET ANGELUS TESTAMENTI, QVEM VOS VVLTIS; Ecce venit, dicit Dominus exercituum.

Quoad posterius Antecedentis membrum, nempè abrogationem ceremoniarum Leviticarum, de eâ sic differit Jeremias c. 3, 15. Dabo vobis pastores juxta cor meum (intellige Apostolos) & pascent vos doctrinâ & scientiâ. Cumq; multiplicati fueritis, & creveritis in terrâ, in diebg illis, non dicent ultrà de arcâ fœderis Domini, nec ascendet super cor, nec recordabuntur illius, neque visitabunt eam, neque sacrificabitur ultrà ibi: sed in tempore illo erit Jerusalem solium Domini, & congregabuntur ad eam omnes gentes.

Jeremiæ adstipulatur Daniel, quando in postremâ Septimanâ, in quâ Christus Suum fœdus multis confirmaturus sit, Sacrificium & oblationem antiquandam scribit: cap. 9. v. 27. Undè Messias etiam dicitur Sacerdos secundum ordinem Melchisedech, non secundum ordinem Aarónis. Psalm. 110. vers. 4.

Quæ omnia licet Sole meridiano clariora sint, & Messiam jamdudùm venisse in mundum, ipsos etiam Judæos irrefragabiliter convincant: tanta tamen eorum est cœcitas, vel potiùs contumacia, ut, ne nostrum Messiam recipere necesse haberent falsos alios Messias, sed cum præsentissimo suo exitio, fabricarunt: Quales fuerunt ante destructam Hierolymam Theudas, & Judas Galilæus: Act. 5. v. 36. Joseph. lib. 20. antiquitat. 3. Qualis etiam fuit Barochba, qui anno quinqvagesimo secundo post destructam urbem Messiam sese venditavit: Cui cùm Judæorum plurimi adhærerent, Romani Imperii jugum excessuri factum, ut sub Hadriano Imp. plures Judæorum, quàm in ipsâ urbis devastatione, unà cum suo Messiâ fictitio, miserabiliter prostrati sint. Qva de re videatur ipsum etiam Judæorum Thalmud, lib Sanhedrin. pag. 97.


### On King Christ or Messiah: Just now in (continued)

And it is memorable what the Christian Gerson reports from Zemach David, page 61, that in the year of Christ 1500, a certain Rabbi Lemle prophesied in Austria, and established that very year, the fifteen hundredth, as the most certain term of the coming of the Messiah, provided that the Jews performed serious repentance. Giving credence to whose words, the Jews throughout that entire year, and indeed in the whole world where they lived dispersed, performed serious repentance, daily expecting the coming of the Messiah: but with vain effort and result. For that prophet soon perished, and that hoped-for Messiah appeared nowhere.

But let it suffice to have discoursed thus far concerning the first argument of our Demonstration, taken from the circumstance of Time.

We seek the OTHER argument from the circumstance of the Place, in which the promised Messiah had to be both born and educated, according to the prophecies of the Prophets: and thus we argue.

If that place alone, which was destined by the divine oracles of the Prophets for both the birth and the education of the Messiah, has utterly perished more than five hundred years ago, so that today it no longer exists: just as indeed, by the admission of the Jews themselves, it exists nowhere today, nor does any trace of it appear: It is a consequence, Either that the Messiah was brought into the world before as many years: or that GOD was not sufficiently consistent with himself in his predictions. But the latter is impious and blasphemous even to think: Therefore that former point remains settled and firm.

Now as for the truth of the Antecedent, not even the Jews themselves can deny that Bethlehem was destined by GOD himself for the birth, but Nazareth for the education and habitation of the Messiah. For thus Micah, ch. 5, v. 2. And you Bethlehem Ephrathah, although you are the least among the leaders of Judah, yet from you shall come forth to me, who is to be the ruler in Israel. Thus Isaiah defines the town of Nazareth through the נצר or root of Jesse and David, ch. 11, v. 1. For in vain do some seek and dispute whether the town of Nazareth of Galilee is written with Tsade, or indeed with Zain.

For it is manifest that, among the Jews, both letters were used in the word Nazareth: and that the Greek letter Zita corresponds to both. Therefore, whether the word Nazareth is derived from the Hebrew נצר Nezer with a Tsade, which signifies a sprout, shoot, or seedling: or from the Hebrew נזר Nezer, with a Zain, which signifies a crown: this epithet truly applies to Christ our Savior. For first, he himself is that Sprout, or shoot of the root of Jesse: then he is also crowned, separated, consecrated, and ordained to a certain office, proper to the Messiah. Where Pagninus rightly notes that the name נָזִיר Nazir, which signifies Separated, applies not only to him who is a Nazarene by vow: but to him who by the dignity of his office is separated from the common people. But the Evangelist Matthew clearly implies that the name of Nazarene is neither a name of a vow nor of an office, but a Gentile name: chap. 2. 23. He dwelt, he says (the child Jesus) in a city which is called Nazareth: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the Prophets, He shall be called a Nazarene. Nor does that anxious dispute of Chrysostom, Jerome, and others move us much, who ask, Where in the Scriptures has it been predicted of Christ? He shall be called a Nazarene? For 1. All the Nazarenes of the Old Testament bore the type of the Nazarene Messiah or Christ. 2. Judg. 13, 5. it is read concerning Samson: He shall be called a Nazarene of GOD from the womb. Now indeed Samson bore the type of the Messiah himself in most things. Therefore, nothing prevents us from applying that definition of the name to the Messiah as well. 3. There seems to be no need for us to take refuge in that place of Judges 13. 5. For because the Evangelist Matthew asserts that it was predicted not in the singular, but in the plural number, by the PROPHETS, He shall be called a Nazarene: he certainly wished to point us, as if with an index finger, to those oracles of the Prophets in which the future Messiah of the World is called נצר, that is, a sprout, twig, plant, or germ, not only by reason of birth or origin, but also allusively to the Place in which the Messiah was to dwell, as the Evangelist Matthew teaches. Such prophecies of the Prophets exist not only in Isa. 11. v. 1. But also in Isa. 60. v. 21. And thy people shall all be righteous, they shall inherit the land forever, the branch of my planting, the work of my hands, that I may be glorified.

But, to return to the matter, it is not obscure or unknown even to the Jews themselves, that both Bethlehem and Nazareth are towns so destroyed, devastated, and reduced to ashes, that hardly any trace of them appears anymore. Therefore, the Conclusion maintains its immovable truth, by which it is inferred that the King Messiah, or Christ the Lord, has already come into the flesh, and has been born.

THE THIRD argument of our demonstration we seek from the notation of the family, or tribe of Judah, from which the Prophets long ago predicted that the Messiah would be born: that which was above from the prophecy of the Patriarch Jacob Gen. 49.

v. 10. has been abundantly proven, so that not even the Jews themselves dare to deny it. Now, however, for more than fifteen hundred years, there has been, and today still is, such a confusion of the twelve Jewish tribes, that where or which is the tribe of Judah cannot be known even to the Jews themselves. Therefore, from this also it is gathered quite evidently that the Messiah has long since come into this world: and that he is no longer to be expected.

THE FOURTH and final argument is supplied by those prophecies of the Prophets which affirm in express words that, once the Messiah is exhibited, all Nations and peoples will come to the Messiah, and through him will believe in the GOD of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, having left their Idols and abominations. Now, indeed, that this very thing happened more than fifteen hundred years ago, both sacred and Ecclesiastical history testifies, which describes the conversion of the nations. Therefore, that the Messiah has already now, and indeed so many centuries ago, been truly exhibited to the world, can be a doubt to no pious person. And as long as the Jews cannot prove that the Nations follow and embrace anyone else besides the GOD of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob? so long are they held convicted in their own conscience that they have absolutely no just causes for tergiversation.

These things being thus settled, it remains that we respond to the principal arguments of the Jews, by which they impiously and stubbornly deny that the Messiah has not yet come into the world.

The first and chief point is almost that which we have already touched upon above, where we dealt with the Circumstance of Time, destined in the scriptures for the advent of the Messiah: showing that no sin, either of the Jews or of the Gentiles, could have been so atrocious or horrendous that it could have overturned, changed, or in any way hindered those predictions of GOD.

The remaining points, which one may read in P. Galatinus and other writers, are these:

FIRST: they imagine that two distinct and clearly different Messiahs were predicted by the Prophets: one the son of David, the other the son of Joseph, of whom the latter indeed came into the world long ago, but because he was not that true Messiah who could liberate the Jewish people from servitude, he was therefore killed by the Jews themselves; but the former has not yet come into the world, because that liberation of the people has not yet actually occurred. Now, that dream of the Jews concerning two different Messiahs, the Talmud, in its explanation of the prophecy of Gen. 49:14, 'Issachar is a strong ass,' strives to confirm as follows: It is written in Isa. 32:20, 'Blessed are they that sow beside all waters': if anyone does so, he shall merit Elijah and the two Messiahs: For thus it is in the Prophet: 'Sending forth the foot of the ox and the ass': For as it is read in the Hebrew רגל השׁור והחמור

Where by the word (Senders) Elias is to be understood, according to that in the last of Malachi, v. 5. Behold I send you Elias the Prophet. But by the foot of the ox is to be understood the Messiah, son of Joseph: according to that, Deut. 33. v. 17. His firstling bull, his glory. Finally, by the foot of the Ass is to be understood the other Messiah, son of David: of whom it is written Zach. 9. v. 9. Poor and riding upon an ass. Which very fable of the Jews is repeated in the book of the same Talmud, whose title is, Succah, chapter Hahelil hannischa, in these words: The Rabbanae, that is, the Masters, have handed down, that the Messiah son of David, who is to redeem, will quickly redeem in our days, and the Holy and blessed God will say to him: Ask of me something, and I will give it to thee: And when this Messiah, son of David, shall have seen the other Messiah, son of Joseph, killed, he himself will say to God: Lord of the world, I do not ask of thee anything, except life. Then the Holy God will say to him: Dost thou ask life of me? And this thy father David already prophesied concerning thee, Psal. 21, 5. He asked life of thee, and thou gavest him length of days for ever and ever. Thus far the Talmud of the Jews.

can powerfully perform and accomplish. Which description of the Messiah, since it contains an exclusive force in itself, and admits no other anointed one into the fellowship of that anointing: it is inferred by irrefragable necessity, that neither two, nor more: but only one has been predicted as the Messiah, or Christ the Redeemer of the World. Whence Daniel also calls this Anointed one or Messiah, in distinction to all other anointed ones, κατ' ἐξοχήν קֹדֶשׁ קָדָשִׁים Holiness of Holinesses, or as the Latin interpreter rendered it; Holy of Holies, for the reason that this One is to finish the transgression, that is, to expiate sins, and to bring in everlasting righteousness upon the people. Daniel 9. v. 24.

But that this fable may be utterly overturned, its individual members must be weighed more accurately. And in the beginning indeed we do not deny, that the Hebrew מָשִׁיחַ Messiah, by reason of its etymology and signification (for it signifies the same as anointed) generally pertains not to any one Individual, but to all those anointed in the Old Testament, whether Kings or Priests, being indeed anointed with a certain oil, which is described Exod. 30. v. 23. & seqq. Whence Saul, 1. Reg. 24. v. 7. and Cyrus, Isa. 45. v. 1. are named Messiah, Anointed. And according to this general signification, we willingly grant to the Jews, that not one only, nor just two, but more Messiahs are noted in the Scriptures of the Old Testament. But now, as to the other member of the response, a malicious change of the State of the Controversy is committed, regarding the present dispute. For this does not come into question: Whether the Holy Spirit in the Prophetic Scriptures adapts the word Messiah to many? which we do not deny: But this is the question: Whether the same Holy Spirit, in the same Prophetic Scriptures, describes such a Messiah, who κατ' ἐξοχήν alone and as one, claims for himself the name and office of Messiah, the Redeemer of the whole World. Here we hold the affirmative against the Jews in all respects, moved by the irrefragable evidence of the Prophetic oracles, which make mention of one Shiloh, one Christ or Messiah, Genesis 40. Daniel 9. v. 24. indeed of such an anointed one, who admits no mortal into the society of his anointing: according to that Psal. 45. v. 8. Thy GOD hath anointed thee, O GOD, with the oil of gladness above thy fellows: namely with an infinite fullness of the Holy Spirit, by whose virtue he might powerfully and effectively perform and accomplish that redemption of the world. Thirdly, that the Jews imagine a Messiah, who is to be the redeemer of the people, will not be killed: in that they truly betray a stupendous blindness, and ignorance of the prophetic predictions: For what could ever have been said more clearly on this matter, than what Daniel pronounces in express words concerning this very Messiah the Redeemer of the World, v. 26. And after sixty-two weeks מָשִׁיחַ יִכָּרֵת the Messiah shall be cut off? that the same Zacharias chap. 12. v. 10. in express words expresses the very kind of death, by which the Messiah the redeemer of the World was to be killed, namely Crucifixion: They shall look, he says, אֶת־אֲשֶׁר־דָּקָרוּ whom they have pierced? We therefore invert the argument of the Jews, and we invincibly conclude from this very thing, that our Messiah is that promised Messiah of the World, because he was killed: so much so, that even if all the other criteria of the Messiah belonged to our Messiah the son of David, but this one were lacking, then he could not, and should not, be recognized and held as the true Messiah. Nor does that of Psal. 21. v. 5. stand in the way. For although the Messiah according to the flesh truly died: yet this very Flesh of Christ was even in death vivifying, indeed life itself, not only by reason of the most efficacious merit for the life of the world: but also by reason of itself, insofar as by this his vivifying virtue, he raised his flesh from the dead, and recalled it to life, so that death can no longer have dominion over him, and this promise of the Psalm was most truly fulfilled: He asked life of thee, and thou gavest him length of days for ever and ever.

Latin:

Et memorabile est, quod Christianus Gerfon ex Zemach David. pag. 61. refert, Anno Chr sti 1500. in Austria prophetasse quemdam Rabbi Lemle, & terminum certissimum adventus Messiæ constituisse illum ipsum annum millesimum quingentesimum, modò Judæi seriam agerent pœnitentiam. Cujus verbis fidem adhibentes Judæi per integrum illum annum, & toto quidem orbe, ubi dispersi vivebant, seriam agebant pœnitentiam, indies expectantes Messiæ adventum: sed irrito conatu & eventu. Nam & Prophetâ ille mox periit, & Messias ille speratus nuspiam apparuit.

Sed de primo Demonstrationis nostræ argumento, à Temporis circumstantiâ petito, hæc hactenus disseruisse, sufficiat.

ALTERUM argumentum petimus à circumstantiâ Loci, in quo & nasci & educari debuit promissus Messias, secundum Prophetarum vaticinia:& sic argumentamur.

Si solus ille, qui divinis Prophetarum oraculis, tùm nativitatis, tùm educationi Messiæ fuit destinatus; antè annos qvingentos ampliùs funditus periit, ut hodiè non exsistat ampliùs: qvemadmodum sanè ipsis fatentibus Judæis hodiè nuspiam extat, neq; ullum ejus apparet vestigium: Consequens est, Aut Messiam ante totidem annos in mundum fuisse editum: aut DEUM in prædictionibus suis sibi non satis constitisse. At posterius hoc vel cogitatu impium ac blasphemum: Ergò ratum ac firmum manet illud prius.

Jam qvoad Antecedentis veritatem, negare ne ipsi quidem Judæi possunt, Bethlehemum nativitati: Nazarethum verò educationi & habitationi Messiæ à DEO ipso fuisse destinatum. Sic enim Mich. c.5.v. 2. Et tu Bethlehem Ephrataa, licet minima sis in ducibus Judæ, ex te tamen mihi egredietur, qui sit dominator in Israel. Sic Esaias definit per נצר sive radicem Isai & Davidis, oppidum Nazareth cap. 11. v. 1. Frustra enim quærunt & disputant nonnulli, num Nazareth oppidum Galilææ, per Tsade, an verò per Zain scribatur.

Manifestum enim est, apud Judæos utramq; literam in voce Nazareth usurpatam fuisse : utriq; respondere etiam Græcam literam Zita. Sive ergò vocabulum Nazareth derivetur ab Hebræo נצר Nezer per Tsade, qvod germen, surculum, sive plantulam significat : sive ab Hebræo נזר Nezer, per Zain, qvod coronam significat: verè tamen hoc epitheton Christo Servatori nostro competit. Nam primùm ipse est Germen illud, sive surculus radicis Isai: deinde est & coronatus, separatus, consecratus, & ordinatus ad certum officium, Messiæ proprium. Ubi rectè annotat Pagninus, nomen נָזִיר Nazir, quod Separatum significat, non tantùm competere ei, qvi exvoto sit Nazarenus: sed qui dignitate officij à vulgo sit separatus. Verùm Evangelista Matthæus, Nazaræi nomen neque voti, neque officij, sed nomen Gentile esse, perspicuè innuit: cap. 2. 23. Habitavit, inquiens (puerulus Iesus) in urbe, quæ dicitur Nazareth: ut impleretur, quod dictum est per Prophetas, Nazarenus vocabitur. Neque nos multùm movet anxia illa disputatio Chrysostomi, Hieronymi, & aliorum, quærentium, Ubinam in Scripturis de Christo prædictum sit? Nazaræus vocabitur? Nam 1. Omnes Nazaræi Veteris Testamenti gesserunt typum Nazaræi Messiæ sive Christi. 2. Iudic. 13, 5. de Simsone legitur: Nazaræus DEI vocabitur ab utero. Jam vero Simson typum gessit ipsius Messiæ in plerisque. Nihil ergò obstat, quò minùs & istam nominis definitionem ad Messiam accommodeinus. 3. Non opus esse videtur, ut ad locum istum Iudicum 13. 5. confugiamus. Quia enim Evangelista Matthæus non in singulari, sed plurali numero, per PROPHETAS prædictum esse asserit, Nazaræus vocabitur: utique tanquàm digito indice ablegare nos voluit ad ea Prophetarum oracula, in qvibus futurus Mundi Messias נצר, hoc est, surculus, virgula, planta, germen passim nominatur, non modò ratione nativitatis sive originis, sed & allusivè ad Locum, in quo Messias esset habitaturus, sic docente Evangelista Matthæo. Talia Prophetarum vaticinia extant non modò Esa. 11. v.1. Sed & Esa. 60. v. 21. Et populus tuus omnes ipsi justi, in seculum hæreditate accipient terrâ נֵצֶר מַטָעַוֹ virgultum plantationum mearum, opus manuum mearum, ad glorificandum me.

Sed, ut ad rem redeamus, nec ipsis etiam Judæis obscurum ut incognitum est, & Bethlehemum, & Nazarethum oppida esse ita diruta, vastata, & in cineres redacta, ut vix eorum ullum ampliùs appareat vestigium. Constat ergo Conclusioni sua immota veritas, qvâ infertur Regem Messiam, sive Christum Dominum jam in carnem venisse, & natum esse.

TERTIUM demonstrationis nostræ argumentum petimus à notatione familiæ, sive tribus Judah, ex quâ Messiam nasciturum Prophetæ jam olim prædixerunt: id qvod suprà ex vaticinio Patriarchæ Jacobi Genes. 49.

vev. 10. abundè comprobatum est, ita ut ne ipsi quoque Judæi id negare ausint. Jam verò annis mille qvingentis ampliùs ea fuit, hodieque est duodecim tribuum Judaicarum confusio, ut ubinàm vel qvænàm sit tribus Juda, ne ipsis qvidem Judæis constare possit. Ergò vel indè quoque satis evidenter colligitur, Messiam jampridem hunc in mundum venisse: nec ampliùs ipsum expectandum esse.

QVARTUM & postremum argumentum suppeditant ea Prophetarum vaticinia, quæ disertis verbis affirmant, exhibito Messiah, omnes Gentes & populos venturos ad Messiam, & per ipsum credituros in DEUM Abraham, Isaac, & Iacob, suis relictis Idolis & abominationibus. Jam verò hoc ipsum itidem ante annos mille quingentos ampliùs evenisse, testatur historia tùm sacra, tùm Ecclesiastica, quæ conversionem gentium describit. Ergò Messiam jam modò, & quidem ante tot secula verè in mundum exhibitum esse, pio nemini potest esse dubium. Et quamdiu Iudæi probare non possunt, Gentes alium quem piam, præter DEUM Abraham, Isaac, & Jacob sequi & amplecti? tamdiu in propria conscientiâ convicti tenentur, se plane nullas habere justas tergiversandi causas.

His ita expeditis, reliquum est, ut ad præcipua Iudæorum argumenta, quibus Messiam nondùm in mundum venisse, impiè & præfractè negant, respondeamus.

Primum ac præcipuum est fermè illud, quod jam suprà, ubi de de Circumstantiâ Temporis, adventui Messiæ in sacris destinatæ, egimus, protrivimus: ostendentes, nullum vel Iudæorum, vel Gentilium peccatum, tam atrox aut horrendum esse potuisse, quod prædictiones illas DEI invertere, mutare, aut quovis modo impedire potuerit.

Reliqua, quæ apud P. Galatinum, & alios Scriptores legere licet, sunt ist hæc:

PRIMUM: fingunt duos distinctos ac planè diversos Messias per Prophetas prædictos fuisse: Unum filium Davidis: alterum filium Josephi, quorum iste jampridem quidem in mundum venerit, sed quia non fuerit verus ille Messias, qui populum Judaicum ex servitute liberare poterat, ideoque à Judæis ipsis interfectus sit: ille verò nondum in Mundum venerit, quia liberatio illa populi nondum ipso actu evenerit. Somnium verò illud de duobus diversis Messijs Judæorum Thalmud in explicatione vaticinij Gen. 49, 14. Isaschar asinus fortis, sic confirmare studet: Scriptum est Ies. 32. ult. Beati seminantes super aquas: si quis ita fecerit, merebitur Eliam, & duos Messias: Sic enim apud Prophetam: Mittentes pedem bovis, & pedem asini: Nam ut in Hebræo legitur רגל השׁור והחמור

Ubi per vocabulum (Mittentes) Elias est intelligendus, secundum illud Malachiæ ultimo, verf. 5. Ecce ego mitto vobis Eliam Prophetam. Per pedem verò bovis intelligendus est Messias, filius Joseph: secundum illud, Deut. 33.v.17. Primogenitus bos ejus, decor ejus. Per pedem deniq; Asini intelligendus est alter Messias, filius David: de quo scriptum est Zach. 9. v. 9. Pauper & equitans super asinam. Quæ ipsa Judæorum fabella repetitur in libro ejusdem Talmud, cui titulus est, Succhæ, cap. Hahelil hannischa, his verbis: Tradiderunt Rabbanæ, hoc est, Magistri, quòd Messias filius David, qui redemturus est, citò redimet in diebus nostris, dicetq; ei Deus Sanctus & benedictus: Pete à me aliquid, & dabo tibi: Cùmque hic Messias, filius David, viderit Messiam alterum filium Josephi interfectu, dicet ipse ad Deum: Domine seculi, non ego peto à te, nisi vitam. Tum dicet ei Deus Sanctus: Vitam petis à me? Et hoc jam prophetavit super te David pater tuus, Psal. 21, 5. Vitam petiit à te, & dedisti ei longitudinem dierum in seculum & ultra. Hactenus Talmud Judæorum.

caciter præstare & perficere possit. Quæ Messia descriptio, cùm vim exclusivam in se contineat, & nullum alium unctum in consortium istius unctionis admittat: irrefragabili necessitate infertur, neque duos, neque plures: sed unicum tantùm prædictum esse Messiam, sive Christum Mundi Redemtorem. Undè Daniel quoq; Unctum istum sive Messiam, ad differentiam reliquorum omnium unctorum, nominat κατ' ἐξοχήν קֹדֶשׁ קָדָשִׁים Sanctitatem Sanctitatum, vel ut Latinus interpres reddidit; Sanctum Sanctorum, eò quòd Unus iste consummaturus sit prævaricationem, hoc est, expiaturus peccata, & adducturus super populum sempiternam justitiam. Daniel. 9. v. 24.

Cæterùm ut hæc fabella funditùs evertatur, singula ejus membra accuratiùs expendenda veniunt. Ac initiò quidem non negamus, Hebræum מָשִׁיחַ Messiah, ratione etymi & significationis (idem enim, ac unctum significat) generaliter non uni alicui Individuo, sed omnibus in Veteri Testamento unctis, sive Regibus, sive Sacerdotibus competere, quippè inunctis certo quodam oleo, quod describitur Exod. 30. v. 23. & seqq. Undè Saul, 1. Reg. 24. v 7. & Cyro, Jes. 45. v. 1. nominantur Messiah, Uncti. Et secundum generalem hanc significationem, ultrò largimur Judæis, non unum tantùm, neque duos duntaxat, sed plures Messias in Scripturis Veteris Testamenti notari. Jam verò, quòd alterum responsionis membrum est, malitiosa committitur Status Controversiæ mutatio, quoad præsentem disputationem. Non enim hoc in quæstionem venit: An Spiritus Sanctus in Scripturis Propheticis vocabulum Messiah ad plures accommodet? id quod nos non negamus: Sed hoc quæstionis est: An idem Spiritus Sanctus, in iisdem Scripturis Propheticis, talem aliquem Messiam describat, qui κατ' ἐξοχήν solus & unus, nomen & officium Messiæ, totius Mundi Redemtoris sibi vendicet. Hic nos affirmativam contra Judæos per omnia tenemus, moti irrefragabili evidentiâ oraculorum Propheticorum, quæ unius Siloh, unius Christi sive Messiæ, Genesi. 40. Daniel. 9. v. 24. imò ejusmodi uncti meminerunt, qui in societatem unctionis suæ neminem mortalium admittat: secundù illud Psal. 45. v.8. Unxit te DEUS tuus ô DEUS, oleo lætitiæ ultra consortes tuos: nempè infinitâ Spiritus Sancti plenitudine, cujus virtute Redemtionem illam mundi potenter & effiTertiò, quòd Judæi fingunt Messiam, qui redemtor futurus populi, non interfectum iri: in eò sanè stupendam cæcitatem, & vaticiniorum propheticorum ignorantiam ipsimet produnt: Quid enim clarius hac de re dici unquam potuisset, quàm quòd Daniel de hoc ipso Messiah Mundi Redemtore, disertis verbis pronunciat, v.26.Et post hebdomadas sexaginta duas מָשִׁיחַ יִכָּרֵת excindetur Messias? quòd idem Zacharias cap.12. v.10. disertis verbis ipsum genus mortis, quo Messias Mundi redemtor interimendus erat, Crucifixionem nimirùm, exprimit: Adspicient inquiens, אֶת־אֲשֶׁר־דָּקָרוּ quem transfixerunt? Invertimus ergò argumentum Judæorum, & invictè vel indè colligimus, ob hoc ipsum Messiam nostrum verum esse illam promissum Mundi Messiam, quia interfectus fuit: usq; adeò, ut si vel maximè relinquamnia Messiæ κριτήρια, Messiæ nostro Davidis filio competerent, hoc unum autem deesset, tùm pro vero Messiah agnosci, haberique nec posset, nec deberet. Nequ: obstat illud Psal.21. v.5. Nam licet Messias secundum carnem verè sit mortuus: hæc ipsa tamen Caro Christi etiam in morte erat vivifica, imò vita, ipsa non modò ratione meriti efficacissimi pro mundi vitâ: sed & ratione suiipsius, quatenùs hàc suâ virtute vivificâ, carnem suam ex mortuis resuscitavit, & in vitam revocavit, ita, ut mors ipsi ampliùs dominari non possit, & verissimè impleta hæc promissio Psalmi: Vitam petiit à te, & dedisti ei longitudinem dierum in seculum seculi.


### On King Christ or Messiah: Just now in (continued)

Fourthly, it is a pure and unadulterated lie, that the Jews assert that Jesus of Nazareth the son of Mary is not the son of David: but of Joseph: which will be demonstrated to the eye in the following second question. Finally, regarding the Prophetic oracle Isa. 32. v. 20. Blessed are ye who sow upon all waters, sending forth the foot of the ox and the ass, a clearly violent and malicious depravation of the text is committed. For first, it is a clearly inept and ridiculous argument, by which they conclude thus: Elias is said to be about to be sent in Malachi, but here it is held in the text, Senders: Therefore Elias is noted here.

…For 1. a gross fallacy of many terms is detected. 2. nothing militate

ἐλεγχο̃ in connexo. 3. In this passage it is found in the plural, Mittentes: Therefore, one individual Elijah is not expressed. 4. This interpretation fights diametrically against the Prophetic intention, as will be shown presently; thus it is a ridiculous and impudent fiction that by the foot of an ox one Messiah is denoted, namely the son of Joseph: and by the foot of an ass, the other Messiah, the son of David. For even the Jews themselves understand that all these things are twisted and violent. For although Moses in Deut. 33.v.17, in the blessing of Joseph, predicts that his beauty or glory will be like that of a firstborn bull: yet this does nothing to confirm a certain distinct Messiah, different from the other son of David. For the Rabbis of the ancient Jews themselves also understood not two different Messiahs, but two distinct and diverse advents of one and the same Messiah: so that by the Son of Joseph they denoted his humility and meekness; by the Son of David, his nobility and Kingdom: concerning which matter Nicolaus Lyra discourses both orthodoxly and acutely upon this very passage of Deuteronomy, saying: Christ is the fatted calf, which the Father sacrificed, being the first-born from the herd of the Fathers: who, being raised on the third day, appeared glorious: who is the first-born of the dead and the prince of the kings of the earth: after the glory of the resurrection, from the power of the passion he adds the horns of the Rhinoceros, that is, the horns of the cross, of which Habakkuk says in chapter 3: There is his strength hidden. For through the infirmity of the flesh, like a ram, he is crowned with the thorns of those who mocked him; he stuck to these horns. For by the incomparable fortitude of his passion, the Unicorn stood forth as the victor of death, and of him who held the empire of death: Whence: That which is weak of GOD, is stronger than men.

Furthermore, regarding that passage in Zech. 9:9, "Lowly and riding upon an ass," the Jews clearly prove themselves to be struck by the gadfly of a horrendous blindness by the fact that they interpret it as referring to a second Messiah, the son of Joseph. For is not that supposed son of Joseph, but truly the son of David, the one who is riding upon an ass? Is he not the one to whom, according to the prophecy of Zechariah, the Jews themselves shouted: "Hosanna to the son of David: Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord: Hosanna in the highest"? Matt. 21:9. Is he not the very one who, having entered Jerusalem poor and humble, was three days later, at the insistent demand of the Jews, affixed to the cross? Away, therefore, with that ἀσύστατον and self-contradictory fiction of a double Messiah: one the son of Joseph, the other the son of David. But as regards the proper and genuine sense of the words of Isaiah, the Prophet describes the happiness of the New Testament by means of metaphorical words, having instituted this consideration and comparison with the Old Testament. For in the Old, and indeed in Deut. 22.v.10, it was forbidden to the Jews that in plowing they should use both an ox and an ass together: namely, one animal clean, the other unclean; one tractable, the other intractable and stubborn; one born for plowing, the other for carrying burdens. Which Law allegorically and spiritually denoted that the divine worship of the Church of the Old Testament was yoked to the ox, that is, to that people which was subject to the offering of sacrifices and to Levitical ceremonies, namely, the Jewish. Alluding therefore to this Law, the Prophet Isaiah, in figurative words likewise, shows that it would be the liberty of the Church of the New Testament that one should plow not with the ox alone, but with the ox and the ass: that is, that the sermons of the Apostles and the entire worship of the New Testament, which consists in the preaching of the Word and the administration of the Sacraments, would be common to the Gentiles and the Jews, and that the doctrine of the Gospel, as that incorruptible seed, is to be scattered and proposed in every field throughout the whole world: or, as Lyranus explains, that the strong and the weak, the learned and the simple, are to be taught indifferently and without respect of persons.

The second argument of the Jews, taken from Scripture, is as follows: In Isaiah 11, v. 12, it is read: In that day the root of Jesse shall set up a sign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.

And yet this has not yet come to pass: for the sad dispersion of Israel and the exile of Judah continues even to this day.

Therefore.

I answer. A gross ignorance of the Elenchus is committed, born from that preconceived dream of the Jews concerning an external and corporal kingdom of the Messiah, and concerning an external liberation and gathering of the Jewish people: and their restitution to their former dignity: which error we correct in this manner, arguing from the prophecy both of Isaiah and of the remaining Prophets.

Such as the kingdom of the Messiah was to be: such was the deliverance and gathering together of the Jews predicted by the prophets, resulting from this kingdom of the Messiah.

And yet the kingdom of the Messiah was not to be an external or corporal kingdom, but a spiritual one.

Therefore such a liberation and gathering of the Jews was also foretold by the Prophets.

The assumption was evident from chapter 2 of this treatise concerning the kingdom of Christ. The truth of the conclusion, however, is clear in itself.

For this very spiritual liberation and gathering of the Jewish people was accomplished and fulfilled when, through the preaching of the Gospel, many thousands of Jews were converted to the faith of Christ, and together with the Gentiles were gathered from the whole world into the fellowship of one kingdom. This spiritual liberation or gathering of the dispersed of Israel began at the feast of Pentecost of the New Testament: and was subsequently continued through the ministry of the Apostles: where not even the Jews themselves can deny that a great multitude of Jews embraced the doctrine and faith of Christ. This very collection endures even today, and will endure until the very end of the age, and indeed not without the evident conversion of many Jews. For according to that of the Apostle, blindness in part has happened to Israel, until the fullness of the Gentiles should come in: and so all Israel should be saved: Rom. 11. v. 25. But to which collection John also looked, chap. 11. v. 52, writing that Jesus was to die for the nation, and not for the nation only: but also that he should gather together in one the children of GOD that were scattered abroad. Speaking summarily, there is predicted in this place that spiritual association of Jews and Gentiles, scattered throughout the whole world, into the unity and fellowship of the Church of the New Testament: so that Israel and Judah denote not so much a certain nation, as a profession and the Christian faith. For they are not all children of the flesh who are children of GOD: but they who are the children of the promise are counted for the seed: For in Isaac shall thy seed be called: Gen. 21. v. 12. Rom. 9. v. 7. & 8.

is to be accepted as benefits. For God promises in this place that He will heap upon the Jews, brought back from Babylon, more ample benefits than their fathers had experienced. Now if you look at external and bodily benefits, this was never fulfilled in them. It remains, therefore, that if this divine promise is to have its truth stand firm, this promise must be accepted concerning spiritual benefits, conferred upon the Jews under the kingdom of the Messiah through the preaching of the Gospel. Which very thing is irrefragably proven from the sixth verse of this same chapter, which promises to the Jews the spiritual circumcision of the heart, which is done through the preaching of the Gospel and the illumination of the Holy Spirit.

The FOURTH Argument, taken from chap. 6, 12 of Zechariah, the more recent Jews formulate thus: Thus saith the Lord of hosts, saying: Behold the man, whose name is the Branch, and he shall grow up out of his place, and he shall build the temple of the Lord: Even he shall build the temple of the Lord, and he shall bear the glory, and shall sit and rule upon his throne: And he shall be a Priest upon his throne: and the counsel of peace shall be between them both. But these things have not yet happened: for neither has a third temple been built, indeed it has never even begun to be built.

Therefore the Messiah has not yet come into the world.

I RESPOND. That the Prophet is speaking of Christ or the Messiah is, on our part also, beyond controversy. For the Messiah is a man, because he was born a true man: He is indeed also the Branch צמח not only by reason of the promises made of old concerning the Messiah: but also, because (as the Hebrew text has it) under himself, or from himself under himself, the Messiah was to sprout, ומתחתיו יצמח, inasmuch as, of course, by his own power, without human aids, he was to be a man and was to administer his own kingdom. And concerning this, there is no dispute in this place. The other matter rather comes into question: whether the following words of the Prophet prove that this Messiah, brought forth into the world, would build a third temple in these lands? which the more recent Jews affirm. But we deny it: and indeed for reasons that are far more evident. For 1. concerning the building of any third temple, namely an external and earthly one, to be adorned by the Messiah in this world, in the entire Holy Scripture one cannot find even a single little word. 2. The Rabbis of the Jews themselves refute this figment, when in the book Neziruth, that is, of Separation, chap. Bethsammai, upon the words of Jeremiah 7. v. 4, Trust ye not in lying words, saying, The temple of the Lord, The temple of the Lord, The temple of the Lord: they commented thus: What is that which is written, The temple of the Lord, The temple of the Lord? That is the first and second Sanctuary.

Latin:

Quartò purum putum est mendacium, quòd Judæi asserunt, Jesum Nazarenum Mariæ filium, non esse filium Davidis: sed Josephi: id quod subsequente quæstione altera ad oculum demonstrabitur. Tandem quoad oraculum Propheticum Jesa. 32. v. 20. Beati, qui seminatis super omnes aquas mittentes pedem bovis & asini, violenta planè & malitiosa committitur textus depravatio. Nam primùm, ineptum planè est & ridiculum argumentum, quo sic colligunt: Elias apud Malachiam dicitur Mittendus, atqui hic habetur in textu, Mittentes: Ergò hic notatur Elias.

Nam 1. crassa deprehenditur ἀσυλλογιsia plurium terminorum. 2. nullus militat

ἐλεγχο̃ in connexo. 3. hoc loco habetur in plurali, Mittentes : Ergò non exprimitur Unum Eliæ individuum. 4. Cum intentione Propheticâ hæc interpretatio diametraliter pugnat, uti mox ostendetur, sic ridiculum & impudens figmentum est, per pedem bovis notari unum Messiam, nempè filium Josephi: per pedem Asini, alterum Messiam, filium Davidis. Contorta enim & violenta esse hæc omnia, vel ipsi Judæi intelligunt. Nam licèt Moses Deut 33.v.17. in benedictione Josephi prædicit, pulchritudinem sive gloriam ejus, futuram instar primogeniti tauri : nihil tamen hoc facit ad confirmandum distinctu quendam Messiam, ab altero Davidis filio diversum. Nam ipsi quoque Judæorum antiquiorum Rabbini non duos diversos Messias, sed duos distinctos ac diversos adventus unius numero, ejusdemq́; Messiæ intellexerunt: ita ut per Filium Josephi humilitatem ac man suetudinem; per Filium Davidis nobilitatem, ac Regnum ipsius notarent : Quâ de re sic & orthodoxe & argutè disserit Nicolaus Lyra, super hunc ipsum locum Deuteronomii: Christus, inquiens, vitulus est saginatus, quem de armento Patrum primogenitum Pater immolavit : qui die tertia suscitatus, gloriosus apparuit : qui est primogenitus mortuorum & princeps Regum terræ: post resurrectionis gloriam de virtute passionis adjungit cornua Rhinocerotis, id est, cornua crucis, de quibus ait Habacuc cap. 3. Ibi abscondita est fortitudo ejus. Per infirmitatem namq́; carnis, quasi aries, illusorum spinis coronatur; his cornibus hæsit. Scilicet passionis incomparabili fortitudine Unicornis extitit mortis victor, & ejus, qui habebat mortis imperium: Undè: Quod infirmum est DEO, fortius est hominibus.

Porrò quoad illud Zachar. 9.v.9. Pauper & equitans super asinam: id quod de altero Messiah filio Davidis accipiunt, semetipsos Judæi horrendæ cæcitatis æstro percitos esse luculenter comprobant. Annon enim Messias ille Josephi putatitius: verè autem Davidis filius, est iste equitans super asinam? Annon ille est, cui ex Zachariæ vaticinio acclamatum ab ipsis Judæis: Hosianna filio David: Benedictus, qui venit in nomine Domini: Hosianna in altissimis? Matth. 21. v. 9. Annon ille ipse est, qui pauper & humilis Hierosolymis ingressus, triduo pòst, sic flagitantibus Judæis, cruci fuit affixus? Facescat ergò ἀσύστατον istud, & nullâ sui cohærens figmentum de duplici Messiah: Uno Josephi, altero Davidis filio. Sed quoad proprium ac genuinum sensum verborum Esaiæ, describit Propheta verbis Metaphoricis felicitatem Novi Testamenti institutâ hujus consideratione & collatione ad Vetus Testamentum. Nam in Veteri, & quidem Deut. 22.v.10. prohibitum erat Judæis, ut in arando simul uterentur & bove, & asino: altero videlicet animante mundo, altero immundo: altero tractabili, altero intractabili & contumace : altero ad arandum, altero ad ferendum onera nato. Quæ Lex allegoricè & spiritualiter notabat, cultum divinum Ecclesiæ Veteris Testamenti allegatum esse ad bovem, hoc est, ad eum populum qui sacrificiis offerendis, & ceremoniis Leviticis subjacebat, nempè Judaicum. Ad hanc Legem ergo alludens Propheta Esaias, verbis itidem figuratis, ostendit, eam fore libertatem Ecclesiæ Novi Testamenti, ut non in solo bove, sed in bove & asino sit arandum : hoc est: Apostolorum conciones, & universum Novi Testamenti cultum, qui in prædicatione Verbi, & administratione Sacramentorum consistit, fore gentibus & Judæis communem, doctrinamq; Evangelii, tanquam semen illud incorruptibile, in omni agro, per totum terrarum orbem spargendam ac proponendam esse : vel uti Lyranus explicat, indifferenter, & sine acceptatione personarum docendos esse fortes & debiles: literatos & simplices.
