Alterum Judæorum argumentum ex Scripturâ petitum sic habet: Jesaię 11. v. 12. legitur: In die illâ radix Jesse levabit signum in nationes & congregabit profugos Israel, & dispersos Juda colliget à quatuor plagis terræ.

Atqui hoc nondum evenit : Tristis enim dispersio Israelis, & exilium Judab hodieq́; durat.

Ergò.

Respondeo. Committitur crassa ignoratio Elenchi, nata ex præconcepto illo somnio Judæorum de externo ac corporali Messiæ regno, deque externâ liberatione & collectione populi Judaici : Ejusdemque restitutione in dignitatem pristinam : Quem errorem corrigimus hunc in modum ex vaticino tùm Esaiæ, tùm reliquorum Prophetarum argumentati.

Quale futurum erat regnum Messiæ: talis à prophetis prædicta est liberatio, & recollectio Judæorum, ex regno hoc Messiæ resultans.

Atqui regnum Messiæ non externum, aut corporale, sed spirituale futurum erat regnum.

Ergò talis quoque per Prophetas prædicta est Judæorum liberatio & recollectio.

Assumptio patebat ex cap. 2. hujus Tractationis de regno Christi. Conclusionis autem veritas per se liquet.

Facta enim, & impleta est hæc ipsa spiritualis populi Judaici liberatio & recollectio, quando per prædicationem, Evangelij Judæorum multa millia ad fidem Christi sunt conversa, & una cum gentibus ad unius regni societatem ex toto terrarum orbe sunt congregati. Qvae spiritualis liberatio sive congregatio dispersorum Israel cepit in festo Pentecostes Novi Testamenti: & postmodum per ministerium Apostolorum continuata fuit: ubi magnam Judæorum multitudinem Christi doctrinam fidemq; amplexam esse, nec ipsi Judæi inficiari possunt. Hæc ipsa collectio etiamnum hodie durat, & durabit ad finem usqve seculi, & qvidem non sine evidenti plurimorum Judæorum conversione. Siqvidem secundum illud Apostoli, Israeli ex parte tantùm obtigit cæcitas, donec plenitudo Gentium intraret: & sic omnis Israel salvus fieret: Rom. 11. v. 25. At qvam collectionem respexit etiam Iohannes, cap. 11. v. 52. scribens, Jesum moriturum fuisse pro gente, & non tantùm pro gente: sed & ut filios DEI, qui erant dispersi, congregaret in unum. Summatim loqvendo, prædicitur hoc loco spiritualis illa consociatio Judæorum & gentium, in toto orbe disfersorum, ad unitatem & societatem Ecclesiæ Novi Testamenti: ita ut Israel & Juda non tam certam qvandam gentem, qvàm professionem, fidemq; Christianam notet. Non enim, qui filii carnis, hi filii DEI: sed qui filii promissionis sunt, æstimantur in semine: In Isaac enim vocabitur tibi semen: Genes. 21. v. 12. Rom. 9. v. 7. & 8.

neficiis esse accipiendam. Nam promittit hoc loco Deus, se Judæos ex Babylone reductos amplioribus beneficiis cumulaturum, qvàm Patres ipsorum affecti fuerint. Iam verò externa & corporalia beneficia si spectes, nunqvam hoc in illis completum fuit. Relinqvitur ergò, ut, si modò divinæ huic promissioni sua constare debeat veritas, de spiritualibus beneficiis, sub regno Messiæ per prædicationem Evangelii, in Judæos collatis, promissio hæc accipiatur. Qvod ipsum ex versu sexto hujus ipsius capitis, qvi spiritualem cordis circumcisionem, qvæ fit per prædicationem Evangelii, & illuminationem Spiritus Sancti, Judæis pollicetur, irrefragabiliter evincitur.

QUARTUM Argumentum ex cap. 6,12. Zachariæ petitum, recentiores Iudæi sic informant: Sic dicit Deus exercituum, dicens: Ecce vir, Germen nomen ejus, & subter eum germinabit, & ædificabit Templum Domini: Et ipse extruet templum Domini, & ipse portabit gloriam, & sedebit, & dominabitur super solio ejus: Et erit Sacerdos super solio ejus: & consilium pacis erit inter ambos ipsos. Atqui isthæc nondum evenerunt: neq; enim tertium templum ædificatum, imò ne quidem ædificari cœptum unquàm fuit.

Ergò Messias nondum in mundum venit.

RESPONDEO I. De Christo sive Messiah loqvi Prophetam ex nostra quoqve parte extra controversiam est. Est enim Messias vir, qvia homo verus natus est: Est verò est & Germen צמח non modò ratione promissionum de veteribus de Messiah factarum: sed &, qvia (ut textus Hebræus habet) subter se, vel de se sub se germinaturus erat Messias, ומתחתיו יצמח quatenus nimirum virtute propriâ, absq; humanis præsidiis homo futurus, suumq; regnum administraturus erat. Et de hoc propriè hoc loco non contravertitur. Illud alterum potiùs sub qvæstionem venit, an seqventia Prophetæ verba evincant, Messiam hunc in Mundum editum, ædificaturum tertium templum hisce in terris? id qvod Iudæi recentiores affirmant? Nos verò negamus: & qvidem ob rationes longè evidentissimas. Nam 1. de tertii alicujus templi, externi nimirùm & terreni ædificatione, per Messiam hoc in mundo adornanda, in universâ Scripturâ Sacrâ, ne unicum qvidem verbulum reperire licet. 2. Ipsorum Iudæorum Rabbini hoc figmentum retundunt, qvando in lib. Neziruth, hoc est, Separationis, cap. Bethsammai super verba, Ieremiæ 7. v. 4. Nolite confidere in verbis mendacii, dicentes, Templum Domini, Templum Domini, Templum Domini: sic commentati sunt: Quid est, quod scriptum est, Templum Domini, Templum Domini? Istud est Sanctuarium primum & secundum.


### On King Christ or Messiah: Just now in (continued)

The THIRD Argument, taken from Deut. 30. v. 3. & seqq., holds thus: It is written and promised by God through Moses, that in the time of the Messiah He wills to bring back the Israelitic people from their captivity, and again to gather them from all the peoples among whom they have been dispersed. But this has not yet happened to the Jews. Therefore.

I respond 1. If the text is weighed more accurately, it has nothing at all concerning the Messiah, or concerning the state of the Jewish people under the kingdom of the Messiah exhibited in the world: but concerning future events, while the Jewish polity still endured. Furthermore, this promise made to the Jews is not absolute, but conditional, if indeed under the yoke of captivity they should perform repentance, and, with idolatrous worship removed, should turn themselves to the true God; just as in the same place God threatens the Jews with dispersion and exile, if, neglecting the true worship of God, they should turn themselves to idols. The fulfillment of both of these prophecies happened in the very act, when first the ten tribes of Israel were led away into Assyria: but a little later the two tribes of Judah were led away into the Babylonian captivity: when likewise these two tribes, having performed serious repentance in Babylon, were brought back into their fatherland: with the remaining ten tribes left in the Assyrian captivity by just judgment on account of their extreme impiety and contumacy. 2. If we should even grant that this promise is to be understood concerning the times of the Messiah, the very evidence of the text nevertheless proves that it is not concerning external or bodily benefits. By those things, therefore, which have been said, it is openly shown that the Temple will not be built a third time: nor can Jewish depravity prove by any evident reason that it must be rebuilt a third time: since there ought to have been no more than two Temples on earth: namely, the first, which was constructed by Solomon and overturned by Nebuchadnezzar; and the second, which was founded under Zerubbabel and finally destroyed by Titus. But the third Temple is to be placed not on earth but in heaven, and in the supernal and heavenly Jerusalem. 3. The words of Zechariah, when weighed more closely concerning some external restoration of either a second or some third Temple, accomplish nothing at all: however much the Prophet may repeat twice that the Messiah is to build a temple. For in the preceding chapter 4, v. 9, the Prophet asserted concerning Zerubbabel that his hands founded that house, and his hands finished it. Therefore, if Zerubbabel put the finishing touch to the second Temple: then certainly the Messiah, who was to sprout forth only after this second temple had been built, could not perform that. Again, because the Prophet immediately adds: He himself shall rule upon his throne, and he shall be a Priest upon his throne: he clearly hints that the form of the Messiah's Temple will be entirely new, in which, namely, he himself is to be both King and Priest at the same time: which is to be understood concerning the spiritual kingdom and temple of the Messiah, as the Prophet David had already predicted long ago, Psalm 110, v. 1 and following. The Lord said to my Lord: Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies your footstool: The Lord shall send forth the scepter of your power from Zion: Rule in the midst of your enemies: The Lord has sworn, and it will not repent him: You are a Priest forever, according to the order of Melchizedek. 4. The words of Zechariah that immediately follow confirm this interpretation of ours: And the counsel of peace shall be between those two: namely, the Priesthood and the Kingdom: As if he were to say: Hitherto the offices of Priest and King have been distinct in both temples: indeed, frequently the most bitter discords and disputes have occurred between these two orders. But in the person of the Messiah they shall be most closely joined, and both his kingdom and his Priesthood shall be directed toward one and the same goal, which is the redemption of the human race and eternal salvation. Which description of the Messiah alone utterly destroys and overturns that Jewish dream concerning the building of some third earthly temple. Concerning which opinion Nicolaus de Lyra writes orthodoxly upon this very passage: Behold the man, the Orient is his name. The Chaldean translation, which is authentic among the Hebrews, has it thus: Behold the man, the Messiah is his name: and thus it is understood literally of Jesus of Nazareth, who is truly the Messiah, predicted in the Law and the Prophets: Who is called the Orient in this place, because according to his Deity he rises eternally from the Father. But the Prophet adds: Under him he shall rise: because he was to be born according to his humanity temporally from a mother.

And he himself shall build the temple of the Lord, that is, the Church from his faithful, as if from living stones. And there shall be a counsel of peace between both of them, that is, between the Jews and the Gentiles; from whom one Church has been made, under one shepherd Jesus Christ. Thus far Lyranus. The ordinary gloss supports this, in these words: Under the Orient Jesus shall rise a multitude of believers, which shall build a Church to God: and he himself, crowned in his individual members, shall bear their glory: and he himself, King and Pontiff, shall sit on a throne both royal and Pontifical: And the counsel of peace shall be between both, because both glories shall consent in the Lord Jesus.

And these indeed are the principal arguments by which the more recent Jews attempt to put some gloss upon their impiety. The rest, which they are accustomed to use in battle, are so diluted and childish that they do not require a lengthy refutation. For the fact that they contend in the fifth place that the Messiah has not yet come because not all Jews have been saved is clearly nonsensical. For although it is written in Jeremiah 23, v. 6: In his (the Messiah's) days Judah shall be saved, and Israel shall dwell with confidence: yet it is nowhere written that all Jews are to be saved. For as the Fathers rightly noted: the word Judah in this place is not gentile: but denotes Confession: so that as many as shall confess the Messiah, that is, shall believe in him with true faith, are also to be saved through him: according to that of Isaiah 45, v. 22. Be converted to me, and all the ends of the earth shall be saved. But concerning the rest, who are not saved, the same Isaiah discourses gravely, chapter 59, v. 1. Behold, he says, the hand of the Lord is not shortened, that it cannot save, nor is his ear heavy, that it cannot hear: But your sins have divided between you and your God: and your iniquities have hidden his face from you, that he might not hear. And in verse 20. The redeemer shall come to Zion, and to those who return from iniquity in Jacob, says the LORD, etc. And this very thing was fulfilled when many thousands of Jews acknowledged Jesus of Nazareth as the true Messiah of the World, and confidently believed in him.

VI. It is of the same futility that they clamor in the sixth place that the Messiah has not yet come, because Gog and Magog have not yet been slain and overturned: understanding by those enemies the Gentiles, under whose power and dominion they have the necessity of living even today. But this is nothing other than an old woman's dream. For that the Messiah is to fight with some external force against Gog and Magog is nowhere predicted in the Prophets.

Isaiah indeed has it, that the Messiah is to kill the impious one with the Spirit of his mouth, chap. 11, 4. But this has nothing to do with Gog or Magog. Rather, this prophecy was abundantly fulfilled when, through the preaching of the Gospel, Antichrist, that son of perdition and the adversary, was revealed and refuted, and is fulfilled today, and will be fulfilled until the coming of the Son of GOD for judgment. Thus, in Ezekiel 38, the victory of the mountains of Israel, that is, of the Church, against Gog and Magog is indeed described. But from this the Jews dream in vain that by those enemies are understood the Roman Emperors, under whose yoke the Jews are as it were held captive: and from whom that fictitious Messiah is to liberate them. For Gog and Magog, together with the remaining peoples who are expressly named by the Prophet, denote in the Prophetic Style all the enemies of the Christian name and religion, such as were the Scythians, Getae, Massagetae, and especially in our time are the Turks and Mahometans: whose power and tyranny, however great it may have been, never prevailed against the mountains of Israel, nor will it ever prevail. Moreover, if we look rather at the etymology of these words, Gog in the Hebrew appellation signifies the same as roof, or hidden: but Magog denotes that which is from the roof, or even uncovered, or open. Proverbs 25, verse 24: It is better to sit in a corner of the Gag, i.e., of the roof, than with a contentious woman, and in a common house. Holding this as a task, those do not err who determine that by these words two different kinds of enemies of the Church are denoted: one of which is open and manifest, as if uncovered: namely, that which rages with open force and cruelty: the other is hidden and covered, which under the guise of brothers and friends lays snares for the Church of GOD and the purer religion. Therefore, whichever interpretation they wish to seize upon, whether historical or etymological, they will obtain nothing at all. For our Messiah, according to the flesh he assumed, sitting at the right hand of GOD the Father, so sends forth the Scepter of his power from Zion, and rules in the midst of his enemies, that neither hidden nor manifest enemies have hitherto prevailed against his Church, nor will they ever prevail.

lamb: the leopard with the kid: the lion with the sheep: the bear with the calf: the lion to eat straw with the ox: and the little ones to be delighted over the hole of the asp, and over the den of the basilisk. Isa. 2. v. 2. 3. & 4. chap. 11. v. 6. & seqq. & chap. 65. v. 25. Mic. 4. v. 1. 2. & 3. But these things have not yet happened, not even in Jesus of Nazareth born into the world. For neither was he born in the end of days: since many centuries have passed since his birth and death: 2. nor under him was the mountain of the house of the Lord raised above the heads of the other mountains: 3. nor did all nations, not the Saracens, not the Tartars, not the Mahometans, flow unto him: 4. nor was it ever heard: Come, let us ascend to the house of the Lord, and to the temple of the GOD of Jacob: but Come, let us ascend to the house of Mary, Peter, Nicholas, Thomas, Anne, of all the Saints: 5. nor finally did such peace and concord ever exist, either among rational or irrational living creatures, as was predicted to be under the Messiah. Therefore the Messiah has not yet been brought into the world, much less can or should Jesus of Nazareth be held for the Messiah.

Latin:

TERTIUM Argumentum petitum ex Deut. 30. v. 3. & seqq. tribus, sic habet: Scriptum & promissum est à Deo per Mosen, quod tempore Messiæ velit reducere populum Israeliticum de capti, vitate suâ, & rursus congregare de cunctis populis, inter quos dispersus sit. Atqui hoc nondum obvenit Judæis. Ergò.

Respondeo 1. Si textus accuratiùs expendatur, nihil qvicqvam ille habet de Messiah, vel de statu populi Judaici, sub regno Messiæ in mundum exhibiti: sed de futuris eventibus, durante adhuc politiâ Judaicâ. Deindè promissio hæc Judæis facta, non absoluta est, sed conditionata, si nimirum sub captivitatis jugo pœnitentiam egerint, & cultu Idololatrico sublato, ad verum Deum se converterint; qvemadmodum etiam ibidem Deus dispersionem, & exilium Judæis comminatur, si neglecto vero Dei cultu, ad Idola se converterint. Utriusq; hujus vaticinii complementum ipso actu evenit,qvando primùm decem tribus Israelis,in Assyriam: paulò pòst verò duæ tribus Judah in Babylonicam captivitatem sunt abductæ: qvando item duæ hæ tribus, actâ in Babylone seriâ pœnitentia, reductæ sunt in patriam: reliqvis decem tribubus in Assyriacâ captivitate propter extremam impietatem & contumaciam justo judicio relictis. 2. Si maximè largiamur, promissionem hanc de temporibus Messiæ esse intelligendam, ipsa tamen textus evidentia evincit, non de externis sive corporalibus bePer ea igitur, qvæ dicta sunt, palàm ostenditur, qvòd Templum non re ædificabi tur tertiò: neqve Iudaica pravitas potest aliqva evidenti ratione probare, illud tertiò reædificandum esse: Cùm non nisi duo in terrâ Templa esse debuerint:Primum scilicet, qvod à Salamone constructum fuit, & à Nebucadnezare subversum: & Secundum, qvod sub Zorobabel conditum est, & à Tito demùm destructum. Tertium autem Templum non in terrâ sed in cælo, atqve in superno cælestiqve Hierusalem ponendum est. 3. Verba Zachariæ pressiùs expensa de externâ aliqvâ vel secundi, vel tertii alicujus Templi restauratione, nihil qvicqvam agunt: qvantumvis Propheta bis repetat, qvòd Messias ædificaturus sit templum. Nam præcedente cap. 4. v. 9. de Zorobabele asseruit Propheta, qvòd manus ipsius fundaverit domum istam, & manus ejus perfecerint eam. Ergò si Zorobabel extremam manum imposuit Templo secundo: utiq; Messias, qvi extructo demùm templo isto secundo, germinaturus erat, istud præstare non potuit. Rursus, qvia statim subjicit Propheta: Ipse dominabitur super solio suo, & erit Sacerdos super solio suo: perspicuè innuit, novam planè futuram formam Templi Messiæ, in qvo videlicet ipse Rex simul & Sacerdos futurus sit: id qvod de spirituali regno & templo Messiæ intelligendum esse, jam olim prædixerat Propheta David, Psalm. 110. v. 1. & seqq. Dixit Dominus Domino meo: Sede à dextris meis, donec ponam inimi cos tuos, scabellum pedum tuorum: Sceptrum virtutis tuæ emittet Dominus è Sion: Dominare in medio inimicorum tuorum: Juravit Dominus, & non pænitebit eum: Tu es Sacerdos in æternum, juxta ordinem Melchisedech. 4. Hanc nostram interpretationem confirmant immediatè subseqventia verba Zachariæ: Et consilium pacis erit inter duo ista: Sacerdotium nimirùm & Regnum: Qvasi dicat: Hactenus in utroq; templo distincta fuerunt Sacerdotis & Regis officia: imò freqventer inter duos hosce ordines discordiæ & lites acerrimæ inciderunt. At in personâ Messiæ arctissimè conjungentur, & ad unum, eundemq; scopum, tàm regnum ipsius, qvàm Sacerdotium dirigentur, qvi est, humani generis redemtio, & salus sempiterna. Qvæ vel una Messiæ descriptio, somnium illud Judaicum, de tertii cujusdam terreni templi ædificatione funditus diruit, & evertit. Qvam in sententiam orthodoxè scribit Nicolaus de lyra, super hunc ipsum locum: Ecce vir, oriens nomen ejus. Translatio Chaldaica apud Hebræos authentica sic habet: Ecce vir, Messias nomen ejus: & sic intelligitur ad literam de Jesu Nazareno, qui est verè Messias, in lege & Prophetis prædictus: Qui dicitur hoc loco Oriens, quia secundum Deitatem æternaliter oritur à patre. Sed addit Propheta: Subter eum orietur: quia erat nasciturus secundum humanitatem temporaliter de matre.

Et ipse ædificabit templum Domini, id est, Ecclesiam de fidelibus suis, tanquã de lapidibus vivis. Et erit consilium pacis inter ambos illos, id est, inter Iudæos & gentiles; ex quibus facta est una Ecclesia, sub uno pastore Jesu Christo. Hactenus Lyranus. Suffragatur glossa ordinaria, his verbis: Sub Oriente Iesu orietur multitudo credentium, quæ ædificabit Ecclesiam Deo: & ipse in singulis membris coronatus, portabit gloriam illorum: & ipse Rex & Pontifex sedebit in throno càm regali, quàm Pontificali: Et consilium pacis erit inter utrumǫ, quia utraǫ gloria consentiet in Domino Iesu.

Et hæc quidem præcipua sunt argumenta, quibus recentiores Judæi impietati suæ fucum aliqvem facere conantur. Reliqva, quibus militare consueverunt, usŕve adcò sunt diluta & puerilia, ut prolixam refutationem non desiderent. Nam quòd qvinto loco contendunt, Messiam nondum venisse, quia non omnes Judæi sint salvati, planè nugatorium est. Etsi enim Jerem. 23. v. 6. scriptum est: In diebus ejus (Messiæ) salvabitur Juda, & Israël habitabit cum fiducia: nuspiam tamen scriptũ est, quòd omnes Judæi sint salvandi. Nam uti rectè annotarunt Patres: Judæ vocabulũ hoc loco non est gentile: sed Confessionem notat: ita, ut qvotqvot confitebuntur Messiam, hoc est, verâ fide in ipsum credent, per ipsum qvoqve salvandi sint: secundum illud Jesai. 45. v. 22. Convertimini ad me, & salvabimini omnes fines terræ. De reliqvis verò, qvi non salvantur, idem Esaias graviter disserit, cap. 59. v. 1. Ecce, inquiens, non est abbreviata manus Domini, ut salvare nequeat, neque aggravata est auris ejus, ut non exaudiat: Sed peccata vestra diviserunt inter vos & Deum vestrum: & iniquitates vestræ absconderunt faciem ejus à vobis, ne exaudiret. Et versu 20. Veniet Sion redemptor, & eis qui redeunt ab iniquitate in Jacob, dicit DOMINUS &c. Et hoc ipsum impletum, qvando multa Judæorum millia, Jesum Nazarenum pro verò Mundi Messia agnoverunt, inq; eum confidenter crediderunt.

VI. Ejusdem futilitatis est, qvod sexto loco clamitant, Messiam nondum venisse, quia Gog & Magog nondum sint interemti & eversi: per hostes illos intelligentes Gentes, sub qvorum potestate, & dominio hodieǫ; vivere necessum habent. Est verò & hoc nihil aliud, qvàm anile somnium. Nam quòd Messias externâ qvâdam vi pugnaturus sit adversus Gog & Magog, nuspiam in Prophetis prædictum.

Esaias qvidem habet, qvòd Messias Spiritu oris sui interfecturus sit impium cap. 11, 4. Atqvi hoc nihil ad Gog vel Magog. Qvin hoc potiùs vaticinium impletum abundè, cùm per prædicationem Evangelii Antichristus filius ille perditionis, & ἀντικείμενος est revelatus & refutatus, hodieq; impletur, & implebitur ad adventum usqve Filii DEI ad judicium. Sic Ezech. 38. describitur qvidem montium Israelis, hoc est, Ecclesiæ victoria contra Gog & Magog. Sed indè frustrà somniant Judæi, per hostes illos intelligi Imperatores Romanos, sub qvorum jugo captivi qvasi teneantur Judæi: & à qvo Messias ille fictitius ipsos sit liberaturus. Nam Gog & Magog unà cum reliqvis populis, qvi apud Prophetam nominatim exprimuntur, notant Stylo Prophetico omnes hostes Christiani nominis ac religionis, qvales fuerunt Scythæ: Getæ, Massagetæ, & comprimis nostro tempore sunt Turcæ: & Mahometistæ: Qvorum vis & tyrannis, qvanta qvanta unqvàm fuerit, nunqvàm tamen adversus montes Israel prævaluit, neqve prævalebit unqvàm. Cæterùm si etymon potiùs istorum vocabulorum spectemus, Gog appellatione Hebræà idem significat, qvod tectum, sive occultum: Magog autem notat id, qvod est de tecto, vel etiam detectum, sive apertum. Proverb. 25. vers. 24. Melius est sedere in angulo גג Gag, i. e. tecti, quàm cum muliere litigiosa, & in domo communi. Hoc pensi habentes, non errant, qvi per ista vocabula, duo diversa hostium Ecclesiæ genera notari statuunt: Qvorum unum apertum est, & manifestum, quasi detectum: illud videlicet, qvod apertà vi, & crudelitate grassatur: Alterum est occultum & tectum, qvod sub fratrum & amicorum schemate, Ecclesiæ DEI, & puriori religioni insidias struit. Qvamcunqve ergo velint interpretationem arripiant, sive historicam, sive Etymologicam, nihil qvicqvam obtinebunt. Messias enim noster, secundum assumtam carnem, sedens ad dextram DEI Patris, ita emittit Sceptrum virtutis suæ è Sion, & dominatur in medio inimicorum suorum, ut neqve occulti neqve manifesti hostes adversus Ecclesiam suam hactenùs prævaluerint, neqve unqvàm sit prævalituri.

agno: pardum cum hædo: leonem cum ove: ursum cum vitulo: Leonem comesturum paleam cum bove: & pusillos delectatum iri super foramine aspidis, & super spelunca basilifci. Jes. 2. v. 2. 3. & 4. cap. 11. v. 6. & seqq. & cap. 65. v. 25. Mich. 4. v. 1. 2. & 3. Atqui hæc nondum evenerunt, ne quidem in mundum nato Jesu Nazareno. Neq; enim ille natus in fine dierum: quin plurima secula ab ipsius nativitate & morte præterfluxerunt: 2. neq; sub ipso mons templi Domini elevatus super capita reliquorum montium: 3. neq; omnes gentes, non Sarraceni, non Tartari, non Mahometistæ ad ipsum confluxerunt: 4. neq; auditum unquàm: Venite, ascendamus ad domum Domini, & ad templum DEI Jacob: sed Venite, ascendamus ad domum Mariæ, Petri, Nicolai, Thomæ, Annæ, omnium Sanctorum: 5. nec deniq; tanta pax & concordia unquàm vel inter rationalia, vel irrationalia animantia extitit, qualis sub Messia futura prædicta fuit. Ergo Messias nondum in mundum est editus, nedum Jesus Nazarenus pro Messia haberi potest aut debet.


### On King Christ or Messiah: Just now in (continued)

Moreover, for refuting this objection, that single Response of the Savior would suffice, Matt. 22. v. 29: You err, not knowing the Scriptures. For, as the Apostle testifies, 2 Cor. 3. v. 14, to this very day a veil is drawn over the eyes of the Jews in the reading of the Old Testament, and placed upon their heart, so that they do not understand it; but clinging to the bark of the letter, they relish and dream of mere external and carnal things, ignorant of the power of the Scripture. Whence it happens that by perpetual sophisms of the figure of speech they deceive themselves and others, while they interpret literally and according to the letter those things which were spoken figuratively, and ought to be understood allegorically or Spiritually.

In the beginning, therefore, that we may answer each point more accurately, by the last days, in which the Messiah was to be born, the Prophets do not understand a few certain years preceding the end of the world: but, with Daniel as interpreter, that fourth and last Monarchy, which will not end except with the end of the world itself. Daniel 2, verse 44.

Then by the Mountain of the house of the Lord, that mountain Moriah is not understood, on which the Jerusalem Temple was built: but the Church of the Messiah is denoted Spiritually, which is and is called a Mountain, partly by reason of the promises made to the Church, which stand firm and immovable like some mountain: partly by reason of the protection which is always prepared for the Church against any enemies whatsoever from the presence of the Messiah. In which sense David also, Psalm 125. v. 1, compares those who trust in the LORD to Mount Zion, which shall not be moved forever. Now indeed, such as is this mountain of the house of the LORD, such also is its elevation or exaltation to be understood: namely, not some bodily one, by which, according to the Jewish dream, the mountain of the Jerusalem temple is to be elevated upwards by three leagues: or by which GOD is to [bring] Mount Tabor and Carmel into some one

Finally, they heap together various prophecies of the Prophets concerning the Messiah, which have not yet, and not even in our Jesus of Nazareth, been fulfilled, in this manner: The Prophets predicted: 1. That the Messiah would be born in the end of days: 2. that upon his being brought into the world, the mountain of the house of GOD would be prepared or elevated at the head of the mountains: 3. that all nations would be gathered unto him: 4. that at the coming of the Messiah the peoples would excite one another and say: Come, let us ascend to the house of the Lord, and to the house of the GOD of Jacob. 5. That there would be such peace in the days of the Messiah that swords would be changed into plowshares, that is, weapons of war would be converted into rustic instruments serving agriculture. Indeed, that the wolf would dwell with the lamb, and that he is about to heap up a place, and to place Jerusalem with the temple upon their summit: as R. Johanan and R. Pinhas have childishly dreamed in their Talmud: but it is clearly spiritual, and indeed a twofold one. One in respect to the citizens of the Church. For the promise, rights, and privileges of the Church will not pertain only to the Jews under the Messiah: but to all nations whatsoever. indeed, by reason of the supreme happiness and prosperity which will flourish in the Church under the kingdom of the Messiah: concerning which below in the fifth and sixth place. Which interpretation is also held by R. Solomon and R. Aven Ezra, as Galatinus testifies, book 4, chapter 3.

Thirdly, the Jews lie splendidly when they deny that all nations have been gathered to Jesus of Nazareth. Certainly, even by this very pact, the mountain of the house of the Lord, that is, the Church of the New Testament, is elevated above all other mountains, because all nations that are under heaven have flowed into it, not even excluding the Saracens or the Tartars. For they were converted to the Church and the faith of the Messiah under the Emperor Valens, at the request of their own queen, or duchess, Mavia, and furthermore at her insistence that a certain presbyter, by the name of Moses, be given as priest and pontiff to the Saracen nation: as can be seen in Theodoret, book 4, chapter 23, and Socrates, book 4, chapter 29, and Nicephorus, book 11, chapter 47. These latter, namely the Tartars, also joined themselves to the faith of Christ: so that in the year of Christ 1299, the Prince of the Tartars, Erkaldus, wrote to the King of France, who was then staying with his army in Cyprus, that not only had he himself embraced the Christian religion many years before, but also the Great Khan, the Prince of the Tartars. Moreover, a witness worthy of faith is William Postel, writing that even today Christians survive in Great Tartary, and indeed more than are found in our Europe. Nor is it an obstacle that very many of these peoples, by their own impregnable stubbornness and ingratitude, have lost this most holy deposit of the Communion of Saints for themselves and their descendants, so that by the just judgment of God they are now clearly exiles from the Church. For this very thing also was predicted by the Prophets.

Fourthly, it is childish that the Jews urge the sound of the words more than the sense. For the Prophet did not wish to note precisely with what words the citizens of the Kingdom of the Messiah would incite one another to perform the worship of God: but rather he expressed their affection, namely that they would gather themselves to the Church with joined zeal and effort, and for that very reason which the Prophet immediately subjoins: That they may learn the ways of the Lord, and walk in his paths: Because, indeed, the Law is to go forth from Sion, and the Word of the Lord from Jerusalem. But that the temples of Christians are designated by the names of various saints: this is not done to designate the worship itself which ought to be exhibited to those saints: which the Church of Christ has always condemned in the Romanists: but it is done for a merely political end, to distinguish the many temples or chapels of one city: meanwhile depending for the worship itself upon the one and only God of Jacob.

Fifthly and lastly, spiritual peace and prosperity are described again in figurative words, by which the most diverse peoples, Gentiles and Jews, are to coalesce into one body in such a way that those who were previously separated by a certain wall, and were no more alienated from one another regarding the worship of God than the wolf from the sheep: the leopard from the kid: the bear from the calf: the lion from the lamb, are now, under the kingdom of the Messiah, that wall being broken down, to be gathered into one assembly and one Church, and to exhibit one worship of God. And just as this peace was nothing but spiritual, so also it had to be asserted and preserved not by external, but by spiritual weapons, namely the preaching of the Gospel and the administration of the Sacraments. And what, I pray, is this blindness, to dream of that peace under the kingdom and that it is perpetual, when nevertheless Daniel asserts something clearly different, chapter 9, verse 26, expressly declaring that in the times of the Messiah, the people with the coming Leader will destroy the city and the Sanctuary: Likewise, a certain blasphemous horn, which, having sprouted between the horns of the fourth beast, or the Roman Monarchy, is to pluck out the three former horns, that is, the three Oriental kingdoms, and open its mouth against God: nay, even to make war against the Saints, and to prevail against them, until the Ancient of days comes, and gives judgment to the Saints: that is, until the very last day. Daniel 7, 9, 21, and 22. Finally, if the Jews wish to interpret these prophetic predictions according to the letter and the proper sound of the words; they should have declared what, then, is to be the sense of those predictions in which it is predicted that, in the time of the Messiah, the mount of Olives is to be divided into four parts, towards the four quarters of the world: rivers are to arise from all the mountains: all the valleys are to be exalted: on the contrary, the mountains and hills are to be cast down: Jerusalem is not to be closed either by day or by night because of the abundance of those arriving: its foundations and gates are to be built from gems; the city itself, however, is to be without walls, because of the multitude of the inhabitants, etc. That the sense of these predictions is not external and bodily, but spiritual, the Jews must needs confess, whether they like it or not: unless they wish to defile the prophetic Scriptures with most inept glosses: nay, even to accuse them of manifest contradictions. For example: Zechariah chapter 2, verse 4, affirms that in the time of the Messiah the city of Jerusalem is to be inhabited without walls: On the contrary, however, David, Psalm 51, 20, asserts that under the kingdom of the Messiah the walls of Jerusalem are to be rebuilt. Thus the prophets predict everywhere that Jerusalem is to be repaired under the kingdom of the Messiah: And yet Daniel, chapter 9, verse 26, announces that in the time of the Messiah Jerusalem is to be so overturned that it is never to be restored again, but that perpetual waste and desolation is to drip upon it.

Thus the same prophets predicted that the Messiah would be the Savior of his people: But now Isaiah affirms that the same Messiah would be a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense to the two houses of Israel, for a snare and for a ruin to the inhabitants of Jerusalem: Isa. 8, 14 and 15. Therefore, if the Jews wish to interpret these oracles according to the letter, there can be no doubt for anyone that they entangle both themselves and the Scripture in manifest snares of contradictions. Therefore, having relegated these Jewish absurdities to hell, it will be safest and in every way consistent with the truth to accommodate these and other such prophetic oracles of Scripture to the analogy of faith, and to interpret them according to the nature and quality of the Kingdom of Christ, concerning which we shall treat expressly in the second chapter of this treatise.

both from the various Hebrew appellations by which the future Messiah of the World is indicated in Moses and the Prophets, and which evidently argue for his divine nature: concerning which P. Galatinus discourses learnedly in book 3 of his work on the mysteries of the Catholic truth, from chapter 1 to 18, indeed throughout that entire book: but also from the clear prophecies of the prophets, such as these following.

I. 1 Chron. 17:17. וּרְאִיתַנִי כְּתוֹר הָאָדָם הַמַּעֲלָה יְהוָה אֱלֹהִים that is: You look, or have looked upon me according to the form of the man who is the Lord God in the heights. Which words in the Vulgate Latin are rendered less conveniently thus: And you have made me visible above all men, O Lord GOD. For David does not speak of himself in this place, and he did not wish to express how much excellence and dignity had been conferred upon him by GOD: But as the words immediately preceding prove, he weighs more deeply the promise of the Messiah, who is to be born one day from his loins, saying: This was a small thing in your sight (namely, that you have established me as king of your people, and have granted me a son who is to build a house for God) but you have spoken concerning the house of your servant for the future, and you have looked upon me, as it were the figure of the man (namely, that man) who is the Lord God in the heavens. Which if he says: I understand well that these things do not apply to me, but to the Messiah of the World, who will indeed be born a man from my loins, but such a man who is the Lord God in the heavens, and thus in one person will be the future true man. Nor can these words of David, or the preceding divine Promise, v. 11 and following, be understood in any way concerning Solomon, the son of David. For what God says to David: When you have completed your days, that you may go to your Fathers; that is, when you have died, I will raise up your seed after you: that certainly cannot be accommodated to Solomon, since he was created King while David his father was still living. But if God had wished this to be understood concerning Solomon, he would certainly not have said in the following: I will raise up your seed after you: and that will be of your sons: But he would have said: I have already raised up for you a seed, which is from you. Thus what follows in v. 14. And I will establish him in my house, and in my kingdom forever: And his throne shall be most firm for eternity: do not fit Solomon: For Solomon was not established in GOD's house or kingdom forever, or for a long time, nor was his throne most firm. Therefore, since God speaks to David concerning a kingdom that will last forever, and David himself accepted these things only concerning the Messiah, it is concluded ἐξ ἀνάγκης (by necessity) that the Messiah promised to David in this place would be also the true GOD, since to him alone the eternity of the Kingdom belongs: and not merely a naked man.

Latin:

Cæterùm objectioni huic refutandæ unica illa Responsio Servatoris sufficeret, Matth. 22. v. 29. Erratis, nescientes Scripturas. Est enim Apostolo teste, 2. Cor. 3. v. 14. in hodiernum usque diem velamen, in lectione Veteris Testamenti, Judæorum oculis obductum, & positum super cor eorum, ut illud non intelligant; sed in cortice literæ inhærentes, mera externa & carnalia sapiant, & somnient, virtutem Scripturæ ignorantes. Undè fit, ut perpetuis Sophismatis figuræ dictionis seipsos, & alios decipiant, dum quæ figuratè dicta sunt, & allegoricè sive Spiritualiter intelligi debent, ipsi propriè & secundum literam interpretantur.

Initiò igitur, ut ad singula accuratiùs respondeamus, per dies novissimos, quibus nasci debuit Messias, non intelligunt Prophetæ paucos quosdam annos, finem mundi præcessuros: sed interprete Daniele, quartam illam, & ultimam Monarchiam, quæ non nisi cum ipso mundi fine definet. Daniel. 2. vers. 44.

Deinde per Montem domus Domini, non intelligitur mons ille Morijah, in quo Templum Hierosolymitanum fuit extructum: sed notatur Spiritualiter Ecclesia Messiæ, quæ est ac dicitur Mons, partim ratione promissionum Ecclesiæ factarum, quæ instar montis alicujus stant firmæ ac immotæ: partim ratione præsidii, quod Ecclesiæ adversus quosvis hostes, ex Messiæ præsentia semper est paratum. Qvo sensu David quoque Psalm. 125. v. 1. illos, qui confidunt in DoMINO, comparat monti Sion, qui in æternum non commoveatur. Jam verò qualis est mons iste domus DOMINI: talis etiam ejus elevatio sive exaltatio est intelligenda: nimirùm non corporalis aliqua, quâ secundum somnium Judaicum, mons templi Hierosolymitani, tribus leucis, sursum sit elevandus: vel quâ DEUS montem Thabor & Carmelum in unum aliqvem

Tandem coacervant varia Prophetarum vaticinia de Messiâ, qvæ nondum, & ne qvidem in nostro Iesu Nazareno sint completa, hunc in modum: Prædixerunt Prophetæ. 1. Messiam nasciturum in fine dierum: 2. ipso in mundum edito, paratum sive elevatum iri montem domus DEI, in capite montium: 3. ad ipsum congregatum iri omnes gentes: 4. in adventu Messiæ populos se invicem excitatuoos, & dicturos: Venite, ascendamus ad domum Domini, & ad domum DEI Jacob. 5. tantam fore pacem in diebus Messiæ, ut enses commutandi sint in ligones, hoc est, arma bellica convertenda in instrumenta rustica, & agriculturæ inservientia. Imò lupum habitaturum cum locum sit congesturus, & super verticem ipsorum positurus Hierosolymam cum templo: uti pueriliter in suo Thalmud fabulati sunt, R. Iohannan & R. Pinhas: sed Spiritualis planè, & ea quidem gemina. Una respectu civium Ecclesiae. Neq; enim sub Messia ad Iudaeos duntaxat: sed ad omnes omninò gentes, pertinebunt Ecclesiae promissio, jura & privilegia. Deinde verò ratione felicitatis & prosperitatis summae, quae sub regno Messiae florebit in Ecclesia:de qua infra loco qvin. to & sexto. Qvam interpretationem tenent etiam R. Salomon, & R. Aven Ezra, teste Galat. l. 4. c. 3.

Tertiò splendidè mentiuntur Iudaei, qvando negant, omnes gentes congregatos esse ad Jesum Nazarenum. Certè vel hoc etiam pacto, mons domus Domini, hoc est, Ecclesia Novi Testamenti, super omnes alios montes est elevata, qvia ad eam confluxerunt omnes gentes, quae sub coelo sunt, ne quidem Saracenis, aut Tartaris exclusis. Illi enim ad Ecclesiam & fidem Messiae nostrae conversi fuerunt, sub Imp. Valente, petente hoc ipsorum regina, sive ducissa Mavia, & insuper flagitante, ut qvidam presbyter, cognomento Moyses, genti Sarracenae Sacerdos & Pontifex daretur: uti videre est apud Theodoretum lib. 4. cap. 23. & Socratem lib. 4. cap. 29. & Nicephorum lib. 11. cap. 47. Hi verò, Tartari nimirùm, ad fidem Christi se qvoqve adsociarunt: ita, ut anno Christi 1299. Princeps Tartarorum Erkaldus, ad Regem Gallię, tùm cum exercitu in Cypro subsistentem scripserit, non modò se ante annos permultos: sed etiam Chamum Magnum Tartarorum Principem, Christianam Religionem amplexum esse. Qvin testis fide dignus est, Gulielmus Postellus, scribens, hodieq; in Tartaria magna superesse Christianos, & quidem plures, quàm in Europa nostra reperiantur. Neqve obstat, quòd populorum istorum plurimi inexpugnabili sua contumacia, & ingratitudine, Sacrosanctum hoc depositum Communionis Sanctorum sibi & posteris perdiderunt, ita, ut justo DEI judicio jam ab Ecclesia sint planè extorres. Nam hoc ipsum qvoqve per Prophetas fuit praedictum.

Quartò puerile est, qvod Judaei verborum magis sonum, quam sensum urgent. Neqve enim Propheta praecisè notare voluit, qvibus verbis Cives Regni Messiae, seipsos ad cultum DEI obeundum, invicem essent excitaturi: sed affectum potiùs ipsorum expressit, quòd nimirùm conjuncto studio & opera sint se aggregaturi Ecclesiae, & eam quidem ob causam, quam immediatè subjicit Propheta: Ut discant vias Domini, & ambulent in semitis ejus: Quia nimirùm de Sion proditura sit Lex, & Verbum Domini de Jerusalem. Quòd verò Templa Christianorum à diversis Sanctorum nominibus indigitantur: non fit ad designandum ipsum cultum, qvi Sanctis illis exhiberi debeat: id qvod in Romanensibus Christi Ecclesia semper damnavit: sed fit ob finem merè politicum, ad distinguenda plura unius urbis templa sive sacella: cultum interim ipsum soli atque uni DEO Jacob dependentes.

Qvintò & postremò, verbis rursum figuratis describitur Spiritualis pax & prosperitas, quâ diversissimi populi, Gentes & Judæi ita in unum corpus sit coalituri, ut qui prius per parietem quendam inter gerinum erant distincti, & ab invicem haud magis, quoad cultum DEI, alienati, atque lupus ab ove: pardus ab hædo: ursus à vitulo: leo ab agno, jam sub regno Messiæ, disrupto illo pariete, in unum cœtum, unamque Ecclesiam sint congregandi, unamque DEI cultum exhibituri. Et quemadmodum pax hæc non nisi Spiritualis erat, ita etiam non externis, sed spiritualibus armis asseri & conservari debuit, nempè prædicatione Evangelii, & administratione Sacramentorum. Et quæ obsecro hæc cæcitas est, somniare sub regno eamque perpetuam pacem, cùm tamen diversum planè asserat Daniel, cap. 9. v. 26. disertè edicens, temporibus Messiæ, populum cum Duce venturo, dissipaturum esse civitatem, & Sanctuarium: Item, Cornu quoddam blasphemum, quod inter cornua quartæ bestiæ, sive Monarchiæ Romanæ enatum, sit tria anteriora cornua evulsura, hoc est, tria regna Orientalia, & os suum aperturum in Deum: imò facturum bellum adversus Sanctos, & prævaliturum contra eos, donec veniat antiquus dierum, & judicium det Sanctis: hoc est, ad diem usque novissimum. Daniel. 7, 9, 21. & 22. Tandem, si secundum literam, & proprium verborum sonum, vaticinia isthæc Prophetica interpretari velint Judæi; edisserant, ecquis ergo illorum vaticiniorum futurus sit sensus, in quibus prædicitur, Tempore Messiæ, montem Oliveti divisum iri in quatuor partes, versus quatuor mundi plagas: flumina exoritura de cunctis montibus: omnes valles exaltatum iri: montes contrà & & colles dejectum: Hierosolymam præ adventantium copiâ neque die, neque noctu claudendam: fundamenta & portas ejus ex gemmis construendas; ipsam vero sine muris futuram, præ inhabitantium multitudine &c. Horum vaticiniorum sensum, non externum & corporalem, sed spiritualem esse, nolint velint fateantur Judæi, necesse est: nisi Scripturas Propheticas ineptissimis glossis conspurcare: imò easdem manifestarum contradictionum insimulare velint. Ut Exempli gratia: Zacharias cap. 2. v. 4. affirmat, Tempore Messiæ urbem Hierosolymam sine muris inhabitandam: Contrà verô David Psalm. 51, 20. asserit, sub regno Messiæ muros Hierusalem reædificatum iri. Sic passim prædicunt Prophetæ, sub Messiæ regno reparandam esse Hierosolymam: Atqui Daniel cap. 9. v. 26. tempore Messiæ Hierosolymam sic eversum iri prænunciat, ut nunquam ampliùs sit restauranda, sed stillatura super eam perpetua vastitas & desolatio.

Sic iidem prophetæ prædixerunt, Messiam fore Salvatorem sui populi: Jam verò Jesaias affirmat, eundem Messiam fore lapidem offensionis, & petram scandali duabus domibus Israel in laqueum, & in ruinam habitantibus in Hierusalem: Jes. 8, 14. & 15. Ergò si secundum literam oracula isthæc interpretari velint Judæi, quin manifestis Contradictionum laqueis & seipsos, & Scripturam implicent, nemini potest esse dubium. Proindè ineptiis hisce Judaicis ad orcum relegatis, tùm hæc, tùm id genus alia Scripturæ Propheticæ oracula, ad analogiam fidei accommodare, & secundú naturam, & qualitatem Regni Christi, de qua capite secundo hujus tractatus ex professo agemus, interpretari, tutissimum, ac veritati per omnia consentaneum fuerit.

tùm ex variis appellationibus Hebræis, quibus futurus Mundi Messias in Mose, & Prophetis indigitatur, quæqve divinam ipsius naturam evidenter arguunt: de quibus eruditè differit P. Galatinus, lib. 3. de arcanis Catholicæ veritatis: à capite 1. ad 18. usque, imò per integrum istum librum: sed & ex perspicuis Prophetarum vaticiniis, qualia sunt hæc sequentia.

I. 1. Paralip. 17. v. 17. וּרְאִיתַנִי כְּתוֹר הָאָדָם הַמַּעֲלָה יְהוָה אֱלֹהִים hoc est; Aspicis, vel aspexisti me secundum formam hominis, qui in excelsis est Dominus Deus. Quæ verba in vulgatâ Latinâ, sed minus commodè sic sunt reddita: Et fecisti me spectabilem super omnes homines, Domine DEUS. Nam David hoc loco non de se loquitur, & quantum præstantiæ atque dignitatis in se à DEO collatum sit, exprimere voluit: Sed uti verba immediatè præcedentia evincunt, promissionem Messiæ, ex lumbis suis aliquando nascitur, altiùs expendit, dicens: Hoc parum visum est in conspectu tuo (quòd nimirùm me regem constituisii populi tui, & filium mihi largitus es, qui domum sit ædificaturus Deo) sed locutus es super domum servi tui in futurum, & respexisti me, quasi figuram hominis (scilicet illius hominis) qui est in supernis Dominus Deus. Quas si dicat: Probe intelligo, in me ista non competere, sed in Mundi Messiam, qui ex meis quidem lumbis homo nascetur, sed talis homo, qui in supernis est Dominus Deus, & sic in unâ personâ futurus verus homo. Neque vel isthæc verba Davidis, vel præcedens Promissio divina, vers. 11. & seqq. de Salomone, Davidis filio, ullo pacto possunt intelligi. Quòd enim dicit Deus ad Davidem; Cùm compleveris dies tuos, ut vadas ad Patres tuos; hoc est, cùm mortuus fueris, suscitabo semen tuum post te: illud certè ad Salomonem accommodari non potest: quippè qui, Davide Patre adhuc vivente, Rex creatus fuit. Quod si de Salomone hoc intelligi voluisset Deus, utique non dixisset in sequentibus: Suscitabo semen tuum post te: & illud erit de filiis tuis: Sed dixisset: Suscitavi jam tibi semen, quod est de te. Sic quæ sequuntur v. 14. Et statuam eum in domo mea, & in regno meo usq; in æternum: Et thronus ejus firmissimus erit in sempiternum: ad Salomonem non quadrant: Nam Salomo neque in DEI domo sive regno constitutus est in sempiternum, vel longo tempore, neq; thronus ejus fuit firmissimus. Proinde cùm de regno æternùm duraturo loquatur Deus ad Davidem, David verò ipse non nisi de Messiâ hæc acceperit, ἐξ ἀνάγκης concluditur, Messiam Davidi hoc loco promissum fore DEUM etiam verum, quippe cui soli Regni æternitas competit: non verò nudum tantùm hominem.


### On King Christ or Messiah: Question II. Whether Jesus of Nazareth, son of Mary, is that very promised Messiah of the world?

IF those individual and universal proofs of the true Messiah of the World, defined long ago by the prophets in the Sacred Scriptures, apply to no one except the one and only Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Mary: and in him alone all things have been completed: then it is concluded by infallible necessity that this one and only Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Mary, is also that true promised Messiah of the World, and that no other is to be expected. But that former point can be obtained by invincible demonstrations. Therefore, that latter point will also be established. The connection of the major premise needs no proof. For it is placed beyond all risk of doubt that to whomever the definition applies, the defined also applies to the same. The assumption therefore contains the point to be judged, which is: Whether in Jesus of Nazareth alone, the son of Mary, the individual and universal proofs of the promised Messiah, defined in the Scriptures of the Old Testament, have been so completed that they could never have applied to any other individual, nor can they today: which we shall demonstrate by parts, and in order, according to the individual proofs.

THE FIRST promised Messiah of the World, therefore, not only that he should be born a mere man in time, but that he should have been the true God from eternity, the ancient Rabbis of the Jews also knew and perceived from the Scripture of the Old Testament. Certainly Caiaphas, the High Priest of the Jews, Matt. 26, v. 63, adjuring Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Mary, whether he himself is the Christ, or that Messiah the Son of God? εἰ σὺ εἶ ὁ χριστὸς ὁ ὑιὸς τῇ θεᾶ; shows not obscurely that he expects such a Messiah or Christ, who is to be at the same time the son of God: which the doubling of the prepositive article clearly proves.

But the Jews learned that, not

II. Isaiah 7, v. 14. Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and shall bring forth a son, and shall call (the mother herself, or the virgin) his name Immanuel, that is, GOD with us. Which appellation of Immanuel clearly proves, against the more recent Jews, the union of two natures in the person of the Messiah: of which one is divine, by reason of which He ought to be named אל, that is, GOD: but the other is human, in respect of which He is to be called עמנו, that is, With us.

Furthermore, the promised Messiah of the world is expressly named in Isaiah 9:6 אל גבור, Mighty God: likewise אבי־עד, Everlasting Father.

To this also pertains the fact that Jeremiah affirms that the name of the coming Messiah, by which they shall call Him, shall be יְהוָה צִדְקֵנוּ, THE LORD our Righteousness, Jerem. 23, v. 6. Thus, from that solemn promise of the Messiah made to David, God Himself testifies that He will be a Father to the Messiah, and He Himself shall be a son to Him: 2 Sam. 7, v. 14. That David understood this not of adoptive, but of that eternal and essential filiation, is clear from Psalm 45, v. 7 & 8, where, describing the kingdom of the Messiah, He addresses Him in these words: Thy throne, O GOD, is for ever and ever: the sceptre of thy kingdom is a right sceptre: thou hast loved righteousness, and hated iniquity: therefore God, thy God, hath anointed thee with the oil of gladness above thy fellows. Where the Messiah is twice expressly named GOD.

What of the fact that the Messiah Himself, speaking of Himself in Psalm 2, v. 6 & 7, again in express words names GOD, and indeed not by adoption, but by eternal generation: saying, I have been constituted King by Him, upon Sion His holy mountain, preaching His decree: The Lord said unto me: Thou art my Son: I have THIS DAY BEGOTTEN THEE. Which words the following arguments prove can be understood of no mortal: 1. because no man has been made the Son of GOD by the Father through eternal generation. 2. because it applies to no man, what GOD the Father says here to this Son of His: Ask of me, and I shall give thee the nations for thine inheritance, and the uttermost parts of the earth for thy possession. Which cannot be applied to David, since the extent of his kingdom was enclosed by the narrow borders of Palestine. 3. Neither do these things befit any mortal: Kiss the Son, lest He be angry, and ye perish from the way, when His wrath is kindled but a little: Blessed are all they THAT PUT THEIR TRUST IN HIM. These certainly cannot be understood of any man, whether David, or Solomon, or anyone else: as of those concerning whom GOD Himself rather pronounces through the Prophet: Cursed is he that trusteth in man, and maketh flesh his arm. Jerem. 17.

To this also pertain those attributes which are predicted in the Prophetic Scriptures concerning the Messiah: such as that His goings forth are said to be from the days of eternity: Micah 5, v. 2. that He sits at the right hand of GOD: Psalm 110, v. 1. that He has received eternal power over all tribes, languages, and peoples. Daniel 7, v. 14. that He is constituted Lord over all the works of the hands of GOD: Psalm 8, v. 7. Which, and others of this kind, can never fall to a naked and simple man. This proof of ours, P. Galatinus, lib. 7, cap. 19, wished to encompass with this argument: Whatever is moved, necessarily has a mover and governor: but the heavens are moved: therefore they have a mover and governor: Thus, from the humanity of the Messiah, because of His divine operations, it is shown that His subject is GOD, the creator and governor of the whole world. For just as the heavens show the glory of their mover, and the moderation of this lower world, by means of the influence of His grace: So the humanity of the Messiah shows the magnificence and the lordship of the inventor and mover of this World, by means of the influence of Salvation, which GOD pours into His humanity.

Finally, there is added to this the fact that the offices of the Messiah could not be performed by a naked man: such as were: to bruise the head of the serpent, Gen. 3, v. 15. to bring a blessing to all nations, Gen. 12, v. 3. to bear the sins of His people and to justify many by the knowledge of Himself, Isaiah 53, v. 11. to tread the winepress of the wrath of GOD, Isaiah 63, v. 3. to bring forth the prisoners out of the pit wherein is no water, in the blood of His covenant, Zech. 9, v. 11. to acquire everlasting righteousness, transgressions having been taken out of the way, Daniel 9, v. 24. and very many others of this kind, which were impossible for a naked and simple man to perform.

And this indeed is the first criterion of the promised Messiah, that He must necessarily have been not a pure, mere, and simple man: but true GOD and man in one person.

Now, it remains to make the application to Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Mary. Although, indeed, in this part we are compelled to use the proofs of the New Testament: and the Jews stubbornly despise and reject them: yet nothing of the solidity of our proof departs from it. For, in the first place, most of those things which we bring forward concerning Jesus of Nazareth from the New Testament, not even the Jews themselves can deny, even if they very much wanted to. Secondly, as long as the Jews can show no one else in whom the individual and universal criteria of the Messiah have been truly fulfilled: and now, indeed, beyond all hazard of doubt, even with the Jews themselves admitting it, it is established that the time destined for the advent of the Messiah has passed by more than fifteen centuries: for so long our demonstration concerning Jesus of Nazareth, however much (in respect of the application) it is sought from the New Testament, will stand firm and immovable.

In the beginning, therefore, regarding the first criterion of the Messiah, that He was to be GOD Himself, it is evident from Jer. ch. 23, v. 5 and ch. 33, v. 16, where He is called Jehovah. Now, indeed, that JESUS of Nazareth is not a naked man, but also true GOD in one person, very many of the Jews, moved by the evidence of the miracles performed by Him, have been compelled to admit: so that from the Pharisees

Having left the school, Nicodemus published this Confession concerning Christ, both in his own name and in the name of his Colleagues: WE KNOW that you have come from God, and no one can do these signs that you do, unless God were with him, John 3, v. 2. Indeed, even the most perverse of the Jews, seeing those stupendous miracles and portents which occurred at the death of Christ, compelled by the force of truth, exclaimed: Truly this was the Son of GOD. Matt. 27, v. 54. Those testimonies of Scripture and arguments drawn from the analogy of faith, by which we asserted the eternal Divinity of Christ in the Article concerning the Person of Christ against the Jews and any heretics, now pertain to this matter: which can be sought from there.

THE OTHER criterion is that the promised Messiah of the World had to be born not in a common and natural way, but in a way that is clearly singular and admirable, namely from the Virgin Mary, by the overshadowing of the Most High and the power of the Holy Spirit, without male seed. For thus Isaiah ch. 7, v. 14: Behold, a Virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel. The more illustrious this prophecy is, the greater the effort with which the more recent Jews attempt to obscure and pervert it. There are some among them who contend that nothing at all concerning the birth of the Messiah is being dealt with in this passage, but that only the son Hezekiah is being promised to King Ahaz, who, because of his singular piety and zeal, ought to be called Immanuel. But this gloss is manifestly repugnant to the text. For the Prophet Isaiah prophesies in this place about such a thing as ought to be a Sign to King Ahaz of most certain liberation from enemies: therefore he says to him: Ask for yourself a sign from the Lord your GOD, either in the deep or in the height: When Ahaz did not want to ask, Isaiah infers: For this reason the Lord himself will give you a Sign: Behold, a virgin shall conceive. Now the birth of the son of Hezekiah could not be in the place of a sign, since he was conceived and born according to the customary order of nature, with the intervention of the commingling of male and female. Furthermore, as Galatinus also notes from R. Solomon, If you count the years of Hezekiah, you will find that he was born nine years before the reign of his father Ahaz. For Ahaz the father reigned for sixteen years, 2 Kings 16, v. 2. To whom succeeded in the kingdom his son Hezekiah, when he was in his twenty-fifth year of age, 2 Kings 18, v. 2. Therefore, when his father Ahaz had begun to reign, Hezekiah was already a boy of nine years: and consequently this prophecy, issued to King Ahaz in the fourth year of his reign, can in no way be understood or ought to be understood as referring to the son of Hezekiah, as he was already a youth of thirteen years.

Latin:

SI singula & universa illa veri Mundi Messiæ τεκμήρια, jam olim in scripturis Sacris prophetas definita, nemini, præter solum atque unum Jesum Nazarenum Mariæ filium competunt: inqve eo solo completa sunt universa: utique infallibili necessitate concluditur, solum etiam istum, atque unum Jesum Nazarenum, Mariæ filium, esse verum illum promissum Mundi Messiam, neque ullum expectandum alium. Atqui prius illud invictis demonstrationibus obtineri potest. Ratum ergo erit & illud posterius. Connexum Majoris probatione nulla indiget. Nam extra omnem dubitationis aleam est positum, quòd cuicunque convenit definitio, eidem conveniat & definitum. Assumtio ergò continet τὸ κρινόμενον, quod est: An in solo Jesu Nazareno, Mariæ filio, ita completa sint singula & universa promissi Messiæ τεκμήρια, in Scripturis Veteris Testameti definita, ut nulli alii individuo ea unquam competere potuerint, neq; hodiè possint: id quod nos per partes, & ordine, secundum singula τεκμήρια demonstrabimus.

PRIMUM igitur promissum Mundi Messiam, non nudum duntaxat hominem in tempore nasci, sed & verum Deum ab æterno esse debuisse, veteres quoque Judæorum Rabini, ex Scripturâ Veteris Testamenti, cognitum, perspectumq; habuerunt. Certè Cajaphas Pontifex Judæorum Maximus, Matth. 26. v. 63. adjurans Jesum Nazarenum, Mariæ Filium, an ipse Christus, sive Messias ille Filius Dei? εἰ σὺ εἶ ὁ χριστὸς ὁ ὑιὸς τῇ θεᾶ; haud obscurè ostendit, se talem expectare Messiam sive Christum, qui simul futurus sit filius Dei: id quod Articuli præpositivi geminatio luculenter evincit.

Didicerunt autem istud Judæi, non tan-

II. Jesai. 7. v. 14. Ecce virgo concipiet, & pariet filium, & vocabit (ipsa mater, sive virgo) nomen ejus Emanuel, hoc est, DEUS nobiscum. Quae Emanuelis appellatio duarum in persona Messiae naturarum Unionem, contra recentiores Judaeos luculenter evincit: quarum una sit divina, ratione cujus אל, hoc est, DEUS nominari debeat: altera vero humana, respectu cujus עמנו h. e. Nobiscum, vocandus sit.

Porro Promissus Mundi Messias, Jesa. 9, 6. diserte nominatur אל גבור Deus fortis: Item אבי־עד Pater aternitatis.

Huc pertinet etiam, quod Jeremias Messiae venturi nomen, quo ipsum sint vocaturi, affirmat fore יְהוָה צִדְקֵנוּ DEUS Justitia nostra, Jerem. 23. v. 6. Sic a solenni illa promifsione Messiae, Davidi facta, Deus ipse testatur, se Messiae fore in Patrem: & ipsum sibi fore in filium: 2. Sam. 7. v. 14. Quod non de adoptiva, sed aeterna illa & Essentiali filiatione Davidem intellexisse, patet ex Psal. 45. v. 7. & 8. ubi Messiae Regnum describens; his ipsum verbis alloquitur: Sedes tua, DEUS, in seculum seculi: virga rectitudinis, virga regni tui: dilexisti justitiam, & odisti iniquitatem: propterea unxit te, Deus, Deus tuus oleo laetitiae prae consortibus tuis. Ubi bis Messias expresse DEUS nominatur.

Quid quod Messias ipse de se verba faciens, Psalm. 2. v. 6. & 7. rursus expressis verbis DEUM nominat, & quidem non per adoptionem, sed per aeternam generationem: Ego, inquiens, constitutus sum Rex ab eo, super Sion montem sanctum ejus, praedicans praeceptum ejus: Dominus dixit ad me: Filius meus es tu: Ego HODIE GENUITE. Quae verba de nemine mortalium intelligi posse: sequentia evincunt argumenta: 1. quia nullus hominum a DEO Patre per Generationem aeternam Filius DEI factus est. 2. quia nulli hominum competit, quod DEUS pater hoc loco ad hunc filium suum: Postula a me, & dabo tibi gentes haereditatem tuam, & possessionem tuam terminos terrae. Quae Davidi accommodari non possunt, quippe cujus regni amplitudo angustis Palaestinae terminis claudebatur. 3. Nulli mortalium conveniunt etiam isthaec: Osculamini filium, ne forte irascatur, & pereatis in via, cum exarserit vel paululum furor ejus: Beati omnes QUI SPERANT IN EO. Haec certe de ullo homine, sive Davide, sive Salomone, sive quocunque alio intelligi non possunt: ut de quibus potius DEUS ipse per Prophetam pronunciat: Maledictus qui confidit in homine, & ponit Carnem brachium suum. Jerem. 17.

Pertinent huc ea etiam attributa, quae in Scripturis Propheticis de Messia praedicantur: ut quod egressus ejus dicitur esse a diebus aeternitatis: Mich. 5 v. 2. quod ad dexteram DEI sedeat: Psalm. 110. v. 1. quod potestatem aeternam super omnes tribus, linguas & populos acceperit. Daniel. 7. v. 14. quod sit constitutus Dominus super omnia opera manuum DEI: Psal. 8. v. 7. Quae & id genus alia in nudum ac simplicem hominem cadere nunquam possunt. Quam probationem nostram P. Galatinus, lib. 7. cap. 19. hoc argumento complecti voluit: Quodcunq́; movetur, necessario motorem habet atque gubernatorem: Cœli autem moventur: Motorem igitur habent, atque gubernatorem: Ita ex Messiæ humanitate, propter ejus divinas operationes ostenditur, suppositum ipsius esse DEUM, universi orbis conditorem & gubernatorem. Sicut enim cœli ostendunt motoris sui gloriam, & hujus orbis inferioris moderationem, mediante sua gratiæ influentiâ: Ita Messiæ humanitatis ostendit magnificentiam, & dominum inventoris & motoris hujus Mundi, Mediante Salvationis influentiâ, quàm Humanitati DEUS influit.

Tandem huc accedit & illud, quòd Messiæ officia non à nudo homine expediri poterant: qualia erant: calcare caput serpentitis, Genes. 3. v. 15. afferre benedictionem omnibus gentibus, Genes. 12. v. 3 peccata populi sui portare & notitiâ sui justificare multos. Jesai. 53. vers. 11. calcare torcular iræ DEI Jesai. 36. v. 3. in sanguine Testamenti sui educere vinctos è foveâ, in quâ non est aqua, Zach. 9. v. 11. transgresfionibus è medio sublatis sempiternam acquirere justitiam. Daniel. 9 v. 24. & id genus alia quàm plurima, quæ nudo ac simplici homini præstitu erant impossibilia.

Et hoc quidem primum est κριτήριον promissi Messiæ, quòd nimirùm non purus merus, ac simplex homo: sed verus DEUS & homo in unâ personâ esse debuerit.

Jam ut ad Jesum Nazarenum, Mariæ filium, fiat applicatio, reliquum est. Quanquam verò hac in parte, Novi Testamenti probationibus uti cogimur: eas verò Judæi præfractè contemnunt, ac rejiciunt: nihil tamen quicqvam probationis nostræ soliditati indè decedit. Nam intitiò pleraque illa, quæ de Jesu Nazareno ex Novo Testamento proferimus, ne ipsi quidem Judæi negare possunt, si maximè velint. Deindè, quamdiu Judæi nullum alium monstrare possunt, in quo Messiæ κριτήρια singula & universa verè sint impleta: Jam verò extra omnem dubitationis aleam, ipsis quoque Judæis fatentibus, sit positum, Tempus adventus Messiæ destinatum, ante quindecim ampliùs secula præterfluxisse: tamdiu Demonstratio nostra de Jesu Nazareno, quantumvis (respectu ἀποδόσεως siye applicationis) ex Novo Testamento petita, stabit firma & immota.

Initiò igitur, quoad primum Messiæ κριτήριον, DEUM ipsum futurum fuisse, constat ex cap. Jer. 23. v. 5. & cap. 33. v. 16. ubi Jehovah vocatur. Jam verò JESUM Nazarenum non nudum esse hominem, sed & verum DEUM in unâ personâ, Judæorum plurimi, moti miraculorum ab ipso editorum evidentiâ fateri necessum habuerunt: ita ut ex Pharisæoru

Scholâ Nicodemus egressus, hanc & suo, & Collegarum nomine, Confessionem de Christo ediderit : SCIMUS, quod à Deo venisti, & nemo potest hæc signa facere, quæ tu facis, nisi fuerit Deus cum eo, Johan. 3. v. 2. Imò Judæorum etiam perversissimi, videntes stupenda illa miracula & ostenta, quæ in morte Christi evenerunt, vi veritatis adacti, exclamârunt: Verè hic Filius DEI fuit. Matth. 27. v. 54. Pertinent jam huc ea & Scripturæ testimonia, & ex analogiâ fidei petita argumenta, quibus æternam Divinitatem Christi, in Articulo de Persona Christi, contra Judæos & hæreticos quosvis asseruimus: quæ indè peti possunt.

ALTERUM κριτήριον est, quòd promissus Mundi Messias, non communi & naturali, sed singulari planè & admirando modo, nempè ex Mariâ Virgine, ex obumbratione altissimi, & virtute Spiritus Sancti, sine virili semine nasci debuit. Sic enim Esaias cap. 7. v. 14. Ecce Virgo concipiet, & pariet filium, & vocabit nomen ejus Emmanuel. Quod vaticinium quò illustrius est, eò majore conatu illud obscurare, & pervertere conantur recentiores Judæi. Sunt ex illis qui nihil quicquam de Messiæ nativitate hoc loco agi, sed tantùm Regi Achatz filium Ezechiam promitti contendunt, qui ob singularem pietatem & Zelum dici debeat Emmanuel. Verùm glossa hæc textui manifestè repugnat. Nam Propheta Esaias de tali re hoc loco vaticinatur, quæ Regi Achatz pro Signo certissimæ liberationis ab hostibus esse debeat: proindè dicit ad ipsum : Postula tibi signum à Domino DEO tuo, sive in profundo, sive in excelso: Quod cùm petere nollet Achatz, infert Esaias : Propter hoc Dominus ipse dabit vobis Signum: Ecce virgo concipiet. Jam signi loco esse non potuit filii Ezechiæ nativitas, quippè qui secundum consvetum naturæ ordinem conceptus & natus fuit, interveniente commixtione virilis feminis. Deinde ut Galatinus quoque ex R. Salomon annotat, Si annos Ezechiæ numeraveris, invenies ipsum ante regnum Patris Achatz, annos novem natum fuisse. Achatz enim pater sedecim regnavit annis, 2. Reg. 16. v. 2. Cui succesfit in regno Ezechias filius, cùm annum ætatis ageret vicesimum quintum, 2. Reg. 18. v. 2. Ergo cùm Pater Achatz regnare cepisset, Ezechias jam erat puer novem annorum : ac proinde vaticinium hoc Regi Achaz quarto regni ipsius anno editum, de filio Ezechiæ nullo modo intelligi vel potest, vel debet: ut qui jam tùm tredecim annorum erat adolescens.


### On King Christ or Messiah: Question II. Whether Jesus of Nazareth, son of Mary, is that very promised Messiah of the world? (continued)

There are, furthermore, some among the Jews who pretend that the son of the Prophet Isaiah himself is being promised in this place. But the vanity of these men also is openly revealed. For Scripture mentions two sons of Isaiah: One, who had been born to the Prophet just before this prophecy: But the other is mentioned in the eighth chapter, who nevertheless, by the command of GOD himself, was not to be called Immanuel, but had to be designated by other names, as is evident from verse 3 of the eighth chapter.

Thirdly, others cavil that the birth of the Messiah could have nothing to do with the present matter. For because a Sign had to be given to King Ahaz of Judah from the present, by which he would be rendered most certain of liberation from those two enemies, namely from the King of Israel and the King of Syria: But the birth of the Messiah was to happen only many centuries later. Therefore it could not be given in the place of a sign. But the text itself answers this cavil, clearly showing, 1. That Ahaz did not want to ask for a Sign from GOD, for the reason that he thought such a Sign either could not be performed, or if it were performed, he would not want to place faith in the promises concerning that future liberation. But then GOD, offended by this partly hypocrisy and partly diffidence of King Ahaz, gave the Sign, not to Ahaz, whom He judged unworthy, but to the house of David and all his posterity: therefore the Prophet no longer addresses Ahaz, but the house of David, and promises this Sign to it, and indeed such a Sign that it could not only lift up the spirits of the Jews, who were dismayed by the present danger, but which would also be of benefit to believers in the very birth of the Messiah during any calamities whatsoever. For such was the nature of the Jewish people that as often as any more serious calamity loomed, so often did they fear the excision of their lineage, so that at the same time all the promises that had ever been issued anywhere concerning the coming Messiah were rendered void. Therefore, intending to apply a remedy to this fear and pusillanimity, God in this place wished not only to lift up those who were already trembling, but also to provide firm consolation in the future various calamities of the people, not only by repeating the promise concerning the exhibiting of the Messiah, but also by illustrating the same with a new promise. For the first and most ancient promise held that the Seed of the woman would crush the head of the serpent. This promise had afterwards been illustrated in such a way that in place of the Seed of the woman, it was named the Seed of Abraham, from the loins of David. But because he who was named the Seed of Abraham and David could be thought to be about to arise by customary generation, from the commingling of male and female: Therefore, now that the family was known, the Lord returns to explain that which had not yet been observed in that very first promise: namely, that the Messiah would indeed be born from the seed of Abraham and David, yet would not be the Seed of a man, but the Seed of a woman, and indeed of a pure and immaculate virgin. Now, therefore, as long as that virginal birth was deferred, for so long the Jews ought to have been certain that this people would not be entirely destroyed or cut off until that virginal birth was brought forth: which is what the prophecy of the Patriarch Jacob also hinted at, as was shown above. With these things considered, it is manifest that no sign more appropriate for consolation could have been given to the Jews, than this very thing, that it was not limited to any one calamity of this people: but extended itself to the Messiah himself for very many centuries. At length there are some among the Jews who deny that in this place the Hebrew word עַלְמָה Almah signifies a virgin, but denotes only the condition of youthful age, so that it can be explained as a young woman even if corrupted or married: in this sense: Behold a young woman shall conceive and bear: For if he had spoken of the conception of a virgin, he would not have said, Behold הָעַלְמָה Haalma, that is, a young woman: but, Behold בְּתוּלָה Bethulah, that is, a virgin shall conceive. But the scope and intention of the Prophet evidently demonstrates from the beginning the stupendous vanity of this objection. For by the command of GOD he wished to erect a certain miraculous sign for the Jews, from which they might seek a certain and infallible argument in any calamities whatsoever, that they would not yet be entirely cut off or destroyed, because this Sign had not yet been fulfilled, that is, because a virgin had not yet borne a son. For that a young woman, whether married or corrupted, should bear a son, could not be in the nature of a Sign. Furthermore (as Galatinus also notes, book 7, chapter 15) there are three words among the Hebrews, signifying almost the same thing; namely נַעֲרָה Naarah: בְּתוּלָה Bethulah: & עַלְמָה Almah: among which the first, namely Naarah, is referred only to the age of women, whether they be virgins or have been known by a man: Whence it signifies any girl or young woman as yet. But the second, namely Bethulah, signifies virginity, not only of young women, but also of women more advanced in years and age.

Finally the third, namely Almah, having regard to both, comprehends and expresses youthful age and virginity in one and the same name. Therefore, according to the proper Hebrew affection of these three words, every woman, whether she be a young woman or aged, as long as she is a virgin, can be called Bethulah. But as long as she is a young woman, whether she be still a virgin or corrupted, she is called Naarah. But no one can be called Almah unless she is at once both a young woman and an intact virgin: which the etymology of the word itself also proves. For it is derived from the root עָלַם which signifies to hide or to conceal: so that the name עַלְמָה Almah denotes a young woman as if still hidden from the sights of men, occult, and entirely intact, concerning whose modesty and integrity there is no doubt: especially when the article is prefixed to this name, which among the Hebrews is the letter ה He. Nor in the whole Holy Scripture is this expression הָעַלְמָה Haalmah found, with the article He, except in three places, in which it always denotes a young virgin, pure and undefiled: as Gen. 24:43, Rebecca, before she was betrothed to Isaac: then Exod. 2:8, Miriam the sister of Moses, still very much a girl, as one may conjecture from the chronology: and finally the mother of the Messiah, in this place, Isa. 7:14. Just as therefore the Holy Spirit in the two preceding places, through the word הָעַלְמָה Haalmah, wished to denote nothing but a young virgin, and one entirely unblemished: there can certainly be no doubt for any pious person that in Isaiah also he wished to express the same thing through the same articulated word. For this very reason also, he wished to name the mother of the Messiah not Bethulah, but Haalmah: so that he might express both, namely both youth and virginity: For if he had said: Behold a Bethulah shall conceive, then he would have expressed only one thing, namely virginity, but not youth. Besides these three places, there occurs yet one more, Prov. 30:19, where Solomon says: There are three things hidden from me, and four, or the fourth I have not known: The way of an eagle in the heavens: the way of a serpent upon a rock: the way of a ship in the heart of the sea: and the way of a man in a virgin, בְּעַלְמָה גֶּבֶר וְדֶרֶךְ . Concerning which place some not only Jews are in an uproar: but also Christian Hebrew interpreters, among whom are Pagninus in his Lexicon, Mercerus on this place, and others, contending that by Almah in this place is denoted a young woman already corrupted, and therefore the virginity of the mother of the Messiah cannot be evidently demonstrated from the nature and affection of this word. But the very evidence of the text sufficiently argues against this thoughtlessness of those interpreters. For that Solomon does not understand that natural union of a man with a virgin is argued by the fact that he says he cannot at all know or understand this, when nevertheless that natural way of a man with a virgin is most known to most people: to Solomon above all, who had the natures of men, animals, and plants known and perceived down to the smallest details. 1 Kings 4:29 & seqq. Therefore it is absolutely necessary that Solomon is speaking of some other entirely supernatural way of a man in a virgin. But that supernatural way, and one unknown to Solomon, will be none other than that which Isaiah treats in this place, namely that a virgin shall bear a son, and of which the Prophet Jeremiah speaks more clearly in chapter 31: GOD shall create a new thing upon the earth: A woman shall encompass a man, and indeed a man גֶבֶר Ghever, that is, a strong, powerful one, namely GOD himself. The way therefore of the strong and powerful man in an almah, according to Solomon, is nothing else than the very incarnation of the Son of GOD from a virgin. And this way indeed Solomon could not fully and perfectly know: In what manner, namely, a virgin could conceive without human seed, and contain perfect GOD and man in her womb, and bear a son, and remain a virgin even after birth, neither could Solomon's intellect fully grasp, nor any tongue ever explain.
