And although we do not value highly the fables of the Romanists concerning the Divisions of the Apostles, as also the very feast of this Division, which they have been accustomed to celebrate on the fifteenth of July, being as they are entirely destitute of the faith of both the Scriptures and approved historians in this part: Although we also leave that tradition in its place, which reports that the whole world was divided among the Apostles, and indeed so distinctly: That the regions of the East [were assigned] to Thomas and Bartholomew: The Southern region, to Simon and Matthew: The Northern peoples, to Philip and Thaddaeus: The Mediterranean provinces, to Matthias and James the Just: the place of the Mediterranean sea, to John and Andrew: the Western regions, to Peter and James of Zebedee: and finally the whole world was assigned to Paul: yet there is no doubt for us that either such a division, or some similar one, was made among the Apostles: so that each one had a certain region of the world, as it were, assigned to himself, not that it was not lawful for them to run out into other provinces as well: but that he might care for that one especially above the others, and plant it with the preaching of the Gospel concerning Christ. And the Apostle seems to allude to some such division, Galatians 2, verses 7 and 8, asserting that the Gospel of the Circumcision had been entrusted to Peter, that is, to be preached among the Jews: but to himself the Gospel of the uncircumcision, that is, to be announced among the Gentiles. But whatever may be the case, whether in this or in another way the Apostles divided their labors among themselves throughout the whole world, that is nevertheless placed beyond all doubt whatsoever that by their work, the Kingdom of Christ, through the preaching of the Gospel, has been founded, confirmed, and established in the whole world among all nations, languages, regions, provinces, and peoples who are under the Sun: so much so that the Apostle, a witness greater than any exception, did not hesitate to write that, in his own time, the Gospel had been preached to every creature which is under heaven. Colossians 1, verse 23.

But how the preaching of the Gospel sounded throughout the whole world even after the times of the Apostles, Irenaeus reports in book 1 against heresies, chapter 3, in these words: Having received this preaching and this faith, as we have said before, the Church, although disseminated throughout the entire world, guards it diligently, as if inhabiting one house, and believes these things similarly, namely as if having one soul and one heart, and consistently preaches, teaches, and hands these things down, as if possessing one mouth. For even if there are various and dissimilar kinds of languages in the world: yet the power of the doctrine is one and the same. And neither do these Churches which are founded in GERMANY believe otherwise, or teach otherwise, nor those which are in Spain, nor in Gaul, nor in the East, nor in Egypt, nor in Libya, nor those which are founded in the middle of the world. But just as the Sun, a Creature of GOD, is one and the same in the entire world: So also the preaching of the Truth shines everywhere, and illuminates all men who wish to arrive at the knowledge of the Truth.

To which opinion Tertullian also writes in his book against the Jews, chapter 7. Their sound has gone out into all the earth, and their words to the ends of the earth. For in whom else have all nations believed, except in Christ who has already come? For in whom have other nations also believed, the Parthians, Medes, Elamites, and those who inhabit Mesopotamia, Armenia, Phrygia, Cappadocia, and those dwelling in Pontus, and Asia and Pamphylia; those staying in Egypt, and those inhabiting the region of Africa which is beyond Cyrene; the Romans and the inhabitants; then also the Jews in Jerusalem, and other nations, as now the varieties of the Gaetulians, and the many borders of the Moors, all the ends of the Spains, and the diverse nations of the Gauls, and the places of the Britons inaccessible to the Romans, but subjected to Christ, and of the Sarmatians, and of the Dacians, and of the Germans, and of the Scythians, and of many hidden nations, and provinces, and many islands unknown to us, and which we are less able to enumerate? In all of which places the name of Christ, who has already come, reigns: as one before whom the gates of all cities are opened, and to whom none are closed: before whom iron bars have been strengthened, and bronze valves have been opened. Although these things also are to be understood spiritually, whereby the hearts of individuals, besieged in various ways by the devil, are opened by the faith of Christ: yet they have been clearly fulfilled, as in all of which places a people of the name of Christ dwells.

And a few things: Christ's kingdom and name are extended everywhere, are believed everywhere, are worshipped by all the nations enumerated above, reign everywhere, are adored everywhere, are attributed to all everywhere equally; there is no greater grace of a King with him, no joy of some imperious Barbarian, no distinct merits of dignities or of anyone's birth; he is equal to all, King to all, judge to all, GOD and Lord to all. Volume 1 of his Works, page 164 in my edition.

And although in the progress of time many regions and provinces have shaken off this yoke of the Kingdom of Christ, namely the preaching of the Gospel, in such a way that they have returned to the former darkness of ignorance, and errors, and idolatry, like a dog to its vomit: yet Christ, through his infinite goodness and mercy, has caused very many of them to be called back again to the boundaries of his kingdom through the faithful heralds and Doctors of his Word: as is evidently clear from the histories concerning the Conversions of the Gentiles: But above all, he has always established the Church in an illustrious place, so that the fame concerning the true worship of GOD might flow even to the most remote peoples: and even now this Kingdom of Grace lies open to all peoples, tribes, and languages which are under heaven.

Latin:

THEOREMA Octavum. Vis & uti-

litas Regni Christi, quod non nisi Spirituale est, in duobus potissimùm consistit. 1. Quòd Christus nos bonis omnibus, ad æternam animarum salutem necessariis locupletat. Quicquid ergô in Christo felicitatis nobis promittitur, non subsistit in externis commodis, ut in hoc mundo, vitam bonis & delitiis carnalibus affluentem transigamus: sed ad cœlestem vitam totum referendum est. Et quid prodesset nobis, sub cœlestis Regis imperium colligi, nisi extra terrenæ vitæ statum fructus ejus constaret. Sicut ergo externæ felicitatis pars una continetur bonorum secularium copia: ita Piorum in eo consistit felicitas, quòd Christus suos bonis ad salutem animarum necessariis ditat.

2. Deinde: Quòd robore etiam, & virtute Christus suos munit, ut sint adversus hostes quoslibet inexpugnabiles. Regia enim ejus unctio, non ex oleo, & aromatibus confecta fuisse legitur: sed ideò Christus dictus fuit, quia oleo lætitiæ præ consortibus suis unctus fuit: Psal. 45. v. 8. nempe quia super eum reqvievit Spiritus sapientiæ, intelligentiæ, consilii, fortitudinis & timoris DEI: Jesa. 11. v. 2. Neque enim privatim ipse sibi ditatus est, dum Spiritus ipsi datus est, non ad mensuram, Johan. 3.v.34. sed sic est perfusus abundantiâ, ut de plenitudine ejus omnes acciperemus gratiam pro gratia: Johan.1.v.16. Unde colligimus, non sibi magis regnare Christum, quàm nobis: Unde & Christiani haud immeritò dicimur. Quæ omnia eò tendunt, ut quia Christi regnum non terrênum, aut carnale esse, quod corruptioni subjaceat: sed Spirituale esse, intelligimus, qvod ad vitam æternam nos attollat: hinc discamus primùm Vitam hanc sub ærumnis, contemtu, probris, molestiis parienter transigere, eo uno contenti, quòd Rex noster non sit nos destituturus: sed communicaturus ea, quæ ex usu salutis nostræ sunt futura: Deinde, quia Virtute suâ nos roborat; verâ fiduciâ animati depugnemus cum Diabolo, peccato & morte. Tandem, ut oleo gratiæ ab ipso perfusi, & donis liberaliter repleti, non mundi aut carnis scorias: sed veros Spiritus fructus in ipsius gloriam vicissim proferamus.

THEOREMA Nonum Maxima est diversitas Regni Christi, & Regnorum hujus mundi. Nam & substantiâ differunt, naturâque, & duratione temporis, & beneficiorum genere, & finium qualitate, & Fortunæ disparitate, & administrationis formâ ac conditione, & summatim loquendo, communitatis inter se nihil quicquam habent, præter Nomen, & Mundum istum, qvo communi interdum in hoc seculo utuntur. Nam duratio etiam, quamvis utrinqve non est sempiterna: Siquidem utrisqve (diverso tamen respectu, uti suprà theoremate qvinto ostensum) incumbet abrogatio: tamen imperia & regna mundi, statim in adventu Christi, cum mundo ipso abolebuntur: Regnum autem Christi domitis demùm, subjugatisq́; hostibus omnibus, & inter hos, morte etiam ipsâ, quæ postremus hostis est, sublatâ, postquàm plenissima illius consummatio tandem facta fuerit, assertis ad cœlestem gloriam electis universis, DEO Patri in ipsâ æternitatis gloriâ demùm tradetur, Christo ipso, cujus partes in defensione & salvatione Ecclesiæ suæ, jam erunt impletæ, exinde cum Patre & Spiritu Sancto versaturo in regno Gloriæ sempiterno & simplicissimo, quale ante conditum genus humanum, ab ipsâ æternitate, priùs etiam possederat.

THEOREMA Decimum & postremû: Tam latè patet Regnum hoc Gratiæ, quàm latè se diffundit totus terrarum orbis. Etsi enim Messias noster illud initiò inchoavit in Judæâ, sive Palæstinâ, Judæis tantùm prædicando Evangelium: Esse enim debuit Minister Circumcisionis, propter veritatem DEI, ad confirmandas promissiones Patrum: Rom. 15.v.18. mox tamen post ascensionem, per Apostolos Regni hujus sui terminos ad omnes fines orbis terrarum extendit, dum universas gentes, quæ sub cœlo sunt, ad ejus societatem, per prædicationem Evangelii perduxit, ut nulla sit gens, nulla natio, nulla provincia, nullus populus, ad quem sonus prædicationis Evangelicæ non exierit. Matth. 28. v. 19. Marci 16. v. 15. Rom. 10. vers. 18. Coloss. 1. v. 13. Theorematis hujus veritas patet partim ex historia Actorum Apostolocorum: partim verò ex historia Ecclesiastica. Certè in prima illa Pentecoste Novi Testamenti, unica concione Petri, ultra tria millia ad regnum hoc Christi sunt associata, non tantùm ex Judæis, sed ex omni natione hominum, qui sub cœlo sunt, ita ut præter Judæos, Parthi quoque & Medi, & Elamitæ, & habitatores Mesopotamiæ, Judææq́ue, & Cappadociæ, Ponti & Asiæ, Phrygiæ & Pamphilie, Ægypti, & partium Libyæ ejus, quæ est finitima Cyrenæ, & advenæ Romani, Judæiq́ue & Proselyti, Cretes & Arabes, & alii Apostolos sua quisque lingua, in qua natus erat, audirent loquentes magnalia DEI. Act. 2. v. 5. & seqq.

Salaminæ prædicaverunt Evangelium; Actor. 13. v. 5. totamq́; illam insulam perambularunt usque ad Paphum, v. 6. & peragratâ prætereà Pamphiliâ & Pisidiâ, ac constitutis Ecclesiis, Antiochena Iconiensi, Lystranâ, Derbenâ, Pergensi, Attaliensi, Antiochiam redierunt. Actor. 13. v. 13. 14. Actor. 14. v. 1. 6. 20. 24. & 25. sed ita, ut postmodum ab invicem divulsi, Paulus quidem peragraret Syriam & Ciliciam: Barnabas autem rursum in Cyprum navigaret. Actor. 15. v. 39. & seqq.

Paulus ergò itinere hoc suscepto revisit Ecclesias Asiaticas, & adjuncto sibi Timotheo, Phrygiam & Galatiam prædicatione Evangelii ad Christum convertit. Actor. 16. v. 1. & 6. Postmodum volens ire in Pythiniam, prohibitus à Spiritu Sancto Verbum loqui in Asia & Misia, Troade descendit in Macedoniam: peragratâ Samothraciâ, & Neapoli, & Philippis, & Amphipoli, & Apollonia, Thessalonica, Beroeâ, Athenis. Actor. 16. vers. 17. & 8. & 11. Actor. 17. v. 1. 10. & 15. Inde digressus venit Corinthum Act. 18. v. 1. prædicans & disputans in Synagogis de Jesu apud Judæos & Græcos, v. 4. postea verò rediens in Asiam per Ephesum, relicto ibi Aquila, & Ecclesias Asiæ denuò revisit. Actor. 18. v. 19. salutatis Ecclesiis Cæsariensi & Antiochenâ v. 22.

Deindè ortâ persecutione Hierosolymis, & Apostolis quidem ibidem remanentibus, fidelium tamen plurimi, qui dispersi fuerant per regiones Judææ & Samariæ, Verbum DEI annunciarunt, & usque ad Phœnicen, Cyprum & Antiochiam posteà transierunt, non solis Judæis, sed & Antiochiz Græcis, hoc est, gentibus prædicantes DOMINUM JESUM Act. 8. v. 1. 4.

Porrò Epheso discedens rursus, rediit in Macedoniam & Græciam, Actor. 19. v. 21. & cap. 20. v. 1. & 2. Ubi cum insidias sibi structas esse intellexisset, relictâ Syriâ, quam cogitabat, per Macedoniam reverti voluit, Troadeque solvens, Asson, Mytilenen, Samum, & inde Miletum navigavit, ubi presbyteris Ephesinis valedixit, Actor. 20. indeq́; Rhodum, Pataram, Tyrum, Ptolemaida, Cæsaream, & rursus Hierosolymam pervenit, ubi seditione à Judæis contra ipsum mota, à tribuno Lysia in vincula conjicitur, Act. 21. inde Romam abductus, peragrato toto littore Asiæ & Cretæ, tandem Miletum naufragus appellit. Act. 27. ac tandem causam coram Nerone dicit: indeq́; salutatis primùm Ecclesiis Syriæ, Asiæ, & Græciæ, in Occidentem reversus, Italiam, Galliam, & Hispaniam toto ferme decennio peragravit, & prædicatione Evangelii implevit.

Quo ipso tempore Philippus, qui Actor. 21. v. 8. nominatur Evangelista, & unus ex septem Diaconis erat, prædicavit Evangelium Samariæ, convertit in viâ Gazam tendente, Eunuchum, præfectum Candaces reginæ Æthiopum: inde Azotum profectus, evangelizavit cunctis civitatibus, donec veniret Samariam. Actor. 8. v. 5. & 26. ac seqq. & 40.

Eâdem occasione Petrus quoque & Johannes missi sunt ab Apostolis in Samariam, ut in prædicando Evangelio operas quasi auxiliares præstarent Philippo Evangelistæ, Actor. 8. v. 14. Et Petrus cum primis peregrinatione tum susceptâ annunciando Christum omnes, priùs scilicet enumeratas, Judææ, Galileæ, & Samariæ, Ecclesias peragravit, Lyttam quoq́; pervenit: inde Assaronem & Joppen: inde peculiari revelatione Cæsaream ad Gentes, & quidem ad Cornelium Centurionem evocatus. Actor. 9. v. 32. 36. Actor. 10. v. 10. & seqq.

Patescit ex brevi hac tabella, non tantùm quantis quamqve variis periculis ac laboribus Apostolus sese ob propagationem Regni Christi objecerit: sed &, quàm longè lateq́ve per unum istum Apostolum, Regnum Christi dilatatum, amplificatumq́ve fuerit: ita ut haud falsò de se ipso scribat, Rom. 15. v. 17. & seqq. Habeo, quod glorier per Christum Jesum, in his, quæ ad DEUM pertinent: Non enim ausim loqui quicquam eorum, quæ non effecit Christus per me, in obedientiam Gentium, Verbo & Facto, in potentia signorum ac prodigiorum, in potentia Spiritus DEI, ut ab Hierusalem, & in circumjacentibus regionibus, usque ad Illyricum impleverim Evangelium Christi.

Hæc dum ita gerebantur, Paulus Apostolus, qui prius Saulus nominabatur, in via ad Damascum, mirabiliter à DEO conversus, Actor. 9. v. 1. & seqq. prædicabat Evangelium de Christo gentibus, & disputabat cum Græcis, Actor. 9. v. 29. postmodùm verò unâ cum Barnabâ, à Spiritu Sancto, per reliquos Apostolos segregatus fuit, in opus, ad quod accersebantur: Actor. 13. v. 2. Hi cùm Seleuciam abiissent, inde in Cyprum navigarunt: ac

Sed neque reliquorum Apostolorum labor & industria suo successu, fructuque caruit. Nam cùm à Christo Servatore ante ascensionem jussi essent docere Evangelium in toto terrarum orbe, nihil certè studio omni fecerunt reliquum, quin Regni Christi terminos, cum universi orbis latitudine æquarent, non quidem confusè, sed distinctè divisis inter se operis. Et quanquam fabellas Romanensium de Divisionibus Apostolorum, ut & ipsum festum Divisionis hujus, quod decimo qvinto Julii celebrare consueverunt, non magni facimus, qvippe & Scripturarum, & probatorum historicorum fide hac in parte prorsus destituti : Qvanquam etiam traditionem illam suo loco relinqvimus, quæ totum terrarum orbem inter Apostolos divisum, & ita qvidem distinctum esse refert : Ut Orientis regiones, Thomæ & Bartholomæo: Meridionalis plaga, Simoni & Matthæo: Septentrionales populi, Philippo & Thaddæo: Mediterraneæ provinciæ, Matthiæ & Jacobo Justo : loco maris Mediterranei, Johanni & Andreæ : Occidentales regiones, Petro & Jacobo Zebedæi: Paulo deniqve totus pariter mundus sit assignatus: tamen nullum nobis est dubium, quin vel talis, vel consimilis aliqva Divisio inter Apostolos facta sit: ut quisque certam quasi mundi plagam sibi haberet assignatam, non quòd ad alias etiam provincias ipsi excurrere non fas esset : sed ut eam potissimùm præ cæteris curaret, & prædicatione Evangelii de Christo plantaret. Et ad talem aliqvam divisionem alludere videtur Apostolus, Galat. 2. v. 7. & 8. asserens, Petro creditum esse Evangelium Circumcisionis, hoc est, apud Judæos prædicandum : sibi verò Evangelium præputii, hoc est, inter gentes annunciandum. Sed quicqvid sit, sive hoc, sive alio modo Apostoli operas per totum terrarum orbem, inter se diviserint, illud tamen extra omnem prorsus dubitationem est positum quòd ipsorum operâ, Regnum Christi, per prædicationem Evangelii, in toto terrarum orbe apud omnes gentes, linguas, regiones, provincias, populos, qui sub Sole sunt, sit fundatum, confirmatum, stabilitum: usque adeò, ut D. Apostolus, testis omni exceptione major, scribere non dubitaverit, suo jam tempore, Evangelium prædicatum fuisse universæ creaturæ, quæ sub cœlo est. Coloss. 1. v. 23.

Quomodo verò etiam post Apostolorum tempora, prædicatio Evangelii in toto terrarum orbe sonuerit, refert Irenæus lib. 1. de hæresibus, cap. 3. his verbis : Hanc prædicationem cum acceperit, & hanc fidem, quemadmodum prædiximus, Ecclesia, & quidem in universum mundum disseminata, diligenter custodit, quasi unam domum inhabitans, & similiter credit iis, videlicet quasi unam animam habens, & unum cor, & consonanter hæc prædicat, & docet, & tradit, quasi unum possidens os. Nam etsi in mundo varia sunt & dissimilia linguarum genera: una tamen, eademq; est virtus doctrinæ. Et neq; hæ, quæ in GERMANIA sunt fundatæ Ecclesiæ, aliter credunt, aut aliter docent, neq; hæ, quæ in Hispaniis, neq; in Gallis, neq; in Oriente, neq; in Ægypto, neq; in Libia, aut in medio orbis terrarum fundatæ sunt. Sed quemadmodum Sol, Creatura DEI, unus & idem est in universo mundo: Ita & prædicatio Veritatis ubique lucet, & illuminat omnes homines, qui ad agnitionem Veritatis pervenire volunt.

Qvam in sententiam scribit etiam Tertullianus in lib. adversus Judæos cap. 7. In universâ terrâ exiit sonus eorum, & usq; ad terminos terræ verba eorum. In quem enim alium universæ gentes crediderunt, nisi in Christum, qui jam venit? Cui enim & aliæ gentes crediderunt, Parthi, Medi, Elamitæ, & qui inhabitant Mesopotamiam, Armeniam, Phrygiam, Capadociam, & incolentes Pontum, & Asiam & Pamphyliam; immorantes Ægyptum, & regionem Africæ, quæ est trans Cyrenen, inhabitantes; Romani & incolæ; tunc & in Hierusalem Judæi, & cæteræ gentes, ut jam Getulorum varietates, & Maurorum multi fines, Hispaniarum omnes termini, & Galliarum diversæ nationes, & Britannoru inaccessa Romanis loca, Christo verò subdita & Sarmatarum, & Dacorum, & Germanorum, & Scytharum, & abditarum multarum gentium, & provinciarum, & insularum multarum nobis ignotarum, & quæ enumerare minùs possumus? In quibus omnibus locis Christi nomen: qui jam venit, regnat: utpote ante quem omnium civitatum portæ sunt apertæ, & cui nullæ sunt clausæ: ante quē seræ ferreæ sunt communitæ, & valvæ æreæ sunt apertæ. Quanquam & ista spiritualiter sunt intelligenda, quo præcordia singulorum variis modis à diabolo obsessa, fide Christi sint referata: attamen perspicuè sunt adimpleta, utpote in quibus omnibus locis, populus nominis Christi inhabitet.

Et pauca: Christi regnum & nomen ubiq; porrigitur, ubiq; creditur, ab omnibus gentibus suprà enumeratis colitur, ubiq; regnat, ubiq; adoratur, omnibus ubique tribuitur æqualiter, non Regis apud illum major gratia, non Barbari alicujus imperiosi lætitia, non dignitatum, aut natalium cujusquam discreta merita, omnibus æqualis, omnibus Rex, omnibus judex, omnibus DEUS & Dominus est. Tom. 1. Operum pag. mihi 164.

Et quanquam progressu temporis multæ regiones ac provinciæ, jugum hoc Regni Christi, prædicationem nimirùm Evangelii ita excusserunt, ut ad pristinas ignorantiæ, & errorum, & idololatriæ tenebras, tanquam canis ad vomitum reversæ sint: plurimas tamen earum Christus rursus pro infinitâ suâ bonitate ac misericordiâ per fideles Verbi sui præcones ac Doctores, ad pomeria regni sui evocari curavit: quemadmodum ex historiis de Conversionibus Gentium evidenter patet: Cumprimis autem Ecclesiam in illustri semper loco constituit, ut fama de vero DEI cultu ad remotissimos etiam populos dimanaverit: ac etiamnum Regnum hoc Gratiæ pateat universis populis, tribubus & linguis, quæ sub cælo sunt.


### On the Quality, Form, and Condition of the Kingdom of Christ: II. Most Anciently Striking Against the Purer Doctrine of the Kingdom of Christ. Into the present Article concerning the Kingdom of Christ…

IN the present Article concerning the Kingdom of Christ, various and manifold depravations have been brought in; indeed most diverse in time: but so related by the pestilence of errors, that they all seem to have conspired for the destruction of the kingdom of Christ.

Prophetic and metaphorical, for certain reasons proper to the shadows of the Old Testament. Therefore, the interpretation of this figurative speech must be sought and defined solely from the writings of the New Testament and the Gospel itself: by the example of the Apostles, who refer the prophetic oracles concerning the kingdom promised to David explicitly to the spiritual Kingdom of Christ, subject in this world to perpetual calamities and persecutions; this universal authentic rule having been promulgated, Acts 14:21: Through many tribulations we must enter into the kingdom of GOD. This method of interpreting they learned from their master, Christ the Savior, who, having sharply rebuked and refuted several times that carnal opinion or persuasion of the disciples concerning some worldly and external kingdom to be built on this earth, relegated them to the School of the Cross and taught them to feel and believe nothing but what is spiritual concerning his kingdom: proposing again a new law, clearly absurd to the intellect of the disciples: I appoint unto you, as my Father hath appointed unto me a kingdom: The kings of the Gentiles exercise lordship over them; and they that exercise authority upon them are called benefactors. But ye shall not be so. Luke 22:25 & 29. But neither did the Prophets themselves involve this spiritual condition of the Kingdom of Christ in total silence. For while they prophesied both things concerning this kingdom: namely, that it would be eternal, Dan. 2:44, and that the King Messiah himself was to be killed, Dan. 9:26, Isa. 53:10, nay more, that the Church in this world would be subject to perpetual afflictions: according to that Psalm 2:2, The kings of the earth set themselves, and the rulers take counsel together, against the Lord, and against his Christ: certainly by this very thing they insinuated clearly enough that Christ's kingdom in this world is not to be measured or defined by external splendor, but rather by internal and spiritual glory. To which pertain especially those two chapters, 11 and 12 of Daniel, concerning the most afflicted state of the kingdom of Christ under the tyranny of that typical Antiochus, namely the Roman Antichrist.

The Jews claim the first place for themselves, who have trifled, and still trifle today, that the Messiah Christ would establish such an empire on earth, by which, having subdued this visible world by force and arms and purged it of the dregs of all infidels, the Jews alone, and those who have embraced their religion, would reign in perpetual peace and happiness under Christ, and abound in the affluence of all earthly things. The vanity of which delusion so occupied the minds of the Jewish people of old, that it even took root in the minds of Christ's disciples, in the uprooting of which he himself labored diligently throughout the time of his ministry, but he did not fully pull them out until, having been endued with power from on high at the feast of Pentecost, they finally truly learned what the condition of the Kingdom of Christ in this world would be. A proof of which matter is provided by the story of the mother of the sons of Zebedee, asking that it be granted that one of them sit at the right hand, the other at the left of King CHRIST, in the governance of the kingdom. Matt. 20:21. Likewise the contention of the disciples concerning primacy: Luke 22:24. Acts 1:6.

But this delusion obscures the nature, condition, and all the power and splendor of the kingdom of Christ: it overwhelms the spiritual consolations to be sought from the spiritual Kingdom of CHRIST: it enervates the hope of the pious concerning the kingdom of Glory and eternal blessedness: finally, it removes the spiritual exercises pertaining to the Spiritual Kingdom of Christ. The Prophets certainly, describing the state and condition of Christ everywhere, define nothing worldly, earthly, or corporeal: but express his affections partly as spiritual, partly as clearly opposed to this world: such as are: 1. That under the Kingdom of the Messiah all the nations of the earth are to be blessed: Gen. 12:3 & 22:18. Now if they are to be blessed, they are certainly not to be oppressed, not to be reduced to servitude, and finally not to be utterly extirpated. 2. That King Messiah is predicted to be poor regarding the external form of this world, Zech. 9:9. 3. That under the coming of the Messiah there will be an end of wars, and he himself will speak peace to the Gentiles. Zech. 9:10. Therefore if he speaks peace to the Gentiles, he will not cut them off or exterminate them. 4. That the Messiah, brought into the world, is to suffer and die for the sins of men. Isa. 53:10. Dan. 9:26. 5. That the Kingdom of the Messiah is not to be enclosed within the narrow borders of the Jewish people, but to be extended to the ends of the earth. Ps. 72:8.

Latin:

IN præsentem Articulum de Regno Christi variæ ac multiplices depravationes sunt ingestæ; tempore quidem diversissimæ: sed errotum pestilentiâ ita cognatæ, ut omnes in perniciem regni Christi conjurasse videantur.

Propheticus, ac methaphoricus, certis de causis umbrarum Veteris Testamenti proprius. Figurati ergò istius sermonis interpretatio ex Novi Testamenti scriptis, ipsoque Evangelio unicè est petenda & definienda: Exemplo Apostolorum, qui oracula Prophetica de regno Davidi promisso, desertè referunt ad Regnum Christi spirituale, calamatitatibus & persecutionibus perpetuis hoc in mundo subjectum; universali hac promulgatâ authenticâ, Actor. 14. v. 21. Per multas tribulationes oportet nos ingredi in regnum DEI. Quem interpretandi modum didicerunt ex magistro suo, Christo Servatore, qui carnali illa discipulorum de mundano quopiam & externo regno, hisce in terris extruendo, sive opinione, sive persvasione acriter aliqvoties reprehensâ, & refutatâ, ad Crucis Scholam ipsos relegatos, & nihil nisi Spirituale de regno suo sentire & credere docuit: novâ rursus, & discipulorum intellectui absurdâ planè propositâ lege hac: Ego dispono vobis, sicut disposuit mihi Pater regnum: Reges gentium dominantur, & magnates potestatem exercent; Vos autem non sic. Luc. 22. v. 25. & 29. Sed neque Prophetæ ipsi quoque Spiritualem hanc Regni Christi conditionem omni silentio involverunt. Nam dum utrumqve de regno hoc vaticinantur: nempè illud fore & æternum, Dan. 2. v. 44. & Regem ipsum Messiam occidendum esse, Dan. 9. v. 26. Esa. 53. v. 10. quin imò Ecclesiam hoc in mundo perpetuis afflictionibus fore subjectam: secundum illud Psalm. 2. v. 2. Surrexerunt reges terræ, & convenerunt in unum, adversus Dominum, & adversus Christum ejus: certè hoc ipso satis dilucidè insinuarunt, Christi regnum hisce in terris non externo splendore: sed internâ potiùs, ac spirituali gloriâ metiendum, ac definiendum esse. Qvò pertinent cumprimis duo etiam illa capita, 11. & 12. Danielis, de afflictissimo regni Christi statu, sub tyrannide Antiochi illius typici, nempe Antichristi Romani.

Primum locum sibi vendicant Judæi, qui nugati sunt, hodieqve nugantur, Messiam Christum tale imperium in terris constituturū, qvo in hoc visibili mundo, vi, armisqve subacto, & à colluvie infidelium omnium repurgato, Judæi soli, & qui ipsorum religionem amplexi sunt, in pace, & felicitate perpetuâ sub Christo dominaturi sint, & abundaturi rerum omnium terrenarum affluentiâ. Cujus delirii vanitas ita occupavit olim Judaicæ gentis animos, ut radices etiam egerit in discipulorum Christi animis, in quibus extirpandis ipse toto ministerii sui tempore sedulò allaboravit, sed haud priùs penitus eas evulsit, quàm in festo Pentecostes virtute ex alto induti, demum verè didicerunt, quænam Regni Christi hisce in terris futura esset conditio. Cujus rei documentum præbet historia de matre filiorum Zebedæi, petente, ut alter illorum à dextris, alter â sinistris Regi CHRISTO, in gubernatione regni assidere concedatur. Matth. 20. v. 21. Item contentio discipulorum de primatu: Luc. 24. v. 24. Actor. 1. v. 6.

Obscurat autem delitium hoc naturam, conditionem & virtutem omnem, ac splendorem regni Christi: obruit consolationes spirituales, ex spirituali Regno CHRISTI petendas: enervat spem piorum de regno Gloriæ, & æternæ beatitudinis: tollit denique exercitia spiritualia, ad Spirituale Regnum Christi pertinentia. Prophetæ certè passim describentes statum, & conditionem Christi, nihil mundanum, terrenum, aut corporale definiunt: sed spirituales partim, partim mundo huic planè oppositas ejus affectiones exprimunt: quales sunt: 1. Quòd sub Regno Messiæ benedicendæ sint omnes gentes terræ: Genes. 12, v. 3. & 22, 18. Jam si benedicendæ, utique non opprimendæ, non in servitutem redigendæ, non denique penitus extirpandæ. 2. Quòd Rex Messias prædicitur qvoad externam mundi hujus formam futurus pauper, Zach. 9. vers. 9. 3. Quòd sub adventum Messiæ finis sit futurus bellorum, ipseq; locuturus pacem Gentibus. Zach. 9. v. 10. Ergò si loquetur pacem Gentibus, eas non excindet, aut exterminabit. 4. Qvòd Messias in mundum editus passurus ac moriturus sit pro peccatis hominum Jes. 53. v. 10. Daniel. 9. v. 26. 5. Qvòd Regnum Messiæ non angustis populi Judaici terminis sit claudendum, sed ad fines usque orbis terrarum extendendum. Psal. 72. v. 8.


### On the Quality, Form, and Condition of the Kingdom of Christ: II. The Error of the Chiliasts

CONCERNING THE KINGDOM OF CHRIST.

The Chiliasts occupy the second place in the class of those erring concerning the Kingdom of CHRIST, so called from the thousand-year number: for they contended that the pious and the elect, after the first Resurrection, would reign with Christ for a thousand years in a worldly and corporeal manner: and would feast on all the pleasures of the body. Some ascribe this error to Papias, the bishop of Hierapolis, a hearer of the Blessed John, and a teacher of Irenaeus, and a companion of Polycarp: Jerome seems to be of this opinion, both elsewhere and in his Commentary on Ezekiel: who also makes Irenaeus himself a partner in this error: which, however, can hardly be demonstrated from the writings of Irenaeus: and not even from chapters 21 and 24.

Those oracles of the Prophets, which for the most part describe the glory of the kingdom of Christ in words and phrases drawn from the nature and likeness of earthly kingdoms, and under the figures of some worldly splendor and earthly happiness, seem to have provided the handle for that most gross error of the Jews. But that style was of the fifth book: where he indeed recites the opinion of the Chiliasts, but does not expressly approve it. Regarding Papias, however, the matter is clearer: according to the testimony of Eusebius, book 3, Ecclesiastical History, chapter 39. Others attribute this error to Cerinthus, a man accustomed to the worst morals, as its author. For since he was most fond of his body and flesh, it is established that he invented a heresy worthy of this genius of his: as Eusebius reports about him from Dionysius of Alexandria, book 3, Ecclesiastical History, chapter 28, and book 7, chapter 23. Nicephorus, book 3, Ecclesiastical History, chapter 14. A certain Nepos, whom Eusebius mentions in book 2, chapter 22, held opinions related to this error; Justin in his Dialogue with Trypho the Jew; Tertullian against Marcion, book 3; Lactantius, book 7, chapter 24. In this age of ours, Thomas Müntzer, the spark and trumpet of peasant sedition, certainly revived this error: and most Anabaptists today follow him: of whom more separately below. But especially the new Enthusiasts, who boast that they have learned from certain revelations made to them when this Kingdom of Christ is to have its beginning in these lands, and that it will last for a thousand years in this world, where, with all Emperors, Kings, Princes, and magistrates oppressed, slain, and utterly destroyed, they alone are to rule: to divide among themselves all kingdoms, empires, and provinces: to trample the necks of Kings and Princes under their feet: and finally, in the abundance of all things, to live in this world with their followers and disciples, until, those thousand years completed, they are translated into heaven with Christ. They seek the handle for their error from the Apocalyptic passage: Revelation 20, verse 1 and following. Which single passage even imposed upon many in antiquity, so that they thought this book was not Apostolic, but written by Cerinthus or another man of that stamp, and foisted upon the Church ψευδωνύμως (falsely named). The words of John, which the Chiliasts abused, are as follows: v. 1. I saw an Angel descending from heaven, having the key of the abyss, and a great chain in his hand: 2. Who apprehended the Dragon, the ancient serpent, which is the Devil and Satan, and bound him for a thousand years. 3. And cast him into the abyss, and closed, and sealed it over him, that he might not seduce the nations any more, until the thousand years are completed. And after this he must be loosed for a little time. 4. Then I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given to them: and the souls of those who were beheaded for the testimony of Jesus, and for the word of GOD, and who did not adore the beast, nor his image, nor received his character on their foreheads, or in their hands: and they will live and reign with Christ for those thousand years. 5. But the rest of the dead will not live again, until those thousand years are completed. This is the first resurrection. 6. Blessed is the holy one who has a part in the first resurrection: in these (indeed) the second death has no power: but they will be Priests of GOD and of Christ, and will reign with him for a thousand years. 7. But when the thousand years are completed, Satan will be loosed from his prison.

There are, however, four principal things which the Chiliasts urged from these words to obtain their opinion. 1. That first resurrection, in which the holy and blessed are to have a part. 2. The time of a thousand years, and the state of the same, under which, with Satan closed and bound in the abyss, there is to be rest, so that he can no longer seduce the nations. 3. The other little time of depression and affliction, under which, after the thousand years have elapsed, the Devil is to be loosed again, and what state is to be in the world at that time. 4. The second resurrection, to which the future general judgment of all men is to be connected.

This passage has no small amount of obscurity, which has tortured and exercised the minds of all ages, even the most acute, and has drawn not a few of them into the Chiliastic error. Most of the Fathers whose writings are extant, and who preceded the age of Jerome and Augustine, were of this opinion. In this number is Justin Martyr, who in his Dialogue against Trypho the Jew expressly confesses that he follows this opinion. Many today make Irenaeus ὁμόψηφον (of the same vote) with Justin, but, if I may say so with their kind permission, they do not prove it from the writings of Irenaeus, nor can they prove it so easily. For although he writes in book 5, chapter 23: The days of the Lord are as a thousand years, and thus not obscurely approves that Jewish δελτέρωσιν (second tradition), or tradition, concerning the six thousand years that this world is to last: yet no one will build Chiliasm from that. But as for Tertullian, he himself assented to this error, as is evident from book 2 against Marcion. Lactantius also patronized it in book 7, chapter 24, having alleged the Sibylline verses to the same sense.

And although there were those who in the same centuries opposed this opinion even with public writings, among whom was especially that Dionysius of Alexandria: yet it generally prevailed in public, especially with the growing authority of that Papias, which was great in the Church, according to the testimony of Eusebius, book 3, chapter 39, to whom afterwards Nepos the Egyptian, and Coration, Eusebius book 7, chapter 22, Apollinaris, and Victorius of Poitiers provided themselves as reinforcements. But finally, in the age of Jerome and Augustine, the fabrication of this Jewish fable began to be laughed at. And although Jerome, in his commentary on chapter 19 of Jeremiah, confesses that he hardly dares to condemn this opinion, because many ecclesiastical men and Martyrs defended it: yet he refutes it here and there, but especially in chapter 66 of Isaiah, and Ezekiel 37, 38, 39, and in the life of Papias. Which Augustine also did in book 20 of The City of GOD, chapters 7 and 8.

Moreover, that we may make an approach to the refutation of that error, it strikes at the beginning against the analogy of the Christian faith, since it defines Christ's kingdom as nothing but spiritual, and confirms that he will return not twice, but only once for judgment, or, to speak with the Savior, that error arises from ignorance of the Scriptures and of the divine power. For in the Resurrection there will be no place for marriage: but they will be blessed like the Angels of God in heaven: Matt. 22. v. 30. Indeed, it arises from ignorance of that condition of his which the Apostle expressed concerning the Kingdom of Christ in Romans 14. v. 17. The Kingdom of GOD is not food and drink: but righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit. Furthermore, it is too dizzying to build a matter of such importance upon the obscurity of a single Apocalyptic passage: to establish such an interpretation and meaning for it, which is both analogous and consistent with the analogy of faith, with the Apostolic sense, and indeed with the very words themselves: this is the work, this is the labor.

However, the exposition of this passage was far more difficult for the ancient Fathers than it is for us today, for this reason at least, because to interpret prophecies and prophetic visions before their fulfillment is not for everyone, but only for the prophetic spirit, which is not given to all: but after fulfillment, the interpretation of the same is easier and more straightforward. Having therefore left aside and put behind those interpretations of the ancients and the moderns which render the reader perplexed and doubtful, we shall first provide such an interpretation as may not in the least dissent from the analogy of faith, may correspond entirely with ecclesiastical history, and may more closely reach the scope of the Apocalyptic passage: then, however, we shall briefly subjoin the sophistries by which both ancient and modern Chiliasts strive to attach a meaning to the Apocalyptic passage that is clearly foreign to it.

And at the beginning, it is indeed placed beyond controversy that this vision is to be understood concerning the State of the Church of Christ in this world, as it is to be until the very last day. Now a Resurrection is attributed to the Church, and that the first one: but given a Resurrection, a death is necessarily presupposed which preceded the Resurrection. What kind of death this was is to be judged not from our own brain, but from the whole coherence of the Apocalyptic text.

It shows, however, that by death in this place one ought to understand not that natural death, but metaphorically that most sorrowful time of the Church, when the profession of the Christian faith was clearly a capital offense, and through continuous persecutions, under those first Roman Emperors, such cruelty was inflicted upon Christian blood that the Church could truly say, 'For Christ's sake we are killed all the day long; we are accounted as sheep for the slaughter': Psalm 44. v. 22. Now, when around the year of CHRIST three hundred, under the Emperor Constantine the Great (to whom the sign of the Cross shining in the sky appeared, with this inscription, 'In this you shall conquer,' as witnessed by Eusebius lib. 9. cap. 9., Tripart. lib. 1. cap. 5., Sozomen lib. 1. cap. 3., Socrates lib. 1. cap. 2., Nicephorus lib. 7. c. 29. Orosius lib. 7. ca. 28.) peace was restored to the Church, the temples of the Christians and oratories were restored everywhere, and the profession of the Christian faith became not only unpunished but also honored: then it began to breathe again, as it were, from this spiritual death and to rise to that new life: Which happiness of the Church indeed lasted for a thousand years, so that while this millennium was running, although even then the mystery of iniquity began to have its beginnings, 2 Thess. 2. v. 7., both in the Eastern and also in the Western region: with the Devil not only conceiving but also bringing forth that offspring which he finally gave birth to: yet the Church was accustomed to labor more within than to be attacked from without: and with Satan strongly bound, seduction did not spread so horribly among the nations, with the boundaries of the Church propagated even to the most remote places of the habitable earth. At the end of this millennium, which occurred around the year of the Lord 1300, a time of affliction began, in which, with the release of the Devil having taken place, his immense fury began to spread, through

Gog and Magog, just as the Apocalypse predicted would happen in this place. To which Boniface VIII in the West, and the Ottoman House in the East, gave the auspices. For around that time the Imperial power began to become worthless in both regions of the world, not only with the Empire of the East reduced to extreme straits, but also in the West with the Exarchate of Ravenna and the Senatorial power of the city of Rome transferred to the Pontiff, by the new Pontifical Law, promulgated in the sixth of the Decretals, and a little later in the Clementines, with the Jubilee first introduced, in which the Pope ordered it to be proclaimed: 'Behold, here are two swords'; with Emperors begging for coronation from the Popes; but the Popes themselves transferring kingdoms and Empires at their own whim, wherever they wished. Around the same time, the thunderbolts of Papal Excommunications, the veneration of Saints, superstitions, and idolatrous worship, the studies of Scholastic Theology, the impunity of crimes, and the lusts of the Clergy began to prevail, and the authority of Holy Scripture, true piety, along with sincere worship and every legitimate order of hierarchies, began to fade away, so that nothing but the extreme fury of the Devil, though for a short time if we look at the quiet of the preceding millennium, was seen in the Church.

Moreover, since horrible persecutions stirred up by pagan Emperors against Christians preceded this captivity and imprisonment of Satan, which began under Constantine the Great and continued for a thousand years: therefore John introduces the souls of those who were killed under those ten notable persecutions, and asserts that judicial seats were given to them, so that they might judge their persecutors. This Johannine assertion, on account of its Hebraism and the disturbed order of Subject and Predicate, with the predicate placed before the subject and the relative before its antecedent, is a little obscure: which, however, if the entire sentence be reduced to its as it were natural order, emerges as follows:

I saw the souls of those not worshipping the beast, or his image, nor receiving his mark on their foreheads or hands; but of those dying for Christ, living and reigning with him, and sitting on thrones, and judging concerning the impious, and condemning them, for a thousand years, that is, in the Prophetic manner, for all eternity. For these thrones were prepared for them from all eternity, according to the assertion of the Savior, Matt. 19, v. 26. Amen I say to you, you, who have followed me in the regeneration, when the Son of Man shall sit on the throne of his glory, you also shall sit on twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel, while indeed they shall take away all excuse from the persecutors, and shall bear witness before them concerning their immense hatred and cruelty: Just as in chapter 12 of Matthew, verses 41 and 42, it is affirmed concerning the Ninevites and the Queen of the South, that in the final judgment they are to judge the unbelieving Jews.

With this interpretation standing, it becomes plain that those words of John also, by which he denies that the rest of the dead lived again, are to be understood neither of bodily death, nor of the resuscitation of the body: but of spiritual death in sins: Which death is proper to the unbelievers or the impious. For these, after their death, do not live again spiritually any more, that is, they will no longer be converted to Christ, and therefore they will never live or reign with him, as the pious and the elect do. And although John adds the particle until, asserting that they would not live again until the thousand years are completed: nevertheless the particle Until in this fifth verse does not set any definite time: but is to be taken negatively in the Hebrew phrase: according to the most useful rule of Nazianzen, Orat. 2 on the Son of God: The particle Until and As far as is not always placed for the negation or distinction of future time: but it indeed sets the limit: but it does not deny what follows from it. The sense therefore is that the spiritually dead are never to reign with Christ. John himself confirms this, immediately adding: This is the first resurrection: expressly hinting that he is not speaking of that second Resurrection, which will be of bodies, and indeed common to all men: but of that spiritual Resurrection, by which in this age the Elect rise again from the death of sins and security: and thus even in this life, in hope: but soon after death, even before the resuscitation of bodies, they truly live in their souls with Christ.

And this interpretation of this most obscure Apocalyptic passage, consistent with the analogy of faith and most consistent with itself, we embrace for this time: not about to resist more stubbornly those showing straighter paths. And thus we place the beginning of this Millennium, which is in question, in the year of Christ 300, in which Constantine the Great, Emperor, put an end to the persecutions that had preceded and had hitherto pressed the Church most harshly. But its completion, or end, in the year of Christ 1300, in which the Turkish empire acquired its strength, and those hostile nations, Gog and Magog, namely the Turks, Tartars, Muscovites: together with the Roman Antichrist, began to rage horribly against the Church: so that then truly the Devil, with the chains by which he had been bound in the preceding millennium, i.e., repressed and restrained by divine power, now broken and loosened, seemed to have begun to ravage in the Church.

With these things thus established, it now becomes plain by what sophistries the Chiliasts, both ancient and more recent, strive to deprave the Apocalyptic passage. For 1. They take that first resurrection concerning a special resurrection of the elect alone, and concerning that carnal constitution of the Kingdom of Christ to be possessed by the Saints alone on these earths: that which fights diametrically with the universal Scripture and the analogy of faith. 2. They falsely take the happiness of that millennium concerning an external and worldly dominion over Kings, Princes, and all Nations: concerning which dominion the Apocalyptic text has not even a jot. 3. They do violence to the text when they dream that, that millennium having been completed, they will be immediately translated with Christ into heaven, and then the universal judgment over the living and the dead will be instituted. The Text cries out against this, which clearly affirms that after that millennium the Devil is to be loosed again, and very many are to be seduced by him, v. 7. 4. & lastly they deprave and mutilate the text, which shows that a time, albeit a small one, of depression and affliction of the Saints will follow that millennium: concerning which the Chiliasts have nothing or know nothing, and thus they distort the truncated Apocalyptic text to their own delirium. Therefore, those fanatics being dismissed, we subscribe entirely to the Analogy of faith and the interpretation consistent with it.

There are indeed other interpreters who seek the beginning of this millennium from the Jerusalem excision: but they place its end in the year of Christ 1073, where Gregory VII, Pontiff, commonly called Hildebrand, or rather Hellenbrandt, agitated by infernal furies, began to rage and riot against the Roman Monarchy in such a way that under his Pontificate Satan also could have seemed to have been loosed from all bonds and freed from his prison. But that which prevents us from subscribing to this calculation is that perpetual and most atrocious persecution of the Church, by which the Ethnic Emperors boiled and raged with insatiable fury against the kingdom of Christ throughout that space: so that before the year 300 of Christ, it was hardly ever permitted for the Church of God to breathe, so far is it from the case that we can establish that Satan was bound in chains and enclosed in prison at that time.

Blessed Luther and others constitute the beginning of this millennium from the time of the writing of this Apocalyptic book and the making of this vision, but the completion in the first beginnings of the Turkish kingdom: so that Christians in the meantime remained and reigned even under the Pagan Emperors themselves, although the Devil was unwilling. But this opinion also labors under the same disadvantage as the one immediately preceding. But if even to these, or to other similar interpretations, room is left, yet none of them confirms this dream of the new Enthusiasts about an earthly kingdom of Christ, which is to last for a thousand years: rather, all of them thoroughly undermine and overturn it. And let these things suffice concerning the former of those errors.

But there is another error of the same vanity and monstrous blindness, by which they sweetly promise to themselves and their own the external possession of the kingdoms of this world, after Emperors, Kings, Princes, and all Magistrates have been cut down and utterly destroyed. In which part they support (although they dare to deny it strenuously) the most profligate society of the Anabaptists, who occupy the third place in the class of those who err: concerning which it follows.

Latin:

DE REGNO CHRISTI.

ALterum locum in classe errantium de Regno CHRISTI, occupant Chiliastæ, à millenario annorum numero sic appellati: Contendebant enim isti, pios atque electos post Resurrectionem primam, cum Christo mille annis regnaturos modo mundano, ac corporali: & in voluptates corporis omnes epulaturos. Hunc errorem non nulli adscribunt Papiæ Hierapolitano antistiti, B. Johannis auditori, ac Irenæi Præceptori, & Polycarpi sodali: Qva in sententiâ videtur esse Hieronymus, tum alibi, tum in Commentario super Ezechielem: qui ipsum quoq; Irenæum erroris hujus socium constituit: id qvod tamen ex scriptis Irenæi vix demonstrabitur: & ne qvidem ex cap 21. & 24.

Errori isti Judæorum crassissimo ansam præbuisse videntur ea Prophetarum oracula, qvæ gloriam regni Christi, verbis ac phrafibus ex terrenorum regnorum naturâ ac similitudine petitis, & sub mundani alicujus splendoris, & terrenæ felicitatis figuris, ut plurimùm describunt. Verùm fuit stylus iste libri quinti: ubi Chiliastarum sententiam recitat quidem, sed non expresse approbat. De Papia autem res est manifestior: teste Eusebio lib. 3. hist. Eccl. cap. 39. Alii Cerintho, homini pessimis moribus assueto, tanquam autori errorem hunc acceptum referunt. Hic enim cùm corporis & carnis suae esset amantissimus, genio huic suo condignam haeresin invenisse statuitur: quemadmodum de eo ex Dionys. Alexandrino refert Eusebius lib. 3. hist. Ecclesiast. cap. 28. & lib. 7. cap. 23. Nicephorus lib. 3. hist. Eccles. cap. 14. Errori huic cognatas sententias tenuerunt Nepos quidam, cujus meminit Eusebius lib. 2. cap. 22. Justinus in Dial. cum Tryphone Judæo: Tertull. contra Marcionem, lib. 3. Lactant. lib. 7. cap. 24. Nostro sanè hoc seculo errorem istum interpolavit Thomas Mentzerus, fax & tuba seditionis rusticæ: & hunc hodiè sequentes Anabaptistae plærique: de quibus infrà seorsim. Cumprimis autem novelli Enthusiastæ, qui ex certis revelationibus sibi factis didicisse se gloriantur, quando Regnum hoc Christi hisce in terris suum habiturum sit initium, & quòd duraturum illud, hoc quidem in mundo mille annis, Ubi oppressis, cæsis, & funditùs deletis omnibus Imperatoribus, Regibus, Principibus, & magistratibus, ipsi soli sint dominaturi: regna, imperia, provincias omnes inter se divisuri: colla Regum ac Principum pedibus suis conculcaturi: in summâ deniq; rerum omnium affluentiâ, cum suis asseclis, & discipulis, hoc in mundo victuri, usque dum expletis mille istis annis in cœlum cum Christo transferantur. Ansam erroris petunt ex loco Apocalyptico: Apocal. 20. v. 1. & seqq. Qui vel unicus locus multis ex antiqvitate etiam imposuit, ut existimarent, hunc librum non esse Apostolicum: sed à Cerintho, aut alio istius farinæ homine conscriptũ, & ψευδωνύμως Ecclesiæ obtrusum. Verba Iohannis, quibus Chiliastæ abutebantur, sic habent: v. 1. Vidi Angelum descendentem è cælo, habentē clavem abyssi, & catenam magnam in manu sua: 2. Qui apprehendit Draconem, serpentem antiquũ, qui est Diabolus, & Satanas, & ligavit eum per annos mille. 3. Et conjecit eum in abyssum, & clausit, & obsignavit super ipsum, ut non seducat ampliùs gentes, donec consummentur mille anni. Et post hoc oportet illum solvi modico tempore. 4. Deinde vidi thronos, & sederunt super eos, & judicium datum est eis: & animas eorum, qui securi percussi sunt propter testimonium Jesu, & propter sermonem DEI, quiq; non adorarunt bestiam, neq; imaginem ejus, nec acceperunt characterem ejus in frontibus suis, aut in manibus: viventq; & regnabunt cũ Christo mille illis annis. 5. Reliqui verò ex mortuis non reviviscent, donec expleti fuerint illi mille anni. Hæc est resurrectio prima. 6. Beatus est sanctus, qui habet partem in resurrectione primâ: in hos (enim) secunda mors non habet potestatem: sed erunt Sacerdotes DEI & Christi, & regnabunt cum eo mille annis. 7. Cùm verò expleti fuerint anni mille, solvetur Satanas è carcere suo.

Qvatuor autem sunt præcipua, quæ ex verbis istis, pro suâ obtinendâ sententiâ urserunt Chiliastæ. 1. Est resurrectio illa prima, in quâ sint habituri partem sancti & beati, 2. Mille annorum tempus, ejusdemq; Status, sub quo in abyssum clauso & ligato Satanâ, quies sit futura, ne ille amplius possit seducere gentes. 3. Tempus alterum modicum depressionis & afflictionis, sub quo post elapsos annos mille, iterum solvendus sit Diabolus, quisq; eo tempore in mundo sit futurus Status. 4. Resurrectio altera, cui connexum sit futurum generale omnium hominum judicium.

Habet locus iste haut parum obscuritatis, quæ omnium ætatum ingenia etiam acutissima torsit & exercuit, & eorum non pauca in errorem pertraxit Chiliasticum. In quâ sententiâ fuerunt Patres plærique omnes, quorum qvidem scripta extant, quique ætatem Hieronymi & Augustini antecesserunt. Quo in numero est Justinus Martyr, qui in Dialogo contra Tryphonem Judæum expressè fatetur, se hanc sequi sententiam. Justino ὁμόψηφον multi hodiè faciunt Irenæum, sed qvod bonâ ipsorum pace dixerim, ex scriptis Irenæi id non probant, neque ita facilè probare possunt. Etsi enim lib. 5. cap. 23. scribit: Dies Domini sunt quasi mille anni, & sic Judæorum illam δελτέρωσιν, sive traditionem, de sex millibus annorum duraturi hujus mundi, haud obscurè comprobat: tamen Chiliasmum nemo inde extruet. Verùm qvoad Tertullianum adstipulatus est ipse errori huic, ut patet ex lib. 2. contra Marcionem. Patrocinatus est illi qvoqve Lactantius lib. 7. cap. 24. allegatis in eundem sensum carminibus Sibyllinis.

Et quanquam fuerunt, qui iisdem seculis opinionem istam publicis etiam scriptis oppugnarunt, inter qvos præcipuè fuit Dionysius ille Alexandrinus: tamen publicè passim ferè obtinuit, præsertim crescente autoritate Papiæ illius, qvæ magna fuit in Ecclesiâ, teste Eusebio lib. 3. cap. 39. cui postmodum sese succenturiatos præbuerunt Nepos Ægyptius, & Coration, Euseb. lib. 7. cap. 22. Appollinaris, & Victorius Pictaviensis. Sed tandem Hieronymi & Augustini ætate, fabulæ hujus Judaicæ commentum rideri cœpit. Et qvanqvam Hieronymus in commentario super cap. 19. Jeremiæ, fatetur, se opinionem istam vix audere damnare, qvia multi Ecclesiastici viri & Martyres eam defenderint: passim tamen præcipuè autem in cap. 66. Esaiæ: & Ezechielis 37. 38. 39. & in vitâ Papiæ eam refutat. Qvod & fecit Augustinus lib. 20. de Civit. DEI, cap. 7. & 8.

Cæterùm, ut ad refutationem erroris istius accessum faciamus, impingit ille initiò in anologiam fidei Christianæ, quippe quæ non nisi spirituale Christi regnum definit, eundemqve non bis, sed semel tantùm ad judicium rediturum confirmat, vel, ut cum Servatore loquamur, oritur ille ex ignorantia Scripturarum, & virtutis divinæ. Nam in Resurrectione nuptiis non erit locus: sed erunt beati tanquam Angeli Dei in cœlo: Matth. 22. v. 30. Imò oritur ille ex ignorantia conditionis ejus, quàm de Regno Christi Apostolus expressit Roman. 14. v. 17. Regnum DEI non est cibus & potus: sed justitia, pax & gaudium in Spiritu Sancto. Deinde vertiginosum nimis est, rem tanti momenti unius Apocalyptici loci obscuritati superstruere: Cujus talem interpretationem, sensumque statuere, qui tùm analogiæ fidei, tùm sensui Apostolico, quin etiam verbis ipsis, sit ἀνάλογος & consentaneus: hoc opus hic labor est.

Fuit autem priscis Patribus longè difficilior, quàm nobis hodiè est, loci istius expositio, eam saltem ob causam, quia vaticinia, & visiones Propheticæ antè impletionem interpretari, non est, nisi spiritus Prophetici, qui non est datus omnibus: post impletionem autem, facilior est atque expeditior eorundem interpretatio. Relictis ergò & posthabitis veterum, & recentiorum interpretationibus illis, quæ Lectorem perplexum & dubium reddunt, initiò talem dabimus interpretationem, quæ ab analogia fidei minimè dissentiat, historiæ Ecclesiasticæ ex asse congruat, & scopum loci Apocalyptici propiùs attingat: deinde verò paucis subjiciemus sophisticationes, quibus tùm veteres, tùm recentiores Chiliastæ, loco Apocalyptico alienum planè sensum affingere student.

Ac initiò quidem extrà controversiam est positum, de Statu Ecclesiæ Christi in hoc mundo, qualis ad diem usque novissimum est futurus, visionem istam accipiendam esse. Jàm tribuitur Ecclesiæ Resurrectio, eaque prima: Atqui datâ Resurrectione necessariò præsupponitur mors, quæ antecesserit Resurrectionem. Quæ mors, qualis fuerit, non ex nostro cerebro, sed ex totâ cohærentiâ textûs Apocalyptici judicandum est.

Ostendit verò ea, mortem hoc loco intelligi debere non naturalem illam, sed μεταφορικῶς tristissimum illud tempus Ecclesiæ, quo capitalis planè fuit fidei Christianæ professio, & per continuas persecutiones, sub primis illis Romanis Imperatoribus, sic fuit sævitum in sanguinem Christianum, ut verè dicere potuerit Ecclesia, propter Christum mortificamur totâ die, æstimati sumus sicut oves occisionis: Psalm. 44. v. 22. Jàm verò cum circa annum CHRISTI trecentesimum, sub Constantino M. Imp. (cui ostentum Crucis in cœlo fulgentis apparuit, cum hac inscriptione, In hoc vinces, teste Eusebio lib. 9. cap. 9. Tripart. lib. 1. cap. 5. Sozomeno lib. 1. cap. 3. Socrate lib. 1. cap. 2. Nicephoro lib. 7. c. 29. Orosio lib. 7. ca. 28.) pax Ecclesiæ redderetur, templa Christianorum, atque oratoria passim instaurarentur, & non impunìs tantùm: sed & honorata fieret Christianæ fidei professio: tunc ex morte hac spirituali respirare quasi, & ad novam resurgere illa cœpit: Quæ sanè Ecclesiæ felicitas duravit annis mille, ita ut millenario hoc currente, licèt jam tum initia cœperit mysterium iniquitatis, 2. Thess. 2. v. 7. tum in Orientali, tum Occidentali etiam plaga: Diabolo non concipiente tantùm, sed & parturiente fœtum eum, quem tandem est enixus: Ecclesia tamen tum magis intus laborare, quàm forinsecus oppugnari consuevit: & Satanâ fortiter ligato, seductio inter gentes non ita horribiliter grassata fuit, pomeriis Ecclesiæ ad remotissima etiam terræ habitabilis loca propagatis. Exeunte hoc millenario, quod circâ annum Domini 1300. factum est, afflictionis tempus cœpit, quo folutione Diaboli factâ, furor ejus immensus grassari cœpit, per

Gog & Magog, uti Apocalypsis hoc loco futurum prædixit. Cui Bonifacius VIII. in Occidente: Domus verò Ottomannica in Oriente auspicium dedit. Nam circa id tempus Cæsarea potestas in utraque mundi plaga vilescere cœpit, non tantùm in extremas angustias redacto Orientis Imperio: sed in Occidente etiam cum Exarchatu Ravennate, & potestate Senatoria urbis Romæ, ad Pontificem translatâ, novo Jure Pontificio, in sexto Decretalium, paulò etiam post in Clementinis promulgato, Jubilæo primùm introducto, in quo Papa acclamari jussit: Ecce hîc duo gladii; Imperatoribus coronationem à Papis flagitantibus: Papis autem ipsis regna & Imperia pro libidine transferentibus, quò vellent. Circa idem tempus Excommunicationum Papalium fulmina, venerationes Sanctorum, superstitiones, & cultus Idololatrici, Schola-\sticæ Theologiæ studia, flagitiorum impunitas, Cleri libidines invalescere, Scripturæ Sacræ autoritas, vera pietas, cum sincero cultu, & omni hierarchiarum legitimo ordine exolescere cœpit, ut nil nisi furor Diaboli extremus, sed modico tamen tempore, si præcedenti millenarii quietem spectemus, in Ecclesia sit conspectus.

Cæterùm cùm hanc Satanæ captivitatem, & incarcerationem sub Constantino M. cœptam, & annis mille continuatam, præcesserint horribiles persecutiones ab Impp. Ethnicis contra Christianos motæ: Ideò Johannes illorum, qui sub decem illis insignibus persecutionibus interfecti fuerunt, Animas introducit, eisque sedes judiciarias datas esse asserit, ut judicarent persecutores suos. Quæ assertio Johannitica ob Hebraismum, & perturbatum Subjecti & Prædicati ordinem, prædicato poffto ante Subjectum, & Relativo ante suum Antecedens, paulò est obscurior: Qui tamen, si Oratio integra in suum quasi naturalem ordinem redigatur: emergit talis:

Vidi animas non adorantium bestiam, aut imaginem ejus, neque accipientium Characterem ejus in frontibus aut manibus; sed morientium pro Christo, vivere & regnare cum ipso, & sedere in Thronis, ac judicare de impiis, eosq; damnare, mille annis, hoc est, more Prophetico, in omnem æternitatem. Nam hi throni præparati illis fuerunt ab omni æternitate, secundum assertionem Servatoris, Matth 19. v. 26. Amen dico vobis, vos, qui secuti estis me in regeneratione, cum sederit Filius Hominis in throno gloriæ suæ, vos etiam sedebitis in thronis duodecim, judicantes duodecim tribus Israel, dum videlicet omnem persecutoribus excusationem adiment, & de immani ipsorum odio & crudelitate coram ferent testimonium: Quemadmodum cap. 12. Matth. vers. 41. & 42. de Ninivitis, & Regina Austri affirmatur, quòd in judicio novissimo sint judicaturi Judæos incredulos.

Stante hac interpretatione, planum sit, verba etiam illa Johannis, quibus negat, cæteros mortuos revixisse, neque de morte corporali, neque de corporis resuscitatione, esse intelligenda: sed de morte spirituali in peccatis: Quæ mors incredulorum sive impiorum est propria. Hi enim post mortem sua non ampliùs reviviscunt spiritualiter, hoc est, non ampliùs convertentur ad Christum, ac proinde cum eo etiam nunquam vivent, aut regnabunt, sicut pii & electi. Et licet Johannes subjiciat particulam donec, asserens, eos non revicturos, donec consummentur mille anni: tamen particula Donec versu hoc quinto non ponit definitú aliquod tempus: sed negativè est accipienda phrasi Hebræa: secundum utilissimam regulam Nazianzeni Orat. 2. de Filio DEI: Particula Donec, & Usque non ponitur semper ad negationem sive distinctionem futuri temporis: sed ponit illa quidem, Quousque: verùm quod ab eo sequitur, non negat. Sensus ergò est, quòd spiritualiter mortui nunquàm sint regnaturi cum CHRISTO. Confirmat hoc Johannes ipse, mox immediatè subjiciens: Hæc est resurrectio prima: disertè innuens, se non de secundâ illâ Resurrectione loqui, quæ erit corporum, & quidem omnibus hominibus communis: sed de spirituali illa Resurrectione, qua in hoc quidem seculo Electi à morte peccatorum, & securitatis resurgunt: & sic hac etiam in vita, in spe: mox autem post mortem, etiam ante resuscitationem corporum, verè secundum animas vivunt cum Christo.

Et hanc sanè interpretationem obscurissimi loci hujus Apocalyptici, analogiæ fidei consentaneam, & sibi maximè constantem, hac vice amplectimur: rectiora monstrantibus haud morosius reluctaturi. Et sic initium Millenarii hujus, de quo quæritur, ponimus in Annum Christi 300. quo Constantinus M. Imp. finem persecutionibus antegressis, & hactenus Ecclcsiam durissimè prementibus, imposuit. Complementum autem ejus, sive finem in Annum Christi 1300. quo imperium Turcicum robur suum acquisivit, & infestæ illæ gentes, Gog & Magog, nempe Turcæ, Tartari, Moscovitæ: unà cum Antichristo Romano, adversus Ecclefiam horribiliter sævire cœperunt: ita ut tùm verè Diabolus, catenis, quibus millenario præcedenti ligatus, h. e. divinâ virtute represfus ac cohibitus fuerat, jam ruptis, solutisque in Ecclesia grassari visus fuerit.

His ita constitutis, planum jam fit, quibus Sophisticationibus Chiliaftæ tùm veteres, tùm recentiores, locum Apocalypticum depravare studeant. Nam 1. Resurrectionem illam primam accipiunt de speciali resurrectione solorum electorum, & de carnali illâ constitutione Regni Christi hisce in terris à solis Sanctis possidendi: id quod cum Scripturâ universâ, & analogiâ fidei è diametro pugnat. 2. Fœlicitatem millenarii illius falsò accipiunt de externo & mundano dominatu super Reges, Principes, & Gentes universas: de quo sane dominatu textus Apocalypticus ne γρῦ quidem habet. 3. Vim inferunt textui, quando somniant, expleto illo millenario, se cum Christo statim in cœlum translatum, & tùm judicium universale super vivos & mortuos institutum iri. Reclamat Textus, qui post millenarium illum Diaboli rursus solvendum, & plurimos ab ipso seductû iri perspicue affirmat, v. 7. 4. & postremò depravant, & mutilant textum, qui ostendit, millenarium illum secuturum tempus licèt modicum depressionis & afflictionis Sanctorum: de quo nihil habent, aut noverunt Chiliastæ, & fic textum Apocalypticum truncatè ad suum delirium detorquent. Proinde fanaticis istis missis, Analogiæ fidei, & interpretationi cum eâ consentienti omninò subscrimus.

Sunt quidem interpretes alii, qui initium hujus millenarii ab excisione Hierosolimitanâ petunt: finem autem ejus collocant in annum Christi 1073. ubi Gregorius VII. Pontifex, vulgò Hildebrandus, vel potiùs Hellenbrandt dictus, furiis infernalibus agitatus, adversus Monarchiam Romanam ita sævire ac tumultuari cœpit, ut sub ejus Pontificatu Satanas quoque vinculis omnibus solutus, & de carcere suo liberatus fuisse, videri potuerit. Verùm quò minùs Supputationi huic subscribamus, obstat perpetua illa, & atrocissima persecutio Ecclesiæ, quâ Imperatores Ethnici per illud spatium adversus regnum Christi insatiabili furore æstuarunt ac sævierunt: ita ut ante annum 300. Christi, vix unquam Ecclesiæ DEI respirare licuerit, tantùm abest, ut isto tempore Satanam catenis ligatum, & carceri inclusum fuisse, statuere queamus.

B. Lutherus, & alii initium hujus millenarii constituunt à tempore scripti hujus libri Apocalyptici, & factæ hujus visionis, complementum verò in prima initia regni Turcici: ita ut Christiani interea temporis sub ipsius etiam Imperatoribus Ethnicis manserint & regnarint, invito licèt Diabolo. Verùm laborat hæc quoqve sententia eâdem incommoditate, qvâ præcedens proxima. Sed si maximè his etiam, vel consimilibus aliis interpretationibus loc9 relinquatur, nulla tamen earum somnium hoc novelorū Enthusiastarum, de terreno Christi regno, mille annis duraturo, confirmat : qvin omnes potiùs funditùs illud subruunt & evertunt. Et hæc de priore istorum errore sufficiant.

Est verò ejusdem vanitatis, & prodigiosæ cæcitatis alter etiam error, qvo externam regnorum hujus mundi possessionem, excisis, funditùsq; deletis Imperatoribus, Regibus, Principibus, ac Magistratibus universis, sibi, suisqve suaviter pollicentur. Qva in parte Anabaptistarum profligatissimæ societati (licet strenuè id negare ausint) suffragantur, qvi tertium locum in classe errantium occupant: de qvo seqvitur.


### On the Quality, Form, and Condition of the Kingdom of Christ: The Error of the Anabaptists concerning the Kingdom of Christ

Among the remaining errors which the Anabaptists cherish, this one is by no means the last, which they have concocted concerning an external and worldly Kingdom of Christ, and concerning the possession of the kingdoms of this world, and the community of all goods, fixing the seat of this Kingdom at Münster in Westphalia. For when, for the defense of their Anabaptist error, the leaders of these men were ordered to descend into the arena of disputation in the year 1534, in which they were to contend with the party of our theologians from the foundations of Holy Scripture alone, and were now to publicly assert their laws, which they had enacted concerning the community of things and concerning a new form of Magistrates and judgments: they, having rejected this condition, labored for the protection of establishing some kingdom, from which they might defend their furies by force and arms. Now when that seat of the Anabaptist kingdom, namely Münster in Westphalia, had been surrounded by a siege by some orders of the Empire: during the siege, the Anabaptists brought to light a book, the title of which was inscribed RESTITUTIO, in which, among other things, they profess that the condition of the Kingdom of Christ before the last day will be such in this age, that the pious and the elect alone shall reign: with the impious having been everywhere routed and utterly destroyed by them. To this paradox they added other things no less fanatical and impious: namely, that it is lawful for subjects to abrogate all political magistrates: that it is permitted for ministers of the Church to take the power of the sword to themselves, and to constitute a new Republic by armed force: that no one is to be tolerated in the Church unless he is truly a Christian: that all the pious must live in a promiscuous community of all faculties: And speaking summarily, they referred all the benefits of total Christian liberty to external things, to the abrogation of the distinction of dominions, to the removal of public rights, and finally to the designation of the lust for any crimes whatsoever: that is, they imagined such a kingdom of Christ, which was entirely the kingdom of Satan. Since the refutations of these furies, however old-womanish and futile they may be, have been made by Philipp [Melanchthon], Justus Menius, and Urbanus Rhegius in public writings and are openly available: we shall not undertake the refutation of all of them expressly. However, we oppose two arguments to this impiety that are clearly invincible and irrefutable. 1. The Kingdom of Christ in these lands is nothing but Spiritual. Therefore, it is heretical and diametrically opposed to the Scriptures, whatever the fanatics dream about an external and worldly Kingdom. We proved the antecedent in the first part of the theological [treatise]. THE OTHER. The Kingdom of Christ will never consist of only the Elect and Saints in this world, but always of both good and evil. Therefore, it is heretical and diametrically opposed to the Scriptures, whatever the fanatics imagine about a Kingdom of Christ constituted of only Saints and Elect in these lands. The Savior himself confirms the antecedent in Matthew 13 throughout almost the whole chapter, and Luke 8, v. 4 and following. What? That the same Savior, when the servants desired to eradicate the tares, seriously forbids them to do this: but to permit both, both the wheat and the tares, to grow until the Son of Man sends his Angels, and they gather out of his KINGDOM all stumbling blocks, and those who do iniquity, Matthew 13, v. 28 and 41. And although according to the surface of the letter, Scripture seems to hint that there will be no impious persons in the Kingdom of Christ, but only those who are written in the life of Jerusalem, Isaiah 4, verse 3; likewise that no polluted or uncircumcised ones will pass through Jerusalem; but those clothed in garments of glory, Isaiah 35, v. 8 and chapter 52, v. 1. Ezekiel 44, v. 9; nevertheless, these and other sayings of that kind, partly (according to the subject matter) look to the state of the future heavenly Jerusalem, namely eternal life: but partly they denote by synecdoche the nobler part of the Church, namely the invisible assembly of the Elect: who are clean and unpolluted, both imputatively and inchoatively: as was expressly shown in the article concerning the Holiness of the Church.

Latin:

INter reliqvos errores, qvos Anabaptistæ fovent, minimè est postremus iste, qvem de Regno Christi externo & mundano, deqve possessione regnorum hujus mundi, bonorumq; omnium communione confinxerunt, Regni hujus sedem figentes Monasterii in Westphalia. Nam cùm pro defensione erroris sui Anabaptistici, primores istorum juberentur descendere in aream disputationis, Anno 1534. in qvâ ex solis Sacræ Scripturæ fundamentis, cum nostratium Theologorum parte confligerent, & leges suas, qvas de communione rerum, deqve novâ formâ Magistratuum & judiciorum tulerant, nunc publicè assererent: illi conditione hac repudiatâ, ad regni alicujus constituendi præsidium elaborarunt, ex qvo per vim & arma suos surores defenderent. Jam cum sedes illa regni Anabaptistici, nempè Monasterium Westphaliæ, à nonnullis Imperii ordinibus obsidione cincta esset: durante obsidione, Anabaptistæ librum, cui titulus erat inscriptus, RESTITUTIO, in lucem emittunt, in qvo inter alia profitentur, Regni Christi ante diem novissimam, hanc futuram esse in hoc seculo conditionem, ut pii & electi soli regnent: impiis per eosdem ubiq; profligatis, & omninò deletis. Cui paradoxo subjunxerunt & alia haud minùs fanatica, & impia: nempe fas esse subditis, magistratus politicos omnes abrogare: Ecclesiæ ministris licitum esse, Jus gladii sibi sumere, & per vim armatam novam Remp.constituere: in Ecclesiâ neminem, nisi reverâ Christianum, esse tolerandum: piis omnibus in promiscuâ facultatum omnium communione vivendum esse: Et summatim loqvendo, totius libertatis Christianæ beneficia omnia, ad res externas, ad distinctionem dominiorū abrogandam, ad tollenda jura publica, ad designandam deniq; quorumvis flagitiorum libidinem refere bant: hoc est, tale regnum Christi fingebant, quod prorsus erat regnum Satanæ. Horum furorum, qvantumvis anilium ac futilium refutationes, à Philippo, Justo Menio, Urbano Regio, publicis scriptis factæ, cùm palàm prostent: Nos omnium illorum refutationem ex professo non suscipiemus. Duo autem isthæc impietati huic opponimus invicta planè & ἀνάλυτα argumenta. 1. Regnum Christi hisce in terris non est nisi Spirituale. Hæreticum Ergò, & Scripturis ἀντιφατικῶς oppositum, qvicqvid de externo & mundano Regno fanatici somniant. Antecedens evicimus parte priore 9ελική. ALTERUM. Regnum Christi non ex solis Electis & Sanctis hoc in mundo unqvam constabit, sed semper ex bonis & malis. Hæreticum Ergo, & Scripturis ἀντιφατικῶς oppositum, qvicqvid de Regno Christi ex solis Sanctis & Electis, hisce in terris, constituto, fingunt fanatici. Antecedens confirmat Servator ipse Matth. 13. per totum fermè caput, & Luc.8. v. 4. & seqq. Qvid? qvòd idem Servator, servis cupientibus eradicare zizania, seriò interdicit, ne hoc faciant: sed permittant utraqve, & triticum, & zizania crescere, usqvedū Filius Hominis mittat Angelos suos, & colligant è REGNO suo omnia offendicula, & eos, qvi faciunt iniqvitatem, Matth. 13. v. 28. & 41. Et qvanqvam secundum superficiem literæ, Scriptura innuere videtur, in Regno Christi nullos fore impios, sed eos tantùm, qvi scripti sunt in vita Jerusalem, Esa. 4. vers. 3. nullos item pollutos, aut incircumcisos pertransituros Ierusalem; sed indutos vestimentis gloriæ, Esa. 35. v. 8. & cap. 52. v. 1. Ezech. 44. v. 9. hæc tamen, & id genus alia dicta, partim (pro subjecta materia) respiciunt statum futuræ cœlestis Hierosolymæ, nempe vitæ æternæ:partim verò Synecdochicè nobiliorem partem Ecclesiæ, invisibilem nimirùm Electorum cœtum notant: qvi mundi & impolluti sunt, tùm imputativè, tùm inchoativè: uti in articulo de Sanctitate Ecclesiæ ex professo fuit ostensum.


### On the Quality, Form, and Condition of the Kingdom of Christ: V. The Error of the Calvinists concerning the Kingdom of Christ

The Romanists err very gravely while they imagine a monarchical government of the Church in these lands, and one visible head and judge of the same, by whom the whole and universal Church may be governed, and individual controversies arising concerning religion may be examined, judged, and settled. The chief foundation of which error Bellarmine and his associates seek from the best form of government in politics, and the conformity of ecclesiastical and political government, Bellar. Contr. 2. Colloq. Ratisb. Sess. 9. But the vanity of this fiction is evident in many ways. For 1. not whatever is best in politics is immediately also the best in ecclesiastical government. For there are many things in civil polity that are best, which are not even lawful in the Church: for example, to coerce a criminal by external force: Matth. 13. v. 4. & cap. 26. v. 52. 2. And to administer a polity, that is to reign. But to administer the Church is not to reign, but to serve. 3. Furthermore, whatever is said of a kingdom can never be rightly said of the Church. 4. Christ himself administers his Church here on earth monarchically, which could be done by no other man, not even by the Apostle Peter, since one man does not suffice to administer the whole Church dispersed throughout the whole world. 5. It is forbidden that any of the ministers of the Church should lord it over others. 6. The Apostle in Ephes. 4. & 1. Cor. 12., in the description of the whole ecclesiastical hierarchy, made no mention of a monarchical one, when he expressed the manner of our conjunction with Christ. 7. Not all things to one: but to individual members of the Church some portion has been given. 8. All ministers of the Church were sent by Christ, not in a different, but in one and the same manner. 9. Not even the whole world is governed by one external king and visible head in secular matters: so that it is least of all possible for this to be done in the Church on account of the complexity and abundance of cases.
