The same Abimelech, King of the Philistines, afterwards struck a covenant for the same reason with Isaac, the son of Abraham, both sides binding themselves by an oath to perform their faith and to cultivate public peace. Gen. 26. 28. and following.

Such a covenant Laban, certainly an idolater, the son of Bethuel, when he had overtaken Jacob, the pious and faithful, his son-in-law, fleeing on Mount Gilead, being prohibited by GOD from being able to harm him, struck with him concerning not offending. Gen. 31. 44. Those who defend the deniers in this matter also raise objections here, contending that these covenants of the saints were of fact, not of right: and because those very saints sometimes lapsed, it is more likely that GOD indeed dispensed in this matter: but in the meantime they ought to have obeyed the divine edicts, by which it was prohibited to join covenants with the impious and men of a different religion. Exod. 23. 32. and ch. 34. 12. & 15. Deut. 7. 2. & 3. Which precepts Joshua indeed thought were to be observed so holily by him, that he would not wish to enter into a covenant with the inhabitants of the land of Canaan, being indeed infidels: although they vehemently solicited it.

Latin:

Talis fides, spes ac fiducia si nobis quoq; firma esset, & non plus confiderem9 hominibus, quàm DEO, nunquàm profectò Ecclesiæ & Religionis causam, vel manifestè impiis, vel diversæ religionis hominibus, tuendam committeremus. Tertium medium, præmissis duobus præcedentibus, nobis omninò est relictũ, ut si necessitas ipsa ferat, vel soli, vel adhibitis in Religione fratribus, sine alieno auxilio, cõjunctis viribus fortiter, & intrepido animo præliemur adversus eos, qui per vim ac tyrannidem, nobis libertatem Religionis, contra omnia jura, sacra ac profana eripere conantur, quam per Dei gratia honestis mediis acquisivimus, legitimis medijs hactenus asseruimus. Quo casu fratrum auxilia implorare illicitum non fuerit. Ubi sane qui nostrae Religioni sunt ὁμόψηφοι difficiles se nunquam praestabunt: Fratrum enim pericula ducere pro suis, postulat fraternum officium, & Charitatis regula, a Christo ipso expressa: Quae vultis, ut faciant vobis homines, facite idem & ipsis. Tale fuit foedus Joabi, cum fratre Abisæo: 2. Sam. 10. 11 & 12. Si praevaluerint adversum me Syri, eris mihi auxilio: Si autem filij Ammon praevaluerint adversum te auxiliabor tibi. Esto vir fortis, & pugnemus pro populo nostro, & civitate DEI nostri: Dominus autem faciet quod bonum est in conspectu suo. Et talia mutua fratrum auxilia usque adeo DEO placent, ut Ephraimitas non accuset modo perfidiae, sed & caedi permittat, eo quod Jephthen pugnantem contra Ammonitas deseruisseut Judic. 12. 2. 4. & sequentibus. Sic Jabesenses excidio plectuntur, eo quod in tali foedere cotra Benjamitas deseruissent Israelem. Judic. 21. 8. & 10. Quarto Stratagemata hoc casu (modo sine violatione pactorum, si qua intercesserunt, id fiat) non sunt prohibita: ut si forte hostes honesta aliqua ratione inter se committi, & in mutua praelia dividi queant, illud non intermittatur: Sic enim vel utraqs, vel altera certe pars facilius vinci & expugnari potest. Talia enim Stratagemata nihil sunt aliud, quam media, quae Deus ipse in commodum Ecclesiae suae monstrat, & pars sunt prudentiae civilis.

Jam vero fides Christiana, & Prudentia politica se mutuo non tollunt, multo minus Conscientiam fidelium laedunt. Est vero in hujusmodi etiam foederibus, inter fratres, & in Religione ὁμοψήφους initis, magna cautione & circumspectione opus. 1. quidem, ne nimis generaliter, & sine omni exceptione in quibusvis casibus, frater fratri promittat auxiliu & defensionem: sed justoru maxime, ac summe necessarioru bellorum exprimatur, & servetur conditio. 2. Ne caeco impetu & temere: sed sanis & communicatis consiliis omnia fiant. Quam ad rem, & Theologica, & Civili prudentia opus est. 3 Ut in foederibus istis, inter fratres, & in Religione socios contractis, non confidamus, sed a solo DOMINO speremus & petamus auxilium, haud minus, ac si nulla prorsus externa nobis parata essent praesidia. 4. Ut versemur tantum in terminis defensivis, neque ex curiositate & temeritate bellum non necessarium moveamus hostib9 religionis nostrae etiam infensissimis. 5. Ut foedera cum fratribus etiam nostris inita, certis ac justis conditionibus utrinque firmentur, ne postmodum (quod fieri solet saepissime) ex confoederatorum mutabilitate & inconstantia, novum periculum atque incommodum nobis sit extimescendum. Quo respiciens nunquam satis laudatus Elector Saxoniae FRIDERICUS cognomento Sapiens, ab aliis Principibus, in Religione sociis & fratribus, ad societatem foederum solicitatus, respondiffe legitur: Foedera quidem bona sunt, sed Va illa servantibus: innuens eam piorum saepius esse infirmitatem, eam ingeniornm,volunta tum,consiliorum varietatem, mutabilitatem, & dissimilitudinem,ut plerumque vel optima Unio,ac confoederatio in societatem leoninam degeneret: altera parte, vel praeter spem deserta, vel multis difficultatibus implicita, vel plane oppressa. 6. & postremo:Ut sub nullo praetextu Impiis, & diversae Religioni addictis,in primo hoc foederum genere,locus ullus relinquatur. Alias finis & Catastrophe diversarum partium, & confoederationum nulla expectanda alia, quam quae sub Judaeorum confoederatione cum Aegyptiis admodum graphice describitur: Jesaiae 31. a versu 1 ad 4. usque: Va, qui descendunt in Aegyptum ad auxilium, sperantes in equis, & habentes fiduciam in quadrigis, quod multae sunt: & in equitibus, quod fortes sunt nimis: & non posuerunt fiduciam in Sanctum Israel, & DOMINUM non requisiverunt. Ipse autem sapiens adduxit malum,& verba sua non abstulit: & consurget contra domum pessimorum, & contra auxilium operantium iniquitatem. Aegyptus homo, & non DEUS: & equi eorum, Caro & non Spiritus: & DOMINUS extendet manum suam, & corruet auxiliator, & cadet, cui praestatur auxilium, simulq; omnes consumentur. Sed de primo hoc foederum genere isthæc sufficiant.

navigationum, itinerum, deq; similibus ad conservandam civilem societatem pertinentibus, contracta, nihil sunt aliud,quam nervi & vincula Pacis publicae. Ergo foedera etiam hujusmodi suo calculo approbat Apostolus:ita ut ne quidem hostibus nostris malum pro malo reddi velit, privato nimirum ausu & arbitrio: vel caeco quodam impetu, aut stulta temeritate, capite eodem 12.17. Quo pertinet etiam admonitio Epistolae ad Hebraeos, cap. 12.14. Pacem sectamini cum omnibus. Neque vero prima haec probatio ideo nervo & evidentia caret, quia ad privatos ista scripserunt Apostoli. Certum enim est, praecepta ac regulas Christianae Charitatis, non ad certa tantum quaedam individua: sed ad universam genus fidelium sive Christianorum pertinere. Et sane vult Apostolus Pacis hoc studium erga omnes, Christianis esse commendatissimum,ita ut nihil quicquam adversus illud designent:id quod evincit geminus ille προσδιορισμὸς: εἰ δυνατὸν, si fieri potest, & si pacem ab infidelibus impetrare potestis. 2. τὸ ἐξ ὑμῶν Quantum in vobis situm est.

Deinde confirmant Affirmativam nostram exemplaSanctorum,qui sic urgente necessitate, foedera cnm infidelibus, & diversae Religionis hominibus percusserunt. Abrahamus certe pater ille credentium foedus iniit cum Amorrhaeo sive Cananaeo, nempe cum Mambre, Escole, & Anere contra Reges Orientales, sive Persas, qui Sodomitis bellum moverant, & Lothum cum familia captivu abduxerant. Gen. 14.13. Quanquam vero non defunt,praecipue ex recentioribus interpretibus, qui foederibus istis cum infidelibus contractis, suum calculum addere recusant, & contendunt, Exemplum Abrahami nihil ad rem facere, eo quod viri isti, sive Principes Sodomita, Mambre, Escol, & Aner, facti prius sint fideles, & Abrahami religioni se adjunxerint, quam in societatem foederis admitterentur: Tamen quod dicunt isti, non probant,neque ex historiis sacris aut prophanis unquam probabunt: Quin potius circumstantiae textus Mosaici haud obscure innuunt, Abrahamum ab incolis loci illius, hominibus infidelibus, rogatum & invitatum fuisse ad foederis pactionem: in quam Abrahamus non obstante Religionis diversitate consenserit, partim ne ipse quoque pro hoste haberetur,partim veroLothum jam captivum adductum tanto facilius liberare posset, qui alias cum suis domesticis profligandae regum Orientalium tyrannidi non solus sufficeret. Sed si maxime concederetur, quod illi excipiunt hoc loco, plura tamen hujus rei exempla sunt in promtu longe evidentissina.

ALTERUM foederum Genus diximus supra esse mere Politicum, ac Objecti loco tantum spectare pacem publicam, & tranquillitatem civilem. De hoc quaeritur: An Christiani,sic urgente necessitate, vel cum impiis ac plane infidelibus, vel cum diversae Religionis hominibus, Foedera Pacis, (non Religionis, sed publicae ac civilis) salva Conscientia inire possint? Nos freti & Scripturaru, & Sanctorum Patriarcharum ac Regum autoritate, respondemus affirmate: idque sic probamus:

1. Quicquid salva Conscientia, & sine jactura Religionis praestare licet: illud utiq; mediante transactione foederali pacisci etiam licet. Atqui pacem publicam ac communem praestare ac colere debent fideles,cum omnibus hominibus: & cum primis Magistratus pij officium est,subditorum jura ac privilegia ita asserere, ut Civilis societas, & qua hujus sunt vincula & nervi,contractus,navigationes,mercimonia, & id genus alia libere & tuto exerceri possint. Ergo hoc ipsum,mediante etiam transactione foederali, pacisci licet cum omnibus hominibus.

Affumtionem probo ex cap.12.18. ad Romanos: Si fieri potest,quantum in vobis est, cum omnibus hominibus pacem colite. Romani certe fideles,temporeApostoli Pauli vivebant inter Ethnicos: Hoc tamen non obstante, cum his quoque pacem coli vult Apostolus. Jam foedera hujusmodi de tuendis finibus terra mariq;, de securitate possessionum, contractuum,

Idem certeAbrahamus in Palaestina habitans, & opibus plurimum auctus,cu Abimelecho rege Geraroru, homine certe infideli, & cum Phicole archistratego, vel, ut alij volunt, Cancellario ejusdem regis, fœdus junxit, jure jurando interposito, de non lædendo se mutuò. Finis ergo fœderis istius erat Pax communis & publica. Genes. 21. 22. 27 & 32. Idem Abimelechus Rex Palestinus, postea cum Isaaco Abrahami filio, eandem ob causam fœdus percussit, utrinq; jure jurando ad præstandam fidem, & colendam pacem publicam se obstringentes. Gens. 26. 28. & sequentibus.

Tale fœdus Laban certè Idololatra Bathuelis filius, cùm Jacobum pium ac fidelem, generum suum, fugientem in monte Galaad, assecutus esset, à DEO prohibitus, ne illi nocere posset, fœdus cum eo percussit de non offendendo. Gen. 31. 44. Obstrepunt & hoc loco, qui Negantem hac in parte tuentur, contendent, Fœdera isthæc Sanctorum facti esse, non juris: & quia illi ipsi Sancti interdum lapsi sint, verisimilius esse, DEUM quidem hac in parte dispensasse: sed interim debuisse ipsos edicta divina obtemperare, quibus fœdera cum impiis, & diversæ religionis hominibus jungere, prohibitum erat. Exod. 23. 32. & cap. 34. 12. & 15. Deut. 7. 2. & 3. Quæ sanè præcepta Josua ita sanctè observanda sibi esse duxerit, ut nollet usum inire fœdus cum incolis terræ Canaan, quippe infidelibus: licet illud vehementer sollicitarent.


### Chapter Two. Concerning Christian Consolation, both general and special, in any…: Concerning the Treaties of Christians (continued)

I answer that this argument is devoid of every probable nerve at least, let alone concluding anything certain. For 1. what they say about divine dispensation, they cannot prove from the text, indeed not even from the entire sacred code, regarding the present question. 2. We do not deny that the saints also lapsed more often: but that they lapsed in making these covenants with the impious, that is not yet proven. Therefore, the principle is begged. 3. No one has ever denied that the saints are also obligated to perform obedience to divine mandates. But there are no qualities of a non-entity: And as the Apostle has it, Rom. 4. 15. Where there is no law, there is no transgression. Now that mandate, concerning not entering into a covenant with the impious, had not yet been promulgated in the times of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. 4. Let us also concede that: Although this law had not yet been promulgated: GOD nevertheless wished some distinction to appear between His people and the infidels, not only regarding worship, but also regarding external conversation: yet nothing on that account departs from our affirmative. Since cases of necessity, and impending dangers, require far different counsels and means of maintaining public peace than those which are wont to be entered into otherwise when affairs flow according to our will. 5. Those mandates of GOD also, concerning not striking covenants with impious men, were not universal with respect to all the impious and the faithful: but were directed solely to certain peoples, namely the inhabitants of the land of Canaan. For GOD, by a singular counsel, simply wished these to be destroyed and cut off. But the consequence from the singular to the universal is not valid. 6. If this divine prohibition were to be taken so generally: certainly not only would no confederation be to be entered into with infidels: but it would not even be permitted to dwell with them, and among them. For the same prohibition wished that the Jews should not bear such infidels in their midst. But this was clearly impossible afterwards under the Kings, and especially under the first foundation of the Church of the New Testament. 7. That prohibition was conditional: so that such confederations might not yield to a snare for the Jews, who were indeed most prone and inclined to idolatry. 8. That prohibition pertained to the Mosaic forensic law, which can in no way obligate us today. Since now under the New Testament the middle wall of partition between the Jews and the Gentiles has been taken away, and the wall broken down. Eph. 2. 14. Col. 3. 11. 9. Indeed, from the very intention of GOD, it ought to have lasted at least for a time, namely until the Canaanites had been thoroughly cut off, being indeed singularly cursed by GOD.

The pious Jewish kings acknowledged this, especially David and Solomon; who are read to have entered into such covenants with King Hiram, so that voyages to Tarshish and other political commerce of that kind could be safely instituted and exercised on both sides: as one may read, 1 Kings 5. 1. and following, 2 Sam. 5. 11, 1 Chron. 14. 1. If the later Kings of Judah and Israel had kept themselves within these merely political bounds, they would never have been reproved on account of covenants contracted with the impious.

We seek the third argument of our affirmative from the fact that GOD Himself wished such political covenants, confirmed by an oath, to be holily kept, and most severely punished their violation.

The Gibeonites, formerly Hivites, when they saw the successors of Joshua in subduing enemies, and by the command of GOD, to be destroyed to extermination, in order to provide for their own lives, circumvented Joshua with wondrous cunning, so that he might enter into a covenant with them, without consulting the LORD, as if they were a most remote people, Josh. 9. 3. and following. That covenant and oath was certainly vicious in many ways. For 1. it was extorted by deceit. 2. against the command of the LORD. 3. without the will and consent of the same. 4. without the consent of the people. 5. performed to Gentiles and absolute infidels. But Joshua, even when the deceit was known, and the people complaining, wished this covenant to be holy, and answered the people murmuring on this account fearlessly: We have sworn to them in the name of the LORD GOD of Israel, and therefore we cannot kill them. Josh. 9. 19. What? That he not only never moved his own hand against them: but also when they were sought by five kings of the Amorites with war and arms, mindful of the covenant once entered into with the Gibeonites, by sending auxiliary troops, he rendered them free and immune from the violence of the enemies: holding the religion of the oath so holy, however much it was performed to men of a different, indeed clearly Gentile, religion. Josh. 10. 5. and following. Indeed, GOD Himself so ratified this oath in the heavens, that, when a whole century later, King Saul, intending to show favor to the Judeans and Israelites, broke the bond of the covenant and attempted to destroy the Gibeonites to the point of extermination: [God] punished that treachery most severely with a three-year famine, even though Saul was already dead: and when asked through an oracle, He replied that there would be no end to the punishment until the crime committed by Saul against the Gibeonites was expiated. Whence David, at the request of the Gibeonites, handed over seven of Saul's surviving male descendants, whom they hanged at Gibeon on the mountain before the LORD. Which having been done at last, the punishment for the treachery ceased. 2 Sam. 21. 1. and following.

Thus the most pious Kings of the ancient people not only entered into covenants and peace treaties with men of the most diverse religions, but also kept them most firmly once entered into: as David with Toi, King of Hamath, 2 Sam. 8. 9, with the Kings of Syria and the Ammonites, 2 Sam. 10. 19, Solomon with Pharaoh, King of Egypt, 1 Kings 3. 1, with Hiram, King of Tyre, 1 Kings 5. 12, Asa, King of Judah, with Benhadad, King of Syria. 1 Kings 15. 18.

Nor is it an objection that it is not rarely read in the Prophets that GOD was gravely angry with His people on account of covenants contracted with infidels. For by observing the distinction between that which is of the substance itself and a vicious accident, this objection is most correctly solved. For covenants contracted with the impious are not condemned in themselves, but accidentally: partly because the Judeans trusted more in covenants than in the help of GOD: partly because they did not contain themselves within merely political bounds, but also participated in the religion, or rather the impiety, of their confederates: partly because they relied on the aid of their confederates in an unjust cause. In this way, Ahaz was rightly rebuked, who, to gain the favor of the King of Syria, erected an altar in the Jerusalem temple similar to the one in Damascus. 2 Kings 16. 10. and following. 2 Chron. 28. 22. and following. And Solomon, when, seduced by the company of foreign women, he worshipped foreign gods: 1 Kings 11. 4. and following, when Ahab, out of excessive love for his infidel wives, built an altar to Baal and planted a grove in Samaria. 1 Kings 16. 31. and following, and chap. 20. 34. and following. Thus Jehoshaphat is gravely censured on account of the covenant contracted with the impious King Ahaziah, in that he was a participant in his most impious works. 2 Chron. 20. 37. To which pertains that sharp rebuke in Isa. 5. 18: Woe to you who are bound with cords of iniquity, to do evil. To this is added that among the Judeans, in the making of covenants, private πλεονεξία (greed) often carried more weight than regard for the public utility, as well as deceit, ambition, exalting oneself above one's partners, infidelity in deserting others against one's given word, and similar vices, which, where they are present either singly or in some combination, covenants can neither please GOD nor be lasting or happy. Such was the covenant of Jehoshaphat with the impious King Ahab. 1 Kings 23. But above all, those covenants are an abomination to GOD in which trust is placed: Whence in Hosea 12. 1, concerning the Ephraimites, the Prophet says that they feed on the East wind and multiply lies and desolation, trusting in the covenant entered into with the Assyrians: To which pertain also other threats of the Prophets, such as exists in Isa. 30. 2 and 7: Woe to you who take counsel, and not from me: who weave a web, and not by my Spirit; that you might add sin upon sin; who walk to go down into Egypt, and have not asked at my mouth, hoping for help in the strength of Pharaoh, and having TRUST in the hand of Egypt. And the strength of Pharaoh shall be to your confusion, and the trust in the shadow of Egypt to your ignominy: for Egypt shall help in vain and to no purpose: therefore I have cried out concerning this: It is only pride, be still.

Such threats exist also in Isa. 31. 2 and 3. Jer. 37. 5 and following.

And in these cases and conditions, we maintain that even today covenants entered into with the impious and with men of a different religion must be held as illicit, impious, and therefore unhappy, even if they are merely political.

But outside of those cases and vices which happen to covenants, if the contracting parties, and especially the faithful, keep themselves within legitimate bounds, it is so certain that there is no vice or impiety underlying them, that from the entire Holy Scripture not even a single point can be brought forward by which it could be demonstrated that merely political covenants legitimately contracted with infidels and men of a different religion, and justly observed, have displeased GOD. What is more? God Himself in Ezekiel 17, through almost the entire chapter, sharply rebukes the violation of an oath, even one given to impious confederates, in King Zedekiah, in that the covenant made was not of men, but of GOD Himself. After Jeconiah, King of Judah, had been led away captive to Babylon by the King of Babylon, the same Babylonian king appointed King Zedekiah in the place of Jeconiah, the uncle of Jeconiah, and entered into a covenant with him, with an oath of fidelity interposed. Where it was certainly just that Zedekiah, since he was reigning by another's favor, should render all duties of fidelity to the Babylonian. But he, having despised the sanctity of the oath, enters into a covenant with the King of Egypt, so that he might shake off the Babylonian yoke. Where Zedekiah certainly thought that he had violated a faith given only to a man, and indeed to an infidel man: nor did he esteem this matter of great moment: just as the perfidy of the great in making covenants is not infrequent: and too truly, and from the very use of things, someone pronounced: As boys play with dice, so Kings play with oaths: nevertheless, God confirms with a great asseveration of words that the covenant made void by Zedekiah was not of a man, but of GOD Himself: not only because Zedekiah had bound his faith to the Babylonian with an intervening oath: but also because this had been the judgment of the LORD, that the power of reigning should be taken away from the family of the Judean Kings. 2 Kings 25 and 17. 2 Chron. 36. 10 and 13. Jer. 37. 12 and ch. Ezek. 17. 13. 15. and following. Shall he, says God, prosper, or attain safety, who has done

Latin:

Respondeo, argumentum hoc omni probabili saltem nervo destitui, nedum certi quid concludere. Nam 1. de dispensatione divina quod dicunt, ex textu probare nõ possunt, imò ne quidem ex universo sacro codice, quo ad præsentem quæstionem. 2. Sanctos etiam sæpiùs lapsos esse, non negamus: sed quòd in ferendis istis fœderibus cum impiis lapsi sint, id nondum probatum. Petitur ergò principium. 3. Sanctos ad obedientiam divinis mandatis prestãdã obligari etiam, nemo negavit unquã Sed non entis nullę sunt qualitates: Et ut Apostolus habet, Rom. 4. 15. Ubi non est lex, ibi nõ est prævaricatio. Jam mandatum illud, de non ineundo fœdere cum impiis, temporibus Abrahami, Isaaci, Jacobi, nondum promulgatũ fuerat. 4. Concedamus & illud, Licèt lex hæc nondum promulgata fuerit: DEUM tamen discrimen aliquod apparere voluisse inter suum populum, & infideles, non modò qua cultũ, sed & quoad externam Conversationem: nihil tamen propterea decedit nostræ Affirmativæ. Siquidem necessitatis casus, & impendentia pericula, longè alia requirunt consilia, & media tuendę pacis publicę quàm quę aliàs rebus ad voluntatem nostram fluentibus, iniri solent. 5. Mandata etiam illa DEI, de non pangendis fœderibus cum hominibꝫ impiis, nõ erant universalia respectu omnium impiorũ & fidelium: sed ad certos populos, nempe incolas terræ Canaan, unicè directa. Hos enim DEUS singulari consilio simpliciter volebat deletos & excisos. A singulari autem ad Universale nõ valet consequentia. 6. Si prohibitio hæc divina ita generaliter esset accipienda: certè non modò non cum infidelibus nulla esset ineunda confoederatio : sed & cum illis, & inter illos ne quidem habitare liceret. Nam eadem prohibitio volebat, ut Judæi, tales infideles in medio sui non ferrent. Atqui hoc postea sub Regibus, & cumprimis sub prima fundatione Ecclesiæ Novi Testamenti planè erat impossibile. 7. Prohibitio illa erat conditionata: ut ne Judæis, quippe ad idololatráam maximè pronis ac prochvibšs, ejusmodi confoederationes cederent in laqueum. 8. Prohibitio illa pertinebat ad legem Mosaicam forensem, quæ nos hodie obligare nullo modo potest. Siquidem jam sub Novo Testamento τό μεσότοιχον inter Judæos & gentes est sublatum, & maceria diruta. Ephe. 2. 14. Coloß. 3, 11. 9. Quin ex ipsa etiam intentione DEI, ad tempus saltem durare debuit, eò usque nimirum, donec Cananæi penitùs essent excisi, quippe à DEO singulariter maledicti.

Agnoverunt hoc pij reges Judaici, cumprimis David & Salomon; qui cum rege Hiramo talia foedera inijsse leguntur, ut navigationes in Tharsis, aliasq́; id genus politica commercia tutò utrinque institui, & exerceri possent: sicut legere licet, 1. Reg. 5, 1. & sequentibus, 2. Sam. 5, 11, 1. Paral. 14, 1. Intra quos terminos merè politicos si posteri Reges Juda & Israel se continuissent, nunquàm propter foedera cum impiis contracta, reprehensi fuissent.

TERTIUM affirmativæ nostræ argumentum petimus inde, quod Deus ipse fœdera hujusmodi politica, juramento confirmata, sanctè servari voluit, eorúmqué violationem severissimè punivit.

Gabaonitæ olim Hevæi, cum successumi Josuæ in subigendis hostibus, & ex DEI præcepto, ad internecionem delendis, viderent, ut vitæ suæ consulerent, mira calliditate Josuain circumvenerunt, ut foedus cum ipsis, inconsulto DOMINO, tanquàm cum remotissimis populis iniret, Jos. 9, 3. & sequentibus. Erat certè foedus & juramentum istud multis modis vitiosum. Nam 1. dolo erat extortum. 2. contra præceptum DOMINI. 3. citra voluntatem, & consensum ejusdem 4. citra consensum populi 5. Gentilibus, & prorsus infidelibus præstitum. Verùm Josua, dolo etiam cognito, & populo reclamante, foedus hoc sanctum esse voluit, & populo hoc nomine murmuranti intrepidè respondit: Juravimus eis in nomine DOMINI DEI Israel, & iccircò non possumus eos occidere. Jos. 9, 19. Quid? quòd non ipse modò manů adversů illos nunquàm movit: sed & cùm à quinq; Regibus Amorrhæorů, bello, armisq; peterentur, memor foederis semel cum Gabaonitis initi, missis copiis auxiliaribus, ab hostium vi liberos ac immunes ipsos præstitit: usque adeò sanctam ducens Juramenti religionem, quantumvis diversæ, imò planè Genntilitæ Religionis hominibo præstitam. Jos. 10, 5. & sequentibus. Quin imò DEUS ipse Juramentum hoc in cœlis ita ratum habuit, ut, cùm integro seculo pòst, Rex Saul Judæis & Israelitis gratificaturus, rupto fœderis vinculo, Gabaonitas, ad internecionem perdere conaretur: perfidiam istam, Saule etiam jam demortuo, triennali fame severissimè puniret: & rogatus per oraculum responderet, haud priùs pœnæ fore finem, quàm expiaretur Saulis facinus contra Gabaonitas admissum. Unde David, petentibus Gabaonitis, septem de Saulis familia superstites masculos tradidit, quos ipsi ad Gabaam in monte suspenderunt DOMINO. Quo demùm facto, perfidiæ pœna cessavit. 2. Sam. 21. 1. & sequentibus.

Sic piissimi Reges veteris populi, fœdera & pacificationes, cum diversissimarum Religionum hominibus non modò inierunt: sed & inita firmissimè servarunt: ut David cum Thoi rege Hemathæo, 2. Sam. 8. 9. cum Regibus Syriæ & Ammonitarum, 2. Sam. 10. 19. Salomo cum Pharaone Rege Ægypti, 1. Reg. 3. 1. cum Hiramo rege Tyri, 1. Reg. 5. 12. Asa Rex Juda cum Benhadado rege Syriæ. 1. Reg. 15. 18.

Neque obstat, quòd haud rarò DEUS apud Prophetas populo suo, ob fœdera cum infidelibus contracta, graviter succensuisse legitur. Nam observato discrimine inter id, quod est ipsius substantiæ, & vitiosi accidentis objectio isthæc rectissimè solvitur. Non enim reprehenduntur fœdera cum impiis contracta per se: sed per accidens: partim, quòd Judæi magis confidebant in fœderibus, quàm in auxilio DEI: partim, quòd inter terminos merè politicos se non continebant, sed & confœderatorum religione, potiùs impietate participabant: partim in causa injusta confœderatorum auxiliis nitebantur. Hoc pacto jure reprehendebatur Achatz, qui in gratiam confœderat Regis Syriæ erexit in templo Hierosolymitano altare Damasceno simile. 2. Reg. 16. 10. & seqq. 2. Paral. 28. 22. & seqq. Et Salomon, quando ex consortio alienigenarum seductus, DEos alienos coluit: 1. Reg. 11. 4. & seqq. quando Achab ex nimio amore infidelium uxorum, ædificavit altare Baal, & plantavit nemus in Samaria. 1. Reg. 16. 31. & seqq. & cap. 20. 34. & seqq. Sic graviter taxatur Josaphat, propter fœdus cum Ochozia impio rege contractu, eò quòd particeps esset operum ipsius impiissimorum. 2. Paral. 20. 37. Quò pertinet acris illa reprehensio Jes. 5. 18. Væ qui colligati estis funiculis iniquitatis, ad faciendum malum. Huc accedit, quod apud Judæos in pangendis fœderibus sæpiùs plus valebat πλεονεξία privata, quàm utilitatis publicæ respectus, item dolus, ambitio, extollens se supra socios, infidelitas deserens alios contra datam fidem, & similia vitia, quæ ubi vel singula, vel aliqua adsunt, fœdera neque DEO placere, neq; diuturna aut felicia esse possunt. Quale fuit fœdus Josaphati cum impio rege Achab. 1. Reg. 23. Cumprimis autem DEO abominatio sunt ea fœdera, in quibus fiducia collocatur: Unde Oseæ 12. 1. de Ephraimitis, mitis, confidentibus in fœdere cum Assyriis inito, dicit Propheta, quòd pascantur vento Orientali, & multiplicent mendacium & vastitatem: Quo pertinent & aliæ comminationes Prophetarum, qualis extat, Jesa. 30 2 & 7. Væ, qui facitis consilium, & non ex me: ordinatis telam, & non per Spiritum meum; ut adderetis peccatum super peccatum; qui ambulatis, ut descendatis in Ægyptum, & os meum non interrogastis, sperantes auxilium in fortitudine Pharaonis, & habentes FIDUCIAM in manu Ægypti. Et erit vobis fortitudo Pharaonis in confusionem, & fiducia umbræ Ægypti in ignominiam: Ægyptus enim frustrà & vanè auxiliabitur: ideò clamavi super hoc: Superbia tantùm est, quiesce.

Quales comminationes extant etiam Jesa. 31. 2. & 3. Jerem. 37. 5. & sequentibus.

Et his quidem casibus & conditionibus hodieq; fœdera cum impiis, ac diversæ religionis hominibus inita, pro illicitis, impiis, ac proinde infelicibus habenda esse, si maximè merè sint politica, omninò statuimus.

Cæterùm extra istos casus & vitia, quæ fœderibus accidunt, si intra terminos legitimos contrahentes, & præsertim fideles se contineant, nihil vitij aut impietatis illis subesse, usq; adeò certum est, ut ex universa Scriptura Sacra, ne unicus quidem apex proferri queat, quo demonftrari possit, Fœdera mere politica cùm infidelibus, & diversæ Religionis hominibus legitimè contracta, & juste observata, DEO displicuisse. Quid? quòd Deus ipse Jezechiel. 17. per totum fermè caput violationem juramenti, impiis etiam confœderatis præstiti, in rege Zedekia acriter reprehendit, eò, quòd non hominum, sed ipsius DEI fœdus factum sit irritum. Postquam Rex Juda Jechonias à Rege Babylonis captivus abductus fuerat in Babylon,idem rex Babylonius in locum Jechoniæ constituit Regem Sedechiam; patruum Jechoniæ, cumque ipso fœdus iniit, fidelitatis juramento interposito. Ubi sanè æquum erat, Sedechiam, quippe alieno beneficio regnantem,omnia fidelitatis obsequiaBabylonio præstare Verùm ipse comtemta juramenti religione, fœdus init cum rege Ægypti, ut jugum Babylonicum excuteret. Ubi sanè Sedechias existimavit, se homini tantùm, & quidem homini infideli fidem datam violasse: neque hanc rem magni momenti æstimabat: quemadmodum haud infrequens est Magnatum in fœderibus pangendis perfidia: & nimis verè, atque ex ipso rerum usu quidam pronunciavit; Ut pueri talis ludunt, ita Reges ludere juramentis: tamen Deus magna verborum asseveratione confirmat, à Zedechia irritum factum esse fœd?, non hominis, sed ipsius DEI: non modò quia interveniente juramento fidem suam Babylonio Zedechias adstrinxerat: sed etiam, quia DOMINI hoc fuerat judicium, ut regnandi potestas à JudaicorumRegum familia auferetur. 2. Reg. 25. & 17. 2. Paral. 36. 10. & 13. Jerem. 37. 12. & c. Jezech. 17. 13. 15. & sequentibus. Numquid, inquit Deus, prosperabitur, vel consequenter salutē, qui fe-


### Chapter Two. Concerning Christian Consolation, both general and special, in any…: Concerning the Treaties of Christians (continued)

these things? and he who breaks the covenant, shall he escape? As I live, says the Lord GOD, surely in the place of the king who made him king, whose oath he made void, and whose covenant he broke, which he had with him, in the midst of Babylon he shall die. For he had despised the oath, to break the covenant: as I live, says GOD, surely the oath which he despised, and the covenant which he dissolved, I will put upon his own head, etc.

Of which severity GOD has provided sufficiently horrible examples in all times among those who, having contracted covenants even with the impious and men of a different religion, broke them without just and evident cause, and did not observe the given faith sacredly. On which matter let historians be consulted. Let that one example suffice for us, illustrious above others, which happened in the memory of our fathers. Vladislaus, King of Hungary and Poland, fought most successfully against the Turk several times, as did John Hunyades, Voivode of Transylvania. But afterwards, a covenant was entered into between them and the Turk, and a truce was made, indeed confirmed by a religious oath. But when, at the instigation of Julian Cesarini, a Roman Cardinal and legate of the Pope, they violated the truce sworn to Amurath, Emperor of the Turks, by breaking the covenant (the Roman Pope Eugenius IV releasing them from the bond of the oath), they soon experienced the just nemesis and vengeance of GOD, so that King Vladislaus, together with the Pope's legate, was killed in the very first battle, while Hunyades, thrown into shameful flight, not only lost the praise of a brave man, but was also afterwards defeated in battle by Amurath, with the Pannonians whom he led, in a close-fought engagement not far from Bulgaria. Fulgos. lib. 1. cap. 2. Anton. Bonfin. lib. 26.

And thus far we have confirmed our affirmative regarding this second type of covenants sufficiently evidently, not doubting at all that if not all, yet most Orthodox Theologians will be clearly of one mind with us. From these foundations, indeed, various confederations have arisen and been confirmed between Christian Emperors and barbarian and infidel peoples. Thus, even today, on the same foundation, covenants and truces exist between our Emperor and the Turk. Hence the Christian Kings of France, Poland, Spain, the States and Orders of Belgium, and the Venetian Duchy cultivate covenants of peace with the Turks, with the Tartars, and with the Muscovites. Which covenants, however, are not general, adapted to every event, but limited and determined, partly so that a firm peace may be established for our country, partly so that they need not fear any offense from us, and finally, partly so that if an enemy invades our borders and inflicts damage upon us either by sea or by land, he may be repelled by common aid and forces. From this principle arose the most salutary Pacification of Religion, which, as long as it stood inviolate on the part of the Romanists, for so long did a golden peace shine at home and abroad for the Roman Empire and for all and singular of its orders. But as soon as it was broken and dissolved by the Romanists, then immediately the public peace began to crack, and the whole Roman Empire began to crumble, so that even to this day it cannot resume its former strength. Thus we have Germany as a common country: therefore, when danger threatens, it must be protected by common aid, notwithstanding the diversity of religion, even if no covenant intervenes. For here, humanity itself and mutual love, which Christians are bound by divine law to cultivate and exercise among themselves, if only because of the commonality of the name, are valid. How much more should the religion of a covenant inflame and impel the confederated Orders to this end?

There remains the THIRD and last type of covenants, which we have called Mixed, and which encompasses the assertion and care of both religion and public peace. Regarding this type, the inquiry today is most especially in the Roman Empire; but in such a way that the diversity of emerging cases and the variety and discrepancy of judgments render the question itself more obscure and its decision more difficult. We, without ambiguity, will touch upon and explain the core of the matter at hand, which is as follows.

In the year 1555, on the 25th of September, the Formula of the Passau Transaction, which is otherwise accustomed to be called the Pacification of Religion (den Religions Frieden), was sanctioned by the consent of the Emperor and all the Orders of the Empire, solemnly confirmed, and publicly proclaimed: Because of the doctrine, religion, and faith of the Augsburg Confession, Caesar Ferdinand the King, and the other Princes and Orders, shall not violently force anyone in the whole Empire in any way, nor compel them by mandates or any other reason to abandon their religion, ceremonies, and laws, which the associates of the Augsburg Confession have already instituted or will hereafter institute in their own territory, nor shall they despise them; but they shall permit this religion to be free to them, and at the same time their goods, faculties, revenues, possessions, and rights, so that they may peacefully use and enjoy them: Also, let the religious dispute be composed by no other than pious, friendly, and tranquil methods, etc. Those who are not of either religion are not included in this part.

And after a few words: Let sacred jurisdiction not be exercised, nor have place against the religion, faith, rites, laws, and ecclesiastical ministry of the Augsburg Confession: but let it remain suspended and stayed, nor let it bring any impediment to them, until the dissension shall have been entirely removed. These things are from book 26 of Sleidan, a historian confirmed by Imperial authority.

The German words in the Recesses of the Diets of the year 1555, page 90, are as follows: Therefore the Imperial Recess was publicly read on the twenty-fifth day of September, as is the custom, to this effect: The Emperor, King Ferdinand, and other princes and estates shall in no way force anyone in the Empire on account of the doctrine of the Augsburg Confession, nor shall they force those who hold to the religion, ceremonies, and statutes of the Augsburg Confession in their lands now established or hereafter might establish to abandon through givers or in any other ways, nor despise them, but leave them this religion together with their property, goods, incomes, rights, and justices free, so that they might quietly enjoy and use the same: Also the discord in religion shall not otherwise than through Christian, friendly and peaceful means be reconciled, etc. Which now are not of these two religions/shall not be included in this peace. And after a few. The spiritual jurisdiction or church power shall not be exercised/and have place against the religion/faith/laws/church customs/and services of the Augsburg Confession, but remain in status quo, stand still/and do the adherents of the Confession no harm, until the discord is entirely removed.

By the force of this Pacification, men of the most diverse religions, namely Papists and Lutherans, coalesced into one body as it were, and peace and concord, both ecclesiastical and political, flourished for very many years, and was long most desired: nor was it lawful for anyone to break or violate in any way the conditions of this peace, in which the safety of the Roman Empire entirely and almost solely consisted.

Moreover, this very Pacification was as it were a stake burnt at the tip in the eyes of the Antichrist, or the Roman Pontiff: he held nothing more urgent or ancient than that, this treaty being broken, all peace in Germany should wither away. Indeed, through Cardinal Alexander Farnese, he inflamed both the Emperor CHARLES V himself and King FERDINAND to take up arms against the Lutherans, using this cruel expression: That an expedition should be prepared against the Lutherans rather than against the Turks: for the Lutherans were much worse than the Turks.

A little later in the Council of Trent, under the beautiful scheme and pretext of the CATHOLIC CHURCH, the Pontiff made a decree, published the act, and fortified the published act with an anathema, so that the Emperor and the remaining Catholic Orders (falsely so called), having undertaken the most accurate execution of the decrees of that Council, might proceed most severely against the dissenters (the Lutherans): and not desist until the entire heretical (Lutheran) blood had been extirpated by the roots.

In the progress of time, the Pontiff obtained through the fans of the Jesuits that the Papists were persuaded that faith is not to be kept with heretics. Hence therefore, alas, this holy PALLADIUM of Germany, the Religious Pacification, began to crack and fall apart entirely, so that certain Catholic Princes and Bishops, having broken the federal pacts, did not shudder to rage against the life, fortunes, rights, and privileges of the Lutherans, both political and ecclesiastical. And the matter finally came to this, alas, that the Papists took upon themselves at will the sacred or ecclesiastical jurisdiction over the Evangelical Orders: and troubled them with new mandates, laws, and institutions,

and did not hesitate to proscribe and persecute those resisting as if they were guilty of the crime of high treason; having abused for this purpose the very August name and authority of the Emperor.

Here therefore a question arises, what is to be done by the Evangelical Orders, and those immediately subject to the Roman Empire, in such a case: Whether one should sleep on both ears, as the saying goes, and permit those oath-breakers, at their will, even to the point of insanity, to rage against our lives, bodies, fortunes, rights, and privileges: Or whether it is lawful by legitimate means, and specifically, whether by joining treaties with others even of a different religion, to repel and drive back such force, injuries, and persecutions? A grave and difficult question indeed, about which I would prefer to hear the opinion of the Orthodox, and of theologians, and of politicians, than to offer my own. For on both sides the matter is not without evident danger. For if you embrace the affirmative, you will be accused of sedition and conspiracy against the Emperor, nay, you will be charged with having broken the Passau treaty. But if you depart into the negative, you will seem to have basely betrayed not only your life and fortunes, but also the religion itself, which everyone is bound to redeem even with their own blood. Therefore, there will be need of great caution and prudence, lest you sin either in excess or in defect. Which, so that we also may employ it, following the advice of the philosopher, we will give two answers to the two questions, and according to the diverse questions that occur, we will embrace what seems to us to be the case, but briefly, with certain distinctions and aphorisms: being most ready to yield to those who show better things.

FIRST Aphorism: Pacts, treaties, and agreements once entered into, approved, and confirmed between the Orders of the Empire, must be kept sacredly, and cannot by any law be broken or violated even by the Emperor himself: unless perhaps the other party to the treaty contumaciously neglects and despises the conditions of the treaty.

1 For just as the epistle to the Hebrews ch. 6. 16. rightly establishes that an oath applied for confirmation is the end of all controversy: so the rest of the entire Scripture evidently confirms that GOD is the most severe avenger of even those federal oaths which have been performed concerning the preservation of peace and public and political faith, as we have evidently demonstrated above concerning the second kind of treaties with examples and sayings taken from Scripture. Cyril relates in his book against Julian that the ancients observed this custom in making treaties, that they would divide either a bull or a calf, and pass through the middle of the divided parts, praying such things upon themselves: Unless I keep the treaty, may I myself be divided thus: To such an extent was the religion of keeping a promise once made sacred to them. Looking to which, GOD himself, in Jeremiah 34:18, is read to have passed the same sentence of commutation and punishment upon the covenant-breakers: I will give the men who have not observed the words of the covenant which they made before me, the calf which they cut in two, and passed between the parts thereof, the princes of Judah, and the princes of Jerusalem; I will give them, I say, into the hands of their enemies, and into the hands of them that seek their lives.

Latin:

est hæc? & qui dissolvit fœdus, numquid effugiet? Vivo ego, dicit Dominus DEUS, quoniam in Loco regis, qui constituit eum regem, cujus fecit irritum juramentum, & rupit fœdus, quod habuit cum eo, in medio Babylonis morietur. Spreverat enim juramentum, ut solveret fœdus: vivo ego DEUS, quoniam juramentum, quod sprevit, & fœdus quod dissolvit, ponam in caput ejus &c.

Cujus severitatis exempla DEUS nullis non temporibus horrenda satis edidit in illis; qui fœdera, cum impiis etiam, & diversæ Religionis hominibus contracta, præter justam & evidentem causam ruperunt, & datam fidem non sanctè observarunt. Quâ de re côsulantur historici. Sufficiat nobis unum illud, præ cæteris illustre, quod Patrum nostrorum memoriâ accidit. Pugnaverunt adversus Turcam aliquoties felicissimè, Vladislaus Hungariæ & Poloniæ Rex: ut & Johannes Hunniades, Vaivoda Transylvanus. Sed postmodum fœdus inter hos & Turcam initum, & induciæ factæ, imò religioso juramento confirmatæ sunt. Cùm verò impulsu Juliani Cesarini Cardinalis Romani atq; legati Pontificis, fracto fœdere, inducias Amurathi Turcarum Imperatori juratas violarent, (juramenti vinculo eos solvente Pontifice Romano Eugenio IV.) justam DEI nemesin ac vindictam mox experti sunt, ita ut Rex Vladislaus unâ cum legato Pontificis, in primo statim prælio occideretur, Hunniades verò in turpem fugam conjectus, non solùm viri fortis laudem amitteret, sed & postmodum cum Amurathe, confertâ manu haud longe à Bulgariâ, cum Pannoniis, quibus præerat, prælio vinceretur. Fulgos. lib. 1. cap. 2. Anton. Bonfin. lib. 26.

Et sic hactenus Affirmativam nostram de secundo isto Fœderum genere satis evidenter confirmavimus, nullatenus dubitantes, quin si non omnes, plerosque tamen Orthodoxos Theologos habituri simus planè ὁμοψήφως. Ex his profectò fundamentis variæ ortæ & confirmatæ sunt confœderationes inter Imperatores Christianos, & barbaros ac infideles populos. Sic hodieque ex eodem fundamento Imperatori nostro cum Turcâ intercedunt fœdera & induciæ. Hinc Reges Christiani Galliæ, Poloniæ, Hispaniæ, Status & Ordines Belgici, Ducatus Venetus, fœdera Pacis colunt cum Turcis, cum Tartaris, cum Moschovitis. Quæ tamen fœdera non sunt generalia, ad omnem eventum accommodata: sed limitanea, & determinata, partim ut Pax firma nostræ constet patriæ, partim ut illi nihil offensionis à nobis sibi metuere necesse habeant: partim denique, ut si hostis oras nostras invadat, damnumque nobis sive mari, sive terra inferat, communibus auxiliis & copiis ille repellatur. Ex quo principio orta est Pacificatio Religionis longè saluberrima, quæ quamdiu ex parte Romanensium stetit inviolata, tamdiu etiam pax aurea domi forisque affulsit Romano Imperio, fingulisque ac universis ejusdem ordinibus. Quamprimùm autem rupta ea à Romanensibus ac soluta fuit:tum statim etiam pax publica rimas agere,totumque Romanum Imperium fatiscere cepit: ita ut nec in hanc usque diem pristinas vires resumere possit. Sic communem habemus patriam Germaniam : Ingruente ergo periculo communi auxilio,non obstante Religionis diversitate ea tutanda fuerit : etiam nullo interveniente foedere. Valet at hic ipsa Humanitas, & Dilectio mutua, quam Christiani, vel ob nominis communitatem, inter se colere atq; exercere jure divino tenentur. Quanto magis Foederis Religio Ordines confoederatos hanc ad rem inflammare atq; impellere debet?

Superest TERTIUM & postremum Foederum genus,quodMixtum appellavimus; & partimReligionis,partim pacis publicae afsertionem, curamq; complectitur. De quo genere hodie potissimum in Romano Imperio quaeritur: sed ita,ut casuum emergentium diversitas, judiciorumque varietas ac discrepantia, & Quaestionem ipsam reddat obscuriorem, & ejus decisionem difficiliorem. Nos sine ambagibus nervum rei, de quo agitur, tangemus, & explicabimus, qui sic habet.

Anno supra sesquimillesimum quingentesimo quinto, septimo Calendarum Octobris, Formula Transact ionis Passaviensis, quam alias Pacificatione Religionis den Religions Frieden appellare sole, consensu Imperatoris, omniumq; Imperij Ordinum, tatu sancita, solenniter confirmata, & publice proclamata fuit: Propter Augustanae Confessionis doctrinam, Religionem atq; fidem, Caesar Ferdinandus Rex, caeteriq; Principes ac Ordines, neminem totius Imperij quoquo modo violent, nec ad deserendam Religionem suam, Ceremonias atq; leges, quas in sua ditione, vel jam instituerunt, vel posthac instituent Confessionis Augustanae socij, mandatis; aut alia quavis ratione cogant, neve contemnant etiam: sed hanc religionem illis liberam permittant, simulque bona, facultates, vectigalia, possessiones atq; jura,sic ut pacate possint eis uti frui: Dissidium quoque Religionis non alio, quam pio, amico & tranquillo rationibus componatur &c. Qui non sunt alterutrius Religionis, hac parte non comprehendantur.

Et post pauca: Jurisdictio sacra non exerceatur, neq; locum habeat adversum Augustanae Confessionis religionem, fidem, ritus, leges, ministerium Ecclesiasticum: sed suspensa maneat, & fistatur, nec ullum impedimentum eis inferat, quoad integre sublatum fuerit dissidium. Haec ex lib. 26. Sleidani, historici Imperiali autoritate confirmati.

Verba Germanica in Recessibus Comitiorum anni 1555. pag.90.sic habent: Derhalben wurde des Reichsabschied am fünff vnd zwantzigsten Tagk des Herbstmonats öffentlich verlesen / wie der Brauch ist / auff diese meinung: Der Keyser/König Ferdinand/vnd andere Fürsten/vnd Stände/sollen niemand im Reich/von der Lehre/wegen der Augspurgischen Confession, in keinerley weise vergewaltigen / noch die Religion / Ceremonien vnd Satzung / welche der Augspurgischen Confessions verwante / in jhren Landen jezt angericht/oder forthin auffrichte möchte/ durch Geber / oder jrgent in andere wege/zuverlassen zwinge/ noch sie verachten/ sondern ihnen diese Religion/sampt jhren Haab/Gütern/Einkommen/Recht vnd Gerechtigkeitē/ frey lassen / also, das sie derselbigen geruhig möchten geniessen vnd gebrauchen: Sol auch der Zwiespalt in der Religion/ anders nicht/ denn durchChristliche,freundliche vnd friedliche Mittel verglichen werden / etc. Welche nun dieser beyder Religion nicht seynd/sollen in diesem Fried nicht begriffen sein. Vnd nach wenigen. Die Geistliche Jurisdiction oder Kirchengewalt sol gegen die Religion / Glaube/ Gesetze/ Kirchengebräuch / vnd Dienste der Augspurgischen Confession nicht geübet werden/ vnd stat haben/ sondern eingestalt bleiben/ still stehen / vnd den Confession verwanten so lange/biß der Zwiespalt gäntzlich auffgehoben/ keinen eintrag thun.

Pacificationis hujus vigore , diversissimarum Religionum homines, Pontificij nimirùm & Lutherani, in unum quasi corpus coäluerunt, pax utrinque & Concordia, cùm Ecclesiastica, quàm Politica,annis bene multis longè opratissima floruit : neque fas cuiquam fuit, Conditiones pacis hujus, in quâ Salus Romani Imperij tota & unicè fermè consistebat, quovis modo rumpere aut violare.

Fuit autem hæc ipsa Pacificatio sudes quasi præusta in oculis Antichristi, sive Pontificis Romani: nihil prius aut antiquius habuit, quàm ut fœdere hoc rupto, pax omnis in Germania exolesceret. Quin per Alexandrum Farnesium Cardinalem, tùm Imperatorem ipsū CAROLUM V. tùm Regem FERDINANDUM, ad arma contra Lutheranos subinde inflammavit, crudeli hac voce usus: In Lutheranos potius, quàm in Turcas expeditionem adornandam esse: multò enim Turcis deteriores esse Lutheranos.

Paulò pòst in Concilio Tridentino, sub pulchello Schemate & prætextu ECCLESIÆ CATHOLICÆ decretum fecit Pontifex, factum publicavit, publicatum anathemate munivit, ut Imperator, & reliqui Ordines Catholici (falsò sic appellati) susceptâ accuratissimâ executione Decretorum illig Concilij, in contradicentes (Lutheranos) severissimè animadverterent: neque priùs desisterent, quàm Sanguis hæreticus (Lutheranus) universus radicitùs extirpatus esset.

Progressu temporis id per flabella Esawitas obtinuit Pontifex, ut persuasum esset Pontificiis, Hæreticis non esse servandam fidem. Hinc ergò, proh dolor, Sanctum hoc Germaniæ PALLADIUM, Pacificatio Religionis, rimas agere, & tota fatiscere cepit, ita ut Principes & Episcopi quidam Catholici, ruptis pactis fœderalibus, in Lutheranorum vitam, fortunas, jura, privilegia tàm politica, quàm Ecclesiastica, sævire non exhorruerint. Et res eò tandem, proh dolor, devenit, ut Pontificij Jurisdictionem Sacram sive Ecclesiasticam,in Ordines Evangelicos pro lubitu sibi sumere:novis mandatis, legibus, institutis eos turbare,

& contra nitentes, tanquam criminis læsæ Majestatis reos proscribere, & persequi non dubitarent; abusi hanc ad rem ipsius Imperatoris Augusto nomine & autoritate.

Hîc ergò Quæstio oritur, Quid tali casu Ordinibus Evangelicis, & immediate Romano Imperio subjectis sit faciendum: An in utramque, quod dicitur, aurem indormiendum, & permittendum, ut fœdifragis illis, pro lubitu, ad insaniam usq; in vitam, corpora, fortunas, jura & privilegia nostra sæviant: An verò legitimis mediis, & nominatim, an junctis cum aliis diversæ etiam Religionis hominibus fœderibus, ejusmodi vim, injurias, persecutiones repellere, ac propulsare liceat? Gravis profectò & difficilis quæstio, de quâ Orthodoxorum & Theologorum, & Politicorum sententiam audire, quàm meam ferre optârim. Nam ex utraque parte res non caret evidenti periculo. Si enim Affirmativam amplectaris, Seditionis & Conjurationis contra Imperatorem accusaberis, imò rupti fœderis Passaviensis insimulaberis. Sin in Negantem discedas, non modò vitam & fortunas, sed & Religionem ipsam, quam vel sanguine proprio quisque redimere tenetur, turpiter prodidisse videberis. Ergò magna cautione ac prudentia opus fuerit, ne vel in excessu, vel in defectu pecces. Quam ut nos quoque adhibeamus, secuti consilium Philosophi, πρὸς τὰ δύο ἐρωτήματα, δύο καὶ ἀποκρίσεις dabimus, & secundum diversas quæstiones, quæ occurrunt, certis distinctionibus ac Aphorismis, quid nobis videatur, sed breviter complectemur: meliora monstrantibus cedere paratissimi.

PRIMUS Aphorismus: Pacta, fœdera, & conventa inter Ordines Imperij semel inita, approbata, cõnfirmata, sanctè servari debent, & ne quidem ab Imperatore ipso rumpi aut violari jure ullo possunt: nisi fortè altera pars paciscentium conditiones fœderis contumaciter negligat & contemnat.

1 Quemadmodum enim epistola ad Hebræos cap. 6. 16. rectè statuit, Omnis Controversiæ finem esse Juramentum ad Confirmationem adhibitum: ita Scriptura reliqua universa evidenter confirmat, DEUM severissimum esse vindicem eorum etiam juramentorũ fœderalium; quæ de pace & fide publicâ ac politicâ conservâda, sunt præstita, uti suprà de secundo genere Fœderum exemplis & dictis è Scriptura petitis evidenter demonstravimus. Refert Cyrillus libro contra Julianum, Veteres in paciscēdis fœderibus morem hunc observasse, ut vel taurum, vel vitulum dividerent, & per partes divisas medij transirent, talia sibi imprecati: Nisi fœdus servâro, ipse sic dividar: Usque adeò sancta illis erat semel promissi servandi Religio. Quo respiciens DEUS ipse, Jeremiæ 34. 18. eandem Communationis & pœnæ sententiam in fœdifragos tulisse legitur: Dabo viros, qui non observârunt verba fœderis, quibus assensi sunt in cõspectu meo, vitulum, quem conciderunt in duas partes, & transierunt inter divisiones ej9, Principes Juda, & Principes Jerusalem: dabo, inquam, eos in man9 inimicorum suorum, & in manusquærentiũ animas eo-


### Chapter Two. Concerning Christian Consolation, both general and special, in any…: Aphorism: The Emperor cannot, by divine Right, compel the Evangelical Estates to embrace his Religion

stium, and their dead bodies shall be for food to the birds of the air and to the beasts of the earth. The opinion of the first part of this Aphorism therefore stands unmoved: that the Papists, as covenant-breakers, cannot by any human or divine law clear themselves of the guilt of perfidy.

II. Faith is to be kept even with a heretic: nor are the simpler sort to be deceived in any way or respect. For GOD solemnly testifies that He will not hold him guiltless who has taken His name in vain or deceitfully: Exod. 20. 7. And Zech. 8. 16. & 17. He promulgated this general authentic rule: Speak the Truth every man to his neighbor (and indeed the Samaritan heretic is also our neighbor, Luke 10. 36. & 37.) execute the TRUTH and JUDGMENT OF PEACE in your gates: and love no FALSE OATH: For all these are things that I HATE, says the LORD. From this foundation the Pope has hitherto judged that faith is to be kept with the Jews, however much they blaspheme the adorable Trinity and our Redeemer JESUS CHRIST, nay, even though they are manifest and sworn enemies of all Christians. Why then should the Papists not religiously keep the faith sworn to the Lutherans? O the times, O the customs! Faith is to be kept with blasphemers: the Pope decrees it is not to be kept with heretics. The Law of GOD commands that the former be removed from the midst, but that the latter be avoided, not deprived of life. Are the Lutherans then worse than the perfidious and blasphemous Jews? I think not: the Lutherans are certainly Christians: the Jews are enemies both of Christ and of all Christians: the Lutherans are washed by holy baptism, grafted into the Church, and made members of Christ through the grace of regeneration: the Jews are strangers to the covenant of Christ and all divine promises. The Lutherans, by the admission of the Papists themselves, rightly teach and believe concerning the Most Holy Trinity, and the Person and office of Christ: the Jews trample both mysteries under blasphemous feet. The Lutherans, from the deepest recesses of their hearts, have all their hope and confidence of salvation fixed and placed solely in the mercy of GOD and the merit of Christ, apprehended by faith. The Jews, having abolished the Gospel, attempt to restore the yoke of the Levitical Ceremonies, and from that they impiously promise themselves salvation. The Lutherans, to say nothing more of the heads of Religion, strive to live piously, justly, and soberly, as much as can be done by the grace of GOD in such great weakness and corruption of strength: they willingly and with due submission of mind and reverence pay and perform to the Roman Emperor, and to any ordinary Magistrate, that which both sacred and civil laws demand of them: Matt. 22. 21. Rom. 13. 1. & 7. The Jews, on the contrary, pay tribute and tax only when forced, and that indeed extorted deceitfully from Christians, and from the Papists themselves by right or wrong: they defile all laws, sacred and profane: and if it stood with them, they would swallow up not so much the Lutherans as the Papists themselves in one gulp. What then, by the immortal GOD, could be the reason that the Romanists can tolerate Jews, Anabaptists, and any other heretics whatsoever: but judge that only the Lutherans are to be slaughtered and extirpated? Certainly the cause is not, nor can it be, the Religion of the Lutherans considered in itself and by itself: for it is exactly congruent and conformable to the Word of GOD: But the lust for dominion, and the inexhaustible avarice and pride of the Roman Apostolic See, or rather of the Pope. While the Lutherans refuse to subject themselves to this as slaves, to pay most iniquitous tributes, and to acknowledge him as Monarch and head of the Universal Church, and to revere him as the supreme Dictator: it is all over, the Lutherans are now worse than all heretics, and even the Jews themselves, and no faith is to be kept with them. This Aphorism shows that whose use can be greatest regarding the dissolution of the proposed question: namely, that the Papists have hitherto broken, and today still break, rights, pacts, agreements, and treaties, and hate us, pursue us with hostility, and plot against our lives and fortunes, not primarily and principally because of doctrine and Religion itself: but because of the denied simple and absolute obedience to the Pope and the Roman Church, both in ecclesiastical and in secular matters. Which end is to be well noted.

III. Aphorism: The Emperor cannot by divine law compel the Evangelical Estates to embrace his Religion. But by Evangelical Estates I understand those who are immediately subject to the Roman Empire, and are its certain members: so that all things ought to be deliberated and decreed in the Empire by the vote and consent of these, as well as of the Papists. A different judgment must be passed on those who are subject to the Emperor not only as Emperor: but also as a hereditary Lord: of which elsewhere. David certainly is nowhere read to have ruled not only over Israelites who were of one mind in Religion, but also over Philistines, Moabites, Ammonites, Syrians, Damascenes, peoples of the most diverse religions, and indeed to have asserted the worship of the purer religion in the kingdom of Judah: but to have compelled the remaining peoples to embrace the same by war and arms, or to have arrogated to himself any dominion over their consciences. 2 Sam. 8. 1. and following. Solomon, the wisest and most powerful of all kings, is read to have reigned from the river of the land of the Philistines unto the border of Egypt: but that he raged with force and arms against their faith and religion, or for this reason broke treaties and pacts entered into with them, is nowhere read: Scripture is rather a witness that he, content with the tributes and pensions which they were compelled to pay as a sign of subjection, granted them the liberty of exercising their own Religion. 1 Kings 4. 21. Thus Nebuchadnezzar, the first King and Monarch of Babylon, converted to the GOD of Israel, did not immediately force all the subject provinces to that faith by external force: but caused this to be proclaimed, that it should not be lawful for anyone to offer blasphemy to the GOD of Israel. For the formula of the Edict was thus: A decree is made by me, that every people, tribe, and language, which shall speak blasphemy against the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, shall perish, and their house shall be laid waste. Which zeal against blasphemers, however, is clearly absent among the Papists, who tolerate Jews in their dominions, especially at Rome. Cyrus the first of the Persians The monarch permitted the Jews the freedom of practicing their own religion, although he himself was not addicted to the faith of the Jews, Ezra 1. 2. & following. Which permission the King of Persia, Darius, also held valid: so that, although Artaxerxes, circumvented by the counsels of certain courtiers, had promulgated a mandate concerning the suppression of the religion of the Jews, Ezra 4. 21, Darius nevertheless, having been informed of that first Sanction of Cyrus, wished it to be held entirely valid, with this most grave threat added: Whoever shall change this law, let a beam be taken from his house, and let it be erected, and let him be fastened upon it, and let his house be confiscated: Ezra 6. 6. & 11. Guided by the religion of these Kings and Monarchs, the Most Christian Emperor MAXIMILIAN II emulated them remarkably, so that to some instigators inciting him to shed Lutheran blood, he once replied with great spirit: No sin is graver than the desire to dominate consciences: for they oppose GOD himself who wish to dominate consciences in the cause of Religion. Crato in funeral oration.

IV. No mortal, not even the Pope, can absolve the Emperor from faithfully keeping an oath given to confederates of any Religion whatsoever: rather, he is bound to perform and keep it religiously. For it is not likely that the Emperor would pledge his faith to anyone regarding things that are impious and by their nature illicit: where such an Absolution would have a place. The Loyolan monks do indeed contend that the Pope can most fully absolve both the Emperor and the remaining Papal Estates of the Empire from an oath of fidelity given to a Heretic, so that no punishment for perjury remains for them at all.

But is this, I do not say a theological, but at least a human statement, deed, or thought? For what? Is the power of the keys of those who absolve granted to the Church to this end, that by their use, an oath legitimately taken may be made illusory? That a mutual obligation, pledged and confirmed with the religious attestation of the divine Being (which GOD willed to be indissoluble in His word), may be rendered vain and void? May GOD rebuke you, Satan, and quickly crush you under his feet: So be it, so be it. The proper matter or Object of Evangelical absolution is not the faith owed in political matters either to GOD or to men: which no key, whether in Heaven or on earth, can dissolve or remove: But only the guilt of sins, by which we offend against the precepts of GOD. What? That the power of absolution does not depend either on some magical or secret virtue of the words that are pronounced: or on the dignity or intention of the person either absolving or being absolved: but only on the will and ordination of Him who instructed the Church with the power of that Key: namely, CHRIST the Savior, with whom perfidy and perjury agree no more than light with darkness, or truth with a lie. And how vain, frivolous, and nugatory such a Papal Absolution is in this case, even that tragic end alone of Vladislaus, King of Hungary and Poland, proves and evinces clearly enough. Where there was such force in this Papal Absolution that the King himself was miserably slaughtered: Cardinal Cesarini was killed in flight: and finally thirty thousand Christians perished: as witnessed by Jovius in Amurathes II. Woe therefore to those Catholic Emperors and Princes who allow themselves to be imposed upon by the Pope in this matter. On the contrary, however, their magnanimity, faith, and constancy are to be celebrated with perpetual praises, who, to break a federal pact once religiously decreed and confirmed with the Lutherans, have allowed themselves to be moved by no blandishments of words or arguments. Among whom the invincible Emperor CHARLES V easily holds the first place, who, when he was instigated by certain Papal instigators and furies at the Diet of Worms not to keep the faith given to LUTHER, because according to the decree of the Council of Constance, faith is not to be kept with a Heretic; he spiritedly replied: Even if faith in promised things should be banished from the whole world, it must nevertheless remain with the Emperor. Guliel. Zenocartis in the life of Charles. The Emperor FERDINAND emulated this heroic greatness of spirit, who is read to have been so studious and observant of the Pacification once confirmed with the Lutherans: that before his death, suffused with singular joy, he would often break out into these words: Among the highest things which GOD granted me in the government of the Empire, I count this as the FIRST and GREATEST in my judgment of mind, that I applied my mind to settling public discords, and GOD gave me the Formula of Tolerance in Religion into my mind. See the preliminary epistle of Crato à Crafftheim, in the Bohemian history of Dubravius: We do not doubt in any way that the same pious and most generous spirit exists today in the Invincible Emperor Matthias: venerating GOD as suppliants, that, emulating his ancestors and predecessors who can never be praised enough, he may never allow himself to be led astray by the crafty counsels of other slaves of the Pope, whether Jesuits or certain others.

From these aforementioned hypotheses, for the decisive opinion of the proposed question, we conclude evidently and irrefragably: 1. That not we, but the Papists bear the blame for perfidy and broken peace. 2. That the cause of the violated Peace of Passau is none other than the lust for domination, which the Roman Antichrist arrogates to himself, and which he strives to establish and confirm again in Germany as if by a right of postliminy. 3. That tyranny is exercised against the Evangelical Estates contrary to all sacred and profane laws by those Princes or Papal Bishops who strive to entangle them again in the yoke of Papal Idolomany, and indeed by force and arms. 4. That it is debated today between the Evangelical Estates and the Papists, first and principally on account of Religion: but on the part of these indeed for asserting the Dominion of the Roman Pontiff: while indirectly, as it were, the Romanists arrogate to themselves some Right and authority over the privileges, dignities, and Ecclesiastical Regalia, as they call them, of the Lutherans: that is, Roman Episcopal Jurisdiction over is likewise not for Religion considered in and of itself: but for that Liberty which we have obtained concerning the exercise of Religion, by honest means, and through the intervention of most sacred federal sanctions: Also for asserting the public and civil peace, which the Romanists strive to snatch from us by force and Tyranny, and to reduce us to most miserable servitude. Although, therefore, some regard for Religion is altogether observed by both sides under these disturbances: yet it is not simple and absolute, but accidental.

These things being thus established, the Principal Question returns to this: Whether the Lutherans can, with a good conscience, resist the Papists who rashly and contrary to right and equity break leagues, pacts, and agreements, even those confirmed by religious Oath, and who attempt everything by force and arms, and fight to assert the liberty into which they came by just title, and which they possess by the force of federal pacts, and seek auxiliary hands from men of a different Religion through the intervention of a legitimate union, and join them to themselves? To which I answer in the Affirmative, relying on the same reasons and arguments which we have already produced above from the Holy Scriptures, where we discussed the second kind of Leagues. For in both cases the reason is one and the same, the end and scope are one and the same: Therefore, the Truth is also one and the same in both. Therefore, although it is forbidden in sacred matters to join and covenant in leagues with men of a different Religion in a case of simple and absolute Religion: since a league of Religion cannot be entered into with such, unless the concord of faith or Religion precedes, which is the bond and foundation of a religious league. Now, however, in the business of Religion there can be no agreement of Christ with Belial: no part for the believer with the infidel: no participation of justice with injustice: no fellowship of light with darkness, 2 Cor. 6:15, and therefore the right hand of fraternity has rightly been denied to the Calvinists hitherto in this case, and ought to be denied henceforth: yet nothing prevents us from extending the right hands of Humanity to them in civil matters concerning our liberty, rights, privileges, life, and fortunes, and receiving them in turn from them: which we know neither B. LUTHER denied to Zwingli, nor the Orthodox to Beza at Montbéliard.

Moreover, lest the manner in this part be exceeded either in excess or in defect, the following cautions must be properly observed:

frustrating, useless, and in many ways harmful to the purer Religion.

2. Nothing whatsoever should be decreed or undertaken through sedition or conspiracy against the Emperor, as the supreme Ordinary Magistrate.

3. Impending evils, and crafty and cruel counsels, insidiously suggested to the Emperor or other Estates of the Empire by the Jesuits and the fans of the Pontiff, should be averted as much as possible by prayers to GOD, serious amendment of life, most humble supplications, entreaties and admonitions, and sounder counsels, which breathe neither slaughter nor blood.

4. If all things are attempted in vain and with fruitless effort, and force is brought against us and ours, it will certainly be lawful to repel force with force, having also called upon our confederates for aid, but provided that we keep ourselves within defensive limits; and that we are not carried away by the success of the war, and thereby abuse it for any Tyranny or cruelty.

5. The conditions in the Passau Transaction, and other Recesses of the Empire, approved and confirmed by the unanimous consent of all the Estates, must by no means be violated by us (if it can be avoided): but all things should be conducted in such a way that we may appear, even to our enemies themselves, not to have sought Religion, but to have asserted justice, public peace, and liberty: and that we have aimed at this one thing, that there may be peace in our towers, and safety in our palaces.

6. Clearly no trust should be placed in such leagues, but they should be held only as means, granted, through which GOD alone, and not external fortification, can save and protect us.

7. Let all greed, deceit, ambition, infidelity, and similar vices be absent among the confederates themselves: if one or more of these are present, the leagues themselves will soon fall apart of their own accord and will have an unhappy outcome.

8. During the expeditions of wars themselves (if necessity so requires), not indeed offensive, but defensive, one should always think of the means and counsels of peace, by which enemies may be mitigated and reconciled to us.

9. Finally, if it be necessary, let the battle be fought bravely, and let the outcome be commended in pious prayers to GOD alone, who is our victory, and is as able to save by few as by many, 1 Sam. 14. 6, provided that due circumspection and prudence are employed, lest our plans become known to the enemy sooner than to ourselves: whence all the moments of conducting affairs are hindered. For, as Augustine says, lib. 6. of questions upon Joshua, quest. 10, when one has undertaken a just war, whether he conquers by open battle or by ambush, it makes no difference to justice, since GOD himself is read to have sometimes commanded ambushes, as may be seen in Joshua c. 8. Where the well-worn adage has its place: ὅπω μὴ ἡ λέαινα ἰσχύει, παρέςχειν τὴν ἀλώπεκα. But let the Politicians see to these and similar precepts.

And let it suffice to have said these things concerning treaties, as a means which it is permitted to use in public calamities. There remains another, namely WAR itself, which we shall briefly examine as to whether it should be used as a means for repressing tribulations, and how.

Latin:

stium, & erit morticinium eorum in escam volatilibus cæli, & bestiis terræ. Stat ergò vi primi hujus Aphorismi sententia immota: Pontificios tanquam fœdifragos perfidiæ, culpâ nullo sive humano, sive divino jure á se amoliri posse.

II. Fides etiam hæretico est servanda: neque decipiendi simpliciores, quovis modo aut respectu. DEUS enim sanctè attestatur, se non insontem habiturum, qui nomen ejus frustrâ aut dolosè affumserit: Exod. 20. 7. Et Zachar. 8. 16. & 17. generalem hanc promulgavit authenticam: Loquimini Veritatem unusquisque proximo suo (est verò etiam Samaritanus hæreticus proximus noster, Luc. 10. 36. & 37.) VERITATEM & JUDICIUM PACIS judicate in portis vestris: & JURAMENTUM MENDAX ne diligatis: Omnia enim hæc sunt, quæ O D I, dicit D OMINUS. Ex hoc fundamento Pontifex fidem hactenus servandam esse censuit Judæis, quantumvis blasphemis in adorandam Trinitatem, & Redemtorem nostrum JESUM CHRISTUM, imò manifestis & juratis omnium Christianorum hostibus. Quidni ergo fidem Lutheranis religiosè juratam servêt Pontificij? O tempora, ô mores! Blasphemis fidem servandam: Hæreticis non servandam statuit Pontifex. Lex DEI illos è mediò tollere: hos verò vitare, sed non vita privare jubet. Anne ergo Lutherani perfidis & blasphemis Judæis sunt deteriores? Haud opinor: Lutherani certè Christiani sunt: Judæi hostes & Christi, & Christianorum omnium: Lutherani sacro baptismate tincti, Ecclesiæ inserti, membraq; Christi per regenerationis gratiam effecti: Judæi sunt expertes fœderis Christi, & omnium promissionum divinarum. Lutherani, ipsis fatentibus Pontificijs, de Sacrosancta Trinitate, de Persona & officio Christi rectè docent ac sentiunt: Judæi utrumque mysterium blasphemis pedibus conculcant. Lutherani ex imis cordium suorum penetralibus, omnem spem atque fiduciam salutis, in solâ DEI misericordiâ & merito Christi, fide apprehenso, unicè fixam, locatamque habent. Judæi abolito Evangelio jugum Ceremoniarū Leviticarum restaurare conantur, ex eoq; salutem sibi impiè pollicentur. Lutherani, ut de Religionis capitibus nihil ampliùs dicamus, piè justè, sobriè, quantum per DEI gratiam, in tantâ, virium infirmitate & corruptione fieri potest, vivere satagunt: Imperatori Romano, & Magistratui cuivis ordinario, sponte & debitâ animi submissione ac reverentiâ exsolvunt, & præstant id, quod jura tum sacra, tum civilia ab ipsis exigunt: Matth. 22. 21. Rom. 13. 1. & 7. Judæi contrâ tributum & mercedem solvunt coacti, & eam quidem per fas, nefasque à Christianis, & ipsis quoque Pontificiis dolosè extortam: conspurcant jura omnia sacra & prophana: & si per ipsos staret, non tàm Lutheranos, quàm ipsos Pontificios uno hiatu absorberent. Quæ ergo per DEUM immortalem causa fuerit, quòd Romanenses ferre possunt Judæos, anabaptistas, & nullos non hæreticos alios: Solos autem Lutheranos mactandos, & excindendos esse judicant? Certè in causa non est, vel effe potest Religio Lutheranorum per se, ac in se considerata: quippe quæ Verbo DEI ex amussim congrua est & conformis : Sed Dominandi libido, & Sedis Apostolicæ Romanæ, vel Pontificis potiùs inexplebilis avaritia & superbia. Huic dum Lutherani se tanquam mancipia subjicere, tributa iniquissima persolvere: ipsumq; pro Monarcha & capite Universalis Ecclesiæ agnoscere, & tanquam Dictatorem summum revereri detrectant: jam conclamatum est, jam Lutherani omnibus hæreticis, ac ipsis Judæis sunt deteriores, fidesq; ipsis nulla servanda. Monstrat hic Aphorismus id, cujus usus circa dissolutionem propositæ quæstionis potest esse maximus: nempe, Pontificios jura, pacta, conventa, fœdera hactenus rupisse, hodieqs rumpere, nosq; odisse, hostiliter persequi, vitæ, fortunisq; nostris insidiari, non primò ac principaliter propter doctrinam, & Religionem ipsam : sed propter negatam Pontifici & Ecclesiæ Romanæ simplicem & absolutam obedientiam cùm in Ecclesiasticis, quàm in secularibus. Qui finis probè notandus.

III. Aphorismus: Imperator ad suam am plexandam Religionem Ordines Evangelicos Jure divino cogere non potest.
