2. From a particular, a Universal is gathered in this manner: GOD does not always hear this or that one; therefore the promises are not certain. That this kind of argumentation is most vicious, both in other sciences and especially in Theology, is manifest in itself.

The fourth and fifth reasons harp on the same string of vanity. For neither David nor Hezekiah trust in the dignity of their own person, or in their own merits: but in the goodness of GOD alone. Nor does the prayer of Hezekiah stand in the way, the sense of which is not that he boasts of the justice of his works and his own merits: But that he calls to mind before GOD that justice of faith, by which, having been sustained until now, he has committed himself with his whole heart to divine mercy in all his afflictions: so that the sense is: I beseech you, O LORD, that you do not now desert me, just as you have never deserted me until now: I have walked before you in truth and with a perfect heart: that is, I have not entrusted myself to you entirely in a feigned or hypocritical manner, but I have believed your Word, which is Truth, with my whole heart in the highest temptations, and I have placed full faith in it: Therefore you have helped me: Why then would you now reject me as I pray, and repel me as I beseech you, who walk before you in the same truth and with the same perfect heart, seeking and calling upon you alone.

Then it must be well noted that this concerns only a bodily benefit, namely, deliverance from a present disease and the danger of death. Now it is by no means denied that GOD in such goods also regards the innocence of life, the pursuit of piety, and good works: according to that Psalm 41:2, Blessed is he who considers the poor and needy: the LORD will deliver him in the day of evil; and verse 4, The LORD will sustain him upon the bed of languishing. Yet this very divine compensation does not proceed from the dignity or merit of the work of beneficence: but from the sole grace and mercy of God who promises.

Regarding Psalm 7:9, David commends to GOD the justice not of his person, but of the deed: showing that he is innocent and entirely free from guilt in that matter for which Saul pursues him: as if he had plotted against the life and kingdom of Saul. He complains, therefore, that an injury is being done to him, and with a joyful conscience he boasts of his innocence in this regard: saying, If I have done this: if there is iniquity in my hands: if I have rewarded evil to him who was at peace with me (Saul): let the enemy pursue my soul. With this standing, the collection of the Papists, adapted for deception under the sophism of ἑτεροζητήσεως (heterozētēseōs), vanishes into smoke. For it is one thing to inquire about the justice of some certain deed: but another to inquire about the justice of a person before GOD: which David himself seeks in the mercy of GOD alone, Psalm 51:2 and following: Have mercy upon me, O GOD, according to your lovingkindness: blot out my transgressions according to the multitude of your tender mercies: For I have done evil before you, etc.

The third cause impelling prayers is our necessity and that of our neighbor. For the afflictions and calamities by which the pious are exercised daily are an incitement and a spur, so that, unless we wish to perish entirely, we may call upon GOD as a helper, who is as optimal as he is maximal.

Isaiah 26:16. In distress, O LORD, we seek your face.

Psalm 18:5, 6, & 7. The sorrows of death compassed me, and the floods of Belial made me afraid: The sorrows of hell compassed me about: and the snares of death prevented me: In this my tribulation I called upon the LORD, and cried unto my GOD: And he heard my voice out of his holy temple, etc.

Psalm 35:16 & 17. Look upon me, and have mercy upon me, for I am solitary and poor: The troubles of my heart are multiplied: bring me out of my distresses.

Psalm 70:6. I am poor and needy: O GOD, make haste unto me: You are my help and my deliverer: O LORD, do not tarry.

Psalm 86:1. Bow down your ear, O LORD, and hear me, for I am poor and needy.

The fourth impulsive cause of prayers is their signal utility, and that is manifold. For 1. through the worship of Invocation the name of GOD is sanctified, and the glory due to him is rendered. 2. The Covenant of Grace, which GOD has entered into with us, is repeatedly renewed, fostered, and confirmed: according to that Isaiah 64:9, Look, we beseech you, for we are your people. 3. Our faith in GOD is wonderfully exercised and becomes confirmed. 4. The effect of being heard is far most wholesome.

The fifth and final cause is the holiness of examples. For we have in the school of prayer a leader and forerunner, Christ, Ps. 22, the whole; Matt. 14, 23; John 17, the whole. We have Moses, David, Solomon, Hezekiah, Daniel, the Apostles, and none who were not pious and faithful, whose examples it is fitting to imitate; indeed, whose being heard can render and confirm our hope and faith concerning a similar being heard. For hence such an argument in theology is of the best consequence, although it is sought from particulars: God heard this one or that one crying out in his necessities: Therefore He will also hear me: He hoped in the LORD, and was delivered from every evil. I likewise will hope in the LORD. Therefore I also shall be delivered. From this very logic of the Holy Spirit, David borrowed an argument, Ps. 34, 7: This poor man cried out: and the LORD heard him: and delivered him from all his tribulations. The commemoration of former benefits bestowed upon us pertains to this: Often until now, indeed always, you have delivered me, O God, when I was calling upon you and trusting in you. Therefore you will certainly deliver me now as well. Thus David, Ps. 31, 8, 9, and 10: I have hoped in the LORD: I will exult and rejoice in His mercy: Because You have regarded my humility, and have delivered my soul from necessities: And have not shut me up in the hands of my enemies: You have set my feet in a spacious place: Now therefore have mercy on me, O LORD, because I am in tribulation. Thus Ps. 3, 5, 6, and 7: I cried to the LORD with my voice, and He heard me from His holy mountain: I slept, and took my rest, and rose up, because the LORD sustained me: Therefore I will not fear the myriads of people surrounding me.

Latin:

QVæstionis hujus observatio maximè necessaria est partim contra Epicuræos ac profanos homi nes: partim verò contrà Sacramentarios. Illi enim absurdum esse somniant, si statuatur DEUS flecti precibus humanis: imò nihil prorsus opus esse precibus, eò quòd DEUS nostri curam ampliùs non gerat, vel certè sua sponte, quippè naturâ suâ bonus & beneficus, bona necessaria in nos conferat, si velit: sin nolit, frustrà precibus nostris ipse fatigetur. Hi verò, nempè Sacramentarij, omnem orandi necessitatem penitùs è medio tollunt, quàmdiu pro absoluto, omnesque causas antegrediente DEI decreto, salutis & reprobationis nostræ, pugnare pergunt. Absolutum enim quod est, id causas intermedias, & fatentibus ipsis Calvinianis, ne quidem fidem in Christum admittit. Stante ergo tali absoluto & Salutis, & Reprobationis decteto: frustrà omninò vel pro donāda mihi salute æterna: vel pro avertenda æterna itidem damnatione DEUM invocavero. Nam si ad illam electus : vel ad hanc immutabili & absoluta DEI voluntate ab æterno destinatus sum: alterutrum etiam necessariò & immutabiliter mihi obtingat, necesse est. Hoc nimirùm est pietatem omnem radicitùs tollere, & ex Ecclesia DEI precum omnium studium eliminare: vel certè preces tantùm, tanquàm notam ac tefferam aliquam Electorum, vel tanquàm fructum Electionis absolutæ concedere quidem; sed interim omnem earum vim, quoad promovendam & conservandam salutem nostram, ut & ad avertendam æternam damnationem, simpliciter negare & evertere.

Ab his ergò impietatibus divortium facientes nostræ Ecclesiæ, statuunt & docent, Invocationem DEI non esse ἀδιάφορον, liberam aut indifferentem, inq; nostro arbitrio positam: sed simpliciter & absolutè necessariam, propter causas sequentes quinq;.

I. Causa est Mandatum DEI, cultum hunc à nobis seriò expetentis: Psal. 27, 8. Cor meum cogitat verbum tuum : Quærite faciem meam: Tuam ergo faciem quæro.

Pfal. 50, 15. Invoca me in die tribulationis & eripiam te : & glorificabis me. Jefa. 55, 6. Quærite DOMINVM, dum inveniri potest : invocate eum,dum propè est. Matth. 7, 7. Petite, & dabitur vobis: Quærite,& invenietis : pulsate, & aperietur vobis. 1. Tim. 2, 1. Hortor,ut ante omnia fiant deprecationes, orationes, interceßiones, gratiarum actiones pro omnibus hominibus.

Primæ huic causæ duo potissimùm obvertit Ratio nostra. Primùm enim sic colligit : DEVS est omnifcius, & curam agit pro nobis ergò non necesse est, ut per preces demùm in memoriam revocentur ipsi, quibus rebus indigeamus. Antecedens patet ex ipsa Scriptura : Hebr. 4,13. Omnia sunt nuda, & aperta oculis ejus Psal. 121 4. Ecce non dormit, nec dormitat, qui custodit Israël: Matth. 6, 31, & 32. Nolite esse solliciti, dicentes: Quid manducabimus, aut quid bibemus, aut quo vestiemur ? Hæc omnia gentes requirunt: Scit enim Pater vester quòd his omnibus indigeatis.

Deinde verò hunc in modum obstrepit Ratio : DEVS largitur omnia, etiam sine nostris precibus, quemadmodum Solem suum oriri sinit citra nostras preces Jefa. 65, 24. Antequàm clament, ego exaudiam psal. 21, 4. Prævenisti eum benedictionibus bonis Matth. 6, 8. Novit Pater ille vester, quibus sit vobis opus, antequàm petatis ab eo. Ergò Preces, sive Invocatio DEI non est necessaria.

Et tantâ quidem vis fuit istarum rationcularum, ut teste Clemente Alexandrino lib. 7.Stromatum, jam olim mox post Apostolorum tempora fuerint hæretici,qui neque preces,nequeSacrificiaDEO offerenda esse contenderunt, eò quòd DEUS ex his nullam voluptatem capiat.

Verùm utriusque cavilli vanissima vanitas per se est manifesta. Nam prioris antecedens elencho omni destituitur: & crassum Sophisma vitiosi consequentis committitur, imò turpissima petitio Principij. Non enim sequitur: DEUS omnia novit. Ergo non debet invocari. Hoc ipsum enim quæritur, an ideò DEVS invocari debeat,quia omnia novit? Vbi Affirmativam tenemus,& vel ideò DEUM in vocandum esse statuimus, quia omnes lachrymas & suspiria nostra in numerato habet, & auxilium ab ipso peti præcipit.

Quâ ipsa geminâ Sophisticatione laborat etiam posterius cavillum. Non enim consequens ex antecedente sequitur Quia rursus invertitur argumentum, & inferimus; Hanc ipsam ob causam DEVM ardentius invocandum esse. Nam si DEUS etiam citra nostras preces omnia largitur : Ergo multò magis, multò plura ac excellentiora largietur, â nobis invocatus : non quidem propter dignitatem precum nostrarum: sed propter promifsionum suarum immotam certitudinem. Emergit ergo & hinc Sophisticatio Petitionis Principij. Nam hoc ipsum esset probandum, quòd DEUS ideò non sit invocandus, quia citra preces nostras pijs omnia largitur.

ALTERA causa precum impulsiva, est Promissionum divinarum certitudo & Infallibilitas. DEUS enim per & propter Christum Mediatorem invocatus, vota precesq́; nostras exauditurum se, tàm sanctè recepit, ut nisi semet ipsum negare, imò DEUS ampliùs esse ac manere nolit, nostris necessitatibus affici, ijsdemque opem ferre necesse habeat: secundum dulcissimas promissiones: Psal. 145, 18. & 19. Propè est DOMINVS omnibus invocantibus eum: omnibus invocantibus eum in veritate: Voluntatem timentium se faciet, & deprecationem eorum exaudiet, & salvos faciet eos.

Jes. 65, 24. Et erit, antequam clament, ego ex audiam: adhuc illis loquentibus ego audiam.

Matth. 7, 6. & 8. Qui petit, accipit: qui quærit, invenit: & pulsanti aperietur.

Matth. 11, 28. Venite ad me omnes qui laboratis, & onerati estis: Ego reficiam vos.

Joh. 14, 13. & 14. Quicquid petieritis innomine meo, hoc faciam, ut glorificetur Pater in filio: Siquid petieritis in nomine meo: ego faciam.

Joh 16. 23. Amen, amen dico vobis, siquid petieritis à patre in nomine meo, dabit vobis.

Jacob. 5, 15. Oratio fidei sanabit infirmum, & eriget eum DOMINVS, & si in peccatis sit, remittetur ei.

Dulcissimas hasce promissiones de exauditione certissimâ precum fidelium, gens Esavvitica mirum in modum corrumpere, obscurare, & in desperationis laqueum convertere student: his freti ratiunculis.

I. Promissiones prosunt servantibus legem: Atqui qui ex solâ fide orant, & bonis operibus, atque meritis proprijs destituantur, Legem non servant. Ergo promissiones de exauditionis certitudine, nihil illis prosunt.

II. Promissio conditionalis neminem reddit certum. Atqui promissio de exauditione & auxilio, an nexam habet conditionem voluntatis divinæ Ergo non reddit nos certos de exauditione, & auxilio.

III. Multi invocantes etiam DEVM, calamitatibus oppressi succumbunt, & non exaudiuntur: Ergo Exauditionis certitudo non dependet à promissionibus de auxilio.

IV. Rex Ezechias invocans in tribulatione suâ DOMINVM, non promissiones illas, sed sua potiùs merita DEO ad animum revocat: Memento inquiens, DOMINE, quòd ambulaverim coram te in veritate, in corde perfecto, & rectè fecerim in ocutis tuis. 2. Reg. 20, 3. Ergo meritis potiùs nostris, quàm nudis promissionibus, in precatione confidendum.

V. Sic David Psal. 7, 9. & aliâs passim exaudiri rogat, propter justitiam suam: Judica inquiens, me DEVS secundum innocentiam meam, & secundum justitiam meam. Ergo ubi non est propriè justitia & sanctitas, Promissiones de exauditione precum nihil prosunt.

Verùm impietas istarum rationum ultrò elucescit, si ad analogiam fidei, tanquam infallibilem Veritatis Cynosuram, examinentur.

PRIMA ergò fallit turpi Sophismate

ὁμωνυμίας ἑτεροζητήσεως. Duo enim sunt genera promissionum divinarum. Quædam enim sunt Legales: Quædam verò Evangelicæ. Concludit ergo argumentum, vere quidem de promissionibus legalibus, quarum utilitas nulla est, nisi accedat impletio legis per nostra bona opera ac merita: Falsò autem de promissionibus Evangelicis, quæ ratione nostri purè sunt gratuitæ. Jam promissiones de exauditione precum sunt Evangelicæ quippè fundatæ in solâ DEI misericordiâ per & propter Christi meritum, fide apprehensum: sine omni respectu ad nostram dignitatem, opera aut merita: Sicut Daniel suo exemplo orare nos docuit, cap. 9. 18. Inclina DEVS meus aurem tuam, & audi: aperi oculos tuos, & vide desolationem nostram, & Civitatem, super quam invocatum est nomen tuum: neque enim in justitiis nostris prosternimus preces ante faciem tuam: sed in miserationibus tuis multis. Exaudi DOMINE: placare DOMINE: attende & fac, ne moreris PROPTER TEMETIPSVM. DEVS meus &c. Exemplo hoc & praxi omnium piorum edocti, in precibus nostris, nitimur promissionibus non legalibus, quæ exauditionis fundamentum ponunt impletionem Legis, & Operum merita: sed in promissionibus Evangelicis, quæ impletionem Legis à nobis non flagitant: sed in sola DEI misericordiâ propter Christi meritum, sunt fundatæ: ac proinde longè certissimæ.

ALTERA Ratio ijsdem vitijs laborat, & vera tantùm est de promissionibus legalibus, quarum conditio neminem potest reddere certum de exauditione, proptereà quòd nemo Legi perfectam præstat obedientiam quam DEUS in Lege à sectatoribus legis exigit: Falsissima autem de promissionibus Evangelicis, quæ voluntatem DEI de juvandis & exaudiendis nobis, non alligant ad conditionem aliquam dignitatis nostræ: sed in solidum ad misericordem DEI voluntatem, quâ vult exaudire omnes, Per Christum invocantes ipsum.

TERTIA Satio fellit Sophismate ὧδε τὸ μὴ ἑπόμενον, καὶ τὸ πῆ καὶ παρεξ ἁπλῶς. Nam 1. Promissiones de exauditione, in corporalibus, semper habent annexam exceptionem Crucis: Ubi DEUS summè bonus novit, è salute nostrâ esse, ut non semper ad nostrum placitum nos exaudiat. Hinc autem ad evertendam communem regulam, decertitudine promissionum, non valet Consequentia. Causæ enim DEO constant, ob quas non semper in corporalibus nos exaudiat: & quia voluntati ipsius nos, nostraque omnia, in hoc bonorum genere subjicimus utique DEUS etiam tum exaudit, quando negat, quod petimus: uti infrà de Exauditione ostendetur.

2. Ex particulari colligitur Universale in hunc modum: DEVS non semper exaudit hunc vel istam: Ergo promissiones non sunt certæ. Quod argumentandi genus tùm in alijs scientijs, tùm in Theologia præsertim, vitiosissimum esse, per se manifestum est.

QVARTA & QVINTA rationes eâdem vanitatis chordâ oberrant. Neque enim vel David vel Hiskias confidunt in dignitate personæ suæ, vel in meritis proprijs: sed in solâ DEI bonitate. Neque obstat Oratio Hiskiæ, cujus sensus non est, quòd glorietur de justitia operum, & proprijs meritis: Sed quòd DEO, ad animum revocat Justitiam illam fidei, quâ hactenus sustentatus, se toto Corde divinæ misericordiæ in omnibus afflictionibus commiserit: ut sit sensus: Obsecro, DOMINE, ut nunc me non deseras, quem admodum hactenus me nunquam deseruisti: Ambulavi coram te in veritate, & Corde perfecto: hoc est. non simulatè, aut hypocriticè tibi me totum concredidi, sed ex toto corde credidi Verbo tuo, quod est Veritas, in summis tentationibus, & plenam fidem ei adhibui: Ideò mihi auxiliatus es: Cur igitur nunc deprecantem reijceres, & orantem repelleres qui eadem veritate, eodemque corde perfecto, coram te ambulo, Te solum quæro & invoco.

Deinde probè notandum, de corporali tantùm hîc agi beneficio, nempe Liberatione ex præsenti morbo, & periculo mortis, Jam negatur minimè, quod DEUS in hujusmodi bonis respiciat etiam vitæ innocentiam, studium pietatis, & bonorum operum: secundum illud Psalm. 41, 2. Beatus qui sub venit egeno & pauperi: in die malâ liberabit eum DOMINVS & versu 4. Dominus opem feret ei super lectum doloris ejus. Quæ ipsa tamen divina compensatio non provenit ex dignitate, sive merito Operis beneficientiæ: sed ex solâ gratiâ & misericordiâ Dei promittentis.

Quoad Psalm. 7, 9. commendat David DEO justitiam non personæ, sed facti: ostendens se innocentem esse, & culpâ prorsus vacare in eo, cujus gratiâ Saul ipsum persequatur: ac si vitæ ac regno Saulis insidiatus esset. Injuriam ergo sibi fieri conqueritur, & lætâ conscientiâ gloriatur, de suâ hac in parte innocentiâ: Si feci, inquiens, istud: si est iniquitas hæc in manibus meis: si retribui mala benefactori meo Sauli: persequatur hostis animam meam. Quo stante in fumum abit collectio Pontificiorum, sub Sophismate ἑτεροζητήσεως ad decipiendum accommodata. Aliud. enim est quærere de justitia certi alicujus facti: aliud verò de Justitia personæ coram DEO: quam David ipse in sola DEI misericordia quærit, Psal. 51, 2 & sequentibus: Miserere mei DEUS secundum magnam misericordiam tuam: dele iniquitates meas multitudine miserationum tuarum: Quia malum coram te feci &c.

TERTIA causa precum impellens est Necessitas nostra & proximi. Nam afflictiones & calamitates, quibus indies exercetur pij, incitamento & calcari sunt, ut, nisi planè perire velimus, invocemus DEVM opitulatorem, uti maximum, ita optimum.

Jesa. 26, 16. In angustijs DOMINE quærimus faciem tuam.

Psal. 18, 5. 6. & 7. Circumdederunt me dolores mortis, & torrentes Belial conturbaverunt me: Funes inferni circumdederunt me: & laquei mortis præoccupaverunt me: In tribulatione hac mea invocavi DOMINVM, & ad DEVM meum clamavi: Et exaudivit de templo sancto suo vocem meam, &c.

Psal. 35, 16. & 17. Respice in me, & miserere mei, quia solitarius & pauper sum ego: Tribulationes cordis mei multiplicatæ sunt: de necessitatibus meis erue me.

Psal. 70, 6. Ego egenus & pauper sum: DEVS adjuva me: Adjutor meus, & liberator meus es tu: DOMINE ne morêris.

Psal. 86, 1. Inclina DOMINE aurem tuam, & exaudi me, quoniam inops & pauper sum ego.

QUARTA causa præcum impulsiva, est insignis earum utilitas. eaque multiplex. Nam 1. per cultum Invocationis sanctificatur nomen DEI, & gloria ipsi debita persolvitur. 2. Fœdus Gratiæ, quòd DEUS nobiscum inijt, subinde renovatur, fovetur, confirmatur: secundum illud Jesa. 64, 9. Respice quæsumus nos, quia populus tuus sumus. 3. Fides nostra in DEUM mirificè exercetur, & fit confirmatior. 4. Effectus exauditionis longè saluberrimus.

QUINTA & postrema causa est Exemplorum Sanctitas. Habemus enim in Schola precum Ducem & præcursorem Christum, Psal. 22. toto Matth. 14, 23. Joh. 17, toto Habemus Mosen, Davidem, Salomonem, Ezechiam, Danielem, Apostolos, & nullos non pios ac fideles, quorum exempla imitari decet: imò quorum exauditio spem fidemque nostram de simili exauditione certam reddere ac con firmare potest. Hinc enim argumentum tale in Theologia optimæ est consequentiæ, licèt è singularibus petitum: Hunc vel illum in necessitatibus suis clamantem exaudivit DEUS: Ergò & me exaudiet: Ille speravit in DOMINVM, & liberatus est ab omni malo. Ego itidem sperabo in DDMINVM. Ergo & liberabor. Ex hac ipsa Logica Spiritus Sancti argumentum mutuatus est David, Psal. 34, 7. Iste pauper clamavit: & DOMINVS exaudivit eum: & de omnibus tribulationibus ejus eripuit eum. Pertinet hùc priorum in nos collatorum beneficiorum commemoratio: Sæpius hactenus, imò semper eripuisti me DEVS, invocantem & confidentem in te. Ergo & jam me certò eripies. Sic David Psal. 31, 8. & 9. & 10. Ego speravi in DOMINO: exultabo & lætabor in misericordiâ ejus: Quoniam respexisti humilitatem meam, & eripuisti de necessitatibus animam meam: Nec conclusisti me in manibus hostium meorum: statuisti in loco spacioso pedes meos: Nunc ergo miserere mei DOMINE, quoniam tribulor. Sic Psal. 3, 5, 6. & 7. Voce meâ ad DOMINVM clamavi, & exaudivit me de monte sancto suo: Ego dormivi, & soporatus sum, & exurrexi, quia DOMINVS sustentavit me: Non ergo timebo myriades populi circumdantis me.


### Whether God is to be invoked: II. Question

II. Question.

Latin:

II. Quæstio.


### Whether the Only GOD is to be invoked

The Catholic Faith establishes that God alone, who is the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, is to be invoked: as the source of the whole adorable Trinity, and likewise of all goods, both spiritual and corporal. Nor indeed is the Son or the Holy Spirit excluded when we invoke the Father: since these three persons are one and the same God: and therefore, because of the undivided Unity of the divine Essence, when the Father is invoked, the Son and the Holy Spirit are invoked at the same time: and when either the Son or the Holy Spirit is invoked, God the Father is also invoked. In which sense also all three persons, in the Lord's Prayer and in the Holy Scriptures, are expressed by the one word of Father: Eph. 4:6. One God and Father of all, who is above all, and through all, and in all: not ὑποστατικῶς (hypostatically) but ὀυσιωδῶς (essentially) and indeed with the word Father taken only in respect to us.

Nor indeed does this assertion of ours conflict with our thesis, by which we confirmed above that it is also permitted to implore help from living men: nay, that men are obligated by the Law of God to provide mutual help. For 1. this imploring differs greatly from religious invocation. For the latter is done with full trust in God's mercy: but the former, if it be joined with trust in men, is so displeasing to God that it degenerates into manifest idolatry and blasphemy. 2. As much as the principal efficient cause and some instrument through which it acts differ from each other: so much do God and men differ from each other: so that He is always the Principal agent, but men behave as secondary causes, and means or instruments, through which God is often accustomed to derive his goods to others, as if through channels. Therefore the help of men is implored for no other end and respect than that, moved by these appeals of ours, they may do us good from that which divine kindness has liberally granted to them. 3. Although it is entirely permitted to implore the help of men in many things, it is not, however, granted in all. For those things which God alone can provide immediately, and does provide: such as those which concern the salvation of our soul: such as Regeneration: Repentance: Faith: Charity: Perseverance: Renewal: Salvation and eternal life: it would be a sin to ask these from men. For although in conferring these goods God uses the ministry of men: He alone nevertheless provides them, and bestows the blessing upon that ministry: without which, if it were absent, no mortal would ever become a participant in these goods; even if he were to use the ministry of men throughout his whole life.

Latin:

SOLUM DEUM, qui est Pater DOMINI nostri JESU CHRISTI, invocandum esse, statuit Fides Catholica : tanquàm fontem uti totius adorandæ Trinitatis, ita bonorum omnium & spiritualium, & corporalium. Neque verò excluditur Filius aut Spiritus Sanctus, cùm invocamus Patrem: Siquidem tres hæ personæ, unus & idem DEUS sunt: ac proinde propter indivisam Essentiæ divinæ Unitatem, invocato Patre, invocantur simul Filius, & Spiritus Sanctus: invocato verò vel Filio, vel Spiritu Sancto, invocatur etiam DEUS Pater. Quo sensu etiam omnes tres personæ, in Oratione Dominicâ, & in Scripturis sacris, Uno patris vocabulo exprimuntur: Ephes. 4, 6. Vnus DEVS & Pater omnium, qui est super omnes : per omnes; & in omnibus: non ὑποστατικῶς sed ὀυσιωδῶς & quidem respectu nostri tantùm accepto Patris vocabulo.

Neq; verò assertio hæc nostra repugnat Thesi nostræ, quâ supra confirmavimus, licet etiam ab hominibus viventibus axilium implorare: imò Homines ad mutua præstanda auxilia Lege DEI obligatos esse. Nam 1. imploratio hæc, á religiosâ invocatione plurimùm differt. Hæc enim fit cum plenâ fiduciâ in DEI misericordiam: Jlla verò si cum fiduciâ in homines sit conjuncta, tàm non Deo placet, ut in manifestam Jd測olatríam & blasphemiam degeneret. 2. Quantum inter se distant causa efficiens principalis, & Jnstrumentum aliquod, per quod illa agit: tantùm mutuò differunt DEUS, & Homines: ita, ut ille semper sit agens Principale, Homines verò habent se ut causæ secundæ, & media sive Jnstrumenta, per quæ DEUS sæpius sua bona, in alios, tanquam per canales derivare solet. Jmplorantur ergo auxilia hominum non alio fine ac respectu, quàm ut nostris hisce compellationibus moti, nobis benefaciant ex eo, quod divina benignitas ipsis liberaliter concessit 3. Licet multis in rebus hominum auxilia implorare omninò liceat, non tamen in omnibus id concessum. Quæ enim solus DEUS immediatè præstare potest, & præstat: qualia sunt, quæ animæ nostræ salutem spectant: ut Regeneratio: Pœnitentia: Fides: Charitas: Perseverantia: Renovatıo: Salus & vita æterna: ea ab hominibus petere nefas fuerit. Etsi enim in bonis istis conferendis DEUS utitur hominum ministerio: Ipse solus tamen ea præstat, & benedictionem ministerio isti largitur: sine quâ si esset, nemo mortalium unquàm istorum bonorum evaderet particeps; si maximè per omnem vitam Hominum ministerio uteretur.


### Whether the Only GOD is to be invoked: God is to be invoked

God is to be invoked.

Furthermore, the arguments by which it can be invincibly demonstrated against ancient and recent heretics that the cult of adoration or invocation is to be rendered to God alone, one in essence and three in persons, are these principal ones.

FIRST: The Word of God, which is the infallible rule and measure of all those things which pertain to faith and religion, teaches that God alone is to be invoked. Therefore. The antecedent is clearly evident from the following testimonies of Scripture.

Exod. 20:2. I am the Lord thy God: Thou shalt not have strange gods before me. But what it is to have strange gods is accurately explained in Deut. 6:13 and 14. Thou shalt fear the Lord thy God, and shalt serve Him ONLY, and shalt not swear by His name: You shall not go after strange gods of all the nations. Now indeed, let us have Christ the Savior as our interpreter of what it is to serve God alone, Matt. 4:10. Thou shalt adore the Lord thy God, and Him only shalt thou serve. And indeed God himself claims this cult of invocation as so proper to himself that he protests in express words that he will not give this glory to another: Isa. 42:8. and that there is no other God besides him: nor is there a just and saving God, besides him: Isa. 45:21.

And indeed by the evidence of this argument, at least by the instinct of nature, even the Gentiles themselves, however much they were idolaters, decided that only he who was God should be invoked. For although they worshipped almost infinite gods: yet they opined that those very ones were truly gods: and therefore they worshipped them religiously: otherwise, if they had known that they were not gods, they would never have worshipped them thus. In which part the Romanists err much more gravely today than the Gentiles. For the latter erred in that they thought there were many gods: but they did not err in that they decided that no one should be invoked unless he were God. But the Romanists err more dangerously in both ways: 1. that they impiously contend that many, besides God alone, are to be pursued with divine honor: 2. that they defer this cult specifically to angels and deceased saints, whom, however, they themselves deny to be gods.

What? That even the brute animals themselves bear witness to this first argument of ours against the Romanists. For David asserts concerning them that they invoke none but God: Ps. 147:9: Who giveth to beasts their food, and to the young ravens that call upon him. For although they do not know God and therefore, speaking properly, do not invoke him: yet the Holy Spirit implies that animals, with nature as their guide, do not cry out except to God, as the author and preserver of nature. In which sense philosophers rightly establish that animals are ruled by an unerring intelligence, namely, by God. In which sense also in the Psalms animals and other inanimate creatures are read to praise God.

THE SECOND: Invocation is the principal part of divine worship, and is always joined with adoration. Whence in the Scriptures it is defined as the Sacrifice of lips confessing the name of the LORD.

Now indeed divine worship, as also the glory of adoration, belongs to no creature, whether in heaven or on earth, outside of and beyond God. Therefore, neither does invocation.

THIRD: Whoever is to be invoked, in him must concur and be present all those requirements, or προσκείμενα, which must necessarily be present in him who can hear and answer our prayers: such as: 1. that he have the power of helping in all necessities: 2. that we be undoubtedly certain of his will to help: 3. that he look into the very hearts, sighs, and groans of men, i.e., that he be able to discern the internal affection of the mind and the serious from the hypocritical: 4. that he be able to be present with us in tribulation: 5. that he be supremely wise, and know what we need for salvation, as also how, when, and how far we are to be delivered: 6. and lastly: that he be supremely just, and according to the promises and communications promulgated in the Word of God, be able to render to each his own. But all these things befit none but the one and only God: as he who is 1. The only Omnipotent: Gen. 17. v. 1. Isa. 40. v. 10. & following: 2. he alone is merciful, and has the undoubted will to help us: Psalm 50. v. 15. Call upon ME in the day of tribulation, and I will deliver you. Ps. 91. v. 15. I am with him in tribulation, I will deliver him: John 16. v. 23. & 27. Whatever you ask the Father in my name, he will give you: For the Father himself loves you, because you have loved me. 3. God alone is the καρδιογνώστης Rom. 8. v. 27. He who searches the hearts knows what the Spirit desires. 4. God alone is present with us in tribulations. Ps. 91. v. 15. & Isa. 43. v. 2. Do not fear, you are mine: If you pass through the waters, I will be with you; and the rivers shall not cover you: When you walk in the fire, you shall not be burned, and the flame shall not burn in you: Because I the Lord your God, the Holy One of Israel, your Savior. 5. God alone knows what is profitable for us for salvation: Matt. 6. v. 9. Your Father knows what you need before you ask. Rom. 8. v. 26. The Spirit helps our infirmity: for we do not know what we should pray for as we ought.

Finally, God alone is supremely just, who crowns those who trust in him with every blessing: but he does not answer sinners, that is, the impenitent and the stubborn: But if anyone worships God and does his will, him he answers. John 9. v. 31. With these things standing thus, it is invincibly concluded that God alone is also to be invoked: and besides him no other creature, whether in heaven or on earth.

Which collection God himself instituted concerning himself Isa. 46. v. 3. & following: Hear me, O house of Jacob, and all the remnant of the house of Israel, who are carried by me from the womb, who are borne by me from the belly: Even to old age I am he, and even to gray hairs I will carry: I have made, and I will bear: I will carry, and I will save. To whom have you likened me, and made me equal, and compared me, and made me similar? Because you pour out gold from the bag, and weigh silver on the scales: hiring a goldsmith to cast a God: and they fall down, and worship: They carry him on their shoulders, bearing him, and placing him in his place, and he shall stand, and shall not move from his place; but also when they cry to him, he will not hear: he will not save them from tribulation. Remember this, and be confounded: return, O transgressors, to the heart: Remember the former age, for I am God and THERE IS NO OTHER GOD, nor is there any like me. My counsel shall stand, and all my will shall be done.

FOURTH: In whom alone one believes: he alone is also to be invoked. But one believes in God alone. Therefore God alone is to be invoked. The major premise is αὐτόπιστος καὶ ἀναπόδεικτος, since it has the Apostle as its author, Romans 10. v. 14. How shall they call upon him in whom they do not believe? The certainty of the minor premise is clearer than the midday sun from the entire scope of Holy Scripture: which aims solely at this, that all faith and hope be placed in GOD alone: so much so that the Romanists themselves have hitherto denied that one must believe in the Saints: thus cutting their own vines, as they say, or slaying themselves with their own sword.

FIFTH: He alone is to be invoked for help, to whom alone also thanks are to be given for help provided, and all the glory of benefits received is to be rendered. But to no creature, whether in heaven or on earth, is the glory of thanksgiving due. Therefore, neither is the glory of invocation. The connection of the major premise is manifest in itself: for the bestowing of help and the giving of thanks mutually posit and remove each other. The assumption is evident from the fact that GOD himself demands this glorification: Ps. 50. v. 15. and expressly protests that he will not give this glory to another. Isa. 42. v. 8. Whence the Church also is accustomed to conclude its prayers with this doxological verse: Glory be to the Father and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit, etc.

SIXTH: The end of all afflictions sent by God is this primary one, that our spirit, excited by the Holy Spirit through prayers and sighs, may be coupled to Christ by the bond of Faith, Hope, and love: and through Christ to the Father, and thus we may become One with God John 17. v. 21. but all these things look to the one and only God. Therefore in afflictions also God alone is to be invoked.

SEVENTH: No one of the Saints is ever read, either in the Old or in the New Testament, to have invoked anyone besides God alone: Ps. 115. v. 9. & following: The house of Israel has hoped in the Lord: he is their helper and their protector: The house of Aaron has hoped in the Lord: he is their helper and their protector: all who fear the Lord have hoped in the Lord: he is their helper and their protector. And the Epistle to the Hebrews chap. 13. v. 15. promulgated this general authentic rule: Through Christ let us offer the sacrifice of praise to GOD always, that is, the fruit of lips confessing his name. Whence the Savior himself, about to prescribe to us the most perfect manner of praying, teaches that God alone is to be invoked: by saying: Our Father, who art in heaven. Matt. 6. v. 9. Luke 11. v. 2.

EIGHTH and last is sought from the unanimous consent of Orthodox Antiquity. Cyprian Sermon 6. on the Lord's Prayer: To pray otherwise than Christ taught is not only ignorance, but also a fault: because he himself said: You have rejected the commandment of GOD because of your traditions. Tertullian in Apologeticus, chapter 30. Christians invoke the eternal God, the true God, and the living God. And a little later: I cannot pray for these things from any other than from Him from whom I know I shall obtain them: since He Himself is the one who alone grants them: and I am His servant, who observe Him alone, who offer to Him the rich and greater sacrifice, which He Himself commanded, prayer proceeding from a chaste body, from an innocent soul, from the Holy Spirit.

Chrysostom, Volume 5, in Homily 10 on repentance, Homily 4, column 856. Pay attention, therefore, you too, if you should see something too troublesome occurring, do not by any means flee to men, or look to the help of men: but passing over all, fly to that medicine of souls: for He alone can cure the heart, who fashioned our hearts individually. And after some things: Knowing these things, therefore, let us always flee to God, both willing and able to resolve our troubles.

But concerning this consensus of Antiquity, it shall be examined expressly against the Romanists in chapter 2.

Now concerning this second question, that one thing remains to be observed, that just as we showed above, with God the Father invoked; the Son and the Holy Spirit are also invoked at the same time: so now let us duly note the clear passages of Scripture confirming the invocation of both persons, both of the Son and of the Holy Spirit.

Latin:

eus invocandus.

Cæterùm argumenta, quibus Soli DEO uni essentiâ, trino personis, cultum adorationis sive Jnvocationis dependendum esse, contrà veteres & recentiores hæreticos invictè demonstrari potest, præcipua sunt hæc.

PRIMUM: Verbum DEI, quod infallibilis est regula ac mensura omnium eorum, quæ ad fidem ac religionem pertinent, Solum DEVM invocandum esse docet. Ergo. Antecedens ex sequentidus Scripturæ testimoniis luculenter patet.

Exod. 20, 2. Ego sum DOMINVS DEVS tuus: Non habebis Deos alienos coram me. Quid sit autem habere Deos alienos, accuratè explicatur Deut. 6, 13. & 14. DOMINVM DEVM tuum timebis, & illi SOLI servies, ac per nomen illius nõ jurabis: Nõ ibitis post Deos alienos cunctarum Gentium. Jam verò quid sit servire Soli DEO, habeamus interpretem CHRISTUM, Servatorem, Matth. 4, 10. DOMINVM DEVM tuum adorabis, & illi soli servies. Et sané DEus ipse cultum hunc Jnvocationis ita sibi proprium vendicat, ut disertis verbis protestetur se hanc gloriam non daturum alteri: Jesa. 42, 8. & non esse alium DEVM absque se: nec esse DEVM justum ac salvantem, præter se: Jes. 45, 21.

Et sanè argumenti hujus evidentiâ, Naturæ saltem instinctu, ipsi quoque Gentiles, quantumvis Jdololatræ moti, non nisi eum invocandum esse statuerunt, qui esset DEUS. Etsi enim infinitos fermè DEOS coluerunt: tamen illos ipsos reverà DEos esse opinati sunt: atque ideo religiosè adorarunt: aliàs si DEOS ipsos non esse, scivissent, nunquam ipsos sic coluissent. Quâ in parte multò gravius hodie errant Romanenses, quàm Gentiles. Hi enim errarunt in eo, quòd putarunt multos esse Deos: non autem errarunt in eo, quòd neminem, nisi qui DEVS esset, invocandum statuerunt. At Romanenses utroque modo periculosius errant: 1. quòd plures, præter DEUM solum, divino honore prosequendos impiè contendunt: 2. quòd Angelis & Sanctis defunctis cultum hunc in specie deferunt, quos tamen ipsi Deos esse negant.

Quid? quòd ipsa quoque bruta animantia primo huic nostro argumento contra Romanenses testimonium perhibent. De his enim asserit David, quòd invocent non nisi DEVM: Psal. 147, 9: Qui dat jumentis escam suam, & pullis corvorum invocantibus eum. Etsi enim non noverunt DEUM ac proindè propriè loquendo, ipsum non invocant: innuit tamen Spiritus Sanctus, Animantia naturâ duce, non clamare nisi ad DEUM, tanquam Naturæ autorem & conservatorem. Quo sensu rectè statuunt Philosophi, Animalia regi ab intelligentiâ non errante, nempè à DEO. Quo sensu etiam in Psalmis animalia & creaturæ cæteræ inanimatæ leguntur laudare DEUM.

ALTERUM: Invocatio est præcipua pars cultus divini, & semper conjuncta est cum adoratione. Vnde in Scripturis definitur Sacrificium labiorum confitentium nomini DOMINI.

Jam verò cultus divinus, ut & adorationis gloria, extra & præter Deum, nulli creaturæ vel in cœlo, vel in terra competit. Ergo neq; Invocatio.

TERTIUM: Quicunq; est invocandus, in eo debent concurrere, & esse præsentia omnia illa requisita, sive προσκείμενα, quæ necessario inesse debent illi, qui preces nostras audire & exaudire possit: qualia sunt: 1. ut potentiam juvandi in omnibus necessitatibus habeat: 2. ut de voluntate juvandi indubitatò nobis constet: 3. ut introspiciat ipsa corda, suspiria & gemitus hominum, h. e. internum animi affectum, & serium ab hypocritico discernere queat: 4. ut nobis in Tribulatione adesse possit: 5. ut sit summè sapiens, & norit, quibus ad salutem indigeamus, quomodo item, quando & quousq; simus liberandi: 6. & postremò: ut sit summè justus, & secundum promissiones ac communicationes, in Verbo Dei promulgatas, suum cuiq; tribuere possit. Atqui hæc omnia non nisi soli & uni Deo conveniunt: ut qui est 1. Omnipotens solus: Gen. 17. v. 1. Jes. 40. v. 10. & sequentibus: 2. solus misericors est, & indubia nos juvandi voluntatem habet: Psalm. 50. v. 15. Invoca ME in die tribulationis, & EGO eripiam te. Psal. 91. v. 15. Cum ipso sum in tribulatione, eripiam eum: Joh. 16. v. 23. & 27. Quicquid petieritis à Patre in nomine meo, dabit vobis: Ipse enim Pater amat vos, quia vos amastis me. 3. Solus DEUS est καρδιογνώστης Rom. 8. v. 27. Qui scrutatur corda, scit quid desideret Spiritus. 4 Solus DEUS nobis præsens adest in tribulationibus. Psal. 91. v. 15. & Jes. 43. v. 2. Noli metuere, meus es tu: Si transieris per aquas, tecum ero; & flumina non operient te: Cùm ambulaveris in igni, non combureris, & flamma non ardebit in te: Quia ego Dominus Deus Sanctus Israël Salvator tuus. 5. Solus DEUS novit, quid prosit nobis ad salutem: Matth. 6. v. 9. Scit Pater vester, quid opus sit vobis, antequàm petatis. Rom. 8. v. 26. Spiritus adjuvat infirmitatem nostram: nam quid oremus, sicut oportet, nescimus.

Tandem solus DEUS est summè justus qui confidentes in se omni benedictione coronat: peccatores autem, impœnitentes scilicet & præfractos non exaudit: Sed si quis Deum colit, & voluntatem ejus facit, hunc axandit. Joh. 9. v. 31. Quibus ita stantibus, invictè colligitur, Solum etiam Deum esse invocandum: & præter eum nullam creaturam aliam sive in cœlo, sive in terris.

Quam collectionem DEUS ipse de se instituit Jes. 46. v 3. & sequentibus: Audite me domus Jacob, & omne residuum domus Israël, qui portamini à meo utero, qui gestamini à meâ vulvâ: Usque ad senectam ego ipse, & usq; ad canos ego portabo: ego feci, & ego feram: ego portabo, & salvabo, Cui assimilastis me, & adæquastis, & comparastis me, & fecistis similem? Quia confertis aurum de sacculo, & argentum staterâ ponderatis: conducentes aurifabrum, ut fundat Deum: & procidunt, & adorant: Portant illum in humeris gestantes, & ponentes in loco suo, & stabit, ac de loco suo non movebitur; sed & cùm clamaverint ad eum, non audiet: de tribulatione non salvabit eos. Memento istud, & confundamini: redite prævaricatores ad Cor: Recordamini prioris seculi, quoniam ego sum Deus & NON EST ULTRA DEUS, nec est simili mei. Consilium meum stabit, & omnis voluntas mea fiet.

QUARTUM: In quem solum creditur: ille solus etiam est invocandus. Atqui in solum Deum creditur. Ergo solus Deus est invocandus. Major est αὐτόπιστος καὶ ἀναπόδεικτος, quippe auctorem habens Apostolum, Roman. 10. v. 14. Quomodo invocabunt eum, in quem non credunt? Minoris certitudo ex Scripturæ sacræ scopo universo, Sole meridiano clariùs patet: qui eo unicè collineat, ut omnis fides & spes in solo DEO collocetur: usque adeò, ut Romanenses ipsi, in Sanctos credendum esse, hactenùs negaverint: sic propria, quod ajunt, vineta cædentes, sive proprio se jugulantes gladio.

QUINTUM: Is solus in auxilium est invocandus, cui etiam soli pro auxilio præstito agendæ sunt gratiæ, & omnis acceptorum beneficiorum gloria est exolvenda. Atqui nulli creaturæ sive in cœlo, sive in terrâ, Gratiarum actionis gloria debetur. Ergo neq; Invocationis gloria. Connexum Majoris per se est manifestum: Auxilii enim collatio, & Gratiarum actio se mutuò ponunt & tollunt. Assumtio patet ex eô, quòd DEUS ipse Glorificationem hanc efflagitat: Psal. 50. v. 15. & Gloriam hanc alteri se non daturum differtè protestatur. Jes. 42. v. 8. Unde Ecclesia etiam semper preces suas concludere consvevit hoc versiculo δοξολογικῷ: Gloria Patri & Filio, & Spiritui Sancto &c.

SEXTUM: Finis afflictionum omnium à Deo immissarum, est primarius iste, ut Spiritus noster, à Spiritu Sancto per preces & suspiria excitatus, Fidei, Spei, & amoris vinculo copuletur Christo: & per Christum Patri, & ita fiamus Unum cum Deo Joh. 17. v. 21. atqui hæc omnia solum ac unum Deum respiciunt. Ergo in afflictionibus etiam solus Deus invocandus.

SEPTIMUM: Nemo Sanctorum unquàm vel in Veteri, vel in Novo Testamento legitur invocasse alium, præter Deum solum: Psal. 115. v. 9. & sequentibus: Domus Israël speravit in Domino: adjutor eorum, & protector eorum est: Domus Aaron speravit in Domino: adjutor eorum, & protector eorum est: omnes qui timent Dominum, speraverunt in Dominum: adjutor eorum, & protector eorum est. Et Epistola ad Hebræos cap. 13. v. 15. generalem hanc promulgavit authenticam: Per Christum offeramus hostiam laudis semper DEO, hoc est, fructum labiorum confitentium nomini ejus. Unde Servator ipse, perfectissimam orandi rationem nobis præscripturus, solum Deum invocandum esse docet: dicendo: Pater noster, qui es in cœlis. Matth. 6, v. 9. Luc. 11. v. 2.

OCTAVUM & postremum petitur ab unanimi consensu Orthodoxæ Antiquitatis. Cyprianus Serm. 6. de Oratione Dominicâ: Aliter orare, quam docuit Christus, non ignorantia sola est, sed & culpa: quia ipse dixit: Rejecistis mandatum DEI propter traditiones vestras. Tertull. in Apologetico cap. 30. Christiani invocant Deum æternum, Deum verum, & Deum vivum. Et paulò pòst: Hæc ab alio orare non possum, quàm a quo scio me consecuturum : quoniã & ipse est, qui solus præstat: & ego sum famulus eius, qui eum solum observo, qui ei offero opimam & majorem hostiam, quàm ipse mandavit, orationem de carne pudica, de animâ innocente, de Spiritu S. profectam.

Chrysostomus Tom. 5. in hom. 10. de pœnitentia, hom. 4. col 856. Adverte ergò & tu, si quid nimis molestum incidens videres, nequaquam ad homines confugeris, aut ad hominum perspexeris auxilium : sed universos transiens, ad animarum medicamentum illud evola : Cor enim curare solus potest, qui finxit sigillatim corda nostra. Et post aliqua: Hæc igitur scientes, ad Deum semper confugiamus, & volente, & potente nostras molestias solvere.

Verùm de hoc Antiquitatis consensu, capite 2. ex professo contra Romanenses fuerit dispiciendum.

Jam circa quæstionem hanc secundam, unum illud observandum restat, ut quemadmodum suprà ostendimus, invocato Deo patre; invocari simul etiam Filium, & Spiritum Sanctum: ita jam perspicua Scripturæ, utriufque personæ, & Filii & Spiritus S. invocationem confirmantia probè notemus.


### On the Invocation of the Son of GOD

Therefore, these sayings prove the invocation of the Son in the Old Testament: Psalm 45, verse 7. Your throne, O God, is for ever and ever: the sceptre of your kingdom is a right sceptre. Psalm 97, verse 8. Worship him, all you his angels. Psalm 98, verse 5. Exalt the Lord our God: and worship at his footstool, for it is holy. Isaiah 11, verse 10. In that day (there shall be) the root of Jesse, who stands for an ensign of the people, the Gentiles shall pray to him. Which prophetic prediction the Apostle in the New Testament applies to Christ in explicit words: Romans 15, verse 12. Again Isaiah said: There shall be a root of Jesse: and he that shall rise to reign over the Gentiles, in him shall the Gentiles hope. Philippians 2, verses 9 and 10. God exalted Christ: and gave him a name which is above every name: that in the name of JESUS every knee should bow, of things in heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth: and that every tongue should confess that Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father. Hebrews 1, verse 6. When he brought the firstbegotten into the world, he said: And let all the angels of God worship him, etc. Hence in the Gospel history one may read everywhere that the afflicted and those who were ill invoked and worshipped Christ, and indeed not only as he is God: but also as he is Man. This is evident from the customary formula of prayer: Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me. Matthew 20, verse 30. Luke 18, verse 38.

Thus the Canaanite woman, Matthew 15, verse 22. Have mercy on me, O Lord, Son of David. Thus the citizens of Jerusalem: Matthew 21, 9. Hosanna to the son of David. Thus the ten lepers: Luke 17, 13. Jesus, Master, have mercy on us. Stephen, Acts 7, 56 and 59. Behold, I see the heavens opened, and the SON OF MAN standing on the right hand of GOD: And they stoned Stephen, saying: LORD JESUS, receive my spirit. Ananias, Acts 9, verses 10 and 14. Lord, he has authority here to bind all who invoke your name. Revelation 5, verses 12, 13, and 14. Worthy is the Lamb that was slain to receive power, and riches, and wisdom, and strength, and honour, and glory, and blessing: But also every creature which is in heaven, and which is on the earth, and under the earth, and in the sea, and all that are in them, I heard saying: To him that sits upon the throne and to the LAMB be blessing, and honour, and glory, and power for ever and ever: And those four living creatures said, Amen: And those twenty-four elders fell down on their faces, and worshipped him who lives for ever and ever.

In the same manner, the father of the lunatic, Matthew 17, verse 14, and that man born blind, John 9, verse 38, bowed their knees and fell down on their faces before the humanity of Christ.

Pious Antiquity also supports this doctrine, as was shown in the Article on the Person of Christ: under the title concerning the worship of adoration communicated to the human nature of Christ. Let one Cyril suffice in this place, who in chapter 16 of John, Tractate 11, has it thus: In my name, says Christ, ask, that he may show himself to be the mediator and the bestower. For no one shall approach the Father, except through the Son, through whom we have access to the Father in the Spirit. Therefore, he says, no one comes to the Father, except through me: For in so far as he is Son and God, together with the Father he bestows good things upon us, which Paul showing said: Grace to you and Peace from God the Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ: But in so far as he is Mediator, and High Priest, and Advocate, he brings our prayers to the Father: for he himself bestows upon us freedom and confidence toward the Father. Therefore, one must pray in the name of the Saviour, if we wish to be heard by the Father.

Nor indeed is it the case, as heretics object, that Christ was invoked by men only with civil adoration, because he excelled in miracles. For Scripture attributes religious adoration to Christ in express words, testifying everywhere that men believed and placed all their trust in Christ.

Latin:

FIlii ergò Invocationem in Veteri Testamento probant hæc dicta: Psal. 45. v. 7. Solium tuum ô Deus, in seculum & sempiternum : Sceptrum rectum est sceptrum regni tui. Psal. 97. v. 8. Adorate eum omnes Angeli ejus. Psal. 98. v. 5. Exalte Dominum Deum nostrum : & adorate scabellum pedum ejus, quoniam sanctum est. Jesa. 11 v. 10. In die illa (celebris erit) radix Jesse, qui stat in signum populorum, ipsum gentes deprecabuntur. Quod vaticinium Propheticum Apostolus in Novo Testamento ad Christum difertis verbis accommodat: Rom. 15. v. 12. Rursus Jesaias dixit: Erit radix Jesse : & qui exurget ad imperandum Gentibus, in ipso Gentes sperabunt. Phil. 2. v. 9. & 10. Deus exaltavit Christum: & donavit illi nomen, quod est super omne nomen: ut in nomine IESU flectatur omne genu cælestium, terrestrium, & inferorum : & omnis lingua confiteatur, quod Dominus sit Jesus Christus in gloriam DEI patris. Hebr. 1. v. 6. Cùm introduxit primogenitum in orbem terræ dixit : Et adorent eum omnes Angeli Dei &c. Hinc in historiâ Evangelicâ passim legere licet, quòd afflicti & malè habentes, invocârint, & adorarint Christum, & quidem non tantùm qua Deus : sed & qua Homo est. Patet hoc ex consueta precationis formula: Jesu Fili David, miserere mei. Matth. 20. v. 30. Luc. 18. v. 38.

Sic mulier Cananæa, Matth. 15. vers. 22. Miserere mei Domine, Fili David. Sic Cives Hierosolymitani: Matth. 21, 9. Hosianna filio David. Sic decem leprosi: Luc. 17, 13. Jesu præceptor, miserere nostri. Stephanus Actor. 7, 56. & 59. Ecce video cœlos apertos, & FILIUM HOMINIS stantem à dextris DEI: Et lapidabant Stephanum dicentem: DOMINE JESU suscipe Spiritum meum. Ananias Actor. 9. v. 10. & 14. Domine, hic habet potestatem ligandi omnes, qui invocant nomen tuum. Apoc. 5. v. 12. 13. & 14. Dignus est agnus, qui occisus est, accipere virtutem, & divitias, & sapientiam, & fortitudinem, & honorem, & gloriam, & benedictionem: Sed & omnem creaturam, quæ in cœlo est, & quæ super terram, & sub terrâ, & in mari, & quæ in eis sunt omnia, audivi dicentia: Sedenti in throno & AGNO benedictio, & honor, & gloria, & robur in secula seculorum: Quatuor autem animalia illa dicebant, Amen: Et viginti quatuor illi seniores prociderunt in facies suas, & adorarunt eum, qui vivit in secula seculorum.

Eundem in modum genua sua flexerunt, & in facies suas prociderunt coram humanitate Christi, Pater Lunatici, Matth. 17. v. 14. & cæcus ille natus, Joh. 9. v. 38.

Doctrinæ huic suffragatur etiam pia Antiquitas, uti ostensum in Articulo de Persona Christi: tit. de cultu adorationis humanæ Christi naturæ communicato. Sufficiat hoc loco unus Cyrillus, qui in cap. 16. Joh. Tract. 11. sic habet: In nomine meo, inquit Christus, petite, ut mediatorem se, & collargitorem ostendat. Nullus enim accedet ad Patrem, nisi per Filium, per quem adductionem habemus ad Patrem in Spiritu. Idcò inquit, nemo venit ad Patrem, nisi per me: Nam in quantum Filius & Deus est, unà cum Patre nobis bona lar gitur, quod ostendens Paulus dicebat: Gratia vobis & Pax à Deo Patre, & Domino Jesu Christo: In quantum verò Mediator est, & Pontifex, & Paracletus, nostras preces ad Patrem adducit: ipse enim nobis libertatem ac fiduciam ad Patrem largitur. Orandum igitur in nomine Salvatoris, si exaudiri à Patre volumus.

Neqve verò est, ut excipiant hæretici, Christum civili tantùm adoratione invocatum fuisse ab hominibus, eò quòd miraculis excelleret. Nam Scriptura religiosam adorationem Christo tribuit expressis verbis, passim testificans, homines credidisse, omnemq; suam fiduciam posuisse in Christum.


### On the Invocation of the Holy Spirit

That the HOLY SPIRIT is true GOD, consubstantial with the Father and the Son, we take for granted in this place: and from this we invincibly conclude that he is to be followed with the worship of Adoration. For which reason it is also evident that he is named in the scriptures as the Spirit of Grace, of supplications, and of prayers: Zech. 12. v. 10.

2. We ought to call upon Him in whom we believe. But we believe in the Holy Spirit just as we do in GOD the Father and the Son: since we believe in GOD one in essence, but three in persons. Therefore we ought to call upon the Holy Spirit. Rom. 10, 14.

3. We ought to follow Him into whom we are baptized with the religious worship of adoration. But we are baptized into the Holy Spirit no less than into the Father and the Son. Therefore we ought to follow the Holy Spirit with the religious worship of adoration. The connection of the major premise is evident from this: Because Baptism is a covenant of a good conscience with GOD: But this covenant cannot be kept safe and sound except by faith, which is always joined with religious invocation. Therefore. The minor premise is evident from the formula of Baptism, prescribed by Christ Himself: Matth. 28, 19. Baptize them in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit.

4. Whoever is the author and bestower of all good things, he is to be invoked. But the Holy Spirit is the author and bestower of all good things. 1 Cor. 12, 3. and following. Therefore.

5. That He whom the Angels themselves adore is also to be adored by us, no pious person can doubt. But the Angels adore the Holy Spirit. Isa. 6, 3. Holy, Holy, Holy is the Lord GOD of hosts. Therefore. The minor premise is irrefutably evident from the fact that in Acts 28, 25, 26, & 27, that prophecy of Isaiah is expressly applied to GOD the Holy Spirit Himself.

6. Finally, the Apostles themselves, in praying for a divine blessing for their hearers, made express mention not only of the Father and the Son, but also of the Holy Spirit Himself: As in 2 Cor. 13, 13. The grace of our LORD JESUS CHRIST, the love of GOD, and the communion of the Holy Spirit be with you all. Amen.

Question III. Through whom one must pray.

Since GOD dwells in light unapproachable, and no mortal has ever seen Him, nor indeed can see Him, as the Apostle testifies in 1 Tim. 6, 16. The question is, through whom, whether Advocate, or Mediator, or intercessor, access may be opened to Him for our prayers. Here the Orthodox and the Romanists go into different opinions. For the latter thrust upon us in this place the departed heavenly ones, whom they call Saints: and they dream that our prayers are carried to GOD through their meditation, or intercession, or imploration. The vanity of which paradox we shall expressly refute in the second chapter. The Orthodox, however, themselves also admit a Mediator, indeed they urge Him as absolutely necessary: But they acknowledge no other, except CHRIST JESUS our Savior and only Mediator alone. They have, moreover, reasons and arguments for this affirmation that are clearly irrefutable. And indeed they bring forward the following foundations from the Scriptures:

John 14, 6. I am the way, the truth and the life, says the Savior: No one comes to the Father, except through me.

John 14, 13. Whatever you ask in my name, I will do it, that the Father may be glorified in the Son: And whatever you ask from me in my name, I will do it.

John 16, 23. Amen, amen I say to you, if you ask anything of the Father in my name, He will give it to you.

Acts 4, 12. There is no other name given under heaven among men, in which it is necessary to be saved, except the name of JESUS.

Rom. 3, 25. GOD set forth Christ as a propitiation.

Rom. 8. 34. Who is he that condemns? It is Christ Jesus, who died, nay rather who also rose again, and is at the right hand of GOD, and intercedes for us.

Ephes. 3, 12. In Christ we have boldness and access in confidence through faith in him,

Coloss. 1, 20. It pleased GOD, in CHRIST to reconcile all things.

1, Tim. 2, 5. There is one GOD, and one mediator between GOD and men, the Man Christ Jesus.

Hebr. 4, 15. & 16. We do not have a High Priest who cannot sympathize with our infirmities: but we have one who has been tempted in all things similarly, yet without sin: Let us therefore approach with confidence to the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy, and find grace for timely help. Hebr. 5. from verse 1. to 11. And chap. 7, 24. & 25. Christ, because he remains forever, has an everlasting Priesthood: Whence he is also able to save forever those who approach GOD through himself, always living to intercede for us.

Hebr. 9, 24. Jesus did not enter into Holy places made by hands, which are copies of the true: but into heaven itself, that he might now appear in the presence of GOD for us.

Hebr. 13, 15. Through Christ let us always offer a sacrifice of praise to GOD, that is, the fruit of lips confessing his name.

1. Petr. 1, 21. Through Christ you are believers in GOD, who raised him from the dead, and gave him glory, so that your faith and hope might be in GOD.

1. Petr. 2, 5. Built upon Christ, as living stones, to offer spiritual sacrifices, acceptable to GOD through Jesus Christ.

1. Joh. 2, 1. If anyone has sinned, we have an Advocate with the Father, JESUS CHRIST.

The whole Orthodox Antiquity supports this doctrine: from which it may suffice to have culled one or two testimonies in this place.

Ambrose, Vol. 4, book on Isaac and the soul, chap. 8. Christ, he says, is our eye, so that through him we may see the Father: he is our voice, through whom we speak to the Father: he is our right hand, through whom we offer sacrifice to GOD the Father.

Augustine, book 10 of the Confessions, chap. 42. Whom should I find to reconcile me to you, O GOD? Was I to go to the Angels? By what prayer? By what sacraments? Many trying to return to you, and not being able by themselves, as I hear, attempted these things, and fell into a desire for curious visions: and were deemed worthy of illusions. For the Devil was transforming himself into an Angel of light: but the Mediator between GOD and it was necessary for men, that he should have something similar to GOD, and something similar to men: lest in both he be similar to men, and be far from GOD, or in both similar to GOD, and be far from men, and thus not be a Mediator.

And what need is there of many words, when the whole Church of God, not even the Roman one excepted, has always most accurately observed these two things: 1. That it should close individual prayers to God the Father with this formula: Through JESUS CHRIST our Lord, Amen. 2. That it should for the most part make mention of the Cross and Passion of Christ, so that it might attribute the parts of the Mediator to Christ alone and exclusively.

With these things standing thus, Amandus Polanus is a blasphemer, who, so that he might not seem to ascribe the worship of adoration to Christ even according to his human nature, as Mediator: part 2 of his Syntagma, page 751, foists this truly twin distinction upon the Church of GOD. 1. The Mediator is adored, not for the sake of his created humanity, but for the sake of his eternal and omnipotent Deity itself. 2. According to his Deity he is adored, so that he may look upon hearts, hear groans, give the Holy Spirit, and other goods, according to his immense wisdom and power. But according to his humanity he is adored, so that he may approve of prayers and the hearing of them also by his human will: and in it, do what is his own. This opinion teems with the grossest errors. For 1. the state of the Controversy is changed Sophistically. For it is not asked, Whether the Cause, source, and origin of Adoration depends upon the assumed humanity, as if from a creature? For this very thing we also deny. But this is the Question, whether this Flesh, from the hypostatic Union with the λόγῳ, just as it has arrived into a real κοινωνίαν of the divine Majesty, so also into a participation of Adoration, in such a way that it is permitted to direct all our prayers, groans, and sighs to this very flesh of ours, as Omnipotent, Omniscient, Life-giving, Omnipresent, Adorable: not indeed separately, as if to flesh subsisting by itself; which thing Cyril in his work on the true faith to Theodosius, and in the Anathema opposed to Nestorius, rightly condemns as heretical; but as the Flesh of the Son of GOD, in the Unity of the person? Where we certainly hold the Affirmative, relying on those foundations, about which we have expressly disputed in the Place concerning the Person of Christ.

Furthermore, this Heretic attributes nothing more to the flesh of Christ than the approval of our prayers: and the operation of those things which exceed and surpass his natural powers. But he simply denies to the same flesh the hearing of groans, the searching of hearts, and the bestowing of the Holy Spirit. But what is it to recall Nestorianism into the Church with full sails, if this is not: For that distraction of operations necessarily implies the distraction of the Person, and the tearing asunder of the same into two. To which impiety we deservedly oppose the IVth Anathematism in the Ephesian Synod opposed to the Nestorian heresy in these words: If anyone divides the expressions which are contained in the Apostolic writings in two subsistences: and assigns some of those which are said about Christ by the Saints, or by himself, to a man, who is understood specially apart from the word of GOD: but deems others as worthy of GOD, to the word of GOD the Father alone, let him be Anathema.

Latin:

SPIRITUM SANCTUM esse verum DEUM, Patri ac Filio ὁμοούσιον, hoc loco pro confesso sumus: ac exinde Adorationis cultu ipsum prosequendum esse invictè colligimus. Quam ob causam etiam Spiritum Gratiæ, supplicationum, & precum, ipsum in sacris nominari constat: Zach. 12. v. 10.

2. In quem credimus, illum invocare debemus. Atqui in Spiritum Sanctum æque, ac in DEUM Patrem & Filium credimus: siquidem credimus in DEUM unum essentia, trinum vero personis. Ergo Spiritum sanctum invocare debemus. Rom. 10, 14.

3. In quem baptizamur, illum religioso adorationis cultu prosequamur, oportet. Atqui in Spiritum Sanctum haud minus atq; in Patrem ac Filium baptizamur. Ergo Spiritum Sanctum religioso adorationis cultu prosequamur oportet. Majoris connexum inde patet: Quia Baptismus est foedus bonæ conscientiæ cum DEO: Atqui foedus hoc non nisi fide, quæ cum religiosa invocatione semper est conjuncta, potest sartum tectum conservari. Ergo. Minor patet ex formula Baptismi, ab ipso Christo præscripta: Matth. 28, 19. Baptizate eos in nomine Patris, & Filii & Spiritus Sancti.

4. Quicunq; est autor & largitor bonorum omnium, ille est invocandus. At Spiritus Sanctus est autor & largitor bonorum omnium. 1. Cor. 12, 3. & sequentibus. Ergo.

5. Quem Angeli ipsi adorant, quin is nobis quoque adorandus sit, nemini pio potest esse dubium. at qui Angeli adorant Spiritum sanctum. Jes. 6, 3. Sanctus, Sanctus, Sanctus Dominus DEUS exercituum. Ergo. Minor irrefragabiliter patet inde, quod Actor. 28, 25. 26. & 27. concio illa Jesaiæ, ad ipsum DEUM Spiritum Sanctum expressè accommodatur.

6. Tandem Apostoli ipsi divinam benedictionem suis precati Auditoribus, non Patris tantum & Filii; sed ipsius quoque Spiritus Sancti expressam fecerunt mentionem: Ut 2. Cor. 13, 13. Gratia DOMINI nostri JESU CHRISTI, Charitas DEI, & Communicatio Sancti Spiritus sit cum omnibus vobis. Amen.

Quæstio III. Per quem sit Orandum.

CUm DEUS lucem inhabitet inaccessam, neque mortalium quisquam ipsum vide rit unquam, sed nec videre possit, teste Apostolo 1. Tim. 6, 16. Quæritur, per quem sive Advocatum, sive Mediatorem aut intercessorem, precibus nostris ad ipsum pateat accessus. Hic in diversas sententias abeunt Orthodoxi & Romanenses. Hi enim obtrudunt nobis hoc loco defunctos coelites, quos Sanctos appellant: & horum sive meditatione, sive intercessione sive imploratione, preces nostras ad DEUM deferri somniant. Cujus paradoxi vanitatem capite secundo ex professo refutabimus. Orthodoxi autem Mediatorem quidem & ipsi admittunt, imo ceu absolute necessariam urgent: Sed nullum agnoscunt alium, præter solum CHRISTUM JESUM Servatorem nostrum & Mediatorem unicum. Habent autem affirmati hujus rationes & argumenta plane αδιαλυτα. Et quidem ex Scripturis sequentia proferunt fundamenta:

Joh. 14, 6. Ego sum via, veritas & vita, inquit Servator: Nemo venit ad Patrem, nisi per me.

Joh 14, 13. Quicquid petieritis a Patre, in nomine meo, hoc faciam. ut glorificetur pater in filio: Et quicquid petieritis a me, in nomine meo, hoc faciam.

Joh. 16, 23. Amen, amen dico vobis, si quid petieritis a Patre in nomine meo, dabit vobis.

Act. 4, 12. Non datum est aliud nomen sub coelo hominibus, in quo oporteat salvari, praeter nomen JESV.

Rom. 3, 25. DEUS proposuit Christum propitiatorium.

Rom. 8. 34. Quis est, qui condemnet? Est Christus Jesus, qui mortuus, imo qui & resurrexit, & est ad dexteram DEI, & interpellat pro nobis.

Ephes. 3, 12. In Christo habemus fiduciam & accessum in confidentia per fidem ipsius,

Coloss. 1, 20. Complacuit DEO, in CHRISTO reconciliare omnia.

1, Tim. 2, 5. Unus est DEUS, unus est & mediator DEI & hominum, Homo Christus Jesus.

Hebr. 4, 15. & 16. Non habemus Pontificem, qui non possit compati infirmitatibus nostris: sed habemus tentatum in omnibus similiter, absq; tamen peccato: Adeamus ergo cum fiducia ad thronum gratiae, ut misericordiam consequamur, & gratiam inveniamus ad auxilium opportunum. Hebr. 5. a versu 1. ad 11. usque. Et cap. 7, 24. & 25. Christus, eo quod maneat in aeternum, sempiternum habet Sacerdotium: Vnde & salvare in perpetuum potest, accedentes ad DEVM, per semetipsum, semper vivens ad intercedendum pro nobis.

Hebr. 9, 24. Non in manufacta Sancta Jesus intravit, exemplaria verorum: sed in ipsum coelum, ut appareat nunc vultui DEI, pro nobis.

Hebr. 13, 15. Per Christum offeramus hostiam laudis semper DEO, hoc est, fructum labiorum confitentium nomini ejus.

1. Petr. 1, 21. Per Christum estis fideles in DEO, qui suscitavit eum a mortuis, & dedit ei gloriam, ut fides vestra, & spes esset in DEO.

1. Petr. 2, 5. Aedificati super Christum, tanquam vivi lapides, ad offerendum spirituales hostias, acceptabiles DEO per Jesum Christum.

1. Joh. 2, 1. Si quis peccaverit, Advocatum habemus apud Patrem, JESUM CHRISTUM.

Doctrinae huic suffragatur tota Orthodoxa Antiquitas: ex qua unum & alterum suffragium delibasse, hoc loco sufficiat.

Ambrof. Tom. 4. lib. de Isaac & anima, cap. 8. Christus, inquit, est oculus noster, ut per eum videamus Patrem: Ipse vox nostra, per quam loquamur ad Patrem: ipse dextera nostra, per quam DEO Patri Sacrificium offeramus.

August lib. 10. Confess. cap. 42. Quem invenirem, qui me reconciliaret tibi DEUS? An eundum mihi fuit ad Angelos? Qua prece? Quibus Sacramentis? Multi conates ad te redire, nec per seipsos va lentes, sicut audio, tentaverunt haec, & inciderunt in desiderium curiosarum visionu: & digni habiti sunt illusionibus. Diabolus enim erat transfigurans se in Angelum lucis: Mediator autem inter DEUM & homines oportebat, ut haberet aliquid simile DEO, & aliquid simile hominibus: ne in utroq; similis hominibus, longè esset à DEO, aut in utroq; DEO similis, longè esset ab hominibus, atque ita Mediator non esset.

Et quid multis opus, cum universa Ecclesia Dei, ne Romana quidem excepta, duo isthæc semper accuratissimè observarit: 1. Ut singulas ad Deum Patrem preces clauderet hac formula: Per IESUM CHRISTUM Dominum nostrum, Amen. 2. Ut plerumq; mentionem faceret Crucis & Passionis Christi, ut sic Mediatoris partes uni atq; soli Christo acceptum referret.

Quibus ita stantibus blasphemus est Amandus Polanus, qui ne Christo etiam secundum humanam naturam adorationis cultum, tanquam Mediatori adscribere videri possit: part. 2. Syntagmatis, pag. 751. geminam hanc verè distinctionem Ecclesiæ DEI obtrudit. 1. Adoratur Mediator, non humanitatis creatæ, sed æternæ & omnipotentis ipsius Deitatis causâ. 2. Secundum Deitatem adoratur, ut inspiciat corda, audiat gemitus, det Spiritum Sanctum, & alia bona, pro immensâ suâ sapientiâ & potentia. Secundum humanitatem verò adoratur, ut preces, & exauditionem etiam humana sua voluntate approbet: & in ea, quod ipsius est, faciat. Scatet hæc sententia crasfissimis erroribus. Nam 1. mutatur Sophisticè status Controversiæ. Non enim quæritur, An Causa, fons & origo Adorationis pendeat ab humanitate assumta, tanquam à creatura? Nam hoc ipsum & nos negamus. Sed hoc Quæstionis est, an Caro hæc, ex Unione hypostatica cum λόγῳ, uti in realem κοινωνίαν divinæ Majestatis, ita in consortium quoq; Adorationis ita pervenerit, ut ad hanc ipsam carnem nostram, tanquam Omnipotentem, Omnisciam, Vivificam, Omnipræsentem, Adorabilem, omnes nostras preces, gemitus ac suspiria dirigere liceat: non quidem seorsim, tanquam ad carnem per se subsistentem: id quod Cyrillus de rectâ fide ad Theodosium, & in Anathematismo Nestorio opposito, rectè ut hæreticum damnat; sed tanquam Carnem Filii DEI, in Unitate personæ? Ubi sanè Affirmativam tenemus, illis freti fundamentis, de quibus in Loco de Persona Christi ex professo disputavimus.

Deinde plus non tribuit Hæreticus iste carni Christi, quàm approbationem nostrarum precum: & earum rerum operationem, quæ naturales ipsius vires excedunt & superant. Exauditionem autem gemituum, scrutationem cordium, collationem Spiritus Sancti, eidem carni simpliciter negat. Quid verò est Nestorianismum plenis velis in Ecclesiam revocare, si hoc non est: Distractio enim ista operationum necessariò subinfert distractionem Personæ, ejusdemq; divulsionem in duas. Cui impietati meritò opponimus Anathematismum IV. in Synodo Ephesina Nestoriana hæresi oppositum his verbis: Si quis in duabus subsistentiis, eas voces, quæ in Apostolicis scriptis continentur, dividit: & quæ de Christo dicuntur à Sanctis, vel ab ipso, aliquas quidem ex his, velut homini, qui præter DEI verbum specialiter intelligatur, accommodaverit: aliquas autem tanquam dignas DEO, soli DEI Patris verbo deputaverit, Anathema sit.


### On the Invocation of the Holy Spirit: Virtues which are required in the one praying

Just as every good work, unless it proceeds from faith, cannot please GOD: Rom. 14, 23. Heb. 11, 6. So every Invocation, with whatever external splendor it may consist, if it is destitute of faith, is an abomination before GOD: Whence he introduces a general Aphorism in the same epistle to the Hebrews in the same chapter and verse. It is necessary for him who approaches GOD to believe that he is GOD, and that he bestows rewards upon those who seek him. For confidence of certain hearing and performance of those things which are asked, resting upon the promises, truth, and omnipotence of GOD, is the soul of true and saving invocation, as Scripture teaches 1 John 5, 15. We know that he hears us whatever we have asked: we know that we have those things which we ask from him. And James 1, 5 and 6. If any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask from GOD, who gives to all abundantly, and does not reproach: and it will be given to him: But let him ask in faith, doubting nothing: For he who doubts is like a wave of the sea, which is moved and driven about by the wind: therefore let not that man think that he will receive anything from the Lord.

Moreover, so that this Faith, regarding the right invocation of GOD, may contain itself within certain boundaries as it were, and not degenerate into some carnal security, it ought always to look to certain προσεχόμενα or requirements, expressed in sacred writings. But those are of two kinds: For they either regard the Person of the one praying: or the Object of the Prayer, which concerns the things being asked.

In the person of the one praying is required the ἐνέργεια of faith, not that saving faith which is treated in the article of Justification, but that which breaks forth into acts, as it were, external both with respect to GOD and with respect to the neighbor: a thing which Scripture is accustomed to define and express through certain operations of the Theological virtues. And such indeed are the virtues or operations.

1. True humiliation or contrition of the Heart, which, despairing utterly of one's own holiness and righteousness, seriously acknowledges, deplores, and detests both the internal corruption of all powers and external sins, and anxiously seeks and desires its gratuitous pardon on account of Christ. GOD never casts away such a contrite and humbled Heart, Ps. 51:19. Rather, He protests in express words in Isaiah that He will not look except upon the humble, the contrite in heart, and the one who trembles at the words of the LORD. Isa. 66:2.

2. Serious love of GOD and neighbor. For neither can be separated from the other, or subsist apart, according to the authentic word of John, ch. 4:20. If anyone says that he loves GOD and hates his brother, he is a liar. For he who does not love his brother, whom he sees, how can he love GOD, whom he does not see?

Latin:

QUemadmodum omne opus bonum, nisi ex fide proveniat, DEO placere non potest: Rom. 14, 23. Hebr. 11, 6. Ita omnis Invocatio, quocunque etiam externo splendore constet, si fide destituatur, coram DEO est abominatio: Unde generalem Aphorismum eadem epistola ad Hebræos infert cap. & versu iisdem. Accedentem ad DEUM oportet credere, quòd sit DEUS, & præmia largiatur iis, qui ipsum requirunt. Fiducia enim certæ exauditionis & præstationis eorum, quæ petuntur, nitens promissionibus, veritate, & omnipotentia DEI, est anima veræ & salutaris invocationis, sic docente Scriptura 1. Joh. 5, 15. Scimus quia audit nos quicquid petierimus: scimus, quod habeamus ea quæ petimus ab eo. Et Jac. 1, 5. & 6. Si quis vestrum indiget sapientia, postulet à DEO, qui dat omnibus opulenter, & non exprobrat: & dabitur ei: Postulet autem in fide, nihil hæsitans: Qui enim hæsitat, similis est fluctui maris, qui à vento movetur & circumfertur: non ergo existimet homo ille, quòd aliquid accipiat à Domino.

Cæterùm ut Fides hæc, quoad rectam DEI invocationem intra certos quasi cancellos se contineat, neque in securitatem aliquam carnalem degeneret, semper ad certa quædam προσεχόμενα sive requisita, in sacris expressa, respicere debet. Ea verò duûm sunt generum: Vel enim respiciunt Personam Orantis: vel Orationis Objectum, quod versatur circa res petendas.

In Orantis persona requiritur ἐνέργεια fidei non illa salvifica, de quâ in Justificationis articulo agitur: sed quæ in actus quasi externos tùm respectu DEI, tùm respectu proximi erumpit: id quod Scriptura per certas virtutum Theologicarum operationes definire & exprimere solet. Et tales quidem virtutes sive operationes sunt.

1. Vera Cordis humiliatio sive contritio, quæ de propriâ sanctitate & justitiâ penitùs despe rans, tum internam omnium virium corruptionem, tum externa peccata seriò agnoscit, deplorat & detestatur, ejusq; gratuitam condonationem propter Christum anxiè petit & desiderat. Tale Cor contritum & humiliatum DEUS nunquàm abijcit Psal. 51, 19. Quin disertis potiùs verbis apud Jesaiam protestatur, se non respecturum, nisi super humilem, contritum corde, & trementem verba DOMINI. Jesa. 66, 2.

2. Seria DEI & proximi dilectio. Neutra enim ab alterâ separari, aut seorsim subsistere potest: secundum authenticam Johannis, 1. cap. 4, 20. Si quis dixerit, quòd diligat DEUM & fratrem suum oderit, mendax est. Qui enim non diligit fratrem, quem videt: DEUM, quem non videt, quomodo potest diligere?


### On the Invocation of the Holy Spirit: Assiduity, Constancy and perseverance in praying

Both of these are most required in the true invocation of GOD: since the End of the law and of the commandments of GOD is Charity from a pure heart, and a good conscience, and faith unfeigned: 1 Tim. 1:5. If, therefore, without Charity these things [exist], no commandment of GOD can be truly kept: certainly without it, that which concerns the right invocation of GOD will not be kept either. Hence in sacred writings, the worship of all those who were destitute of these things by charity, however holy, religious, and splendid it may be, is read to have been an abomination to GOD: As Prov. 12:13, He who shuts his ear to the cry of the poor, he himself also shall cry, but shall not be heard. And hence it is that true worshippers [pray] not only for their own needs and those of our own, but also for others, and indeed as much for enemies and foes as for our brothers and friends.
