Quod utrumque à Stylo Spiritûs Sancti, & autoritate Canonicorum librorum simpliciter abhorret. Et quanquam Bellarminus primæ huic nostræ responsioni objicit exemplum Evangelistæ Lucæ, qui & ipse disertè fateatur, se historiam à se conscriptam mutuatum esse ab aliis: neque tamen ideò autoritatem Canonicam historiæ Lucæ fuisse negatam: Responsio tamen in promptu est longè evidentissima, quòd utrobique maxima se offert disparitas. Nam Lucas simul liquidò testatur, se historiam mutuatum esse ab iis, qui & ipsi habuerunt testimonium inhabitantis Spiritûs Sancti.

Deinde sanctè attestatur, se penitùs esse assecutum omnia, quæ ad historiam de Christo pertinebant. Luc. 1, 2. & 3. & 4. Verùm Macchabæorum historiæ autor, quoad librum secundum, ex scriptore planè Ethnico sua consarcinavit: deinde ipsemet de veritate omnium historiarum subdubitat. Unde de ficulneâ & plusquàm stramineâ exceptione Esavviticâ fieri potest judicium. Sed ad rem.

Secundo ergò loco quoad ipsum factum Judæ Macchabæi offerunt se in eo quædam laude & imitatione: quædam verò repehensione digna. Laude enim dignum est 1. quòd justum DEI judicium in interfectis agnoscit, ideò videlicet in prælio occisis, quòd anathemata sive donaria ex templo idololatrico, quòd apud Jamniam fuerat, furripuissent, & sub tunicis occultas-sent. 2. quòd cum suis ad preces conversus, orat, ne propter admissum peccatum totus exercitus deleatur. 3. quòd hortatur populum, ut tragico sociorum exemplo monitus, à consimilibus vel aliis peccatis sibi caveat. 4. quòd benè ac religiosè de Resurrectione cogitavit. Contrà verò reprehensione dignissimum, quòd Judas duodecim millia drachmarum (tot enim ex vulgatâ vitiosâ versione numerant Romanenses: quanquam textus Græcus duo tantùm habet millia, κατασκευάσαντες εἰς ἀργυρῖς δραχμὰς δισχιλίας) misit Hierosolymam, ut offerretur sacrificium pro peccato admisso in salutem interfectorum. Nam in totâ lege Mosaicâ ne unam quidem syllabam reperire licet, de aliquo pro mortuis sacrificio: Sic in universa Scriptura nullum mandatum, nulla promissio, nulla formula vel idea ullius precationis pro defunctis se offert. Factum ergò hoc Judæ, si maximè, prout narratur; ita evenerit, nullum novum articulum contra Scripturas Canonicas fabricare potest. Quid quòd illud quoque cum Romanensium exequiis diametraliter pugnat. Judas enim semel tantùm sacrificium pro mortuis offerre curavit, si modò curavit. At Romanenses unâ oblatione non contenti, exequias subinde repetunt, & primis jungunt septimas: septimis addunt tricesimas: his adjiciunt tandem anniversarias, eo fine, ut à simplicioribus omnem fermè defunctorum hæreditatem emungant, & inde inæstimabilem kquæstum faciant. Tandem ex universâ hac historiâ constat, Judam magis sollicitum fuisse de exercitu adhuc superstite, ne & ille in furore Domini exscinderetur: quàm de militibus interfectis. Curavit ergò offerri sacrificium non pro mortuorum, sed pro viventium adhuc salute. Quod factum uti suum habet fundamentum, in lege Mosis: ita énormiter errat Scriptor Ethnicus Jason, qui mortuorum causa id factum esse somniat: id quòd vel inde luculentiùs patet, quòd eadem historia describitur etiam 1. Macchab. 5, 57. & seqq. ubi tamen Sacrificii hujus nullum prorsus extat vestigium.

Objicitur SECUNDO locus ex Tobiæ 4, 14. Panem tuum, & vinum tuum super sepulturam justi constitue : & noli ex eo manducare & bibere cum peccatoribus.

Respondeo crassam committi ignörationem Elenchi, qui in præsenti argumento planè nullus militat. Neque enim vel γρῦ hoc loco habetur de precibus sive intercessionibus pro defunctis: sed tota hæc admonitio respicit tantùm curam pauperum superstitum, quæ fiebat ad sepulchra recens defunctorum. Erat enim veteribus illius temporis in more & consuerudine positum, ut post amicorum funerationes convivia celebrarent: & inde cibum ac panem mitterent ad sepulchra defunctorum, idque in usum pauperum, qui ibi convenire solebant. Quæ consuetudo si omnis absit superstitio, nihil per se vitii in se habebat: sed ad preces pro defunctis ex purgatorio liberandis nihil quicquam præsidii confert.

TERTIO objiciunt Esavvitæ exempla Sanctorum, quorum fit mentio in historia Canonica. Nam 1. Sam. 31. sive ultimo capite, versu 13. leguntur cives in Jabes Galaad, auditâ morte Saulis jejunasse septem diebus. Et 2. Sam. 1, 11. & 12. David flevisse & jejunasse scribitur pro Saule & Jonatha, & aliis in prælio occisis. Et cap. 3, 32. & 35. pro Abnero confosso à Joabo.

Sed quàm elumbia hæc sint argumenta, vel ipse agnovit Bellarminus, sic cauteriata nimis conscientiâ scribens, lib. 1. de purgatorio cap. 3. Col. 1784. Quanquam luctus, fletus & jejunia Davidis, ac aliorum pro interfectis, videntur facta fuisse in signum doloris & tristitiæ: tamen CREDIBILE est, præcipue facta esse ad juvandas animas defunctorum. Verùm Credibile hoc solvimus per non-Credibile, imò per manifestum crimen falsi. Ex universa enim historiâ Davidis, ejusdemq; Psalmis ne unus quidem proferri potest apex, qui in speciem saltem probabiliter confirmet, credidisse ipsum, animas defunctorum precibus superstitum vel ex inferno liberari, vel pœnas saltem earum mitigari posse: imò contrariam planè praxin ipsum observasse, liquidò constat, ex 2. Sam. 12, 14. ad versum usque 24. Ægrotante enim adhuc puero, ex adulterio cum Bethsabéa Uriæ uxore commisso, progenito, deprecabatur David DOMINUM pro parvulo, & jejunavit, humi prostratus, neque quicquam de cibo aut potu gustare voluit priùs, quàm parvulus diem suum obiisset: Quo defuncto, nullas amplius pro ipso ex limbo infantum liberando preces concepisse legitur: sed sic habet textus: propter infantem dum adhuc viveret, jejunavi & flevi: dicebam enim: Quis scit, si fortè eum mihi donet DOMINUS & vivat puer? Nunc autem quia mortuus est, quare jejunem amplius? Numquid potero revocare ipsum in vitam? Ego vadam magis ad eum (num ad limbum infantum, ex quo exclusi sunt senes?) ille verò non revertetur ad me.

Quibus ita se habentibus, respondemus ad producta exempla, fletus, luctus, & jejunia sanctorum, nihil fuisse aliud, quam signa doloris, & tristitiæ, cùm ex tragico obitu Saulis hostis, quàm ex amicorum Jonathæ & Abneri præmaturâ morte conceptæ. Quam luctus sui causam David ipse definivit, sic compellans reliquos aulicos, 2. Sam. 3, 38. & 39. Num ignoratis, quòd princeps & maximus cecidit hodiè in Israël. Ego autem adhuc tener sum, & modò unctus Rex. Quod ipsum de luctu civium in Jabes Galaad omninò est statuendum.

QVARTO objiciunt autoritatem S. Patrum, qui preces pro mortuis approbarunt. Sed paucis respondetur, nobis haud obscurum esse, quòd Epiphanius contra Arrianos, hæres. 75. Tertullianus de corona militis, & alibi, Augustin. lib. 9. Confess. capp. 12. & 13. Item in libro de curâ pro mortuis, si modò liber iste autorem Augustinum agnoscit: Item Serm. 34. de verbis Apostoli: Arnobius lib. 4. adversus gentes sub finem: & complures alii preces pro defunctis mirificè commendaverint: sed & illud constat, Patres hac in parte sibi non satis constitisse: id quod vel inde patet, quòd apud eosdem Patres in contrariam plane sententiam haud leviora legere licet testimonia: ut quando Augustinus Epist. 80. ad Hesychium scribit: In quo quemque invenerit suus dies novissimus, in hoc eum comprehendet dies mundi novissimus: Quoniam qualis in die isto quisque moritur, talis in die illo judicabitur.

Item Tractatu 49. in Johannem: Unusquisq;, cum suâ causâ dormit, & cum suâ causâ resurget.

Quod ipsum repetit lib. 2. quæst. Evangel. cap. 38. Et Serm. 15. de Sanctis.

Quam dissonantiam, imò manifestam contradictionem, si Esavvitæ in scriptis Patrum, quoad præsentem quæstionem, ita conciliaverint, aut nullus dubitationis scrupulus maneat reliquus: tum demum Patrum consensum ex istorum stare partibus largiemur. Rectè autem quidam Theologus hoc loco annotat: Patribus istis accidisse, quod hodiè quoq; doctis hominibus accidere videmus, ut nonnunquàm ad receptam suorum temporum opinionem ac consuetudinem scribendo respiciant: aliquando verò rem eandem ad normam sacrarum Scripturarum, absque Catholicæ opinionis ac consuetudinis respectu accuratiùs tractent, atque ita sit, ut de illâ diversimodè loquantur. Et hoc illis in hac quoque causa usu venit. Ubi de illâ secundum Scripturas loquantur, talia dicunt, quæ haudquaquàm opinioni ac à consuetudine receptæ, de sacrificio ac precibus pro mortuis faciendis patrocinantur: Ubi verò sese inconsultis scripturis consuetudini accommodant, ea dicunt, quæ contra nos adversarii adducunt.

Quis autem cordatus non videt, quàm alia sit illa (ut Cicero alicubi monet) cùm veritas ipsa limatur, in disputatione subtilitas: alia, cùm ad opinionem communem accommodatur oratio? & quàm in iis rebus, quæ fidem ac pietatem, salutemq; nostram concernunt, plus sit habendũ fidei doctrinæ sacris scripturis conformi, quàm receptis opinionibus absque Scripturis accommodatæ? Sanè quantum interest inter veritatem & opinionem communem, & quantum certiùs tenenda est veritas, quàm opinio: tantùm interest inter ea, quæ de statu mortuorum secundũ Scri pturas, & inter ea, quæ de sacrificiis & precibus prò mortuis faciendis, secundum usitatam opinionem dicuntur, tantumq; priora posterioribus sunt anteponenda. Hæc ille.

TANDEM objiciunt inveteratam Ecclesiæ consuetudinem orandi & sacrifican di pro mortuis. Sed & hæc ratio facilè refuratur. Nam 1. consuetudo nulla, quantumvis vetusta, facit vel articulum fidei Christianæ, vel errori parit patrocinium, nisi fundamentum ejus in sacris sit exprefsum vel ratione mandati, vel ratione promissionis. Deindè licèt vetusta ea sit, non tamen est vetustissima, neque ad Apostolorum ætatem pertingit: sed longo pòst tempore, tùm à Gentilitate, tùm ex quadam naturali affectione erga mortuos ortum habuit: ac zelo quòdam bono Episcoporum quorundam in Ecclesiâ retenta fuit, quanquam zelus ille non erat κατ᾽ ἐπίγνωσιν secundum scientiam, ac proinde vim Regulæ non obtinet. Rom. 10. Placet autem hoc loco audire Polydorum Virgilium lib. 6. cap. 9. pag. mihi 443. de origine justorum funebrium sic differentem: Quòd hodiè demortuorum anniversaria justa fiunt postridie Calendarũ Novembrium, ejus rei, ut fama est, & Petrus Damianus testatur, Odilo autor fuit. Is vir præfectus monachorum Cluniacensium, quum in Sicilia, sedente Joan. XVIII. Rom. Pontifice, circa Ætnam montem frequenter audiret gemitus clamoresq;, qui ibi, teste Trogo, partim ex fremitu ferventis æstus maris, partim ex eructatione Ætnéi ignis, ubi acrior per spiramenta cavernarum ventus incumbit, jugiter fiunt, ratus est Cacodæmones lamẽtari, quod per preces & sacrificia Christianorum, animæ mortuorum ab illis suppliciis liberarentur: nam cõstans vulgi opinio est, ad Ætnam montem, ubi perpetuum incendium tot jam seculis flagravit, aut ad inferos aditum patere, vel igneâ voragine sontiúm animas expiare. Itaque protinus egit cum suis monachis, ut postquàm Calendis Novembribus in divorũ omnium honorem sacrificâssent, sequenti itidem die cunctis vitâ privatis justa facerent. Quod institutum ut Pietatis plenum, Patres demùm receperunt. Fuit is annus circiter millesimus alter humanæ salutis.

Et post pauca. Apud gentes jampridem fiebant annua parentalia, id est, sacrificium quotannis ad honorem mortuorum: id quod (præter Tul lium in primâ Philippicâ, & in orat. pro Flacco) Macrobius & Cato tradunt, ita scribentes, Laurentiam annuæ parentationis honore dignatam. Erant enim Parentalia justa & convivia, quæ in funere, & ad sepulchrum parentum, cognatorumq;, concelebrabantur à filiis ac consanguineis, quorum autor

Aeneas fuisse fertur, qui eo pacto Anchisen parentem PRIMUS OMNIUM honoravit, supplicationibus coluit, atq; ejus memoriam nominis consecravit, veluti Virgilius lib. 5. Aeneidos describit. Sic nos illud ipsum institutum pro salute mortuorum servamus. Unde omninò factum videtur, ut Odiloni in mentem venerit hujus religionis celebrandis anniversarias demortuorum exequias.

Hactenus Polydorus Virgilius, qui eod. lib. 6. cap. 10. pluribus hac de re differit, & ostendit, quomodo ex consuetudine gentilium novendialia & septendialia sacrificia pro mortuis ad Ecclesiam DEI propagata sint. Quam sanè originem & autoritatem hujus cultus Romanensibus libenter & in solidum relinquimus: nostris verò Ecclesiis gratulamur, quòd cum superstitione & cæcitate istâ gentilitiâ nihil habent commercii. Et hoc unum est hoc loco notatu dignum.

Deinde Veteris Ecclesiæ consuetudo longè alium scopum ac finem sibi habebat propositum, quàm qualem hodie Romana urget Ecclesia. Quod ut evidenter pateat: audiamus hac de re differentem Dionysium libro de hierarchiâ Ecclesiast. cap. 7. in hunc modum: Sancto cœtu congregato, Pontifex, si Sacerdos fuerit, Orationem ad Deum inchoat, & gratiarum actionem. Psalmos accommodatos Pontifex & sacer chorus canunt. Ministri de sacris eloquiis promissiones nobis de resurrectione factas recitant. Deinde Archidiaconus, principalisq; Minister solos Catechumenos à foribus templi excludit, sanctos jam piè defunctos concelebrat. Pari panegyri & laude nuper functum prosequitur: hortatur omnes ad sibi lætam in Christo postulandam consummationem. Venerabilis præsul accedens, sacratissimam super quiescentem precem peragit. Post Orationem Pontifex defunctum salutat: Et post illum pariter omnes, qui adsunt. Super salutatum sanctum fundit oleum. Mox honesto in loco corpus cum aliis corporibus sanctis collocatur.

Hæc est summa totius capitis septimi hierarchiæ Ecclesiasticæ Dionysii. Unde patet, Orationes illas ad sepulchra sanctorum habitas, non fuisse satisfactiones pro peccatis mortuorum; proque eorundem liberatione ex purgatorio, neque pro mitigatione pœnarum & cruciatuum infernalium: sed laudationes piè defunctorum publicæ, & applicationes promissionum divinarum de Resurrectione carnis: exhortationes superstitum ad pietatis studium: declarationes denique Christianæ συμπαθείας & luctus, qui ex obitu tùm amicorum, tùm piorum quorumvis concipitur. Bestia enim, non homo esset, qui mortalitatis statu & conditione, à quâ ne Sanctissimi quiq; sunt excepti, longè miserrimâ non afficeretur. Et tales orationes pro mortuis, nostris in Ecclesiis non prohiberi asserit Apologia Confessionis Augustanæ: Et B. Lutherus in Confessione Majore.

Et quanquam progressu temporis accesserunt sacrificia: non tamen fuerunt ea Sacrificia propitiatoria pro peccatis, pœnis, & culpis defunctorum: sed tantum Sacrificia laudis & Gratiarum actionis, quibus DEO partim agebantur gratiæ, pro conservatione Ecclesiæ, & ministerio piorum: partim verò Sanctorum defunctorum virtutes & merita celebrabantur. Et de his Sacrificiis agit Cyprianus, lib. 4. epist. 5. ostendens, quomodo pro martyribus Laurentio, Ignatio, & reliquis consueverit Ecclesia offerre Sacrificia: agunt etiam plærorumque Patrum & Græcorum & Latinorum dicta, magno numero à Bellarmino producta, lib. 1. de Purgatorio cap. 6. ita ut in illorum citatione perpetua committatur Sophisticatio non causæ ut causæ, & turpis diversissimorum finium confusio.

Facessant ergò blasphemæ, & ipso verborum sono execrandæ orationes Romanensium pro mortuis: ut quando clamant: Libera DOMINE animas omnium fidelium defunctorum de pœnis inferni, & de profundo lacu, libera eas de ore leonis, ne absorbeat eas tartarus, ne cadant in obscurum. Impietatem certè hanc pleno ore redarguit Servator Luc. 23, 43. ad latronem dicens: HODIE mecum eris in Paradiso: redarguit liber Sapientiæ cap. 3, 1. Justorum animæ sunt in manu DEI, & NON TANGET eas tormentum mortis, sed sunt in PACE: Redarguit Apostolus 2. Cor. 5, 10. Reportabit unusquisq; juxta id, quod fecit in corpore: Et Gal. 6, 5. Unusquisq; proprium onus portabit: Quicquid enim seminaverit homo, hoc & metet: Redarguit Justinus Philosophus & Martyr: Post animæ, inquiens, excussum statim fit bonorum & malorum distinctio: Ducuntur enim ad loca ab Angelis, quæ eis digna sunt: Bonorum quidem animæ in Paradisum: Improborum verò ad inferorum loca: Redarguit denique B. Hieronymus, inquiens: Mortis tempestate submersus, quasi lignum, ubicunque cecideris, ibi manebis jugiter, sive te rigidum & trucem, sive clementem & misericordem, ultimum invenerit tempus.

Sed de hac quæstione hoc loco plus satis: Quæ in specie de Purgatorio Pontificio observationem merentur, infrà in Articulo de inferno expedientur.


### Question VIII. On the hearing of our prayers

The whole Scripture testifies that the prayers of the just, calling upon him in Spirit and in truth, are of great moment before GOD: As Ps. 18:7: In my distress I called upon the LORD, and cried to my GOD: And he heard my voice from his holy temple: and my cry came into his sight to his ears. Ps. 50:15: Call upon me in the day of trouble, I will deliver you, that you may honor me. Ps. 91:15: He called upon me, and I will hear him, and I am with him in trouble, and I will deliver him, and glorify him. Ps. 118:5: From trouble I called upon the LORD, and he heard me and set me in a broad place. Ps. 145:18: The LORD is near to all who call upon him, to all who call upon him in truth: And ver. 19: He will do the will of those who fear him, and will hear their supplication, and will save them. Isaiah 58:9: Then you will call, and the LORD will hear you: you will cry, and he will say: Behold I am here, because I the LORD your GOD am merciful. And ch. 65:24: It shall be, before they call, I will hear, says the LORD: while they are still speaking I will hear. John 16:23: Amen, amen I say to you: Whatever you ask the Father in my name, he will give you. Furthermore, GOD himself wishes a clear distinction to be sought from this, between the idols of the nations and the true GOD of Israel: so that the idolaters, put to shame by their idols, at length execrate them, and raging against GOD rush into desperation and blasphemy. An illustrious example of which thing may be read in the history of Elijah, who insults the idol of the Baalites for the reason that it cannot hear the prayers of those crying out: Call, he says, upon the names of your Gods: and I will call upon the name of the LORD my GOD: and the GOD who hears by fire, let him be GOD. Therefore the prophets of Baal called upon the name of Baal from morning until noon, saying: Baal hear us, and there was no voice, nor anyone to answer. And when it was already noon, Elijah mocked them saying: Cry with a louder voice: for he is a GOD, perhaps he is meditating, or is on a journey, or certainly he is sleeping, so that he may be awakened, etc. 1 Kings 18:24 and following. Such an opposition is read also in Psalm 115:3 and following. Our God is in heaven: All things whatsoever he wills, he does. But the idols of the nations are gold and silver, and the works of the hands of men: They have a mouth, and do not speak: they have eyes, and do not see: They have ears, and do not hear: they have noses, and do not smell: they have hands, and do not feel: they have feet, and do not walk: neither is there any speech in their throat, etc. Concerning which matter let chapter 6 of Baruch be seen, Isaiah 44:10 and following, and ch. 46:6 and following, Wisdom 15:15 and following. Hence the Prophet foretold confusion to the Idolaters, Isaiah 1:29.

Latin:

Magni apud DEUM momenti esse preces justorum, invocantium eum in Spiritu & veritate, universa testatur Scriptura: Ut Psal. 18, 7. In angustia mea invocavi DOMINUM, & ad DEUM meum clamavi: Et exaudivit de templo sancto suo vocem meam: & clamor meus in conspectu ejus pervenit ad aures ejus. Psal. 50, 15. Invoca me in die tribulationis, eripiam te, ut honore me afficias. Psal. 91, 15. Clamavit ad me, & exaudiam eum, & cum ipso sum in tribulatione, & eruam eum, ac glorificabo eum. Psal. 118, 5. De tribulatione invocavi DOMINUM, & exaudiens me collocavit in lato. Psal. 145, 18. Prope est DOMINUS omnibus invocantibus eum, omnibus invocantibus eum in veritate: Et ver. 19. Voluntatem timentiu se faciet, & deprecationem eorum exaudiet, & salvabit eos. Jesaiæ 58, 9. Tunc invocabis, & DOMINUS exaudiet te: clamabis, & ipse dicet: Ecce adsum, quia misericors sum DOMINUS DEUS tuus. Et cap. 65, 24. Erit, antequam clament, ego exaudiam, dicit DOMINUS: adhuc illis loquentibus ego audiam. Johan. 16, 23. Amen, amen dico vobis: Quicquid petieritis Patrem in nomine meo, dabit vobis. Deinde DEUS ipse luculentum discrimen peti vult ex eo, inter idola gentium, & inter verum DEUM Israëlis: ut quod Idololatræ pudefacti ab idolis suis, tandem ea execrantur, & fremebundi contra DEUM ruunt in desperationem, & blasphemiam. Cujus rei illustre exemplum legere licet in historia Eliæ, qui Baalitarum idolo ideo insultat, quòd preces clamantium exaudire non possit: Invocate, inquiens, nomina Deorum vestrorum: & ego invocabo nomen DOMINI DEI mei: & DEUS qui exaudierit per ignem, ipse sit DEUS. Prophetæ ergo Baal invocabant nomen Baal de mane usq; ad meridiem, dicentes: Baal exaudi nos, Et non erat vox, nec qui responderet. Cumq; esset jam meridies, illudebat eis Elias dicens: Clamate voce contentiore: DEUS enim est, forsitan meditatur, aut in itinere est, aut certè dormit, ut excitetur &c. 1. Reg. 18, 24. & seqq. Qualis oppositio legitur etiam Psalmo 115, 3. & seqq. Deus noster in cælo: Omnia quæcunq; vult, facit. Idola autem gentium sunt aurum & argentum, & opera manuum hominum: Os habent, & non loquuntur: oculos habent, & non vident: Aures habent, & non audiunt: nares habent, & non olfaciunt: manus habent, & non palpant: pedes habent, & non ambulant: nec loquela est ulla in gutture ipsorum &c. Quâ de re videatur caput 6. Baruch Iesa. 44, 10. & seqq. & cap. 46, 6. & seqq. Sap. 15, 15. & seqq. Hinc Propheta Idololatris Confusionem prædixit, Iesa. 1, 29.


### Caput II. A'ntioetikon

Thirdly, there are readily available examples of the pious, testifying quite clearly concerning the hearing of prayers. By the prayers of Joshua, the Sun certainly stood still in the midst of the heavens for the space of one day, so that he might defeat his enemies: Jos. 10. By the prayers of the Patriarch Abraham, GOD took away the ignominy of barrenness from the house and family of Abimelech. Gen. 20. By the prayers of Isaac, his wife conceived and bore a son. Gen. 25. By the prayers of Jacob, the hostile spirit of his brother Esau was changed. Gen. 32. By the prayers of Moses, frogs, flies, hail, thunder, and locusts ceased to devastate the land. Exod. 8. and ch. 9. and ch. 10. The Amalekites are defeated Exod. 17. The fury of the LORD is appeased regarding the worship of the calf, when He was willing to cut off the whole people: Exod. 32. and ch. 33. His sister Miriam is cured of leprosy Num. 12. The people are delivered from fiery serpents. Num. 21. And who could enumerate each and every example of those who, by their prayers, obtained from GOD whatever they asked, such as Samson, Judg. 15. and ch. 16. Anna the mother of Samuel, 1 Sam. 1. Samuel himself, 1 Sam. 7. and ch. 12. David throughout the Psalms: Solomon, 1 Kings 8. and ch. 9. Elijah, 1 Kings 17. and ch. 18. Elisha, 2 Kings 4. Hezekiah, 2 Kings 20. The Apostles, Acts 4. Peter, Acts 9. Cornelius, Acts 10. Paul and Silas, Acts 16. and the last chapter.

And with the same philanthropy and clemency with which GOD followed the prayers of those, He follows ours as well: so that no one of the pious can doubt the hearing of his prayers. For they were not heard on account of any singular merits or some singular holiness, but on account of this very goodness and mercy of His, which He promised to all who call upon Him in Spirit and in truth, that is, out of true faith. Whence the Savior introduces a general Aphorism John 16, 23. Amen, amen I say to you: Whatever you ask the Father in my name, He will give to you, and James ch. 5, 16. The assiduous prayer of a just man avails much.

And this hope of being heard is so built upon the truth and certainty of divine promises among the pious; that they hold it as most certain that GOD always hears prayers, not only by granting what is asked, but also by denying the same. For He never denies spiritual gifts to those who call upon Him by the power of His promises, but always bestows them. But if He denies bodily gifts, even if He does not grant them according to our pleasure, He nevertheless hears our prayers. The reason is: Because we asked for those goods with this condition, namely, if His holy will so permits, if it can even contribute to His glory and our salvation. When, therefore, GOD denies such things, what else will a pious mind judge than that GOD did not will it, since it was contrary to His glory and our salvation? By which agreement, surely, no pious person will doubt that our prayers have also been heard by GOD. Hence rightly Augustine somewhere: GOD in His mercy denies some things which He grants in His anger.

Latin:

Tertiò in promptu sunt exempla piorum, de exauditione satis dilucidè testantia. Ad preces certè Josuæ Sol in medio cœli unius diei spatio constitit, ut hostes profligare posset: Jos. 10. ad preces Patriarchæ Abrahami, sterilitatis ignominiam à domo & familia Abimeleci abstulit DEUS. Genes. 20. Ad preces Isaaci concepit uxor, & peperit filium. Genes. 25. ad preces Jacobi mutatus Esavi fratris animus hostilis. Gen 32. ad preces Mosis cessant vastare terram ranæ, muscæ, grando, tonitrua, locustæ. Exod. 8. & cap. 9. & cap. 10. profligantur Amalecitæ Exod. 17. placatur furor DOMINI ob cultum vituli, exscindere volentis universum polum: Exod. 32. & cap. 33. curatur à leprâ soror ipsius Mirjam Num. 12. liberatur populus à serpentibus igneis. Num. 21. Et quis enumeraret singula & universa exempla eorum, qui ad preces suas impetrarunt à DEO, quicquid petierunt, ut Simsonis, Judic. 15. & cap. 16. Anna mater Samuelis. 1. Sam. 1. Samuel ipse, 1. Sam. 7. & cap. 12. David passim in Psalmis: Salomon, 1. Reg. 8. & cap. 9. Elias, 1. Reg. 17. & cap. 18. Elisæus. 2. Reg. 4. Ezechias, 2. Reg. 20. Apostoli, Act. 4. Petrus, Act. 9. Cornelius, Act. 10. Paulus & Silas, Act. 16. & cap. ultimo.

Et quâ philanthropiâ & clementiâ prosecutus est DEUS istorum preces, eâdem nostras quoque prosequitur: ita ut piorum nemo de exauditione suarum precum dubitare possit. Neque enim exauditi illi fuerunt, propter singularia quæpiam merita, aut singularem quandam sanctitatem, sed propter hanc ipsam suam bonitatem, & misericordiam, quam promisit omnibus invocantibus ipsum in Spiritu & veritate, hoc est, ex verâ fide. Unde Servator generalem infert Aphorismum Joh. 16, 23. Amen, amen dico vobis: Quicquid petieritis Patrem in nomine meo, dabit vobis, & Jacobus cap. 5, 16. Multùm valet deprecatio justi assidua.

Et hæc Exauditionis spes apud pios ita est superstructa veritati & certitudini promissionum divinarum; ut exploratissimum habeant, DEUM semper non tantùm largiendo petita, sed & eadem negando exaudire preces. Nam spiritualia dona vi promissionum suarum invocantibus nunquàm negat, sed semper confert. Corporalia verò dona si maximè neget, & ad nostrum placitum non largiatur, nihilominùs tamen exaudit preces nostras. Ratio est: Quia bona illa cum hac conditione expetivimus, si nimirùm ita ferat sancta ipsius voluntas, si cedere etiam id possit ad gloriam ipsius, & nostram salutem. Quando ergo DEUS talia negat, quid judicabit mens pia aliud, quàm DEUM illud noluisse, quippè suæ gloriæ & saluti nostræ adversum. Quo sanè pacto preces etiam nostras exauditas esse à DEO, nemo pius dubitaverit. Hinc rectè Augustinus alicubi: Quædam negat DEUS propitius, quæ concedit iratus.


### Caput II. A'ntioetikon: Chapter II. Antithetical. the Errors of the Romanists Mostly concerning the Worship and invocation of Saints and Angels, and the blessed in…

CHAPTER II. ANTITHETICAL. THE ERRORS OF THE ROMANISTS MOSTLY CONCERNING THE WORSHIP and invocation of Saints and Angels, and the blessed in heaven: and of inanimate things, such as consecrated hosts, relics, and also the Cross or the Crucifix.

Overcome by the evidence and irrefragable certainty of these arguments, the Romanists find nowhere to turn: and therefore, so that they may at least in some way palliate and disguise the worship of deceased Saints, they transform themselves into various forms: which we shall briefly taste.

And at the beginning, indeed, the more recent Jesuits stubbornly deny that it was ever taught or believed in the Papacy that Saints are to be adored. Hence they invent various species of Invocation and adoration, and indeed mostly three, according to the three excellences of the Objects, concerning which Bellarmine speaks thus in book 1 of the beatitude of the Saints, ch. 12, page 195 for me.

The first is divine and infinite excellence: to which corresponds the first species of adoration, namely latria, which is a certain highest prostration and inclination of the will with the apprehension of GOD as the first principle and last end, and thus the highest good: Such Adoration belongs to GOD alone. The second is human or natural excellence, which is placed in human virtues, dignities, and ranks: To which corresponds civil worship and a certain human observance: concerning which there is no dispute in this place. The third excellence is a certain mean between divine and human: such as the Grace and glory of the Saints: And to this excellence corresponds dulia: But because among holy creatures, the Humanity of Christ, if considered separately, excels singularly on account of the Union to the Word: and similarly the B. Virgin, as mother of the Son of God, so surpasses other Saints that she can be called our Lady and Queen, which does not befit other Saints, except very imperfectly: therefore Theologians divide dulia into dulia properly so called, and hyperdulia: attributing the former to other Saints: but the latter only to the Humanity of Christ, and his mother.

Bellarminus urges the same second evasion, and indeed against that argument of ours, by which we proved from chapter 63, 16 of Isaiah: Abraham does not know us, and Israel does not recognize us: and consequently the Saints, since they are ignorant of our affairs, are not to be invoked. Therefore he answers two things: 1. That Abraham, Israel, and the remaining fathers of the Old Testament did not know their living descendants, because, being established in limbo at that time, they were not yet blessed. 2. That the saints indeed do not know our affairs naturally and by their own power. as they are manifested to them by God, just as God revealed many things to Elisha and the prophets, whether through the beatific vision or through a new revelation. For because they enjoy the brightness of God, therefore they see all things in GOD. lib. 1. de Sanct. beat. cap. 20. pag. mihi 1990. 1991. lit. A. & D.

The same Esauvite frames the third evasion thus: cap. 17. pag. mihi 1967. lit. C. It is not permitted to ask of the saints that they grant us glory and grace, and other means to blessedness, as if they were the authors of divine benefits. For help is to be expected from the saints, not as from authors, but as from intercessors: and therefore, the saints are not to be invoked as God, but as those who can obtain from GOD what they wish.

The same Bellarmine has a fourth evasion in lib. 1. de Sanct. beat. cap. 17. From the invocation of the saints nothing is taken away from the office of Christ, who is our advocate and intercessor before the Father. For the saints are not our immediate intercessors before God: but whatever they obtain for us from GOD, they obtain through CHRIST. And pag. mihi 1968. & 1969. Nothing, he says, is asked of the saints other than that they intercede before God, so that the merit of Christ may be applied to us. Hence that trite distinction of the Romanists took its origin, between a Mediator of Redemption and a Mediator of intercession.

But these are fig leaves with which the Romanists strive to cover the shameful parts of their impiety.

For as regards the first evasion, it is almost more riddled with faults than it is completed with words. For first, the state of the controversy is changed, which does not consist in that which the Esauvite takes upon himself to prove, namely, whether a different and distinct honor belongs to GOD, and another to men. For we ourselves concede this very thing, nor do we despoil the saints of their due honor. But this is the question: whether that honor which is owed to the saints, and to the angels, and to the heavenly ones, and which the Romanists name δουλείαν and ὑπερδουλείαν, is to be defined by the worship of Invocation? Because Bellarmine does not prove this, he basely begs the question and trifles sophistically. Augustine indeed urges the distinction between the honor owed to GOD and the honor owed to the saints everywhere: but not in the Papist sense. For he says only this, that the worship which is owed to GOD must be accurately distinguished from that honor with which parents, and magistrates, and others who have deserved well of the Church and the Christian faith, whether living or deceased, are to be treated: and he calls it idolatry in express words if anyone wishes to transfer the honor which is owed to GOD to creatures: saying, the saints are to be honored for the sake of imitation, not adored for the sake of religion.

2. This distinction is destitute of all support from the Scriptures. For although different words occur in the Hebrew sources, which signify either to serve, or the same thing as to bow oneself for the sake of reverence, or to supplicate, or to adore: yet always, when they are predicated of GOD, they denote religious worship, and indeed expressed not only by the word λατρείας, or προσκυνήσεως Adoration, but also by the word δυλείας. For that same GOD who said: You shall adore the LORD your GOD: also said: You shall serve HIM ALONE. Deut. 6, 13. Matth. 4, 10. Hence in the New Testament that religious worship of GOD is most frequently defined by δυλείαν. Matth. 6, 24. Act. 20, 19. Rom. 7, 6. & 25. & cap. 16, 18. 1. Thes. 1, 9. Nay more, the word λατρείας, which the Romanists take as referring only to the religious worship of GOD, is adapted in the Scriptures even to those services which are accustomed to be rendered to men, as is evident from the version of the LXX interpreters. Levit. 22, 7. (in the Latin edition it is chapter 23.) πᾶν ᄇργον λατρευτὸν ὐ ποιήσετε, You shall do no servile work. Num. 28, 25. πᾶν ᄇργον λατρευτὸν ὐ ποιήσετε. The Esauvite distinction therefore collapses and has gone up in smoke: and Ludovicus Vives deserves more credit, who in his commentaries on chapter 4 of book 10 of St. Augustine's City of God, proves from Suidas the Greek lexicographer and Laurentius Valla that these two words δυλεύειν and λατρεύειν are to be used indifferently. The word ὑπερδουλείας, as far as the present business is concerned, is clearly fictitious: and its meaning can be proven neither from the Old nor from the New Testament (for in the latter it is clearly not found).

3. This distinction of the Esauvites diametrically conflicts with the analogy of faith. Because since invocation is the chief part of divine worship: certainly he who invokes either angels or saints transfers the worship owed to GOD alone to creatures, and is an idolater.

4. This protestation of the Romanists is contrary to the fact: and indeed in two ways. 1. Because something different is taught by Papist writers. Gabr. Biel on the Canon of the Mass, Lect. 30, writes: We have recourse to the saints, so that by their merits and prayers we may arrive at the glory of immortality: and by their suffrages we may be led from faith to vision: from hope to the reality: from effort to the prize: from life to the fatherland. And in lib. 3. Sent. dist. 19. Although the passion of CHRIST is the principal merit, on account of which grace, the opening of the kingdom, and glory are conferred: yet it (namely, the passion of Christ) is never the sole and total meritorious cause. And a little later: Although the removal of an obstacle is the remission of sin, both original and actual: the opening of the kingdom is the conferring of Grace: yet to both, some merit of the Fathers cooperated, by which they merited the remission of sins by congruity,

Latin:

CAPUT II. Α'ΝΤΙΘΕΤΙΚΟ'Ν. ROMANENSIUM POTISSIMUM ERRORES CIRCA CULtum & invocationem Sanctorum & Angelorum, & beatorum cœlitum: rerumq; inanimatarum, ut hostiæ consecratæ, reliquiarum, item Crucis sive Crucifixi.

ARgumentorum istorum evidentiâ & irrefragabili certitudine victi Romanenses, quò se vertant, nuspiam inveniunt: ac proinde ut aliquo saltem modo cultum Sanctorum defunctorum palliare & fucare possint, in varias formas se transmutant: quas paucis delibabimus.

Ac initiò quidem recentiores Esavvitæ mordicùs negant; In Papatu unquam vel traditum, vel creditum fuisse, Sanctos esse adorandos. Hinc varias Invocationis & adorationis species, & quidem potissimùm tres, secundum tres Objectorum excellentias confingunt, de quibus sic Bellarminus lib. 1. de Sanctorum beatitudine, cap. 12. pag. mihi 1951.

Prima est excellentia divina & infinita: cui respondet prima species adorationis, nempe λατρεία, quæ est summa quædam voluntatis prostratio, & inclinatio cum apprehensione DEI, ut primi principii, & ultimi finis, atque adeò summi boni: Qualis Adoratio soli DEO convenit. Secunda est excellentia humana seu naturalis, quæ posita est in humanis virtutibus, dignitatibus, gradibus: Cui respondet cultus civilis, & observantia quædam humana: de quâ hoc loco non disceptatur. Tertia excellentia est quædam media inter divinam & humanam: qualis est Gratia & gloria Sanctorum: Et huic excellentiæ respondet δουλεία: Sed quia inter sanctas creaturas, Humanitas Christi, si seorsim consideretur, singulariter excellit propter Unionem ad Verbum: & similiter B.Virgo, ut mater Filii Dei, ita præstat aliis Sanctis, ut dici possit Domina & Regina nostra, quod aliis Sanctis non convenit, nisi admodùm imperfectè: ideò Theologi δουλείαν dividunt in δουλείαν propriè dictam, & ὕπερδουλείαν: tribuentes illam Sanctis cæteris: istam verò soli Humanitati Christi, & matri ejus.

Alterum effugium idem urget Bellarminus, & quidem contra illud nostrum argumentum, quo ex cap. 63, 16. Esaiæ comprobavimus: Abrahamus nescire nos, & Israëlem ignorare nos: ac proinde Sanctos, quippe rerum nostrarum nescios, non esse invocandos. Duo ergò respondet: 1. Abrahamum, Israëlem, & patres reliquos Veteris Testamenti, non cognovisse posteros suos viventes, quia tum in limbo constituti, nondum beati erant. 2. Sanctos nescire quidem res nostras, naturaliter, & virtute propria. Cognoscere verò eas, quatenus à Deo ipsis manifestantur, quemadmodum Elisaeo & Prophetis multa Deus revelavit, sive per beatificam visionem, sive per novam revelationem. Quia enim Dei claritate fruuntur, ideò eos in DEO omnia videre. lib. 1. de Sanct. beat. cap. 20. pag. mihi 1990. 1991. lit. A. & D.

Tertium effugium idem Esauvita sic informat: cap. 17. pag. mihi 1967. lit. C. Non licet à Sanctis petere, ut nobis tanquàm autores divinorum beneficiorum gloriam & gratiam, aliaq; ad beatitudinem media concedant. Expectandum enim est auxilium à Sanctis, non ut ab autoribus, sed ut ab impetratoribus: ac proinde, Sancti non sunt invocandi, ut Dei: sed ut qui impetrare à DEO possunt, quod volunt.

Quartum effugium idem Bellarminus habet lib. 1. de Sanct. beat. cap. 17. Ex invocatione Sanctorum nihil decedit officio Christi, qui est advocatus, & intercessor noster apud Patrem. Sancti enim non sunt immediati intercessores nostri apud Deum: sed quicquid à DEO nobis impetrant, per CHRISTUM impetrant. Et pag. mihi 1968. & 1969. Nihil, inquit, à Sanctis petitur aliud, quàm ut intercedant apud Deum, quò nobis Christi meritum applicetur. Hinc originem traxit trita illa Romanensium distinctio, inter Mediatorem Redemtionis, & Mediatorem intercessionis.

Verùm folia sunt hæc ficulnea, quibus impietatis suæ pudenda Romanenses tegere satagunt.

Nam quoad primum effugium, pluridus illud fermè scatet vitiis, quàm verbis absolvitur. Primùm enim mutatur status controversiæ, qui non in eo consistit, quod sibi probandum sumit Esauvita, nempè, An alius ac diversus honor DEO, alius hominibus competat. Nam hoc ipsum & nos concedimus, neque Sanctos debito suo honore spoliamus. Verùm hoc est in quæstione, An honor ille, qui Sanctis, & Angelis, & cœlitibus debetur, & quem Romanenses δουλείαν & ὑπερδουλείαν nominant, per cultum Invocationis definiendus sit? Quòd dum non probat Bellarminus, turpiter petit principium, & Sophisticè nugatur. Augustinus sanè distinctionem inter honorem DEO, & honorem Sanctis debitum, passim urget: sed non sensu Pontificio. Hoc enim tantùm inquit, cultum, qui debetur DEO, accuratè distinguendum esse ab eo honore, quo afficiendi sunt parentes, & magistratus, aliiq; de Ecclesiâ & fide Christianâ benè meriti, sive viventes, sive defuncti: ac disertis verbis Idololatriam appellat, si quis honorem, qui DEO debetur, ad creaturas transferre velit: Honorandi, inquiens, sunt sancti propter imitationem: non adorandi propter religionem.

2. Distinctio haec omni Scripturarum praesidio destituitur. Etsi enim in fontibus Hebraeis diversa occurrant vocabula, quae vel servire, vel idem significant, ac reverentiae causa sese inclinare, vel supplicare, vel adorare: semper tamen, quando de DEO praedicantur, religiosum cultum notant, & quidem non λατρείας tantùm, sive προσκυνήσεως Adorationis, sed & δυλείας vocabulo expressum. Nam idem ille DEUS, qui dixit: DOMINUM DEUM tuum adorabis: dixit etiam: Illi SOLI servies. Deut. 6, 13. Matth. 4, 10. Hinc in Novo Testamento religiosus ille cultus DEI, per δυλείαν frequentissimè definitur. Matth. 6, 24. Act. 20, 19. Rom. 7, 6. & 25. & cap. 16, 18. 1. Thes. 1, 9. Quin imò λατρείας vocabulum, quod de solo religioso cultu DEI accipiunt Romanenses, in Scripturis accommodatur ad ea etiam servitia, quae hominibus solent praestari, uti patet ex versione LXX. interpretum. Levit. 22, 7. (in Lat. edit. est caput 23.) πᾶν ᄇργον λατρευτὸν ὐ ποιήσετε, Omne opus servile non facietis. Num. 28, 25. πᾶν ᄇργον λατρευτὸν ὐ ποιήσετε. Corruit ergò, & in fumum abiit distinctio Esavvitica: & potiorem fidem meretur Ludovicus Vives, qui in commentariis super cap. 4. libri 10. D. Augustini de Civitate DEI ex Suida Lexicographo Graeco, & Laurentio Valla comprobat, duobus istis vocabulis δυλεύειν & λατρεύειν indifferenter utendum esse. ὑπερδυλείας vocabulum, quoad praesens negotium, planè est fictitium: ejusque significatio neque ex Veteri, neque ex Novo Testamento (in hoc enim planè non reperitur) probari potest.

3. Distinctio haec Esavvitarum diametraliter pugnat cum analogiâ fidei. Quia enim invocatio est praecipua pars cultus divini: utique qui invocat vel Angelos, vel Sanctos, cultum soli DEO debitum transfert ad creaturas, & Idololatra est.

4. Protestatio haec Romanensium est contraria facto: & quidem dupliciter. 1. Quia diversum docetur à Scriptoribus Pontificiis. Gabr. Biel. super Canonem Missae Lect. 30. scribit: Ad Sanctos recurrimus, ut eorum meritis & precibg ad immortalitatis gloriam perveniamus: atque eorum suffragiis de fide perducamur ad visionem: de spe ad rem: de studio ad brabeson: de vita ad patriam. Et in lib. 3. Sent. dist. 19. Licet CHRISTI passio sit principale meritum, propter quod cõ- fertur gratia, apertio regni & gloria: nunquam tamen ea (Christi videlicet passio) est Sola & totalis causa meritoria. Et paulò pòst: Quanquam ablatio obstaculi est Remissio peccati, tam Originalis, quàm actualis: apertio regni est collatio Gratiae: ad utrũq̃, tamen aliquod meritum Patrũ cooperabatur, quo meruerunt remissionem peccatorũ de Congruo,


### Caput II. A'ntioetikon: Formula of adoration and of the saints under the Papacy

and the opening of the kingdom by merit, without which neither would sin have been forgiven, nor the kingdom opened. Thus even today under the Papacy this Formula of Absolution obtains: May the Passion of CHRIST, the merit of the most blessed virgin Mary, of Peter, of Paul, and of all the Saints, absolve you from all your sins.

Then: Because the formulas of prayers directed to the Virgin Mary and the Saints testify to something different, and clearly contrary to the Efavvitic confession. Certainly the whole Davidic Psalter is adapted to the virgin Mary, with the same words of adoration, worship, invocation, and similar terms, which denote honor owed to GOD alone, being retained. Hence in the Antidotarium Mariae the Romanists incite one another to a clearly divine worship of Mary, with these words: Come let us exult to our Lady, let us rejoice to the virgin our savior: Come, let us adore, and fall down before her. Let us confess our sins to her with tears: Come to her all you who labor and are burdened, and she will give refreshment and solace to your souls: She is mercy and pardon, giving refusal to no one, and a most kind helper. May you kindly receive and hear this suppliant prayer, and grant us eternal life. I know that you can do all things that you wish: I adore and bless your most high feet, with which you trampled the head of the ancient Serpent, with all his pomps.

Of the same kind or impiety is also that invocation of Mary, which is read in the Horarium, whose title is, History according to the Augustan choir, concerning the commemoration of the most blessed virgin Mary: Rejoice heavenly matron, exulting magnify your GOD the Savior, who made you singular: You wished to call yourself the handmaid of JESUS CHRIST: But the divine Law also teaches, You are His Lady: For justice and reason have it, that the Mother is superior to the Son: Therefore pray suppliantly, and command sublimely, that in the evening of the world, He may lead us to the heavenly kingdoms: You are the repairer of the age, the end of exile, the washing away of sin, the way of counsel, the confidence of the reward, the ladder of heaven, the gate of Paradise.

Such also is that one: O my Lady Saint Mary, I commend to you today, and daily, and in the hour of my departure, my soul and my body into your blessed faith, and singular custody, and into the bosom of your mercy: ALL my hope, and my consolation: all my anxieties and my miseries: I commit to you my life and the end of my life, so that through your most holy intercession, and through your merits, all my works may be directed and disposed, according to your will and that of your Son, and my necessity, Amen.

And in another these things are read: I pray you, Mary, that you may save me from sins, from scandals, from all human confusion, from the wrath of the tremendous judgment, from unclean thoughts, from all mortal sin, from sudden and unforeseen death, from all dangers of soul and body, of honor and of my affairs: and never permit me to commit such a sin, by which I might lose your grace. Give me amendment for the past: custody for the present: caution for the future. Give me prompt help in this life: Be for me in the tremendous judgment an advocate before your Son, our Lord Jesus Christ: Amen.

Thus regarding the remaining Saints, it can by no means be denied that divine worship and honor is paid to them even today in the Papacy, which is evident 1. from the Pontifical Litany. 2. from the prayers directed separately to each of the Saints, which one may read in the Examination of the Council of Trent by M. Chemnitz, among which also stands out this one directed to Bartholomew: Saint Bartholomew, by the grace which you have merited, I, a miserable and polluted servant, a most filthy sinner, beseech you, that by your precious merits you may free me from all the wiles of the Devil, and from the snares and terrors, and from the damnation and illusion of the visible and invisible enemy, in the day of the wrath of the Lord, and at the end of my life, that you may come to my aid against my adversaries, and supported by twin lights, show me the footsteps of the lamb.

Thus they also invoke Cyriacus: Most holy Cyriacus, renowned martyr of Christ, who expelled demons from the two daughters of kings in the name of Christ: expel from me every demonic illusion, whether I sleep or wake, lest they exercise any power over me: but may I always be protected by your help, and be saved for ever and ever, Amen.

3. This is evident from the practice of the Roman Church, which, through a certain pagan impiety, has set over individual things, diseases, and necessities, and even the goods of fortune, certain and peculiar gods, and indeed as helpers or assistants to be implored. Hence Catherine presides over philosophical studies, just as Pallas did among the pagans. Hence Nicholas and Christopher preside over the sea, just as Neptune and Palaemon, and other marine gods and goddesses, did among the pagans. Hence Anna and Erasmus, when invoked, grant wealth and riches, just as Juno did among the pagans: Hence George is the patron of warriors and knights, just as Mars, Castor, and Pollux were among the Gentiles: Hence Urban and Medard preside over the cultivation of vineyards, just as Bacchus did among the Gentiles. Hence Lawrence and Florian rule over fire, just as Vulcan and Vesta did among the pagans: Hence Cosmas and Damian preside over medicine: Ivo over jurisprudence: Luke over painting: Crispin and Crispinian over shoemakers; Severus over fullers, etc. Hence individual patron gods or helpers are assigned to almost every nation: Olaus to the Swedes: Canute to the Danes, etc. Hence certain gods are assigned to individual diseases, as if they were physicians: St. Valentine cures epilepsy: Anthony the holy fire: Roch and Sebastian the plague: Apollonia toothache: Odilia and Juliana dimness of the eyes, etc.

With these things standing thus, it is clearer than the midday sun that those testimonies of the Scriptures, which confirm that in all necessities help is to be sought from GOD alone, and that Christ alone is the door, the gate, and the ladder of heaven, are laboring and utterly collapsing. Psalm 71:5. You, O LORD, are my expectation and my hope: You are my trust from my youth. Jer. 17:7. Blessed is the man who has trust in Jehovah and whose confidence is Jehovah.

Thus Christ alone is proclaimed our hope: 1 Tim. 1:1, 1 Pet. 1:21. And Christ himself: I am the way, the truth, and the life: No one comes to the Father, EXCEPT THROUGH ME. John 14:6. Nor does Christ share this glory with his mother, the virgin Mary: For here he obtains that [saying], Matt. 12:48: Who is my mother? Behold, these are my mother and my brothers: For whoever shall have done the will of my Father, who is in heaven, he is my brother, and mother, and sister. To which pertains that [saying] of Epiphanius, Tom. 2, lib. 3, haer. 79: In truth, the body of Mary was holy: But not God: in truth she was a virgin, a virgin and honored: but not given for adoration: but she herself adoring him who was born from her flesh. And after a few words: Let Mary be in honor: But let the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit be adored: let no one adore Mary: I do not say to a woman, nay, not even to a man, but to GOD is this mystery owed. Nor do the Angels grasp such glory: ναὶ μὴν ἅγιον ἦν τὸ σῶμα τῆς Μαρίας, οὐ μὴν θεός· ναὶ δὴ παρθένος ἦν ἡ παρθένος, καὶ τετιμημένη, ἀλλ᾿ οὐκ εἰς προσκύνησιν ἡμῖν δοθεῖσα, ἀλλὰ προσκυνοῦσα τὸν ἐξ αὐτῆς σαρκὶ γεγεννημένον. And after some things: ἐν τιμῇ ἔστω Μαρία, ὁ δὲ πατὴρ, καὶ υἱὸς, καὶ ἅγιον πνεῦμα προσκυνείσθω· τὴν Μαρίαν μηδεὶς προσκυνείτω· οὐ λέγω γυναικὶ, ἀλλ᾿ οὐδὲ ἀνδρὶ θεῷ προστέτακται τὸ μυστήριον. ὅτε ἄγγελοι χωρῶσι δοξολογίαν τοιαύτην. And again. What scripture has told of this? Which of the prophets has commanded that a man be adored, much less a woman? It is indeed an excellent vessel, but a woman, and in nothing changed from her nature: but in understanding and sense honored in honor, just as the bodies of the Saints: ποῖα δὲ τίς γραφὴ διηγήσατο περὶ τούτου; ποῖος προφητῶν ἐπέτρεψεν ἄνθρωπον προσκυνεῖσθαι, οὐ μὴν γυναῖκα λέγειν; ἐξαίρετον μὲν γάρ ἐστι τὸ σκεῦος. [Greek text omitted]. And again after a few words: The ancient error shall not rule over us, that we should abandon the living, and adore those things which have been made by him: For if he does not wish the Angels to be adored, how much more [not] her, who was born from Anna, etc. [Greek text omitted].

But that we may at last fully complete the refutation of this most futile Elavvitic distinction, in the fifth and final place, the observation and that [point] deserves [attention], that the assertion of Bellarmine is clearly heretical, establishing that Christ, as man, is to be worshipped with a different and inferior degree of adoration than that which properly belongs to GOD. For although the Flesh of Christ does not obtain the cult of adoration from its own nature, yet we follow both GOD and the Man personally united to GOD with one, not a double, veneration: as has been evidently shown and proven in the article concerning the person of Christ.

THE OTHER evasion collapses by its own futility. For as to its first member: 1. A shameful begging of the question is committed. For this very thing must be proven before it is asserted, that Abraham and Jacob, having been liberated from limbo (which is itself also fictitious), and established in a state of beatitude, have some distinct knowledge of our affairs, or needs, or prayers: which we, relying on the prophetic oracle of Isaiah 63:16, utterly deny. 2. This is a new Elavvitic absurdity, simply unknown to the older Roman Church. For there are not lacking Pontifical writers who have established that even the souls of the Saints themselves, however much they are established in purgatory (let alone in the limbo of the Fathers), pray for us. Emmanuel Sa: which is also evident from the Pontifical Litany, which seeks intercession from some about whom it is not undeservedly doubted whether they are in Heaven, or will ever arrive there, and [from whom] liberation would be most especially hoped for from hell, or that fictitious purgatory of the Romanists. What of the fact that Bellarmine himself, forgetting himself, lib. 2 de purgat. cap. 15, p. 1884 for me, lit. D, asserts in express words: That souls even established in purgatory pray and intercede for us. 3. If before the descent of Christ to the underworld and the liberation of the Fathers from limbo the Saints did not know the state of their descendants: as the Elavvita asserts: certainly all the arguments which are brought forward by the Pontificials for the Invocation of Saints from the Old Testament will have to be wiped out with one stroke. 4. The example of the Prophet Elijah argues and convicts this Elavvitic hypothesis of manifest falsehood, who, not certainly to be snatched into limbo, but into heaven itself by fiery chariots, said thus to his disciple Elisha: Ask what you wish, that I may do for you, before I am taken from you: thus evidently implying that it would be in vain to ask anything of him afterwards, once he was taken up into the heavens. 2 Kings 2:9.

The latter member of this evasion again consists of a shameful begging of the question. For this very thing must again be proven before it is asserted, namely that GOD reveals to the Saints, already established in a state of beatitude, our affairs and state, just as in this life he revealed many things to Elijah, Elisha, and the remaining Prophets. We simply deny this hypothesis, as it is destitute of all support from the Scriptures. But the Esavvita adds, If not through a singular revelation, yet through the beatific vision of God, those things which are done with the pious in this world are known to the Saints. I answer that the question is again being begged; for although it is not at all denied that the blessed Saints see GOD in heaven: yet this is not yet proven, that they see and know all things which GOD knows and sees, as in a mirror, as the Scholastic Doctors used to speak. But if this mirror of the Trinity were some brute thing, such as our mirrors are, perhaps this Esauvitic fiction might obtain some color of truth. And yet this Mirror of the Trinity, which is GOD himself, is endowed with a most free will. Therefore, from that beatific vision there shine forth only those things which GOD wills to be made known both to the Angels and to the Saints. If a complete Syllogism is formed, it will emerge as follows: Whoever sees GOD, who sees and knows all things in heaven, he also sees and knows all things. But the Saints in Heaven see God, who sees and knows all things. Therefore, they themselves also see and know all things. Where the Major proposition is most false: which is proved by the Example of the Angels, who always, as the Savior testifies, Matt. 18:10, see the face of the heavenly Father: and yet they do not see or know all things in GOD. They were certainly ignorant of the propagation of the Gospel to the Gentiles, as the Apostle teaches in Eph. 3:8 and following. To me it was given, to evangelize among the Gentiles the unsearchable riches of Christ, and to illuminate all, what is the dispensation of the mystery hidden from ages in GOD, that NOW νῦν might be made known to the Principalities and powers in the heavenly places, through the Church, the manifold wisdom of GOD. Thus the Angels are ignorant of the last day: Matt. 24:36, Mark 13:32. For which very reason also, things that are done by men are sometimes revealed to the Angels, as is clear from the history of Cornelius, Acts 10:4, so that, because they are ministering Spirits, created by GOD for the ministry of the pious: yet nothing follows from that to prove a revelation that might happen to the Saints in heaven. For such an office is in no way entrusted to them. Finally, this Esauvitic Evasion labors under a manifest absurdity. For let us ask Bellarmine: When he himself cries out: Saint Peter, have mercy on me, and pray for me: Whence does Peter know that he is being invoked? The Esauvite will answer, From the Revelation of GOD. Be it so: let the Esauvite further answer, Whence can he prove that God, hearing this prayer in the heavens, says to Peter: Hey Peter, the Roman Cardinal Bellarmine is invoking you, so that you may have mercy on him, and intercede with me for him: What do you think should be done? Is it thus, then, that GOD, hearing, seeing, and knowing the thoughts, groans, and desires of our hearts, would not hear us praying before he has reported the matter as if to a Senate of heavenly Saints, and from their opinion has made a certain decree concerning the hearing of prayers? O stupendous madness!

The third evasion again foists upon us a futile distinction of the Church, destitute of all support from the Scriptures. For it is false, impious, and blasphemous that the Saints obtain by their intercessions and prayers the things which we need. For Christ, and indeed He alone, performs this duty and office in such a way that He does not admit any colleague or coadjutor. 1 John 2:1 and 2. Heb. 7:25. And Scripture sends us to this sole intercessor, Mediator, and obtainer of every good: Rom. 5:2 and ch. 8:34. Eph. 2:18. 1 Tim. 2:5. Heb. 4:15. When, therefore, the Saints are invoked, either so that they may grant us what is asked in prayer; or at least that they may obtain that GOD may grant us what we seek: certainly that which, according to the Scriptures, belongs to GOD alone and to Christ alone is ascribed to the Saints. But this is impious and sacrilegious: as will be more fully evident from the refutation of the last evasion.

The fourth and last evasion vehemently increases the impiety of the Esauvitic dogma: when it invents two Mediators, not only against the authority of the Scriptures, but also against the office assigned to Christ by GOD the Father, both with respect to Redemption and with respect to Intercession. 2. It is absurd, nay, openly impious and blasphemous, to establish that CHRIST is only a Mediator between GOD and the heavenly Saints: but that the Saints are Mediators between Christ and us. The Apostle certainly was ignorant of this paradox: There is, he says, one Mediator of GOD and men, the Man Christ Jesus. 1 Tim. 2:5. And through Christ alone we have access to GOD the Father through faith: Rom. 5:2. Eph. 2:18. And Christ himself says: No one, he says, comes to the Father, EXCEPT THROUGH ME. John 14:6. And Matt. 11:28, directly, and not through detours or through Saintly intermediaries, he calls us to himself: Come to me, he says, you who labor and are burdened, and I will refresh you. 3. The Romanists inflict a notable injury upon Christ, asserting not obscurely that we cannot approach Christ, as an angry judge, with greater confidence than to some Saint immediately. Certainly Christ is preached in the Scriptures as more merciful toward us than all angels and men: and that he pursues us with greater love than any of the Angels or holy men, since he alone died for us, as Christ himself teaches: John 15:13. Greater love than this no one has, than that one should lay down his life for his friends. Hence the Epistle to the Hebrews, ch. 4:15. We do not have, he says, a High Priest who cannot sympathize with our weaknesses, having been tempted in all things: whence he had to be made like his brothers in all things, that he might be a merciful and faithful High Priest. The same thing is repeated in ch. 2:17 and 18, and ch. 7:26 and following, so that we are commanded to approach him alone with confidence. 4. No intercession can have a place before GOD without redemption: For the power of all intercession depends solely upon this. Whoever, therefore, is established as a Mediator of intercession, he is also established as a Mediator of Redemption: Which very thing was long ago handed down and believed in the Papacy: as is clear from the Psalter of Mary, and prayers directed to the Saints: and from pictures quite common in the temples of the Romanists. For you may see in them Christ painted, Mary painted, the Saints painted standing opposite: Christ indeed all livid and swelling with anger, nay, threatening the supplicants with the deadly darts of damnation: Mary, however, standing at the side, and blandly showing her breasts, and turning her mantle toward the angry son: the Saints finally showing their wounds, stigmata, and merits, by which they might render Christ more appeased. From which bloody religion, because we have been liberated, it is right that we give thanks to Christ the High Priest, and our only mediator, for infinite ages. AMEN.

Latin:

& apertionem regni de Condigno, sine quo nec peccatum fuisset remissum, nec regnum apertum. Sic hodieq; sub Papatu obtinet Absolutionis Formula isthæc: Passio CHRISTI, Meritum beatissimæ virginis Mariæ, Petri, Pauli, & omnium Sanctorum, absolvat te ab omnibus peccatis tuis.

Deinde: Quia precationum formulæ ad Mariam Virginem & Sanctos directæ, diversum, & protestationi Efavviticæ planè contrarium testantur. Certè totum Psalterium Davidicum ad Mariam virginem est accommodatum, iisdem adorationis, cultus, invocationis, & similibus vocabulis, quæ honorem soli DEO debitum notant, retentis. Hinc in Antidotario Mariæ Romanenses se invicem excitant ad Mariæ cultum planè divinum, his verbis: Venite exultemus Dominæ nostræ, jubilemus virgini salvatrici nostræ: Venite, adoremus, & procidamus ante eam. Confiteamur ei cum fletibus peccata nostra: Venite ad eam omnes, qui laboratis, & onerati estis, & ipsa dabit refrigerium, & solatium animabus vestris: Ipsa est misericordia & venia, nulli dans repulsam, & auxiliatrix benignissima. Hanc orationem supplicem clementer suscipias & exaudias, & vitam æternam nobis tribuas. Scio, quia potes omnia, quæ vis: Adoro & benedico altissimos pedes tuos, quibus antiqui Serpentis, cum omnibus pompis ejus, caput calcasti.

Ejusdem generis vel impietatis est & illa Mariæ invocatio, quæ in Horario, cujus titulu est, Historia secundum chorum Augustensem, de commemoratione beatissimæ virginis Mariæ, legitur: Gaude matrona cælica, exultando magnifica DEUM tuum Salutarem, qui te fecit singularem: Tu ancillam JESU CHRISTI te vocare voluisti: Sed & docet Lex divina, Tu ipsius es Domina: Nam jus habet & ratio, Matrem præesse Filio: Ergo ora suppliciter, & præcipe sublimiter, ut nos in mundi vespera, ad regna ducat supera: Tu reparatrix seculi, terminus exilii, ablutio peccati, via consilii, fiducia præmii, scala cæli, janua Paradisi.

Talis est & illa: ô Domina mea Sancta Maria, me in tuam benedictam fidem, & singularem custodiam, & in sinum misericordiæ tuæ hodie, & quotidie, & in horâ exitus mei animam meam, & corpus meum tibi commendo: OMNEM spem meam, & consolationem meam: omnes angustias & miserias meas: Vitam & finem vitæ meæ committo tibi, ut per tuam sanctissimam intercessionem, & per tua merita, omnia mea dirigantur & disponantur opera, secundum tuam, Filiiq; tui voluntatem, & meam necessitatem, Amen.

Et in aljâ isthæc leguntur: Precor te, Maria, ut serves me à peccatis, à scandalis, ab omni confusione humana, ab ira judicii tremendi, ab immundis cogitationibus, ab omni mortali peccato, à subitanea & improvisâ morte, ab omnibus periculis animæ & corporis, honoris & reru mearum: nec unquam me tale permittas facere peccatum, quo gratiam tuam amittam. Da mihi de præteritis emendationem: de præsentibus custodiam: de futuris cautelam. Da mihi in hac vitâ promtum adjutorium: Esto mihi in tremendo judicio prælocutrix apud Filium tuum, Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum: Amen.

Sic quoad Sanctos reliquos, negari nulla ratione potest, divinum cultum ac honorem illis hodieque in Papatu dependi, id quod 1. patet ex Litania Pontificia. 2. ex precationibus seorsim ad quemlibet Sanctorum directis, quas in Examine Concilii Tridentini B. Chemnitii legere licet, inter quas eminet etiam isthæc ad Bartholomæum directa: Sancte Bartholomæe, per gratiam, quam meruisti, miser ego & pollutus servus, sordidissemus peccator, Te deprecor, ut me tuis pretiosis meritis liberes ab omnibus versutiis Diaboli, & insidiis & terroribus, & damnatione & illusione visibilis & invisibilis hostis, in die furoris Domini, & in fine vitæ meæ, contra adversarios meos in adjutoriū meum venias, & binis luminibus suffultum, vestigia agni ostendas.

Sic Cyriacum quoque invocant: Sanctissime Cyriace, matyr Christi inclyte, qui dæmones ex duabus regum filiab9 expulisti in Christi nomine: expelle à me omnem dæmoniacam illusionem, sive dormiam sive vigilem, ne ullam supra me exerceant potestatem: sed tuo semper protegar auxilio, & salver in sæcula sæculorum, Amen.

3. Patet hoc ex praxi Ecclesiæ Romanæ, quæ per Ethnicam quandam impietatem, singulis rebus, morbis, & necessitatibus, bonis etiam fortunæ, certos & peculiares Deos præfecit, & quidem ut auxiliatores sive opitulatores implorandos. Hinc Catharina præest studiis philosophicis, quemadmodum apud Ethnicos Pallas. Hinc Nicolaus & Christophorus præsunt mari, sicut apud Ethnicos Neptunus & Palamon, ac cæteri Dii, Deæq́; marinæ. Hinc Anna & Erasmus invocati dant opes & divitias, quemadmodum apud Ethnicos Juno: Hinc Georgius est patronus bellatorum & equitum, sicut apud Gentiles Mars, Castor ac Pollux: Hinc Urbanus & Medardus vinearum culturæ præsunt, sicut apud Gentiles Bacchus. Hinc Laurentius & Florianus igni dominantur, quemadmodum apud Ethnicos, Vulcanus & Vesta: Hinc medicinæ præsunt, Cosmas & Damianus: Jurisprudentiæ, Ivo: pictoriæ, Lucas: Sutoribus Crispus & Crispianus; Fullonibus, Severus &c. Hinc singulis fermè nationibus singuli Dii tutelares sive opitulatores adsignati: Suecis Olaus: Danis Canutus &c. Hinc singulis morbis certi Dii, tanquam medici tributi: S. Valentinianus medetur Epilepsiæ: Antonius igni sacro: Rochus & Sebastianus pestilentiæ: Apollonia dolori dentium: Otilia & Juliana caligini oculorum &c.

Quibus ita stantibus, Sole meridiano clarius liquet, laborare & penitùs corruere ea Scripturarum testimonia, quæ in quibusvis necessitatibus auxilium à solo DEO petendum: solumq́; Christum januam, portam & scalam cœli esse confirmant. Psalm. 71, 3. Tu DOMINE es expectatio & spes mea: Tu fiducia mea à pueritiâ mea. Jer. 17, 7. Beatus vir, qui fiduciam habet in Jehovah & cujus confidentia est Jehovah.

Sic Christus solus prædicatur spes nostra: 1. Tim. 1, 1. 1. Pet. 1, 21. Et Christus ipse: Ego sum via, veritas, & vita: Nemo venit ad Patrem, NISI PER ME. Joh. 14, 6. Neq; hanc gloriam Christus cum matre sua virgine Maria communem habet: Hic enim obtinet illud, Matth. 12. 48. Quæ est mater mea: Ecce bi(discipuli) sunt mater mea, & fratres mei: Quicunque enim fecerit voluntatem Patris mei, qui in cælis est, ipse meus frater, & mater, & soror est. Quo pertinet illud Epiphanii Tom. 2. lib. 3. hær. 79. Reverà Sanctum erat corpus Mariæ: Sed non Deus: reverà virgo erat ipsa, virgo & honorata: sed non ad adorandum data: sed ipsa adorans eum, qui ex ipsius carne genitus est. Et post pauca: Sit in honore Maria: Sed Pater, Filius & Spiritus Sanctus adoretur: Mariam nemo adoret: non dico mulieri,imò neque viro sed DEO debetur hoc mysterium. Neque Angeli capiunt talem gloriam: ναὶ μὴν ἅγιον ἦν τὸ σῶμα τῆς Μαρίας, ὐ μὴν θεὸς· ναὶ δὴ παρθέν@ ἦν ἡ παρθένος, καὶ τετιμημένη, ἀλλ᾿ οὐκ εἰς προσκύνησιν ἡμῖν δοθεῖσα, ἀλλὰ προσκυνοῦσα τὸν ἐξ αὐτῆς σαρκὶ γεγεννημένον. Et post aliqua: ἐν τιμῇ ἔσω Μαρία, ὁ δὲ πατὴρ, καὶ υἱὸς, καὶ ἅγιον πνεῦμα προσκυνείσθω; τὴν Μαρίαν μηδεὶς προσκυνείτω ὐ λέγω γυναικὶ, ἀλλ᾿ ἐδὲ ἀνδρὶ θεῷ προστέτακται τὸ μυστήριον. ὅτε ἄγγελοι χωρῶσι δοξολογίαν τοιαύτην. Et rursus. Quæ scriptura de hoc narravit? Quis prophetarum præcepit, Hominem adorari, nedum mulierem? Eximium quidem est vas, sed mulier, & nihil à naturâ immutata: verum intellectu & sensu in honore honorata, velut corpora Sanctorum: ποῖα δὲ τὶς γραφὴ διηγήσατο περὶ τέτε; ποῖος προφητῶν ἐπέτρεψεν ἄνθρωπον προσκυνεῖσθαι, ὐ μὴν γυναῖκα λέγειν; ἐξαίρεῖον μὲν γάρ ἐσι τὸ σκεῦ@. ἀλλὰ γυνὴ καὶ ἐδὲν τὴν φύσιν παρηλλαγμένη, τὴν δὲ γνώμην, καὶ τὴν αἴσθησιν ἐν τιμῇ τετιμημένη, ὥσπερ τὰ σώματα τῶν ἁγίων. Et rursus post pauca: Non dominabitur nobis antiquus error, ut relinquamus viventem, & adoremus ea, quæ ab ipso facta sunt: Si enim Angelos adorari non vult, quanto magis eam, quæ genita est ab Anna &c. & κυριεύσει ἡμῶν ἡ ἀρχαία πλάνη καταλιμπάνειν τὸν ζῶντα καὶ προσκύνειν τὰ ὑπ᾿ αὐτὲ γεγονότα, εἰ γὰρ ἀγγέλες προσκυνεῖσθαι ἐ θέλει, πόσῳ μᾶλλον τὴν ἀπὸ Ἄννης γεγενημένην.

Sed ut refutationem futilissimæ hujus distinctionis Elavviticæ vel tandem plenè expediamus, Quinto & postremo loco observationem & illud meretur, quòd hæretica planè est assertio Bellarmini, statuentis, Christum, quà homo, alio & inferiore adorationis gradu, quàm quò DEO proprie competit, colendum esse. Etsi enim non ex naturâ suâ Caro Christi adorationis cultum obtinet, unâ tamen non geminâ veneratione prosequimur & DEUM, & Hominem DEO personaliter unitum: uti in articulo de personâ Christi evidenter ostensum & comprobatum.

ALTERUM effugium propriâ futilitate corruit. Nam quod prius ejus membrum. 1. turpis committitur petitio Principii. Nam hoc ipsum probandum prius, quàm asserendum, quòd Abrahamus & Jacobus ex limbo (qui & ipse fictitius est) liberati, & in statu beatitudinis constituti, discretam aliquam nostrarum vel rerum, vel necessitatum, vel precum notitiam habeant: id quod nos freti oraculo prophetico Esaï. 63, 16. pernegamus. 2. Novum hoc est ἀδόξον Elavviticum, antiquiori Ecclesiæ Romanæ simpliciter incognitum. Neque enim desunt ex Scriptoribus Pontificiis, qui ipsas etiam animas Sanctorum, quantumvis in purgatorio (nedum in limbo Patrum) constitutas, pro nobis orare statuerunt. Emmanuel Sa: id quod ex Litaniâ etiam Pontificiâ patet, quæ intercessionem petit à nonnullis, de quibus haud immeritò dubitatur, an in Cœlo sint, vel unquàm eò perventuri, & maximè ex inferno, vel fictitio illo Romanensium purgatorio speranda esset liberatio. Quid quòd Bellarminus ipse, sui oblitus lib. 2. de purgat. cap. 15. pag. mihi 1884. lit. D. disertis verbis asserit: Animas in purgatorio etiam constitutas, pro nobis orare & impetrare. 3. Si ante descensum Christi ad inferos & liberationem Patrum è limbo Sancti nesciverunt posterorum suorum statum: uti assitmat Elavvita: certè unâ liturâ expungenda erunt omnia argumenta, quæ pro Invocatione Sanctorum è Veteri Testamento à Pontificiis proferuntur. 4. manifestæ falsitatis arguit, & convincit hanc hypothesin Elavviticam exemplum Prophetæ Eliæ, qui, non certè in limbum, sed in cœlum ipsum quadrigis igneis rapiendus, sic ad Elisæum discipulum: Pestula quod vis, ut faciam tibi, antequàm tollar à te: sic evidenter innuens, frustrà postmodum à se, in cœlos sublato, aliquid postulati. 2. Reg. 2, 9.

Posteriùs effugii hujus membrum, rursus turpi constat petitione principii. Hoc ipsum enim rursus probandum prius, quàm asserendum, nempè DEUM Sanctis, jam in statu beatitudinis constitutis revelare res & statum nostrum prout hac in vita Eliæ, Elisæo & Prophetis reliquis, multa revelavit. Nos hypothesin hanc, quippe omni Scripturarum præsidio destitutam, simpliciter negamus. Sed subjicit Esavvita, Si non per singularem patefactionem, tamen per visionem Dei beatificam constare Sanctis ea, quæ cum piis hoc in mundo geruntur. Respondeo rursum peti principium; Etsi enim minimè negatur, Sanctos beatos videre in cœlo DEUM: tamen hoc nondum probatum, ipsos omnia, quæ DEUS scit & videt, tanquam in speculo, uti quondam Doctores Scholastici loquebantur, videre & scire. Quod si speculum hoc Trinitatis esset brutum quiddam, qualia nostra sunt specula, fortè coloris aliquid obtineret hoc commentum Esavviticum. Atqui Speculum hoc Trinitatis, quod est DEUS ipse, liberrimâ voluntate est præditum. Relucent ergo ex visione illâ beatificâ tantùm ea, quæ DEUS & Angelis, & Sanctis vult innotescere. Si integer formetur Syllogismus, talis emerget: Qui DEUM videntem & scientem omnia in cœlo videt, is quoq; omnia videt & scit. Atqui Sancti in Cœlo vident Deum videntem & scientem omnia. Ergo ipsi quoque omnia vident & sciunt. Ubi Major propositio est falsissima: id quod probatur Exemplo Angelorum, qui semper, teste Servatore, Matth. 18, 10. vident faciem patris cœlestis: & tamen non omnia in DEO vident aut sciunt. Ignorarunt certè Evangelii propagationem ad Gentes, sic docente Apostolo Ephes. 3, 8. & seqq. Mihi datum est, inGentibus evangelizare investigabiles divitias Christi, & illuminare omnes, quæ sit dispensatio mysterii absconditi à seculis in DEO, ut NUNC νῦν innotescat Principibus &potestatibus in cœlestibus, per Ecclesiam, multiformis sapientiaDEI. Sic ignorant Angeli diem novissimum: Matth. 24, 36. Marc. 13, 32. Quam ipsam etiam ob causam Angelis interdum revelantur ea, quę fiunt ab hominibus, ut patet ex historiâ Cornelii, Actor. 10, 4. ut, quia sunt Spiritus administratorii, conditi à DEO in ministerium piorum: nihil tamen inde sequitur, ad probandam revelationem, quæ fiat in cœlo Sanctis. Tale enim officium ipsis nullatenùs est demandatum. Tandem manifestâ absurditate laborat Effugium hoc Esavviticum. Quæramus enim ex Bellarmino: Quando ipse clamat: Sancte Petre, miserere mei, & ora pro me: Undenam Petrus sciat, se invocari? Respondebit Esavvita, Ex Revelatione DEI Sit ita: Respondeat porrò Esavvita, Undenám probare possit, Deum in cœlis audientem hanc precationem dicere Petro: Heus Petre, Cardinalis Romanus Bellarminus, invocat te, ut ipsius miserearis, & apud me pro ipso intercedas: Quid putas faciendum? Siccinè ergo DEUS audiens, videns, sciens, cogitationes, gemitus ac desideria cordium nostrorum, non prius nos orantes exaudiret, quàm rem quasi ad Sanctorum cœlitum Senatum retulerit, & ex horum sententiâ, de exauditione precum, certum decretum fecerit? ô stupendam vesaniam!

Tertium effugium rursus futilem, & omni Scripturarum præsidio destitutam distinctionem Ecclesiæ obtrudit. Falsum enim, impium, & blasphemum est, Sanctos suis intercessionibus & precibus impetrare ea, quibus indigemus. Hoc enim munere, atque officio ita Christus, & quidem solus defungitur, ut Collegam, sive coadjutorem aliquem non admittat. 1. Johan. 2, 1. & 2. Hebr. 7. 25. & ad hunc solum intercessorem, Mediatorem; & impetratorem omnis boni ablegat nos Scriptura: Rom. 5, 2. & cap. 8, 34. Eph. 2, 18. 1. Tim. 2, 5. Hebr. 4, 15. Quando ergo invocantur Sancti, vel ut nobis præstent, quæ in oratione petuntur; vel saltem imperrent, ut quæ petimus, DEUS nobis tribuat: certè Sanctis adscribitur, quod secundum Scripturas, & solius DEI, & solius Christi est. Est autem hoc impium & sacrilegum: uti ex refutatione postremi effugii pleniùs patebit.

Quartum & postremum effugium impietatem dogmatis Esavvitici vehementer auget: quando duos Mediatores comminiscitur, non modò contra Scripturarum autoritatem, sed & contra officium Christo à DEO patre, tùm respectu Redemtionis, tùm respectu Intercessionis adsignatum. 2. Absurdum, imò palàm impium & blasphemum est, statuere, CHRISTUM esse tantùm Mediatorem inter DEUM & Sanctos cœlites: Sanctos verò esse Mediatores inter Christum, & inter nos. Apostolus certè ignoravit hoc paradoxon: UNUS, inquiens, est Mediator DEI & hominum Homo Christus Jesus. 1. Tim. 2, 5. Et per solum Christum habemus accessum ad DEUM patrem per fidem: Rom. 5, 2. Ephes. 2, 18. Et Christus ipse. Nemo, inquit, venit ad Patrem, NISI PER ME. Johan. 14, 6. Et Matth. 11, 28. rectâ, & non per ambages, sive per internuncios Sanctos, vocat nos ad se: Venite ad me, inquiens, qui laboratis, & onerati estis, ego reficiam vos. 3. Insigni injuriâ Christum Romanenses adficiunt, haud obscurè asserentes. Nos majori cum fiducia non posse accedere ad Christum, quippe iratum judicem, quam ad Sanctorū aliquem immediatè. Certè Christus prædicatur in Scripturis clementior omnibus angelis atq; hominibus erga nos: & majori nos prosequi amore, quàm ullus vel Angelorum, vel Sanctorum hominum, quippe qui solus pro nobis mortuus est, sic docente ipso Christo: Johan. 15, 13. Majorem hac dilectione nemo habet, quàm ut quis ponat animam suam pro amicis suis. Hinc Epistola ad Hebr. cap. 4, 15. Non habemus, inquit, Pontificem, qui non possit compati infirmitatibus nostris, tentatum per omnia: unde debuit per omnia fratribus adsimilari, ut misericors esset, & fidelis Pontifex. Quod ipsum repetitur cap. 2, 17. & 18. & cap. 7, 26. & seqq. ita ut ad ipsum solum cum fiduciâ accedere jubeamur. 4. Nulla intercessio apud DEUM locum habere potest, sine redemtione: Nam ab hac omnis intercessionis vis unicè dependet. Quicunque ergo statuitur esse Mediator intercessionis, ille statuitur etiam esse Mediator Redemtionis: Quod ipsum in Papatu jam olim traditum & creditum fuit: uti patet ex Psalterio Mariæ, & precibus ad Sanctos directis: & ex picturis in templis Romanensium satis usitatis. Videas enim in illis pictum Christum, pictam Mariam, pictos Sanctos ex opposito stantes: Christum quidem totum lividum, & irâ tumentem, imò invocantibus letifera damnationis jacula minitari: Mariam verò ad latus stantem, & blandè ostentantem sua ubera, & irato filio obvertentem pallium suum: Sanctos denique ostendentes sua vulnera, stigmata, & merita, quibus Christum placatiorem reddant. A quâ cruentâ religione, quòd liberati sumo, est quod Christo Pontifici, & mediatori nostro unico, gratias agamus seculis infinitis. AMEN.


## 34 On the Civil Magistracy

OIKONOMIA of the Treatise.

The name and office of the political magistrate has always and everywhere been held in honor, not only in the Republic of Christians, but even among the Gentiles themselves. Aristotle certainly did not hesitate to call a Prince νόμον ἔμψυχον, an animate law: Homer, ποιμένα λαω̃ν, a shepherd of the peoples: Plato, σωτη̃ρα, φύ- λακα, καὶ ἐπίκουρον, a Savior, guardian, and helper: Theseus, in Euripides, εὐεργέ- την καὶ φίλον μέγαν, a benefactor and great friend.
