Similar examples may be seen in the Ephraimites rising up against Jephthah: Judg. 11, v. 33; in Absalom against David: 2 Samuel 18, v. 9; in Zedekiah against the king of Babylon.

It must be observed, however, in this case that the heretic is put to death by the Christian Magistrate, not as a heretic—that is, insofar as he fosters and defends errors directly impinging upon the foundation of the faith—but insofar as, having spurned all laws and edicts, he did not hesitate to stubbornly resist the Magistrate and show himself seditious. For this reason, Thomas Müntzer, the torch and trumpet of the peasant sedition, was punished with the penalty of death. For this reason, also, very many Anabaptists were struck with the sword, not because of their errors or heresy, but because of their seditions. Thus Nicolaus Crell, jurist and formerly Chancellor of the Saxon Electorate, was beheaded by the order of the Elector, not because he was addicted to Calvinism, but because, contrary to his pledged faith, he deceived the most excellent Elector with manifest lies; with wondrous arts and frauds, he strove to encrust Calvinism without the Elector's knowledge; he blocked all access to the Elector for the Orthodox theologians; he wickedly and basely perverted their most humble petitions; he either did not present the suppliant letters of the subjects at all, or, having presented them, twisted them into a foreign sense; he wickedly dragged the provincial officials themselves, whom he had noticed did not support Calvinism, into danger of life and fortune; indeed, he did not even hesitate to sow clearly fatal dissensions among Princes joined by blood. There is no reason, therefore, for the Calvinists to clamor that either Crell, or Peucer, or Cracow, or others were punished by our Princes with prison, or exile, or death, for the mere profession of Calvinism.

Thirdly, if the question is about a heretic, insofar as he is such, and he abstains from seditions and blasphemies, but continues to defend his error stubbornly and obstinately after being admonished and convinced: I deny that such a person should be visited with the penalty of death by the Magistrate. Nor does it stand in the way that such heretics are also found not to be immune from blasphemies, insofar as every error against the foundation is, of course, a blasphemy against the heavenly truth. For they do not persevere in error out of destined malice, but are persuaded by a zeal for inquiring into and asserting the truth. In this way, they differ greatly from blasphemers properly so called. And the same thing usually happens to these heretics that the Apostle affirms of the Jews, Rom. 10, v. 2: that they are zealous for the truth, but their zeal is not κατ' ἐπίγνωσιν, according to knowledge. For if they knew for certain and determined in their heart that they were erring regarding the faith, they would certainly return to the way; but although they are convinced by the Orthodox, so that they freely admit they are unable to respond to the arguments of our side, they nevertheless think they feel correctly, whether blinded in this way by the Devil or hardened by some persuasion of the mind. And it is about these that the controversy is properly agitated today between us and the Romanists and the Sacramentarians: whether such heretics ought to be coerced by the Magistrate with the ultimate penalty: where we hold and defend the negative, against their affirmative, relying on these reasons and arguments.

1. Because the Kingdom of Christ is not governed and propagated in these lands by external arms, but by spiritual ones, according to the assertion of the Savior, John 18, v. 36: My kingdom is not of this world: if it were of this world, my disciples would fight (namely, with external arms) for it. Hence the Apostle: The weapons of our warfare, he says, are not carnal: but mighty through God to the pulling down of strongholds, etc. 2 Cor. 10, v. 4.

2. The Apostle, Tit. 3, v. 10, warning that a heretical man is to be avoided after one or two admonitions, shows the process by which one should deal with heretics. He does not indeed decree that they are to be tolerated, or that the chairs of the Church and public schools are to be entrusted to them, since he wishes them to be avoided; meanwhile, however, he does not permit or advise that they be removed from human affairs by iron, flame, noose, and other punishments, according to the practice of the Romanists and Calvinists. But when he commands them to be avoided, and indeed after one or two admonitions, he shows what is the legitimate mode of dealing with heretics. First, that they be admonished and instructed more correctly about the catholic truth from the Word of God. Then, if nothing is achieved by this first attempt, he wishes that a second admonition also be added, by which the falsity of the heresy is uncovered, and the truth is so demonstrated from the Word of God that they are convinced and find no support in the Scriptures. Finally, if every admonition lacks salutary fruit, he wishes them to be avoided: which is done by their being cut off from the rest of the society of the Church, and being ordered either to lead their lives privately, or if there is a danger of seduction, they be banished elsewhere, to those among whom they can have free power to profess their heresy: or if they are unwilling to do so at the cost of their property and goods, let them be restrained in such a way that no harm is inflicted by them upon either the Church or the Republic.

heretics, certainly even by this arrangement we would be encouraging the Roman Antichrist against ourselves, so that because he considers us heretics, he may also determine that he must rage against us in such a manner. Whence the Church of GOD would be subject to perpetual slaughter, partly by Orthodox magistrates, and partly by heretical ones.

3. Because if such heretics are killed, the political magistrate seems by this arrangement both to cut off their time for conversion and to invade the tribunal of GOD itself. The former for this reason: because such persons have very often, by the singular mercy of GOD, acknowledged their error at the very point of death and have been converted to GOD: which would not have happened if they had been subjected to capital punishment for a simple heresy. The latter for this reason: because God himself is accustomed to issue the judgments of his severity upon such heretics and apostates, by the example of Julian the apostate, who, boiling with insatiable fury against the Christians, was pierced by a hostile weapon (which could not be known from where it had flown), and with the blood that flowed from the wound projected upwards, and with these words belched forth: You have conquered, Galilean: he perished miserably. Thus Cerinthus perished, crushed by the ruin of a bath. Arius, urged by divine vengeance, ejected and poured out his own bowels. Thus perished most apostates by the singular vengeance of GOD; Franciscus Spira, Latomus, Hesmeisterus, Sixtus Thammerus, and others. It is ill-advised for the magistrate to block the way to these divine judgments by a violent and bloody process against heretics: especially since the remaining reasons hold this to be most alien to the magistrate: and Christ himself wishes that the tares not be rooted up: for this is to be fully resolved at length by divine judgment.

8. Because the Apostolic, Catholic Church never approved that custom, that where errors were to be killed, men were killed. Certainly that first Church of the Apostles did not adjudge Hymenæus, Philetus, and Alexander the coppersmith, who were heretics, to capital punishment: but rather with all gentleness admonished them of their error, refuted them, rebuked them, and strove to recall them to the way of truth. 2 Tim. 2:17 and ch. 4:14. Thus in ecclesiastical history, heretics were nowhere handed over to executioners to be slaughtered for heresy alone by Emperors. Which very opinion was defended even by the Orthodox Fathers. Whence Augustine writes in book 3 against Cresconius the Grammarian, ch. 50: At that time the opinion was received and approved by the WHOLE Church, which pleased no good man in it, if anyone, even a heretic, were to be treated with cruelty unto death.

And in book 1 against the letters of Petilianus, ch. 29: Love men, kill errors, contend for the truth without cruelty.

And against the Epistle of Manichæus called Fundamental: Let those rage against you who do not know with what labor truth is found, and how difficult it is to avoid errors. Let those rage against you who do not know how rare and arduous it is to overcome carnal phantasms with the serenity of a pious mind. Let those rage against you who do not know with what difficulty the eye of the inner man is healed, so that it may be able to behold its Sun, not this one which you worship, which is fleshly and shines and radiates with a celestial body to both men and cattle: but that one of which it is written by the Prophet: The Sun of righteousness has risen for me: and of which it is said in the Gospel: It was the true light, which illuminates every man coming into this world. Let those rage against you who do not know with what sighs and groans it comes to pass that God can be understood from any part whatsoever. Finally, let those rage against you who have not been deceived by any such error as they see you deceived by, etc.

4. Because the Savior in the New Testament gave no command about killing heretics: but rather, when the Apostles wished that the impiety of the Samaritans be restrained by heavenly fire, after the example of Elijah, such an answer is given: You do not know of what spirit you are: The Son of man did not come to destroy souls, but to seek and to save that which was lost. Luke 9:56.

5. Because consciences cannot or ought not to be forced by any violence to a certain faith, whether true or false: although they can be compelled to the means of faith which are by no means to be neglected, as was shown above.

Although indeed Augustine, as was indicated above at the beginning of the first Question, later conceded to that opinion, that he judged that heretics should be restrained not only by word and disputations, but also by external force through ordinary magistrates: Epist. 48 to Vincentius: yet he seems to have determined this only concerning a certain kind of heretic, not all: and indeed concerning the Donatists and Circumcellions, who it is established were both turbulent and seditious.

6. Because there is a danger that from the constancy and animosity of heretics in enduring punishments, many may be inflamed to embrace the same heresy, determining that it cannot happen without the special Spirit, inspiration, and assistance of GOD: when nevertheless the Devil also has his own martyrs: just as Joannes Brentius writes somewhere that an example of this matter occurred in his time.

Then the reasons assigned by Augustine prove that by external force he did not understand the sword of slaughter, but either

7. Because if our people were to rage with the sword against fines, or beatings, or imprisonments, or exiles, or other punishments of this kind, which do not take away life: because, of course, he immediately adds: This does not seem to him useless, because many have been corrected by this agreement: a thing which cannot be affirmed of those who have been killed. For indeed, one killed by the sword can be said not to be corrected, but snatched away.

Tertullian supports Augustine, thus to Scapula: It is a matter of human right and natural power for each one to worship what he thinks fit: nor does the religion of another help or harm anyone. But it is not of Religion to compel Religion, which ought to be undertaken of one's own accord, not by force.

Chrysostom, Sermon on Anathema: Impious dogmas, and those which have proceeded from heretics, ought to be refuted and anathematized. But men are to be spared, and one must pray for their salvation.

Jerome in chapter 2 of Hosea: How will he not despair of the salvation of a heretic? In what way will he provoke him to repentance? By what reason will he show that he desires his salvation, he who hands him over to the Magistrate to be killed?

Thus Canon Law expressly prohibits that Spiritual persons should kill anyone for heresy, either by themselves or through others: and that they should accommodate neither their will, nor their deed, nor their counsel to that end. Causa 23. q. ult. or 50. C. His quibus.

Which very practice was also observed in the Roman Church: so that Innocent I, Pope of blessed memory, seems to have been the first who, impelled by the Spirit of Antichrist, did not hesitate to compel heretics to the Roman faith—not the Roman [faith]—by the sword: around A.D. 415. Although some of his successors very rarely observed this harsher mode and process of dealing with heretics, until the Roman Antichrist established dominion in the Church, and defiled it with the blood of the Martyrs of Jesus, and rendered it formidable to the whole Christian world.

In which opinion was also the blessed Luther, in his exposition of the parable of the Tares: We are taught, he says, how we ought to conduct ourselves toward heretics: for it is not right to extinguish and cut them off. For Christ openly says here: Let both grow: one must act against them only with the Word of God. For so it usually happens in this matter, that he who errs today, may tomorrow be able to return to the way. For who knows when the Word of God will draw the heart of anyone? But if he is burned, or otherwise removed, certainly he is hindered, so that he cannot be brought back to the way: nay, it is necessary that he perish who otherwise could have been freed from error.

And from the Calvinist people, Wolfgang Musculus Dusanus clearly holds the same opinion in his Locis Communibus: tit. de Hæresi: page 611 in my edition. The spirit of cruelty, he says, is not of true Christians, but of heretics. The Christian magistrate indeed takes action against heretics, but so moderately that they may be able to repent. He does not allow them to teach about the faith: nor does he permit them to gather churches, to ordain bishops and other ministers: he deprives some of honors: he takes away from others the communion of the city: he proscribes some: he punishes others with a monetary fine: which we read was done in the times of Augustine. He coerces and detains those impostors and seducers themselves, once they appear incorrigible, enclosed in prisons for so long until, having returned to themselves, they repent. Thus are those to be coerced who do not endure to be compelled to the good. By this moderation of punishments, the goal can be reached at which a Christian magistrate ought to aim. That is, that heretics may be converted from their errors, and once converted, be saved. He who kills one erring in his error either does not believe that he errs perniciously and damnably before God: or if he does believe this, he is little concerned for his salvation. I speak of those heretics who, even if they err gravely, are nevertheless not blasphemous against God. The law of God does not allow a blasphemer to live, etc. Thus W. Musculus.

Latin:

UT quæstionis hujus decisio ritè expediatur, præmittendæ sunt distinctiones nonnullæ, quæ toti huic Controversiæ lucem inferre possunt. Ac initiò quidem probè observandum, per hæreticum non intelligi quemlibet Schismaticum aut errantem. Humanum enim est errare: & Ecclesiæ ager semper inter triticum Zizania aspersa habet: siquidem vel inter Doctores ipsos, vel auditores semper sunt, qui super fundamentum ædificant fœnum, ligna & stipulas, 1. Cor. 3. v. 12. Sed intelligi talem hominem qui fidem Christianam professus, caput sive articulum aliquem fidei aut Religionis Christianæ directè corrumpit, depravat, negat: & monitus etiam imò convictus, nihilominus obstinatè errorem conceptum tueri ac defendere pergit.

Deinde accuratè distinguendum inter Hæreticum & manifestè blasphemum: & rursum, inter eum, qui sciens volensq; destinato consilio & proposito errores spargit, Deumque & sacra omnia, diris & execrandis blasphemiis proscindit: & inter eum, qui inscius hoc facit, & non destinatâ malitiâ aut consilio: sed errore & simplicitate mentis, ac judicii imbecillitate, à Satana fascinatus,& ab ejusdem organis illectus peccat, ut errores agnoscere haud queat.

Tandem distinguendum etiam inter Hæreticum, ut Hæreticum: & inter hæreticum quatenus ille simul est rebellis & seditiosus.

Tribus istis sive distinctionibus, sive hypothesibus præsuppositis, ad propositum Ζήτημα distinctè etiam respondemus. Nam initiò quoad manifestè blasphemos, qui scientes volentesq; moniti etiam aliquoties, obstinatè tamen & contumaciter diras evomunt blasphemias in Deum, & religionem Orthodoxam: jam supra quæstione 1. ex Scripturis evicimus, Magistratum Christianum gladio etiam in tales animadvertere debere: ut qui spontè & desultoriâ impietate à DEO ad Diabolum deficientes, omnem DEI gratiam petulanter à se repellunt: ita ut de ipsorum emendatione spei nihil possit super esse reliquum. Hinc Deus ipse talem interfici, & è societate populi Christiani tolli præcepit: Levit.24. v. 15. & 16.

Deinde quoad haereticos propriè sic dictos, si vel maximè excellenti hoc gradu non sint blasphemi: sed praeter haeresin, rebellionem, motus & seditiones contra Magistratum Orthodoxum, ejusdemq́; edicta publica concitent, factiones in Ecclesia moveant, lites, & contentiones inter Auditores Verbi serant: Religioni puriori insidias struant: tûm tales, pro qualitate delicti, vel verberibus, vel carcere, vel mulctis, vel gladio etiam puniri posse ac debere, omninò statuo: fretus illis Scripturarum praeceptis & statutis, quibus ejusmodi poenae in seditiosos sunt à Deo ipso constitutae: exemplo Chore, Dathan, Abiron, & domesticorum, qui seditiosi contra Aaronem, cum thuribulis suis ad tabernaculum prosilierant, suffitus faciendi caussa: à Deo autem ita puniti fuerunt, ut igni è thuribulis yi divinâ excitato, & exardescente, ipsorumq́ve corpora corripiente, miserabili morte perire necesse haberent. Num. 16. per totum fermè caput. Similia exempla cernere licet in Ephraïmitis contra Jephtah insurgentibus: Jud. 11. v. 33. in Absolone contra Davidem: 2. Samuel. 18. v. 9. in Zedechia contra regem Babylonis.

Observandum autem hoc casu Haereticum interfici à Magistratu Christiano, non ut haereticum, hoc est, quatenus errores in fundamentum fidei directè impingentes fovet & defendit: sed quatenus spretis omnibus legibus & edictis, Magistratui contumaciter reluctari, & seditiosum se praebere non dubitavit. Hanc ob causam Thomas Monetarius seditionis rusticae, fax & tuba, capitis supplicio affectus fuit. Hanc ob causam Anabaptistarum etiam benè multi, non propter errores, sive haeresin, sed propter seditiones gladio percufsi sunt. Sic Nicolaus Crellius JCtus, Electoratus Saxonici quondam Cancellarius, ad mandatum Imperatoris capite plexus fuit, non quod Calvinismo esset addictus: sed quòd contra fidem datam, manifestis mendaciis Electore optimum circumvenit: miris artibus ac fraudibus, inscio Electore Calvinismum incrustare studuit: Theologis Orthodoxis omnem ad Electorem aditum interclusit: ipsorumq́; petitiones humilimas improbè & nequiter pervertit: Subditorum literas supplices vel planè non exhibuit, vel exhibitas in alienum sensum detorsit: provinciales ipsos, quos quidem Calvinismo non patrocinari animadverterat, in capitis fortunarumq́; discrimen nequiter pertraxit: quin ne quidem inter Principes sanguine junctos, dissidia planè fatalia serere non dubitavit. Non est ergò, ut Calviniani vel Crellium, vel Peucerum, vel Cracovium, vel alios à nostris Principibus, vel carcere, vel exilio, vel capite, ob solam Calvinismi professionem mulctatos esse, clamitent.

Tertiò, si quaestio sit de Haeretico, quatenus talis est, & à seditionibus & blasphemiis abstinet, errorem autem suum admonitus & convictus contumaciter & obstinatè defendere pergit: talem à Magistratu capitis supplicio afficiendum esse nego. Neque obstat, quòd tales quoque hæretici à blasphemiis non immunes esse deprehenduntur: quatenus nimirùm omnis error contra fundamentum, est blasphemia in cœlestem veritatem. Nam non ex destinatâ malitiâ: sed veritatis inquirendæ & asserendæ studio persuasi, in errore contumaciter perseverant. Quo pacto à blasphemis propriè sic dictis, plurimùm differunt. Et idem fermè hæreticis istis obvenire solet, quòd de Judæis affirmat Apostolus, Rom. 10. v. 2. Zelotas illos esse pro veritate, sed Zelum ipsorum non esse κατ' ἐπίγνωσιν secundum scientiam. Nam si certò scirent, & statuerent in corde suo, se errare circa fidem, utiq́; in viam redirent: sed quanquam ab Orthodoxis convicti sunt, ita ut se ad argumenta nostrorum respondere haud posse ultrò fateantur: tamen rectè se sentire autumant: sive sic excœcati à Diabolo, sive inductione quadam animi obfirmati. Et de his propriè inter nos & Romanenses atque Sacramentarios hodiè agitatur controversia: an tales Hæretici ultimo supplicio à Magistratu coerceri debeant: Ubi nos Negativam, contra illorum Affirmativam, tenemus ac defendimus: his freti rationibus & argumentis.

1. Quia Regnum Christi non armis externis: sed Spiritualibus gubernatur, & propagatur in his terris: secundum assertionem Servatoris, Joh. 18. v. 36. Regnum meum non est de hoc mundo: Si esset de hoc mundo, discipuli mei pugnarent (scilicet externis armis) super eo. Hinc Apostolus: Arma militiæ nostræ, inquit, non sunt carnalia: sed potentia Deo, ad destructionem munitionum &c. 2. Cor. 10. v. 4.

2. D. Apostolus Tit. 3. v. 10. monens hominem hæreticum post unam atque alteram admonitionem vitari, monstrat processum, quo cum hæreticis sit agendum. Non quidem tolerandos eos, vel Ecclesiæ, Scholarumq́ve publicarum cathedras ipsis credendas esse, statuir: siquidem eos vult vitari: Interim tamen neque ferro, flamma, laqueo, aliisq́; suppliciis, secundum praxin Romanensium, & Calvinianorum è rebus humanis tollendos eos esse, permittit aut suadet. Quando verò eos jubet vitare, & quidem post unam atque alteram admonitionem, ostendit, quis cum hæreticis agendi modus sit legitimus. Primùm ut moneantur, & ex Verbo DEI rectiùs de veritate catholicâ erudiantur. Deinde, si hoc primo conatu nihil proficiatur, vult, ut altera etiam accedat admonitio, quâ hæreseos falsitas detegatur: & ex Verbo DEI veritas ita demonstretur, ut convincantur, nec in Scripturis ullum inveniant præsidium. Tandem, si omnis admonitio fructu salutari careat, vult ut vitentur: id quod fit, abscindantur à reliquâ societate Ecclesiæ, & vel privatim vitam agere jubeantur, vel si seductionis subsit periculum, aliò, & ad eos relegetur, apud quos liberam suæ hæreseως profitendæ potestatem habere possunt: vel si cum facultatum, & bonorum jacturâ facer re id nolint, sic coerceantur, ut ne quid da mni vel Ecclesiæ, vel Reipublicæ ab illis in feratur.

hæreticos, certè vel hoc pacto Antichristum Romanum, contra nosmetipsos essemus animaturi, ut quia nos pro hæreticis habet, in nos quoq; tali modo sibi sæviendum esse statuat. Unde Ecclesia D E I perpetuis lanienis, ex parte tùm Orthodoxorum, tùm hæreticorum Magistratuum futura esset obnoxia.

3. Quia si tales hæretici occidentur, Magistratus Politicus hoc pacto ipsis & Con. versionis tempus præcidere, & ipsius D E I tribunal invadere videtur. Prius illiùs ideò: Quia tales sæpiùs singulari D E I miseratione, vel in ipso mortis articulo errorem agnove runt, & ad D E U M conversi sunt: id quod non evenisset, si ultimo supplicio ob simpli cem hæresin affecti fuissent. Posterius hoc ideò: Quia Deus ipse plærumque in ejusmodi hæreticos & Apostatas severitatis suæ judicia edere consuevit, exemplo Juliani apo. testatæ, qui insatiabili furore contra Christia. nos æstuans, infesto telo (quod unde volafset, sciri haud poterat) transverberatus, & sanguine, qui è vulnere manabat, sursum projecto, hisque eructatis verbis: Vicisti Galilæe: miserabiliter interiit. Sic Cerinthus ruinâ balnei oppressus periit. Arius, divinâ vindictâ urgente, sua ejecit & effudit viscera. Sic singulari DEI ultione perierunt Apostatæ plærique; Franciscus Spira, Latomus, Hesmeiste. rus, Sixtus Thammerus & alii. Hisce DEI judiciis viam ut Magistratus violento & sangui. nolento in hæreticos processu intercludat, inconsultum est: præsertim cum reliquæ rationes hoc à Magistratu velint esse alienissimum: & Christus ipse velit, ne eradicentur Zizania: Hoc enim judicio divino tandem plenè expeditum iri.

8. Quia Ecclesia Apostolica, Catholica nunquam approbavit illum morem, ut, ubi interficiendi fuerunt errores, interfecti sunt homines. Certè prima illa Ecclesia Apostolorum, Hymenæum, Philetum, Alexandrum fabrum ærarium, hæreticos, non ultimo adjudicavit supplicio: sed cum omni potiùs mansuetudine eos erroris admonuit, redarguit, objurgavit, & in viam veritatis revocare studuit. 2. Tim. 2. v. 17. & cap. 4. v. 14. Sic in historiâ Ecclesiasticâ hæretici ob solam hæresin nuspiam ab Imperatoribus mactandi sunt carnificibus traditi. Quæ ipsa sententia ab Orthodoxis etiam Patribus defensa. Unde Augustinus lib. 3. contra Cresc. Grammaticum, cap. 50. scribit: Tunc recepta erat, & à TOTA Ecclesiâ approbata sententia, quæ nulli bono in ea placebat, si usq; ad mortem in quenquam, licet hæreticum, sæviretur.

Et lib. 1. contra literas Petiliani, cap. 29. Diligite homines, interficite errores, sine sævitiâ pro veritate certate.

Et contra epistolam Fundamenti: Illi in vos sæviant qui nesciunt, cum quo labore verum inveniatur, & quàm difficilè caveantur errores. Illi in vos sæviant, qui nesciunt, quàm rarum & arduum sit, carnalia phantasmata, piæ mentis serenitate superare. Illi in vos sæviant, qui nesciunt, cum quantâ difficultate sanetur oculus interioris hominis, ut poßit intueri Solem suum, non istum, quem colitis cælesti corpore carneus oculus, & hominum & pecorum fulgentem, atque radiantem: sed illum, de quo scriptum est per Prophetam: Ortus est mihi justitia Sol: & de quo dictum est in Evangelio: Erat lumen verum, quod illuminat omnem hominem venientem in hunc mundum. Illi in vos sæviant, qui nesciunt, quibus suspiriis & gemitibus fiat, ut ex qualicunque parte poßit intelligi Deus. Postremo in vos illi sæviant, qui nullo tali errore decepti sunt, quali vos deceptos vident. &c.

4. Quia Servator in Novo Testamento nullum de occidendis hæreticis dedit præceptum: sed potiùs Apostolis volentibus, ut Samaritanorum impietas, exemplo Heliæ, cœlesti igne coerceatur, tale datur responsum: Nescitis, cujus Spiritus sitis sitis: Filius hominis non venit perdere animas, sed quærere, & salvare, quod perierat. Luc. 9. v. 56.

5. Quia conscientiæ ad fidem certam sive veram, sive falsam nullâ vi cogi possunt vel debent: licèt compelli possint ad media fidei minimè negligenda, uti suprâ ostensum.

Quanquam verò Augustinus, uti suprà sub initium Quæstionis primæ indicatum, in eam postea concessit sententiam, ut judicaret, Hæreticos non verbo tantùm, & disputationibus, sed vi etiam externa per Magistratus ordinarios coercendos esse: Epist. 48. ad Vincentium: tamen de certo tantùm hæreticorum genere, non de omni, id statuisse videtur: & quidem de Donatistis, & Circumcellionibus, quos simul tur bulentos, & seditiosos fuisse constat.

6. Quia periculum est, ut ex constan, tiâ & animositate hæreticorum, in perferendis suppliciis, multi ad eandem hæresin am. plexandam inflammentur, statuentes, id sine peculiari DEI Spiritu, afflatu & assistentia fieri non posse: cùm tamen Diabolus etiam suos habeat Martyres: Quemadmodum hujur rei exemplum suo tempore obtigisse scribit alicubi Joannes Brentius.

Deinde rationes ab Augustino assignatæ evincunt, per vim externam illum non intellexisse gladium occisionis, sed vel

7. Quia si nostri gladio sævirent in mulctas, vel plagas, vel carceres, vel exilia, vel hujus generis pœnas alias, quæ vitam non adimunt : Quia nimirùm statim subjicit : Hoc sibi non videri inutile, propterea quòd multi hoc pacto sint correcti : id quod de occisis affirmari nequit. Siquidem gladio interfectus non correctus, sed correptus dici potest.

Augustino suffragatur Tertullianus, sic ad Scapulam : Humani juris, & naturalis potestatis est, unicuig, quod putaverit colere : nec alii prodest aut obest alterius religio. Sed nec Religionis est cogere Religionem, quæ sponte suscipi debet, non vi.

Chrysostomus Serm. de Anathemate : Dogmata impia, & quæ ab hæreticis profecta sunt, arquere & anathematizare oportet. Hominibus autem parcendum, & pro salute eorum orandum.

Hieron. in cap. 2. Hoseæ : Quomodo de hæretici salute non desperabit ? quo pacto ad pœnitentiam eum provocabit ? Quá ratione ejus salutem se optare ostendet is, qui Magistratui eum necandum tradit ?

Sic jus Canonicum disertè prohibet, ne Spirituales ob hæresin quenquam occidant, vel per se, vel per alios : & neque voluntatem, neque factum, neque consilium suum ad id accommodent. Causa 23. q. ult. sive 50. C. His quibus.

Quæ ipsa praxis in Ecclesiâ quoque Romanâ observata fuit: ita ut Innocentius. I. P. M. primùm extitisse videatur, qui Antichristi Spiritu impulsus, hæreticos ad fidem Romanam non Romanam, gladio cogere non dubitavit : circa A. C. 415. Quanquam aliquot ejus successores, duriorem hunc cum hæreticis agendi modum, & processum, rarissimè observarunt : usque dum Antichristus Romanus dominatum in Ecclesia stabilivit, & sanguine Martyrum Jesu eum conspurcavit, & formidabilem toti orbi Christiano reddidit.

Quâ in sententiâ fuit etiam B. Lutherus, in expositione parabolæ de Zizaniis : Docemur, inquiens, quomodo nos gerere debeamus erga hæreticos : non enim eos extinguere & exscindere oportet. Apertè enim hic Christus ait : Sinite crescere utraq; : Solo Dei Verbo contra eos agendum. Ita enim hac in re evenire solet, ut qui hodie erret, cras possit redire in viam. Quis enim novit, quando Dei Verbum Cor cujusquam attracturum sit ? Si autem exuratur, vel aliàs tollatur, certè impeditur, ne possit in viam reduci : imò jam perire eum necesse sit, qui aliàs potuisset ab errore liberari.

Et ex gente Calvinianâ idem planè sentit Wolfgangus Musculus Dusanus in Locis Communibus : tit. de Hæresi : pag. mihi 611. Spiritus, inquiens, crudelitatis est non verorum Christianorum, sed hæreticorum. Christianis Magistratus animadvertit quidem in hæreticos, verùm sic moderatè, ut sint, qui resipiscere possint. Non patitur, ut de fide doceant: nec permittit, ut Ecclesias colligant, episcopos & alios ministros ordinent: alios privat honoribus: alios adimit civitatis communicationem: alios proscribit: alios multâ pecuniariâ punit: quod Augustini temporibus factum esse legimus. Ipsos impostores ac seductores, ne illi, postquàm incorrigibiles apparent, ultrà quemquam seducant, carceribus inclusos tamdiu coercet, ac detinet, donec in se reversi resipiscant. Sic coërcendi sunt, qui cogi se ad bonum non sustinent. Hac pœnarum moderatione ad scopum pertingi potest, ad quem collimare debet Christianus magistratus. Is est, ut convertantur hæretici ab erroribus suis, & conversi salventur. Qui errantem in errore suo occidit, aut non credit, quod perniciosè & damnabiliter coram Deo erret: aut si hoc credit, parum est de salute illius sollicitus. De illis hæreticis loquor, qui etsi graviter errent, haud tamen blasphemi sunt adversus Deum. Blasphemum lex Dei vivere non patitur &c. Hæc W. Musculus.


### Chapter II. On the Office of the Political Magistrate: Question IV. Whether the civil magistrate may arrogate to himself, as a political prerogative, the vocation and dismissal of ministers of…

There are and are found not a few from the number of those, whether Nobles or Magnates, in whose possession are the rights of patronage, as they are commonly called by ecclesiastics, who, when they understand that they possess the Right of patronage over one or another Church: insolently persuade themselves that they are the Lords of those Churches, and therefore deem the Right of calling and dismissing ministers of the Church to belong to them alone as a political royal prerogative, such that they decree that no right here is to be conceded either to the ecclesiastical ministry or to the remaining Hearers of the Word. However, this is tyranny, which neither the authority of the Scriptures, nor of pious Emperors or Princes, nor even of any reasons, can establish. For 1. God indeed says of Kings and Princes of the Church that they shall be its nursing fathers. Isa. 49. v. 23. but whether it ought to be understood of such a dominion over the Church, the same Holy Spirit explains through the same Prophet, in the same verse: Saying, with face bowed to the earth they shall worship you, and lick the dust of your feet: How this is to be understood is taught more plainly, Isa. 60. v. 10. Kings shall minister to you. Therefore, their principal duty is that, as an excellent member of the Church, they use their power, with which they have been divinely instructed. for the planting and increase, not for the overthrow of the Church. But the Church is overthrown, not planted, when Magnates, perhaps touched by a somewhat harsh sermon of a Minister of the word, arrogate to themselves dominion over him, and by their own daring, according to the mere dictates of perverse flesh and passions, attempt to eject him from the office legitimately entrusted to him: deeming him in this respect of equal lot and condition with a herdsman or a stable-boy: or when, in calling Ministers, they are solicitous for 'Placentines,' that is, persons of such a kind who wink at any crimes and villainies whatsoever.

2. If the right of calling and dismissing Ministers of the Church pertains to political royal prerogatives, it would follow that either in those first three hundred years after the birth of Christ, during which the Church lacked a Christian Magistrate, it did not have legitimately called ministers of the Word: or that the right of calling Ministers does not pertain to political royal prerogatives. But the former is simply false: Therefore, the latter is true.

3. Not even the prescriptions or laws of Civil law can be brought forward, by which they might be able to prove that some such power over the Ministers of the Church has been granted to them. By Canon law, certainly, all Politicians are simply barred from such dominion. What else, therefore, shall we conclude, than that they are usurpers of another's right and dominion, and indeed of that dominion which, by the institution of Christ, belongs to the whole Church.

For the fourth reason is that the right of calling ministers of the Church belongs to the whole Church, and to its individual orders, as to a royal Priesthood: as was invincibly demonstrated in the Question concerning the calling of Ministers of the Church. In which way Matthias and Barnabas are read to have been called to teach the Gospel in the primitive Church: the former indeed in Acts 1:23 and 24, the latter in Acts 11:22. And a most firm reason underlies this ordination: Because what touches all, ought to be approved by all. When, therefore, the political order, whoever that may be, calls a minister of the Church without the knowledge and consultation of the remaining orders: or dismisses one already called without the legitimate cognition and judgment of the whole Church (which today Presbyteries or Consistories represent): he commits a great sacrilege.

5. Rights of patronage grant no more to the Patron than that, when the ministry is vacant, he has the power of nominating some person, and presenting him to the presbytery or Consistory, which acts in the place of the Church, and, as they say, exercises Episcopal jurisdiction, though with vicarious power: but in such a way that it leaves the judgment concerning the dignity and gifts, and thus the quality of that person, free and entirely to the Church. When, therefore, some Politician arrogates to himself more right and authority in this regard, he manifestly betrays his own stupendous rudeness and ignorance, in that he does not understand what, in this place and in this question, the Right of Patronage is, and how far it extends.

Finally, the examples of certain most praiseworthy Emperors correct the insanity of these braggarts. The Emperor Valentinian, certainly, when a Synod had made the election free for him, so that he might choose whom he wished and appoint him Bishop of the Church, is read to have replied: Such an election is above us. For you, having obtained divine grace and shining with that splendor, will be able to choose better. And thus, the Emperor later gave his assent to the election made by the Bishops. Thus the constitution of the Emperors Charles and Louis is this, dist. 63: Not ignorant of the Sacred Canons, so that the holy Church may more freely enjoy its honor in the name of GOD, we give our assent to the Ecclesiastical order, that Bishops be chosen by the election of the clergy and people, according to the statutes of the canons. But the constitution of the Emperor Justinian 6. & 123, is as follows: When a Bishop is to be chosen in any Church, then the Ministers of that Church and the Magistrates in the city ought to convene, and make their election from three persons.

Latin:

SUnt & reperiuntur non pauci ex eorum si, ve Nobilium, sive Magnatum numero, penes quos sunt Jura patronatus, uti vulgò loquuntur Ecclesiastici, qui cùm intelligant se possidere Jus patronatus, in unam vel alteram Ecclesiam: insolenter sibi persuadent, se esse Dominos illarum Ecclesiarum, ac proinde Jus vocandi & dimittendi ministros Ecclesiæ, tanquam regale Politicum ita ad se solos pertinere autumant, ut nihil hic juris, vel ministerio Ecclesiastico, vel Auditoribus Verbi reliquis, concedendum esse, statuant. Cæterùm tyrannis hæc est, quam neque Scripturarum, neque piorum Imperatorum aut Principum, neque rationum etiam ullarum autoritas, stabilire potest. Nam 1. de Regibus & Principibus Ecclesiæ dicit quidem Deus, quòd futuri sint ejus nutritii. Jes. 49. v. 23. sed num de tali aliquo dominio in Ecclesiam illud accipi debeat, idem Spiritus Sanctus per eundem Prophetam explicat, eodem versu: Vultu inquiens in terram demisso adorabunt te, & pedum tuorum pulverem lingent: Quod quomodo intelligendum sit, planius docetur, Jesa. 60. v. 10. Reges ministrabunt tibi. Principale ergo ipsorum officium est, ut tanquam eximium Ecclesiæ membrum, potentiâ suâ, quâ divinitùs instructi sunt, utantur ad plantationem & incrementum, non ad eversionem Ecclesiae. Evertitur autem, non plantatur Ecclesia, quando Magnates vel duriuscula fortè legis concione tacti à Ministro verbi, dominium sibi in ipsum arrogant, & officio legitimè ipsi demandato, proprio ausu, ad solum carnis perversae & affectuum dictamen, ejicere conantur: paris hac in parte sortis & conditionis cum bubulco aut stabulario ipsum arbitrati: vel quando in vocandis Ministris de Placentinis, hoc est, ejusmodi personis sunt solliciti, quae ad quaevis scelera & flagitia conniveant.

2. Si ad regalia politica pertinet Jus vocandi & dimittendi Ministros Ecclesiae, consequens fuerit, aut primis illis trecentis annis post Christum natum, quibus Ecclesia caruit Magistratu Christiano, non habuisse ministros Verbi legitimè vocatos: aut Jus vocandi Ministros non pertinere ad Regalia politica. Atqui prius illud simpliciter falsum: Ergo posterius hoc verum.

3. Ne quidem juris Civilis praescripta sive leges proferri possunt, quibus talem aliquam potestatem in Ministros Ecclesiae sibi concessam esse probare queant. Jure certè Canonico à tali dominio simpliciter omnes Politici arcentur. Quid ergo aliud statuemus, quàm alieni juris & dominij usurpatores eos esse, & quidem illius Dominij, quod ex institutione Christi, toti Ecclesiae competit.

Nam quae quarta est ratio, Jus vocandi ministros Ecclesiae, ad totam Ecclesiam, & singulos ejus ordines, tanquam ad regale Sacerdotium pertinet: uti in Quaestione de vocatione Ministrorum Ecclesiae invictè fuit demonstratum. Quo modo in primitiva Ecclesia Matthias & Barnabas ad docendum Evangelium vocati esse leguntur: Ille quidem Actor. 1. 23. & 24. Hic verò Actor. 11. 22. Et subest huic ordinationi firmissima ratio: Quia quod omnes tangit, ab omnibus approbari debet. Quando ergo ordo politicus, quisquis etiam ille sit, insciis, & inconsultis reliquis ordinibus ministrum Ecclesiae vocat: vel jam vocatum sine legitima totius Ecclesiae (quam hodiè presbyteria sive Consistoria repraesentant) cognitione, & judicio dimittit: is grande sacrilegium committit.

5. Jura Patronatus plus non largiuntur Patrono, quàm quòd vacante ministerio, ipse potestatem habet, personam aliquam nominandi, eamque presbyterio sive Consistorio, quod vices Ecclesiae gerit, & ut loquuntur, Episcopali jurisdictione, potestate tamen vicaria, fungitur, praesentandi: sed ita, ut de dignitate & donis, adeoque qualitate illius personae judicium liberum, & insolidum Ecclesiae relinquat. Quando ergò plus sibi juris & autoritatis Politicus aliquis hac in parte arrogat, is stupendam suam ruditatem & inscitiam manifestè prodit, quòd nimirùm non intelligat, quid hoc loco, & in hac quaestionæ Jus Patronatus sit, & quousq; se extendat.

Tandem laudatissimorum quorundam Imperatorum exempla, Thrasonum istorum insaniam corrigunt. Valentinianus certè Imp. cùm Synodus liberam ipsi fecisset electionem, ut quem vellet, eligeret, & præficeret Ecclesiæ Episcopum, respondisse legitur. Super nos est talis electio. Vos enim gratiâ divinâ potiti, & illo splendore fulgentes, melius poteritis eligere. Et sic Electioni ab Episcopis factæ, Imperator postmodùm suum præbuit assensum. Sic Caroli, & Ludovici Imperatorum constitutio hæc est, dist. 63. Sacrorum Canonum non ignari, ut DEI nomine sancta Ecclesia suo honore liberiùs potiatur, assensum ordini Ecclesiastico præbemus, ut Episcopi per electionem cleri & populi, secundum statuta canonum eligantur. Justiniani verò Imperatoris constitutio 6. & 123. sic habet: Cùm Episcopus in aliqua Ecclesia eligendus est, tum Ecclesiæ illius Ministri, & Magistratus in urbe convenire debent, deq; tribus personis electionem suam facere.


### Chapter II. On the Office of the Political Magistrate: Question V. Does the political magistrate have the right and power of forbidding ministers of the Church, from the pulpit, to censure…

Whether the Political Magistrate has the right and power of forbidding Ministers of the Church to attack heretics, especially Calvinists by name, from the pulpit?

There are found today, especially in the courts of Calvinizing Princes, political counselors who, inflated by an excessive persuasion of their own wisdom, attempt to prescribe laws to the Doctors and Ministers of the Church, with a clearly Praetorian and Dictatorial authority, that they should either not refute errors at all, especially those of the Calvinists, or at least do so with their names suppressed. Whence those mandates and edicts took their origin, by which, under the threat of a most grave penalty, at the very least the deprivation of office, such a 'Moderation,' as they call it, is enjoined upon the Ministers of the Church. It must be noted, however, in this place, that this is not the primary question and point of controversy: Whether in refuting heretics due moderation ought to be employed by the Ministers and Doctors of the Word, which we ourselves also repeatedly inculcate to future heralds of the word and Theologians, diligently warning them that in naming and refuting the Calvinists and their errors, they should leave room for a spirit of gentleness and meekness, renounce every movement of private affections, and not attack the persons rather than the errors themselves out of hatred for the errors, they inveigh against the Calvinists. And indeed, the untimely zeal of some, who in discoursing against Sectarians, whether Papists, or Calvinists, or any others whatsoever, so burn with anger and vehemence of emotion that, often because of an immoderate can by no means be approved, nor ought it to be.

That such men should be restrained by the authority of the Civil Magistrate and kept within the limits of due moderation, we ourselves do not disapprove: especially if the presbytery performs its duty too negligently in this regard, and does not rebuke and correct the preposterous and inordinate zeal of such a preacher with just severity.

But this is the proper and legitimate state of the controversy: Whether a Minister of the Church, even while keeping himself within the legitimate limits of due moderation, ought to abstain, at the interdict of the Civil Magistrate, from criticizing and refuting heretics, and especially Calvinists, by name in his sermon? Where the Calvinists fight for the affirmative, but beyond and against Scripture and all reason: We hold the negative in all respects, maintaining that such edicts, since they fight against the command of GOD, are not to be obeyed: according to the decision of Peter in the final terms, who, when ordered by the princes and Elders of the people not to make mention of the name of JESUS in his sermon, answered manfully and intrepidly: judge for yourselves whether it is right to obey you rather than GOD. Acts 4.18 & 19 & ch. 5. 28 & 29. Now our principal reasons for this negative are these:

I. The office of ministers requires that they take good care that wolves and sectarians do not rush upon the wretched sheep, but that they act as watchmen, keeping constant guard so that no harm is done to the purer religion by any heretics whatsoever, to the ruin of the hearers. This duty God demands so severely from the Doctors of the Word that if any perish through their sloth, they must necessarily answer for their blood. The following testimonies of Scripture pertain to this: Isaiah 58: 1. Cry aloud, do not cease, lift up your voice like a trumpet, and announce to my people their transgressions, and to the house of Jacob their sins. Jeremiah 1. 10. Behold, I have put my words in your mouth: behold, I have set you this day over the Nations, and over kingdoms, to root out, and to pull down, and to destroy, and to throw down, and to build, and to plant. Jeremiah 6. 17. I have set watchmen over you: Hear the sound of the trumpet: and they said: We will not hear, etc. Ezekiel 3. 18. Son of man, I have made you a watchman to the house of Israel: and you shall hear the word from my mouth: and you shall announce it to them from me: If, when I say to the wicked: You shall surely die: you do not announce it to him, nor speak to him, that he may turn from his wicked way, and live: the same wicked man shall die in his iniquity; but his blood I will require at your hand, etc.

Which same thing is repeated in almost the same words, Ezekiel 33. 7. & seqq.

In the New Testament these are the principal ones:

Matthew 5. 13. You are the salt of the earth: But if the salt has lost its taste, with what shall it be salted?

Acts 20. 28. Take heed to yourselves, and to the whole flock, in which the Holy Spirit has placed you as Bishops, to rule the Church of GOD, which He has acquired with His own blood. I know that after my departure wolves will enter, not sparing the flock: And from among yourselves men will arise, speaking perverse things, to draw away disciples after them: therefore WATCH.

2 Timothy 4. 2. Preach the word: be instant in season, out of season: reprove, rebuke with all gentleness and doctrine: for there will be a time when they will not endure sound doctrine: and they will turn their ears away from the truth: But you watch in all things, do the work of an Evangelist, fulfill your ministry.

Tit. 1. 9 & seqq. A bishop must be powerful in exhorting in sound doctrine: and in refuting adversaries or those who contradict: For there are many seducers, whose mouths must be stopped. For which reason rebuke them sharply, that they may be sound in the faith.

And chap. 2. 7. In all things show yourself an example in doctrine, and in severity concerning sound speech, which cannot be condemned: that he who opposes himself from the opposite side, may be ashamed.

II. The practice of the Church of GOD of all times of both Testaments demands the same: nay, the express commands of GOD, seriously enjoining that the error of no False Teacher or heretic be in any way covered or palliated: but rather, that it be brought into the sight of the whole people, and being convicted of error, be killed: and in this matter let neither brother, nor son, nor daughter, nor wife, nor intimate friend be spared. Such an edict may be read, Deut. 13. 1, & seqq. If there shall arise in the midst of you a Prophet, or one who says he has seen a dream, and says to you: Let us go, and follow strange GODS which you do not know, and let us serve them: you shall not hear the word of that Prophet, or dreamer: for the Lord your GOD is testing you, so that it may be made plain whether you love him or not, with your whole heart, and with your whole soul. Follow the LORD your GOD, and fear him, and keep his commandments, and hear his voice, you shall serve him, and to him you shall adhere. But that prophet or dreamer of dreams shall be put to death: because he has spoken to turn you away from the LORD your GOD, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, and redeemed you from the house of bondage: to make you wander from the way, which the Lord your GOD commanded you: and you shall take away the evil from the midst of you. If your brother, the son of your mother, or your son or daughter, or the wife who is in your bosom, or the friend whom you love as your own soul, shall wish to persuade you, saying secretly: Let us go, and serve strange gods, which you do not know, nor your Fathers: do not obey him, nor hear him, nor let your eye spare him, so as to have pity, and hide him, but you shall immediately kill him: let your hand be first upon him, and after you let all the people cast their hand: he shall be killed, overwhelmed with stones: because he wished to draw you away from the LORD your GOD &c. Thus far the authentic Mosaic [law]. Although this law concerning the killing of false prophets and any heretics whatsoever was indeed proper to the Mosaic polity, and therefore does not oblige us to its observance, but when that polity of the Jews itself met its end: yet the very kind or general practice, which is to be observed by the Church of GOD concerning heretics, is most rightly elicited from this: namely, that pains must be taken so that they may in no way inflict damage upon the Church and the purer religion, and that they may not draw men away from the true GOD to an alien god, that is, such a one as is not revealed in the Scriptures: which thing certainly can be done by no other reason than if such false teachers are expressly and publicly censured, their errors are detected and refuted, and it is openly shown with what falsehoods and blasphemies they labor.

Jeremiah the Prophet observed this practice, publicly and by name arguing against the false prophet Hananiah: Hear, Hananiah: The LORD has not sent you, and you have made this people trust in a lie. And ch. 29. 8. Your prophets, who are in your midst, seduce you: do not attend to your dreams, which you dream. Because they prophesy falsely to you in my name. And a little later in verse 21. Thus says the LORD of hosts, to Ahab the son of Kolaiah, and to Zedekiah the son of Maaseiah, who prophesy to you in my name falsely: Behold, I will deliver them into the hands of Nebuchadnezzar, etc.

Christ held the same practice, who argues against and condemns the Pharisees by name for their errors: Matt. 23. and Luke 11. 42. and following. Likewise John the Baptist, who calls the Pharisees a brood of vipers, Matt. 3. 7. Likewise the Apostle, who censures Phygellus, Hermogenes, and other false teachers by name, 2 Tim. 1. 15. etc.

The third reason is sought from the command of Christ, Matt. 7. 15. Beware of false prophets, who come to you in sheep's clothing, but inwardly are ravenous wolves. Therefore heretics are to be avoided, but who can be avoided, who are known to us neither by name nor by doctrine: Furthermore, they are to be avoided all the more studiously, the greater simplicity and holiness they are accustomed to feign under the clothing of sheep. This mask must be stripped from them, and the sheep's clothing cast off, by an accurate refutation of the most foul errors which they insidiously conceal: and then it will be clear to the whole Church of GOD how savage and truculent wolves they are, seeking dominion for themselves over the miserable sheep, so that they may be able to range freely and with impunity among them, to their eternal destruction. Mindful of this command, the Apostle seriously exhorts his Philippians to beware of dogs and of evil workers, designating false teachers by these two titles. For they are 1. dogs, as those who fix the lethal bites of false opinions into the minds of men: who like dogs in the Church of GOD make a tumult, barking with a cursing mouth at everything, however rightly and laudably constituted, and as much as in them lies, tear apart and rend. They are furthermore evil workers, directing all their studies, counsels, and actions solely to the destruction of the sheep and the infection of Christ's sheepfold: which thing is also most clearly evident from the practice of the Calvinists.

Latin:

An Magistratus Politicus jus & potestatem habeat interdicendi Ministris Ecclesiæ, ne pro suggestu hæreticos, præsertim Calvinianos nominatim perstringant?

REperiuntur hodiè, in aulis præsertim Principum Calvinizantium Consiliarii politici, qui nimia persuasione sapientiæ inflati, Doctoribus & Ministris Ecclesiæ, Prætoriâ planè, & Dictatoriâ autoritate, leges præscribere conantur, ut errores aut omninò non confutent, Calvinianorum præsertim, vel certè id suppresso ipsorum nomine faciant. Unde mandata illa, & edicta traxerunt Originem, quibus sub comminatione pœnæ gravissimæ, ad minimum privationis officij, talis, uti loquuntur, Moderatio Ministris Ecclesiæ præcipitur. Notandum autem hoc loco, non illud potissimùm quæri & controverti: An in refutandis hæreticis debita moderatio à Ministris, & Doctoribus Verbi sit adhibenda, quam nos ipsi quoque futuris verbi præconibus, & Theologis etiam atque etiam inculcamus, sedulò monentes, ut in nominandis, refutandisq; Calvinianis, eorumq; erroribus, lenitatis & mansuetudinis Spiritui locum relinquant, omni privatorum affectuum motui nuncium remittant, neque personarum potiùs, quàm ipsorum errorum odio, in Calvinianos invehantur. Et profectò nullo prorsus pacto probari potest, aut debet intempestivus quorundam zelus, qui disserendo contra Sectarios, sive Pontificios, sive Calvinianos, sive alios quoscunque, ita ira & affectuum vehementia exardescunt, ut sæpiùs præ immoderata animi impotentia, ex orationis cursu præcipites acti, quid dicant, propemodùm ipsi ignorent.

Tales Magistratus etiam Politici autoritate coërceri, & intra limites debitæ moderationis contineri, ipsimet non improbemus: præsertim si presbyterium hac in parte negligenciùs faciat officium, & ejusmodi Concionatoris Zelum præposterum & inordinatum, non justa severitate reprehendat & corrigat.

Verùm hic est proprius & legitimus Controversiæ status: An Minister Ecclesiæ etiam intra legitimos debitæ moderationis limites se continens, ad interdictum Magistratus Politici ab hæreticis, & potissimùm Calvinianis, pro concione nominatim perstringendis, & refutandis, abstinere debeat? Ubi Calvinianis pro affirmativa, sed præter & contra Scripturam & rationem omnem pugnantibus: Nos negativam per omnia tenemus, statuentes, Ejusmodi edictis, quippe cum mandato DEI pugnantibus non esse obtemperandum: secundum decisionem Petri in terminis terminantibus, qui à principibus & Senioribus populi jussus, ne pro concione mentionem faceret nominis JESU, masculè & intrepidè respondit: vos ipsi judicate, an justu sit, Vobis magis, quàm DEO obedire. Actor. 4.18. & 19. & cap. 5. 28. & 29. Negativæ autem hujus nostræ rationes præcipuæ sunt hæ:

I. Ministrorum officium exigit, ut probè observent, ne lupi & sectarii irruant in miseras oves, sed tanquam speculatores subinde excubias agant, ne puriori religioni, in perniciem Auditorum, ullo pacto damni quid inferatur ab hæreticis quibusvis. Quod officium adeò severè Deus à Doctoribus Verbi efflagitat, ut si socordia ipsorum aliqui perierint, sanguinem istorum ipsi luere necessum sint habituri. Huc pertinent sequentia Scripturæ testimonia: Esai. 58: 1. Clama, ne cesses, instar tubæ exalta vocem tuam, & annuncia populo meo prævaricationes eorum, & domui Jacob peccata eorum. Jerem. 1. 10. Ecce, dedi verba mea in ore tuo: ecce, constitui te hodie super Gentes, & super regna, ut evellas, & destruas, & disperdas, & dissipes, & ædifices, & plantes. Jerem. 6. 17. Constitui super vos speculatores: Audite vocem tubæ: & dixerunt: Nō audiemus, &c. Jezech. 3. 18. Filii hominis, speculatorem dedi te domui Israël: & audies de ore meo verbum: & annuntiabis eis ex me: Si dicente me ad impium: Morte morieris: non annunciaveris ei, neq; locutus fueris, ut avertatur à via sua impia, & vivat: ipse impius in impietate sua morietur: sanguinem autem ejus de tua manu requiram &c.

Quod ipsum iisdem penè verbis repetitur, Ezech. 33. 7. & seqq.

In Novo Testamento præcipua sunt isthæc:

Matth. 5 13. Vos estis sal terræ: Quod si sal infatuatus fuerit, quo salietur?

Actor. 20. 28. Attendite vobis, & universo gregi, in quo vos Spiritus Sanctus posuit Episcopos, ut regatis Ecclesiam DEI, quam acquisivit sanguine suo. Ego scio, quòd post discessum meum intrabunt lupi, non parcentes gregi: Et ex vobis ipsis exurgent viri, loquentes perversa, ut abducant discipulos post se: propterea VIGILATE.

2. Timoth. 4. 2. Prædica verbum: insta tempestive, intempestive: argue, objurga cum omni lenitate & doctrina: nam erit tempus quo sanam doctrinam non tolerabunt: & à veritate aures avertent: At tu vigila in omnibus, opus perage Evangelistæ, ministerij tui PLENAM fidem facito

Tit. 1. 9 & seqq. Oportet Episcopum esse potentem ad exhortandum in sanâ doctrinâ: & ad arguendos adversarios sive contradicentes: Sunt enim multi seductores, quibus oportet os obstruere. Quam ob causam eos redarguito durè, ut fiant sani in fide.

Et cap 2 7. In omnibus teipsum præbe exemplum in doctrina, & severitate circa sanum sermonem, qui damnari non possit: ut qui se ex adverso opponit, erubescat.

II. Idem exigit praxis Ecclesiæ DEI, omnium temporum utriusque Testamenti: imò expressa DEI mandata, seriò precipientia, ut nullius Pseudo Doctoris sive hæretici error quovis modo tegatur, aut palliétur: sed potiùs, ut in conspectum toti9 populi producatur, & erroris convictus occidatur: & hac in parte nec fratri, nec filio, nec filiæ, nec uxori, nec familiari parcatur. Quale edictum legere licet, Deut. 13 1, & seqq. Si surrexerit in medio tui Propheta, aut qui somnium se vidisse dicat, & dixerit tibi: Eamus, & sequamur DEOS alienos quos ignoras, & serviamus eis: non audies verbum Prophetæ illius, aut somniatoris: quia tentat vos Dominus DEUS vester, ut palàm fiat, utrum diligatis eum annon, in toto corde, & in tota anima vestra. DOMINUM DEUM vestrum sequimini, & ipsum timete, & mandata illius custodite, & audite vocem ejus, ipsi servietis, & ipsi adhærebitis. Propheta autem ille aut fictor somniorum interficietur: quia locutus est, ut vos averteret à DOMINO DEO vestro, qui eduxit vos de terrâ Ægypti, & redemit vos de domo servitutis: ut errare te faceret de viâ, quam tibi præcepit Dominus DEUS tuus: & auferes malum de medio tui. Si tibi voluerit persuadere frater tuus, filius matris tuæ, aut filius tuus vel filia, sive uxor, quæ est in sinu tuo, aut amicus, quem diligis ut animam tuam, clàm dicens: Eamus, & serviamus diis alienis, quos ignoras tu, & Patres tui: non obedias ei, neq; audias, neque parcat ei oculus tuus, ut miserearis, & occultes eum, sed statim interficies: sit primùm manus tua super ipsum, & post te omnis populus mittat manum: lapidibus obrutus necabitur: quia voluit te abstrahere à DOMINO DEO tuo &c. Hactenus authentica Mosaica. Quanquam verò lex hæc de occidendis Pseudoprophetis & hæreticis quibuslibet, Politæ Mosaicæ fuit propria, & iccircò nos ad sui observationem non obligat: sed cùm ipsa politia Judæorum finem sortita est: ipsum tamen genus sive praxis generalis, quæ Ecclesiæ DEI circà hæreticos observanda, rectissimè hinc elicitur: quòd nimirùm opera danda, ut ne ullo pacto damnum inserant Ecclesiæ, & puriori religioni, & à DEO vero, ad DEum alienum, hoc est, talem, qualis in Scripturis non est revelatus, homines abstrahant: id quod certè nulla ratione alia fieri potest, quàm si ejusmodi falsi Doctores nominatim publicè perstringantur, errores ipsorum detegantur, & refutentur, & quibus falsitatibus ac blasphemiis laborent, palàm ostendatur.

Hanc praxin observavit Jeremias Propheta, publicè & nominatim Pseudoprophetam Hanani arguens: Audi Hanani: Non misit te DOMINUS, & tu confidere fecisti populum istum in mendacio. Et cap. 29. 8. Vos seducunt Prophetæ vestri, qui sunt in medio vestri: ne attendatis ad somnia vestra, quæ vos somniatis. Quia falsò ipsi prophetant vobis in nomine meo. Et paulò post versu 21. Hæc dicit DOMINUS exercituum, ad Achab filium Coliæ, & ad Sedeciam filium Maasiæ, qui prophetant vobis in nomine meo mendaciter: Ecce ego tradam eos in manus Nebucadnezaris, &c.

Eandem praxin tenuerunt Christus, qui Pharisæos nominatim errorum arguit & damnat: Matth. 23. & Luc. 11. 42. & seqq. Item Johannes Baptista, qui Pharisæos nominat progeniem viperarum, Matth. 3. 7. Item Apostolus, qui Phygellum Hermogenem, & alios falsos Doctores nominatim perstringit, 2.Tim. 1. 15. &c.

Tertia ratio petitur à mandato Christi, Matth. 7. 15. Cavete vobis à Pseudoprophetis, qui veniunt ad vos vestitu ovium tecti, intus autem sunt lupi rapaces. Cavendi ergò sunt hæretici, sed qui caveri possunt, qui nobis neque à nomine, neque à doctrina sunt cogniti: Deindè tantò studiosiùs sunt cavendi, quantò majorem simplicitatem & sanctitatem sub vestitu ovium simulare solent. Hæc larva ipsis detrahenda est, & vestitus ovilis exuendus, accurata refutatione errorum fœdissimorum, quos insidiosè occultant: & tum patebit toti Ecclesiæ DEI, quàm sævi & truculenti lupi, dominium sibi quærant in miseras oves, ut in eas, cum æterno ipsarum exitio, liberè & impunè grassari possint. Mandati hujus memor Apostolus Philippenses suos seriò exhortatur, sibi caveant à canibus, & à malis operariis, duobus hisce titulis falsos doctores indigitans. Sunt enim 1. canes, ut qui morsus lethiferos falsarum opinionum infigant animis hominum: qui tanquam canes in Ecclesia DEI tumultuantur, omnia quantúmvis rectè ac laudabiliter constituta, rictu maledico allatrant, & quantum in ipsis, dilacerant, ac discerpunt. Sunt deinde mali operarij, omnia sua studia, consilia, actiones, ad exitium ovium, & infectionem ovilis Christi unicè dirigentes: id quod ex praxi Calvinianorum etiam luculentissimè patet.


### Chapter II. On the Office of the Political Magistrate: Question V. Does the political magistrate have the right and power of forbidding ministers of the Church, from the pulpit, to censure… (continued)

The fourth reason can be taken from the constitutions and practice of the ancient Orthodox Church, which willed that heretics be publicly and by name condemned. For thus the Fifth Ecumenical Synod of Constantinople defined: can. 11. If anyone does not anathematize Arius, Eunomius, Macedonius, Apollinaris, Nestorius, Eutyches, and Origen, with their impious writings, and all other heretics who have been condemned and anathematized by the Holy Catholic and Apostolic Church of GOD, or by the aforementioned four Holy Councils: but also those who have thought or have not been willing to think similar things with the aforementioned heretics, and have remained in their own impiety until the end, let such a one be anathema.

Examples of this ecclesiastical practice are readily available everywhere in great numbers. Certainly when John of Antioch was supporting Nestorius, for the reason especially that he had not yet been sufficiently heard, nor legitimately convicted of error: and therefore was unwilling to censure Nestorius and his dogma by name, and publicly condemn them: Cyril struck him with anathema no less than Nestorius: until he acknowledged the error, and publicly abjured and detested the dogma of Nestorius.

Fifthly, there is the greatest danger, and the most present destruction of the purer Religion, if a free power is granted to heretics to range in the Church: and they are not pointed out to the hearers either by name or by finger, so that they may be avoided. Concerning which matter Selneccer writes that Philip Melanchthon, in the year 1552, discoursed in this manner for a public lecture at Torgau: Unnecessary contention does not edify the Church. But the matter stands far otherwise when in a case of Confession the truth must be defended. When in the Churches of the East it was requested that the orthodox doctrine concerning the divinity of the Son of GOD be proposed integrally, and the contrary doctrine be refuted with the name of Arius or the Arians suppressed. Many complied with this request. But the Orthodox, having perceived the fraud, said that it is a part of Confession, and not an indifferent matter, to separate themselves by name from Arianism in the refutation of false doctrine. Hence many were expelled, and a horrible persecution arose: And when Emperors and Princes connived at and were silent about the heresies of Arius and other fanatics scattered in Asia and elsewhere, the punishment followed that all those regions were polluted by Turkish blasphemies, the strength of Kings and Princes being broken, etc.

The Calvinists make two main exceptions in this place: First, that they do not in themselves disapprove of the refutations of false dogmas: provided that one does not descend to the hypothesis and to the individuals themselves. It is therefore entirely open to any Doctor of the Church to refute the errors of the Calvinists, if they favor any, provided that the persons themselves are spared, the naming of whom would contribute nothing to the matter. But I reply, This very thing is in question, whether that general refutation of false dogmas suffices, with the names of the heretics suppressed? Where we hold the negative in all respects, for these very reasons which we have already set forth.

Then they clamor that the denominations of sectarians, such as some being called Lutherans, others Zwinglians, others Calvinists, others Sacramentarians, etc., are by no means to be tolerated, since that one title of Christians applies to all equally, and therefore all these ought rather to be named Christians: Whence the Apostle also gravely rebukes the Corinthians, because one said he was of Paul, another of Apollos, another of Cephas, 1 Cor. 3.

But long ago it was shown to these censors that there is a huge dissimilarity in the examples: For in the doctrine itself Paul, Apollos, and Cephas did not dissent among themselves: but they taught and professed one and the same CHRIST, one and the same faith: and therefore the citizens of the Corinthian Church were to be named from CHRIST alone. But when some dogma is thrust upon the Church of GOD, which diametrically opposes the doctrine of CHRIST and the Apostles, and thus the Doctors themselves dissent among themselves: then the disciples and hearers not undeservedly obtain a denomination from their preceptors and masters, whose doctrine they follow.

And why, I pray, do the Calvinists themselves in their writings everywhere not only name Eutychians, Marcionites, Arians, and Nestorians in this way from the masters who were the authors of those heresies, but also openly condemn them? Why do they publicly and by name call us Ubiquitarians, Concordists, and Confessionists, if they are acting in earnest, and sincerely maintain, without pretense, that one must simply abstain from such denominations? Furthermore, things that are subordinate do not fight, much less destroy one another.

The appellation of Lutherans, therefore, does not take away the name of Christians: but only determines it: since otherwise the denomination of Christians is too general, which every heretic claims for himself. Which is the reason that in the Apostolic Creed also we profess that we believe the Church, not only Christian, although built upon CHRIST alone as the cornerstone: but also Apostolic: in distinction to the Pseudo-Apostles, who likewise boasted themselves to be citizens of the Christian Church. From this foundation the Apostle, distinguishing faithful Jews from the rest who were so called by name, names them children of Abraham, Gal. 3:7. And CHRIST names Nathanael an Israelite, 1 John 1:48. And Paul again names himself a Pharisee, expressly distinguishing himself by this denomination from the sect of the Sadducees, Acts 23:6.

Finally, the whole Orthodox Antiquity stands on our side in this place. Justin in Trypho: They are distinguished by surnames, denominated from certain men, as each was the author of some new doctrine: Of these some are called Marcionites: others Valentinians: others Basilidians: others Saturninians: others by another word, each from the first inventor of his dogma.

Athanasius, Sermon 1 against the Arians: The people never received a name from their Bishops, but from the LORD, in whom they believed. Certainly we did not obtain our appellations from the blessed Apostles, our preceptors: but we are, and are called, Christians from CHRIST. But those who derive the origin of their faith from elsewhere, DESERVEDLY bear the names of their authors before them. Wherefore, since we all were and were called Christians from CHRIST, Marcion, the inventor of heresy, was expelled. But the rest, who remained, retained the title of Christian. But those who followed Marcion were no longer called Christians from that point, but Marcionites. So also Valentinus, Basilides, Manichaeus, and the others imparted names to their followers.

These things being thus established, it is manifest that the adversaries who are averse to the names of sectarians are lying in ambush. For they see that, if they prevail in having these diverse names of diverse confessions proscribed from the Church of GOD, it could easily happen that under the equivocal and general title of Christians, they could invade any Church whatsoever, and under this venerable cloak spread their poison freely and with no one noticing. And here lies the snake in the grass, which is deservedly to be trampled upon and crushed by sensible and Orthodox Theologians.

They object with the words of the Blessed LUTHER, from Tom. 1. Witteb. fol. 7. There are some who, when they have read a leaf or two or heard a sermon, wipe it away quickly, and do nothing more than drive over it, and promise others with their being. They do it because they want to be seen as good Lutherans. Not so, you fool; hear, and let yourself be told; first I ask that one would be silent about my name, and not call themselves Lutheran but Christian. What is LUTHER? The doctrine is not mine. How did I, a poor stinking sack of maggots, come to it, that one should call the children of Christ with my unholy name? Let us abolish the partisan names, and be called Christians. But this passage and sentiment of B. LUTHER does not harm us in the least, nor does it help the Adversaries even a little. For LUTHER himself distinguishes between Person and Doctrine: and he reproves those who, neglecting the doctrine of Luther, venerate his name only externally, and carry it in their mouths. Just as today some of the Calvinists, with a protesting conscience, boast that the name and eulogy of Lutherans truly belongs to them, when they do not have even a γρῦ in common with the doctrine of LUTHER. Furthermore, they offer manifest violence to the words of Luther, while they recite them partly truncated, partly twisted into a foreign sense. The end and scope proposed to B. LUTHER is unique, that he may show: 1. That the foundation of faith is not built upon any mortal: but upon CHRIST alone: Wherefore he immediately adds: I am, and will be no master. That the doctrine of the Gospel cannot be propagated by those external denominations alone: For thus the words of LUTHER, placed in their entirety, cohere: Tom. 2. Germ. Wit. p. 4. There are some who, having read a leaf or two, or heard a sermon, snatch it up quickly and do nothing more than run over and promise the others with their ways, as if they were not Evangelical, not considering that they are sometimes simple, plain people who would gladly learn the truth if one told it to them: that I have taught to no one, and S. Paul has strictly forbidden it. They do it only because they want to know something new, to be seen as good Lutherans. But they misuse the H. Gospel for their own willfulness, with that you will never drive the Gospel into the hearts, you will much rather frighten them away, and must give a heavy answer that you have thus driven them from the truth. Not so you fool, Hear &c. 3. The discourse of LUTHER is to those who were ὁμόψηφοι in doctrine and faith. Wherefore he adds: Not so dear friends, let us abolish the partisan names, and be called Christians, whose doctrine we have. Which sentiment of LUTHER, as we approve it entirely, so we maintain that it can in no way be proven from it that it is not permitted for those who are true Christians to openly distinguish and separate themselves and their Churches from the heretical confessions of the Papists, Calvinists, Arians, and other Sectarians by a certain denomination taken from the confession itself (by certain Confessional Names). Thus, therefore, the Calvinists in citing LUTHER err and are deceived, by perpetual Sophistries of the Ignorance of the Elenchus, from the dictum secundum quid: and of vicious division.

Latin:

Quarta ratio sumi potest ab antiquæ Orthodoxæ Ecclesiæ constitutionibus, & praxi, quæ hæreticos publicè & nominatim damnari voluit. Sic enim definivit Synodus Constantinopolitana V. Oecumenica: can. 11. Si quis non anathematizat, Arium, Eunomium, Macedonium, Apollinarem, Nestorium, Eutychen, & Origenem, cum impiis eorum scriptis, & omnes alios hæreticos, qui condemnati sunt, & anathematizati à Sancta DEI Catholica & Apostolica Ecclesia, vel prædictis quatuor Sanctis Concilijs: sed & eos, qui similia cum prædictis hæreticis sapuerunt, aut sapere noluerunt, & usq; ad finem permanserunt in propria impietate, talis anathema sit.

Exempla praxews hujus Ecclesiasticæ in promtu sunt passim plurima. Certè cùm Johannes Antiochenus Nestorio suffragaretur, ided potissimùm, quòd nondum satis esset auditus, neque erroris legitimè convictus: ac proindè Nestorium ipsiusque dogma nominatim perstringere, & publicè damnare nollet: Cyrillus haud minùs atque Nestorium anathematẽ ipsum percussit: usque dum errorem agnosceret, & Nestorij dogma publicè abjuraret, ac detestaretur.

Quinto summum subest periculum, & purioris Religionis præsentissimum exitium, si hæreticis in Ecclesia grassandi libera concedatur potestas: neque illi Auditoribus vel nomine, vel digito monstrentur, ut caveri possint. Qua de re Philippum Melanchthonem, Anno 1552. pro publica lectione Torgæ tunc in modum disseruisse scribit Selneccerus: Contentio non necessaria non ædificat Ecclesiam. Longè autem aliter res se habet, cùm in casu Confessionis tuenda est veritas. Cùm in Ecclesiis Orientis peteretur, ut de Filij DEI divinitate orthodoxa doctrina proponeretur integrè, & contraria doctrina refutaretur suppresso nomine Arij, aut Arianorum. Huic petitioni multi obtemperaverunt. Orthodoxi autem animadversa fraude dixerunt, partem Confessionis esse, & non esse rem diaphoram, se in refutatione falsæ doctrinæ nominatim ab Arianismo separare. Hinc multi expulsi fuerunt, & orta est horrenda persecutio: Et cum Imperatores & Principes ad sparsas in Asia, & alibi hæreses Arij, & aliorum fanaticorum conniverent, & tacerent, pœna secuta est, ut omnes illæ Regiones Turcicis blasphemiis sint pollutæ, fracto robore Regum & Principum &c.

Duo potissimum excipiunt hoc loco Calviniani: Primùm scripta pr, se non impro bare falsorum dogmatum refutationes: dammodò non ad hypothesin, & ad ipsa individua descendatur. Integrum proinde esse cuilibet Doctori Ecclesiæ, refutare errores Calvinianorum, si quos faveant, modò personis ipsis parcatur, quarum nominatio nihil id rem faciat. Sed respondeo, Hoc ipsum esse in quæstione, an Generalis illa falsorum dogmatum refutatio sufficiat, suppressis hæreticorum nominibus? Ubi Negativam per omnia tenemus, his ipsis mox rationibus, quas jam expedivimus.

Deinde clamitant, Sectariorum denominationes, ut alij Lutherani, alij Zvvingliani, alij Calviniani, alij Sacramentarij & c. appellentur, minimè ferendas esse, cum unus ille Christianorum titulus omnibus ex æquo competat, ac proinde Christiani potius hi omnes nominari debeant: Unde Apostolus etiam Corinthios graviter objurget, quòd alius se Pauli, alius Apollo, alius Cephæ se esse dixerit, 1. Cor. 3.

Sed jam pridem censoribus istis monstrata est ingens dissimilitudo in exemplis: Etenim in doctrina ipsa non dissentiebant inter se Paulus, Apollo, Cephas: sed unum & eundem CHRISTUM, unam eandeque fidem docebant, & profitebantur: ideoque à solo CHRISTO denominandi erant cives Ecclesiæ Corinthiacæ. Cæterùm quando dogma aliquod Ecclesiæ DEI obtruditur, quod cum doctrina CHRISTI & Apostolorum è diametro pugnat, adeoque Doctores ipsi inter se dissentiunt: tùm discipuli & Auditores, à suis Præceptoribus atque Magistris, quorum doctrinam sequuntur, denominationem haud immerito fortiuntur.

Et cur obsecro Calviniani ipsi suis in Scriptis passim Eutychianos, Marcionitas, Arianos, Nestorianos, non solùm à Magistris hæresewn istarun autoribus sic denominant: sed & apertè damnant? Cur nos publicè & nominatim Ubiquitarios, Concordistas, Confessionistas appellant, rem seriam si agunt, & ab hujusmodi denominationibus simpliciter abstinendum esse, sine fuco sincerè statuunt? Porrò sub ordinata non pugnant multò minus se destruunt.

Lutheranorum ergo appellatio, Christianorum nomen non tollit: sed tantùm determinat: cùm alioqui nimiùm generalis Christianorum sit denominatio, quam hæretici quique sibi vendicant. Quæ causa est, quòd in Symbolo etiam Apostolico credere nos profitemur Ecclesiam, non modò Christianam, licèt soli CHRISTO superstructam, tanquam lapidi angulari: sed & Apostolicam: ad differentiam Pseudo-Apostolorum, qui itidem Christianæ Ecclesiæ cives sese jactitabant. Ex hoc fundamento Apostolus discernens Judæos fideles, à reliquis nominétenus sic dictis, nominat filios Abrahæ, Gal. 3. 7. Et CHRISTUS Nathanaëlem nominat Israëlītam, 1. Johan. 1. 48. Et Paulus rursum nominat se Pharisæum, hac denominatione à Saducæorum secta, se expressè discernens Actor. 23. 6.

Tandem à nostris hoc loco partibus stat tota Orthodoxa Antiquitas. Justinus in Tryphone: Sunt distincti cognominibus, denominati à quibusdam viris, ut quisque fuit autor alicujus novæ doctrinæ: Ex iis alij vocantur Marcionitæ: alij Valentiniani: alij Basilidiani: alij Saturniniani: alij alio vocabulo, quisque à primo inventore sui dogmatis.

Athanasius Serm. 1. contra Arianos: Nunquàm populus ab Episcopis suis, sed à DOMINO, in quem creditum fuit, nomen accepit. Certè à beatis Apostolis, præceptoribus nostris appellationes adepti non sumus: sed à CHRISTO Christiani sumus, & nuncupamur. Illi verò, qui aliunde originem suæ fidei deducunt, MERITO autorum suorum nomina præ se ferunt. Quapropter cùm à CHRISTO omnes Christiani essemus, & diceremur, explosus est Marcion inventor hæreseos. Reliqui autem, qui remanserunt, Christiani titulum retinuerunt. Qui verò Marcionem secuti sunt, non jam indè Christiani, sed Marcionistæ appellati sunt. Ita quoque Valentinus, Basilides, Manichæus, & cæteri Sectatoribus suis nomina impertierunt.
